Title: Current economic situation and monetary policy measures
text: Current economic situation and monetary policy measures Published: 17.11.2003. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Release date of the statement Topic Event Event Event Event Date of events 17.11.2003. Croatia's economic policy in 2004 11th Consultation of the Croatian Society of Economists Opatija 12.11.2003. -15.11.2003. 1. In the IMF's "Staff Report for the Second Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement" material, prepared for the Board meeting on 12 December 2015, On November 30th, it is noted that croatia will achieve a higher rate of economic growth this year with lower-than-expected inflation, and that the fiscal deficit and current account deficit of the balance of payments will be maintained within the framework of the subsequently projected 4.6% and 5.9% of GDP. These are 0.2% and 1.3% of GDP lower deficits than achieved in the previous year. Nevertheless, it said, the country's payment position remains weak and Fond expresses concern about the growth of the system's external vulnerability, urging Croatian authorities to take appropriate fiscal and monetary policy measures to further reduce the balance of payments and foreign debt deficits. Such assessments are based on the assumptionthat the debt-to-debt ratio will be gdp in 2003 should be maintained at last year's level of 68.5%, after which, according to the Fund's scenario, its relative reduction should begin to be reduced to below 60% by 2007. 2. However, the Fund's initial assumption proved to bemore optimistic. Debt growth in the first nine months of the year was a34.6bn. USD nominally or 3.4 billion. This is 74% of GDP, with a tendency to reach 80% of GDP in unchanged conditions in the coming year, compared with 57% in 2001. /By the way, in euro terms, the debt-to-GDP ratio grows from 58% (2001) to 62% (2002) and 72% (2003). And In parallel, other indicators of the degree of indebtedness have deteriorated: 2001. debt/foreign exchange reserves debt/export(RS) the Fund's warning in this part is fully justified. 3. The question arises, of course, how the debt accumulated so far and whether this accumulation was manageable, or whether it simply "happened" to us. Observed at the level of macroeconomic aggregates, the increase in debt over the past three years is the result of a rise in the share of invastititia in GDP from 22n 26.5%, while at the same time saving has stagnated at levels between 18 and 19%. Whose investments are we talking about? If banks' foreign borrowing to sectors is deregistered by the beneficiaries of bank loans in the country and adds direct borrowing of these sectors abroad, it follows that in the structure of the total increase in foreign debt, the public sector (state and public enterprises) participates with 47%, private and mixed enterprises with 29%, and the population with 24%. There are similar relations in the structure of the achievedrzine foreign debt (49 : 34 :17%). Since it thus gives almost half of the debt under the direct or indirect control of the state (the Government and parliament in the sphere of budget and state institutions in the sphere of ownership), that part of the borrowing of mixed enterprises is realized with the drice guarantees and gives the bulk of the debt of the population formed under the influence of imports of durable consumable goods, the demand of which is generally price elastic and can be acted upon by fiscal policy measures, it follows that about 70% of the increase in foreign debtand either directly manageable by economic policy in a broader sense. Thus, by its actions or the absence of this action, it has significantly influenced the effect of the demand for foreign loans. Justified or not, it remains to be seen. First of all by the futureem movement of exports and foreign exchange inflows necessary to repay these loans. 4. It would, however, be naefve to look for the causes of rising debt only in the sphere of demand. Alexandre Lamfalussy (former Director General of BIS) warned of the elementary fact: "There can be no extensive accumulation of debt without the demand for funds encountering their adequate supply and vice versa. There can't be "over-indebtedness" without "re-enactment." In some cases, it is difficult to distinguish whether the responsibility for the accumulation of debt lies with theaspiration or on offer. Who can say, for example, that over-indebtedness is not induced or at least encouraged by creditors. Finally, traveling presentations are often organized or assisted by investment banks looking for opportunities for lenders or investors to place funds. 5. These are all activities that take place under the auspices of the process of globalization, where - encouraged by the IMF and the World Bank -during the 90s and developing countries liberalize their financial systems and open them up for the entry of foreign capital. In doing so, about 70% of foreign capital enters these countriesas a bank loan, and only 30% as investments in equity and bonds. 6. The benefits resulting from this process for debtors are undeniable: the entry of capital, technology and new organisations into the real sector, which increases its productivity, the strengthening of the potential andfikasity of the financial sector with the falling prices of its services, and the general strengthening of market discipline. 7. However, it is also undeniable that the marked benefits that international capital mobility brings to creditors are the basic driving motives of the essence of the 'free market' ideology. One of the most radical critics of this process, Nobel laureate J. Stiglitz , says in the latest book "The Rumblings of the 90s": "The ideology of the free market is in the direct function of ensuring the access of companies from developed countries to foreign marketsand, especially the markets of transition countries, and is not symmetrical for the placement of products from these countries to developed markets. Its primary motive is to create new or at least retain existing jobs in developed countries. It is even worse in the sphere of financial market liberalisation, where "the liberalisation of financial services has even been detrimental to some developing countries: as large international banks have crushed local competitors, the funds they have accumulated have been/directly or indirectly/ channelsdirected towards international companies, not small and medium-sized local firms." 8. Between the two groups uses or, from the debtor's point of view, between the benefit and the price they have to pay for it, there is an area of risk, which is essentially asymmetrical for creditors and borrowers. These are risks to macroeconomic stability when entering and, in particular, when capital leaves the country and the operational risks of capital management. 9. These risks can generate and in practice have generated financial crises in transition countries. Recent research (Calvo) shows that economies that have the following three characteristics are particularly exposed to this danger: 1. closure to international exchange - in terms of a small share of export products in relation to the domestic absorption of imported products 2. znacajnate size of foreign and public debt 3. high dollarisation of the financial system with high currency mismatches of assets and liabilities. Namely, such economies are: 95 highly sensitive to changes in the international environment, which may require sudden and major changesin the balance of payments and exchange rates 95 major exchange rate changes can turn a sustainable fiscal position into an unsustainable and lead to the problem of state solvency 95 addressing the solvency crisis requires significant redistribution of incomes and assets between sectors, with the pauperisation and rising unemployment 95 Vulnerability economies are relatively independent of the exchange rate regime, so exchange rate flexibility can only somewhat affect the reduction of imbalances, but at the same time it can also lead to the opacity of economic policies. 10. If we apply this form to Croatia, it just does not seem to fit into it. Namely: (1) With an average share of exports of goods and services in GDP of 43% (in the period 1996-2003), the Croatian economy is not, of course, closed. However, these exports are insufficient in fromthe nose to the needs and preferences towards imports, so in the trade in goods there is a permanent deficit at the average level of 21% of GDP, and in the exchange of goods and services of 9% of GDP. (2) With the current deficit of the consolidated general government of 4.7% of GDP (2002 and 2003) and with a public debt ratio of about 50%, Croatia does not have a particularly unfavourable fiscal position. However, since the foreign debt of the general government amounts to about 27% of GDP, and the majority of the internal debt is indexed by currency, while the original income of the state is in KUNA, there is a high currency risk. That is why the formal comparison with the criteria ofMaastricht has only a very limited meaning. On the other hand, financing the internal deficit with foreign funds increases foreign exchange reserves, but also makes it difficult to conduct monetary policy, which I will tell more about later. (3) Although the share of foreign currency deposits in the structure of total deposits tends to decrease (which can also be understood as strengthening confidence in the kuna), they are still the dominant element of monetary aggregates, accounting for 81% of savings deposits and 59% of total liquid assets. On the other hand, due to the use of total foreign exchange liabilities to finance imports, the degree of cover of foreign exchange liabilities with liquid foreign exchange assets of the banking system (including the CNB) is reduced from 60% in 2000 to 45% today, so that the short foreign exchange position of the system has increased from 2.6 to 5.5 billion euros, or from 13% to 22% of GDP. Because of all this, the financial system in Croatia is very sensitive to potential shocks and therefore maintaining its stability is a first-class task ofthe overall economic policy. 11. The key move to its liberalization was made by privatising larger banks during 1999 and 2000, after which over 90% of the banking sector was taken over from foreign banks, which thus gradually take control of the axisof the current parts of the financial system (pension and investment funds, leasing companies, insurance companies...) This was followed by amendments to the foreign exchange law, which, according to the IMF's suggestion, allowed the holding of foreign currency deposits of legal entities and, in accordance with the Sporazon Stabilisation and Association, and to adopt a new Foreign Exchange Act, which carried out almost complete liberalisation of long-term capital flows and announced a gradual liberalisation of short-term capital flows. With a loud outcry from brokers,they would also like to liberalize short-term capital immediately. 12. Such liberalisation comes during a period of strong slowdown in growth and then stagnation of economic activity in the EU (eurozone), accompanied by a drastic drop in interest rates and rates of return on capital and government bonds. (Thus, the GDP growth rate decreased from 3.5% in 2000 to just 0.2% in the second quarter of 2003, and exports from 12.5% to -0.6%. Interest rates also fell: 95 in the money market (3mj. dep.) from 4.4% to 2.2% (IX.) 95 loans from commercial banks (over 1 year) from 6.3% to 4.5%, as well as government bond yield rates (2 years) from 4.9% to 2.5%.) In such conditions, a small market, such as the Croatian market, becomes of interest to foreign capital, and for the management of this market it is especially important to establish control over the banking sector. That is why this sector is the most internationalized of all sectors in the Croatian economy. 13. After the initial effects of increasing deposits at the time of conversion of the euro have been exhausted, banks are starting to borrow from their parent banks abroad for the purpose of expanding their credit potential. Thus, during 2002 and I-IX- IX 2003, banks borrowed a total net of EUR 3.4 billion. USD per current or 2.7 billion. USD at a constant exchange rate. Of these, 62% were realized as an increase in deposits of non-residents, which is essentially short-term capital. By placing these funds, banks achieved an average return on capital of 18%. The result was an acceleration of GDP growth from 3.8% (2001) to about 5% (2002-2003) but also a growth in imports at rates of 9%, and a doubling of the current account deficit from about 4% in 2001 to, according to the new calculation, 8.7% of GDP in 2002. 14. Under such conditions, the CNB had to significantly modify its policy. While in 2000 and 2001 it was aimed at increasing the general aspectof the system's vision, by reducing the reserve requirement and interest rates of the central bank, after that the CNB began to pull the brakes. In doing so, in 2002, its policy remained largely within the framework of an orthodox approach - the purchase of foreign currency into foreign exchange reserves, to prevent appreciation, and then partial sterilization of kuna by emission of cashier's records. They increased by 44% and reached 5 billion euros. kuna, which is the equivalent of 16% Ml or 22% MB. Of course, such a policy cannot be rational in the long run and that is why already at the very beginning of 2003 the approach was changed. Accordingly, the CNB's activities during 2003 took place in three steps, interconnected but also somewhat differently motivated. (1) At the beginning of the year: 95 An initial withdrawal of kuna liquidity was carried outand the sale of 315m euros was carried out. after which the CNB no longer directly intervened in the foreign exchange market towards banks, but only through transactions with the state. 95 In parallel, the Decision on the mandatory registration of treasury records and the Decision on 35% coverage of banks' foreign exchange liabilities with liquid foreign exchange receivables were made. The aim was to slow down placements and the overall offer of money without additional sterilization and to limit and increase the transfer of bank in-debt to domestic placements. Despite orchestrated criticism from foreignbanks, politicians and the IMF itself, and the efforts of banks to circumvent the measures by transferring receivables to parent banks and other financial institutions, encouraging leasing deals in other ways, these measures have basically achieved their primary figure. The growth of bank placements slowed down from 26% in the first ten months of 2002 to 11.3% in the same period in 2003, and the growth of money mass slowed from 23% to 6.4%, while the degree of cover of foreign currency liabilities to liquid receivables of banks, which wasfrom 28% in February, increased to 36% by the end of September. (2) The second step was in September when the decision was taken to increase the share of kuna allocation of the required reserve on the foreign exchange liabilities of banks from 25% to 35%, whose financial weight was about 2.1 billion euros. marten. This measurewas partly adopted to support the action of the Decision on the mandatory registration of treasury records, but in essence it was aimed at deflating the surplus liquidity held by banks in the ordinary treasury bills Records. The state of those records has been reduced to zero, while intereston the money market has temporarily jumped from 4% to over 9%. Then there was also a substantive conceptual conflict with the IMF, which goes beyond the framework of the individual monetary policy measure. In fact, at the time, the Fund requested that the tightening of monetary policy be realizedby an orthodox approach to raising interest rates on BZ, which is actually behind a simple logic: if you do not want the liberalized entry of foreign capital to cause you problems in the sphere of financing of consumption and balance of payments deficits, you should provide it with alternative placements at higher rates of return than the domicile ones, at low exchange rate and no credit risk. In other words, transfer part of the emission profits to foreign banks. Access hardly acceptable to any country with monetary sovereignty. (3) The third korak was made in November by taking decisions on further raising the share of kuna allocation of the required reserve on the foreign exchange liabilities of banks from 35% to 42%, weighing HRK 1.5bn. It was made despite the announcement that no new measures would be taken by the end of the year andcaused by the monetary effects of changes in the fiscal position. In fact, contrary to the initial commitment that samurai bonds are merely a bridging loan to generate revenues from the privatisation of INA, after which the largest part will be the equivalent of these bonds of 216m euros. USD to be deposited with the CNB and used to repay the inodugs at the beginning of 2004, the Ministry of Finance, with the tacit consent of the IMF, changed the financing structure of the budget deficit in such a way that samurai bonds represent a substitutefor lower, but also more expensive, borrowing of the budget in the domestic non-bank sector. In such a construction, 400 out of a total of 505m euros. USD of ina revenues are used to finance budget expenditures until the end of 2003 and are not deposited with the CNB for engagementin the coming year. At the same time, for reasons that I would not comment on, the IMF also asked for a change in the methodology of nuir calculations in such a way that the deposits of the state with the central bank do not enter into this calculation, without at the same time agreeing tocover the amount of minimum necessary foreign exchange reserves for the effects of these operations. Consequently, in order to achieve the minimum amount of NUIR set out in the Memorandum of Economic and Financial Policy for this year, the CNB needs to definitively buy at least 400m euros by the end of the year. dollars, i.e. emit about HRK 2.7bn, although for the sezoincrease in demand for money it would be enough to emit only about HRK 1.2bn. The difference, then, should be sterilized either: (a) BZs emissions at high interest rates, as again preferred by the IMF; (b) an increase in the reserve requirement, as decided by theCNB, whereby the choice of a measure with long-term action to alleviate the short-term problem was done, inter alia, in order to have a more permanent impact on the liquidity of banks before the expiry of the Decision on the mandatory registration of treasury records. There was,nravno, an option for the CNB to buy back only 200 million euros. USD and to so consciously go to the non-compliance with the minimum level of foreign exchange reserves set out in the Memorandum, but this would probably lead to the termination of the arrangement, with certain - more political than economic - connotations. 15. After all, if 2003 is viewed from the point of view of monetary policy, the operational objectives of this policy have largely been achieved. The growth of bank placements and the total supply of money has halved compared to the previous year, and when the official placements of banks are added to the placements realized through other financial institutions, the growth of total placements is by a third slower than last year's. The average interest rate on placements, which was 8.1% in September, is lower than last year's, the inter-year inflation rate in October is only 1.5%, and the core inflation rate is 1.0%, the real exchange rate is stable. The slowdown in the growth of money supply has not had a negative impact on economic activity, so it is estimated that the growth of gross domestic product this year will be5%. Not however, it managed to improve relations in trade in goods with foreign countries, so that only good results in the export of services reduced the current account deficit of the balance of payments from 8.7% last year to, it is estimated, 7% of GDP, or to 5.8% if a one-off profit transfer made by Pliva is not counted. The question remains, of course, whether more could have been achieved in the area of reducing the goods deficit and slowing foreign debt growth, and if so, why it did not. The answer is simple. It did notgo any further because the partial slowdown in the growth of the money supply supply, which, due to competition between banks and the high interest rate forward did not induce a rise in interest rates on loans, could not have had a significant impact on the demand for loans and their financed imports , while measures of other policies that could have achieved this were absent. The only potentially effective measure under such conditions could have been capital restrictions, but their introduction by monetary authority (as short-term measures) whenneutrally sobbing other policies to the level and structure of demand could initially cause exactly the kind of effects with which financial crises usually begin (strong exchange rate depreciation and/or fall in foreign exchange reserves, high interest rate growth and effect of all operating r izika). That is why the CNB has not decided on this move, which does not mean that in the future it will not, if it were necessary and consistently incorporated into the whole of economic policy. 16. As for next year, the CNB will continue to have a restrictive effect on the offer of money in order to keep its rast at the level of about 10%, at an inflation rate of less than 2.5% and at a stable exchange rate. In this regard, without real need, some specific additional measures will not be introduced, but the room for manoeuvre left to banks by existing measures will be reduced. The previousand treasury records as an instrument of fine-tuning will be largely replaced by operations on the open market. With expectations that other policies will act consistently towards regulating demand, and boosting export supply, gross domestic product could grow at a rate of 4.5% in the coming year, while the current account deficit of the balance of payments could be reduced to about 5% of GDP. 17. The thinking that is growing louder again, that the main goal of government policy is to maximize economic growth, development and employment "at all costs", while maintaining the stability of the financial system, prices and exchange rates is a sideshow for which the central bank is solely responsible, are as wrong as the bids in the supposed alternative: higher growth with less stablet or greater stability at the cost of lower growth. If we think of it that way, we put ourselves in danger of getting into a situation where we will no longer have stability or growth. As for globalization, it should not be run away from it, nor is it objectively possible, but it should not be passively left to it either. It can make a significant contribution to solving part of our problems, but it will not solve them on its own.

O ijim je investicijama rije? Dezagregira li se inozemno zaduivanje banaka prema sektorima korisnicima bankarskih kredita u zemlji i tome doda izravno zaduivanje tih sektora u inozemstvu, proizlazi da u strukturi ukupnog prirasta inozemnog duga javni sektor (drava i javna poduzea) sudjeluju sa 47%, privatna i mjeovita poduzea sa 29%, a stanovnitvo sa 24%. Prije svega po buduem kretanju izvoza i deviznog priljeva potrebnog za otplatu tih kredita. 4. Bilo bi, meutim, naivno uzroke porasta duga traiti samo u sferi potranje. Alexandre Lamfalussy (bivi generalni direktor BIS-a) upozorio je na elementarnu injenicu: "Ne moe doi do ekstenzivne akumulacije duga a da potranja za sredstvima ne naie na njihovu odgovarajuu ponudu i obrnuto. Ne moe biti "prezaduivanja" bez"prekreditiranja". U pojedinim sluajevima teko je razlikovati lei li odgovornost za akumulaciju duga na potranji ili na ponudi. Tko moe npr. kazati da prezaduivanje nije inducirano ili barem ohrabrivano od strane kreditora. Konano, putujue prezentacije esto su organizirane ili pomagane od strane investicijskih banaka koje trae mogunosti za kreditore ili investitore da plasiraju sredstva. tovie, ima mnogo primjera kada se vodea uloga ponude pojavljuje u cjenovnim indikatorima: smanjujui premije za rizik ili jaajui teaj valute zemlje dunika." 5. Sve su to aktivnosti koje se odvijaju pod okriljem procesa globalizacije, gdje - poticane od strane MMF-a i Svjetske banke -tijekom 90-ih godina i zemlje u razvoju liberaliziraju svoje financijske sustave i otvaraju ih za ulazak stranoga kapitala. Pri tome oko 70% stranoga kapitala ulazi u te zemlje kao bankarski kredit, a samo 30% kao ulaganja u equity i obveznice. 6. Neosporne su koristi koje proizlaze iz tog procesa za dunike: ulaz kapitala, tehnologije i nove organizacije u realni sektor to poveava njegovu produktivnost, jaanje potencijala i efikasnosti financijskog sektora s padom cijena njegovih usluga te ope jaanje trine discipline. 7. Meutim, isto je tako nedvojbeno da su izrazite koristi koje meunarodna mobilnost kapitala donosi vjerovnicima osnovni pokretaki motivi sutina ideologije "slobodnog trita". Jedan od najradikalnijih kritiara tog procesa nobelovac J. Stiglitz u najnovijoj knjizi "Tutnjee 90-te" kae: "Ideologija slobodnog trita u izravnoj je funkciji osiguranja pristupa kompanija iz razvijenih zemalja inozemnim tritima, posebno tritima tranzicijskih zemalja, i nije simetrina za plasman proizvoda iz tih zemalja na razvijena trita. Njen primarni motiv je otvaranje novih ili barem zadravanje postojeih radnih mjesta u razvijenim zemljama. Jo gore je u sferi liberalizacije financijskih trita, gdje je "liberalizacija financijskih usluga bila ak i tetna za neke zemlje u razvoju: kako su velike meunarodne banke zgnjeile lokalne konkurente, fondovi koje su one nagomilale bili su/izravno ili neizravno/ kanalizirani prema meunarodnim kompanijama, a ne prema malim i srednjim lokalnim firmama". 8. Izmeu dviju grupa koristi ili, gledano s aspekta dunika, izmeu koristi i cijene koju oni za to moraju platiti, nalazi se podruje rizika, koje je u sutini asimetrino za kreditore i dunike. To su rizici za makroekonomsku stabilnost pri ulasku i, posebno, pri izlasku kapitala iz zemlje te operativni rizici upravljanja kapitalom. 9. Ti rizici mogu generirati i u praksi su generirali financijske krize u tranzicijskim zemljama. Naime, takve ekonomije su:  vrlo osjetljive na promjene u meunarodnom okruenju, koje mogu zahtijevati nagle i velike promjene u platnoj bilanci i teaju  velike promjene teaja mogu pretvoriti odrivu fiskalnu poziciju u neodrivu i voditi prema problemu solventnosti drave  rjeavanje krize solventnosti zahtijeva znaajnu redistribuciju dohodaka i imovine izmeu sektora, s pauperizacijom i rastom nezaposlenosti  ranjivost ekonomija je relativno neovisna o teajnom reimu, tako da fleksibilnost teaja moe samo donekle utjecati na smanjenje neravnotea, ali istodobno ona moe dovesti i do netransparentnosti ekonomskih politika. 10. Primijenimo li ovaj obrazac na Hrvatsku, ona se samo naizgled ne uklapa u njega. Naime: (1) S prosjenim udjelom izvoza roba i usluga u BDP-u od 43% (u razdoblju 1996. - 2003.), hrvatska ekonomija nije naravno zatvorena. Meutim, taj je izvoz nedovoljan u odnosu na potrebe i preferencije prema uvozu, tako daje u robnoj razmjeni permanentno prisutan deficit na prosjenoj razini od 21% BDP-a, a u razmjeni roba i usluga od 9% BDP-a. (2) S aktualnim deficitom konsolidirane ope drave od 4,7% BDP-a (2002. i 2003.) te sa udjelom javnog duga od oko 50%, Hrvatska nema posebno nepovoljnu fiskalnu poziciju. Meutim, s obzirom na to da inozemni dug ope drave iznosi oko 27% BDP-a, a i najvei dio unutarnjeg duga je valutno indeksiran, dok su izvorni prihodi drave u kunama, postoji visok valutni rizik. Zato formalna usporedba s kriterijima izMaastrichta ima samo vrlo ogranieno znaenje. S druge strane, financiranje unutarnjeg deficita inozemnim sredstvima poveava devizne rezerve, ali i oteava voenje monetarne politike, o emu u vie kazati kasnije. (3) lako udio deviznih depozita u strukturi ukupnih depozita ima tendenciju smanjivanja (to se moe shvatiti i kao jaanje povjerenja u kunu), oni su i dalje dominantan element monetarnih agregata, inei 81% tednih depozita i 59% ukupnih likvidnih sredstava. S druge strane, zbog koritenja ukupne devizne pasive za financiranje uvoza, smanjuje se stupanj pokria devizne pasive likvidnom deviznom aktivom bankovnog sustava (ukljuujui HNB) sa 60% u 2000. na dananjih 45%, tako da se kratka devizna pozicija sustava poveala sa 2,6 na 5,5 mlrd. eura, ili sa 13% na 22% BDP-a. Zbog svega toga, financijski sustav u Hrvatskoj je vrlo osjetljiv na potencijalne okove te je zato odravanje njegove stabilnosti prvorazredni zadatak ukupne ekonomske politike. 11. Kljuni potezu njegovoj liberalizaciji uinjen je privatizacijom veih banaka tijekom 1999. i 2000. godine, nakon ega je preko 90% bankarskog sektora preuzeto od stranih banaka, koje time postupno preuzimaju kontrolu i nad ostalim dijelovima financijskog sustava (mirovinski i investicijski fondovi, leasing kompanije, osiguravajue kue...) Uslijedile su izmjene deviznog zakona kojima je, po sugestiji MMF-a, doputeno dranje deviznih depozita pravnih osoba te, sukladno Sporazumu o stabilizaciji i pridruivanju, te donijet novi Zakon o deviznom poslovanju, kojim je izvrena gotovo potpuna liberalizacija tokova dugoronoga kapitala i najavljena postupna liberalizacija tokova kratkoronoga kapitala. Uz glasno negodovanje brokera koji bi i kratkoroni kapital eljeli liberalizirati odmah. 12. Do takve liberalizacije dolazi u razdoblju snanog usporavanja rasta, a zatim i stagnacije ekonomske aktivnosti u EU (eurozoni), praene drastinim padom kamatnih stopa i stopa prinosa na kapital i dravne obveznice. (Tako je stopa rasta BDP-a smanjena sa 3,5% u 2000. na samo 0,2% u drugom tromjeseju 2003. godine, a izvoza sa 12,5 na -0,6%. Pale su i kamatne stope:  na tritu novca (3mj. dep.) sa 4,4 na 2,2% (IX.)  na kredite poslovnih banaka (preko 1 god.) sa 6,3 na 4,5%, kao i stope prinosa na dravne obveznice (2 god.) sa 4,9 na 2,5%.) U takvim uvjetima i malo trite, kao to je hrvatsko, postaje interesantno stranom kapitalu, a za upravljanje tim tritem posebno je znaajno uspostaviti kontrolu nad bankovnim sektorom. Upravo zato je taj sektor i najvie internacionaliziran od svih sektora u hrvatskoj ekonomiji. 13. Nakon to su iscrpljeni poetni efekti poveanja depozita u vrijeme konverzije inovaluta u euro, banke se za potrebe irenja svojega kreditnog potencijala poinju zaduivati kod matinih banaka u inozemstvu. Tako su se tijekom 2002. i I. - IX. 2003. banke ukupno neto zaduile za 3,4 mlrd. USD po tekuem ili 2,7 mlrd. USD po stalnom teaju. Od toga je 62% realizirano kao prirast depozita nerezidenata, to je u sutini kratkoroni kapital. Plasirajui ta sredstva banke su ostvarile prosjeni prinos na kapital od 18%. Posljedica je bila ubrzanje rasta BDP-a sa 3,8% (2001.) na oko 5% (2002. - 2003.) ali i rast uvoza po stopama od 9%, te udvostruenje deficita tekuih transakcija s oko 4% u 2001. na, prema novom izraunu, 8,7% BDP-a u 2002. godini. 14. U takvim uvjetima HNB je morao znaajno modificirati svoju politiku. Dok je u 2000. i 2001. godini ona bila usmjerena na poveanje ope likvidnosti sustava, smanjenjem obvezne rezerve i kamatnih stopa centralne banke, nakon toga HNB poinje povlaiti konicu. Pri tome je, tijekom 2002., njegova politika uglavnom ostala u okvirima ortodoksnog pristupa - otkup deviza u devizne rezerve, da bi se sprijeila aprecijacija, a zatim djelomina sterilizacija kuna emisijom blagajnikih zapisa. Oni su poveani za 44% i dostigli 5 mlrd. kuna, to je ekvivalent od 16% Ml ili 22% MB. Naravno da takva politika ne moe biti dugorono racionalna i zato je ve na samom poetku 2003. godine pristup izmijenjen. Sukladno tome, djelovanje HNB tijekom 2003. godine odvijalo se u tri koraka, meusobno povezana ali i donekle razliito motivirana. (1) Na poetku godine:  Izvreno je inicijalno povlaenje kunske likvidnosti prodajom 315 mil. eura, nakon ega HNB vie nije izravno intervenirao na deviznom tritu prema bankama, ve samo kroz transakcije s dravom.  Paralelno s time donijete su Odluka o obveznom upisu blagajnikih zaapisa te Odluka o 35%-tnom pokriu deviznih obveza banaka likvidnim deviznim potraivanjima. Cilj je bio usporiti plasmane i ukupnu ponudu novca bez dodatne sterilizacije te ograniiti i poskupiti transferiranje inozaduivanja banaka u domae plasmane. Unato orkestriranim kritikama od strane banaka, politiara i samog MMF-a te nastojanju banaka da zaobiu djelovanje mjera prijenosom potraivanja na matine banke i druge financijske institucije, poticanjem leasing poslova i na druge naine, te su mjere u osnovi ipak postigle svoj primarni cilj. Rast plasmana banaka usporenje sa 26% u prvih deset mjeseci 2002. na 11,3% u istom razdoblju 2003. godine, a rast novane mase usporenje sa 23% na 6,4%, dok je stupanj pokria deviznih obveza likvidnim potraivanjima banaka, koji je u veljai iznosio samo 28%, povean do kraja rujna na 36%. (2) Drugi korak bio je u rujnu kad je donijeta Odluka o poveanju udjela kunskog izdvajanja obvezne rezerve na deviznu pasivu banaka sa 25 na 35%, ija je financijska teina iznosila oko 2,1 mlrd. kuna. Taje mjera djelomino donijeta da podri djelovanje Odluke o obveznom upisu blagajnikih zapisa, ali u sutini ona je bila usmjerena na ispuhavanje vikova likvidnosti koju su banke drale u redovnim blagajnikim zapisima. Stanje tih zapisa svedeno je na nulu, dok je kamatna stopa na tritu novca privremeno skoila sa 4% na preko 9%. Tada je dolo i do sutinskog koncepcijskog sukoba s MMF-om, koji prelazi okvire pojedinane mjere monetarne politike. Fond je, naime, tada traio da se zaotravanje monetarne politike realizira ortodoksnim pristupom poveanja kamatnih stopa na BZ, iza ega zapravo stoji jednostavna logika: ako ne elite da vam liberalizirani ulazak stranog kapitala pravi probleme u sferi financiranja potronje i deficita platne bilance, trebate mu omoguiti alternativne plasmane uz vie stope prinosa od domicilnih, pri niskom teajnom i nikakvom kreditnom riziku. Drugim rijeima, transferirati dio emisijske dobiti stranim bankama. Pristup teko prihvatljiv bilo kojoj zemlji s monetarnim suverenitetom. (3) Trei korak uinjen je u studenom donoenjem odluka o daljnjem podizanju udjela kunskog izdvajanja obvezne rezerve na deviznu pasivu banaka sa 35 na 42%, teine 1,5 mlrd. kuna. Ona je donijeta unato najavi da se do kraja godine nee poduzimati nove mjere i uzrokovana je monetarnim efektima promjena fiskalne pozicije. Naime, suprotno poetnom opredjeljenju da su samuraj obveznice samo kredit za premoivanje do ostvarivanja prihoda od privatizacije INA-e, nakon ega e najvei dio protuvrijednost tih obveznica od 216 mil. USD biti deponiran kod HNB-a i sluiti za otplatu inodugova na poetku 2004. godine, Ministarstvo financija je uz preutnu suglasnost MMF-a izmijenilo strukturu financiranja proraunskog deficita na nain da samuraj obveznice predstavljaju nadomjestak za nie, ali i skuplje, zaduivanje prorauna kod domaeg nebankovnog sektora. U takvoj konstrukciji, 400 od ukupno 505 mil. USD prihoda od INA-e slui za financiranje proraunskih rashoda do kraja 2003. godine i ne deponiraju se kod HNB-a za angairanje u iduoj godini. Istodobno, iz razloga koje ne bih komentirao, MMF je traio i promjenu metodologije izrauna NUIR-a na nain da depoziti drave kod centralne banke ne ulaze u taj izraun, a da istodobno nije pristao da se za efekte ovih operacija korigira iznos minimalno potrebnih deviznih rezervi nanie. Posljedino tome, da bi se ostvario minimalni iznos NUIR-a utvren u Memorandumu o ekonomskoj i financijskoj politici za ovu godinu, HNB treba do kraja godine definitivno otkupiti barem 400 mil. dolara, odnosno emitirati oko 2,7 mlrd. kuna, iako bi za sezonsko poveanje potranje za novcem bilo dovoljno emitirati samo oko 1,2 mlrd. kuna. Razliku, znai, treba sterilizirati bilo: (a) emisijom BZs visokim kamatnim stopama, kao to je ponovno preferirao MMF; bilo (b) poveanjem obvezne rezerve, kao to se odluio HNB, pri emu je odabir mjere s dugoronim djelovanjem za ublaavanje kratkoronog problema bio uinjen, izmeu ostalog, i zato da trajnije utjee na likvidnost banaka prije prestanka vaenja Odluke o obveznom upisu blagajnikih zapisa. Postojala je, naravno, i opcija da HNB otkupi samo 200 mil. USD i da tako svjesno ide na neispunjavanje minimalne razine deviznih rezervi utvrene Memorandumom, ali bi to vjerojatno dovelo do prekida aranmana, s odreenim - vie politikim nego ekonomskim - konotacijama. 15. Nakon svega, promatra li se 2003. godina s aspekta monetarne politike, operativni ciljevi te politike uglavnom su ostvareni. Rast plasmana banaka i ukupne ponude novca prepolovljen je u odnosu na prethodnu godinu, a kada se oficijelnim plasmanima banaka pridodaju i plasmani realizirani posredstvom drugih financijskih institucija, rast ukupnih plasmana je za treinu sporiji od prologodinjeg. Prosjena kamatna stopa na plasmane, koja je u rujnu iznosila 8,1%, nia je od prologodinje, meugodinja stopa inflacije u listopadu iznosi samo 1,5%, a stopa temeljne inflacije 1,0%, realni teaj je stabilan. Usporavanje rasta ponude novca nije se negativno odrazilo na privrednu aktivnost, tako da se ocjenjuje da e rast bruto domaeg proizvoda u ovoj godini iznositi 5%. Nije se, meutim, uspjelo poboljati odnose u robnoj razmjeni s inozemstvom, tako da su samo dobri rezultati u izvozu usluga smanjili deficit tekuih transakcija platne bilance sa prologodinjih 8,7% na, ocjenjuje se, 7% BDP-a, odnosno na 5,8% ako se ne rauna jednokratni transfer dobiti izvren od strane Plive. Ostaje, naravno, pitanje da li se moglo postii vie na podruju smanjenja robnog deficita i usporavanja prirasta inozemnog duga, i ako jest, zato nije. Odgovor je jednostavan. Nije se postiglo vie zato to parcijalno usporavanje rasta ponude novca koje, zbog konkurencije izmeu banaka i visokoga kamatnog spreda nije induciralo rast kamatnih stopa na kredite, nije moglo imati znaajniji utjecaj na potranju za kreditima i njima financirani uvoz, dok su mjere ostalih politika kojima se to moglo postii izostale. Jedina potencijalno efikasna mjera u takvim uvjetima mogle su biti kapitalne restrikcije, ali bi njihovo uvoenje od strane monetarne vlasti (kao kratkorone mjere) pri neutralnom utjecaju ostalih politika na razinu i strukturu potranje, moglo inicijalno izazvati upravo onakve efekte s kakvima obino i poinju financijske krize (jaka deprecijacija teaja i/ili pad deviznih rezervi, visok rast kamata te efektuiranje svih operativnih rizika). Zato se HNB nije odluio za taj potez, to ne znai da ubudue nee, ako bi on bio potreban i konzistentno uklopljen u cjelinu ekonomske politike. 16. to se tie idue godine, HNB e nastaviti ograniavajue djelovati na ponudu novca da bi se njezin rast zadrao na razini od oko 10%, pri stopi inflacije nioj od 2,5% i uz stabilan teaj. S tim u vezi nee se, bez stvarne potrebe, uvoditi neke posebne dodatne mjere, ali e se smanjiti manevarski prostor koji bankama ostavljaju postojee mjere. Dosadanji blagajniki zapisi kao instrument finog podeavanja bit e uglavnom zamijenjeni operacijama na otvorenom tritu. Uz oekivanja da e ostale politike konzistentno djelovati u pravcu reguliranja potranje, i poticaja izvozne ponude, bruto domai proizvod mogao bi u iduoj godini rasti po stopi od 4,5%, dok bi se deficit tekuih transakcija platne bilance mogao smanjiti na oko 5% BDP-a. 17. Razmiljanja koja su ponovno sve glasnija, kako je osnovni cilj vladine politike maksimizacija ekonomskog rasta, razvoja i zapoljavanja "pod svaku cijenu", dok je odravanje stabilnosti financijskog sustava, cijena i teaja sporedna stvar za koju je iskljuivo odgovorna centralna banka, jednako su pogrena kao i licitacije u navodnoj alternativi: vii rast uz manju stabilnost ili vea stabilnost pod cijenu nieg rasta. Budemo li tako razmiljali, izlaemo se opasnosti da doemo u situaciju u kojoj vie neemo imati ni stabilnost niti rast. A to se tie globalizacije, od nje ne treba bjeati niti je to objektivno mogue, ali joj se ne smije ni pasivno prepustiti. Ona moe znatno pridonijeti rjeavanju dijela naih problema, ali ih sama nee rijeiti.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary policy
text: Monetary policy Published: 12/5/2008 Type Speech Speaker dr. 8eeljko Rohatinski, governor of the CNB from 12. July 2000 to 7. [ Getty Images] Publish Date Statements 9.5.2008. Event 11. scientific and professional conference Croatian money market Venue Opatija Date of event 8.5.2008. - 9.5.2008. 1. A year ago, I spoke at this same place about the changes thatglobalization of financial flows is making in monetary systems and monetary policies in general, and in small, highly euroized countries, in particular. The basis of these policies can no longer be the complete endogenous creation of the money supply by the central bank, which then, through interaction with demand, deliberately determines the general level of prices, exchange rates and interest rates. Unlike this "neoclassical" picture, monetary policy in the conditions of liberalized financial flows is primarily a "filter" that through the relations of relative prices and yields affects the entry and exit of global capital from the financial system of the country. Primarily through this function, she also acts as one of the moderators of general economic performances. Six months earlier, at the Zagreb Stock Exchange Conference, I recalled the then recent analysis of the BIS how the entry of the BIS capital manifests itself differently in the market of goods and services in relation to the stock and real estate markets. While in the first of these, the proinflationary effects of increased demand in a small country are quickly depreciated by imports, so price stability is often accompanied by a growing balance of payments deficit, in the stock and real estate markets it is possible shock absorbers on the supply side are much weaker. Thus, increased, loan-funded, demand is significantly transferred directly to prices. This encourages investors and increases the face value of collateral, all of which together encourage stimulates even stronger credit expansion with the possibility of the appearance of a pure "bubble effect". In contrast, when expectations change in terms of risk and return on equity or the financial position of the investors themselves, the whole process moves in the opposite direction. Prices are falling, with a negative impact on the real sector now weighed down by high deficits, debt and low investment activity. And, if, in parallel, shocks occur on the supply side of goods and services and trigger inflation, the situation takes on crisis characteristics. So, it is a scenario that quite well anticipated the events that followed, regardless of the fact that their specific causes and place of occurrence are somewhat different from those to which the aforementioned analyses referred. These events were not unexpected in any case, although, of course, it was difficult to accurately predict what, when and where the "trigger" of their effectuation would be. 2. Knowing all this, and being instructed by previous financial crises in certain countries, the CNB has been highlighting for several years the high risks to which the Croatian economy is exposed in a globalized financial system. The risks of both the direct transmission of possible external shocks and internal shocks caused by processes triggered or supported by the inflow of foreign capital in conditions of relatively low levels of disposable income and a high propensity for consumption in the country. Therefore, the primary task of the CNB's policy throughout this period was to dimension the entry of capital into the banking system in such a way that it supports sustainable economic growth, and not to make it its own by the consequences of its uncontrolled expansion. constraint. In doing so, it should be borne in mind that all large banks in Croatia actually operate as financial conglomerates, so foreign capital and alternative forms of domestic savings are integrally directed to the markets, with the aim of maximizing returns at the level of Conglomerates. Such an approach to monetary policy has placed the focus in the selection of its instruments on those that increase the price of banks' external sources of funds, limit their credit multiplicity, or ultimately reduce high rates of return on the capital of banks as the main motive for aggressive loan supply. For this purpose, the CNB primarily used and gradually tightened direct impact measures (GOP, OBZ, minimum foreign exchange receivables, while maintaining a high reserve requirement rate), and then complementary and prudential measures to strengthen and reduced the linearity of the action of direct measures. Such a policy, of course, was not well received by banks, and often by individual political structures. And not just from them. International financial institutions have very accurately detected the risks arising from the expansionary entry of foreign capital, but in the sphere of monetary policy they preferred solutions of prudential and "market" character, emphasizing the long-term harmfulness of "administrative" measures. In addition, they suggested rapid development and deepening of the financial market, including the introduction of new instruments such as e.g. securitization of claims. That is why they were disappointed when the CNB included liquid assets that banks intended to obtain by selling part of their receivables in the basis for calculating mandatory treasury bills, thus significantly complicating the development of such deals in Croatia. In the meantime, it is known what happened in the world and what role the securitization activities associated with a strong credit expansion, whose security could not effectively protect existing prudential regulations, played in this, while "market" measures (e.g. the record low interest rates of central banks) actually directly favored the expansion of these deals. At that time, governments and central banks, in an attempt to repair the damagecaused, resorted to "the goal justifies the means", which have little in common with what they had previously recommended to transition countries, such as Croatia. In such a situation, their proclaimed aversion to "administrative measures" had to be partially weakened, if they were evidently in the function of limiting the causes of the potential occurrence of this kind of problem. This has also significantly changed their rhetoric towards the CNB's policy. We are definitely not "bad guys" anymore, although we will hardly ever become "good guys" for them, because as there are no ideal solutions in general, it is evident that the measures that the CNB is not devoid of certain weaknesses and limitations. However, despite all the limitations and "collateral casualties", the CNB has no realistic alternative and will therefore continue to conduct the current type of monetary policy for as long as necessary. and possible (related to entry into the EU). In doing so, of course, we will closely monitor the developments in the world and, if necessary, adjust the intensity of individual measures. 3. And, as the latest estimates and forecasts show, the current financial crisis in the world, accompanied by acceleration of inflation and slowing economic growth, is much deeper and longer-term than previously assumed. And therefore, while financial sector losses in the U.S. and Western Europe are not expected to be significantly transmitted directly to the economies of transition countries, the indirect impacts of these losses and the psychosis created in the global market in general could be very Respectable. Especially for countries with high balance of payments deficits and foreign debt. In this regard, three aspects of the problem are particularly significant for us. First, the slowdown in economic growth in the "old" EU member states from 2.6% in 2007 to 2.6% in 2007. on, it is projected, 1.3% in 2008, with the consequent slowdown of their import demand from 5.2% to 3.2%. In such conditions, it will not be easy to maintain the dynamics of real growth of total exports of goods and services, which last year amounted to 5.7%, and contributed to the growth of croatia's gross domestic product with 2.9 percentage points. Secondly, the high level of prices of energy, agricultural products and some other raw materials on the world market increases expenditure on imports, which, combined with possible restrictions in the sphere of exports , leaves relatively little room for reducing the balance of payments deficit that is In 2007, it amounted to EUR 3.2bn , or 8.7% of gross domestic product. Third, with such an ongoing deficit, and given that in 2008 the principal amount of external debt of 7 billion is due, the principal amount of foreign debt is due to be collected. 1.4 billion and 1.4 billion. The total need for gross use of foreign loans this year is estimated at around 10.7bn euros. It is in this area that potentially the greatest danger threatens if the financial crisis in the world would have a significant impact on lending conditions, i.e. in an extreme case, on the net withdrawal of capital from the country. In this case, the CNB would, of course, intervene with all available means by maintaining external liquidity and preventing a "credit crunch" in the country. And this is where the positive effects of monetary policy so far come to the fore. They are reflected in two elements. First, although this policy has never been really restrictive in the sense that a lack of money supply limits economic growth, its operation has nevertheless significantly slowed the growth of loans, external debt and thus loan obligations. the one that would be without such a policy. This is now openly acknowledged by the IMF. And secondly, the use of "administrative" instruments allowed the formation of liquid reserves at the level of the total banking system, which can serve as a shock absorber in the event of an external shock. Hypothetically, if necessary, the CNB can lower the reserve requirement rate from 17% to 2%, abolish the reserve limit and the requirements regarding the minimum required foreign exchange claims. This would increase liquidity by 807.6bn at the system level. 30.3 billion euros. marten. To this should be added the net foreign reserves of the central bank of 7.5 billion euros, which is a sufficient guarantee that the system can withstand a one-time external impact and continue to operate relatively normally. Especially in conditions of a stable exchange rate. Although for now there are no indications of the need to take such radical measures on a broad basis, the possibility of their partial use to alleviate individual problems is not excluded. For example, the state budget foresees the issuance of bonds on the foreign market in the amount of 750 million euros this year. euro, which, given the amount, can prove to be a risky operation bearing in mind the recent negative experiences of some other countries. Therefore, starting from the fact that the majority of the funds raised in this way will be used to settle the foreign currency liabilities of the state, the CNB is ready to lower, for the purpose of substituting this foreign borrowing of the state by borrowing from domestic banks the rate of minimum required foreign exchange receivables from the current 32% to 29%. This would also avoid partial displacement of other sectors from the loan market. For the same reason, it is logical to expect that the Government will manage the budget deficit with special attention and, depending on inflation of accelerated growth in nominal revenues, consider the possibilities of its additional reduction in 2008. 4. Except in this element, the whole of monetary developments at the beginning of the year takes place in accordance with forecasts. Increasing the weighting for currency-induced credit risk and conditioning the reaching of the "permitted" growth of bank placements by increasing the capital adequacy rate requires the recapitalisation of banks. In this function, and partly to reduce the impact of domestic market volatility on their liquidity, banks initially received 480m euros of non-resident deposits in the first quarter and increased their external debt by 560m euros in total. Euros. Furthermore, after fluctuations related to the public offer of HT shares and changes in the structure of total savings, the movement of savings deposits has stabilized and in mid-April they are 14.4% higher than last year's at the same time, and foreign currency deposits are 14.4% higher in mid-April. deposits are higher by 17.6%. Finally, following a temporary suspension in January, in order to counter depreciation expectations in the face of increased inflation , the CNB restarted open market operations at levels sufficient to facilitate the management of banks' short-term liquidity. All this has significantly improved the overall liquidity of the system and lowered interest rates in the money market. While at the very beginning of the year they exceeded 10%, since then they have again moved on a daily basis below 5% (average 3.2%), on which the central bank's repo rate is also formed. In accordance with the increase in foreign prices and related to this, the increase in interest rates on domestic sources of funds, interest rates on bank loans have also increased slightly. However, this has largely only returned to levels from the beginning of the upward phase of the current credit cycle during which the policy of lowering interest rates was directly in the function of stimulating demand for loans Finally, the nominal exchange rate stagnates firmly in a narrow range of HRK 7.25 to HRK 7.28 for the euro and, while limiting the growth of bank placements, represents the basic anchor and a way of anti-inflation ary action of monetary policy. In such conditions, and after a targeted slowdown in the second part of 2007, provoked by the tightening of the Decision on mandatory subscription of treasury bills, and then the permitted, and partly only fictitiously realized, "jump" in December, bank placements move in the first four months (state 20. April) at an annual growth rate of 12.0%, approximately the same as the total money supply (10.8%). In parallel, total external debt increased by 960m euros in the first quarter. the euro is 14 % higher than at the same time last year, without pointing to particularly increased problems in the sphere of external financing of enterprises. We therefore assess that, even without further adjustment of the monetary policy instruments, the basic parameters of monetary flows from the first quarter will be maintained throughout 2008, as predicted by the projection, while, with the substitution of foreign domestic borrowing by the government, the total foreign debt could rise by about 3 billion this year. euro or by about 9%. In total, this will be sufficient to finance real gross domestic product growth at a rate of about 4.5%, with an average inflation rate of 5.5 to 6%, but also with a still high balance of payments deficit of about 8.5% of gross domestic product. 5. If these parameters are placed in the context of global developments, it could be concluded that, despite slower production growth and higher inflation than last year, the Croatian economy is going through the current period of global turbulence with relatively small casualties. However, this cannot be a cause for complacency, just as the fact that some other countries have the same or even greater problems does not It can be a comfort. Indeed, all of this points to the need for greater caution. The high balance of payments deficit and external debt are indicators of our persistent vulnerability to changes and disruptions in global financial flows. And, no matter how much these flows externally determine the monetary environment and the supply of money in Croatia, the demand for it and the manner and rationality of its use are decided primarily by our companies, households and State. Within the framework set by the overall economic policy and appropriate financial regulations. It is evident that changes in this area are necessary and should be realized in a relatively short period of time. Namely, as accession to the EU approaches, the moment is approaching when the CNB will abolish the GOP and significantly reduce the reserve requirement rate, i.e. relax the set of instruments that has proven to be a good potential protection against global turbulence and part of domestic irrationality. In doing so , the essence of the problem will not lie in the release of immobilized liquidity - it will occur very gradually, not once - but in the need for the current role of these bid regulation instruments to be taken over by some other instruments and some other policies regulating the demand for money. More restrictive and selective, and therefore riskier than before. And, if someone thinks that by joining the EU these problems will become less, it is enough to look at the problems faced today by some new members who until recently were highlighted as an exemplary example of successful transition and rapid economic growth. If we don't learn anything from it, the only thing left to do is repeat some of their mistakes. a9
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna politika Objavljeno: 12.5.2008. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 9.5.2008. 11. znanstveno-struna konferencija Hrvatsko novano trite Opatija 8.5.2008. -9.5.2008. 1. Prije godinu dana govorio sam na ovom istom mjestu o promjenama kojeglobalizacija financijskih tokova unosi u monetarne sustave i monetarne politike openito, a u malim, visoko euriziranim zemljama, posebno. Osnovu tih politika vie ne moe predstavljati potpuno endogeno kreiranje ponude novca od strane sredinje banke koja onda kroz interakciju s potranjom ciljano determinira opu razinu cijena, teaj i kamatne stope. Za razliku od te "neoklasine" slike, monetarna politika u uvjetima liberaliziranih financijskih tokova je prije svega "filter" koji kroz odnose relativnih cijena i prinosa utjee na ulazak i izlazak globalnog kapitala iz financijskog sustava zemlje. Prvenstveno kroz tu funkciju ona djeluje i kao jedan od moderatora opih ekonomskih performanci. Pri tome taj kapital ima svoju referentnu inozemnu kamatnu stopu, dok njegova konverzija u nacionalnu valutu aprecijacijski utjee na teaj. est mjeseci ranije, na Konferenciji Zagrebake burze, podsjetio sam pak na tada recentne analize BIS-a kako se ulazak kapitala razliito manifestira na tritu roba i usluga u odnosu na trita dionica i nekretnina. Dok se na prvom od njih proinflacijsko djelovanje poveane potranje u maloj zemlji brzo amortizira uvozom pa je stabilnost cijena esto praena rastuim deficitom platne bilance, na tritima dionica i nekretnina mogui amortizeri na strani ponude su mnogo slabiji. Tako se poveana, kreditima financirana, potranja u znaajnoj mjeri izravno prenosi na cijene. To ohrabruje investitore i poveava nominalnu vrijednost kolaterala, a sve to zajedno potie jo snaniju kreditnu ekspanziju s mogunou pojave istog "bubble efekta". Nasuprot tome, kada se promijene oekivanja u pogledu rizika i povrata na kapital ili financijski poloaj samih investitora, cijeli proces kree u suprotnom smjeru. Cijene padaju, s negativnim utjecajem na realni sektor koji je sada optereen visokim deficitom, dugom i niskom investicijskom aktivnou. A, ako jo paralelno s time nastupe i okovi na strani ponude roba i usluga te pokrenu inflaciju, situacija poprima krizna obiljeja. Dakle, rije je o scenariju koji je sasvim dobro anticipirao dogaaje koji su uslijedili, bez obzira to se njihovi konkretni uzroci i mjesto pojave donekle razlikuju od onih na koje su se navedene analize referirale. Ti dogaaji u svakom sluaju nisu bili neoekivani, iako je, naravno, bilo teko precizno predvidjeti to, kada i gdje e biti "okida" njihovog efektuiranja. 2. Spoznavajui sve to, a pouen i ranijim financijskim krizama u pojedinim zemljama, HNB ve vie godina istie visoke rizike kojima je hrvatska ekonomija izloena u globaliziranom financijskom sustavu. Rizike kako izravnog prenoenja moguih eksternih okova, tako i unutarnjih okova izazvanih procesima koje je potaknuo ili koje podrava priljev inozemnog kapitala u uvjetima relativno niske razine raspoloivog dohotka i visoke sklonosti potronji uzemlji. Zato je primarni zadatak politike HNB-a u cijelom tom razdoblju bio da dimenzionira ulazak kapitala u bankovni sustav na nain da on bude podrka odrivom ekonomskom rastu, a ne da posljedicama svoje nekontrolirane ekspanzivnosti postane njegovo ogranienje. Pri tome treba imati na umu da sve velike banke u Hrvatskoj zapravo posluju kao financijski konglomerati pa se u njima angairani strani kapital i alternativni oblici domae tednje integralno usmjeravaju na trita, s ciljem maksimiranja prinosa na razini konglomerata. Takav pristup monetarnoj politici stavio je teite u odabiru njezinih instrumenata na one koji poskupljuju eksterne izvore sredstava banaka, ograniavaju njihovu kreditnu multiplikaciju, odnosno u krajnjoj konzekvenci koji funkcionalno smanjuju visoke stope prinosa na kapital banaka kao osnovni motiv agresivne ponude kredita. U tu svrhu HNB je prvenstveno koristio i postupno zaotravao mjere izravnog utjecaja (GOP, OBZ, minimalno potrebna devizna potraivanja, uz zadravanje visoke stope obvezne priuve), a onda komplementarno i prudencijalne mjere kako bi osnaio i smanjio linearnost djelovanja izravnih mjera. Takva politika, naravno, nije bila dobro primana od strane banaka, a nerijetko i od strane pojedinih politikih struktura. I ne samo od njih. Meunarodne financijske institucije su vrlo precizno detektirale rizike koji izviru iz ekspanzivnog ulaska stranog kapitala, ali su u sferi monetarne politike preferirale rjeenja prudencijalnog i "trinog" karaktera, naglaavajui dugoronu tetnost "administrativnih" mjera. Pored toga, sugerirale su i brzi razvoj te produbljivanje financijskog trita, ukljuujui i uvoenje novih instrumenata kao to je npr. sekuritizacija potraivanja. Zato su bile i razoarane kada je HNB ukljuio likvidna sredstva koja su banke namjeravale pribaviti prodajom dijela svojih potraivanja u osnovicu za obraun obveznih blagajnikih zapisa i time bitno oteao razvoj takvih poslova u Hrvatskoj. U meuvremenu, poznato je to se dogodilo u svijetu i koju su ulogu u tome odigrali upravo poslovi sekuritizacije povezani sa snanom kreditnom ekspanzijom, iju sigurnost nije mogla efikasno zatititi postojea prudencijalna regulativa, dok su "trine" mjere (npr. rekordno niske kamatne stope centralnih banaka) zapravo izravno pogodovale irenju tih poslova. Tada su vlade i centralne banke u pokuaju sanacije nastalih teta posegnule za rjeenjima tipa "cilj opravdava sredstva", koja imaju malo zajednikog s onim to su prethodno preporuivali tranzicijskim zemljama, poput Hrvatske. U takvoj situaciji, morala je djelomino oslabiti i njihova proklamirana odbojnost prema "administrativnim mjerama", ako su one evidentno u funkciji ograniavanja uzroka potencijalnog nastanka takve vrste problema. Time se znaajno promjenila i njihova retorika prema politici HNB-a. Vie definitivno nismo "bad guys" iako teko da emo za njih ikad postati sasvim "good guys", jer kako openito nema idealnih rjeenja tako je evidentno da ni mjere koje poduzima HNB nisu liene odreenih slabosti i ogranienja. Meutim, bez obzira na sva ogranienja i "kolateralne rtve", HNB nema realnu alternativu i zato e nastaviti s voenjem dosadanjeg tipa monetarne politike dokle god to bude potrebno i mogue (vezano uz ulazak u EU). Kod toga emo, naravno, pozorno pratiti zbivanja u svijetu i po potrebi prilagoavati intenzitet pojedinih mjera. 3. A, kao to najnovije procjene i prognoze pokazuju, aktualna financijska kriza u svijetu, praena ubrzanjem inflacije i usporavanjem ekonomskog rasta, znatno je dublja i dugoronija nego to se ranije pretpostavljalo. I zato, iako se ne oekuje da e se gubici financijskog sektora u SAD i Zapadnoj Europi znaajnije izravno prenijeti na ekonomije tranzicijskih zemalja, neizravni utjecaji tih gubitaka i openito psihoze stvorene na globalnom tritu mogli bi biti vrlo respektabilni. Posebno za zemlje s visokim deficitom platne bilance i inozemnim dugom. U tom smislu, za nas su posebno znaajna tri aspekta problema. Prvo, usporavanje ekonomskog rasta u "starim" lanicama EU sa 2.6% u 2007. na, predvia se, 1.3% u 2008. godini, uz posljedino usporavanje njihove uvozne potranje sa 5.2% na 3.2%. U takvim uvjetima, nee biti lako odrati dinamiku realnog rasta ukupnog izvoza roba i usluga koja je u proloj godini iznosila 5.7%, i pridonijela rastu bruto domaeg proizvoda Hrvatske sa 2.9 postotnih poena. Drugo, visoka razina cijena energenata, poljoprivrednih proizvoda i nekih drugih sirovina na svjetskom tritu poveava izdatke za uvoz, to u kombinaciji s moguim ogranienjima u sferi izvoza ostavlja relativno mali prostor za smanjenje deficita platne bilance koji je u 2007. godini iznosio 3.2 mlrd. eura, odnosno 8.7% bruto domaeg proizvoda. Tree, uz takav tekui deficit, a s obzirom da u 2008. godini dospijeva na naplatu glavnica inozemnog duga od 7 mlrd. eura i jo 1.4 mlrd. eura kamata, ukupne potrebe za bruto koritenjem inozemnih kredita u ovoj godini procjenjuju se na oko 10.7 mlrd. eura. Upravo na tom podruju prijeti i potencijalno najvea opasnost ako bi se financijska kriza u svijetu znaajnije odrazila na uvjete kreditiranja, odnosno u ekstremnom sluaju na neto povlaenje kapitala iz zemlje. U tom bi sluaju HNB, naravno, intervenirao svim raspoloivim sredstvima odravajui eksternu likvidnost i sprjeavajui "creditcrunch" uzemlji. I tu zapravo dolaze do izraaja pozitivni efekti dosadanje monetarne politike. Oni se ogledaju u dva elementa. Prvo, iako ta politika nije nikada bila stvarno restriktivna u smislu da nedostatna ponuda novca ograniava ekonomski rast, njeno djelovanje je ipak znatno usporilo rast kredita, inozemnog duga pa time kreditnih obveza u odnosu na onaj koji bi bio bez takve politike. To danas otvoreno priznaje i MMF. I drugo, koritenje "administrativnih" instrumenata omoguilo je formiranje likvidnih rezervi na razini ukupnog bankovnog sustava, koje mogu posluiti kao amortizer u sluaju eksternog oka. Hipotetski, bude li to neophodno, HNB moe spustiti stopu obvezne priuve sa 17% na 2%, ukinuti graninu obveznu priuvu te zahtjeve u pogledu minimalno potrebnih deviznih potraivanja. To bi na razini sustava povealo likvidnost za 7.6 mlrd. eura i 30.3 mlrd. kuna. Tome treba dodati i neto devizne priuve sredinje banke od 7.5 mlrd. eura, to je u ukupnosti sasvim dostatna garancija da sustav moe izdrati jednokratni eksterni udar i nastaviti relativno normalno poslovati. Posebno u uvjetima stabilnog teaja. lako za sada nema indicija o potrebi poduzimanja tako radikalnih mjera na irokoj osnovi, ne iskljuuje se mogunost njihovog parcijalnog koritenja radi ublaavanja pojedinih problema. Tako je npr. dravnim proraunom predvieno u ovoj godini izdavanje obveznica na inozemnom tritu u iznosu od 750 mil. eura, to se, s obzirom na iznos, moe pokazati kao rizina operacija imajui na umu nedavna negativna iskustva nekih drugih zemalja. Zato je, a polazei od injenice da e se glavnina tako prikupljenih sredstava koristiti za podmirenja deviznih obveza drave, HNB spremna da za potrebe supstitucije tog inozemnog zaduivanja drave zaduivanjem kod domaih banaka spusti stopu minimalno potrebnih deviznih potraivanja sa sadanjih 32% na 29%. Time bi se izbjeglo i djelomino istiskivanje ostalih sektora sa trita kredita. Iz istog razloga, logino je oekivati da e Vlada s posebnom pozornou upravljati proraunskim deficitom i, u zavisnosti od inflacijom ubrzanog rasta nominalnih prihoda, razmotriti mogunosti njegovog dodatnog smanjenja u 2008. godini. 4. Osim u ovom elementu, cjelina monetarnih kretanja na poetku godine odvija se u skladu s predvianjima. Poveanje pondera za valutno inducirani kreditni rizik i uvjetovanje dostizanja "dozvoljenog" rasta plasmana banaka poveanjem stope adekvatnosti kapitala trai dokapitalizaciju banaka. U funkciji toga, a dijelom i da smanje utjecaj volatilnosti domaih trita na svoju likvidnost, banke su inicijalno primile u prvom tromjeseju 480 mil eura depozita nerezidenata te ukupno poveale svoj inozemni dug za 560 mil. eura. Nadalje, nakon oscilacija vezanih uz javnu ponudu dionica HT-a i promjena u strukturi ukupne tednje, kretanje tednih depozita se stabiliziralo i oni su sredinom travnja za 14,4% vei od prologodinjih u isto vrijeme, a devizni depoziti vei su za 17,6%. Konano, nakon privremene obustave u sijenju, kako bi se u uvjetima poveane inflacije suzbila deprecijacijska oekivanja, HNB je ponovno zapoeo s operacijama na otvorenom tritu na razinama dostatnim da olakaju upravljanje kratkoronom likvidnou banaka. Sve to znatno je poboljalo ukupnu likvidnost sustava i spustilo kamatne stope na novanom tritu. Dok su na samom poetku godine one premaivale 10%, od tada se ponovno kreu na dnevnoj razini ispod 5% (prosjek 3,2 %), na kojoj se formira i repo stopa sredinje banke. Sukladno poskupljenju inozemnih i povezano s time, poveanju kamata na domae izvore sredstava, neto su poveane i kamatne stope na kredite banaka. Meutim, time su se one uglavnom samo vratile na razine s poetka uzlazne faze aktualnog kreditnog ciklusa tijekom koje je politika smanjivanja kamatnih stopa bila izravno u funkciji poticanja potranje za kreditima Konano, nominalni teaj vrsto stagnira u uskom rasponu od 7.25 do 7.28 kuna za euro i uz ograniavanje rasta plasmana banaka predstavlja osnovno sidro i nain antiinflacijskog djelovanja monetarne politike. U takvim uvjetima, a nakon ciljanog usporavanja u drugom dijelu 2007. godine, izazvanog zaotravanjem Odluke o obaveznom upisu blagajnikih zapisa, i zatim dozvoljenog, a dijelom samo fiktivno realiziranog, "skoka" u prosincu, plasmani banaka kreu se u prva etiri mjeseca (stanje 20. travnja) po godinjoj stopi rasta od 12.0%, priblino kao i ukupna ponuda novca (10.8%). Usporedo s time, ukupan inozemni dug poveanje u prvom tromjeseju za 960 mil. eura i za 14% je vei nego u isto vrijeme prole godine ne ukazujui na posebno poveane probleme u sferi eksternog financiranja poduzea. Ocjenjujemo stoga da e se, i bez dodatnog prilagoavanja instrumenata monetarne politike, osnovni parametri monetarnih tokova iz prvog tromjeseja odrati i u cijeloj 2008. godini, kao to je projekcijom bilo predvieno, dok bi, uz supstituciju inozemnog domaim zaduivanjem drave, ukupan inozemni dug mogao u ovoj godini porasti za oko 3 mlrd. eura ili za oko 9%. U ukupnosti to e biti dostatno za financiranje realnog rasta bruto domaeg proizvoda po stopi od oko 4.5%, uz prosjenu stopu inflacije od 5.5 do 6%, ali i uz i dalje visok deficit platne bilance od oko 8.5% bruto domaeg proizvoda. 5. Stave li se ovi parametri u kontekst globalnih kretanja, mogao bi se izvui zakljuak da, unato sporijem rastu proizvodnje i vioj inflaciji od prologodinje, hrvatska ekonomija prolazi kroz sadanje razdoblje globalnih turbulencija uz relativno male rtve. Meutim, to ne moe biti povod samozadovoljstvu, kao to ni injenica da neke druge zemlje imaju iste ili jo i vee probleme ne moe predstavljati utjehu. Naprotiv, sve ovo upuuje na potrebu jo veeg opreza. Visok deficit platne bilance i inozemni dug indikatori su, naime, nae trajne ranjivosti na promjene i poremeaje u globalnim financijskim tokovima. A, koliko god da ti tokovi eksterno determiniraju monetarni ambijent i ponudu novca u Hrvatskoj, o potranji za njime te o nainu i racionalnosti njegovog koritenja ipak prije svega odluuju naa poduzea, domainstva i drava. U okvirima koja postavlja ukupna ekonomska politika i odgovarajua financijska regulativa. Evidentno je da su promjene na tom podruju nune i da ih treba realizirati u relativno kratkom roku. Naime, pribliavanjem ulaska u EU pribliava se i trenutak kada e HNB ukinuti GOP i bitno smanjiti stopu obvezne priuve, dakle relaksirati skup instrumenata koji se u postojeoj situaciji pokazao kao dobra potencijalna zatita od globalnih turbulencija i dijela domaih neracionalnosti. Pri tome sutina problema nee biti u oslobaanju imobilizirane likvidnosti - do nje e doi vrlo postupno, a ne jednokratno - ve u potrebi da sadanju ulogu tih instrumenata reguliranja ponude preuzmu neki drugi instrumenti i neke druge politike reguliranja potranje za novcem. Restriktivnije i selektivnije, a time i rizinije nego dosad. A, ako netko misli da e samim ulaskom u EU ti problemi postati manji, dovoljno je da pogleda s kakvim problemima se danas suoavaju neke nove lanice koje su do nedavno isticane kao ogledni primjer uspjene tranzicije i brzog ekonomskog rasta. Ako iz toga nita ne nauimo, jedino to nam preostaje je da ponovimo neke njihove greke.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary policy
text: Monetary policy Published: 12.11.2004. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Release date of the statement Topic Event Event Event Event Date of events 12.11.2004. Croatia's economic policy in 2005 12th Consultation of the Croatian Society of Economists Opatija 10.11.2004. -12.11.2004. Unlike good politicians, economists in general, and central bankers in particular, have a bad reputation as people prone to vague expression, frequent use of conditional sentences and making pitiful forecasts. All this for reasons to reduce the risk of later disclosure of errors in their assessments and the shortcomings of a complete view of individual issues. Cases of pure politicking in their appearances are not uncommon. An anecdote is well known when Alan Greenspan, president of the FED, addressed the crowd after one appearance, saying, "Gentlemen, if you understand what I just said, then I expressed myself badly." Naravno, A.G. can afford such a joke at his own expense, but there are few people of his caliber in economic politics, and there are certainly none in Croatia. That's why we just can't afford the luxury of throwing around big, fuzzy, phrases behind which there's oftenjust a big fog. There are three such phrases that have recently appeared on our public scene and are offered as a life-saving solution to all problems. These include a fluctuating exchange rate, the placing of foreign exchange reserves in the function of development and, exclusively in thiscote kstu, the central bank's operations on the open market. The first two of them have already been discussed many times and it would no longer be necessary to waste words on them, if the introduction of operations on the open market did not give them new momentum and makes them potentially achievable na consistent way. Therefore, it is not surprising that the announcement of the CNB's decision to start such operations has been met with approval in the circles of those who are otherwise very critical of the current monetary policy. In doing so, it is usually pointed out that open market operations will allow: 1. acquiring the full autonomy of monetary policy from external factors and its management exclusively in accordance with the development preferences of the national economy; 2. full availability of funds for domestic financing of the budget deficit with lower costs and longer loan repayment periods; 3. more efficient management of public debt, which now comes under the authority of the central bank. Thus, it is believed, monetary policy will become a powerful instrument of economic development stimulus, and not just a soulfultramp over price stability without development. Is that possible? Yes, it is possible, viewed ex-chair and with the willingness to pay a high price in advance for a very uncertain result. The construction is quite simple and can be described in all understandable language. The fluctuating exchange rate in the interpretation of some of our economists is only another name for the policy of asymmetric interventions of the central bank in the camelmarket, that is, interventions that sit by prevent appreciation, and on the other hand allow or directly encourage the depreciation of the kuna. When preventing appreciation, the situation is clear. The CNB just continues to do what it has mostly done for the past four years. The CNB offsets the growth in demand for kunas financed by net foreign borrowing by purchases on the foreign exchange market, i.e . in principle nesteri licks with early emissions of primary money. If the supply of foreign currency exceeds the frameworks of potential growth of kuna liquidity within which low inflation can be maintained, the CNB shall use sterilization instruments. No longer marketable, but administrative (35%, allocation of 42% foreign currency COR in KUNA, 24%), because they proved more efficient than the emission of treasury bills that left considerable room for market speculation. When encouraging depreciation, however, the situation is very different. For this, it is necessary thatthe search for foreign exchange continuously exceeds their offer. How to achieve this in conditions of liberalised current and partially Are you beralizing early to ask inad's transactions with foreign countries? One thing's for sure. It is necessary to maintain or even strengthen the mechanism oflimiting the borrowing of banks abroad and thus limit the supply of foreign currency from this source. Then the question of increasing demand remains, where there are several options: (1) The central bank's "solo game", which involves accumulating foreign exchange reserves through permanent purchases in the foreign exchange market aimed solely at achieving the target level of exchange rates, with the sterilization of such a "surplus" kuna liquidity with treasury bills. It should not be particularly proven that this option is meaningless, because it asks for high interestrates for imports of capital that does not perform any positive function in the Croatian economy. Only foreign banks that achieve high returns without any risk can benefit from this. This was the reason for the conflict with the previous IMF mission in 2003. (2) Creation of additional kuna liquidity (e.g. by reducing the reserve requirement rate or the percentage of foreign currency COR allocated in KUNA) in order to increase the demand for foreign currency within the current transactions of the balance of payments, i.e. through increased imports. Of course this option is out of the question either, but also by the fact that the ultimate objective of the entire operation should be to reduce the current account deficit, and not the creation of money in the function of financing imports. It remains (3) the option to realize depreciation through capital transactions in terms of substitution of part of the foreign debt to domestic debt. This means increasing the kuna liquidity of the system by which debtors, by purchasing foreign currency from commercial banks and, indirectly, from the central bank, will repay foreign debts. However, in the enterprise sector, this option assumes that interest rates on kuna loans with a foreign exchange clause are competitive with interest rates at which they can be borrowed directly abroad, which is not the case now, and the question arises of the social justification for reducing the country's foreign exchange reserves in the direct function of servicing private debts. Therefore, the sector of the state remains, and this is where the announced open market operations enter into play. The construction is again very simple.
