In accordance, in terms of height and dynamics, withthe need of foreign exchange financing of the state budget in the sphere of repayment of foreign public debt annuities and current imports, the CNB buys the existing securities of the state on the secondary market with a "tacit" agreement with the banks that those funds from the primary emissions will beeligible for the purchase of new government securities emissions. Thus, part of the public debt will be monetized, and the state will purchase the necessary foreign currency with the resulting kunas. This will lead to a depreciation of the exchange rate, which the CNB can further control by selling some of the necessaryforeign currency directly to the state from foreign exchange reserves. For this part, previously broadcast money will be cancelled out, so the CNB can balance between monetary and exchange rate objectives in its activities. So we achieve controlled exchange rate depreciation, reduce the need for foreign government borrowing and substitute it with indirect borrowing with the central bank, put foreign exchange reserves into the function of development, and active management of state securities that the central bank can hold to maturity involves the CNB in managingpublic debt as well. Exchange rate depreciation has a positive impact on the balance of current transactions of the balance of payments and increases the rate of economic growth. This also increases the tax base, allowing for the fiscal deficit to be gradually reduced without radical cuts to the sphere ofboth budgetary spending and government investment. That's how we solved all the problems. Or maybe we're not after all? The positive impact of exchange rate depreciation on current balance of payments transactions and on economic growth presupposes high elasticity of both exports and imports in relation to the exchange rate and the absence of external shocks of the oil price growth type. Both assumptions are very problematic. Furthermore, in order for depreciation to trigger exports, it must be realistic, i.e. the depreciation rate must be higher than the rate of growth of domestic prices. Given that some of the costs are relatively fixed in the short term and currency-indexed, real depreciation means that the growth of currency non-indexed costs must be significantly lower than the general inflation rate or, somewhat roughly put, that they must be nominally frozen. This means a real decline in these costs, among which the largest items are net salary and pensions. This is clearly not a popular topic for politicians and about it proponents of the "fluctuating exchange rate" policy are persistently silent, but it can be accepted if we are sure that ultimately the resultof the tanta of gains and costs will be positive. Are we sure, however, that will be the case? Let's look at things statically assuming an initial nominal depreciation of the exchange rate of the kuna against the euro by 10%. In addition to the unchanged all other conditions, this would mean that thegrains of goods and services for the existing level of exports in 2004 would receive a total of about HRK 10.8 billion more, while the owners of foreign currency deposits with the balance of 30 September would be nominally richer by about HRK 8.1 billion. At the same time, for existing imports they would have to pay HRK 12.1bn more, the domestic debt of the company, population and the state to banks would be higher by HRK 13.5bn due to the currency clause, while the kuna equivalent of the foreign debt of the state and the company would be increased by HRK 11.2 billion. This is, of course, a metodologically not very fair addition of flows and stocks, but it is indicative that their sum is deeply negative and amounts to about HRK 17.9bn or 9% of GDP. In a dynamic approach, this effect could be halved with the very optimistic assumption that a 10%nominal depreciation of the exchange rate could increase exports of goods and services by about 5% in real terms and also reduce real imports, but in this approach should be included in the account and the impact of depreciation on domestic prices and on interest rates, which brings us back to the initial figures. This is only the first iteration, and with each subsequent one, net costs increase in absolute but also in relative terms. A spiral of interdependence between costs, prices and exchange rates opens up, which we know from our own past where it leads. Not only in highinflation but also in recession. All this is just another illustration of what, in conditions of high euroization, the fundamental incorporation of the exchange rate into the financial system and all the pores of the Croatian economy is. It determines not only foreign trade directly, but also the purchaseof not economic flows, and thus on its stability depends substantially on the overall stability of the national economy. This does not mean that the exchange rate is fixed or that the CNB allows its fluctuations only in a narrow range that is independent of market funds. On the contrary, the CNB nand will never "maintain" some level of exchange rate that does not correspond to market funds, but will seek to initiate the formation of exchange rates at a level that has no basis in the market through monetary stunts. This is not a question of courage, but a healthyr azum and a sense of responsibility for the economic destiny of the country. Therefore, the CNB will not enter into such experiments. Observed in this context, the introduction of operations on the open market, as the most flexible instrument of liquidity management, plays a completely different role than previously hypothetically described. Their primary function is to mitigate the basic negative phenomenon that accompanies the maintenance of a stable exchange rate in the quasi-currency board system, which are high fluctuations in interest rates in the money market. In recentdays, they have fluctuated to overnight loans ranging between 1% and 11%, which directly prevents the formation of benchmark interest rates on short- and long-term sources of funds, without which there is no development and deepening of financial markets. In order to stabilize these rates, the CNB will start inverse repo deals, with weekly auctions in which the treasury bills of the Ministry of Finance in KUNA without a currency clause will initially serve as collateral. Later, the deals can also be extended to kuna papers alongtheir maturities. At the same time, the CNB will also make appropriate changes to the lombard loan system, and the possibility of introducing intraday loans and depositing funds with the CNB at the end of the working day (the so-called deposit facility) is being considered. In addition, and in a functionof further deepening financial markets, it will carry out with further liberalisation of capital transactions with foreign countries, in terms of lifting restrictions on non-residents' investment in domestic securities in capital and money markets. Of course, already by their very nature, open market operations will also have a positive impact on the possibility of higher and more favourable government borrowing on the domestic market and thus partial substitution of external financing of the current budget deficit by financing from domestic sourcesa. But only to the extent that, in the context of the overall growth of monetary aggregates, will not destabilize the exchange rate, accelerate inflation and lead to the displacement of other sectors from the credit market. Therefore, the indirect monetization of part of the fiscal deficit through operations in theploughed market does not diminish the urgent need to significantly reduce this deficit. On the contrary, the smaller the deficit will be, the wider the scope for open market operations will also expand. If this were not the case, the CNB would have started these operations as early as 2004. Finally,a certain amount of government securities in the CNB portfolio will gradually accumulate, which will begin to actively manage it. But in doing so, it must not be forgotten that open market operations are an instrument of monetary policy, not public finances, so that the management of state securities in the central bank's portfolio will also be solely motivated by reasons of monetary character. That is why this in no way substitutes the scope and responsibility of the Ministry of Finance forthe settlement of public debt as a whole. Anything else would represent a clear conflict of interest. So, let me conclude. Monetary policy in 2005 should be somewhat sofas earlier in the methods of implementation, but no less firm in the fundamental commitments and goalsthan they stand in 2004. Of course, for all those who believe that the growth of goods exports by 18% and real GDP by 4%, with inflation of 2%, the disastrous performance of economic developments during 2004, for them monetary policy will continue to remain forleprosy. But that's their problem.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna politika Objavljeno: 12.11.2004. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Tema Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 12.11.2004. Ekonomska politika Hrvatske u 2005. 12. savjetovanje Hrvatskog drutva ekonomista Opatija 10.11.2004. -12.11.2004. Za razliku od dobrih politiara, ekonomisti openito, a centralni bankari posebno, na loem su glasu kao ljudi skloni nejasnom izraavanju, estoj upotrebi kondicionalnih reenica i davanju pitijskih prognoza. Sve to iz razloga da smanje rizik kasnijeg razotkrivanja pogreaka u njihovim procjenama i nedostataka cjelovitog sagledavanja pojedinih pitanja. Nisu rijetki niti sluajevi istog politikantstva u njihovim istupima. Poznata je anegdota kada se Alan Greenspan, predsjednik FED-a, nakon jednog istupa obratio okupljenim novinarima rijeima: "Gospodo, ako ste shvatili to sam upravo rekao, tada sam se loe izrazio". Naravno, A.G. si moe priutiti takvu alu na vlastiti raun, ali je u ekonomskoj politici malo ljudi njegovog kalibra, a sigurno ih nema u Hrvatskoj. Zato si mi jednostavno ne moemo dopustiti luksuz razbacivanja velikim, nejasnim, frazama iza kojih esto stoji samo velika magla. Tri su takve fraze koje se u posljednje vrijeme javljaju na naoj javnoj sceni i koje se nude kao spasonosno rjeenje za sve probleme. To su fluktuirajui teaj, stavljanje deviznih rezervi u funkciju razvoja i, iskljuivo u tom kontekstu, operacije sredinje banke na otvorenom tritu. Prve dvije od njih ve su mnogo puta raspravljane i ne bi bilo vie potrebno na njih troiti rijei, da im uvoenje operacija na otvorenom tritu ne daje novi zamah i ini ih potencijalno ostvarivima na konzistentan nain. Zato ne udi to je najava odluke HNB-a da zapone s takvim operacijama naila na odobravanje i u krugovima onih koji su inae vrlo kritiki nastrojeni prema aktualnoj monetarnoj politici. Pri tome se obino istie da e operacije na otvorenom tritu omoguiti: 1. stjecanje pune autonomije monetarne politike od eksternih faktora i njeno voenje iskljuivo sukladno razvojnim preferencijama nacionalne ekonomije; 2. punu raspoloivost sredstava za domae financiranje proraunskog deficita uz nie trokove i due rokove otplate kredita; 3. efikasnije upravljanje javnim dugom koje sada dolazi pod ingerenciju sredinje banke. Tako e, smatra se, monetarna politika postati snaan instrument poticaja gospodarskog razvoja, a ne samo duebrinik nad stabilnou cijena bez razvoja. tovie, to e omoguiti i konano naputanje pogubne politike fiksnog i nerealnog teaja, to god pod time mislili. Da li je to mogue? Da, mogue je, gledano ex katedra i uz spremnost da se unaprijed plati visoka cijena za vrlo neizvjestan rezultat. Konstrukcija je vrlo jednostavna i moe se opisati svima razumljivim jezikom. Fluktuirajui teaj u interpretaciji nekih naih ekonomista samo je drugi naziv za politiku asimetrinih intervencija sredinje banke na deviznom tritu, odnosno intervencija koje sjedne strane sprjeavaju aprecijaciju, a s druge doputaju ili izravno potiu deprecijaciju kune. Kod sprjeavanja aprecijacije, situacija je jasna. HNB samo nastavlja raditi ono to je uglavnom i radio u posljednje etiri godine. Rast potranje za kunama financiran neto inozemnim zaduivanjem HNB neutralizira kupovinama na deviznom tritu, odnosno u naelu nesteri lizi ranom emisijom primarnog novca. Ako ponuda deviza premauje okvire potencijalnog rasta kunske likvidnosti unutar kojih se moe odravati niska inflacija, HNB koristi instrumente sterilizacije. Ne vie trine, ve administrativne (35%, izdvajanje 42% devizne OR u kunama, 24%), jer su se oni pokazali efikasnijim od emisije blagajnikih zapisa koja je ostavljala znatan prostor za trine spekulacije. Kod poticanja deprecijacije situacija je, meutim, bitno drugaija. Za to je potrebno da potranja za devizama kontinuirano premauje njihovu ponudu. Kako to postii u uvjetima liberaliziranih tekuih i djelomino li beralizi ranih ka pita Inih transakcija s inozemstvom? Jedno je sigurno. Potrebno je zadrati ili ak i osnaiti mehanizam ograniavanja zaduivanja banaka u inozemstvu i na taj nain limitirati ponudu deviza iz tog izvora. Tada ostaje pitanje poveanja potranje, gdje postoji nekoliko opcija: (1) "Solo igra" sredinje banke, koja podrazumijeva akumuliranje deviznih rezervi permanentnim kupovinama na deviznom tritu usmjerenim iskljuivo ka postizanju ciljane razine teaja, uz sterilizaciju tako produciranog "vika" kunske likvidnosti blagajnikim zapisima. Ne treba naroito dokazivati da je ta opcija besmislena, jer trai visoke kamatne stope za uvoz kapitala koji ne obavlja nikakvu pozitivnu funkciju u hrvatskoj ekonomiji. Koristi od toga mogu imati samo inozemne banke koje ostvaruju visoke prinose bez ikakvog rizika. To je i bio razlog sukoba s prethodnom misijom MMF-a tijekom 2003. godine. (2) Kreiranje dodatne kunske likvidnosti (npr. smanjenjem stope obvezne rezerve ili postotka devizne OR koji se izdvaja u kunama) kako bi se poveala potranja za devizama u okviru tekuih transakcija platne bilance, odnosno kroz poveani uvoz. Naravno da niti ta opcija ne dolazi u obzir, ve i samim time to bi konani cilj cijele operacije trebalo biti smanjenje deficita tekuih transakcija, a ne kreiranje novca u funkciji financiranja uvoza. Ostaje (3) opcija da se deprecijacija realizira kroz kapitalne transakcije u smislu supstitucije dijela inozemnog duga domaim dugom. To znai da se povea kunska likvidnost sustava kojom e dunici, kupnjom deviza od poslovnih banaka i, indirektno, od sredinje banke, otplaivati inozemne dugove. Meutim, u sektoru poduzea ta opcija pretpostavlja da kamatne stope na kunske kredite s deviznom klauzulom budu konkurentne kamatnim stopama po kojima se ona mogu izravno zaduiti u inozemstvu, to sada nije sluaj, a postavlja se i pitanje drutvene opravdanosti smanjivanja deviznih rezervi zemlje u izravnoj funkciji servisiranja privatnih dugova. Preostaje, dakle, sektor drave i tu ulaze u igru najavljene operacije na otvorenom tritu. Konstrukcija je opet vrlo jednostavna. Usklaeno, po visini i dinamici, s potrebama deviznog financiranja dravnog prorauna u sferi otplate anuiteta inozemnog javnog duga i tekueg uvoza, HNB kupuje postojee vrijednosne papire drave na sekundarnom tritu uz "preutni" sporazum s bankama da e one sredstva iz primarne emisije koristiti za kupovinu nove emisije dravnih vrijednosnih papira. Tako e se dio javnog duga monetizirati, a drava e dobivenim kunama kupovati potrebne devize. To e dovesti do deprecijacije teaja koju HNB moe dodatno kontrolirati na nain da dio potrebnih deviza izravno proda dravi iz deviznih rezervi. Za taj e se dio ponititi prethodno emitirani novac, pa HNB moe u svom djelovanju balansirati izmeu monetarnih i teajnih ciljeva. Znai postiemo kontroliranu deprecijaciju teaja, smanjujemo potrebu inozemnog zaduivanja drave i supstituiramo ga indirektnim zaduivanjem kod sredinje banke, devizne rezerve stavljamo u funkciju razvoja, a aktivno upravljanje vrijednosnim papirima drave koje sredinja banka moe drati do dospijea ukljuuje HNB i u upravljanje javnim dugom. Deprecijacija teaja pozitivno utjee na saldo tekuih transakcija platne bilance i poveava stopu gospodarskog rasta. To poveava i poreznu osnovicu, omoguujui postupno smanjivanje fiskalnog deficita bez radikalnih rezova u sferi budetske potronje i dravnih investicija. Tako smo rijeili sve probleme. Ili moda ipak nismo? Pozitivni utjecaj deprecijacije teaja na tekue transakcije platne bilance i na gospodarski rast pretpostavlja visoku elastinost i izvoza i uvoza u odnosu na teaj te odsustvo eksternih okova tipa rast cijena nafte. Obje pretpostavke su vrlo problematine. Nadalje, da bi deprecijacija mogla potaknuti izvoz, ona mora biti realna tj. stopa deprecijacije mora biti via od stope rasta domaih cijena. S obzirom da je dio trokova relativno fiksan u kratkom roku i valutno indeksiran, realna deprecijacija znai da rast valutno neindeksiranih trokova mora biti znatno nii od ope stope inflacije ili, neto grublje reeno, da oni moraju biti nominalno zamrznuti. To znai realni pad tih trokova, meu kojima su najvee stavke neto plae i penzije. To oito nije popularna tema za politiare i o njoj zagovornici politike "fluktuirajueg teaja" uporno ute, ali se moe prihvatiti ako smo sigurni da e u konanici rezultanta dobitaka i trokova biti pozitivna. Jesmo li, meutim, sigurni da e biti tako? Pogledajmo stvari statiki uz pretpostavku inicijalne nominalne deprecijacije teaja kune prema euru za 10%. Uz nepromijenjene sve ostale uvjete, to bi znailo da bi izvoznici roba i usluga za postojeu razinu izvoza u 2004. godini ukupno primili oko 10.8 mlrd. kuna vie, dok bi vlasnici deviznih depozita sa stanjem 30. rujna bili nominalno bogatiji za oko 8.1 mlrd. kuna. Istodobno, za postojei uvoz morali bi platiti 12.1 mlrd. kuna vie, domai dug poduzea, stanovnitva i drave prema bankama bio bi, zbog valutne klauzule, vei za 13.5 mlrd. kuna, dok bi kunska protuvrijednost inozemnog duga drave i poduzea bila poveana za 11.2 mlrd. kuna. Ovdje se naravno radi o metodoloki ne ba korektnom zbrajanju tokova i stokova, ali je indikativno da je njihov zbroj duboko negativan i iznosi oko 17.9 mlrd. kuna ili 9% BDP-a. U dinamikom pristupu, taj bi se efekt mogao prepoloviti uz vrlo optimistiku pretpostavku da bi 10-postotna nominalna deprecijacija teaja mogla realno poveati izvoz roba i usluga za oko 5% i jednako tako smanjiti realni uvoz, ali u tom pristupu treba ukljuiti u raun i utjecaj deprecijacije na rast domaih cijena i na kamatne stope, to nas opet vraa na poetne brojke. To je samo prva iteracija, a sa svakom slijedeom poveavaju se neto trokovi u apsolutnom ali i u relativnom izrazu. Otvara se spirala meuzavisnosti trokova, cijena i teaja, za koju iz vlastite prolosti znamo kamo vodi. Ne samo u visoku inflaciju nego i u recesiju. Sve to samo je jo jedna ilustracija kolika je, u uvjetima visoke eurizacije, fundamentalna inkorporiranost teaja u financijski sustav i sve pore hrvatske ekonomije. On ne determinira izravno samo vanjskotrgovinske, ve ukupne ekonomske tokove i time o njegovoj stabilnosti bitno zavisi i ukupna stabilnost nacionalne ekonomije. To ne znai da je teaj fiksan ili da HNB dozvoljava njegove fluktuacije samo u uskom rasponu koji je neovisan od trinih fundamenata. Naprotiv, HNB nije i nee nikada "odravati" neku razinu teaja koja ne odgovara trinim fundamentima, ali e jo manje monetarnim akrobacijama nastojati inicirati formiranje teaja na razini koja nema osnovu u tritu. Tu se ne radi o pitanju hrabrosti, ve o zdravom razumu i osjeaju odgovornosti za ekonomsku sudbinu zemlje. Zato, u takve eksperimente HNB nee ulaziti. Promatrano u tom kontekstu, uvoenje operacija na otvorenom tritu, kao najfleksibilnijeg instrumenta upravljanja likvidnou, ima sasvim drugu ulogu od ranije hipotetski opisane. Njihova je prvenstvena funkcija da ublae osnovnu negativnu pojavu koja prati odravanje stabilnog teaja u sustavu kvazi valutnog odbora, a to su visoke fluktuacije kamatnih stopa na tritu novca. One u posljednjih godinu dana osciliraju na prekonone kredite u rasponu izmeu 1% i 11%, to izravno onemoguava formiranje referentnih kamatnih stopa na kratkorone i dugorone izvore sredstava, bez kojih nema razvoja i produbljivanja financijskih trita. Radi stabilizacije tih stopa, HNB e zapoeti s inverznim repo poslovima, uz tjedne aukcije u kojima e kao kolateral u poetku sluiti iskljuivo trezorski zapisi Ministarstva financija u kunama bez valutne klauzule. Kasnije se poslovi mogu proiriti i na kunske papire duih rokova dospijea. Istodobno, HNB e izvriti i odgovarajue promjene u sustavu lombardnih kredita, a razmatra se i mogunost uvoenja unutardnevnih kredita te deponiranja sredstava kod HNB krajem radnog dana (tzv. deposit facility). Pored toga, a u funkciji dodatnog produbljivanja financijskih trita, izvrit e sa daljnja liberalizacija kapitalnih transakcija s inozemstvom, u smislu ukidanja ogranienja ulaganja nerezidenata u domae vrijednosne papire na tritima kapitala i novca. Naravno da e, ve po svojoj prirodi, operacije na otvorenom tritu pozitivno utjecati i na mogunost veeg i povoljnijeg zaduivanja drave na domaem tritu i time djelomine supstitucije eksternog financiranja tekueg proraunskog deficita financiranjem iz domaih izvora. Ali samo u mjeri koja u kontekstu ukupnog rasta monetarnih agregata nee destabilizirati teaj, ubrzati inflaciju i dovesti do istiskivanja ostalih sektora sa trita kredita. Zato, indirektna monetizacija dijela fiskalnog deficita kroz operacije na otvorenom tritu ne umanjuje prijeku potrebu znaajnog smanjivanja tog deficita. Naprotiv, to e deficit biti manji, to e se iriti i prostor za operacije na otvorenom tritu. Da nije tako, HNB bi zapoeo s tim operacijama ve u 2004. godini. Konano, razvojem tih operacija postupno e se akumulirati i odreeni iznos dravnih vrijednosnih papira u portfelju HNB, koji e poeti njime aktivno upravljati. Ali, pri tome se ne smije zaboraviti da su operacije na otvorenom tritu instrument monetarne politike, a ne javnih financija, tako da e i upravljanje vrijednosnim papirima drave u portfelju sredinje banke biti iskljuivo motivirano razlozima monetarnog karaktera. Zato to ni na koji nain ne supstituira djelokrug i odgovornost Ministarstva financija za upravljanje javnim dugom u cjelini. Sve ostalo predstavljalo bi isti sukob interesa. Dakle, da zakljuim. Monetarna politika u 2005. godini trebala bi biti neto sofi stici ranija u metodama provoenja, ali ne manje vrsta u temeljnim opredjeljenjima i ciljevima nego stoje bila u 2004. godini. Naravno, za sve one koji smatraju da su rast robnog izvoza za 18% i realnog BDP-a za 4%, uz inflaciju od 2%, pogubne performance ekonomskih kretanja tijekom 2004. godine, za njih e monetarna politika i dalje ostati pogubna. Ali to je njihov problem.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Economic crisis and monetary policy
text: Economic crisis and monetary policy Published: 15.5.2009. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 14.5.2009. 12th Scientific and Professional Conference Croatian Money Market Opatija 14.5.2009. 1. A year ago, the economy grew at a rate of 4.3%, and various rallies talked about the need for even faster growth. About new investments, newjobs, bigger incentives, booming popular shareholding, housing as a locomotive of growth, strengthening the welfare state... Today, the economy is falling by 5% and there is talk about how to mitigate the effects of the transfer of the global crisis to our territories, and then return to the previous upward trajectory as soon as possible on the wave of general economic recovery. Both approaches are wrong. A year ago, the eclatative dangers of the previous type of economic growth were still underestimated, now the desire is to reestablish a pattern that only raised the effects of transmitting the world crisis to the situation and tendencies in the Croatian economy. It's like we didn't get a lesson and it's like we can't learn anything from it. And is that economic growth cannot in the long run be based on the expansion of domesticnecessity, which permanently generates fundamental external and internal imbalances and thus increases general indebtedness. Its growth also increased the risk that potential problems in capital inflows, rising prices or problems in export demand would break the entire growth pattern and turn it into its opposite. That's exactly what happened. Hence, the exit from the current situation cannot in principle be based on the further spread of imbalances, but on their substantial reduction. Even if there are no long-termatrocities in their further financing, especially when these restrictions are very pronounced in the short term. For this, in general, it is necessary to pursue an "anticyclical" economic policy with a "healthy core" and built-in shock absorbers. Sincewe have never had such an integral policy before, we have come to a situation where we have to reduce deficits in times of recession, which can deepen it even further. How did we get into the current situation? 2. Perceptions of the crisis widely expanded in October 2008, primarily related to the stock market crash,after which a broader-scale financial collapse was expected. This did not happen, because the monetary system reacted quickly and efficiently, precisely on the principles of anticyclicity. At that point, it was crucial to prevent savers from losing confidence in the banking system andto maintain the credibility of monetary policy. Without it, the "classic circle" of the financial crisis, which last year's "Nobel laureate" Paul Krugman portrays as the interdependence of three elements: the loss of confidence - the collapse of the exchange rate, the rise of interest rates, the sharp fall in demand - financial problems for businesses, banks and the population, which in turn result in a further loss of confidence, easily all these elements were, and partly still present, the intensity of their manifestations to be maintained within frameworks that are not trigger a chain reaction. To do this: With the abolition of the marginal reserve requirement (450m euros), the CNB has been able to provide a total of 100m euros. euro) and reducing the reserve requirement (1115m euros). euro) released 1,555m euros to banks. euro of immobilised liquidity. In addition, by reducing the minimum foreign exchangelending (28.5% to 20%), it allowed banks to activate their reserves of 2,084m euros. Euros. Other measures have been taken: open position, swap, foreign exchange interventions (net 200m euros). euro). At the same time, banks increased their foreign debt in the fourth threemonths by 2,131m euros. euro, of which a short-term debt of 1898m euros. Euros. Thus, the total net liquidity input by the CNB and foreign banks (45011152131200) was 3,896 million. euro, which corresponds to the value of about 8% of GDP. A third of these funds are directly or indirectly placed to the state to settle domestic obligations and pay off foreign debt, while the rest is aimed at maintaining liquidity in banks' dealings with other sectors. 3. After that, the situation in the monetary sphere begins to gradually consolidate, but with significantly altered structural and dynamic characteristics. 3.1. Foreign debt The risk of partial withdrawal of foreign capital from the country was assessed as the greatest potential danger of directly transferring the global financial crisis to Croatia . By reducing bank deposits and investments in funds, withdrawing profits or not re-financing the foreign liabilities due to the enterprise and the state. So far this has not happened, at least not to a significant extent. Thus, the gross foreign debt at the end of March of this godune amounted to 39.1 billion euros, the same as it was at the end of 2008. In doing so, the company's debt and direct investments increased by about 620m euros, while in the same amount the central government net paid off the overdue principal of its debt, with the announcement of a refinancingof its further liabilities by borrowing on the foreign market. In the current situation, when one does not count on an arrangement with the IMF or some other form of foreign financial support, this undoubtedly represents a positive phenomenon, but also an indication of the radical prekida of the tendencies so far in the inflow of foreign capital through credit channels. In 2008 alone, this influx amounted to EUR 6.4 billion. euro, representing the main source of financing for the growth of domestic consumption and investments. 3.2. Domestic savings After a sharp dropin the savings of its population in banks during October 2008 by about HRK 3.5 billion, it returned in real terms to the previous level by the end of the first quarter of 2009 and is now 10.7% higher than a year ago. This also determines the annual growth of total savings of 7.1%. Medutim: (a) dynamics: The growth of domestic savings in banks is now almost half as slow as the average in previous years (13.5%) and is influenced by the substitution of alternative forms of savings, so the aggregate value of domestic financial assets is significantly reduced (7%). (b) currency structure: The increased perception of currency risk resulted in an increase in the share of foreign currency savings in the structure of total savings, from 66.3% in April 2008 to 72.7% today. This also increases the general degree of euroisation of the Croatian economy, where the share of camelfunds in the structure of total liquid assets has increased from 49.6% to 56.6%. (c) sectoral structure: Unlike household savings, the savings of the enterprise sector have decreased by 6.0% in the last year, which has also reduced its share of thepne savings structure from 19.7% to 17.3%. This indicates a significant deterioration in the financial potential of the sector, which is only a reflection of the reduced liquidity in the sphere of their current business, where the amount of deposit money is reduced by 18.5%, also causing a12.0% decrease in cash mass. 3.3. All this speaks of the pronounced limitations in the growth of credit potential from domestic sources, and related to the stagnation of foreign debt and the stock market situation, and the limitations in the formation of the overall financial potential of the country. The reserves of immobilized liquidity that still exist in this regard with the CNB have already been significantly reduced in the last year (from HRK 51 billion to HRK 41bn), so that the reserve requirement of banks in foreign currency at the end of April is only 628m euros more. euro (towards EUR 2408m). eclock as it was in April last year). Therefore, any further reduction of the reserve requirement rate could hypothetically be only in the function of domestic payments, while the conversion of kunas thus exempted into foreign currency would assume a significant decrease in the central bank's net foreign exchange reserves, with a negative impact on the perception of domestic depositors and foreign creditors. Therefore, such a move would have justification only in the case of credit crunch in foreign markets and a direct threat to the country's external liquidity. 3.4. Plasmans After the liquidity injection by foreign banks and the CNB, the total placements of banks maintained an annual growth dynamic of 14.0% at which they grew on average during the previous five years, but were: (a) Structure: Within total loans, net chalkto the state has grown by as much as 94.6% in the past year, increasing their share of the structure of total bank loans from 6.5% in April last year to 11.1% in April this year. At the same time, loans to other sectors are growing at an annual rate of 8.4% and significancebut are slowing down from previous years (15% in 2007; 10.5% in 2008). This also increases the gap between the effective growth of loans to these sectors and the "permissible", i.e. by the CNB of unpenalized growth. Namely, in relation to the base situation at the end of 2007. Today, these loans are up by 11.1%, while the "limit" is 16% or about HRK 10.2bn more. This is partly the result of a slowdown in demand for loans (due to an increase in interest rates and uncertainty), but also points to the pronounced emergence of the displacement of other sectors from the loan market by the state. (b) Currency aspect: The increase in foreign sources of funds and shares of foreign currency savings shortened the foreign exchange position of banks, whose net foreign liabilities increased from 803.9 billion to 805.3 billion (at the same time, the net foreign assetsof mon etar institutions decreased from 806.1 billion to 803.6 billion). This also increased currency risk for them, so some banks stopped granting pure kuna loans, shifting this risk to the beneficiaries of new loans. Coupled with the increased degree of euroisation, this further underlines the importance of maintaining a stable exchange rate. 3.5. Exchange rate After returning to the initial level of HRK 7.32 per euro at the end of 2008, in the first quarter of this year the exchange rate was depreciated by 2% under the influence of increased foreign exchange demand, but then the weakerof its depreciation expectations and the announcement of foreign borrowing by the state returned it to the framework of relatively high stability. In order to curb depreciation expectations, the CNB intervened directly in the foreign exchange market during this period in the gross amount of about 500m euros. euro, but also by relaxing prudential measures, it has expanded the room for manoeuvre for banks to increase their foreign exchange supply and thus engage themselves in defending exchange rate stability. The "impetus" for this behaviour of banks was a change in the currency structureof allocations on blink reserves and a policy of limited injections of kuna liquidity through open market operations, which occasionally resulted in very high interest rates on overnight loans on the money market. The stabilization of the exchange rate also reduced the pressures of na and these rates, and they are consistently lower than the lombard rate of the CNB and on average amount to 6.5%. 3.6. Interest rates The relaxation of monetary policy measures also reduced unit "regulation costs" for banks by approximately 20%. Thus, for example, to cover these costs at a passive interest rate on a foreign currency deposit of 5% and with an exchange rate risk of 2%, banks should have achieved an average interest rate on placements of 10.2% before, while now this rate has been lowered to 8.1%. The fact that, nevertheless, active interest ratesof ban ka have increased interest rates have increased in the price of foreign borrowing (country risk), an increase in interest rates on domestic deposits due to the strengthening of competition between banks in conditions of slow growth of deposits, and in the deterioration of the quality of placements, i.e. a decreased payability of loans, in particular those granted to the population. 4. Thus, as a whole, the monetary sector has endured the first brunt of the financial crisis and is gradually consolidating. However, it no longer has the capacity to support the current dynamics of aggregate demand growth, nor are the banks themselves willing to pursue an expansionary loan supply policy indiscriminately. In contrast, the real sector is still falling, but this is not solely due to the current financial crisis, but is the result of the gradual cumulation of several factors and begins back in early 2008. Thus, since March of last year, industrial production has been decreasing at an average trend rate of 0.7% per month, while GDP has practically stagnated throughout the whole of last year at the seasonally adjusted level from the last sluggishsturgeon in 2007. Causes: (1) The acceleration of the average annual inflation rate from 2.9% to 6.1%, which in 2008 offset the bulk of nominal current income growth, easily in the second part of 2008 there was an aggregate decrease in consumer prices by about 1% compared to their level from the month of July, the ongoing growth of these prices in the first quarter of this year of 2.1% is an indicator of the possible continuation of negative effects of inflation on disposable incomes and real demand on the domestic market. (2) The decline in the value of the financial assets of the population invested in securities and non-bank institutions due to the blowing of the bubble in the stock and real estate markets. In 2008, it amounted to about 47 billion euros. kuna (for 37.1%) of whichin the fourth quarter about HRK 16 billion, which completely offset the growth of these assets during the previous year. Together with the real stagnation of labour income, such a loss of capital income and liquidity led to a decline in personal consumption and a significant slowdown in investments. (3) Strengthening illiquidity due to the inelasticity of part of current expenditure in conditions of reduced revenues and high credit obligations. And while in this the sectors of the population and businesses had some room for manoeuvre through the reduction of their savings, the sector of the statebehaved very rigidly. Thus, the deficit of the consolidated general government (including HAC and HBOR) increased from EUR 5.6 billion to EUR 5.6 billion. kuna in 2007 to EUR 8.6 billion. kuna in 2008, or from 1.8% to 2.5% of GDP, with this entire deficit concentrated in the last quarter, meaning at the time of the biggest earthquakes in financial markets. Similar developments continued in the first quarter of this year when the central government net borrowed on the domestic market for a further EUR 10.5 billion. of which the net repaid foreign dd ug of HRK 3.3bn, while HRK 7.2bn was used for payments in the country. Of course, liquidity on the domestic market was not sufficient during this period to finance so many needs of the state, and only by informally "conditional" relaxation of monetary policy was itpossible to prevent the occurrence of insolvency of the state in settling its obligations - especially towards abroad. This, however, significantly reduced the possibility of directing these previously immobilised funds directly towards the company sector and maintaining theire liquidity. (4) "Animal spirits", with the so-called multiplizer (non)trusts, i.e. general euphoria in the upward and general panic phase of the cycle, for which economic entities do not behave rationally. An indicator of the current situation in this sphere is also the consumer confidence index, which decreased by over 25 points during 2008 and in the first quarter of 2009 and is at its lowest level since mid-1999. (5) These predominantly domestic factors were followed only at the end of 2008 by a key external shock - a drop in export demand, the negative action of which is raised by the very limited possibility of substitution of export demand by domestic as well as insufficient ability to substitut import demand to domestic supply. It has significantly exacerbated the problem of a key structural mismatchbetween the Croatian economy, which is a deficit in the exchange of goods of 23% of GDP. Care, at such a level, will not be able to cover the very sensitive services and transfer sector for a long time. 5. Thus, unlike the monetary sector, which is consolidating, the real sector is only facing the most difficult problems. Their main cause is a decline in aggregate demand and increased illiquidity, and none of these problems are primarily initiated by monetary factors, nor is it due only to external causes. However, in addressing these problems, the real sector now faces pronounced monetary and financial constraints, which it has significantly caused itself. In doing so, the key is the foreign exchange constraint, which arises from the disproport between the available supply and the current operations generated bythe search for foreign currency and which cannot be rationally covered by any monetary "stunts", but requires an appropriate adjustment to the real sector itself. Conscious or spontaneous. The size of this adjustment is approximately determined by three externally defined assumptions, which are consistent with effective developments in the previous part of 2009. These are: 1. Contraction of export demand, at the current exchange rate about 10%; 2. A drop in foreign direct investment by about 50%; 3. Refinancing of maturing foreign liabilities, with relative stagnationof the debt. In addition to the external constraints assessed in this way, there is a need to reduce the current account deficit of the balance of payments from EUR 4.5 billion. euro in 2008 to "only" EUR 2.8 billion. euro this year (from 9.4% to an estimated 6% of GDP). This presupposesa reduction of about 16% in UV oz, to which the overall policy of regulating domestic demand should be subordinated, and fiscal policy has a special responsibility in this. In these frameworks, monetary policy will support the liquidity of the system only up to a level that will notaffect the exchange rate and through it adversely affect the overall financial system, as has recently happened in some central and eastern European countries. Based on this, it is estimated that bank placements to businesses and households will slow their growth this year to about 8%, approximately like domestic savings, while total liquid assets will increase by about 4%. Under them, however, the cash mass will be reduced by about 9%. If the accuracy of the initial assumptions ofavki is confirmed in practice, in 2009 one can expect a real decrease in domestic aggregate consumption by 5-6%, and a decrease in GDP by about 4%. Whether this decline can be smaller will depend primarily on the development of opportunities in the world, where more favourable developments than now envisaged canto some extent ease external restrictions on the Croatian economy in both the financial and real sectors. However, the same core issue remains. How do you view this crisis? If we see it only as a "temporary stalemate" in the long-term positive tendenciesof economic growth and development, we will solve nothing. In contrast, it should first and foremost be taken as a drastic reminder of the consequences that may arise, and already have, due to the previous disregard for the sustainability problem of economic growth. A warning that would have been even more difficult if the HNB had pursued a different monetary policy in recent years. If we understand that warning, then this crisis is also a chance for a different beginning of thinking about future economic development. Do we have all that strength, knowledge and will - a questionwe won't have to wait long for an answer to?
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Ekonomska kriza i monetarna politika Objavljeno: 15.5.2009. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 14.5.2009. 12. znanstveno-struna konferencija Hrvatsko novano trite Opatija 14.5.2009. 1. Prije godinu dana gospodarstvo je raslo po stopi od 4.3%, a na raznim se skupovima govorilo o potrebi jo breg rasta. O novim investicijama, novim radnim mjestima, veim poticajima, procvatu narodnog dioniarstva, stanogradnji kao lokomotivi rasta, jaanju socijalne drave... Danas gospodarstvo pada 5% i govori se o tome kako ublaiti efekte prenoenja globalne krize na nae prostore, a zatim se na valu opeg ekonomskog oporavka to prije vratiti na prijanju uzlaznu putanju. Oba pristupa su pogrena. Prije godinu dana jo su bile podcijenjene eklatantne opasnosti dotadanjeg tipa gospodarskog rasta, sada se prieljkuje ponovno uspostavljanje obrasca koji je samo potencirao efekte prenoenja svjetske krize na stanje i tendencije u hrvatskoj ekonomiji. Kao da nismo dobili lekciju i kao da iz nje ne moemo nita nauiti. A to je da ekonomski rast ne moe dugorono biti temeljen na ekspanziji domae potranje koja permanentno generira fundamentalne vanjske i unutarnje neravnotee i time poveava opu zaduenost. Njenim rastom poveavao se, naime, i rizik da potencijalni problemi u priljevu kapitala, porastu njegove cijene ili problemi u izvoznoj potranji srue cijeli obrazac rasta i pretvore ga u njegovu suprotnost. To se upravo i dogodilo. Otuda, izlazak iz sadanje situacije naelno se ne moe bazirati na dodatnom irenju neravnotea, ve na njihovom bitnom smanjivanju. ak i da ne postoje dugorona ogranienja u njihovom daljnjem financiranju, a pogotovo kad su ta ogranienja kratkorono vrlo izraena. Za to je, openito, potrebno voditi "anticiklinu" ekonomsku politiku sa "zdravom jezgrom" i ugraenim amortizerima. Kako do sada takvu integralnu politiku nismo imali, doli smo u situaciju da deficite moramo smanjivati u vrijeme recesije, to ju moe jo vie produbiti. Kako smo doli u sadanju situaciju? 2. Percepcija krize iroko je ekspandirala u listopadu 2008., prvenstveno povezana s padom burze, nakon kojeg se oekivao financijski kolaps irih razmjera. To se nije dogodilo, jer je monetarni sustav reagirao brzo i efikasno, upravo na naelima anticiklinosti. Presudno je u tom trenutku bilo sprijeiti gubitak povjerenja tedia u bankovni sustav i zadrati vjerodostojnost monetarne politike. Bez toga aktivirao bi se, naime, "klasini krug" financijske krize kojeg prologodinji "nobelovac" Paul Krugman prikazuje kao meuovisnost triju elemenata: gubitak povjerenja - ruenje teaja, rast kamatnih stopa, nagli pad potranje - financijski problemi za poduzea, banke i stanovnitvo, koji pak rezultiraju daljnjim gubitkom povjerenja, lako su svi ti elementi bili, a dijelom su jo uvijek prisutni, intenzitet njihovog ispoljavanja odranje u okvirima koji nisu potaknuli lananu reakciju. U funkciji toga: HNB je ukidanjem granine obvezne priuve (450 mil. eura) i smanjenjem obvezne priuve (1115 mil. eura) oslobodio bankama 1555 mil. eura imobilizirane likvidnosti. Pored toga, smanjenjem minimalnih deviznih potraivanja (28.5% na 20%) omoguio je bankama da aktiviraju svoje priuve u iznosu od 2084 mil. eura. Poduzete su i druge mjere: otvorena pozicija, swap, devizne intervencije (neto 200 mil. eura). Istodobno, banke su poveale svoj inozemni dug u etvrtom tromjeseju za 2131 mil. eura, od ega kratkoroni dug za 1898 mil. eura. Dakle, ukupni neto input likvidnosti od strane HNB-a i inozemnih banaka (450+1115+2131+200) iznosio je 3896 mil. eura, to odgovara vrijednosti od oko 8% BDP-a. Treina tih sredstava je izravno ili neizravno plasirana dravi za podmirivanje domaih obveza i otplatu inozemnog duga, dok je ostatak usmjeren na odravanje likvidnosti u poslovanju banaka s drugim sektorima. 3. Nakon toga, situacija u monetarnoj sferi poinje se postupno konsolidirati, ali sa znatno izmijenjenim strukturnim i dinamikim obiljejima. 3.1. Inozemni dug Kao najvea potencijalna opasnost izravnog prenoenja svjetske financijske krize na Hrvatsku ocijenjen je rizik djelominog povlaenja inozemnog kapitala iz zemlje. Smanjenjem bankovnih depozita i ulaganja u fondove, povlaenjem dobiti ili nerefinanciranjem dospjelih inozemnih obveza poduzea i drave. Do sada se to nije dogodilo, barem ne u znaajnijoj mjeri. Tako je bruto inozemni dug krajem oujka ove godine iznosio 39.1 mlrd. eura, jednako kao to je bio i na kraju 2008. godine. Pri tome su dug poduzea i izravna ulaganja poveani za oko 620 mil eura, dok je u istom iznosu sredinja drava neto otplatila dospjelu glavnicu svog duga, uz najavu refinanciranja svojih daljnjih obveza zaduivanjem na inozemnom tritu. U postojeoj situaciji, kad se ne rauna na aranman s MMF-om ili na neki drugi oblik inozemne financijske podrke, to nesumnjivo predstavlja pozitivnu pojavu, ali ujedno i naznaku radikalnog prekida dosadanjih tendencija u priljevu inozemnog kapitala kreditnim kanalima. Taj je priljev samo u 2008. godini iznosio 6.4 mlrd. eura, predstavljajui osnovni izvor financiranja rasta domae potronje i investicija. 3.2. Domaa tednja Nakon naglog pada tednje stanovnitva u bankama tijekom listopada 2008. za oko 3.5 mlrd. kuna, ona se do kraja prvog tromjeseja 2009. realno vratila na prethodnu razinu i danas je za 10.7% vea nego prije godinu dana. To odreuje i godinji rast ukupne tednje od 7.1%. Meutim: (a) dinamika: Rast domae tednje u bankama je sada gotovo upola sporiji od prosjenog u prethodnim godinama (13.5%) i pod utjecajem je supstitucije alternativnih oblika tednje, tako da je agregatna vrijednost domae financijske imovine znaajno smanjena (7%). (b) valutna struktura: Poveana percepcija valutnog rizika rezultirala je poveanjem udjela devizne tednje u strukturi ukupne tednje, sa 66.3% u travnju 2008. na 72.7% danas. To poveava i opi stupanj euriziranosti hrvatske ekonomije, gdje je udio deviznih sredstava u strukturi ukupnih likvidnih sredstava porastao s 49.6% na 56.6%. (c) sektorska struktura: Za razliku od tednje stanovnitva, tednja sektora poduzea smanjena je u posljednjih godinu dana za 6,0%, ime je smanjen i njezin udio u strukturi ukupne tednje s 19,7% na 17.3%. To ukazuje na znatno pogoranje financijskog potencijala tog sektora, to je samo odraz smanjene likvidnosti u sferi njihovog tekueg poslovanja, gdje je koliina depozitnog novca smanjena za 18.5%, uzrokujui i smanjenje novane mase za 12.0%. 3.3. Sve to govori o izraenim ogranienjima u rastu kreditnog potencijala iz domaih izvora, a povezano sa stagnacijom inozemnog duga i stanjem na burzi, i o ogranienjima u formiranju ukupnog financijskog potencijala zemlje. Rezerve imobilizirane likvidnosti koje u tom smislu jo postoje kod HNB-a ve su u posljednjih godinu dana znaajno smanjene (sa 51 na 41 mlrd. kuna), tako da obvezna priuva banaka u devizama krajem travnja iznosi jo samo 628 mil. eura (prema 2408 mil. eura koliko je iznosila u travnju prole godine). Prema tome, eventualno daljnje smanjivanje stope obvezne priuve moglo bi hipotetski biti jedino u funkciji domaih plaanja, dok bi konverzija tako osloboenih kuna u devize pretpostavljala znatno smanjenje neto deviznih priuva sredinje banke, s negativnim utjecajem na percepciju domaih tedia i inozemnih kreditora. Zato bi takav korak imao opravdanje jedino u sluaju credit cruncha na inozemnim tritima i izravne prijetnje eksternoj likvidnosti zemlje. 3.4. Plasmani Nakon injekcije likvidnosti od strane inozemnih banaka i HNB-a, ukupni plasmani banaka zadrali su godinju dinamiku rasta od 14,0% po kojoj su prosjeno rasli i tijekom prethodnih pet godine, ali su: (a) struktura: Unutar ukupnih kredita, neto krediti dravi porasli su u posljednjih godinu dana za ak 94,6%, ime je njihov udio u strukturi ukupnih kredita banaka povean sa 6.5% u travnju prole na 11.1 % u travnju ove godine. Istodobno, krediti ostalim sektorima rastu po godinjoj stopi 8.4% i znaajno se usporavaju u odnosu na prethodne godine (15% u 2007; 10.5% u 2008). Time se poveava i raskorak izmeu efektivnog rasta kredita tim sektorima i "doputenog", odnosno od strane HNB-a nepenaliziranog rasta. Naime, u odnosu na bazno stanje krajem 2007. godine, ti krediti su danas vei za 11.1%, dok "limit" iznosi 16% ili oko 10.2 mlrd. kuna vie. Dijelom je to rezultat usporavanja potranje za kreditima (zbog poveanja kamatnih stopa i neizvjesnosti), ali upuuje i na izraenu pojavu istiskivanja ostalih sektora s trita kredita od strane drave. (b) valutni aspekt: Porast inozemnih izvora sredstava i udjela devizne tednje skratio je deviznu poziciju banaka, ija je neto inozemna pasiva poveana sa 3.9 na 5.3 mlrd eura (istodobno je neto inozemna aktiva monetarnih institucija smanjena sa 6.1 na 3.6 mlrd. eura). Time se za njih poveao i valutni rizik, pa je dio banaka prestao odobravati iste kunske kredite, prebacujui taj rizik na korisnike novih kredita. Zajedno s poveanim stupnjem euriziranosti, to jo vie naglaava znaaj odravanja stabilnog teaja. 3.5. Teaj Nakon to se krajem 2008. vratio na poetnu razinu od 7,32 kune za euro, u prvom tromjeseju ove godine teaj je pod utjecajem poveane potranje za devizama deprecirao za 2%, ali su ga zatim slabljenje deprecijacijskih oekivanja i najava inozemnog zaduivanja drave vratili u okvire relativno visoke stabilnosti. Radi zaustavljanja deprecijacijskih oekivanja, HNB je u tom razdoblju izravno intervenirao na deviznom tritu u bruto iznosu od oko 500 mil. eura, ali je i relaksacijom prudencijalnih mjera proirio manevarski prostor bankama da poveaju ponudu deviza te se tako i same ukljue u obranu stabilnosti teaja. "Poticaj" za takvo ponaanje banaka bila je promjena u valutnoj strukturi izdvajanja obvezne priuve te politika ogranienih injekcija kunske likvidnosti kroz operacije na otvorenom tritu, to je povremeno imalo za posljedicu i vrlo visoke kamatne stope na prekonone kredite na tritu novca. Stabilizacijom teaja smanjeni su i pritisci na te stope, te su one konstantno nie od lombardne stope HNB-a i u prosjeku iznose 6.5%. 3.6. Kamatne stope Relaksacijom mjera monetarne politike smanjeni su i jedinini "trokovi regulacije" za banke za priblino 20%. Tako su npr. za pokrie tih trokova pri pasivnoj kamatnoj stopi na devizni depozit od 5% i uz teajni rizik od 2% banke prije trebale ostvariti prosjenu kamatnu stopu na plasmane od 10.2%, dok je sada ta stopa sputena na 8.1%. injenica da su unato tome aktivne kamatne stope banaka porasle ima uzroke u poveanoj cijeni inozemnog zaduivanja (country risk), poveanju kamatnih stopa na domae depozite zbog jaanja konkurencije izmeu banaka u uvjetima usporenog rasta depozita, te u pogoranju kvalitete plasmana, odnosno smanjenoj naplativosti kredita, posebno onih odobrenih stanovnitvu. 4. Dakle, gledano u cjelini, monetarni sektor je izdrao prvi udar financijske krize i postupno se konsolidira. Meutim, on vie nema kapacitet da podrava dosadanju dinamiku rasta agregatne potranje, niti su same banke spremne neselektivno nastaviti s ekspanzivnom politikom ponude kredita. Za razliku od njega, realni sektor jo uvijek pada, ali to nije iskljuivo posljedica aktualne financijske krize, ve je rezultat postupnog kumuliranja vie faktora i zapoinje jo poetkom 2008. godine. Tako se industrijska proizvodnja jo od oujka prole godine smanjuje po prosjenoj trendnoj stopi od 0.7% mjeseno, dok je BDP praktiki stagnirao tijekom cijele prole godine na desezoniranoj razini iz zadnjeg tromjeseja 2007. godine. Uzroci: (1) Ubrzanje prosjene godinje stope inflacije s 2.9% na 6.1 %, koje je u 2008. godini neutraliziralo glavninu nominalnog rasta tekuih dohodaka, lako je u drugom dijelu 2008. godine nastupilo agregatno smanjenje potroakih cijena za oko 1 % u odnosu na njihovu razinu iz mjeseca srpnja, tekui rast tih cijena u prvom tromjeseju ove godine od 2.1% indikator je mogueg nastavka negativnog djelovanja inflacije na raspoloive dohotke i realnu potranju na domaem tritu. (2) Pad vrijednosti financijske imovine stanovnitva uloene u vrijednosne papire i nebankovne institucije uslijed ispuhavanja balona na tritima dionica i nekretnina. On je u 2008. godini iznosio oko 47 mlrd. kuna (za 37.1%) od ega u etvrtom tromjeseju oko 16 mlrd. kuna, ime je potpuno neutraliziran rast te imovine tijekom prethodne godine. Zajedno s realnom stagnacijom dohodaka od rada, takav gubitak kapitalnih prihoda i likvidnosti doveo je do pada osobne potronje i bitnog usporavanja investicija. (3) Jaanje nelikvidnosti zbog neelastinosti dijela tekuih rashoda u uvjetima smanjenih prihoda te visokih kreditnih obveza. I dok su u tome sektori stanovnitva i poduzea imali odreeni manevarski prostor kroz smanjenje svoje tednje, sektor drave ponaao se vrlo rigidno. Tako je deficit konsolidirane ope drave (ukljuujui HAC i HBOR) povean s 5.6 mlrd. kuna u 2007. na 8.6 mlrd. kuna u 2008. godini, ili sa 1.8% na 2.5% BDP-a, pri emu je cijeli taj deficit bio koncentriran u posljednjem tromjeseju, znai u vrijeme najveih potresa na financijskim tritima. Slina kretanja nastavljena su i u prvom tromjeseju ove godine kada se sredinja drava neto zaduila na domaem tritu za daljnjih 10.5 mlrd. kuna, od ega je neto otplatila dospjeli inozemni dug od 3.3 mlrd. kuna, dok je 7.2 mlrd. kuna koristila za plaanja u zemlji. Naravno da likvidnost na domaem tritu nije bila u tom razdoblju dovoljna za financiranje tolikih potreba drave, i jedino je neformalno "uvjetovanom" relaksacijom monetarne politike bilo mogue sprijeiti pojavu nesolventnosti drave u podmirivanju njenih obveza - posebno prema inozemstvu. Time je, meutim, znaajno umanjena mogunost da se ta dotad imobilizirana sredstva izravno usmjere prema sektoru poduzea i odravanju njihove likvidnosti. (4) "Animal spirits", s tzv. multiplikatorom (ne)povjerenja, odnosno ope euforije u uzlaznoj i ope panike u silaznoj fazi ciklusa, zbog koje se ekonomski entiteti ne ponaaju racionalno. Indikator aktualnog stanja u toj sferi je i indeks pouzdanja potroaa koji je tijekom 2008. i u prvom tromjeseju 2009. godine smanjen za preko 25 poena i na najnioj je razini jo od sredine 1999. godine. (5) Na te dominantno domae imbenike, uslijedio je tek krajem 2008. godine kljuni eksterni udar - pad izvozne potranje, ije negativno djelovanje potenciraju vrlo ograniene mogunost supstitucije izvozne potranje domaom kao i nedovoljna sposobnost supstitucije uvozne potranje domaom ponudo. On je bitno zaotrio problem kljune strukturne neusklaenosti hrvatske ekonomije, a to je deficit u razmjeni roba od 23% BDP-a. Njega, na takvoj razini, jo dugo nee moi pokriti vrlo osjetljiv sektor usluga i transfera. 5. Dakle, za razliku od monetarnog sektora koji se konsolidira, realni sektor se tek nalazi pred najteim problemima. Njihov osnovni uzrok su pad agregatne potranje i poveana nelikvidnost, a niti jedan od tih problema nije primarno iniciran monetarnim initeljima, niti je posljedica samo eksternih uzroka. Meutim, u rjeavanju tih problema, realni sektor se sada suoava s izraenim monetarnim i financijskim ogranienjima, koja je u znaajnoj mjeri sam izazvao. Pri tome je kljuno devizno ogranienje, koje proizlazi iz disproporcije izmeu raspoloive ponude i dosadanjim poslovanjem generirane potranje za devizama i koje se ne moe racionalno pokrivati nikakvim monetarnim "akrobacijama", ve zahtijeva odgovarajuu prilagodbu samog realnom sektora. Svjesnu ili spontanu. Veliina te prilagodbe okvirno je odreena s tri eksterno definirane pretpostavke, koje su sukladne efektivnim kretanjima u dosadanjem dijelu 2009. godine. To su: 1. Kontrakcija izvozne potranje, po tekuem teaju oko 10%; 2. Pad izravnih stranih ulaganja za oko 50%; 3. Refinanciranje dospjelih inozemnih obveza, uz relativnu stagnaciju inozemnog duga. Uz tako procijenjena vanjska ogranienja, proizlazi potreba smanjenja deficita tekueg rauna platne bilance sa 4.5 mlrd. eura u 2008. na "samo" 2.8 mlrd. eura u ovoj godini (s 9,4% na, procjenjuje se, oko 6% BDP-a). To pretpostavlja smanjenje uvoza roba i usluga za oko 16%, emu bi trebala biti podreena ukupna politika reguliranja domae potranje, a u tome posebnu odgovornost ima fiskalna politika. U tim okvirima, monetarna e politika podravati likvidnost sustava samo do razine koja nee destabilizirajue djelovati na teaj i preko njega nepovoljno utjecati na ukupan financijski sustav, kao to se nedavno dogodilo u pojedinim zemljama srednje i istone Europe. Temeljem toga, ocjenjuje se da e plasmani banaka poduzeima i stanovnitvu usporiti svoj rast u ovoj godini na oko 8%, priblino kao i domaa tednja, dok e ukupna likvidna sredstva porasti za oko 4%. U okviru njih, meutim, novana masa e biti smanjena za oko 9%. Potvrdi li se u praksi tonost inicijalnih pretpostavki, u 2009. godini moe se oekivati realno smanjenje domae agregatne potronje za 5-6%, te pad BDP-a za oko 4%. Moe li taj pad biti manji, prije svega e ovisiti od razvoja prilika u svijetu, gdje povoljnija kretanja od sada predvienih mogu u odreenoj mjeri ublaiti eksterna ogranienja za hrvatsku ekonomiju i u financijskom i u realnom sektoru. Meutim, i u tom sluaju ostaje isto sutinsko pitanje. Kako gledati na ovu krizu? Ako nju vidimo samo kao "privremeni zastoj" u dugorono pozitivnim tendencijama ekonomskog rasta i razvoja, nita neemo rijeiti. Suprotno tome, nju treba prije svega shvatiti kao drastinu opomenu o posljedicama koje mogu nastupiti, i ve jesu, zbog prethodnog zanemarivanja problema odrivosti ekonomskog rasta. Opomenu koja bi bila jo tea da je HNB u proteklim godinama vodio drugaiju monetarnu politiku. Shvatimo li tu opomenu, tada je ova kriza ujedno i ansa za jedan drugaiji poetak promiljanja budueg ekonomskog razvoja. Imamo li za sve to snage, znanja i volje - pitanje je na koje neemo morati dugo ekati odgovor.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary policy in times of crisis
text: Monetary policy in times of crisis Published: 13.4.2010. Type Speech Speaker Dr. Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the declaration 12.4.2010. Event of the 13th Scientific and Professional Conference Croatian Money Market Opatija venue Date of the event 12.4.2010. There is a huge literature that already exists today on the topic of the current economic crisis. From the description and analysis of concrete events to the generalization of problems in the context of a long history of financial crises and the search for their fundamental causes in the genesis and character of the capitalist system itself. University professors, as well as managers, consultants, journalists, judges, ministers, even congressmen write about this. Thanks to this, and despite all the differences in approach to the topic, a general, rather homogeneous perception of how and why the crisis occurred was formed, and what needs to be done, changed in the system, to reduce the risk of a recurrence of such crises in the future. By contrast, both in literature and even more in practice, there is no firm consensus on how to emerge operationally from the crisis. Initially, it was simply from the assumption that large financial injections combined with a "lesson learned" would in themselves establish an environment sufficient for the action of the market to trigger the recovery, while recently the belief that these injections must be accompanied by strong economic policy interventions has increasingly prevailed. Stiglitz (Freefall) states: Stimulus measures should be based on the following principles: (a) timeliness (rapid action) (b) efficiency (multiplier diversity) (c) focus on long-term problems (d) focus on investments (e) (social)fairness (f) taking into account the difficulties of those most affected by the crisis (g) focus on areas where the biggest drop in employment is Let us consider monetary policy, in the context of the overall economic policy in Croatia, from the point of view of these principles: (1) TIMELINESS (two stages): Preventive action (capital and credit controls, prudential measures) that prevents even bigger bubbles and imbalances. Politics was restrictive in character and moderately expansive in intensity. Indeed, it did not stop but only slowed monetary flows at dynamics significantly higher than GDP growth. By this we were specific and subjected to criticism; Policy significantly changes character as early as mid-2008: minimum foreign currency receivables were reduced from 32% to 28.5%, then to 25%, and to 20%;p the open market operations with a fixed interest rate are of 6%; abolished the marginal reserve requirement; the reserve requirement rate decreased from 17% to 14%, with changes in the structure of the reserve requirement (total effect of these measures around 805bn); the limit on loan increment has been lifted; this year, a further lowering of the reserve requirement rate to 13%. (2) EFFICIENCY (three levels): (a) The functioning of the system as a whole: In interaction with the whole relationship in the financial system, such a policy has directly and indirectly influenced the design of monetary flows where: maintained the external liquidity of the country without the assistance of the IMF (under terms of maturity of the principal and interest of EUR 10.4 billion); preserved foreign exchange reserves and total available foreign exchange funds, even increased (by EUR 1.2 billion); allowing further availability of funds from abroad with a gradual drop in the premium on risk towards pre-crisis levels; maintained exchange rate stability without major direct intervention by the central bank; prevented credit breakage in the domestic market (credit growth 1.8%); together with new foreign borrowing by businesses and the state (802.8bn; growth of 809.5%), total loans grew by 5.1%, mitigating the impact of a fall in current revenues on liquidity and consumption; this increased the ratio of total loans to GDP from 141.2% at the end of 2008 to 152.4% at the end of 2009 and to 148.4% if the impact of the fall in GDP (domestic loans from 78.7% to 82.3% - 80.1%) is excluded; the banking system remained "healthy" with a capital adequacy rate of 15.8% and a yield rate of 6.7% and preserved the confidence of savers (total savings growth of 4.4%) interest rates: after growth during 2008 and I-XI 2009, 6.73% to 8.34% (strong impact on disposable income), the average interest rate on kuna loans with a currency clause begins to decrease slightly (II 2010 averages 8.24%, in which the interest rate on loans to enterprises of 2-3 years is 8.17% - in March the interest rate on loans from model A was lowered below 5%) Thus (viewed on various systems), the reaction of monetary policy to the emergence of the crisis was timely, and in character extremely expansionary, regardless of the fall in monetary aggregates (M1 by 14.6%, and M4 by 0.9%). This also maintained the stability of the financial system at the height of the crisis and avoided some of the more radical problems that have arisen in other countries, to which Croatia is particularly exposed due to its high "external vulnerability". In this regard, the stable functioning of the financial system is expected to continue in 2010, without the need to reintroduce restrictive measures. (b) Sectoral level A fundamentally different situation compared to other countries, where the main problem was the banking sector, and in our country the financing of the state; First, it was necessary to maintain the liquidity and solvency of the state in the conditions: (a) high refinancing needs (a total of HRK 14.2 billion or HRK 4.3% of GDP) at significantly hampered borrowing opportunities in the first part of 2009; and (b) a drop in revenues at the inelasticity of the bulk of expenditure, which increased the current account deficit from 2.7% to 5.2% of GDP (from HRK 9.1bn to HRK 17.3bn) Without it, a moratorium, a downgrade and a high rise in interest rates would have hit the overall economy. The forced linking of expansionary monetary policy to the needs of state financing has also affected the redistribution of loans on the domestic market between the state and other sectors; the increase in loans to the state amounted to EUR 6.4 billion. (up 16.2%), while loans to other sectors were aggregated by EUR 1.5 billion. marten (-0,7%). However, the movement between and within the sector was differentiated: loans to enterprises increased by 2.1% and lending to the population decreased by 2.9% (as part of this, car loans decreased by 19.0% and non-purpose loans by 4.1%, while residential loans increased by 1.2%). In addition, the corporate sector managed to compensate for the slower growth of domestic loans through foreign borrowing and foreign direct investment, so that the total increase in loans to the sector in 2009 amounted to EUR 14.4 billion. (growth of 5.1%), approximately as well as the increment of loans to the state (HRK 14bn, growth of HRK 19.6%). Thus, the sectoral redistribution of loans took place primarily between the state and the population (government and personal consumption of the private sector), the two sectors with the lowest and highest elasticity of demand -so that, if housing loans are included, in 2009 there was no credit breakdown in the manufacturing sector. Hence, monetary policy was effective in the short term from the point of view of solving the key sectoral problem (illiquidity of the state), through the preserved stability of the financial system and exchange rates prevented a strong cost impact on all sectors of the national economy and allowed for a further increase in lending to the manufacturing sector. (c) Micro-level The picture, however, changes when the micro-structure of lending is included, given the different position that individual companies have in the credit market. Large majority-owned enterprises, which participate in the structure of domestic loans to the enterprise sector from 14%, increased their debt by 20.2%, which absorbed more than the total increase in domestic loans to the sector (loans to other companies decreased by 0.4%). As these companies account for a significant part of foreign borrowing (21%, excluding foreign direct investment), the overall structure of lending to companies also changes, and this, judging by the latest developments, according to entities with serious problems in the rationality of the use of funds, and which explicitly use state guarantees and therefore banks are generally more attractive to clients. In 2009, in 2009, 81% of the increase in total loans (at home and abroad) ended up in the public sector, that is, there was an appropriate displacement of the private sector from the credit market. Due to all these changes in the sectoral and micro lending structure, aggregate growth in loans could not significantly compensate in 2009 for the decline in revenues from the sale of private sector goods and services and the lack of income from the capital and real estate markets in order to preserve the liquidity of that part of the economy with a rigid distribution structure. It was this rigid distribution that further raised the problem of "real adjustment" through the reduction of employment in the private part of the manufacturing sector. The sector most affected by the decline in exports and personal consumption, which is the only one and can productively create new jobs. Can more be done in 2010? It was only when the state's ongoing lending stabilised at the end of 2009, open foreign refinancing opportunities in 2010, that "liquidity reserves" (SDR allocation) were established in case of short-term shocks, but the budget deficit reduction policy was also announced, that monetary policy turned more to the private sector. The primary, short-term, problem is not the liquidity of the banking sector, but the aversion to risk on the supply side, but also on the demand for loans. Liquidity: the stability of the financial system has enabled net foreign inflows, with foreign exchange reserves increasing by 80896m. By converting them, primary money increases it by a36.4bn kuna (12.9%) High liquidity of the banking sector in I-III in 2010: average overnight deposit balance of EUR 5.5 billion. kuna; average kam. overnight market rate 0.64% Risk: spoilage of placements - B and C increased by 62.7%, the ratio to total loans increased from 4.9% to 7.8%, in which in enterprises from 7.5% to 12.8%, and in the population from 4.0% to 5.8%. To this should be added and reprogramming of loans at the level of about 4.5% of total loans. CNB measures play the role of "incentives" for risk-taking, and given the lowest price of liquidity freed, they are also in the function of reducing interest rates. Movement I-20. III 2010. During this period, the new measures have not yet been effected, so the credit activity is carried out according to earlier dynamic and structural characteristics. Total loans increased by 2.0% over the period (inter-year stagnation), under which loans to the central government increased by 10.8% (inter-year growth of 5.1%), while loans to other sectors stagnated (-1.1%). In this, loans to enterprises grow by 1.8% (2.2%), while loans to households continue to fall by 0.9% (now they are 3.9% lower than in March 2008). However, the tendency to reduce deposit money has stopped, with the cash mass also increasing by 1.8% in the first three months (inter-year growth of 3.0%), while total liquid assets stagnate. Can there be faster growth in loans to the corporate sector, i.e. what are the opportunities to continue with the reduction of the reserve requirement rate? (3) LONG-TERM PROBLEM - balance of payments and debt, as they are limitations on sustainable growth and employment. This problem also dimensions the possible degree of "expansion" of monetary policy. In 2009, the basic adjustment to the decline in exports (by 19%) and aggregate demand (by nominally 9%) and halved foreign direct investment was a 24.8% reduction in imports of goods and services, so that the deficit in the exchange of goods and services was more than halved (from 803.8bn to 801.7bn) which also reduced the current account deficit from 9.2% to 5.2% of GDP. However, it remains high, with a nominal 2.7% increase in the level of foreign indebtedness from 83.3% to 94.9% of GDP (98.3% including "circular investments") at the same time, and in 2010 (with these investments) it will exceed 100% of GDP. This also results in an increased outflow based on interest paid, which amounted to 2.7% of GDP in 2009 and will reach 3% in 2010. These (deficit, debt) are the main long-term problems of the Croatian economy that require significant changes in the structure of the overall economy and the modalities of economic policy management. In the short term, however, this not only leaves little room for manoeuvre for general monetary expansion, but explicitly assumes its "direction" by the overall policy in a way that will gradually change the "allocation" of liquidity in the system. However, there are pronounced problems of an economic and political nature: (a) Further increased refinancing needs of the consolidated general government in 2010 (HRK 22.9 billion or 6.8% of GDP), while maintaining the current fiscal deficit at the level of about 5% of GDP (HRK 16.3bn, or HRK 4.8% of GDP), to which potential liabilities based on shipbuilding guarantees can be added. Thus, there is no significant fiscal adjustment, which would allow much of the credit potential and total liquidity to be directed towards production; (b) The criteria for syndicated lending and guarantees are primarily based on the financial situation of the borrower, but not on the assessment of the role of his "product" in solving (mitigating) the underlying economic problem (balance of payments). There are two additional problems here: the choice of a 'turning point' (1.VII 2008) to start 'difficulties', as until then companies that developed were relatively best placed precisely on the elements that caused the crisis, rather than those essential for alleviating long-term problems; a certain 'dilution' of credit support, using part of the loan (20%) for settling obligations to the state and banks; (c) The postponement of the auction for guarantees from model B also indicates significant problems in the sphere of investment projects, i.e. the willingness and ability of the entrepreneurs themselves to change their business. This is the "other side of the coin" related to the wicket-formed structure of the economy and the quality of its organization. A problem that no monetary expansion can substantively solve (d) Credit support is not insignificant (10% of the total loan balance of domestic banks to the company sector), but it is not enough to produce significant results on its own. For them, it is necessary to functionally consolidate, that is, channel according to the intrinsic problem, all aspects of financial support. This, in turn, requires changes in the lending system by HBOR, as well as in incentives, subsidies and government guarantee systems. So far, there are none, and only in this way, with the appropriate tax policy, can the development and improvement of the private sector's business be effectively encouraged while reducing its partial dependence on dealings with the state. (4) MOST AFFECTED SECTORS (outside the scope of monetary policy) It is usually pointed out that these are construction with a decrease in gross value added of 6.0% nominally (in real terms 6.1%), trade with a decrease of 12.3% (in real terms 14.3%), and the sharpened problems in agriculture are highlighted. However, these are sectors that have grown above average in previous years precisely on the effects of bubbles, demand financed by foreign loans and changes in relative prices without basis in funds. Here's the case: BDV 2009./2006. (nominal): gradevinarstvo 21,8% agriculture 25.3% total economy 17.9% the biggest problem is in the manufacturing industry: 2009/2008 -7.0% (real -8.5%), 9.6% in 2009/2006 Special measures (200 euros; state investments in road construction) are not on the way of solving the basic problem. (5) FAIRNESS - cannot be a reflection of the current relationship between political forces and daily politics : working active population - social benefits poljoprivrednici-town hall employees in the state and private sectors Projection 2010. There are not many arguments for a further reduction in the reserve requirement rate, because in addition to the current structure of realized demand for loans, a linear increase in liquidity and domestic consumption can only lead to a re-deterioration of the balance of payments relations, and the issue of inflation should not be completely ignored. However, at the current level of liquidity of the banking sector and the gradual effect of the measures taken so far, it is estimated that total loans in the country could increase by about 6% in 2010, with loans to the state by about 10% and loans to other sectors by 5.5%. At the same time, new borrowing by the state and businesses abroad is expected to borrow more by about EUR 3 billion. euro, so total loans could increase by about 7.5% in 2010. Accordingly, the M1 and M4 could increase by about 6.5%, which will relax financial flows to some extent and stabilize domestic demand. It is expected that in such conditions there will gradually be an increase in turnover and prices on the stock exchange, if in fact there will not be any fundamental reasons for this. Contrary. At the same time slow growth in demand in EU countries, in 2010 overall economic activity will mostly stagnate, without major structural changes (dual deficit of 5-6% of GDP). So it will be a year of adapting to the crisis at the level of survival, without the beginning of the formation of stronger impulses for a quick exit from the crisis. Let's go back to the beginning: the reaction of monetary policy to the emergence of the crisis was timely and efficient at the level of the overall system. Perhaps "too effective", er created the impression that the system could continue to function in the previous way. That is why structural changes are absent or slow to initiate - which means functional adjustments of the state, banks and the entrepreneurs themselves - so policy efficiency has also fallen at lower levels. However, without these changes, notably the elimination of irrationalities in the functioning of the public sector, there is no solution to long-term problems, and therefore no rapid exit from the crisis (regardless of the halting of the downturn and the onset of mild GDP growth). In this, as the example of Greece shows, no one will help us if we do not help ourselves.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna politika u vrijeme krize Objavljeno: 13.4.2010. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 12.4.2010. 13. znanstveno-struna konferencija Hrvatsko novano trite Opatija 12.4.2010.
