Ogromna je literatura koja danas ve postoji na temu aktualne ekonomske krize. Od deskripcije i analize konkretnih dogaanja do generalizacije problema u kontekstu duge povijesti financijskih kriza i traenja njihovih fundamentalnih uzroka u genezi i karakteru samog kapitalistikog sustava. O tome piu kako sveuilini profesori, tako i managed, konzultanti, novinari, suci, ministri, ak i kongresmeni. Zahvaljujui tome, a unato svim razlikama u pristupu temi, formirana je jedna opa, prilino homogena percepcija kako i zato je nastupila kriza, te to je potrebno poduzeti, mijenjati u sustavu, da se smanji rizik ponavljanja takvih kriza u budunosti. Nasuprot tome, i u literaturi i jo vie u praksi, ne postoji neki vrsti konsenzus kako operativno izai iz krize. U poetku se jednostavno polazilo od pretpostavke da e velike financijske injekcije u kombinaciji s "nauenom lekcijom" same po sebi uspostaviti ambijent dostatan da djelovanje trita pokrene oporavak, dok u posljednje vrijeme sve vie prevladava uvjerenje kako te injekcije moraju biti praene snanim intervencijama ekonomske politike. Stiglitz (Freefall) navodi: Mjere poticaja trebaju biti zasnovane na slijedeim naelima: (a) pravovremenost (brzo djelovanje) (b) efikasnost (razliitost multiplikatora) (c) usmjerenost na dugorone probleme (d) fokusiranost na investicije (e) (socijalna)pravednost (f) voenje rauna o tekoama onih koji su najpogoeniji krizom (g) usmjerenost na podruja gdje je najvei pad zaposlenosti Razmotrimo monetarnu, u kontekstu ukupne ekonomske politike u Hrvatskoj, s aspekta tih naela: (1) PRAVOVREMENOST (dvije faze):  Preventivno djelovanje (kapitalske i kreditne kontrole, prudencijalne mjere) kojim su sprijeeni jo vei baloni i neravnotee. Politika je po karakteru bila restriktivna, a po intenzitetu umjereno ekspanzivna. Ona, naime, nije zaustavljala ve samo usporavala monetarne tokove pri dinamikama znatno viim od rasta BDP-a. Po tome smo bili specifini i izloeni kritikama;  Politika bitno mijenja karakter ve sredinom 2008.: minimalna devizna potraivanja smanjena su s 32% na 28,5%, zatim na 25%, pa na 20%;poveane su operacije na otvorenom tritu uz fiksnu kamatnu stopu od 6%; ukinuta granina obvezna priuva; stopa obvezne priuve smanjena sa 17% na 14%, uz promjene u strukturi obvezne priuve (ukupan efekt ovih mjera oko 5 mlrd eura); ukinut je limit na prirast kredita; ove godine daljnje sputanje stope obvezne priuve na 13%. (2) EFIKASNOST (tri razine): (a) Funkcioniranje sustava u cjelini:  U interakciji s cjelinom odnosa u financijskom sustavu, takva politika je izravno i neizravno utjecala na oblikovanje monetarnih tokova pri kojima je:  odrana eksterna likvidnost zemlje bez pomoi MMF-a (u uvjetima dospijea glavnice i kamata od 10,4 mlrd. eura);  ouvane devizne rezerve i ukupno raspoloiva devizna sredstva, ak i poveana (za 1,2 mlrd. eura);  omoguena daljnja dostupnost financijskih sredstava iz inozemstva uz postupni pad premije na rizik prema razinama prije izbijanja krize;  odrana stabilnost teaja bez veih izravnih intervencija sredinje banke;  sprijeen kreditni lom na domaem tritu (rast kredita 1,8%);  zajedno s novim inozemnim zaduivanjem poduzea i drave (2,8 mlrd. eura; rast 9,5%), ostvarenje rast ukupnih kredita od 5,1 %, ime je ublaen efekt pada tekuih prihoda na likvidnost i potronju;  time je odnos ukupnih kredita prema BDP povean sa 141,2% krajem 2008. na 152,4% krajem 2009. godine odnosno na 148,4% iskljui li se utjecaj pada BDP-a (domaih kredita sa 78,7% na 82,3% - 80.1%);  bankovni sustav ostao je "zdrav" sa stopom adekvatnosti kapitala od 15,8% i stopom prinosa od 6,7% te je sauvao povjerenje tedia (rast ukupne tednje 4,4%)  kamatne stope: nakon rasta tijekom 2008. i I-XI2009. 6,73% na 8,34% (snaan utjecaj na raspoloivi dohodak), prosjena kamatna stopa na kunske kredite s valutnom klauzulom poinje se lagano smanjivati (II 2010. prosjeno iznosi 8,24%, u emu kamatna stopa na kredite poduzeima od 2-3 godine 8,17% - u oujku je kamatna stopa na kredite iz modela A sputena ispod 5%)  Dakle (promatrano na razni sustava), reakcija monetarne politike na pojavu krize bila je pravovremena, a po karakteru izrazito ekspanzivna, bez obzira na pad monetarnih agregata (Ml za 14,6%, i M4 za 0,9%).  Time je i na vrhuncu krize odrana stabilnost financijskog sustava te su izbjegnuti neki od radikalnijih problema kakvi su se pojavili u drugim zemljama, a kojima je zbog visoke "eksterne ranjivosti" Hrvatska posebno izloena. U tom smislu, oekuje se nastavak stabilnog funkcioniranja financijskog sustava i tijekom 2010. godine, bez potrebe ponovnog uvoenja restriktivnih mjera. (b) Sektorska razina  Bitno razliita situacija u odnosu na druge zemlje, gdje je glavni problem bio bankovni sektor, a kod nas financiranje drave;  Prvo je trebalo odrati likvidnost i solventnost drave u uvjetima: (a) visokih potreba refinanciranja obveza (ukupno 14,2 mlrd. kuna ili 4,3%BDP-a) pri bitno oteanim mogunostima inozaduenja u prvom dijelu 2009. godine; te (b) pada prihoda pri neelastinosti glavnine rashoda, zbog ega je tekui deficit povean sa 2,7% na 5,2% BDP-a (s 9,1 na 17,3 mlrd. kuna) Bez toga, moratorij, pad rejtinga i visok porast kamatnih stopa pogodio bi ukupnu ekonomiju.  Iznueno vezivanje ekspanzivne monetarne politike s potrebama financiranja drave utjecalo je i na preraspodjelu kredita na domaem tritu izmeu drave i ostalih sektora; prirast kredita dravi iznosio je 6,4 mlrd. kuna (rast 16,2%), dok su krediti ostalim sektorima agregatno smanjeni za 1,5 mlrd. kuna (- 0,7%). Meutim, kretanje izmeu i unutar sektora bilo je diferencirano: krediti poduzeima poveani suza 2,1%, a kreditiranje stanovnitva smanjeno za 2,9% (u okviru toga krediti za automobile smanjeni za 19,0%, a nenamjenski za 4,1%,dok su stambeni porasli za 1,2%). Pored toga, sektor poduzea uspio je kompenzirati sporiji rast domaih kredita inozemnim zaduivanjem i izravnim stranim ulaganjima, tako da je ukupni prirast kredita tom sektoru u 2009. iznosio 14,4 mlrd. kuna (rast od 5,1%), priblino kao i prirast kredita dravi (14 mlrd. kuna, rast 19,6%).  Dakle, sektorska preraspodjela kredita odigrala se prvenstveno izmeu drave i stanovnitva (dravne i osobne potronje privatnog sektora), dvaju sektora s najmanjom i najveom elastinou potranje -tako da, ukljue li se i stambeni krediti, u 2009. godini nije bilo nikakvog kreditnog sloma u proizvodnom sektoru.  Otuda, monetarna politika bila je kratkorono efikasna s aspekta rjeavanja kljunog sektorskog problema (nelikvidnosti drave), kroz ouvanu stabilnost financijskog sustava i teaja sprijeila je snaan trokovni udar na sve sektore nacionalne ekonomije te je omoguila daljnji prirast kreditiranja proizvodnog sektora. (c) Mikro razina Slika se, meutim, mijenja kad se ukljui i mikro struktura kreditiranja, s obzirom na razliitu poziciju koju pojedina poduzea imaju na tritu kredita. Velika poduzea u veinskom vlasnitvu drave, koja uestvuju u strukturi domaih kredita sektoru poduzea sa 14%, poveala su svoje zaduenje za 20,2% to je apsorbiralo vie nego ukupan prirast domaih kredita tom sektoru (krediti ostalim poduzeima su smanjeni za 0,4%). Kako na ta poduzea otpada i znaajan dio inozemnog zaduivanja (21%, bez izravnih stranih ulaganja) mijenja se i ukupna struktura kreditiranja poduzea i to, ako je suditi po posljednjim zbivanjima, prema entitetima s ozbiljnim problemima u racionalnosti koritenja sredstava, a koji eksplicitno koriste dravna jamstva i zato su bankama u pravilu atraktivniji komitenti. Povezano s kreditiranjem same drave, tako je u 2009. godini 81% prirasta ukupnih kredita (u zemlji i iz inozemstva) zavrilo u javnom sektoru, odnosno dolo je do odgovarajueg istiskivanja privatnog sektora s trita kredita. Zbog svih tih promjena u sektorskoj i mikro strukturi kreditiranja, agregatni prirast kredita nije u 2009. godini mogao znaajnije kompenzirati pad prihoda od prodaje roba i usluga privatnog sektora te izostanak dohodaka sa trita kapitala i nekretnina da bi se uz rigidnu strukturu raspodjele ouvala likvidnost tog dijela ekonomije. Upravo je ta rigidna raspodjela dodatno potencirala problem "realne prilagodbe" kroz smanjenje zaposlenosti u privatnom dijelu proizvodnog sektora. Sektora koji je najvie pogoen padom izvoza i osobne potronje, a koji jedini i moe produktivno kreirati nova radna mjesta. Moe li se u 2010. godini uraditi vie?  Tek kada je krajem 2009. stabilizirano tekue kreditiranje drave, otvorene mogunosti inozemnog refinanciranja u 2010., uspostavljene "rezerve likvidnosti" (alokacija SDR-a) za sluaj kratkoronih okova, ali najavljena i politika smanjenja proraunskog deficita, mogla se monetarna politika vie okrenuti privatnom sektoru.  Primarni, kratkoroni, problem nije likvidnost bankovnog sektora, ve averzija prema riziku na strani ponude, ali i na strani potranje za kreditima.  Likvidnost: stabilnost financijskog sustava omoguila je neto priljev inozemnih sredstava, te su devizne rezerve poveane za 896 mil. eura. Njihovom konverzijom, primarni novac povea je za 6,4 mlrd kuna (12.9%) Visoka likvidnost bankovnog sektora u l-lll 2010. godine:  prosjeno stanje prekononih depozita 5,5 mlrd. kuna;  prosjena kam. stopa na prekononom tritu 0,64%  Rizik: kvarenje plasmana - B i C poveani su za 62,7%, odnos prema ukupnim kreditima povean s 4,9% na 7,8%, u emu kod poduzea sa 7,5% na 12,8%, a kod stanovnitva s 4,0% na 5, 8%. Tome treba dodati i reprogram kredita na razini od oko 4,5% ukupnih kredita.  Mjere HNB-a imaju ulogu "poticaja" za preuzimanje rizika, a s obzirom na najniu cijenu osloboene likvidnosti i u funkciji su smanjenja kamatnih stopa. Kretanje I-20.III 2010. U tom razdoblju nove mjere jo nisu efektuirane pa se kreditna aktivnost odvija po ranijim dinamikim i strukturnim obiljejima. Ukupni krediti poveani su u tom razdoblju za 2,0% ( meugodinja stagnacija), u okviru ega su krediti sredinjoj dravi poveani za 10,8% (meugodinji rast 5,1%), dok krediti ostalim sektorima stagniraju (-1,1%). U tome, krediti poduzeima rastu 1,8% (2,2%), dok krediti stanovnitvu i dalje padaju za 0,9% (sada su za 3,9% nii nego u oujku 2008. godine). Meutim, zaustavljena je tendencija smanjivanja depozitnog novca, tako da je i novana masa porasla u prva tri mjeseca za 1,8% (meugodinji rast 3,0%), dok ukupna likvidna sredstva stagniraju. Moe li se ostvariti bri rast kredita sektoru poduzea, odnosno kolike su mogunosti da se nastavi sa smanjenjem stope obvezne priuve? (3) DUGORONI PROBLEM - platna bilanca i dug, jer su oni ogranienja odrivom rastu i zapoljavanju. Taj problem dimenzionira i mogui stupanj "ekspanzivnosti" monetarne politike. U 2009. osnovna prilagodba padu izvoza (za 19%) i agregatne potranje (za nominalno 9%) i prepolovljenim izravnim stranim ulaganjima bilo je smanjenje uvoza roba i usluga za 24,8%, tako da je deficit u razmjeni roba i usluga vie nego prepolovljen (sa 3,8 na 1,7 mlrd. eura) ime je i deficit tekueg rauna smanjen sa 9,2% na 5,2% BDP-a. On je, meutim, i dalje visok, te je uz njega, pri istodobnom padu BDP-a za nominalno 2,7%, stupanj inozemne zaduenosti povean sa 83,3% na 94,9%BDP-a (98,3% ukljuujui "kruna ulaganja"), a u 2010. e (s tim ulaganjima) prei 100% BDP-a. To ima za posljedicu i poveani odljev temeljem plaenih kamata, koji je u 2009. iznosio 2,7% BDP-a, a u 2010. e dostii 3%. To su (deficit, dug) glavni dugoroni problemi hrvatske ekonomije koji zahtijevaju bitne promjene u strukturi ukupne ekonomije i modalitetima voenja ekonomske politike. Kratkorono pak, to ne samo da ostavlja mali manevarski prostor opoj monetarnoj ekspanziji, ve eksplicitno pretpostavlja njeno "usmjeravanje" od strane ukupne politike na nain kojim e se postupno mijenjati "alokacija" likvidnosti u sustavu. Tu su, meutim, prisutni izraeni problemi ekonomske, ali i politike prirode: (a) Dodatno poveane potrebe refinanciranja konsolidirane ope drave u 2010. godini (22,9 mlrd kuna ili 6.8% BDP-a), uz zadravanje tekueg fiskalnog deficita na razini od oko 5% BDP-a (16,3 mlrd. kuna, ili 4,8% BDP- a), emu se mogu pridodati i potencijalne obveze temeljem jamstava brodogradnji. Dakle, nema znaajnije fiskalne prilagodbe, koja bi omoguila da se vei dio kreditnog potencijala i ukupne likvidnosti usmjeri prema proizvodnji; (b) Kriteriji za sindicirano kreditiranje i jamstva prvenstveno se temelje na financijskoj situaciji korisnika kredita, ali ne i na ocjeni uloge njegovog "proizvoda" u rjeavanju (ublaavanju) temeljnog ekonomskog problema (platne bilance). Tu postoje jo dva dodatna problema:  izbor "prijelomnog trenutka" (1 .VII2008.) za poetak "tekoa", jer su do tada relativno najbolje stajala poduzea koja su se razvijala upravo na elementima koji su izazvali krizu, a ne ona koja su bitna za ublaavanje dugoronih problema;  odreeno "razvodnjavanje" kreditne podrke, koritenjem dijela kredita (20%) za  podmirivanje obveza prema dravi i bankama; (c) Odgaanje aukcije za jamstva iz modela B ukazuje i na znaajne probleme u sferi investicijskih projekata, odnosno spremnosti i sposobnosti samih poduzetnika da mijenjaju svoje poslovanje. To je "druga strana medalje" vezana uz stihijskih formiranu strukturu ekonomije i kvalitetu njezine organizacije. Problem koji nikakva monetarna ekspanzija ne moe sutinski rijeiti (d) Kreditna podrka nije beznaajna (10% ukupnog stanja kredita domaih banaka sektoru poduzea), ali nije ni dostatna da bi sama poluila signifikantne rezultate. Za njih je potrebno funkcionalno objediniti, odnosno kanalizirati prema sutinskom problemu, sve aspekte financijske podrke. Za to su pak potrebne promjene u sustavu kreditiranja od strane HBOR-a, te u sustavima poticaja, subvencija i dravnih jamstava. Njih za sada nema, a samo se tako, uz odgovarajui poreznu politiku, moe efikasno poticati razvoj i unapreenje poslovanja privatnog sektora uz smanjivanje njegove parcijalne ovisnosti od poslova s dravom. (4) NAJPOGOENIJI SEKTORI (izvan djelokruga monetarne politike)  Obino se istie da su to graevinarstvo s padom bruto dodane vrijednosti od 6,0% nominalno (realno 6,1%), trgovina s padom od 12,3% (realno 14,3%), a naglaavaju se i zaotreni problemi u poljoprivredi. Meutim, to su sektori koji su u prijanjim godinama natprosjeno brzo rasli upravo na efektima balona, potranje financirane inozemnim kreditima i promjenama relativnih cijena bez osnova u fundamentima. Tako je: BDV 2009./2006. (nominalno):  graevi narstvo 21,8%  poljoprivreda 25,3%  ukupna ekonomija 17,9%  najvei problem je u preraivakoj industriji: 2009./2008. -7,0% (realno -8,5%), 2009./2006. 9,6%  Posebne mjere (200 eura; dravne investicije u cestogradnju) nisu na pravcu rjeavanja osnovnog problema. (5) PRAVEDNOST - ne moe biti odraz aktualnog odnosa politikih snaga i dnevne politike:  radno aktivno stanovnitvo - socijalna davanja poljoprivrednici-radnici  zaposlenici u dravnom i u privatnom sektoru Projekcija 2010. Nema mnogo argumenata za daljnje smanjenje stope obvezne priuve, jer uz dosadanju strukturu realizirane potranje za kreditima linearno poveanje likvidnosti i domae potronje moe dovesti samo do ponovnog pogoranja odnosa u platnoj bilanci, a ne treba potpuno zanemariti ni pitanje inflacije. Ipak, pri postojeoj razini likvidnosti bankovnog sektora te postupnom efektuiranju dosad poduzetih mjera, ocjenjuje se da bi ukupni krediti u zemlji mogli u 2010. godini porasti za oko 6%, u emu krediti dravi za oko 10%, a krediti ostalim sektorima za 5,5%. Istodobno, oekuje se i novo zaduivanje drave i poduzea u inozemstvu za oko 3 mlrd. eura, tako bi ukupni krediti mogli u 2010. godini porasti za oko 7,5%. Sukladno tome, Ml i M4 mogli bi porasti za oko 6,5%, to e u odreenoj mjeri relaksirati financijske tokove i stabilizirati domau potranju. Za oekivati je da e u takvim uvjetima postupno doi i do poveanja prometa i cijena na burzi, ako za to zapravo nee postojati neki fundamentalni razlozi. Naprotiv. Uz istodobno spori rast potranje u zemljama EU, u 2010. godini ukupna ekonomska aktivnost e uglavnom stagnirati, bez veih strukturnih promjena (dvojni deficit 5-6% BDP-a). Dakle, bit e to godina prilagoavanja krizi na razini preivljavanja, bez poetka formiranja snanijih impulsa za brzi izlazak iz krize. Vratimo se na poetak: reakcija monetarne politike na pojavu krize bila e pravovremena i efikasna na razini ukupnog sustava. Moda i "preefikasna", er se stvarao dojam da sustav moe i dalje funkcionirati na dosadanji nain. Zato izostaju ili se sporo iniciraju strukturne promjene - to znai funkcionalne prilagodbe drave, banaka i samih poduzetnika - pa je i efikasnost politike padala na niim razinama. Meutim, bez tih promjena, prije svega otklanjanju neracionalnosti u funkcioniranju javnog sektora, nema rjeenja dugoronih problema, pa time ni brzog izlaska iz krize (neovisno od zaustavljanja pada i poetka blagog rasta BDP-a).U tome nam, kao to pokazuje i primjer Grke, nitko nee pomoi, ako si ne pomognemo sami.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary policy
text: Monetary policy Published: 6.5.2011. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 5.5.2011. 14th Scientific and Professional Conference Croatian Money Market Opatija 5.5.2011. 1. For years we have been meeting in this or similar halls and talking about the development of the economic situation in Croatia and the policy of the central bank. As this situation has changed dramatically, so has the content and accents in these conversations, as well as the perception of what the CNB is doing and why it is doing it. 2. In the pre-crisis period, the debate was dominated by issues of rapid growth in foreign debt, the country's credit expansion, high double deficits, rising prices in securities and real estate markets, the country's external vulnerability and the risk of external shock. The central bank's activities were marked in such conditions by the tightening of prudential and implementation of admins ofstraitative measures in the function of reducing the profitability of foreign sources of funds and disincentivizing the expansionary supply of loans from these funds. 3. With the outbreak of the crisis, the aforementioned risks (stopping capital inflows, falling foreign demand) were effected, whichjeopardized the entire financial system. Discussions are dominated by the question of how to prevent the collapse of this system, in particular: how to maintain the external liquidity of the state (threat of a moratorium), prevent the credit breakdown of the groundwork and maintain the stability of theflowing self, not only for the protection of the debtor, but also because of the risk of outflows of savings. The CNB abolishes or substantially eases restrictive measures, injecting additional liquidity of around 4.5 billion euros into the system. 4. By consolidating the financial system, the focus shifts to the question ofits support for the real sector, that is, from the issue of limiting demand, it shifts to the issue of stimulating supply through coordinated monetary and fiscal policy action. This was the subject of my first conversation with the Prime Minister in July 2009. In it, he expressed witham the CNB's readiness to further lower the reserve requirement rate and at the risk of reducing foreign exchange reserves, but also warned of too high a fiscal deficit and the irrational structure of budget expenditures. I also estimated that an appropriate combinationof m monetary and fiscal measures could free up the financial potential of, recalculated, around 802 billion to be channelled into the economy by the end of that year. 5. In doing so, the CNB started from the following principles: (a) it should act quickly; (b) efficiently in termsof achieving the greatest multi-quantitative effects in the short term; (c) focused on long-term problems (balance of payments, inodug); (d) focused on investments; (e) social fairness (private sector, unemployed, pensioners), although this is not explicitly navedeno at the time, it is obvious that it was primarily about supporting the manufacturing and manufacturing services sectors, rather than investments in infrastructure. The meeting did not end with a concrete conclusion, but "the cards were put on the table". 6. The rebalancing of ProraCun for 2009 and the adoption of the 2010 Budget followed, which, however, did not bring about substantive changes in the fiscal position. Nevertheless, the CNB announces a reduction in the reserve requirement rate in 2010 from 14% to 11% and on this basis the release of liquidity of about HRK 9 million. A third of this was realized immediately, and the rest is conditioned by the elaboration of the mechanism of efficient use of these funds for lending to the enterprise sector and concrete results in their application. 7. The Ministry of Finance, HBOR and banks define models A and B, which, however, have not proven to be particularly successful in practice. Out of the initially received HRK 2 billion for model A, HBOR effectively engaged only HRK 855 million in 2010, while the application of model B was not even started. 8. Monetary developments in 2010 Nevertheless, even in such conditions, there has been a revival of the credit market over the past year. After stagnation (-0.4%) in 2009, total bank placements increased by 7.5% in 2010 (increase in 19 billion), under which placements to enterprises by 8.8% and to the state by 14.7%, while real placements to the population (due to chf appreciation) mostly stagnated (real decline by 1.4%). Such growth in loans also resulted in ml growth by 4.2% (in 2009 -14.6%) and M4 by 4.4% (-0.9%). However, as changes in monetarydevelopments were not accompanied by other activities, in parallel with the growth of loans and liquidity, "bad placements" also grew by 51%, increasing their share of total placements from 7.8% to 11.2%. In this, in loans to enterprises, the share of bad placements increases from 12.9% to 17.9%, and in the population from 5.8% to 7.8%. This increases credit risk and slows down the supply of loans to the private sector, and also has a limiting effect on the possibility of an interest rate cut, despite a significant reduction in the "regulatory cost". In parallel, increased caution is also present in the sphere of savings (up 4.5%) in which foreign currency deposits increased by 9.0%, while kuna deposits decreased by 11.0% and at the end of 2010 they were 30% lower than in 2008. This continues the currency substitution (foreign currency savings and total savings) from 70% (2008) to 78% (2009) and 81 % (2010), highlighting the issue of maintaining currency compliance between assets and bank passives. 9. January-March 2011 All this affects the slowdown in loan growth in the first quarter of 2011, the annual rate of which decreased to 6.1%, resulting in both slower annual growth in Ml (2.3%) and M4 (3.1%) than achieved in the last year. 10. The general situation at the turn of the last year 95 After a sharp decline in economic activity during 2009 and in the first pole even in2010, it is now in a phase of relative stagnation. 95 However, this stagnation is not sectorally homogeneous and therefore not stable. 95 Particularly unfavourable is the further decline in industrial production, while construction remains in a deep depression. 95 Their only positivepulse comes from the growth of exports of goods and services (in 2010, two-thirds of its decline in 2009), but it is still insufficient to provide a stronger impulse to overall growth. 95 Acceleration of inflation: in 2011 , 111/XI11.8% as in the whole of 2010, so that the annual inflation staincreased from 1.8% in 2010 to 2.6% in March 2011, and the average annual from 1.1% to 2.1%. As in In 2008, the main generators of acceleration of inflation are the prices of food and liquid fuels, which is justified by the movement of prices on the world market, while again neglecting the issue of concessions on domestic oil and problems in the subsidy system in agriculture. 11. Adaptation to the crisis The decline in foreign savings inflows (from 9.8% of GDP in 2008 to 5.0% in 2009 and to just 0.8% in 2010) and hencethe d of domestic investments and final consumption led to a decrease in imports, and the current account deficit of the balance of payments decreased from 9.1% (2008) to 5.5% (2009) and 1.4% of GDP (2010). Conversely, the consolidated general government deficit increases from 2.6% (2008) to 5.3% (2009 and 2010), with an indication of further growth in 2011111111111. In this situation in the real sector and in relations in the credit market, the CNB at the end of last year deemed it necessary to further increase the liquidity of the financial system. Given the problems in models A and B, as well as the previous effects of the displacement of the private sector in the loan market by the state, the introduction of a new instrument - an open market operation based on government bonds - was considered as one of the channels for inserting new liquidity. Buyingthese bonds from banks' portfolios would actually temporarily monetise some of the public debt, which would free up an appropriate portion of banks' credit potential for private sector lending. This was cautiously announced at the conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange inthe newspaper opadu, but after the adoption of the State Budget for 2011, it had to be abandoned. That is why another, more direct way was chosen - lowering the rate of minimum required foreign exchange receivables from 20% to 17%, which should act on reducing interest rates andreducing risk aversion, both on the supply side and on the demand side for loans. At the same time, in the same function, the renumber rate was reduced from 0.5% to 0.25%, which also reduced the interest rate on overnight deposits of banks with the CNB. We have previously issuedor spoken to banks and entrepreneurs to examine their response to such a measure, and the Government has been indirectly informed about it. 13. The current situation - key issues and the international context The views of the European Commission and the European Central Bank for the resolutionof the ovore on the Pre-accession Economic Programme to be held on 17 May (the ATTITUDES of the IMF are similar). Assessment of the policy so far: (1) Adequate response of the CNB to economic and financial opportunities during the crisis through loosening of monetary policy andsufficient liquidity created. (2) The usefulness of the selected exchange rate policy in conditions of high euroisation of the financial system and balance sheet risks. As for future developments, four issues stand out: (1) Rising inflation requires particular caution, in particular related to a potential second round of effects. (This primarily refers to the impact of inflation on the real prices of factors, interest rates and exchange rates, but also to the limitations in stimulating domestic demand through monetary measures.); (2) Despite the reduction of the current account deficit, the country's external vulnerability has increased as the disparity between exchange rate movements and domestic costs undermines the country's competitive capacity on international markets. Efforts should therefore be stepped up to limit wage growth (lower than productivity growth) and to implementother medium and long-term measures to strengthen competitiveness; (3) Fiscal consolidation and structural reforms are necessary to establish sustainable growth. Maintaining the budget deficit at 2010 and 2011 levels opens up the possibility for public debt to become unsustainable. This would further increase external indebtedness and limit domestic financing opportunities for the private sector. Implementation of the Economic Recovery Programme and the Fiscal Responsibility Act is essential; (4) The CNB and other authorities are encouragedto continue their efforts to reduce the use of the currency clause in deposits and loans. It increases credit risk, while large balance sheet effects make it impossible to use the exchange rate as a means of adjustment. This means for the CNB that it de facto maintains a high capital requirementon the basis of currency-induced credit risk and under the conditions of application of Basel 3 - which does not include such risk in the calculation of capital adequacy. Thus, through individual solutions, the CNB effectively increases the minimum capital adequacy rate of banks from 12% to 14%. law on mandatory relations is beyond the CNB's jurisdiction. Similar assessments are made by other financial institutions. For example, fitch highlights five basic problems of the Croatian economy: 95 insufficient fiscal consolidation without which there is no reduction in the fiscal deficit 95 rapidly rising public debt 95 below-average growth of GDP 95 high foreign exchange exposure of the public and private sectors 95 high foreign indebtedness. Such assessments should not be underestimated, especially not in the context of the fact that foreign financing needs amount to 8017.9 billion (38.4% of GDP) this year, which is 802 billion more than in 2010, and that the country's unfavourable rating can have a significant impact on that financing and its cost. 14. Forecast 2011 The rest of the year is expected to accelerate the credit activity of banks, with a growth in total placements of about 9.5% (an increase of HRK 26 billion), in which placements to businesses and households grew byabout 7% (up 17 billion). This should contribute to halting the current tendency of falling domestic demand and investment, which - with real growth in exports of goods and services of about 4% - could result in GDP growth in 2011 of about 1%. Due to the simultaneousgrowth of imports, a certain increase in the balance of payments deficit to about 2.5% of GDP can be expected, while foreign debt (excluding "circular investments") would stabilise at the level of about 46 billion euros. At the same time, the deficit of the consolidated general government (including HAC) will be about 6% of GDP. The average exchange rate of the kuna against the euro will be around 7.40, while the average inflation rate could be around 3%. Thus, in 2011, some positive developments can be expected, but - as we estimated two years ago - the recovery of the Croatian economy will be long and slow. Did it really have to be that way? I hope that this presentation can also provide part of the answer to that question.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna politika Objavljeno: 6.5.2011. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 5.5.2011. 14. znanstveno-struna konferencija Hrvatsko novano trite Opatija 5.5.2011. 1. Godinama se ve sastajemo u ovoj ili slinim dvoranama i razgovaramo o razvoju ekonomske situacije u Hrvatskoj te o politici centralne banke. Kako se ta situacija dramatino mijenjala, tako se mijenjao i sadraj te naglasci u tim razgovorima, kao i percepcija onoga to HNB radi i zato to radi. 2. U razdoblju prije krize raspravom su dominirala pitanja brzog rasta inozemnog duga, kreditne ekspanzije u zemlji, visokog dvojnog deficita, rasta cijena na tritima vrijednosnih papira i nekretnina, eksterne ranjivosti zemlje te rizika vanjskog oka. Djelovanje centralne banke bilo je u takvim uvjetima obiljeeno zaotravanjem prudencijalnih i implementacijom administrativnih mjera u funkciji smanjenja profitabilnosti inozemnih izvora sredstava i destimuliranja ekspanzivne ponude kredita iz tih sredstava. 3. Izbijanjem krize efektuirali su se spomenuti rizici (zaustavljanje priljeva kapitala, pad inozemne potranje), to je ugrozilo cijeli financijski sustav. Raspravama dominira pitanje kako sprijeiti uruavanje tog sustava, u okviru ega posebno: kako odrati eksternu likvidnost drave (prijetnja moratorija), sprijeiti kreditni slom uzemlji te zadrati stabilnost teaja, ne samo zbog zatite dunika nego i zbog opasnosti odljeva tednje. HNB ukida ili bitno ublaava restriktivne mjere, ime se u sustav ubacuje dodatna likvidnost od oko 4,5 milijardi eura. 4. Konsolidacijom financijskog sustava teite se prebacuje na pitanje podrke realnom sektoru, odnosno s pitanja ograniavanja potranje prelazi se na pitanje poticanja ponude usklaenim djelovanjem monetarne i fiskalne politike. To je bio predmet mog prvog razgovora s predsjednicom Vlade u srpnju 2009. godine. U njemu sam izrazio spremnost HNB-a za daljnje sputanje stope obvezne priuve i uz rizik smanjenja deviznih rezervi, ali i upozorio na previsok fiskalni deficit te neracionalnu strukturu proraunskih rashoda. Iznio sam i procjenu da bi se odgovarajuom kombinacijom monetarnih i fiskalnih mjera mogao do kraja te godine osloboditi financijski potencijal od, preraunato, oko 2 milijarde eura koji bi se usmjerio u gospodarstvo. 5. Pri tome je HNB polazio od slijedeih naela: (a) treba djelovati brzo; (b) efikasno u smislu ostvarenja najveih multiplikativnih efekata u kratkom roku; (c) usmjereno na dugorone probleme (platna bilanca, inodug); (d) fokusirano na investicije; (e) socijalno pravedno (privatni sektor, nezaposleni, umirovljenici), lako to tada nije izriito navedeno, oito je da se prije svega mislilo na podrku preraivakoj industriji i sektoru proizvodnih usluga, a ne na investicije u infrastrukturu. Sastanak nije zavrio konkretnim zakljukom, ali su "karte stavljene na stol". 6. Uslijedili su rebalans Prorauna za 2009. i donoenje Prorauna za 2010. koji, meutim, nisu donijeli sutinske promjene fiskalne pozicije. Unato tome, HNB najavljuje smanjenje stope obvezne priuve u 2010. godini sa 14% na 11% i po toj osnovi oslobaanje likvidnosti od oko 9 milijardi kuna. Treina toga realizirana je odmah, a ostatak je uvjetovan razradom mehanizma efikasnog koritenja tih sredstava za kreditiranje sektora poduzea i konkretnim rezultatima u njihovoj primjeni. 7. Ministarstvo financija, HBOR i banke definiraju modele A i B, koji se, meutim, nisu u praksi pokazali posebno uspjenima. HBOR je od inicijalno primljenih 2 milijarde kuna za model A efektivno angairao tijekom 2010. godine samo 855 milijuna kuna, dok primjena modela B nije ni zapoeta. 8. Monetarna kretanja u 2010. Ipak, i u takvim uvjetima, dolo je tijekom prole godine do oivljavanja trita kredita. Nakon stagnacije (-0,4%) u 2009., ukupni plasmani banaka porasli su u 2010. godini za 7,5% (prirast 19 milijardi), u okviru ega plasmani poduzeima za 8,8%, a dravi za 14,7%, dok su realni plasmani stanovnitvu (zbog aprecijacije CHF) uglavnom stagnirali (realni pad za 1,4%). Takav rast kredita rezultirao je i rastom Ml za 4,2% (u 2009. -14,6%) te M4 za 4,4% (-0,9%). Meutim, kako promjene u monetarnim kretanjima nisu bile praene ostalim aktivnostima, usporedno s rastom kredita i likvidnosti rastu i "loi plasmani" za 51% ime se njihov udio u ukupnim plasmanima poveava s 7,8% na 11,2%. U tome, kod kredita poduzeima udio loih plasmana raste s 12,9% na 17,9%, a kod stanovnitva s 5,8% na 7,8%. To poveava kreditni rizik i usporava ponudu kredita privatnom sektoru, a ograniavajue djeluje i na mogunost smanjenja kamatnih stopa, unato znatnom smanjenju "regulacijskog troka". Usporedno s time, poveani oprez prisutan je i u sferi tednje (rast za 4,5%) u kojoj su devizni depoziti porasli za 9,0%, dok su kunski depoziti smanjeni za 11,0% i krajem 2010. za 30% su bili nii nego 2008. godine. Time se nastavlja valutna supstitucija (devizna tednja I ukupna tednja) sa 70% (2008.) na 78% (2009.) i 81 % (2010.), to naglaava pitanje odravanja valutne usklaenosti izmeu aktive i pasive banaka. 9. Sijeanj-oujak 2011. Sve to utjee na usporavanje rasta kredita u prvom tromjeseju 2011., ija godinja stopa je smanjena na 6,1%, to rezultira i sporijim godinjim rastom Ml (2,3%) i M4 (3,1%) od ostvarenog u proloj godini. 10. Opa situacija na prijelazu iz prole u ovu godinu  Nakon otrog pada ekonomske aktivnosti tijekom 2009. i u prvoj polovini 2010. godine, ona je sada u fazi relativne stagnacije.  Meutim, ta stagnacija nije sektorski homogena pa time ni stabilna.  Posebno nepovoljan je daljnji pad industrijske proizvodnje, dok je graevinarstvo i dalje u dubokoj depresiji.  Jedini pozitivni impuls dolazi od rasta izvoza roba i usluga (u 2010. nadoknaeno je 2/3 njegovog pada u 2009.), ali je on jo nedostatan da prui snaniji impuls ukupnom rastu.  Ubrzanje inflacije: 2011. godine 111/XI11,8% kao i u cijeloj 2010. godini, tako da je godinja stopa inflacije poveana s 1,8% u 2010. na 2,6% u oujku 2011. godine, a prosjena godinja s 1,1 % na 2,1 %. Kao i u 2008. godini, osnovni generatori ubrzanja inflacije su cijene hrane i tekuih goriva, to se opravdava kretanjem cijena na svjetskom tritu, pri emu se ponovno zanemaruje pitanje koncesija na domau naftu i problemi u sustavu subvencija u poljoprivredi. 11. Prilagodba krizi Pad priljeva inozemne tednje (s 9,8% BDP-a u 2008. na 5,0% u 2009. i na samo 0,8% u 2010.) i otuda pad domaih investicija i finalne potronje doveli su do smanjenja uvoza, pa je deficit tekueg rauna platne bilance smanjen s 9,1% (2008.) na 5,5% (2009.) i 1,4% BDP-a (2010.). Suprotno tome, deficit konsolidirane ope drave poveanje s 2,6% (2008.) na 5,3% (2009. i 2010.), s naznakom daljnjeg rasta u 2011.12. U takvoj situaciji u realnom sektoru te odnosima na tritu kredita, HNB je krajem prole godine ocijenio potrebnim dodatno poveati likvidnost financijskog sustava. S obzirom na probleme u modelima A i B, kao i prethodne efekte istiskivanja privatnog sektora na tritu kredita od strane drave, kao jedan od kanala za ubacivanje nove likvidnosti razmatralo se uvoenje novog instrumenta - operacije na otvorenom tritu na bazi dravnih obveznica. Otkupom tih obveznica iz portfelja banaka zapravo bi se privremeno monetizirao dio javnog duga, to bi oslobodilo odgovarajui dio kreditnog potencijala banaka za kreditiranje privatnog sektora. To je oprezno najavljeno i na konferenciji Zagrebake burze u listopadu, ali se nakon usvajanja Dravnog prorauna za 2011. od toga moralo odustati. Zato je izabran drugi, izravniji nain - sputanje stope minimalno potrebnih deviznih potraivanja sa 20% na 17% to bi trebalo djelovati na smanjenje kamatnih stopa te umanjenje averzije prema riziku, i na strani ponude i na strani potranje za kreditima. Istodobno je, u istoj funkciji, smanjena i stopa renumeracije sa 0,5% na 0,25%, ime je smanjena i kamatna stopa na prekonone depozite banaka kod HNB-a. Prethodno smo obavili razgovore s bankama i poduzetnicima da bi ispitali njihovu reakciju na takvu mjeru, a Vlada je o tome bila indirektno obavijetena. 13. Sadanja situacija - kljuna pitanja i meunarodni kontekst Stavovi Europske komisije i Europske sredinje banke za razgovore o Pretpristupnom ekonomskom programu koji e se odrati 17. svibnja (slini su i stavovi MMF-a). Ocjena dosadanje politike: (1) Primjerena reakcija HNB-a na ekonomske i financijske prilike tijekom krize putem labavljenja monetarne politike i kreiranja dostatne likvidnosti. (2) Korisnost odabrane teajne politike u uvjetima visoke euriziranosti financijskog sustava i bilannih rizika. to se tie buduih kretanja, istiu se etiri pitanja: (1) Porast inflacije zahtijeva poseban oprez, posebno povezano s potencijalnim drugim krugom uinaka. (Pri tome se prvenstveno misli na utjecaj inflacije na realne cijene faktora, kamatne stope i teaj, ali i ogranienja u poticanju domae potranje monetarnim mjerama.); (2) Unato smanjenju deficita tekueg rauna, vanjska ranjivost zemlje je poveana jer disparitet izmeu kretanja teaja i domaih trokova umanjuje konkurentsku sposobnost zemlje na meunarodnim tritima. Zato treba pojaati napore na ograniavanju rasta plaa (niim od rasta produktivnosti) i provoenju ostalih srednjoronih i dugoronih mjera za jaanje konkurentnosti; (3) Fiskalna konsolidacija i strukturne reforme nune su za uspostavljanje odrivog rasta. Odravanje proraunskog deficita na razinama iz 2010. i 2011. otvara mogunost da javni dug postane neodriv. Time bi se dodatno poveala vanjska zaduenost i ograniile mogunosti domaeg financiranja privatnog sektora. Kljuna je provedba Programa gospodarskog oporavka i Zakona o fiskalnoj odgovornosti; (4) HNB i ostala tijela vlasti se ohrabruju da nastave napore na smanjenju upotrebe valutne klauzule u depozitima i kreditima. Ona poveava kreditni rizik, dok veliki bilanni uinci onemoguuju upotrebu teaja kao sredstva prilagodbe. To za HNB znai da de facto zadri visoke kapitalske zahtjeve po osnovi valutno induciranog kreditnog rizika i u uvjetima primjene Basela 3 - koji takav rizik ne ukljuuje u izraun adekvatnosti kapitala. Tako, kroz pojedinana rjeenja HNB efektivno poveava minimalnu stopu adekvatnosti kapitala banaka s 12% na 14%. to se tie eventualne zabrane primjene valutne klauzule na kredite, to je pitanje regulirano u lanku 21. i 22. Zakona o obveznim odnosima i izvan je ingerencije HNB-a. Sline ocjene iznose i druge financijske institucije. Tako, primjerice, agencija Fitch istie pet osnovnih problema hrvatske ekonomije:  nedovoljna fiskalna konsolidacija bez koje nema smanjenja fiskalnog deficita  brzo rastui javni dug  ispodprosjeni rastGDP-a  visoka devizna izloenost javnog i privatnog sektora  visoka inozemna zaduenost. Takve ocjene ne treba podcjenjivati, posebno ne u kontekstu injenice da potrebe inozemnog financiranja iznose u ovoj godini 17,9 milijardi eura (38,4% BDP-a), to je za 2 milijarde eura vie nego u 2010. godini, i da nepovoljan rejting zemlje moe znatno utjecati na to financiranje i njegovu cijenu. 14. Prognoza 2011. U nastavku godine oekuje se ubrzanje kreditne aktivnosti banaka, uz rast ukupnih plasmana od oko 9,5% (prirast 26 milijardi kuna), u emu rast plasmana poduzeima i stanovnitvu od oko 7% (prirast 17 milijardi). To bi trebalo pridonijeti zaustavljanju dosadanje tendencije pada domae potranje i investicija, to bi - uz realni rast izvoza roba i usluga od oko 4% - moglo rezultirati rastom BDP-a u 2011. godini od oko 1%. Zbog istodobnog rasta uvoza, moe se oekivati odreeno poveanje deficita platne bilance na oko 2,5% BDP-a, dok bi se inozemni dug (bez "krunih ulaganja") stabilizirao na razini od oko 46 milijardi eura. Istodobno, deficit konsolidirane ope drave (ukljuujui HAC) iznosit e oko 6% BDP-a. Prosjeni teaj kune prema euru kretat e se oko 7,40, dok bi prosjena stopa inflacije mogla iznositi oko 3%. Dakle, u 2011. godini mogu se oekivati odreeni pozitivni pomaci, ali e - kao to smo jo prije dvije godine procjenjivali - oporavak hrvatske ekonomije biti dug i spor. Da li je ba moralo tako biti? Nadam se da i ovo izlaganje moe pruiti dio odgovora na to pitanje.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary policy
text: Monetary policy Published: 11.5.2012. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 10.5.2012. 15th Scientific and Professional Conference Croatian Money Market Opatija 10.5.2012. 1. Six months ago, at a conference of similar content to this one, the tendencies and characteristics of the economic situation were discussed at the turn of last year. Contrary to the pre-election and some post-election announcements of a "path of rapid recovery", it was then assessed that 2011 was a year of stagnation, but not inflection, since it did not establish adequate impulses to sustainable growth, nor can they be established quickly and "painlessly". That's why 2012 will be another year of strong constraints and challenges of dealing with these limitations. 2. The basic limitations in this regard are: (a) External limitations. 95 the return of the recession to the EC (reflecting on foreign demand, mobility and the cost of capital); 95 problems in the banking system, which include its insufficient capitalisation, reduced liquidity and high exposure of parent banks to the region, which also has an impact on the business policies of subsidiaries banks (LDR and si.) (b) The collapse of investment activity in the country. In the last three years, investments have decreased by 28% in total, which has also reduced their share of GDP from 29% (2008) to 23%(2011). There are several reasons for this, and their basic financial aspect is reflected in the substantial decrease in the flowof VA foreign capital from 9.5% of GDP (2008) to only 1.1% (2011), so that investment activity is reduced to a level of stagnant and realistic factors of limited domestic savings (about 20% of GDP). From there, the launch of a new investment cycle implies a very active policy of attracting foreign capital on "sound grounds" with a certain redistribution of domestic sources from consumption by investment. However, many problems and social and political resistance to such a policy are still very pronounced, (c) Youjuice external vulnerability. Although a significant decrease in imports reduced the balance of payments deficit from 9.1% (2008) to 1.0% (2011), thus stabilising foreign debt, its level of about 100% of GDP resulting in high gross foreign financing needs of the Croatian economy of about 18 billion euros per year (38% of GDP). This limits the "number of degrees of freedom" in the conduct of economic policy and Croatia cannot afford to make moves that financial markets would perceive as a step towards destabilizing the economy and withless creditworthiness. The recent successful issue of government bonds was based precisely on assurances about future positive changes in macroeconomic policy, while on the micro-level of enterprises they continue to face a high-risk problem that also affects the high cost of foreign financing. The example of Agrokor clearly confirms this (9.8%). (d) The need for fiscal consolidation. The absence of structural reforms results in a doubling of the deficit of the consolidated general government involving HAC from 3.0% (2008) to 5.8% of BPD (2011)/according to the ESA 95 methodology from 1.4% to 5.1% of BDPa/, and public debt (including HAC) from 34% to 52% of GDP, with a tendency to grow further in 2012 and 2013 above 60% of GDP Fiscal adjustment (through the Fiscal Responsibility Act) and the broader consolidation of the public sector, which also includes a policy of increasing prices with accompanying effects on inflationary income taxation, implies a continued tendency towards a real decline in the disposable income of the population. 3. All these restrictions thenresulted in the assessment that in 2012 it would be difficult to maintain the level of production and employment from the previous year. This only further emphasized the urgency of the need, after three years of "non-empowerment", to finally approach more radical changes in the economic system and politics in order to begin to create substantive assumptions for changing negative tendencies in the coming years. 4. Economic developments in the first quarter of this year clearly demonstrate the correctness of such forecasts. These are primarily marked by the continuation of the acumenof the decline in industrial production (-5.3% year-on-year), the additional contraction of construction activity (-11.7%), the decline in goods exports to EU countries (-2.0%) and total exports (- 0.9%), the decrease in employment (- 0.8%) and the increase in the unemployment rate to 20%, i.e. the gradual acceleration of current inflation (2.0%) based on the increase in energy prices (6.5%). Retail sales are stagnant in real terms, while positive results have only been achieved in tourism (11.4%) increase in overnight stays, with a seasonal marginal splitof bland. 5. Although such developments in the first quarter do not have to be significant for the aggregate picture of the whole year (for seasonal reasons, time-lie between the timing of the undertaking and the effect of certain economic policy measures, etc.), it is unlikely that thedevelopments in the d mock quarter will differ significantly from those in the first quarter, in which conditions even a gradual change in tendencies in the second part of the year can no longer change the sign of key aggregate indicators for the whole of 2012. We estimate that in it GDP will be in real terms lower than last year's by about 1%, determined by an aggregate decrease in domestic consumption by 0.8% and exports of goods and services by 1.2%, with stagnation of investments and imports. The balance of payments deficit will rise from 1% to 2% of GDP (from 450m to about 900m euros). euro), which will also adequately increase foreign debt to the level of about 102% of GDP, but - assuming the credit rating is maintained - it is assessed that foreign liabilities will be able to be refinanced under the current conditions. If the announced fiscal policy measures are implemented, the deficit of the consolidated general government (including HAC) will decrease from 5.8% to about 5% of GDP, while public debt will reach 56% of GDP. Bank placements will increase by about 5%, while current inflation will accelerate from last year's 2.1% to about 3.5% this year, although these predictions are not "glaring" from the point of view of social expectations and political promises, they are not even "tragic", if in the meantime the interaction of economic policy and concrete procedures of economic entities begins to establish basic assumptionsand impulses of sustainable future growth and development. 5. What is the role of monetary policy in this? Recently, it was reported in a daily newspaper that in order to get out of the crisis", another taboo topic should be broken: monetary policy so far .... Fresh money simply has to be squeezed into the economy as they do in the US and England, for example. Without an additional financial injection, the vast majority of companies of the current austerity measures and the decline in purchasing power, will not survive... Frightening and mindless dand today there is as much as HRK 6bn less in circulation than in 2009." This is not about any taboo subject, but about a substantive ignorance of the facts and a misunderstanding of the real situation. When journalists who don't specialize in economic issues say that, it'salosnoyant. However, when university professors with clearly identifiable motives say this, then it is tragic. Not so much for them personally as for their students. 7. So what kind of monetary policy does the HNB run? This policy has passed in the last ten years twoand very different periods. (a) Before the crisis, monetary policy was moderately restrictive and aimed at disincentivizing its strong foreign borrowing of banks and transforming foreign exchange funds acquired on this basis into expansionary growth in domestic loans. It was a necessary response to a substantial increase in the balance of payments deficit, the rapid growth of foreign debt, the formation of a bubble in the securities and real estate markets and, worst of all, the creation of an illusion about the possibilities of permanent growth of consumption and standards onthe basis of relatively favorable and easily accessible foreign loans. The CNB was then subjected to strong internal and external criticism that lasted until the global financial crisis erupted. Only then did it be seen that it was this policy that made it possible to formreserves, which even in the conditions of the general crisis retained financial stability, liquidity in payments to foreign countries and averted credit breakdown. In addition, combined with a stable exchange rate and relatively low inflation, such a policy also resulted in a gradualaffirmation of the domestic currency macia, and the share of foreign currency deposits in the M4 structure decreased from 64.2% at the end of the 2000 at 52.1% at the end of 2008, and the share of total deposits from 71.2% to 57.0%. (b) With hints, and then with the effective outbreak of the financial crisis in the second half of 2008, monetary policy in Croatia is fundamentally changing and becoming extremely expansionary. Since then, the CNB has adopted 18 measures that directly affected the change in liquidity of the banking system and which netly released EUR 6.3 billion. Euros. At the same time, byintercourse on the foreign exchange market, the CNB purchased 801.4 billion from banks and the state net, emitting HRK 10.1 billion, so that (by balancing these two types of monetary operations), the CNB has net-freed the liquidity of the banking system in andexfoliating from, recalculated, about HRK 46 billion from mid-2008 to the present day. This is the equivalent of 83% of the money mass and 21% of the total liquid assets in Croatia 2008, and corresponds to the amount of 13.5% of GDP from that year. If it is borne in mind that these funds are not engaged in Croatiato cover the losses of the banking sector, as has been the case in other countries, the real expansion of our monetary policy was no less than in countries cited as an example of strong monetary impulses. 8. Thus , increased liquidity is primarily used and is used in two functions. In the function of maintaining the external liquidity of the country in conditions when, by halting the inflow of foreign capital, the repayment of principal and interest on foreign debt has become greater than the use of novih loans. Thus, in 2010 and 2011, net repayments of foreign loan annuities totalled EUR 1.6 billion. euro, part of which was repaid by converting debt into capital and part of it from the current liquidity of the banking system. If current h payments are added to this, the net foreign assets of the banking system have decreased by around 801.1bn (by about 20%) in the last three years, with this tendency continuing this year. Nevertheless, this has not been more strongly reflected in the country's foreign exchange liquidity and currency exchange rate, which govploughs into successfully maintaining the stability of the system. In the function of alimony of banks' credit activity, with the total placements of our banks growing from 2009 to 2011 at an average annual rate of 5.5%, against a growth in euro zone loans of only 1.5%. Similar developments are expected this year, so there is no question of any credit crunch, although problems with credit collection have since increased significantly. 9. If such developments in the monetary sphere are linked to those in the real sector, the question logically arises as to why the growth of monetary aggregates has not had a greater impact on the movement of production and under what conditions it could have in the future. There are two important aspects: 95 state behavior 95 transformation of freed liquidity into loans to the real sector. (a) Although not to workon the classic crowding-out effect, the fact is that in times of crisis and uncertainty the state presents banks with a more desirable customer than the private sector. Accordingly, out of the total increase in bank placements between 2009 and 2011 in the amount of HRK 44.6 billion, HRK 16.5 billion (or 37%) was used by the state, whose share in the structure of total bank placements increased from 8.5% (2008) to 12.8% (2011), with a tendency to grow further this year to 13.5%. This is of course a direct consequence of the increased budget deficit in the meantime, where, due to its structure, budget expenditures have had a relatively low multi-quantitative impact on the production and employment of the entire economy. (b) In terms of placement to the real sector, the problem is completely different in nature. Theseplacements r astu at an average annual rate of 3.8%, which is entirely the result of the growth of loans to the company sector (7.1% per year), while the demand for loans of the population sector stagnates, easily these indicators also include the effects of reprogramming liabilities, the achieved growth of loans to the corporate sector is not negligible, but it is of course not enough to substitute the absence of foreign capital in the face of declining production and increasing unit costs. That is why the CNB has been trying to encourage faster growth of these loans all the time while reducing interest rates, but the results so far have been weaker than expected. This applies to both the so-called 2010 Model A and the unintended liquidity release of 2011. In 2015, the same problems arose in both cases: aversion to the riskof banks, customers and the state as intermediaries, the preference of short-term over long-term interests, and the lack of quality production programs that would be financed from such loans. That is why the released liquidity was slow to turn into new loans, while part of it was also used for other purposes, which forced the central bank to withdraw this part of liquidity. These problems persist, as illustrated by the fact that the originally proposed programme of more favourable lending to the economy this year of HRK 12bn (of which the CNB measures would be exempted from HRK 9bn) on the request of banks reduced to the amount of about HRK 8bn, in which the CNB's liquidity-free measures participate with HRK 7bn, and other bank funds with only HRK 1bn. 10. Thus, the essence of the problem is not, as some think, in the insufficient expansion of monetary policy, but in the unfavorable modalities of the formation of supply and demand for loans, that is, in an insufficiently efficient transformation, initially increasingnot liquidity into financial means that will drive production and employment. This is also the fact that in the last three years, when increasing primary money by a total of 25.4%, the cash mass has decreased by 4.3% at the same time, so that the monetary multiplierof the kator has fallen below 1 (from 1.11 in 2008 to 0.82 in 2011), while the net conversion of kunas to foreign currency deposits returns the degree of euroisation of the financial system to levels from the late 1990s. Until these substantive problems begin to be seriously addressed, and this implies further consolidation and rationalization of the public sector, improvement of the system of debt collection and protection of creditors, simplification of the process of entry and exit of economic entities from the market, removing obstacles to the realization of investment services, encouraging greater entrepreneurialism of the private sector, etc., there will continue to be limited flow and bottlenecks in financial flows, which will slow down circulation and hamper the efficient allocation of funds towards productions that can havethe greatest effects for the overall economy. This is not helped by any "throwing money out of helicopters" or "revolutionary" ideas about direct lending of production programs by the central bank, but only long-sought reforms and resulting structuralchanges in the modalities of the functioning of the overall economy. The government is aware of this, and I believe most economists who take a closer look at the state of the Croatian economy and do not slave to cliche9s from other times and different situations. (c) CROATIAN NATIONAL BANKA
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna politika Objavljeno: 11.5.2012. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 10.5.2012. 15. znanstveno-struna konferencija Hrvatsko novano trite Opatija 10.5.2012. 1. Prije est mjeseci, na konferenciji slinog sadraja kao i ova, raspravljalo se o tendencijama i obiljejima ekonomske situacije na prijelazu iz prole u ovu godinu. Suprotno predizbornim i nekim postizbornim najavama o "putu brzog oporavka", tada je ocijenjeno da je 2011. bila godina stagnacije, ali ne i infleksije, budui da u njoj nisu uspostavljeni odgovarajui impulsi odrivom rastu, niti se oni mogu brzo i "bezbolno" uspostaviti. Zato e 2012. biti jo jedna godina snanih ogranienja i izazova suoavanja s tim ogranienjima. 2. Osnovna ogranienja u tom smislu su: (a) Eksterna ogranienja.  povratak recesije u EZ (s odrazom na inozemnu potranju, mobilnost i cijenu kapitala);  problemi u bankarskom sustavu koji obuhvaaju njegovu nedovoljnu kapitaliziranost, smanjenu likvidnost te visoku izloenost matinih banaka prema regiji, to ima utjecaj i na poslovne politike banaka-keri (LDR i si.) (b) Kolaps investicijske aktivnosti u zemlji. U posljednje tri godine investicije su ukupno smanjene za 28%, ime je smanjen i njihov udio u BDP-u s 29% (2008) na 23%(2011). Tome je vie razloga, a njihov osnovni financijski aspekt ogleda se u bitnom smanjenju priljeva inozemnog kapitala sa 9.5% BDP-a (2008) na samo 1.1 % (2011), tako da je investicijska aktivnost svedena na razinu stagnirajue i realnim initeljima ograniene domae tednje (oko 20% BDP-a). Otuda, pokretanje novog investicijskog ciklusa podrazumijeva vrlo aktivnu politiku privlaenja stranog kapitala na "zdravim osnovama" uz odreenu preraspodjelu domaih izvora s potronje prema investicijama. Meutim, brojni problemi te socijalni i politiki otpori takvoj politici jo su uvijek vrlo izraeni, (c) Visoka vanjska ranjivost. lako je znaajnim smanjenjem uvoza deficit platne bilance smanjen sa 9.1 % (2008) na 1.0% (2011) ime je stabiliziran i inozemni dug, njegova razina od oko 100% BDP-a rezultira visokom potrebama bruto inozemnog financiranja hrvatske ekonomije u iznosu od oko 18 mlrd. eura godinje (38% BDP-a). To ograniava "broj stupnjeva slobode" u voenju ekonomske politike te si Hrvatska ne moe dopustiti poteze koje bi financijska trita percipirala kao korak prema destabilizaciji ekonomije i smanjenju njezine kreditne sposobnosti. Nedavno uspjeno izdanje dravnih obveznica temeljilo se upravo na uvjeravanjima o buduim pozitivnim promjenama u makroekonomskoj politici, dok se na mikrorazini poduzea i dalje suoavaju s problemom visokog rizika koji utjee i na visoku cijenu inozemnog financiranja. Primjer Agrokora to jasno potvruje (9.8%). (d) Potreba fiskalne konsolidacije. Izostanak strukturnih reformi rezultira udvostruenjem deficita konsolidirane ope drave u koju je ukljuen i HAC sa 3.0% (2008) na 5.8% BPD-a (2011)/po metodologiji ESA 95 sa 1.4 na 5.1% BDPa/, te javnog duga (ukljuujui HAC) sa 34% na 52% BDP-a, s tendencijom daljeg rasta u 2012. i 2013. godini iznad 60% BDP-a Fiskalna prilagodba (kroz Zakon o fiskalnoj odgovornosti) te ira konsolidacija javnog sektora, koja ukljuuje i politiku poveanja cijena s popratnim uincima na inflacijsko oporezivanje dohodaka, implicira nastavak tendencije realnog pada raspoloivog dohotka stanovnitva. 3. Sva ta ogranienja rezultirala su tada predvianjem da e u 2012. godini biti teko odrati razinu proizvodnje i zaposlenosti iz prethodne godine. To je samo jo vie naglasilo urgentnost potrebe da se, nakon tri godine "nesnalaenja", konano pristupi radikalnijim promjenama u ekonomskom sustavu i politici kako bi se poele stvarati sutinske pretpostavke za promjenu negativnih tendencija u narednim godinama. 4. Ekonomska kretanja u prvom tromjeseju ove godine jasno pokazuju ispravnost takvih predvianja. Njih prvenstveno obiljeava nastavak tendencije pada industrijske proizvodnje (-5.3% na godinjoj razini), dodatna kontrakcija graevinske aktivnosti (-11.7%), pad robnog izvoza u zemlje EU (-2.0%) i ukupnog izvoza (- 0.9%), smanjenje zaposlenosti (- 0.8%) i poveanje stope nezaposlenosti na 20%, te postupno ubrzanje tekue inflacije (2.0%) temeljem poveanja cijene energije (6.5%). Promet u trgovini na malo realno stagnira, dok su pozitivni rezultati ostvareni jedino u turizmu (rast broja noenja 11.4%) pri emu se radi o sezonski marginalnom razdoblju. 5. lako takva kretanja u prvom tromjeseju ne moraju biti signifikantna za agregatnu sliku cijele godine (zbog sezonskih razloga, time-laga izmeu trenutka poduzimanja i efektuiranja pojedinih mjera ekonomske politike i dr.), teko da e se kretanja u drugom tromjeseju znatnije razlikovati od onih u prvom tromjeseju, u kojim uvjetima niti postupna promjena tendencija u drugom dijelu godine ne moe vie promijeniti predznak kljunih agregatnih pokazatelja za cijelu 2012. godinu. Ocjenjujemo da e u njoj BDP biti realno nii od prologodinjeg za oko 1%, determiniran agregatnim smanjenjem domae potronje za 0.8% te izvoza roba i usluga za 1.2%, uz stagnaciju investicija i uvoza. Deficit platne bilance porast e sa 1% na 2% BDP-a (sa 450 na oko 900 mil. eura), ime e se odgovarajue poveati i inozemni dug na razinu od oko 102% BDP-a, ali - uz pretpostavku zadravanja kreditnog rejtinga - ocjenjuje se da e inozemne obveze biti mogue refinancirati pod postojeim uvjetima. Provedu li se najavljene mjere fiskalne politike, deficit konsolidirane ope drave (ukljuujui HAC) smanjit e se sa 5.8% na oko 5% BDP-a, dok e javni dug dostii 56% BDP-a. Plasmani banaka porast e za oko 5%, dok e se tekua inflacija ubrzati sa prologodinjih 2.1% na oko 3.5% u ovoj godini, lako ovakva predvianja nisu "blistava" s aspekta socijalnih oekivanja i politikih obeanja, ona nisu niti "tragina", ako se u meuvremenu interakcijom ekonomske politike i konkretnih postupaka ekonomskih entiteta ponu uspostavljati osnovne pretpostavke i impulsi odrivog budueg rasta i razvoja. 5. Koja je u tome uloga monetarne politike? Nedavno je u jednom dnevnom listu bilo objavljeno kako bi za izlazak iz krize "trebalo sruiti jo jednu tabu temu: dosadanju monetarnu politiku....U gospodarstvo se jednostavno mora utisnuti svjei novac kako to, primjerice, rade u SAD i Engleskoj. Bez dodatne financijske injekcije, velika veina tvrtki sadanje mjere tednje i pada kupovne moi, nee preivjeti...Zastraujue i bezumno da je danas u opticaju ak 6 mlrd. kuna manje nego 2009." Ne radi se ovdje o nikakvoj tabu temi, ve o sutinskom nepoznavanju injenica i nerazumijevanju stvarne situacije. Kad to govore novinari koji nisu specijalizirani za ekonomska pitanja, onda je to alosno. Meutim, kad to govore sveuilini profesori s jasno prepoznatljivim motivima, onda je to tragino. Ne toliko za njih osobno, koliko za njihove studente. 7. Pa kakvu to monetarnu politiku vodi HNB? Ta politika prola je u posljednjih desetak godina dva bitno razliita razdoblja. (a) Prije krize, monetarna politika bila je umjereno restriktivna i usmjerena na destimulira nje snanog inozemnog zaduivanja banaka i transformaciju deviznih sredstava pribavljenih po toj osnovi u ekspanzivni rast domaih kredita. Bio je to nuan odgovor na bitno poveanje deficita platne bilance, brzi rast inozemnog duga, formiranje balona na tritima vrijednosnica i nekretnina i, najgore, stvaranje iluzije o mogunostima permanentnog rasta potronje i standarda na osnovi relativno povoljnih i lako dostupnih inozemnih kredita. HNB je tada bio izloen snanim unutarnjim i vanjskim kritikama koje su trajale sve do izbijanja svjetske financijske krize. Tek tada se vidjelo da je upravo takva politika omoguila formiranje rezervi kojima je i u uvjetima ope krize zadrana financijska stabilnost, likvidnost u plaanjima prema inozemstvu te izbjegnut kreditni slom. Pored toga, u kombinaciji sa stabilnim teajem i relativno niskom inflacijom, takva je politika rezultirala i postupnom afirmacijom domae valute, pa je udio deviznih depozita u strukturi M4 smanjen s 64.2% krajem 2000. na 52.1% krajem 2008. godine, a udio u ukupnim depozitima sa 71.2% na 57.0%. (b) Nagovjetajima, a onda i efektivnim izbijanjem financijske krize u drugoj polovini 2008. godine, monetarna politika u Hrvatskoj se sutinski mijenja i postaje izrazito ekspanzivna. Od tada je HNB donio 18 mjera koje su izravno utjecale na promjenu likvidnosti bankovnog sustava i kojima je neto osloboeno 6.3 mlrd. eura. Istodobno, intervencijama na deviznom tritu, HNB je od banaka i drave neto kupio 1.4 mlrd. eura emitiravi 10.1 mlrd. kuna, tako da je (saldiranjem tih dviju vrsta monetarnih operacija) HNB od sredine 2008. godine do danas neto oslobodio likvidnost bankovnog sustava u iznosu od, preraunato, oko 46 mlrd. kuna. To je ekvivalent od 83% novane mase i 21% ukupnih likvidnih sredstava u Hrvatskoj s kraja 2008. godine, te odgovara visini od 13.5% BDP-a iz te godine. Ima li se pri tome na umu da ta sredstva nisu u Hrvatskoj morala biti angairana za pokrie gubitaka bankarskog sektora, kao to je bio sluaj u drugim zemljama, stvarna ekspanzivnost nae monetarne politike nije bila nita manje nego u zemljama koje se navode kao primjer snanih monetarnih impulsa. 8. Tako poveana likvidnost prvenstveno je koritena i koristi se u dvije funkcije. U funkciji odranja eksterne likvidnosti zemlje u uvjetima kad su zaustavljanjem priljeva inozemnog kapitala otplate glavnice i kamata na inozemni dug postale vee od koritenja novih kredita. Tako su u 2010. i 2011. godini neto otplate anuiteta inozemnih kredita ukupno iznosile 1.6 mlrd. eura, dio ega je otplaen pretvaranjem duga u kapital, a dio iz tekue likvidnosti bankovnog sustava. Dodaju li se tome plaanja po osnovi tekuih transakcija, neto inozemna aktiva bankovnog sustava smanjena je u posljednje tri godine za oko 1.1 mlrd. eura (za oko 20%), s nastavkom te tendencije i u ovoj godini. Ipak, to se nije snanije odrazilo na deviznu likvidnost zemlje i teaj valute, to govori o uspjenom odravanju stabilnosti sustava. U funkciji alimentiranja kreditne aktivnosti banaka, pri emu su ukupni plasmani naih banaka rasli od 2009. do 2011. godine po prosjenoj godinjoj stopi od 5.5%, nasuprot rastu kredita u euro zoni od samo 1.5%. Slina kretanja oekuju se i u ovoj godini, tako da nema govora o nekom kreditnom slomu, iako su problemi s naplatom kredita u meuvremenu znaajno porasli. 9. Poveu li se takva kretanja u monetarnoj sferi s onima u realnom sektoru, logino se postavlja pitanje zato rast monetarnih agregata nije imao vei utjecaj na kretanje proizvodnje i pod kojim uvjetima bi ga mogao imati ubudue. Tu su bitna dva aspekta:  ponaanje drave  transformacija osloboene likvidnosti u kredite realnom sektoru. (a) lako se ne radi o klasinom crowding-out efektu, injenica je da u vrijeme krize i neizvjesnosti drava predstavlja bankama poeljnijeg komitenta od privatnog sektora. Sukladno tome, od ukupnog prirasta plasmana banaka u razdoblju od 2009. do 2011. godine u iznosu 44.6 mlrd. kuna, 16.5 mlrd. kuna (ili 37%) je koristila drava, iji je udio u strukturi ukupnih plasmana banaka povean s 8.5% (2008) na 12.8% (2011), s tendencijom daljnjeg rasta u ovoj godini na 13.5%. To je naravno izravna posljedica u meuvremenu poveanog proraunskog deficita, pri emu su, zbog svoje strukture, proraunski rashodi imali relativno nizak multiplikativni utjecaj na proizvodnju i zaposlenost cijele ekonomije. (b) to se tie plasmana realnom sektoru problem je potpuno druge prirode. Ti plasmani rastu po prosjenoj godinjoj stopi od 3.8%, to je u cijelosti rezultat rasta kredita sektoru poduzea (7.1% godinje), dok potranja za kreditima sektora stanovnitva stagnira, lako ovi pokazatelji ukljuuju i efekte reprogramiranja obveza, ostvareni rast kredita sektoru poduzea nije zanemariv, ali on naravno nije dostatan da supstituira izostanak priljeva inozemnog kapitala u uvjetima pada proizvodnje i poveanja jedininih trokova. Zato HNB cijelo vrijeme pokuava potaknuti bri rast upravo tih kredita uz smanjivanje kamatnih stopa, ali su dosadanji rezultati bili slabiji od oekivanja. To se odnosi i na tzv. model A iz 2010. godine i na nenamjensko otputanje likvidnosti iz2011. godine, pri emu su se u oba sluaja pojavili isti problemi: averzija prema riziku od strane banaka, komitenata i drave kao posrednika, preferiranje kratkoronih u odnosu na dugorone interese te nedostatak kvalitetnih proizvodnih programa koji bi se financirali iz takvih kredita. Zato se osloboena likvidnost sporo pretvarala u nove kredite, dok je dio nje koriten i u neke druge svrhe, zbog ega je sredinja banka bila prisiljena povui taj dio likvidnosti. Navedeni problemi i dalje su prisutni to ilustrira i injenica daje izvorno predloeni program povoljnijeg kreditiranja gospodarstva u ovoj godini od 12 mlrd. kuna (od kojih bi mjerama HNB bilo osloboeno 9 mlrd. kuna) na traenje banaka smanjen na iznos od oko 8 mlrd. kuna, u kojem mjerama HNB-a osloboena likvidnost uestvuje sa 7 mlrd. kuna, a ostala sredstva banaka sa samo 1 mlrd. kuna. 10. Dakle, sutina problema nije, kao to neki misle, u nedovoljnoj ekspanzivnosti monetarne politike, ve u nepovoljnim modalitetima formiranja ponude i potranje za kreditima, odnosno u nedovoljno efikasnoj transformaciji inicijalno poveane likvidnosti u financijska sredstva koja e pokrenuti proizvodnju i zapoljavanje. Izraz toga je i podatak da je u posljednje tri godine pri poveanju primarnog novca za ukupno 25.4%, novana masa istodobno smanjena za 4.3%, tako da je monetarni multiplikator pao ispod 1 (sa 1.11 u 2008. na 0.82 u 2011. godini), dok neto konverzija kunskih u devizne depozite vraa stupanj euriziranosti financijskog sustava na razine s kraja 90-tih godina. Dok se ti sutinski problemi ne ponu ozbiljno rjeavati, a to podrazumijeva daljnju konsolidaciju i racionalizaciju javnog sektora, unapreenje sustava naplate potraivanja i zatite vjerovnika, pojednostavljenje procesa ulaska i izlaska ekonomskih entiteta s trita, otklanjanje prepreka realizaciji investicijskih projekata, poticanje vee poduzetnosti privatnog sektora i dr., i dalje e postojati ograniena protonost te uska grla u financijskim tokovima, koja e usporavati cirkulaciju i oteavati efikasnu alokaciju novanih sredstava prema proizvodnjama koje mogu dati najvee efekte za ukupnu ekonomiju. Tu ne pomae nikakvo "bacanje novca iz helikoptera" ili "revolucionarne" ideje o izravnom kreditiranju proizvodnih programa od strane sredinje banke, ve jedino dugo traene reforme i iz njih proizale strukturne promjene u modalitetima funkcioniranja ukupne ekonomije. Toga je svjesna Vlada, a vjerujem i veina ekonomista koji cjelovitije sagledavaju stanje hrvatske ekonomije i ne robuju klieima iz nekih drugih vremena i drugaijih situacija.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Financial markets and monetary policy
text: Financial markets and monetary policy Published: 13.10.2006. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 13.10.2006. 16th Conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange Rovinj 13.10.2006. 1. The financial industry is by far the most propulsive sector of the Croatian economy in the last five years. Its development is driven by the interdependence of the parallel activities of the two groups of factors. Internal, which include accelerated privatisation, reform and opening up of the financial system, macroeconomic stability as well as expectations regarding the eu accession process, and external ones determined by the combination of financial deregulation, jeftina money and low domicile yield rates that have prompted European banks to expand their operations in transition countries. In a word, the rapid development of the financial sector in Croatia is primarily the result of its inclusion in the process of globalizationsin its financial, technological and ideological sense. Under such conditions, the total assets of the financial industry doubled between the end of 2001 and mid-2006 (June) 2006 from 163 billion to 349 billion, kuna and its relation to GDP increased from 98% to 141%. The majority of this increase relates to banks as leaders and organizers of the whole process (their assets were increased from 143 billion to 271 billion, but within the framework of the system, non-bank institutions developed the fastest, reflecting a significant increase inthe e assortment and diversification of the supply of financial services. Thus, approximately evenly distributed, the assets of investment and pension funds were collectively increased by almost ten times (from HRK 3.5 billion to HRK 31 billion) and the assets of leasing companies by seven times (from HRK 3.3 billion to HRK 22 billion), and the share of non-bank institutions in financial sector assets almost doubled during this period (from 12.5% to 22.4%). 2. The growth of funds is an expression of the realized development of the capital market. On it (Zagreb) the capitalization of shares increased from the level of 15.6% of GDP (2001) to 53% of GDP (September 2006), and the capitalization of bonds from 4.4% to 13.7% of GDP. 3. This has also resulted in dynamic growth in yields. After stagnation in 2003, over the next two years the CROBEX index grew at an average rate of 30%, and this growth in I-IX in 2006 was increased to 72%, making the market very attractive for investors. All to has opened up new financing opportunities for the national economy and undeniably contributed to the growth of the real sector, but together with the credit activity of banks has also resulted in a strong expansion of spending with a deterioration in the balance of payments and an increase in foreign debt. 4. Although, as usual, the development of institutional and legal regulation has "trot" for the very development of the market, and a lot has been done in this area recently: o HANFA was founded, o new laws on: mandatory relationships, investment funds, insurance, accounting, audit, (c) the enforcement law, regulations in the field of foreign exchange, etc., have been amended, o as part of the alignment of legislation with EU standards, new laws will be adopted on leasing, payment transactions, financial collateral, securritization, acquisition of shareholders' securities market, credit institutions, financial conglomerates, mandatory and voluntary pension funds, etc. o These are all steps on the road to rounding up a transparent and complementary financial market in Croatia. 5. However, this is only the "fae7ade" of the building. Interiors and quintessential relationships in this market have been much less impressive so far. Both in quantitative and, even more so, in qualitative terms. 6. In this regard, let's look atthe structure of the net assets of investment funds (March 2006). In it: o 36.8% are deposits, investments abroad and in financial institutions, i.e. this part is 'reversed' within the financial sector itself; b0 37.5% are investments in government papers, half of which (20.8%) are investments in treasury bills where they are used to finance current spending; o so that only 26.3% represent investments in the corporate sector. 7. If pension funds are added to this, the aggregate share of investments in government papers in the net asset structure of theseh two groups of funds increases to 57.3%, and the share of investments in the corporate sector decreases to only 17.3%. In this case, investments in the sector's bonds amount to only 6% of the net assets of the funds. Although such an investment structure may reflect the efforts of investors to disperse risk, it is primarily the result of a very limited supply of corporate sector securities For many reasons on the supply side (e.g. inability to meet the conditions for listing on the stock exchange or does not prefer such afinancing gap) but also on the demand side for securities of the sector as part of the overall policy of placing funds from banks and institutional investors. That is why the sector is still predominantly oriented towards financing with banks' loans in zemilk or, increasingly, directly from Abroad. As a result, the capitalization of corporate bonds and the liquidity of shares range in Croatia at the level of only 2-3% of GDP, which for example is ten times less than in the Czech Republic or Hungary. Within this framework, and since in the structure of the total turnover of shares this year, only three shares participate with 76% (Pliva 61%, Podravka 10%, Adris grupa 5%), and the situation was not very different in the previous period, the overall climate in the equity paper market determinedby the e conjuncture in the sphere of its very narrow segment, so it has no suitable shock absorbers and is potentially very lati I no.
