Thus, such limited financial markets are dominated by the financing of the state, which indirectly absorbs a significant part of the "forced savings" in mandatory pension funds, which allows the clean credit potential of banks to be increased to be directed to other sectors where, as a rule, interest rates and yield rates are proportionate to the risk are significantly higher. In other words, the sitting market allowsfor the choice of alternative forms of savings, on the other hand prefers high certainty of placements, and has a much less direct impact on the financing and development of the corporate sector than in developed countries. 7. At the same time, the fact that investment and pension fonds and leasing companies are predominantly managed by foreign-owned banks puts these banks in a position to manage the overall portfolio, i.e. the financial potential of the domestic market, as financial conglomerates, directing its divergingof domestic and especially foreign components to sectors and placements whose combination maximizes the total profit at the group level - the conglomerate. That is why, although they are formally different in institutional and business terms, the majority of existing entities within the financialsector actually represent a tight-knit organic entity. That is why economic policy as a whole, and monetary policy in particular, should have an integral approach towards this sector. 8. From this point of view, the fact that the entry and distribution of the foreign tothe question within the national economy is manifested differently in the market of goods and services in relation to the securities market and, for example, real estate, is important. In the first case, loans supported by demand for goods and services above short-term domestic supply capacitiesare dwarfed by increased supply from imports, resulting in an increase in the current account deficit of the balance of payments but also maintaining relative price stability in those markets. This is of course not the case in the financial market, where supply is much more limited, so rast demand tends to increase prices, which in its continuity can result in a pure "bubble effect". This can actually enter the classic "vicious circle" of interdependence of financial and monetary flows, where supported by optimistic expectations , credit expansion (financed by capital inflows from abroad) leads to an increase in the prices (asset-sa) of assets in assets, which encourages investors and increases collateral prices, all of which together supports an even stronger credit expansion. At the same time, there is a rapid growth in loans and total monetary aggregates, an increase in the prices of securities and investments, while at the same time inflation measured by the consumer price index remains at low levels. If this process is also linked to the real growth of the economy, it increases the willingness to take risks that gives additional momentum to the credit cycle. Conversely, when risk and return on investment expectations change, and the causes of this may be internal or external in nature (interest rate rises, exchange rate changes, reduced opportunities for orderly debt servicing, political environment and si.) the whole process moves in the opposite direction, prices fall with a negative impact on the real sector, which is now burdened by high debt and low investment activity. All this is strengthened today andthat the primary objective of monetary policy can no longer be only to maintain the long-term stability of prices in the market of goods and services, but also to the stability of the integral price level in the national economy, for which protucyclic action in the sphere of financial flows is particularly significant in the conditions of globalization. 9. It is in this function for our highly euroised economy, with a strong inflow of foreign capital that exerts permanent pressure on exchange rate appreciation and breaks long-term interest rates, especially significant maintenance of exchange rate stability and related short-term interest rates, to the extent that these two aggregates are mutually coherent. As for the nominal exchange rate, it has been very stable in the last four years, with an average daily level ofd 7.44 kunas per euro and a standard deviation of 7 lipa, which gives a variation coefficient of only 0.94%. In contrast, the overall trend of decreasing average interest rates on the money market was accompanied by significant daily volatility (the variation coefficient of the interest rate on overnight loans was 70.8%, and on loans up to seven days 37.5%) and only with the introduction of repo operations on the open market was this coefficient reduced to a relatively acceptable 26.9%. 10. However, by firmly ironing the exchange rate and the ongoing decreasein the vol atility of interest rates, monetary policy is losing a large part of its room for manoeuvre and therefore, in order to mitigate the impact of cyclical foreign capital movements on domestic system imbalances, various administrative constraints, including capital restrictions, must also be used . In our case, these are: high level of reserve requirement, marginal reserve requirement, minimum required foreign currency claims and restrictions in the sphere of exposure of banks' foreign exchange position. These restrictions will almost certainly remain in place until Croatia joins the EU and together with the further maintenance of the stability of the nominal exchange rate, as a reference price in all markets, will be the backbone of the monetary environment in which financial markets will need to function during the orderof the years. 11. On the other hand, just as monetary policy has an impact on financial markets, so developments in these markets have and it is safe to assume that they will have an increasing feedback on monetary flows. The currentbut takeover of Pliva is also an illustration of this. In this total of 2 billion euros worth of transactions, about 800 million euros will need to be effectively converted from foreign currency to kuna and part of that amount again from kuna to foreign exchange. This exceeds the existing liquid capacities of the domestic foreign exchange and cashmarket and requires direct participation of the central bank. However, in order for the transaction to be able to be made without inducing large fluctuations in exchange rates and interest rates immediately before and after the transaction, it is necessary that it be carried out in fullin just one working day, within which, in addition to the necessary currency conversions by the CNB, the foreign buyer will pay the funds, the SDA will transfer them to the accounts of the seller, and non-residents among them take out the funds received from the country so that banks do not have to allocate a marginal reserve requirement to them. This will be followed by a new central bank intervention to sterilize increased kuna liquidity in the domestic market. 12. Quite complicated, but a real joke about the problems that will need to be addressed immediately before joining the EU. Namely, it will then be necessary to lift or significantly loosen existing monetary restrictions, which will free up the now immobilized liquidity of the banking system of about 10 billion euros. In parallel with the already appreciated real flowof the mink, this will require finding and activating mechanisms that would prevent 'initial distortions' in the monetary and financial spheres while increasing the initial competitiveness of the national economy in an integral market. In this sense, one should also look at what financial markets especially prefer, which is the rapid introduction of the euro . It will be an operation that will require much more activity than "mere" fulfillment Maastricht criteria and modification register cash register. The euro transitionwill need to be made in a way and within the deadlines that will result in gains for the national economy, not "cement" its existing weaknesses.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Financijska trita i monetarna politika Objavljeno: 13.10.2006. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 13.10.2006. 16. konferencija Zagrebake burze Rovinj 13.10.2006. 1. Financijska industrija daleko je najpropulzivniji sektor hrvatske ekonomije u posljednjih pet godina. Njen razvoj potaknut je meuzavisnou usporednog djelovanja dviju skupina initelja. Unutarnjih, u koje spadaju ubrzana privatizacija, reforma i otvaranje financijskog sustava, makroekonomska stabilnost kao i oekivanja vezana uz proces pribliavanja EU, te vanjskih koje odreuje kombinacija financijske deregulacije, jeftinog novca i niskih domicilnih stopa prinosa koja je potaknula europske banke na ekspanziju poslovanja u tranzicijskim zemljama. Jednom rijeju brzi razvoj financijskog sektora u Hrvatskoj prvenstveno je rezultat njezinog ukljuivanja u proces globalizacije u njegovom financijskom, tehnolokom i ideolokom smislu. U takvim uvjetima, ukupna imovina financijske industrije udvostruena je u razdoblju od kraja 2001. do sredine (lipanj) 2006. sa 163 na 349 milijardi, kuna i njezin odnos prema BDP-u poveanje sa 98% na 141%. Glavnina tog porasta odnosi se na banke kao leadere i organizatore cijelog procesa (njihova je imovina poveana sa 143 na 271 milijardu, kuna), ali su se u okvirima sustava najbre razvijale nebankovne institucije, odraavajui bitno poveanje asortimana i diverzifikaciju ponude financijskih usluga. Tako je, priblino ravnomjerno distribuirana, imovina investicijskih i mirovinskih fondova zbirno poveana za gotovo deset puta (s 3.5 na 31 milijardu kuna) a imovina leasing drutava za sedam puta (s 3.3 na 22 milijarde kuna), pa je i udio nebankovnih institucija u imovini financijskog sektora gotovo udvostruen u tom razdoblju (s 12.5% na 22.4%). 2. Rast fondova izraz je ostvarenog razvoja trita kapitala. Na njemu je (Zagreb) kapitalizacija dionica poveana s razine od 15.6% BDP-a (2001.) na 53% BDP-a (rujan 2006), a kapitalizacija obveznica sa 4.4% na 13.7% BDP-a. 3. To je rezultiralo i dinaminim rastom prinosa. Nakon stagnacije u 2003. godini, u naredne dvije godine CROBEX indeks je rastao po prosjenoj stopi od 30%, da bi taj rast u I-IX 2006. bio povean na 72%, inei trite vrlo atraktivnim za investitore. Sve to otvorilo je nove mogunosti financiranja nacionalne ekonomije i neosporno pridonijelo rastu realnog sektora, ali zajedno s kreditnom aktivnou banaka rezultiralo je i snanom ekspanzijom potronje s pogoranjem platne bilance i poveanjem inozemnog duga. 4. lako je, kao i obino, razvoj institucionalne i pravne regulative "kaskao" za samim razvojem trita, i na tom je podruju u posljednje vrijeme dosta uinjeno: o osnovana je HANFA, o donijeti su novi zakoni o: obveznim odnosima, investicijskim fondovima, osiguranju, raunovodstvu, reviziji,  izmijenjen je ovrni zakon, propisi iz oblasti deviznog poslovanja itd., o u sklopu usklaivanja zakonodavstva sa standardima EU, donijeti e se novi zakoni o o leasingu, platnom prometu, financijskom kolateralu, sekuritizaciji, preuzimanju dioniarskih drutava, tritu vrijednosnih papira, kreditnim institucijama, financijskim konglomeratima, obveznim i dobrovoljnim mirovinskim fondovima i dr. o Sve su to koraci na putu zaokruivanja transparentnog i komplementarnog financijskog trita u Hrvatskoj. 5. Meutim, to je tek "proelje" zgrade. Interijeri i sutinski odnosi na tom tritu bili su do sada mnogo manje impresivni. I u kvantitativnom i, jo vie, u kvalitativnom smislu. 6. S tim u vezi, pogledajmo prvo strukturu neto imovine investicijskih fondova (oujak 2006). U njoj: o 36.8% ine depoziti, ulaganja u inozemstvo i u financijske institucije, odnosno taj se dio "obre" unutar samog financijskog sektora;  37.5% su ulaganja u dravne papire, od ega polovina (20.8%) u trezorske zapise gdje slue za financiranje tekue potronje; o tako da samo 26.3% predstavljaju ulaganja u korporativni sektor. 7. Dodaju li se tome mirovinski fondovi, zbirni udio ulaganja u dravne papire u strukturi neto imovine tih dvaju grupa fondova poveava se na 57.3%, a udio ulaganja u korporativni sektor smanjuje na samo 17.3%. Pri, tome ulaganja u obveznice tog sektora iznose tek 6% neto imovine fondova. lako takva struktura ulaganja moe odraavati nastojanje investitora da disperziraju rizik, ona je prvenstveno rezultat vrlo ograniene ponude vrijednosnih papira korporativnog sektora Iz mnogih razloga na strani ponude (npr. nemogunost ispunjavanja uvjeta za uvrtavanje na burzu ili ne preferira nje takvog oblika financiranja) ali i na strani potranje za vrijednosnim papirima tog sektora u sklopu ukupne politike plasiranja sredstava banaka i institucionalnih investitora. Zato je taj sektor jo uvijek dominantno orijentiran na financiranje kreditima banaka u zemlji ili, sve vie, izravno iz inozemstva. Posljedica toga je da se kapitalizacija korporativnih obveznica i likvidnost dionica kreu u Hrvatskoj na razini od svega 2-3% BDP-a, to je npr. desetak puta manje nego u ekoj ili Maarskoj. U okviru toga, a s obzirom da u strukturi ukupnog prometa dionica u ovoj godini, samo tri dionice uestvuju sa 76% (Pliva 61%, Podravka 10%, Adris grupa 5%), a situacija nije bila bitno drugaije ni u prethodnom razdoblju, ukupna klima na tritu vlasnikih papira odreena je konjunkturom u sferi njegovog vrlo uskog segmenta, tako da ono nema odgovarajuih amortizera i potencijalno je vrlo vo lati I no. Dakle, na tako ogranienim financijskim tritima dominira financiranje drave koja posredno apsorbira znatan dio "prisilne tednje" u obveznim mirovinskim fondovima, to omoguava da se isti kreditni potencijal banaka poveano usmjerava na ostale sektore gdje su u pravilu kamatne stope i stope prinosa razmjerno riziku znatno vie. Drugim rijeima, trite sjedne strane omoguava izbor alternativnih oblika tednje, s druge strane preferira visoku sigurnost plasmana, te ima bitno manji izravni utjecaj na financiranje i razvoj korporativnog sektora nego u razvijenim zemljama. 7. Istodobno, injenica da investicijskim i mirovinskim fondovima te leasing drutvima dominantno upravljaju banke u inozemnom vlasnitvu stavlja te banke u poziciju da kao financijski konglomerati objedinjeno upravljaju ukupnim portfoliom, tj. financijskim potencijalom domaeg trita, usmjeravajui njegove razliite domae i posebno inozemne komponente na sektore i plasmane ija kombinacija maksimira ukupnu dobit na razini grupe - konglomerata. Zato, iako su formalno razliiti u institucionalnom i poslovnom smislu, glavnina postojeih entiteta unutar financijskog sektora zapravo predstavlja vrsto povezanu organsku cjelinu. Zato i ekonomska politika u cjelini, a monetarna politika posebno, treba prema tom sektoru imati integralni pristup. 8. S tog aspekta, bitna je injenica da se ulazak i rasprostiranje stranog kapitala unutar nacionalne ekonomije razliito manifestira na tritu roba i usluga u odnosu na trite vrijednosnih papira i npr. nekretnina. U prvom sluaju kreditima podravana potranje za robama i uslugama iznad kratkoronih kapaciteta domae ponude zadovoljava se poveanom ponudom iz uvoza, to rezultira porastom deficita tekuih transakcija platne bilance ali i zadrava relativnu stabilnost cijena na tim tritima. To naravno nije sluaj na financijskom tritu, gdje je ponuda mnogo ogranienija pa rast potranje ima tendenciju da poveava cijene, to u svom kontinuitetu moe rezultirati istim "bubble efektom". Time se zapravo moe ui u klasini "zaarani krug" meuzavisnosti financijskih i monetarnih tokova, gdje podravana optimistikim oekivanjima kreditna ekspanzija (financirana priljevom kapitala iz inozemstva) dovodi do poveanja cijena (asset-sa) imovine u aktivi to ohrabruje investitore i poveava cijene kolaterala, a sve to zajedno podrava jo snaniju kreditnu ekspanziju. Tako se istodobno javljaju brzi rast kredita i ukupnih monetarnih agregata, rast cijena vrijednosnica i investicija, a da istodobno inflacija mjerena indeksom potroakih cijena ostaje na niskim razinama. Ako je taj proces povezan i sa realnim rastom ekonomije, on poveava spremnost preuzimanja rizika koji daje dodatni zamah kreditnom ciklusu. Suprotno, kada se promijene oekivanja u pogledu rizika i povrata na investicije, a uzroci tome mogu biti unutarnje ili vanjske prirode (rast kamatnih stopa, promjene teaja, smanjene mogunosti urednog servisiranja duga, politiko okruenje i si.) cijeli proces kree u suprotnom smjeru, cijene padaju s negativnim utjecajem na realni sektor koji je sada optereen visokim dugom i niskom investicijskom aktivnou. Sve to jaa danas spoznaju kako primarni cilj monetarne politike ne moe vie biti samo odravanje dugorone stabilnosti cijena na tritu roba i usluga, ve i stabilnosti integralne razine cijena u nacionalnoj ekonomiji, za koju je u uvjetima globalizacije posebno znaajno protucikliko djelovanje u sferi financijskih tokova. 9. U toj funkciji je za nau visoko euriziranu ekonomiju, sa snanim priljevom inozemnog kapitala koji vri permanentni pritisak na aprecijaciju teaja i obara dugorone kamatne stope, posebno znaajno odravanje stabilnosti teaja i s njime povezanih kratkoronih kamatnih stopa, u mjeri u kojoj su ta dva agregata cijena meusobno koherentna. to se tie nominalnog teaja, on je u posljednje etiri godine bio vrlo stabilan, s prosjenom dnevnom razinom od 7.44 kune za euro i standardnom devijacijom od 7 lipa, to daje koeficijent varijacije od samo 0.94%. Nasuprot tome, opi trend smanjenja prosjenih kamatnih stopa na tritu novca bio je praen znatnom dnevnom volatilnou (koeficijent varijacije kamatnih stopa na prekonone kredite iznosio je 70.8%, a na kredite do sedam dana 37.5%) i tek je uvoenjem repo-operacija na otvorenom tritu taj koeficijent smanjen na relativno prihvatljivih 26.9%. 10. Meutim, vrstim peglanjem teaja i aktualnim smanjenjem volatilnosti kamatnih stopa, monetarna politika gubi veliki dio svog manevarskog prostora te se zato u funkciji ublaavanja utjecaja ciklikog kretanja inozemnog kapitala na neravnotee domaeg sustava mora sluiti i razliitim administrativnim ogranienjima, ukljuujui kapitalske restrikcije. U naem sluaju to su: visoka razina obvezne priuve, granina obvezna priuva, minimalno potrebna devizna potraivanja i ogranienja u sferi izloenosti devizne pozicije banaka. Ta e ogranienja gotovo sigurno ostati na snazi sve do ulaska Hrvatske u EU te e zajedno s daljnjim odravanjem stabilnosti nominalnog teaja, kao referentne cijene na svim tritima, predstavljati okosnicu monetarnog ambijenta u kojem e trebati funkcionirati financijska trita tijekom narednih godina. 11. S druge strane, jednako kao to monetarna politika ima utjecaj na financijska trita, tako i kretanja na tim tritima imaju i za pretpostaviti je da e imati sve vei povratni utjecaj na monetarne tokove. Ilustraciju toga predstavlja i aktualno preuzimanje Plive. U toj ukupno 2 milijarde eura tekoj transakciji, oko 800 milijuna eura trebat e biti efektivno konvertirano iz deviza u kune i dio tog iznosa ponovno iz kuna u devize. To prelazi postojee likvidne kapacitete domaeg deviznog i novanog trita i zahtijeva izravno sudjelovanje sredinje banke. Meutim, da bi se i u takvim uvjetima transakcija mogla obaviti bez induciranja velikih oscilacija teaja i kamatnih stopa neposredno prije i nakon transakcije, potrebno je da se ona u cijelosti obavi u samo jednom radnom danu, unutar kojeg e, uz potrebne konverzije valuta od strane HNB-a, inozemni kupac uplatiti sredstva, SDA ih prenijeti na raune prodavalaca, a nerezidenti meu njima iznijeti primljena sredstva iz zemlje kako banke ne bi na njih morale izdvojiti graninu obveznu priuvu. Nakon toga uslijedit e nova intervencija sredinje banke kojom e sterilizirati poveanu kunsku likvidnost na domaem tritu. 12. Prilino komplicirano, ali prava ala prema problemima koji e trebati rjeavati neposredno prije pristupanja EU. Naime, tada e biti potrebno ukinuti ili znatno olabaviti postojee monetarne restrikcije, to e osloboditi sada imobiliziranu likvidnost bankovnog sustava od oko 10 milijardi eura. Usporedo s ve apreciranim realnim teajem kune, to e zahtijevati iznalaenje i aktiviranje odgovarajuih mehanizama koji bi sprijeili "startne poremeaje" u monetarnoj i financijskoj sferi i istodobno poveali inicijalnu konkurentnost nacionalne ekonomije na integralnom tritu. U tom smislu treba gledati i na ono to financijska trita posebno preferiraju, a to je brzo uvoenje eura . Bit e to operacija koja e zahtijevati mnogo vie aktivnosti od "pukog" ispunjavanja Maastrichtskih kriterija i modificiranja registar kasa. Prelazak na euro trebat e izvesti na nain i u rokovima koji e rezultirati probitci ma za nacionalnu ekonomiju, a ne "zacementirati" njezine postojee slabosti.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation at the 16th Scientific-Professional Conference Croatian Money Market
text: Presentation by CNB Governor Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic at the 16th Scientific and Professional Conference Croatian Money Market Published: 16.5.2013. Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor 16.5.2013. 16th Scientific and Professional Conference Croatian Money Market Opatija 16.5.2013. Ladies and gentlemen, I am very pleased to be able to address you at the 16th Conference of the Croatian Money Market. The banking and economic crisis began in 2007 in the USA, spilled over into Europe in 2008 and in the second part of that year and croatia. Since then, Croatia has been in recession or stagnation. This fall, at the Faculty of Economics in Zscratch, I talked about the macroeconomic causes and consequences of the crisis in Croatia, about the good and bad policy choices to get out of it, as well as about the political economy of these elections. Starting to prepare this performance today, I read this weekend on HNB's website that presentation again and concluded that I wouldn't have anything special to add to it now, half a year later. I could just repeat that speech. Today I would like to say more about the regulation of the banking industry, the regulatory changes that are beingtaken to the banking sector and about the future of Croatia in this dimension. So, I would like to say something about the topic that has been the focus of the entire financial industry, since the beginning of the crisis, which we are discussing in different places on a weekly frequency, and which hasnot yet received the deserved attention in n as. Paul Volcker , recently, provocatively stated that the last really useful innovation in the banking system was the invention of ATM (ATMs). It is, of course, a certain exaggeration, but it is clear what this message is all about. The deregulation and the so-called financial innovations that followed it did not help financial stability - quite the opposite. In order to understand the comprehensive and profound regulatory changes to the banking system that are happening today, that is, to be ableto protect them in the right perspective, it is necessary to remind ourselves where the regulation of the banking industry was about ten years ago. In 1999, the Glass-Steagal Act was revoked in the United States after nearly seven decades of its adoption. It was introduced nakon of the great economic crisis (Great Depression), in 1933, to ensure the separation of investment banking from traditional banking, which is based on taking out deposits and making loans. The Glass-Steagal Act was passed as a regulatory response to the last major economic and financial crisis before the one we are still in. Its abolition was the most significant step to date in a process that was called the deregulation of the financial system in the late 1990s and in the first half of the 2000s. In 2004, the so-called Basel II standard of bank regulation was adopted. It proved inadequate during the crisis, since the amount of capital held by the banks was too small, the risk management was inadequate, and a significant part of the prudential role left to the rating agencies, and indirectly to the banks themselves. In general, at the beginning of this millennium, the so-called soft touch regulation was in vogue, promoted primarily from the banking center of Europe and the world - the UK, that is, byits regulator there - the FSA. In fact, many have promoted the idea of giving the best kind of regulation of the banking system - self-regulation. In the US, however, there has been fragmentation of the regulatory apparatus into a multitude of institutions, often without sufficient teaming, coordinates ofwhich and clear competence. Not everyone at the time, of course, was convinced that such an approach to soft regulation of the banking sector was the best way, but the power of the influence of the largest financial centers did its job. When the first time, at the beginning of the crisis in 2007, thisderegulated system was put on stress-test, it proved completely inadequate. This made the need to reform the regulatory framework painfully obvious and has been going on ever since. Her idea, from the beginning, is less about solving acute crisis problems and more about establishingtighter regulation of the banking system that will reduce the possibility of a major financial crisis like the one we continue to face. A crisis that began as a crisis of the financial system and developed into a macroeconomic crisis, and, finally,a crisis in part of developed countries. Regulatory reforms have a number of objectives. One is to increase the capital of banking institutions. Greater capitalisation, and lower indebtedness, is a guarantee of greater stability for banks. The second is to make large financial institutions at the heart of the system, that is, systematically important institutions, even more resilient, requiring them to have even higher capital adequacy and stricter risk control. The third is to increase the transparency of the business and make the connections and exposures in a financialstance more transparent to all participants. Finally, the goal is to regto relish areas of the financial system directly and indirectly linked to banks, which are sometimes a direct substitutz of banking operations, and which have not been regulated until now, or have been poorly regulated, such as so-called shadow banking and derivatives trading. Finally, the emphasis is placed on macroprudential regulatory measures, which we have used very successfully in Croatia and so far, and today they are recognized as a very useful experience. In parallel with these global regulatory changes, the EU has taken a whole new path that should result in a banking union in the eurozone, or the EU. The consequence of the eurozone crisis is the belief that it gives the only way for the sustainability of the monetary union project to break the link between the risks of banks and the risks of the edastates in which these banks predominantly operate, and this can only be achieved by establishing a banking union. Another obvious reason for establishing a banking union is the fact that in the common European market banks operate transnationally and are supervised nacionally, without ha rmo lower early supervisory criteria, including basic definitions such as poor placements. The fragmentation of the regulatory framework for the functioning of the banking market has also undermined one of the fundamental freedoms of the EU common market - freedom of movement of capital - during the crisis. In seven months, the supervision of all systematically important, i.e. larger banks in the eurozone, passes into the jurisdiction of the joint supervisor - the European Central Bank. Common supervision, however, cannot functionas effectively without a common framework for resolving problem banks or restructuring banks. The proposal for this directive, The Bank Restructuring and Rehabilitation Directive (BRR), is expected in the middle of this year, but it is clear that the adoption of this chainwill not be easy, since it implies the possibility of some kind of division of fiscal costs of resolving problem banks. But without this mechanism, it is very difficult to imagine an effective joint supervision of the banking system, that is, the banking union. The third pillar of the banking union - joint deposit insurance - is the component that is most likely to come up at the latest, since there is the least agreement on the necessity and design of this mechanism at the banking union level. The reason, again, is to assume jointe, implicitly fiscal, liability for secured deposits. As a regulatory framework for Basel III, CRD IV (Capital Requirement Directive IV), as well as for the creation of a banking union, the EU has produced an impressive amount of material, so far, I am told to me by those who,I assume, counted, over 10,000 pages. In addition to higher capital requirements and stricter risk management requirements, a very important part of the regulation that deals with standardizing the definition of bad placements (NPLs) will be very important. Standardisation in this areais an indispensable precondition for the establishment of a single supervisory system. At the end of this year, and by the middle of next year at the latest, on the basis of jointly established criteria, a control of banks' assets will be carried out, in order to establish any need for additional capital, i.e. to meet new, stricter capital adequacy requirements. This will be an extremely important and challenging project. Once implemented, it should be easier to compare the indicators of the banking system of different countries. The current problemis that there is an uneven practice of the definition of bad placements, so that complex mechanisms of risk assessment and capital needs are applied to a relatively arbitrary basis. However, this exercise could significantly increase the capital requirements of individual bankas. In a way, it can also be understood as a purgatory of the banking union. What will determine the results of this control to the greatest extent will be the definition of the criteria by which the risk assessment of the assets will be carried out. There is no doubt that the new regulation of the banking system is necessary. The crisis has shown how wrong the deregulation of the banking system has been over the last fifteen years. The cost of financial crises is, in fact, very high. Globally, on average, blicks 20% of GDP, through the direct costs of saving banks, through lost GDP. In Croatia, indicative estimates show that the direct cost of the major banking crisis of the first half of the 90s was about 30% of GDP, and the crises of smaller and medium-sizedbans towards, in the late 90s, about 5% of GDP. As a result, the costs of increasing credit margins due to more demanding or more expensive regulation have justification. Estimates of the impact of higher capital requirements under Basel III regulation on the increase in the credit margin of the largesth banks range from 8 to 16 basis points (IMF and BIS). This is not much, bearing in mind the cost of bank crises. The problem, however, is that higher capital requirements are now occurring in a situation of stagnation, so they seem pro-cyclical. A good part of the tightening of regulator requirements is timed, to have less of a pro-cyclical effect, however the markets themselves are already looking for stronger capitalization. This is due to past mistakes, as tougher regulation of capital requirements and risk management neededa bi response to the rapid expansion of the financial sector. Instead, deregulation, on a smoldering increase in the risk of bank assets, only added gasoline. Now regulation is tightening at a suboptimal moment, during the crisis. But this does not mean, as some sugersparadise, that regulatory requirements should not now be placed on a sound footing. It's simply a cost-benefit analysis. The cost of loose regulation, as experience shows, is higher than missed GDP growth due to adequate regulation. It's a similarphenomenon as it is with inflation. In the short term, a higher inflation rate sometimes, with certain conditions, primarily related to large closed economies, can stimulate a higher growth rate, but already in the medium term, as experience and research shows, the costs of inflation are higher than the short-term benefit it achieves. That is why today the fundamental goal of central banks is to preserve price stability. Without it, there is no sustainable economic growth. The second goal of central banks, that of a more recent date - the finanation stability of the system - is achieved primarily by setting an adequate regulatory framework. This means that central banks do not necessarily have to play the role of bank supervisors, but they should play a role in designing a regulatory framework relating tocapital adequacy, liquidity requirements and macroprudential instruments in maintaining financial stability. In this context, let us not forget that today the risks remain high due to the extremely expansionary global character of monetary policy. If you look at a market where yields on some types of assets with a CCC rating are at the level of 7 percent, then you have to ask yourself about the sustainability of the risk-price ratio. Where is Croatia in all this? In Croatia, everyone admits this today, we have a better regulatory policyand the banking system than was the case in the EU or the USA. We run a countercyclical regulatory policy. We increased capital requirements before the crisis, and just as importantly, we introduced a whole range of measures, which have only recently been called macroprudencial policies, which further increased both the amount of regulatory capital of the banking system before the crisis and strengthened banks' liquidity reserves. That is why today the capital adequacy of banks in Croatia is 20.5 percent - the highest in the EU - and Croatian banks have no problem of recapitalization in a situation where capital has become expensive. Their mother banks, like many other banks in the 'old' EU member states, are in a much more difficult situation, as they have to increase capital in a situation where the perspective of the banking system does not look nearly as good as it did before the crisis. In a situation where the return on bank capital has fallen to low single digit levels, or is negative. The total tax rates paid by banks at the group level are now around 45 per cent, and regulation goes to making bail-in unquestionable. In other words, the cost of saving the bank will be paid by the owners of ordinary and hybrid capital, while unsecured creditors and depositors will take their place by the so-called bail-in process. We first saw this procedure in action recently, during the Cyprus Crisis. In such conditions, capital has become expensive. In this context, it should also be said that it is naefve to claim that banks do not share the fate of the economy, as can often be heard in Croatia. With a certain time-lapsecoma, they cannot but follow the fate of the economy in which they operate. Relevant research shows that low GDP growth is a fundamental determinant of banking crises, coupled with high inflation, rapid capital inflows and rapid credit growth, poor managementof banks (on an individual level) and low efficiency of the legal system. The best illustration of the contracyclicality of regulatory policy in Croatia is the regulatory cost. Unlike the countries from which the mother banks come, the regulatory cost in Croatia was first increased by the CNB at the stage of a sudden expansion of banks' lending activity, only to significantly reduce it after the beginning of the crisis. The regulatory cost decreased from 2.13 percentage points in the first nine months of 2008 to 0.8 percentage points of the daywith. This, together with the countercyclical reserves built before the crisis, allowed Croatia not to have to request an arrangement with the IMF in 2009, since the domestic banking system had enough capacity to finance domestic needs, in a situation wherethe market was closed. From today's perspective, it could probably be concluded that it would have been better if an arrangement with the IMF had already been requested at that time, since this would probably have accelerated structural reforms, but this is a matter of political economy, which I will not be dealing with today. What is irrefutable is that it gives a countercyclical regulatory and monetary policy left the possibility of choosing for economic policy makers - to make the necessary structural reforms themselves, or to enter into an arrangement with the IMF, and to do so with their conditionality. If the CNB's policy had not been countercyclical, an arrangement with the IMF would have been inevitable, as was the case with some other countries. Likewise, although most are unaware of this, the CNB's expansionary monetary policy has enabled, ceteris paribus, indirectly and nepmediocrely lower fiscal deficits and lower public debt, including reducing risks in the banking system. Due to the contriciclic regulatory policy and the emphatically expansionary monetary policy, croatia did not contract the private sector loansto which occurred in the SAD, i.e. the almost stagnation of credit in the eurozone, although economic growth was much lower than in the US and eurozone. GDP in Croatia fell by 11.8 percentage points between the third quarter of 2008 and the end of 2012, while the growth rate of loans to the private sector was 15.2%. In the US, over the same period, GDP grew by 3.6%, although loans to the private sector decreased by 4.4%, and in the eurozone GDP fell by 2.1%, while loans increased by 3.1%. Thus, it is clearly not the monetary policy and the banksystem that have made Croatia one of the slowest countries in the recovery from the recession, as, without any understanding of reality, some still claim today. In fact, monetary policy and the banking system are, both explicitly and explicitly stated in the report ofrating agencies, as well as in the assessment of the IMF and investment analysts, the part of the Croatian economy that still maintains the economic stability and rating of the country at the level at the level at which they are. Those who seek to destroy this, one of the last strongholds of Croatia's stability, must publicly answer to all as soon as possible that. What, if they succeeded in their intentions, would happen to the investment perspective of the country, what would happen to austerity in the banking system, what fiscal consequences it would have for taxpayers, what would be the prospects of employment and what the real wages and pensions would be afterwards. A few words about booking policy. As a result of five years of recession or stagnation, the share of outstanding receivables due in the banking sector has increased significantly. At 14 percent, where one in ten loans to households and as much as one in four loans given to businesses is bad credit. As a consequence, it sits down, the growth of non-performing loans, and on the other hand, weaker credit activity, and the coverage of non-performing loans with provisions has fallen from 50% in 2008 to 42% in 2012. In order to preserve the medium-term stability of the system, the CNB must require a gradual increase in reservations in such a situation. What, I must say, we were left embarrassed by was the amount of lobbying by banks against increasedbookings, in such a way that the impact of the increase in provisions on banks' balance sheets was untruely inflated. The exaggeration factor was a whopping 3-4 times! Regardless of everything I have said before about the banking sector, as a factor of stability, I must say that this behavior undermines the credibility of institutions that would have to take great care precisely about the chalk of inosti. The errors of their assessments have, in fact, proven to be much greater than the errors of the Government's quantitative assessments that we have recently encounteredif. Many probably don't even understand what reservations are? This is simply an accounting statement of the likelihood that a loan that is not repaid will not be duly charged in full. Thus, banks ensure that they have sufficient capital in case they cannot collecttheir receivables. It is important to say that when extracting reservations, the bank does not have to give any money to anyone, nor allocate it to a special account. He just recognizes the existence of the risk and that's it. Reservations are necessary to ensure that the banking system remains stable and in the event that loans that are not serviced today are not duly managed to be collected even in the future, that is, that the value of the collateral fails to cover the bank's overdue receivables. It is true that the increase in reservations reduces the profitability of the banking system, however, it permanently reduces it only in case the reservation was really necessary, i.e. that the bank fails to collect its claim. Otherwise, the reservation is released and increases profits. In other words, ifthe reserve of attia is excessive, banks will make their profits in the future, instead of showing it today, although they are not sure that it has actually been realized. In the future, however, it is possible that the capital adequacy of banks will gradually decrease. In this situation, the coverage of bad placements with reservations should be gradually increased towards 50%, in order to maintain the high otof the banking system, and therefore the unquestionable financial stability in Croatia. In this sense, even an increase in bookings will not occur in one step but gradually, in a couple of years. This will reduce the stated profits of banks in the short term, but in the medium term they will, sit by, ensure adequate stability of the system, and on the other hand it will allow banks to increase profits in the future. It is clear to me that bankers are not happy about the delay in the statement of profits, that is, the possibility of paying profits, but regulators, unlike them, someone would add and unlike politicians, they should not be myoptical, but take into account the stability of the system in the middle of it m/long term. You can be sure that we will be just as happy as you are when and if it is established that it is possible to release reservations. To understand the risks facing the system, it is enough to look at what has happened in the EU over the last four years. Half of eu members have been through a major or minor banking crisis. Here I do not mean the usual bankruptcies of banks, which always happen, but about systemic events that have affected 10 percent or more of the assets of banking systems. In a large number of countries, a larger or significant part of the banking system, needed assistance, such as Ireland, Netherlands, Slovenia, Belgium, Cyprus, Greece, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, V. Britain, Spain... even Germany or Austria, not to mention Iceland, as a non-member of the EU, or the USA, where the crisis started. In addition, the high level of overdue uncollected receivables, which is not resolved but is pending an increase in the value of collateral in the dalekoj and uncertain future, is also a brake on the growth of new placements, as Raiffeisen Bank, as the second largest lender in Central and Eastern Europe, these days in its analysis notes. It blocks capital in the long term and reduces the likelihood that good long-term projects will be financed. Correct risk recognition is also essential so that new loans do not end up with borrowers who will not generate economic growth. In order to deal with bad placements, however, banks are absolutely right, it is extremely importantbut to improve the efficiency of the judicial system. A few words, finally, about the future of Croatia in relation to the joint European supervision, single supervisory mechanism (SSM), which starts in 7 months. The question is whether Croatia will take advantageof the possibility of op t-in, i.e. joining the mechanism, which is mandatory for all eurozone countries and leaves the possibility of joining all EU countries. After it was decided at the EU Economic and Financial Council in Dublin last month that the rights and obligations of all SSM member states would be the same, whether they are part of the eurozone or not, we are one step closer to the option of accession, but it is too early to reach a final conclusion. The coming months should bring answers to many questions that have not yet been clarified. One is the aforementioned analiza of bank assets, which precedes the launch of the SSM. The design of the criteria for defining the riskiness of assets will be extremely important, as will the implementation of common standards. In this regard, the single standard for the definition of NPLs, on which the EBA works, willdetermine on what basis the common supervisory mechanism and the generally harmonised EU regulatory standard are built. It is also extremely important how the resolution mechanism for troubled banks will be designed. The Bank Restructuring and Resolution Directive (BRR) should be proposed by the middle of this year, its key details are currently being discussed, but establishing a common resolution mechanism for troubled banks, as this week's statement by Germany'sNistra finance warns, will not be an easy job. Without a quality resolution mechanism, however, the banking union remains sketchy. In any case, with or without the EU, Croatia also needs a more efficient and clearer resolution mechanism for banks in trouble. We canstart working on it right away. One thing is certain, in the next year and a half, we are looking at a new amendment to almost the entire legislation regulating the banking sector. A new ZOKI is already in the works. The following are the implementations of the standards of the European Banking Association, CRR, BRR, all over 10,000 pages. I know it's hard for you to keep track of, but, believe me, it's not easy for us anymore. So don't accuse us, we've become unpopular enough during this crisis anyway. To paraphrase Stanley Fischer once again, this time from his farewell speech this week at the governors' meeting at Bank for International Settlements, where he roughly said about central bankers: Until a few years ago we were very popular, although few understood exactly what we were doing, today they know little more, but we've become quite unpopular. From this, however, one should not draw the wrong conclusion. We must continuously continue to explain what and why we do it. And persevere with it. I hope this exposure also partially helps this endeavor. Thanks pouringafter!
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a prof. dr. Borisa Vujia na 16. znanstveno- strunoj konferenciji Hrvatsko novano trite Objavljeno: 16.5.2013. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a 16.5.2013. 16. znanstveno-struna konferencija Hrvatsko novano trite Opatija 16.5.2013. Dame i gospodo, izuzetno mi je zadovoljstvo da vam se mogu obratiti na 16. konferenciji Hrvatskog novanog trita. Bankovna i ekonomska kriza poela je 2007. godine u SAD-u, prelila se 2008. u Europu i u drugom dijelu te godine i na Hrvatsku. Od tada, Hrvatska je u recesiji ili stagnaciji. Jesenas sam na Ekonomskom fakultetu u Zagrebu govorio o makroekonomskim uzrocima i posljedicama krize u Hrvatskoj, o dobrim i loim izborima politika da se iz nje izae, kao i o politikoj ekonomiji tih izbora. Krenuvi pripremati ovaj dananji nastup, proitao sam ovaj vikend na web stranici HNB-a ponovo to izlaganje i zakljuio da tome ne bih imao neto posebno dodati ni sada, pola godine kasnije. Mogao bih taj govor jednostavno ponoviti. Danas bih zato htio neto vie rei o regulaciji bankovne industrije, regulatornim promjenama koje se odnose na bankovni sektor i o budunosti Hrvatske u toj dimenziji. Dakle, htio bih neto rei o temi koja je u sreditu panje cijele financijske industrije, jo od poetka krize, o kojoj na razliitim mjestima raspravljamo na tjednoj frekvenciji, a koja kod nas jo nije dobila zasluenu pozornost. Paul Volcker je, nedavno, provokativno izjavio da je zadnja stvarno korisna inovacija u bankovnom sustavu bio izum ATM-a (bankomata). Radi se, naravno, o odreenom pretjerivanju, no jasno je to je smisao te poruke. Deregulacija i takozvane financijske inovacije koje su je slijedile, nisu pomogle financijskoj stabilnosti - upravo suprotno. Da bismo shvatili sveobuhvatne i duboke regulatorne promjene bankovnog sustava koje se danas dogaaju, odnosno da bi ih mogli smjestiti u pravu perspektivu, potrebno je podsjetiti se gdje je regulacija bankovne industrije bila prije desetak godina. 1999. godine u Sjedinjenim Amerikim Dravama je, nakon gotovo sedam desetljea od donoenja, opozvan Glass-Steagal zakon. On je uveden nakon velike ekonomske krize (Great Depression), 1933. godine, kako bi osigurao odvojenost investicijskog bankarstva od tradicionalnog bankarstva, koje se zasniva na uzimanju depozita i davanju zajmova. Glass-Steagal zakon je donesen kao regulatorni odgovor na zadnju veliku gospodarsku i financijsku krizu prije ove u kojoj jo jesmo. Njegovo ukidanje predstavljalo je najznaajniji korak do tada u procesu koji se krajem devedesetih i u prvoj polovici 2000-tih nazivao deregulacijom financijskog sustava. Godine 2004. usvojen je takozvani Basel II standard regulacije banaka. On se pokazao neadekvatnim tijekom krize, budui daje koliina kapitala koji su banke drale bila premala, upravljanje rizicima neadekvatno, a znatan dio prudencijalne uloge preputen rejting agencijama, pa posredno i samim bankama. Openito govorei, poetkom ovog tisuljea, u modi je bio takozvani soft touch regulation (meka regulacija), promoviran prvenstveno iz bankarskog centra Europe i svijeta - Velike Britanije, odnosno od strane tamonjeg regulatora - FSA. Dapae, mnogi su promovirali ideju daje najbolja vrsta regulacije bankovnog sustava - samoregulacija. U SAD-u, pak, bila je prisutna fragmentacija regulatornog aparata na mnotvo institucija, esto bez dovoljne ekipiranosti, koordinacije i jasne nadlenosti. Nisu, naravno, svi u to vrijeme bili uvjereni da je takav pristup meke regulacije bankovnog sektora najbolji put, no mo utjecaja najveih financijskih centara uinila je svoje. Kada je prvi put, poetkom krize 2007. godine, taj deregulirani sustav stavljen na stress-test, pokazao se potpuno neadekvatnim. To je uinilo bolno oitom potrebu za reformom regulatornog okvira i od tada ona traje. Njena ideja je, od poetka, manje rjeavanje akutnih kriznih problema, a vie uspostavljanje vre regulacije bankovnog sustava koja e smanjiti mogunost izbijanja velike financijske krize poput ove s ijim posljedicama smo i dalje suoeni. Krize koja je poela kao kriza financijskog sustava, a razvila se u makroekonomsku krizu, te, napokon, duniku krizu u dijelu razvijenih zemalja. Regulatorne reforme imaju niz ciljeva. Jedan je poveati kapital bankovnih institucija. Vea kapitaliziranost, a manja zaduenost, garancija je vee stabilnosti banaka. Drugi je uiniti velike financijske institucije u sreditu sustava, odnosno sustavno vane institucije, jo otpornijima, zahtijevajui od njih da imaju jo viu kapitalnu adekvatnost i strou kontrolu rizika. Trei je poveati transparentnost poslovanja i uiniti veze i izloenosti u financijskom sustavu transparentnijima svim sudionicima. etvrti je uspostavljanje mehanizma za rjeavanje problema u sustavno vanim velikim institucijama, odnosno mehanizma za njihovo restrukturiranje, uz to manji rizik/troakza porezne obveznike. Napokon, cilj je regulirati i podruja financijskog sustava direktno i indirektno povezana s bankama, koja su ponekad i izravan supstitutza bankarske poslove, a koja do sada nisu bila regulirana, ili su bila slabo regulirana, poput takozvanog bankarstva u sjeni (shadow banking) i trgovanja izvedenicama. Napokon, naglasak se stavlja na makroprudencijalne regulatorne mjere, koje smo u Hrvatskoj i do sada vrlo uspjeno koristili, te su danas priznate kao vrlo korisno iskustvo. Usporedno s tim globalnim regulatornim promjenama, EU je krenula potpuno novim putem koji bi trebao rezultirati bankovnom unijom na podruju eurozone, odnosno EU. Posljedica krize u eurozoni je uvjerenje daje jedini nain za odrivost projekta monetarne unije raskidanje veze izmeu rizika banaka i rizika pojedinih drava u kojima te banke dominantno posluju, a to je mogue postii samo uspostavom bankovne unije. Drugi oit razlog za uspostavljanje bankovne unije je injenica da na zajednikom europskom tritu banke djeluju transnacionalno, a nadzirane su nacionalno, bez ha rmo nii ranih kriterija nadzora, ukljuujui temeljne definicije poput loih plasmana. Fragmentiranost regulatornog okvira funkcioniranja bankovnog trita dovela je do toga da se tijekom krize naruila i jedna od temeljnih sloboda zajednikog trita EU - slobode kretanja kapitala. Za sedam mjeseci supervizija svih sustavno vanih, odnosno veih banaka na podruju eurozone prelazi u nadlenost zajednikog supervizora - Europske sredinje banke. Zajednika supervizija, meutim, ne moe efikasno funkcionirati bez zajednikog okvira za rjeavanje problematinih banaka odnosno restrukturiranje banaka. Prijedlog te direktive, Bank Restructuring and Rehabilitation Directive (BRR), oekuje se polovicom ove godine, no jasno je da usvajanje tog okvira nee biti jednostavno, budui da podrazumijeva mogunost neke vrste podjele fiskalnih trokova rjeavanja problematinih banaka. No, bez tog mehanizma, vrlo teko je zamisliti efikasan zajedniki nadzor bankovnog sustava, odnosno bankarsku uniju. Trei stup bankovne unije - zajedniko osiguranje depozita - komponenta je koja e najvjerojatnije najkasnije doi na red, budui da je najmanje suglasnosti oko neophodnosti i dizajna tog mehanizma na razini bankovne unije. Razlog je, opet, preuzimanje zajednike, implicitno fiskalne, odgovornosti za osigurane depozite. Kao regulatorni okvir za Basel III, CRD IV (Capital Requirement Directive IV), kao i za stvaranje bankovne unije, EU je proizvela impresivnu koliinu materijala, za sada, tvrde mi oni koji su, pretpostavljam, brojali, preko 10.000 stranica. Osim viih kapitalnih zahtjeva i stroih zahtjeva za upravljanje rizicima, vrlo vaan bit e dio regulative koji se bavi standardiziranjem definicije loih plasmana (NPLs). Standardizacija u tom podruju neophodan je preduvjet za uspostavu jedinstvenog nadzornog sustava. Krajem ove, a najkasnije do sredine idue godine, na temelju zajedniki ustanovljenih kriterija, provest e se kontrola aktive banaka, da bi se ustanovila eventualna potreba za dodatnim kapitalom, odnosno da bi se zadovoljili novi, stroi zahtjevi u pogledu kapitalne adekvatnosti. To e biti izuzetno vaan i izazovan projekt. Nakon to on bude proveden trebalo bi biti lake usporeivati pokazatelje bankovnog sustava razliitih zemalja. Trenutni problem je da postoji neujednaena praksa definicije loih plasmana, tako da se sloeni mehanizmi ocjene rizika i potrebe za kapitalom primjenjuju na relativno arbitrarnu osnovicu. Meutim, ta bi vjeba mogla znaajno poveati kapitalne zahtjeve pojedinih banka. Na neki nain, ona se moe shvatiti i kao istilite bankovne unije. Ono to e u najveoj mjeri determinirati rezultate te kontrole, bit e definiranje kriterija po kojima e se provesti ocjena rizinosti aktive. Nema sumnje daje nova regulativa bankovnog sustava neophodna. Kriza je pokazala koliko je pogrena bila deregulacija bankovnog sustava tijekom zadnjih petnaestak godina. Trokovi financijskih kriza su, naime, vrlo visoki. Na globalnoj razini, u prosjeku, blizu 20 posto BDP-a, to kroz izravne trokove spaavanja banaka, to kroz izgubljeni BDP. U Hrvatskoj okvirne procjene govore da je izravni troak velike bankovne krize prve polovice 90-tih iznosio oko 30 posto BDP-a, a krize manjih i srednje velikih banaka, krajem 90-tih, oko 5 posto BDP-a. Zbog toga trokovi poveanja kreditnih mari uslijed zahtjevnije, odnosno skuplje regulacije imaju opravdanje. Procjene uinka viih kapitalnih zahtjeva u okviru Basel III regulacije na poveanje kreditne mare najveih banaka kreu se od 8 do 16 baznih poena (IMF i BIS). To nije puno, imajui na umu trokove bankovnih kriza. Problem je, meutim, to se vii kapitalni zahtjevi sada dogaaju u situaciji stagnacije, tako da djeluju procikliki. Dobar dio zaotravanja regulatornih zahtjeva je vremenski rasporeen, da bi imao manji procikliki uinak, meutim sama trita ve sada trae jau kapitaliziranost. To je posljedica greaka iz prolosti, jer je otrija regulacija kapitalnih zahtjeva i upravljanja rizicima trebala biti odgovor na naglu ekspanziju financijskog sektora. Umjesto toga, deregulacija je, na tinjajui porast rizinosti bankovne aktive, samo dolila benzin. Sada se regulacija zaotrava u suboptimalnom trenutku, tijekom krize. No, to ne znai, kako neki sugeriraju, da sada ne treba postaviti regulatorne zahtjeve na zdrave temelje. Jednostavno, radi se o analizi trokova i koristi. Trokovi prelabave regulacije, kako pokazuje iskustvo, vii su od proputenog rasta BDP-a uslijed adekvatne regulacije. Radi se o slinom fenomenu kao i kod inflacije. U kratkom roku, viom stopom inflacije je ponekad, uz odreene uvjete, koji se prvenstveno odnose na velike zatvorene ekonomije, mogue potaknuti viu stopu rasta, no ve u srednjem roku, kako pokazuje iskustvo i istraivanja, trokovi inflacije su vei nego kratkorona korist koja se njome postie. Zbog toga je danas temeljni cilj sredinjih banaka ouvanje stabilnosti cijena. Bez nje nema odrivog gospodarskog rasta. Drugi cilj sredinjih banaka, onaj novijeg datuma - financijska stabilnost sustava - postie se prvenstveno postavljanjem adekvatnog regulatornog okvira. To znai da sredinje banke ne moraju neophodno imati ulogu supervizora banaka, ali trebaju imati ulogu u dizajniranju regulatornog okvira koji se odnosi na kapitalnu adekvatnost, likvidnosne zahtjeve i makroprudencijalne instrumente u odravanju financijske stabilnosti. U tom kontekstu, ne zaboravimo da su danas rizici i dalje visoki zbog izuzetno ekspanzivnog globalnog karaktera monetarne politike. Ukoliko pogledate trite na kojem su prinosi na neke vrste imovine s rejtingom CCC na razini od 7 posto, onda se morate zapitati o odrivosti odnosa rizika i cijena. Gdje je u svemu tome Hrvatska? U Hrvatskoj, to danas svi priznaju, imamo bolju regulatornu politiku bankovnog sustava nego to je to bio sluaj u EU ili SAD-u. Mi vodimo kontracikliku regulatornu politiku. Kapitalne zahtjeve smo poveali prije krize, a to je jednako vano, uveli smo cijeli niz mjera, koje se tek u novije vrijeme nazivaju makroprudencijalnim politikama, to je dodatno povealo kako koliinu regulatornog kapitala bankovnog sustava prije krize, tako i pojaalo likvidnosne rezerve banaka. Zbog toga je danas kapitalna adekvatnost banaka u Hrvatskoj 20,5 posto - najvia u EU - te hrvatske banke nemaju problem dokapitalizacije u situaciji kada je kapital postao skup. Njihove banke majke, kao i mnoge druge banke u 'starim' lanicama EU, u znatno su teoj situaciji, jer moraju poveavati kapital u situaciji kada perspektiva bankovnog sustava ne izgleda niti priblino tako dobro kako je to bio sluaj prije krize. U situaciji kada je povrat na kapital banaka pao na niske jednoznamenkaste razine, ili je negativan. Ukupne porezne stope koje banke plaaju na razini grupacija su sada oko 45 posto, a regulativa ide za time da bail-in uini neupitnim. Drugim rijeima, troak spaavanja banke e platiti vlasnici redovnog i hibridnog kapitala, dok e neosigurani kreditori i deponenti postupkom tzv. bail-in-a doi na njihovo mjesto. Taj smo postupak prvi put na djelu vidjeli nedavno, tijekom Ciparske krize. U takvim uvjetima kapital je postao skup. U tom kontekstu treba rei i to kako je naivno tvrditi da banke ne dijele sudbinu gospodarstva, kako se esto u Hrvatskoj moe uti. S odreenim vremenskim pomakom, one ne mogu nego slijediti sudbinu gospodarstva u kojem posluju. Relevantna istraivanja pokazuju da je nizak rast BDP-a temeljna determinanta bankovnih kriza, zajedno s visokom inflacijom, naglim priljevima kapitala i brzim rastom kredita, loim upravljanjem bankama (na pojedinanoj razini) i niskom efikasnou pravnog sustava. Najbolja ilustracija kontraciklinosti regulatorne politike u Hrvatskoj je regulatorni troak. Za razliku od zemalja iz kojih dolaze banke majke, regulatorni troak u Hrvatskoj je HNB prvo poveavao u fazi nagle ekspanzije kreditne aktivnosti banaka, da bi ga, nakon poetka krize, znatno smanjio. Regulatorni troak smanjenje s 2,13 postotnih poena, koliko je iznosio u prvih devet mjeseci 2008. godine, na 0,8 postotnih poena danas. To je, zajedno s protuciklikim rezervama izgraenim prije krize, omoguilo da 2009. godine Hrvatska ne mora zatraiti aranman s MMF-om, budui da je domai bankovni sustav imao dovoljno kapaciteta za financiranje domaih potreba, u situaciji kad su trita bila zatvorena. Iz dananje perspektive vjerojatno bi se moglo zakljuiti da bi bilo bolje da je ve tada zatraen aranman s MMF-om, budui da bi to vjerojatno ubrzalo strukturne reforme, no to je pitanje politike ekonomije, kojim se danas neu baviti. Ono to je nepobitno jest to daje kontraciklina regulatorna i monetarna politika ostavila mogunost izbora nositeljima ekonomske politike - uiniti neophodne strukturne reforme sami, ili ui u aranman s MMF-om, pa to uiniti uz njihovu uvjetovanost. Da politika HNB-a nije bila kontraciklika, aranman s MMF-om bi bio neizbjean, kao to je to bio sluaj s nekim drugim zemljama. Isto tako, iako toga veina nije svjesna, ekspanzivna monetarna politika HNB-a omoguila je, ceteris paribus, posredno i neposredno nie fiskalne deficite i manji javni dug, izmeu ostalog i smanjujui rizike u bankovnom sustavu. Uslijed kontraciklike regulatorne politike i naglaeno ekspanzivne monetarne politike, u Hrvatskoj nije dolo do kontrakcije kredita privatnom sektoru do kakve je dolo u SADu, odnosno gotovo stagnacije kredita u eurozoni, iako je gospodarski rast bio znatno nii nego u SAD-u i eurozoni. BDP je u Hrvatskoj pao 11,8 postotnih poena u razdoblju od treeg kvartala 2008. do kraja 2012. godine, dok je stopa rasta kredita privatnom sektoru iznosila 15,2%. U SAD-u, u istom razdoblju, BDP je porastao 3,6%, iako su se krediti privatnom sektoru smanjili za 4,4%, a u eurozoni je BDP pao za 2,1%, dok su se krediti poveali za 3,1%. Dakle, monetarna politika i bankarski sustav oito nisu ti koji su Hrvatsku uinili jednom od najsporijih zemalja u oporavku od recesije, kao to, bez ikakvog razumijevanja stvarnosti, jo i danas neki tvrde. Dapae, monetarna politika i bankovni sustav su, kako eksplicitno i stoji u izvjeu rejting agencija, kao i u ocjeni MMF-a i investicijskih analitiara, onaj dio hrvatskog gospodarstva koji jo odrava ekonomsku stabilnost i rejting zemlje na razini na kojoj jesu. Oni koji nastoje i to, jedno od zadnjih uporita stabilnosti Hrvatske, unititi, moraju svima javno odgovoriti to nakon toga. to bi se, da uspiju u svojim namjerama, dogodilo s investicijskom perspektivom zemlje, to bi se dogodilo sa tednjom u bankovnom sustavu, kakve bi fiskalne posljedice za porezne obveznike to imalo, kakve bi bile perspektive zapoljavanja i kolike bi realne plae i mirovine nakon toga bile. Par rijei o politici rezervacija. Kao posljedica pet godina recesije ili stagnacije, udio dospjelih nenaplaenih potraivanja u bankovnom sektoru se znatno poveao. Na 14 posto, kod ega je svaki deseti kredit kuanstvima i ak svaki etvrti kredit dan poduzeima lo kredit. Kao posljedica, sjedne strane, rasta loih kredita, a s druge, slabije kreditne aktivnosti, i pokrivenost loih kredita rezervacijama je pala s 50% u 2008. na 42 posto 2012. Da bi se ouvala srednjorona stabilnost sustava, HNB u takvoj situaciji mora zahtijevati postupno poveanje rezervacija. Ono ime smo, moram to rei, ostali neugodno iznenaeni jest koliina lobiranja banaka protiv poveanja rezervacija i to na nain da se neistinito napuhavao utjecaj poveanja rezervacija na bilance banaka. Faktor pretjerivanja je bio nevjerojatnih 3-4 puta! Bez obzira na sve to sam rekao ranije o bankovnom sektoru, kao faktoru stabilnosti, moram rei da takvo ponaanje potkopava kredibilnost institucija koje bi jako morale voditi rauna upravo o kredi bi Inosti. Greke njihovih procjena su se, naime, pokazale znatno vee nego greke Vladinih kvantitativnih procjena s kojima smo se u zadnje vrijeme susretali. Mnogima vjerojatno nije ni jasno to su to rezervacije? To je jednostavno knjigovodstveni iskaz vjerojatnosti da se kredit koji se ne vraa uredno nee u cijelosti naplatiti. Tako banke osiguravaju da imaju dovoljno kapitala u sluaju da ne mogu naplatiti svoja potraivanja. Vano je rei da kod izdvajanja rezervacija banka ne mora nikakav novac nikome dati, niti izdvojiti na poseban raun. Jednostavno prepozna postojanje rizika i to je to. Rezervacije su potrebne kako bi se osiguralo da bankovni sustav ostane stabilan i u sluaju da se krediti koji se danas ne servisiraju uredno ne uspiju naplatiti ni u budunosti, odnosno da vrijednost kolaterala ne uspije pokriti dospjela nenaplaena potraivanja banke. Istina je da poveanje rezervacija smanjuje profitabilnost bankovnog sustava, meutim, ono ju trajno smanjuje samo u sluaju da je rezervacija zaista bila nuna, tj. da banka ne uspije naplatiti svoje potraivanje. U suprotnom, rezervacija se oslobaa i poveava dobit. Drugim rijeima, ukoliko su rezervacije pretjerane, banke e svoju dobit ostvariti u budunosti, umjesto da ju iskazuju danas, iako nisu sigurne da je ona doista i ostvarena. injenica je da je na bankovni sustav u kratkom roku izuzetno otporan na okove, pa i znaajne gubitke, prvenstveno zbog vrlo visoke kapitalne adekvatnosti. U budunosti, meutim, mogue je da e se kapitalna adekvatnost banaka postupno smanjivati. U toj situaciji, pokrivenost loih plasmana rezervacijama treba postupno poveati prema 50%, kako bi se odrala visoka otpornost bankarskog sustava, a time i neupitna financijska stabilnost u Hrvatskoj. U tom smislu niti poveanje rezervacija se nee dogoditi u jednom koraku ve postupno, kroz par godina. To e kratkorono smanjiti iskazanu dobit banaka, no u srednjem roku e, sjedne strane, osiguravati adekvatnu stabilnost sustava, a s druge e omoguiti bankama poveanje profitabiInosti u budunosti. Jasno mi je da bankari nisu sretni zbog odgode iskaza dobiti, odnosno mogunosti isplate dobiti, no regulatori, za razliku od njih, netko bi dodao i za razliku od politiara, ne smiju biti mioptini, ve voditi rauna o stabilnost sustava u sred nje m/dugom roku. Moete biti sigurni da emo biti jednako sretni kao i vi kad i ako se uspostavi da je mogue otputati rezervacije. Za shvaanje rizika s kojima se sustav suoava dovoljno je pogledati to se dogodilo u EU tijekom zadnje etiri godine. Polovica lanica EU prolo je veu ili manju bankovnu krizu. Tu ne mislim na uobiajene bankrote banaka, koji se uvijek dogaaju, ve na sistemske dogaaje koji su pogodili 10 i vie posto aktive bankovnih sustava. U velikom broju zemalja vei ili znatan dio bankovnog sustava, trebao je pomo, poput Irske, Nizozemske, Slovenije, Belgije, Cipra, Grke, Latvije, Litve, Estonije, V. Britanije, panjolske... ak i Njemake ili Austrije, da ne spominjemo Island, kao nelanicu EU, ili SAD, od kuda je kriza i krenula. Pored toga, visoka razina dospjelih nenaplaenih potraivanja koja se ne rjeava ve se eka poveanje vrijednosti kolaterala u dalekoj i neizvjesnoj budunosti, predstavlja i konicu rasta novih plasmana, kako i Raiffeisen banka, kao drugi najvei zajmodavac u sredinjoj i istonoj Europi, ovih dana u svojoj analizi primjeuje. Ona blokira kapital u dugom roku i smanjuje vjerojatnost da e se dobri dugoroni projekti financirati. Ispravno prepoznavanje rizika bitno je i zato da novi krediti ne bi zavrili kod dunika koji nee generirati gospodarski rast. Za rjeavanje loih plasmana, meutim, tu su banke potpuno u pravu, izuzetno vano je unaprijediti efikasnost pravosudnog sustava. Par rijei, na kraju, o budunosti Hrvatske u odnosu na zajedniku europsku superviziju, Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM), koja poinje za 7 mjeseci. Pitanje je da li e Hrvatska iskoristiti mogunost opt-in-a, odnosno prikljuenja tom mehanizmu, koji je obvezan za sve zemlje eurozone, a ostavlja mogunost prikljuenja i svim zemljama EU. Nakon to je proli mjesec na Ekonomskom i financijskom vijeu EU u Dublinu odlueno da e prava i obveze svih zemalja lanica SSM-a biti isti, bile one dio eurozone ili ne, mi smo korak blie opciji prikljuenja, no prerano je za donoenje konanog zakljuka. Idui mjeseci trebali bi donijeti odgovore na mnoga pitanja koja jo nisu razjanjena. Jedan je ve spomenuta analiza aktive banaka, koja prethodi pokretanju SSM-a. Dizajn kriterija za definiranje rizinosti aktive bit e izuzetno vaan, kao i implementacija zajednikih standarda. U tom pogledu i jedinstveni standard za definiciju loih kredita, na kojem radi EBA, kao i standardi rezervacija, odredit e na kojim temeljima se gradi zajedniki supervizorski mehanizam i openito harmonizirani regulatorni standard EU. Izuzetno je vano i kako e biti dizajniran rezolucijski mehanizam za banke u problemima. Bank restructuring and resolution direktiva (BRR) trebala bi biti predloena do polovice ove godine, o njenim kljunim detaljima upravo raspravljamo, no uspostavljanje zajednikog rezolucijskog mehanizma za banke u problemima, kako upozorava ovotjedna izjava njemakog ministra financija, nee biti lak posao. Bez kvalitetnog rezolucijskog mehanizma, meutim, bankarska unija ostaje nedoreena. U svakom sluaju, sa ili bez EU, i Hrvatskoj je potreban efikasniji i jasniji mehanizam rezolucije banaka u problemima. Na njemu moemo odmah poeti raditi. Jedno je sigurno, u iduih godinu-godinu i pol, eka nas nova izmjena gotovo cjelokupnog zakonodavstva kojim se regulira bankovni sektor. Ve je u pripremi novi ZOKI. Slijede implementacije standarda European Banking Association, CRR, BRR, svih preko 10.000 stranica. Znam da je vama to ve teko pratiti, ali, vjerujte, nije vie lako ni nama. Dakle, ne optuujte nas, ionako smo postali dovoljno nepopularni tijekom ove krize. Da jo jednom parafraziram Stanleya Fischera, ovaj put iz njegovog ovotjednog oprotajnog govora na sastanku guvernera u Bank for International Settlements, gdje je otprilike rekao o centralnim bankarima: Do prije nekoliko godina bili smo vrlo popularni, iako je malo tko razumio to tono radimo, danas znaju malo vie, ali smo postali prilino nepopularni. Iz toga, meutim, ne treba izvui pogrean zakljuak. Moramo kontinuirano nastaviti objanjavati to i zato radimo. I ustrajati u tome. Nadam se da i ovo izlaganje djelomino pomae u tom nastojanju. Hvala lijepo!  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation of the governor of the CNB, prof. Dr. Boris Vuji at the 18th Scientific-Professional Conference Croatian Money Market
text: Boris Vujcic, Governor of the Presentation for the 18th scientific and professional conference Croatian Money Market Opatija, 7 May 2015. 1. General economic situation and growth prospects In 2014, the Croatian economy concluded with a real-terms fall in GDP of 0.4%, continuing a streak of six years of consecutive contractions in real economic activity (Figure 1) . The recovery in economic activity was very weak and anemic and took place in conditions of high foreign indebtedness, pronounced macroeconomic imbalances and structural shortcomings of the domestic economy. On the whole year, investments (-4.0%) were significantly reduced and the decline in government spending (-1.9) was noticeable, primarily due to fiscal consolidation measures taken. Figure 1. Fundamental problems, however, remain present. The unfavourable situation in the labour market in the form of high unemployment as well as the continued deleveraging of the population are greatly recovery of personal consumption. Furthermore, the high and rising level of public debt and the necessity to reduce the deficit to an acceptable level, including within the excessive deficit procedure, require a stronger fiscal adjustment in the years ahead. In this regard, for the recovery of domestic demand, the problem of investment recovery remains the key. It will primarily depend on the success of attracting foreign direct investment, especially those in the activities of internationally exchangeable goods, but also on the dynamics of withdrawing funds from EU funds. Finally, the structure of the Croatian economy, in which exports participate with a share of less than 40%, and also contains a relatively high import component, means that the strengthening of net exports that positively contributes to GDP growth, so far has only a limited impact on the overall growth of the domestic economy. What is encouraging is the fact of the rapid and successful adaptation of the export sector to eu entry and exit from CEFTA. In the long run, the only implementation of structural reforms to improve the investment and business environment in general could create the preconditions for stronger economic growth. Although some progress has been made, Croatia still lags far behind other EU countries and, more specifically, Central and Eastern Europe, so the scope for further improvements is significant. According to the World Bank, based on the Doing Business 2008 and Doing Business 2015 reports, Croatia has made significant progress globally in a ranking that measures ease of doing business, but still ranks unenviably last among European Union countries (Figure 7). According to the Doing Business 2015 report, Croatia lags the most behind in the processes of obtaining a building permit and registering ownership, which can be linked to the inefficiency of public administration (Figure 8). Other business environment indicators, such as the Global Competitiveness Index, are similarly confirmed. All central and eastern European countries surveyed recorded lower PMR values in 2013, i.e. on average they have a lower level of product market regulation than Croatia. Slika 10. Expansion of CNB monetary policy The CNB's monetary policy orientation over the past fifteen years, unlike fiscal policy, has been highly countercyclical. This means that in the pre-crisis period, the CNB pursued a policy of curbing excessive lending activity of banks that led to unsustainable growth in personal consumption and the creation of external imbalances of the country, high foreign debt and a deficit in the current account of the balance of payments. Numerous restrictive measures, which often met with great resistance from domestic and foreign entities, accumulated liquidity reserves for future periods. Since the outbreak of the financial crisis, the CNB has acted extremely expansively, by creating primary money and releasing reserves, as well as a number of other incentive measures. The measures released more than 12% of liquidity GDP to banks. By comparison, while in the pre-crisis period 30% of the total assets of banks were immobilized by the regulatory requirements of the CNB, to date this regulatory cost has decreased below 17% of the total assets of banks (Figure 12). The CNB, through monetary and macroprudential policy measures, through the release of kuna and foreign exchange liquidity, while ensuring the sufficiency of international reserves, in conditions of maintaining exchange rate stability, has preserved the financial stability of the country in conditions of reduced capital inflows. At the same time, in many other countries, governments had to save banking systems with taxpayers' funds, which was not the case in Croatia. It should be noted that this was achieved in extremely unfavourable conditions in relation to the environment, since the cumulative fall in GDP since the end of 2008 in Croatia was the second largest, after Greece. At the same time, loans to businesses in Croatia increased by 10% by 10% by the end of last year compared to the end of 2008, while in the eurozone they fell by 7.5 percentage points. This illustrates the limited reach of monetary policy in a situation of structural inefficiencies of the economy. Figure 12. The assets of credit institutions held due to regulation include the accrued reserve requirement in KUNA, the allocated reserve requirement in foreign exchange, the marginal reserve requirement, the CNB's treasury records and the minimum required foreign currency receivables. Source: CNB The extreme expansion of the CNB's monetary policy is most easily recognised in the record high liquidity of the banking system. The average surplus of kuna liquidity of the banking system before the crisis ranged around HRK 1bn, around HRK 4.2bn between 2009 and 2014, and currently exceeds HRK 10bn (Figure 13). This should be added to the surplus foreign exchange liquidity of banks, which is currently around 1.2 billion euros. EUR (over HRK 9bn). Overall, banks had over 5% of excess liquidity GDP at the end of March, exceeding the euro area liquidity surpluses five times relative to their GDP (Figure 14). Figure 13. Interest rates in the interbank money market and yields on Treasury bills of the Ministry of Finance have been maintained at historically low levels for a long time (Figure 13), with yields on treasury bills falling for three years in a row. Since the end of 2009, there has also been a gradual decline in bank interest rates on loans to households and businesses (Figure 15). Thus, short-term interest rates for enterprises decreased by almost 5 percentage points, while the average interest rate on home loans dropped from 6.5% to 5.1%. Favourable liquidity also works to relax the criteria for granting loans, as confirmed by the results of the CNB's regular Bank Lending Survey (Figure 16). Figure 15. They are partly related to weak demand for loans, which is driven by the overload of businesses and households with debt, and their need for deleveraging, as well as generally low business and consumer optimism. In addition, recently a number of companies have been turning to other sources of financing, mainly abroad, where financing conditions are currently extremely favorable (Table 1). These are usually companies with better creditworthiness and financial opportunities that already have access to foreign markets, while smaller companies have to rely on the domestic banking market, where they often have difficult access due to their more riskiness, low capitalization and lack of collateral. Summarily, the character of the CNB's monetary policy is extremely expansionary throughout the crisis period, and within the framework of the existing instrumentation, the CNB has sufficient resources to continue the conduct of such a policy.
