Title: Presentation at the 20th conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange
text: Presentation by CNB Governor Dr. Zeljko Rohatinski at the 20th conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange Published: 29.10.2010. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 29.10.2010. 20th Conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange Sibenik 29.10.2010. It is my honor and pleasure to participate in the work of this Conference. After a truly comprehensive presentation by my colleague Zdravko Maric at the beginningof the tka, I had little left to say. Maybe just to point out some finesse that makes even some grades, which can otherwise be heard, should be viewed as quite relative. The fact is that at the end of a year that is judged to be the majority, at least the world's major economies, we have emerged from a period of technical recession. The rating for the eurozone is GDP growth of 1.6%, for the US and Japanese economies between 2.7% and 2.9%. Acceleration of economic growth of developing countries, amounting to almost 7%, within which in China over 10%, Indiesclose to 10%, etc. is a fact and gives the achieved growth of the economy in our most important trading partners, which, of course, had some implications for the Croatian economy. Equally optimistic are the forecasts for 2011, which in quantitative terms should not differ significantly from this year. However, unlike these, especially media exploited optimistic reviews, great caution still prevails in professional circles, there is no firm assessment that the crisis is over, nor the expectation that the recession cannot return. This is partly demonstrated by estimates for the III quarter of 2010 on GDP growth, which are unfavourable for the majority of the world's economies. But more than just quantifications, it is pointed out the problems that are present and that will continue to be present, and whicheven then have a direct impact on Croatia. First, it is noted that the recovery so far has been very partial and, as they say, fragile, with low private sector investment and very little change in the labour market. The population's propensity for consumption and borrowing in the world remains very low. There are high risks in the financial market, primarily in the eurozone and above all related to the financing of states in these markets. Developing countries, which achieved high growth in 2010, are judged to be entering the period of the pregrian economy, and this also means a renewed risk of forming the factors that generated the crisis in the first place. Thus, the acceleration of inflation, including the rise of prices in the capital market, the rapid growth of loans and the appreciation of the exchange rate. That is why these countries have already started to takemeasures to cool the conjuncture, which includes measures that are already well known in our country, and related to the drop of the Ital restriction. What is a particular problem now is the area, manner and intensity of economic policy action in both the European Union and America. It is believed that this space is now very narrow. On the one hand, central bank interest rates are at zero. On the other hand, although the private sector is reducing its indebtedness, this is more than compensated increasing public sector indebtedness and putting fiscal positions in - so they say - an unsustainable trajectory. The ability of macroeconomic policies to prevent a return to recession is generally considered to be much lower today than it was three years ago. And that is why the main priority is training for a possibleST reaction if necessary. In doing so, everyone agrees that fiscal policy plays a key role, as well as giving the deterioration of the state of public finances in the world the greatest risk to the possibility of a new crisis. This deterioration in the example of the eurozone means an increase in the current account deficit from 2% of BDP in 2008, to 6.3% in 2009 and to about 6.6% in 2010 and on this basis an increase in their public debt - at least in the part that is officially stated, and it is considered that not everything is there - from about 70% to 85%. We know that some countries have already started to introduce austerity measures, we know that these measures seem contractive in the short term. The general assessment is that there is no alternative, since further retention of high debt and a high current account deficit not only significantly reduces the development chances in the medium and long term, but also brings into drinkthe thinner credibility of monetary policy in terms of its ability to maintain low inflation in such conditions. In terms of monetary policy, primarily in the eurozone, it is still expansionary, but in 2011 we should expect a return towards a neutral policyof go and, in this context, the re-formation of positive interest rates of the European Central Bank. Because it is a unique assessment that the continued retention of the policy of low interest rates sits down the side increases the risks, and on the other hand delays the necessary adjustments in there alnom and in the financial sector. Of course, the necessity of a high degree of coherence between monetary and fiscal policy stands out, because there are two risks: the risk of monetary policy tightening too soon, and even greater is the risk of tightening too late. That is why everyone points out that, above all, it is necessary to establish a high credibility of fiscal policy: what is established must be achieved. The last, but not least, phenomenon in these world relations is a change in regulation, in which the most significant is Basel III, with an increasein capital base and liquidity on the banks' balance sheet, easily left a relatively long adjustment period some elements are felt already, and will be present in 2011. Now, if you'll let me, I'd like to say something about Croatia. We are, of course, part of theworld's Mr. Podar and financial crisis. The manifestational forms of this crisis are quite similar, but we cannot say that the causes of the crisis are the same. Nor can we say that the reaction of economic policy to the crisis was the same. And the question is whether we can get out of the crisis in the same way as the rest of the world. We know that in both America and Europe, the crisis was generated in the banking sector, and financially as a whole, and then it transferred to the real economy. We also know that wasn't the case with us. When you look at what has happened in Croatia sometime since 2007 to the present day, then it is clear that our crisis was primarily caused by the collapse of the entire model of economic growth that we had in the past ten years, which was based on the influx of foreign accumulation, which we did not use to build asmoke-oriented, competitive economy, capable of reducing its net debt. The consequence or, rather, the expression of all this was the net increase in debt between 2000 and 2008 of 27 billion euros, an increase in the foreign indebtedness rate from 53% to 83%, a rise in the current account deficit of the balance of payments from 2% to 9% of GDP. The emergence of the global crisis and its transfer to such an economy plagued by imbalances, burdened with debt, burdened by generally inefficiency, was an external shock, which interrupted or significantly reduced the flow of "fresh blood"- the influx of foreign money. Such an economy did not have the strength, the readiness or the knowledge, the observed country as a whole, to face it. It is said, it is a popular thesis, we entered the crisis later than others, so it is logical that we get out of it later. Unfortunately, that's not true. If we look at the beginning of the decline of both GDP and industrial production, both begin at the end of the I quarter of 2008, therefore, long before the Lehman Brothers case. Since then, this decline has been going on, here, for the full eight quarters; in the industry, it is cumulatively more than 12%, GDP is about 9%. The beginning of our decline was caused primarily by domestic factors. One of the main ones was the political cycle and its implications for the economy. It was what at these conferences ranstood out as a shining example, the IPOs of 2007 , which created the "bubble". When the political cycle ended, when there was no longer an attractive supply of shares from the state portfolio, then the actors ran out of new capital revenues. Primarily the population sector , i.e. small shareholders. Second, inflation happened to us. It used to be 2% - I round up all the numbers, not to bother you too much with decimals - then, in early 2008, it rose to 6%. Food, energy, as elsewhere in the world, but with us a lot of you, because our economic policy has behaved towards this inflation very tolerantly, our trade very enterprising, and our manufacturers very logically, pragmatically. And this reduced all disposable income, independent of their nominal movements. Finally, thecentral bank gets involved. With such a balance of payments deficit, with that level of foreign debt, we felt that something needed to be done and we activated all available measures to slow down credit activity at the time. We have never been restrictive, but kredits grew in 2006 approximately 22%, in 2007 15%, and in 2008 "only" 11%. Many, but not enough to satisfy all appetites, including the financial market. Finally, a period of low interest rates ended in the world. Since the cumulative 12 percent drop in industrial production, one half, and since the 9 percent drop in GDP, one-third has occurred before Lehman Brothers. Thus, his own "contribution" to the world economic crisis. Perhaps all this would have ended in one sharp downward trajectory of the conjuncture cycle dand the Lehman Brothers did not happen. But even if it wasn't for him, it's certain we'd have come into crisis eventually. The only question was what would be our trigger and how long it would take for it to be activated. Lehman Brothers, as the personification of everything that happened in the world, had two kinds of negative consequences for us. In the short term, of course, the stock market crash and the loss of financial assets, by approximately 45%, the panic of savers and the withdrawal of deposits, and financial markets closed for Croatia. There were also someunknowns about how foreign banks working in Croatia would behave. And, finally, it is no exaggeration to say that at one point we were really threatened with the danger of a moratorium on external obligations, above all to the state. At that time, the CNB reacted, laying off about one thirdof the total available foreign exchange funds in the country (12% of GDP). An alternative to this was to address the IMF. Both the Government and the CNB and I personally felt that this was not necessary, that we could get away with our own strengths if we do what the profession says that in such situationswhose work should be done. In a similar situation, I would have done the same thing again as I did then, but I think it was a mistake then, because we didn't do what needed to be done. The long-term effects of the global crisis were, of course, a 19% drop in export demand and a halving of foreign investment in 2009. Hence, the decline in economic activity in that year, unlike in 2008, was determined not only by the decline in personal consumption but by all the essential components in the structure of aggregate demand. It means: exports, investments and personal consumption. This is therefore what is commonly referred to as a period of free fall. The decrease and imports, by about one-quarter, which reduced the decline on the seated side, but also hit all those highly import-dependent parts of our economy. The only component that was not reduced was the potof the rose9 state. This period lasted approximately until the Second Quarter of 2009. Then some tendencies reached the point of inflection. First of all exports, because demand began to increase. The decline in personal consumption has also slowed considerably. Government spending continued to stagnate. Thus, at the beginning of 2010, the fall in GDP also decreased significantly, reaching approximately -0.8% quarterly. Our estimates, based on physical indicators, are that in the second part of the year the economy will practically enter a phase of stagnation. This will not be seen at interannual rates, which are likely to continue to be negative, but in terms of economic flow we are now in a stagnation phase. The whole of 2010 is significantly determined by the negative transmission of 2009 and what happened in the first two quarters. At the CNB, we estimate that the fall in GDP will be1.9 percent, although it is possible that it will be somewhat smaller, because the Bureau of Statistics for some not very clear reasons estimates a much more significant foreign exchange inflow from tourism, that is, the contribution of exports of services to the formation of GDP than we do in the CNB. Employment will also bereduced by about 5%, the mass pays 6%, investments by a further 12% and they are the only component that continues to fall and the question is how much longer it will fall. If we look at 2009 and 2010 together, then we have a 7.5% drop in GDP, employment by 7.5%, personal consumption by 11%, investment by 22%. And if we say that this is the price of the crisis that we have paid for in these two years, let's look, at the illustrations for, in the same way, the indicators that say that in the same period the fall in GDP in the eurozone was 2.5% (that is, only one third of our decline), in America it was not even there, and developing countries achieved cumulative growth of 9.5%. The worst is the state of investment. Their share of GDP in 2008 was 31%, and now it is 24%, not because we have cut austerity, but because there was no foreign savingsof it. And the share of foreign savings decreases from 9.5% to 2.2% of GDP. That's what we used to have, spend the way we spent, and now we don't have it anymore. As for imbalances, this crisis has led to one big, forced adjustment that is good, that would even be great withoutbeing done in the way it is. This is a reduction in the current account deficit of the balance of payments from just over 9% in 2008 to 2.8% in 2010. I say, it is a forced adjustment because it was not possible to finance imports, even one for which there was demand in the country, while exports are essentially stagnating. When we exclude ships and oil and oil products, then other exports grow very little or nothing and there is no talk of some new, enhanced export orientation. Of course, reducing the deficit also reduces the increment of foreign debt, which is also good. It was, say, 806.2 billion in 2008 and 802.3 billion this year. But as GDP also decreased by 7.5%, the country's indebtedness increased from 83% to 101% of GDP. Foreign investors are not very enthusiastic about this figure. It should still be borne in mind that the foreign indebtedness of the private sector is decreasing, and that the increase in debt is the result of exclusively public sector borrowing. True, it thereby relieved the pressure on the credit potential of domestic banks, but increasedexternal debt. As for the second deficit, the fiscal one, everything happened with him the opposite of what happened in the paymentbone. We at the CNB define the sector of the state somewhat differently (we include HAC and some other smaller items), so the figuresI present will differ somewhat from those presented a little earlier by our colleague Maric from the Ministry of Finance, but the trends are the same. More broadly, we increased the consolidated general government deficit from 2.7% of GDP in 2008 to 6.9% in 2010. This, of course, meant significantly increased financing needs: in 2008 they amounted to about 5% of GDP, last year 10%, and in 2010 if the state borrows by the end of the year and for the 750 million euros to be repaid at the beginning of next year - financing needs or borrowing rise to 15% of BDP. The implications are clear and should not be elaborated on specifically. In the monetary sphere, as far as loans are concerned, the fact is that, after stagnation in 2009, credit channels have been more strongly activated this year. Gross placements grow by 6%, and in this non-financial privatenom sector by 5.5%. Loans to enterprises increased about 8%, and to the population about 2%. In the growth of loans to enterprises a relatively significant role played by the so-called model A, made possible by reducing the reserve requirement and channeling these funds into HBOR, with all that goes with it . But the fact is that out of the available HRK 2 billion, just over 700 million were used. The question of why it's so far would take us. It should also be said that in parallel with the aforementioned growth in bank placements, the share of non-performing loans is also growing: at the end ofem in 2008 it was about 5%, and at the end of September 2010 it was about 10%. The increase is most pronounced in the enterprise sector. Such a growth in non-performing loans is also reflected in the profits of banks, which has been practically halved. And in such circumstances, it is difficult to expect somespeck of a tacular reduction in interest rates on loans, even after a further reduction in the passive interest rates of banks has been implemented. How do you look at 2011 in all of this ? We see that the starting bases are lean. The economy has just come into stagnation, investment is essentialabout diminished, something sensational from banks is not to be expected, psychosis is not good. Can our environment be helpful in this regard? We at the CNB also have some projections that are quite similar to the projections of the Croatian Government and which mostly say that, with all thislimitations and with the unchanged economic policy that we have now, gdp growth of approximately 1.5% is possible in 2011, which would roughly offset this year's decline, which will not significantly alter the economic situation, especially not in terms of job creation. However, in such a policy and in such a structure of supply and demand, GDP growth of 1.5% also requires an increase in imports by at least 5%. This means that if there is economic growth, we will also have to face an increase in the balance of payments deficit to about 4% of GDP anda further increase in foreign debt to about 103% of GDP. The fiscal deficit, as colleague Maric said, should be reduced, with tax revenues rising and budget expenditure stagnating, but still remaining above 6%. So, with such starting bases and with the existingone by cliff, we are actually trying to get back to that old, pre-crisscross pattern, with the consequences we felt in the crisis. I'm going to skip some of the things I was still thinking about and let me try to deduce in some way. The fact is that weentered the pre-crisis period with a completely devastated structure of the economy and the social structure of society. This reflected permanently high double deficits and ever-increasing debt, external and internal. Until the crisis, we did practically nothing to start changing that structure. On the contrary, in a way we were just ossifying her. When the crisis came, it was just a "trigger" for this whole model to just start collapsing. We were not prepared for this, because not only were warnings not heeded, both external and domestic, but simply no one had the strength to start changing anything more seriously. We're not ready for that now. All this has happened recently shows that we still believe that without, as Ms. Kosor popularly puts it, "painful cuts" we can live on. The belief is that the world's exit from the crisis will pull us out like a locomotive, so we will "tow" after it. That's not going to happen, and it's not going to let us act like that. And one more thing, which has been said many times before, but it does not hurt to repeat it once more. Our aggravated, intrinsic problem was, and especially now, a combination of the country's unsustainable fiscal position and high, rising foreign debt. This debt leaves no option but to gradually further reduce the current balance of payments deficit. Secondly, that we encourage exports, not only through incentive measures but also by directly incorporating all the potentials we have for this, including the potential of the state. And that at the same time we keep imports at a rational level, which also requires a restrictive policy of domestic demand, at leastem in the short term, from wages onwards. With all this, it is important - because it is the biggest item in the Croatian economy - to change fiscal policy. Not only in terms of rapidly reducing the deficit by reducing expenditure, but also by substantially changing the structure of expenditure, moving from consumption to investment. But not on investments in large-scale infrastructure, which is now being talked about, but in what can be sold in the world, directly. In such a policy, the CNB would be ready to ensure sufficient liquidity of the banking sector, to the extent necessary. By further reducing the reserve requirement, including by taking the measures we have shyed away from so far. A year ago, I mentioned the amount of HRK 10 billion. It wasn't a floss. I'm bringing him up now. In the meantime, unfortunately, it turns out that out of that 10 millionijards, so far we are not capable of using even the initial 2 billion. We will maintain the purchasing power of that money, both at home and abroad. If we improve model A, which is defective, and if we start applying model B, then the CNB can directly influence both the furtherreduction of interest rates for production and export. We will also adopt some measures, consistent with Basel III, that will aim to better protect the banking system from both non-performing loans and the dangers of decapitalisation. That's pretty much all the central bank can do at all . The rest is up to everyone else, especially the government, this one or another.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a dr. eljka Rohatinskog na 20. konferenciji Zagrebake burze Objavljeno: 29.10.2010. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 29.10.2010. 20. konferencija Zagrebake burze ibenik 29.10.2010. ast mi je i zadovoljstvo da sudjelujem u radu ove Konferencije. Nakon zaista sveobuhvatnog izlaganja kolege Zdravka Maria na poetku, meni je malo toga ostalo za rei. Moda samo da ukaem na neke finese zbog kojih i neke ocjene, koje se inae mogu uti, treba promatrati kao dosta relativne. injenica je da smo na kraju godine za koju se ocjenjuje da je veina, barem velikih svjetskih ekonomija, izala iz razdoblja tehnike recesije. Ocjena za eurozonu je rast BDP-a od 1,6%, za ameriku i japansku ekonomiju izmeu 2,7% i 2,9%. Ubrzanje gospodarski rast zemalja u razvoju, pa iznosi gotovo 7%, u okviru ega u Kini preko 10%, Indiji blizu 10% itd. injenica je i daje ostvaren rast ekonomije kod naih najznaajnijih trgovinskih partnera, to je, naravno, imalo odreenih implikacija i na hrvatsku ekonomiju. Jednako optimistine su i prognoze za 2011., koja se u kvantitativnom smislu ne bi trebala bitno razlikovati od ove godine. Meutim, za razliku od ovih, osobito medijski eksploatiranih optimistinih ocjena, u strunim krugovima i dalje prevladava veliki oprez, ne postoji vrsta ocjena da je kriza zavrila, kao ni oekivanja da se recesija ne moe vratiti. To dijelom pokazuju i procjene za III kvartal 2010. o rastu BDP-a, koje su za glavninu svjetskih ekonomija nepovoljne. No, vie od samih kvantifikacija ukazuje se na probleme koji su prisutni i koji e i dalje biti prisutni, a koji onda imaju izravni utjecaj i na Hrvatsku. Kao prvo, ukazuje se da je dosadanji oporavak bio vrlo parcijalan i, kako kau, krhak, s niskim investicijama privatnog sektora i vrlo malo promjena na tritu rada. Sklonost stanovnitva potronji i zaduivanju u svijetu je i dalje vrlo niska. Visoki su rizici na financijskom tritu, prije svega u eurozoni i prije svega vezani za financiranje drava na tim tritima. Za zemlje u razvoju, koje su u 2010. ostvarile visok rast, ocjenjuje se da ulaze u razdoblje pregrijane ekonomije, a to znai i u ponovni rizik da se formiraju initelji koji su i generirali krizu. Dakle, ubrzanje inflacije, ukljuujui i rast cijena na tritu kapitala, brzi rast kredita i aprecijacija teaja. Zato su te zemlje ve poele poduzimati mjere za hlaenje konjunkture, to ukljuuje i mjere koje su ve dobro poznate i kod nas, a odnose se na kap italske restrikcije. Ono to je sada poseban problem, to je podruje, nain i intenzitet djelovanja ekonomske politike i u Europskoj uniji i u Americi. Smatra se da je taj prostor sada vrlo uzak. S jedne strane, kamatne stope sredinjih banaka su na nuli. S druge strane, iako privatni sektor smanjuje svoju zaduenost, to je vie nego kompenzirano poveanjem zaduenosti javnog sektora i stavljanjem fiskalnih pozicija u - tako oni kau - neodrivu putanju. Openito se smatra da je sposobnost makroekonomskih politika da sprijee povratak recesije danas mnogo manja nego to je bila prije tri godine. I zato je osnovni prioritet osposobljavanje za mogunost reakcije ako za to bude potrebe. Pritom se svi slau da kljunu ulogu ima fiskalna politika, kao i daje pogoranje stanja javnih financija u svijetu najvei rizik za mogunost pojave nove krize. To pogoranje na primjeru eurozone znai poveanje tekueg deficita s 2% BDPa u 2008, na 6,3% u 2009. i na oko 6,6% u 2010. i po osnovi toga poveanje njihovog javnog duga - barem u dijelu koji je oficijelno iskazan, a smatra se da tu nije sve - sa otprilike 70% na 85%. Znamo da su neke zemlje ve poele uvoditi mjere tednje, znamo da te mjere kratkorono djeluju kontraktivno. Opa ocjena je da alternativa ne postoji, jer daljnje zadravanje visokog duga i visokog tekueg deficita ne samo da bitno umanjuje razvojne anse u srednjem i dugom roku nego i dovodi u pitanje kredibilitet monetarne politike u smislu njene sposobnosti da u takvim uvjetima odrava nisku inflaciju. to se tie monetarne politike, prije svega u eurozoni, ona je jo uvijek ekspanzivna, no u 2011. treba oekivati vraanje prema neutralnoj politici i, u tom kontekstu, ponovno formiranje pozitivnih kamatnih stopa Europske centralne banke. Zato to je jedinstvena ocjena da daljnje zadravanje politike niskih kamatnih stopa sjedne strane poveava rizike, a s druge strane odgaa nune prilagodbe u realnom i u financijskom sektoru. Naravno, istie se neophodnost visokog stupnja usklaenosti monetarne i fiskalne politike, jer postoje dva rizika: rizik da se monetarna politika zaotri prerano, a jo vei je rizik da se zaotri prekasno. Zato svi istiu da je, prije svega, potrebno uspostaviti visoki kredibilitet fiskalne politike: ono to se utvrdi, to se mora i ostvariti. Posljednja, ali ne najmanje vana, pojava u tim svjetskim relacijama je promjena regulative, u emu je najznaajniji Basel III, s poveanjem kapitalske osnovice i likvidnosti u bilanci banaka, lako je ostavljen relativno dugi rok prilagodbe neki elementi se osjeaju ve sada, a bit e prisutni i u 2011. Sada, ako mi dopustite, rekao bih neto o Hrvatskoj. Mi smo, dakako, dio svjetske gospodarske i financijske krize. Manifestacijski oblici te krize su dosta slini, ali ne moemo rei da su i uzroci krize isti. Ne moemo kazati ni da je reakcija ekonomske politike na krizu bila ista. A pitanje je da li i moemo iz krize izii na isti nain kao i ostali svijet. Znamo da je i u Americi i u Evropi kriza generirana u bankovnom sektoru, i u financijskom u cjelini, i da se onda prenijela na realnu ekonomiju. Znamo i da kod nas to nije bio sluaj. Kad se pogleda to se sve u Hrvatskoj zbivalo tamo negdje od 2007. do danas, onda je jasno da je naa kriza prije svega bila uzrokovana uruavanjem cijelog modela gospodarskog rasta koji smo imali unatrag deset godina, a koji je bio zasnovan na priljevu inozemne akumulacije, koju nismo iskoristili da izgradimo izvozno orijentiranu, konkurentnu ekonomiju, sposobnu da smanjuje svoj neto dug. Posljedica ili, bolje reeno, izraz svega toga bio je neto prirast duga izmeu 2000. i 2008. godine od 27 milijardi eura, poveanje stope inozemne zaduenosti s 53% na 83%, rast deficita tekueg rauna platne bilance s 2% na 9% BDP-a. Pojava svjetske krize i njeno prenoenje na takvu ekonomiju optereenu neravnoteama, optereenu dugom, optereenu openito neefikasnou, predstavljala je eksterni ok, koji je prekinuo ili bitno smanjio dotok "svjee krvi"- priljev stranog novca. Takva ekonomija nije imala snage, spremnosti niti znanja, promatrano zemlju u cjelini, da se s time suoi. Kae se, to je popularna teza, u krizu smo uli kasnije od drugih, pa je logino da iz nje kasnije i izaemo. Naalost, to nije istina. Ako gledamo poetak pada i BDP-a i industrijske proizvodnje, i jedno i drugo poinje krajem I tromjeseja 2008. godine, dakle, mnogo prije sluaja Lehman Brothers. Od tada taj pad traje, evo, punih osam kvartala; u industriji iznosi kumulativno vie od 12%, BDP-a oko 9%. Poetak naeg pada bio je izazvan prije svega domaim initeljima. Jedan od glavnih bio je politiki ciklus i njegove implikacije na gospodarstvo. Bilo je to ono to se na ovim konferencijama ranije isticalo kao svijetli primjer, IPO-i iz2007. godine , koji su stvorili "balon". Kad je politiki ciklus zavrio, kad vie nije bilo atraktivne ponude dionica iz dravnog portfelja, onda su akteri ostali bez novih kapitalnih prihoda. U prvom redu sektor stanovnitva, odnosno mali dioniari. Drugo, dogodila nam se inflacija. Prije je bila 2% - sve brojke zaokruujem, da vas previe ne gnjavim decimalama - onda je, poetkom 2008., porasla na 6%. Hrana, energija, kao i drugdje u svijetu, ali kod nas puno vie, jer se naa ekonomska politika ponaala prema toj inflaciji vrlo tolerantno, naa trgovina vrlo poduzetno, a nai proizvoai vrlo logino, pragmatino. I to je smanjilo sve raspoloive dohotke, neovisno od njihovog nominalnog kretanja. Konano, umijeala se i sredinja banka. S onolikim deficitom platne bilance, s onakvom razinom inozemnog duga, smatrali smo da je potrebno neto uraditi i aktivirali smo tada sve raspoloive mjere za usporavanje kreditne aktivnosti. Nismo nikad bili restriktivni, ali krediti su rasli u 2006. otprilike 22%, u 2007. godini 15%, a u 2008. "samo" 11%. Mnogo, ali premalo da se zadovolje svi apetiti, ukljuujui i financijsko trite. Napokon, u svijetu je zavrio period niskih kamatnih stopa. Od kumulativnog pada industrijske proizvodnje za 12 posto jedna polovina, a od pada BDP-a za 9 posto jedna treina dogodila se prije Lehman Brothersa. Dakle, vlastiti "doprinos" svjetskoj gospodarskoj krizi. Moda bi sve to zavrilo u jednoj otroj silaznoj putanji konjunkturnog ciklusa da se nije dogodio Lehman Brothers. No, i da ga nije bilo, sigurno je da bi mi doli u krizu kad-tad. Pitanje je bilo samo to e nam biti okida i koliko e vremena trebati da se on aktivira. Lehman Brothers, kao personifikacija svega onoga to se dogodilo u svijetu, za nas je imao dvije vrste negativnih posljedica. Kratkorono, naravno, pad burze i gubitak financijske imovine, za priblino 45%, paniku tedia i povlaenje depozita, a financijska trita su se za Hrvatsku zatvorila. Bilo je i nekih nepoznanica kako e se ponaati strane banke koje rade u Hrvatskoj. I, konano, nije pretjerano rei da nam je u jednom trenutku stvarno zaprijetila opasnost moratorija na vanjske obveze, prije svega dravi. Tada je HNB reagirao, otputanjem otprilike jednu treinu ukupno raspoloivih deviznih sredstava u zemlji (12% BDP-a). Alternativa tome bila je obratiti se MMF-u. I Vlada i HNB i ja osobno smatrali smo da to nije potrebno, da se moemo izvui vlastitim snagama ako radimo ono to struka kae da se u takvim situacijama treba raditi. U slinoj situaciji uradio bih opet isto to i tada, ali mislim da je to bila tada greka, jer nismo uradili to je trebalo uraditi. Dugoroni efekti svjetske krize su, naravno, bili pad izvozne potranje za 19% i prepolovljena strana ulaganja u 2009. godini. Otuda, pad ekonomske aktivnosti u toj godini, za razliku od 2008., nije odreen samo padom osobne potronje nego svih bitnih komponenti u strukturi agregatne potranje. Znai: izvoza, investicija i osobne potronje. To je dakle ono to se uobiajeno naziva razdobljem slobodnog pada. Smanjenje i uvoz, otprilike za jednu etvrtinu, to je sjedne strane umanjilo pad, ali je i pogodilo sve one visoko uvozno ovisne dijelove nae ekonomije. Jedina komponenta koja nije smanjena bila je potronja drave. To razdoblje trajalo je otprilike do III kvartala 2009. Tada su neke tendencije dole do toke infleksije. Prije svega izvoz, jer potranja se poela poveavati. Znatno je usporen i pad osobne potronje. Dravna potronja je i dalje stagnirala. Tako se na poetku 2010. i pad BDP-a znatno smanjio i kvartalno iznosi priblino -0,8%. Nae su procjene, na bazi fizikih pokazatelja, da e u drugom dijelu godine ekonomija praktiki ui u fazu stagnacije. To se nee vidjeti po meugodinjim stopama, koje e vjerojatno i dalje biti negativne, ali u smislu ekonomskog toka sada smo u fazi stagnacije. Cijela 2010. je bitno odreena negativnim prijenosom iz 2009. i onim to se zbivalo u prva dva kvartala. U HNB-u ocjenjujemo da e pad BDP-a iznositi 1,9 posto, iako je mogue da e biti i neto manji, jer Zavod za statistiku iz nekih ne ba sasvim jasnih razloga procjenjuje dosta znaajniji devizni priljev od turizma odnosno doprinos izvoza usluga formiranju BDP-a nego mi u HNB-u. Zaposlenost e biti smanjena za oko 5%, masa plaa 6%, investicije za daljnjih 12% i one su jedina komponenta koja i dalje pada i pitanje je koliko e jo padati. Ako promatramo 2009. i 2010. zajedno, tada imamo pad BDP-a za 7,5%, zaposlenosti za 7,5%, osobne potronje za 11 %, investicija 22%. I ako kaemo da je to cijena krize koju smo platili u ove dvije godine, pogledajmo, ilustracije radi, na isti nain, pokazatelje koji kau daje u istom razdoblju pad BDP-a u eurozoni iznosio 2,5% (dakle, samo jednu treinu naeg pada), u Americi ga nije ni bilo, a zemlje u razvoju ostvarile su kumulativni rast od 9,5%. Najgore je stanje u podruju investicija. Njihov udio u BDP-u 2008. je bio 31 %, a sada je 24%, ne zato to smo smanjili tednju, ve zbog toga to nije bilo strane tednje. A udjel strane tednje smanjenje s 9,5% na 2,2% BDP-a. To je ono to smo prije imali, troili kako smo troili, a sad vie nemamo. to se tie neravnotea, ova kriza je dovela do jedne velike, prisilne prilagodbe koja je dobra, koja bi ak bila odlina da nije uraena na nain kao to jest. To je smanjenje deficita tekueg rauna platne bilance s neto vie od 9% u 2008. na 2,8% u 2010. Kaem, to je prisilna prilagodba jer nije bilo mogue financirati uvoz, ak ni onaj za koji je postojala potranja u zemlji, dok izvoz u biti stagnira. Kad iskljuimo brodove te naftu i naftne preraevine, onda ostali izvoz raste vrlo malo ili nita i ne moe se govoriti o nekakvoj novoj, pojaanoj izvoznoj orijentaciji. Naravno, smanjivanjem deficita smanjuje se i prirast inozemnog duga, to je takoer dobro. On je, recimo, u 2008. iznosio 6,2 milijarde eura, a ove godine 2,3 milijarde eura. No, kako je i BDP smanjen za 7,5%, zaduenost zemlje poveala se s 83% na 101% BDP-a. Strani investitori nisu ba oduevljeni tom brojkom. Pritom treba jo imati na umu da se inozemna zaduenost privatnog sektora smanjuje, a da je poveanje duga rezultat iskljuivo zaduivanja javnog sektora. Istina, on je time smanjio pritisak na kreditne potencijale domaih banaka, ali je poveao vanjski dug. to se tie drugog deficita, onog fiskalnog, kod njega se sve dogaalo suprotno od toga to se dogaalo kod platnobilannog. Mi u HNB-u neto drugaije definiramo sektor drave (ukljuujemo HAC i jo neke manje stavke), pa e se i brojke koje iznosim poneto razlikovati od onih koje je malo prije iznio kolega Mari iz Ministarstva financija, ali trendovi su isti. Deficit konsolidirane ope drave u irem smislu poveali smo s 2,7% BDP-a u 2008. na 6,9% u 2010. To je, dakako, znailo i bitno poveane potrebe financiranja: u 2008. iznosile su oko 5% BDP-a, prole godine 10%, a u 2010. ako se drava zadui do kraja godine i za onih 750 milijuna eura koje treba vratiti na poetku sljedee godine - potrebe financiranja odnosno zaduivanje rastu na 15% BDPa. Implikacije su jasne i ne treba ih posebno elaborirati. U monetarnoj sferi, to se kredita tie, injenica je da su se, nakon stagnacije u 2009., kreditni kanali ove godine jae aktivirali. Bruto plasmani rastu 6%, a u tome nefinancijskom privatnom sektoru za 5,5%. Krediti poduzeima poveani su oko 8%, a stanovnitvu oko 2%. U rastu kredita poduzeima relativno znaajnu ulogu odigrao tzv. model A, omoguen smanjivanjem obvezne priuve i usmjeravanjem tih sredstava u HBOR, sa svim onim to uz to ide. Ali injenica je i to da je od raspoloivih 2 milijarde kuna iskoriteno tek neto vie od 700 milijuna. Pitanje zbog ega je tako daleko bi nas odvelo. Treba rei i to da usporedo sa spomenutim rastom plasmana banaka raste i udjel loih kredita: krajem 2008. on je iznosio oko 5%, a krajem rujna 2010. oko 10%. Porast je najizraeniji u sektoru poduzea. Takav rast loih kredita odraava se i na profitabiInost banaka, koja je praktiki prepolovljena. A u takvim okolnostima teko je oekivati i neko spektakularno smanjivanje kamatnih stopa na kredite, ak i nakon to se provede daljnje smanjivanje pasivnih kamatnih stopa banaka. Kako u svemu tome gledati na 2011 ? Vidimo da su polazne osnove mrave. Ekonomija je tek dola u stagnaciju, investicije su bitno smanjene, neto senzacionalno od banaka nije za oekivati, psihoza nije dobra. Moe li nae okruenje u tom smislu biti od pomoi? I mi u HNB-u imamo neke projekcije koje su dosta sline projekcijama hrvatske Vlade i koje uglavnom govore da je, uz sva ova ogranienja i uz neizmijenjenu ekonomsku politiku kakvu sada imamo, u 2011. mogu rast BDP-a od otprilike 1,5%, ime bi se otprilike neutralizirao ovogodinji pad, to nee bitno izmijeniti ekonomsku situaciju, pogotovo ne u smislu otvaranja radnih mjesta. No, pri takvoj politici i pri takvoj strukturi ponude i potranje, rast BDP-a za 1,5% zahtijeva i rast uvoza za barem 5%. To znai, ako doe do gospodarskog rasta morat emo se suoiti i s poveanjem deficita platne bilance na otprilike 4% BDP-a i s daljnjim rastom inozemnog duga na oko 103% BDP-a. Fiskalni deficit bi se, kao to je kolega Mari rekao, trebao smanjiti, uz rast poreznih prihoda i stagnaciju proraunskih rashoda, ali i dalje ostaje iznad 6%. Znai, uz takve polazne osnove i uz postojeu politiku mi se u stvari pokuavamo vratiti na onaj stari, predkrizni obrazac, s posljedicama koje smo osjetili u krizi. Preskoit u neke stvari o kojima sam jo mislio govoriti i dopustite da pokuam na neki nain zakljuiti. injenica je da smo u predkrizno razdoblje uli s potpuno devastiranom strukturom ekonomije i socijalnom strukturom drutva. Odraz toga su bili permanentno visoki dvojni deficiti i stalno rastui dug, vanjski i unutarnji. Do krize nismo poduzeli praktiki nita da tu strukturu ponemo mijenjati. Naprotiv, na neki nain smo je samo okotavali. Kad je kriza dola, to je bio samo "okida" da se cijeli taj model jednostavno pone uruavati. Na to nismo bili spremni, jer ne samo da se nisu sluala upozorenja, i vanjska i domaa, nego naprosto nitko nije imao snage da bilo to pone ozbiljnije mijenjati. Nismo to spremni niti sada. Sve ovo to se zbivalo u zadnje vrijeme pokazuje da jo vjerujemo da bez, kako to gospoa Kosor popularno kae, "bolnih rezova" moemo ivjeti i dalje. Uvjerenje je da e nas izlazak svijeta iz krize povui kao lokomotiva, pa emo se mi "lepati" za njim. To se nee dogoditi, niti e nam taj svijet dopustiti da se tako ponaamo. I jo neto, to je ve mnogo puta reeno, ali nije na odmet ponoviti jo jednom. Na osnovni, sutinski problem je bio, a pogotovo je sada, kombinacija neodrive fiskalne pozicije zemlje i visokog, rastueg inozemnog duga. Taj dug ne ostavlja nikakvu drugu mogunost nego da postupno dodatno smanjujemo tekui deficit platne bilance. Drugim rijeima, da potiemo izvoz, ne samo poticajnim mjerama nego i izravnim ukljuivanjem svih potencijala koje za to imamo, ukljuujui i potencijale drave. I da istodobno drimo uvoz na racionalnoj razini, to trai i restriktivnu politiku domae potranje, barem u kratkom roku, od plaa nadalje. Uz sve to bitno je - jer to je najvea stavka u hrvatskoj ekonomiji - promijeniti fiskalnu politiku. Ne samo u smislu brzog smanjivanja deficita smanjivanjem rashoda, nego i bitnom promjenom strukture rashoda, pomakom s potronje na investicije. Ali ne na investicije u krupnu infrastrukturu, o emu se sada govori, ve u ono to se moe prodati u svijetu, izravno. U takvoj politici HNB bi bio spreman osigurati dostatnu likvidnost bankovnog sektora, u mjeri koja bi bila potrebna. Daljnjim smanjivanjem obvezne priuve, pa i poduzimanjem mjera kojih smo se do sada libili. Prije godinu dana spomenuo sam iznos od 10 milijardi kuna. To nije bila floskula. Spominjem ga i sada. U meuvremenu se, naalost, pokazalo da od tih 10 milijardi zasad nismo sposobni iskoristiti niti inicijalne 2 milijarde. Odrat emo kupovnu snagu tog novca, i u zemlji i u inozemstvu. Ako unaprijedimo model A, koji je defektan, i ako ponemo primjenjivati model B, onda HNB moe izravno utjecati i na daljnje smanjivanje kamata za proizvodnju i za izvoz. Donijet emo i neke mjere, sukladne s Baselom III, koje e imati za cilj bolju zatitu bankovnog sustava i od loih kredita i od opasnosti dekapitalizacije. To je vie-manje sve to sredinja banka uope moe uraditi. Ostalo je na svima drugima, a napose na Vladi, ovoj ili nekoj drugoj.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Current economic situation in the country
text: The current economic situation in the country Published: 22.10.2011. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 21.10.2011. 21st Conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange Rovinj 22.10.2011. Condition: On the road to recovery or rushing into depression? The economy is in a state of stagnation, within which some imbalances have been reduced, but there are no stronger impulses to economic growth and structural changes, it faces increased external risks, and strong social and political resistance to change. This situation is not a surprise. In this context, I also recall last year's gathering in Sibenik. 1. A wave of moderate optimism spread around the world at the time as economies emerged from recession (the world -0.6% in 2009 to 5.1% in 2010; the eurozone -4.2% to 1.8%), but there were also strong warnings that: 95 this growth is partial and unstable with low private sector investment and no shiftin the labour market 95 high risk remains in financial markets (in particular the EU) 95 the deterioration of public finances is becoming a major macroeconomic problem, with rising public debt putting fiscal positions on an unsustainable trajectory 95 a small monetary policy room for manoeuvre; which all together does not preclude the possibility of a new recession 2. On the other hand, we pointed out that the crisis in Croatia is not only a reflex of the world crisis, but this one was a "trigger" that faced imbalances and irrationalities-ladenecono mij with an "external shock" that led to the collapse of the entire growth model from the previous period. A model based on the abundant yield of foreign capital that finances domestic consumption, instead of being spent to build an export-orientedand competitive economy. Therefore, there is no exit from the crisis without substantive reforms, contrary to unrealistic expectations that the continuation of the growth of the world economy and the completion of negotiations with the EU will be a "locomotive" that will pull the Croatian economy back without "painful rez". 3. What's happened since then. 3.1. Worldwide, external risks are effected, especially in the eurozone, so it has failed to maintain the growth dynamics of the previous year, and a further slowdown is expected for 2012. Eurozone: 1.8% (2010), 1.6% (2011), 1.1% (2012). In this: Italy 1.3% 0.6% 0.3% Germany 3.6% 2.7% 1.3% 3.2. In Croatia, the reforms and policy changes announced in the Economic Recovery Programme have been prolonged or "watered down". 4. Consequences for Croatia 4.1. Decrease in foreign demand for goods from the largest foreign trade partners. Italy (-11%) Germany (-3%), i.e. aggregated exports to these two countries that normally account for 30% of our total exports, a decrease of about 8%, expressed in current euros. True, this is partly offset by exports to the ostala market so that with a good tourist season (8.3%), total exports of goods and services will be 3.8% nominally higher than last year's. However, when these payment data are translated into GDP statistics and deflated by the corresponding price index, it emergedthat real exports of goods and services in 2011 were 1.5% higher than in 2013. decreased by 0.7%, which knocks gdp down by 0.3% 4.2 Unfavourable developments in financial markets and deterioration of perceptions of Croatia's economic performance (slow recovery, high external debt, high fiscal deficit,delayed reform...) significantly slowed the net inflow of foreign accumulation. In 2011, it amounted to about 370 million euros. euro, cost 45% less than in 2010 and ten times less than in 2008. Its relation to GDP decreased from 9.8% (2008) and 5.7% (2009) and 1.5% (2010) nand only 0.8% (2011). 4.3. The increase in the spread on government bonds in just a few months from 200 to 500 basic points (an indicator of the increased premium on investment risk in Croatia) was also transferred to the borrowing conditions of other sectors. Together with the downgrade of large foreign banks operating in Croatia, this has increased foreign sources of funds. An illustration of this is the fact that the interest paid on foreign debt increased from EUR 1.3 billion to 1.3 billion euros. euro in 2010 at an estimated 801.5 billion. euro in 2011 (by 15%), althoughthe level of debt stagnated, even slightly decreased. This is also transferred to the financing conditions in the country, so that, for example, when increasing the total debt of the consolidated general government in 2011 by about 11%, the interest paid increased by 22%. 4.4. CNB reaction At the beginning of the year- the release of additional liquidity with the aim of relatively reducing the dependence of banks from foreign sources of funds and the impact on interest rates. 95 lowering the reserve requirement rate from 14% to 13%, with the prospect of further descent to 11% (initial effect around HRK 3bn) 95 lowering the rate of minimum required foreign exchange receivables from 20% to 17% (effect of about 830m euros). euro). In addition, interventions were carried out on the foreign exchange market, predominantly on the side of demand for foreign currency, i.e. kuna broadcasting. To date, the CNB has bought 967m euros from the state. euro, emitting HRK 7.1bn, which entered domestic financial flows. Thus, through these channels, additional liquidity of, recalculated, about HRK 16bn was injected into the national economy, which is approximately 25% of the money. However, the effects of such increased liquidity on banks' credit activity and real economic flows have proven to berarely small, due to a series of problems in the sphere of transformation of increased liquidity into private sector loans. The causes of this are: 95 increased aversion of banks towards risk-taking in conditions when poor placements reached the level of 12% of total placements, in which plasmani companies are at a level of 19%. 95 clamping down on customers from further borrowing in conditions of increased uncertainty 95 lack of quality investment programmes 95 serious problems in the application of models A, B and C 95 the use of increased foreign exchange liquidity for harmonisablebalance sheets of banks, internally and in relations with mother banks 95 increased government borrowing needs. In such conditions, although total bank placements accelerated from 7.5% in 2010 to 10% in 2011, private sector loans slowed growth from 6.9% to about 5.5%, while net loans to the state accelerated growth from 14.7% in 2010 to 56% in 2011. In connection with this, the increased and productively uninhabited kuna liquidity begins to create strong depreciation pressures in the second half of the year, so the CNB has no choice but to give again the reductions by selling foreign currency to banks during the summer months in the amountof 419 million euros. euro, and in October to raise the reserve requirement rate again to 14%. All this is demonstrated by the unfoundedness of how expansionary monetary policy can, in itself, drive a real sector without inflation, because it does not take into account whether the sector iscapable of absorbing the increased liquidity of banks in post-described conditions and whether banking channels are sufficiently passable to transfer this liquidity. 4.5. The combination of a decrease in inflows and an increased price of foreign accumulation, along with stagnation of domestic savings and problems in the transformation of liquidity into loans, results in a further decrease in investments by 6.6%, of which in the private sector by about 9%. They are now 27% less in real terms than in 2008. This continues to be particularly affected by the construction sector (a further fall of 9.6%). 4.6. Thus, exports of goods and services and investments, which should be carriers of the recovery, were reduced by 2.8% in real terms in 2011 5. In such conditions, the possibility of production growth predominantly depends on domestic final consumption. In this area, however, there is no room forsignificant movements. Despite the real increase in the average net salary by about 2%, as a result of the reduced tax press, due to the reduced employment, the disposable income of the population stagnates, as well as loans, so that only thanks to prochanges in the structure of household demand (from investments to current consumption), personal consumption in 2011 will increase by about 0.4% overall. The situation is similar in the area of public spending where, however, due to increased interest expenditure and the rigidityof other budget expenditures, the total expenditure of the consolidated general government (including HAC) continues to grow faster than budget revenues. This results in a further increase in the fiscal deficit from a318bn to a318bn. kuna in 2010 to EUR 21 billion. in 2011, i.e. from 5.4% to 6.2% of the estimated GDP. This also increases public debt from 47% to 51% of GDP 6. Building on the decline in exports and investments, the stagnation of final consumption also results in a real decrease in aggregate demand for goods and services in 2011 by about 1%. In addition to changes in its structure, with the strengthening of demand for existential goods and services at the expense of investments, this results in this year and a real decrease in imports by 3.9% (in this import of equipment by about 15%). This is actually a key variable thatdredged the "statistical" picture in 2011. From it, in fact, two macro-balance effects arise: 6.1. A larger drop in imports since the fall in aggregate demand indicates an increased demand orientation towards domestic goods and services, resulting in GDP growing by about 0.5% 6.2. A bigger drop in imports since the drop in exports leads to a reduction in the current account deficit of the balance of payments from about 500m euros. euro in the last one at just 200m euros. euro this year, from 1.1% to just 0.5% of GDP, which also contributes to halting the growth of foreign debt. 7. Figure 2011 - two viewing angles 1. Affirmative: - after a decrease in the previous two years by a total of 7.2%, in 2011 negative tendencies in gdp movements were nevertheless halted 95 current account deficit of the balance of payments, as a key indicator of the macroeconomic imbalances, is reduced to a historical minimum 95 halting the growth of foreign debt and the degree of external indebtedness of the country, successful refinancing of this debt (it amounted to around 8013 billion this year), i.e. the investor's still-present beliefin the country's ability to service its external obligations 95 the same applies to the financing of the current budget deficit, for which purpose the general government managed to borrow grossly abroad by around EUR 2.5 billion. euro, although in both cases this is accompanied by theimportance of interest rates, which are an indicator that the degree of this trust is decreasing. 2. Warning: - GDP growth and reduction of the payment deficit were not achieved in a developmentally promising way, but by differential reduction of all key components of AGRegatta supply and demand. From there, the economy is not growing, but is still in the phase of degressive adaptation to external shock. 95 this adjustment is not, however, uniform, as it has not yet affected the public sector 95 as a result, a further increase in the fiscal deficit and continued rapid growth in public debt, which financial markets recognise as a fundamental problem and interpret as the country's unwillingness to implement the necessary reforms. 95 if the situation in this area does not change soon, it is possible to expectg to kill the credit rating, with all the consequences that result. 8. This is the situation with which we enter 2012. What's in store for us in it? (1) Although imports from Croatia are marginal for the eurozone, a further slowdown in its growth will also have a limiting effect on the demand for our products. In addition, it is difficult to expect that exogenous factors (meteorological conditions, political situation in the Mediterranean...) will be as favorable for our tourism as they were this year. Thus, the situation in the environment represents anousal limitation in the short-term affirmation of exports as a key component of economic growth. (2) The debt crisis in the eurozone and the high exposure of their banks to individual countries, the downgrade, the increase in capital requirements and the difficulty in refinancing the poeof the melon banks, will have a limiting effect on the influx of foreign funds through banking channels. Hypothetically, there is even the possibility of outflow of part of the funds, although it is not very likely. (3) In combination with the perception of the growing risk of investing in Croatia, this does not work in favor of the possibility of reducing interest rates in either foreign or domestic financing. (4) It is a favourable factor that the state's foreign liabilities in 2012 (principal and interest of 801.2bn) are half as much as this year, so that the total foreign financing needs of the country are also about 801bn less than in 2011. However, they are still extremely large (8017.2bn) and cannot be expected to be easily realised. (5) Thus, even in 2012 there will be no external "locomotive" of economic growth, while external financing will be quite "hard". (6) All this further underlines the need to make much more rational use of our own financial and other potentials and to channel them into development, autonomously and in the combinewith the encouragement of foreign direct investment in the non-financial sector. (7) In this case, the issue of fiscal consolidation, i.e. the necessity of reducing the fiscal deficit and changes in the structure of fiscal expenditures, has particular weight. Changes in this area, however, cannotbe achieved without serious commencement of long-announced structural reforms. Notwithstanding the relatively limited and potentially negative short-term impacts of such reforms, they simply depend on the possibility of establishing a long-term sustainable race. How to do that is a question the new government will need to find an answer to quickly. (8) As for monetary policy, it will, as before, be determined by two operational objectives: 95 maintaining sufficient liquidity of the financial system and under external limitation conditions, and 95 maintaining a stable value of money. In addition to the existing instruments, in this function the CNB will also reactivate the mechanisms of operations on the open market. (9) Monetary projection: bank placements 6%, cash mass 7%, inflation 2.5%, average exchange rate 7.50 (10) Thus, suma sumarum, 2012, with moderate optimism, will be quite similar in economic performance in 2011. This, however, is not the most important thing. It is important whether healthy foundations for future growth and development will finally begin to form in it. Due tothe aforement of inertia so far, this process is seriously delayed; and any further delay can have far-reaching and long-term negative consequences.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Aktualno ekonomsko stanje u zemlji Objavljeno: 22.10.2011. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 21.10.2011. 21. konferencija Zagrebake burze Rovinj 22.10.2011. Stanje: Na putu oporavka ili srljanje u depresiju? Ekonomija je u stanju stagnacije, u okviru koje su smanjene neke neravnotee, ali nema jaih impulsa ekonomskom rastu i strukturnim promjenama, suoava se s poveanim eksternim rizicima, te snanim socijalnim i politikim otporima prema promjenama. Takvo stanje ne predstavlja iznenaenje. U tom kontekstu podsjeam i na prologodinji ovakav skup u ibeniku. 1. Svijetom se tada irio val umjerenog optimizma kako ekonomije izlaze iz recesije (svijet -0,6% 2009. na 5,1 % 2010; eurozona -4,2% na 1,8%), ali bila su prisutna i snana upozorenja daje:  taj rast parcijalan i nestabilan s niskim investicijama privatnog sektora i bez promjena na tritu rada  i dalje je prisutan visok rizik na financijskim tritima (posebno EU)  pogoranje javnih financija postaje glavni makroekonomski problem, pri emu rastui javni dug stavlja fiskalne pozicije u neodrivu putanju  mali manevarski prostor monetarne politike; to sve zajedno ne iskljuuje mogunost pojave nove recesije 2. S druge strane, isticali smo da kriza u Hrvatskoj nije tek refleks svjetske krize, ve je ova predstavljala "okida" koji je neravnoteama i neracionalnostima optereenu ekonomiju suoio s "eksternim okom" koji je doveo do uruavanja cjelokupnog modela rasta iz prethodnog razdoblja. Modela zasnovanog na obilnom priljevu inozemnog kapitala kojim je financirana domaa potronja, umjesto da je utroen za izgradnju izvozno orijentirane i konkurentne ekonomije. Zato, nema izlaska iz krize bez sutinskih reformi, nasuprot nerealnih oekivanja da e nastavak rasta svjetske ekonomije i zavretak pregovora s EU predstavljati "lokomotivu" koja e povui i hrvatsku ekonomiju bez "bolnih rezova". 3. to se dogodilo od tada. 3.1. U svijetu, vanjski rizici su efektuirani, posebno u eurozoni, pa ona nije uspjela odrati dinamiku rasta iz prethodne godine, a za 2012. oekuje se i daljnje usporavanje. Eurozona: 1,8% (2010.), 1,6% (2011.), 1,1% (2012.). U tome: Italija 1,3 % 0,6% 0,3% Njemaka 3,6% 2,7% 1,3% 3.2. U Hrvatskoj, reforme i promjene u politici koje su najavljene u Programu gospodarskog oporavka prolongirane su ili "razvodnjene". 4. Posljedice za Hrvatsku 4.1. Smanjenje inozemne potranje za robama kod najveih vanjskotrgovinskih partnera. Italija (-11%) Njemaka (-3%), odnosno zbirno izvoz u te dvije zemlje na koje inae otpada 30% naeg ukupnog izvoza, smanjenje za oko 8%, izraeno u tekuim eurima. Istina, to je dijelom nadoknaeno izvozom na ostala trita tako da e uz dobru turistiku sezonu (8,3%), ukupan izvoz roba i usluga biti za 3,8% nominalno vei od prologodinjeg. Meutim, kad se ti platnobilanni podaci prevedu u statistiku BDP-a i deflacioniraju odgovarajuim indeksom cijena, proizlazi da je realni izvoz roba i usluga u 2011. smanjen za 0,7%, to obara BDP za 0,3% 4.2 Nepovoljna kretanja na financijskim tritima i pogoranje percepcija ekonomskih performansi Hrvatske (spori oporavak, visok vanjski dug, visok fiskalni deficit, odgaanje reformi...) bitno su usporili neto priljev inozemne akumulacije. U 2011. on iznosi oko 370 mil. eura, stoje za 45% manje nego 2010. i deset puta manje nego u 2008. Njegov odnos prema BDP-utime je smanjen sa 9,8% (2008.), te 5,7% (2009.) i 1,5% (2010.) na samo 0,8% (2011.).. 4.3. Poveanje spreada na dravne obveznice u samo nekoliko mjeseci sa 200 na 500 basic points-a (indikator poveane premije na rizik ulaganja u Hrvatsku) prenijelo se i na uvjete zaduivanja ostalih sektora. Zajedno sa smanjenjem rejtinga velikih inozemnih banaka koje posluju u Hrvatskoj, to je poskupilo inozemne izvore sredstava. Ilustracija toga je i podatak da su plaene kamate na inozemni dug poveane sa 1,3 mlrd. eura u 2010. na, procjenjuje se, 1,5 mlrd. eura u 2011. (za 15%), iako je razina duga stagnirala, ak je i neto smanjena. To se prenosi i na uvjete financiranja u zemlji, tako da npr. pri poveanju ukupnog duga konsolidirane ope drave u 2011. godini za oko 11%, plaene kamate su poveane za 22%. 4.4. Reakcija HNB-a Poetkom godine - oslobaanje dodatne likvidnosti sa ciljem relativnog smanjenja ovisnosti banaka od inozemnih izvora sredstava i utjecaja na kamatne stope.  sputanje stope obvezne priuve sa 14% na 13%, s perspektivom daljnjeg sputanja na 11% (inicijalni efekt oko 3 mlrd. kuna)  sputanje stope minimalno potrebnih deviznih potraivanja sa 20% na 17% (efekt oko 830 mil. eura). Pored toga, provoene su i intervencije na deviznom tritu, preteno na strani potranje za devizama, odnosno emitiranja kuna. Tako je do danas HNB otkupio od drave 967 mil. eura, emitiravi 7,1 mlrd. kuna, koje su ule u domae financijske tokove. Dakle, kroz te je kanale ubaena u nacionalnu ekonomiju dodatna likvidnost od, preraunato, oko 16 mlrd. kuna, to je otprilike 25% novane mase. Meutim, efekti tako poveane likvidnosti na kreditnu aktivnost banaka i realne ekonomske tokove, pokazali su se relativno mali, zbog niza problema u sferi transformacije poveane likvidnosti u plasmane privatnom sektoru. Uzroci toga su:  poveana averzija banaka prema preuzimanju rizika u uvjetima kada su loi plasmani dostigli razinu od 12% ukupnih plasmana, u emu plasmani poduzeima razinu od 19%.  sustezanje komitenata od daljeg zaduivanja u uvjetima poveane neizvjesnosti  nepostojanje kvalitetnih investicijskih programa  ozbiljni problemi u primjeni modela A, B i C  koritenje poveane devizne likvidnosti za usklaivanje bilanci banaka, interno i u odnosima s bankama- majkama  poveane potrebe zaduivanja drave. U takvim uvjetima, iako su ukupni plasmani banaka ubrzani sa 7,5% u 2010. na 10% u 2011., plasmani privatnom sektoru usporavaju rast sa 6,9% na oko 5,5%, dok neto plasmani dravi ubrzavaju rast sa 14,7% u 2010. na 56% u 2011. Povezano s time, poveana a produktivno neangairana kunska likvidnost poinje u drugoj polovici godine stvarati snane deprecijacijske pritiske, pa HNB-u nije preostalo drugo nego daju ponovo smanjuje prodajom deviza bankama tijekom ljetnih mjeseci u iznosu od 419 mil. eura, a u listopadu i da ponovo povea stopu obvezne priuve na 14%. Sve to pokazuje i neosnovanostteze kako ekspanzivna monetarna politika moe, sama po sebi, pokrenuti realni sektor bez inflacije, jer ne vodi rauna je li taj sektor u postojeim uvjetima sposoban apsorbirati poveanu likvidnost banaka te jesu li bankarski kanali dovoljno prohodni za transfer te likvidnosti. 4.5. Kombinacija smanjenja priljeva i poveane cijene inozemne akumulacije, uz stagnaciju domae tednje i probleme u transformaciji likvidnosti u kredite, rezultira daljnjim smanjenjem investicija za 6,6%, od ega u privatnom sektoru za oko 9%. One su sada 27% realno manje nego u 2008. godini. Time je i dalje posebno pogoen sektor graevinarstva (daljnji pad za 9,6%). 4.6. Dakle, izvoz roba i usluga te investicije, koji bi trebali biti nosioci oporavka, agregatno su u 2011. realno smanjeni za 2,8% 5. U takvim uvjetima, mogunost rasta proizvodnje dominantno zavisi od domae finalne potronje. Na tom podruju, meutim, nema prostora za znaajnije pomake. Unato realnom poveanju prosjene neto plae za oko 2%, kao rezultatu izvrenog smanjenja porezne presije, zbog smanjene zaposlenosti raspoloivi dohodak stanovnitva stagnira, jednako kao i krediti, tako da e jedino zahvaljujui promjenama u strukturi potranje stanovnitva (sa investicija na tekuu potronju), osobna potronja u 2011. godini ukupno porasti za oko 0,4%. Situacija je slina i na podruju javne potronje gdje, meutim, zbog poveanih rashoda za kamate i rigidnosti dijela drugih proraunskih rashoda, ukupni rashodi konsolidirane ope drave (ukljuujui HAC) i dalje rastu bre od proraunskih prihoda. To rezultira daljnjim poveanjem fiskalnog deficita sa 18 mlrd. kuna u 2010. na 21 mlrd. kuna u 2011. godini, odnosno s 5,4% na 6,2% procijenjenog BDP-a. Time se poveava i javni dug sa 47% na 51% BDP-a 6. Nadovezujui se na pad izvoza i investicija, stagnacija finalne potronje ima za posljedicu i realno smanjenje agregatne potranje za robama i uslugama u 2011. godini za oko 1%. Uz promjene u njezinoj strukturi, s jaanjem potranje za egzistencijalnim robama i uslugama na raun investicija, to rezultira u ovoj godini i realnim smanjenjem uvoza za 3,9% (u tome uvoza opreme za oko 15%). To je zapravo kljuna varijabla koja je odredila "statistiku" sliku 2011. godine. Iz nje, naime, proizlaze dva makrobilanna efekta: 6.1. Vei pad uvoza od pada agregatne potranje ukazuje na poveanu orijentaciju potranje prema domaim robama i uslugama, to rezultira rastom BDP-a za oko 0,5% 6.2. Vei pad uvoza od pada izvoza, dovodi do smanjenja deficita tekueg rauna platne bilance s oko 500 mil. eura u proloj na samo 200 mil. eura u ovoj godini, odnosno sa 1,1% na samo 0,5% BDP-a, to pridonosi i zaustavljanju rasta inozemnog duga. 7. Slika 2011. godine - dva kuta gledanja 1. Afirmativni: - nakon pada u prethodne dvije godine za ukupno 7,2%, u 2011. godini su ipak zaustavljene negativne tendencije u kretanju BDP-a  deficit tekueg rauna platne bilance, kao kljuan indikator dosadanjih makroekonomskih neravnotea, sveden je na povijesni minimum  zaustavljanje rasta inozemnog duga te stupnja vanjske zaduenosti zemlje, ukazuje i na uspjeno refinanciranje tog duga (ono je u ovoj godini iznosilo oko 13 mlrd. eura), odnosno na jo uvijek prisutno povjerenje investitora u sposobnost zemlje da servisira svoje vanjske obveze  isto vrijedi i za financiranje tekueg proraunskog deficita, u koju svrhu se opa drava uspjela bruto zaduiti u inozemstvu za oko 2,5 mlrd. eura, iako je u oba sluaja to praeno poveanjem kamatnih stopa, koje su indikator da se stupanj tog povjerenja smanjuje. 2. Upozoravajui: - rast BDP-a i smanjenje platnobilannog deficita nisu ostvareni na razvojno perspektivan nain, ve diferenciranim smanjivanjem svih kljunih komponenti agregatne ponude i potranje. Otuda, ekonomija ne raste, ve se jo uvijek nalazi u fazi degresivnog prilagoavanja eksternom oku.  to prilagoavanje nije, meutim, ravnomjerno, jer jo uvijek nije zahvatilo javni sektor  posljedica toga je dodatno poveanje fiskalnog deficita i nastavak brzog rasta javnog duga, to financijska trita prepoznavaju kao osnovni problem i tumae kao nespremnost zemlje da provodi potrebne reforme.  ne promijeni li se ubrzo situacija na tom podruju, mogue je oekivati gubitak kreditnog rejtinga, sa svim posljedicama koje iz toga proizlaze. 8. To je situacija s kojom ulazimo u 2012. godinu. to nas u njoj oekuje? (1) lako je uvoz iz Hrvatske marginalan za eurozonu, daljnje usporavanje njenog rasta ograniavajue e djelovati i na potranju za naim proizvodima. Pored toga, teko je oekivati da e egzogeni faktori (meteoroloke prilike, politika situacija na Mediteranu...) biti tako povoljni za na turizam kao to su bili ove godine. Dakle, situacija u okruenju predstavlja ozbiljno ogranienje u kratkoronoj afirmaciji izvoza kao kljune komponente ekonomskog rasta. (2) Dunika kriza u eurozoni i visoka izloenost njihovih banaka prema pojedinim zemljama, pad rejtinga, poveanje kapitalnih zahtjeva te tekoe u refinanciranju pojedinih banaka, ograniavajue e djelovati na priljev inozemnih sredstava kroz bankarske kanale. Hipotetski, postoji ak i mogunost odljeva dijela sredstava, iako ona nije jako vjerojatna. (3) U kombinaciji s percepcijom rastueg rizika ulaganja u Hrvatsku, to ne djeluje u prilog mogunosti smanjivanja kamatnih stopa ni kod inozemnog ni kod domaeg financiranja. (4) Povoljna je okolnost da su inozemne obveze drave u 2012. godini (glavnica i kamate 1,2 mlrd. eura) upola manje nego ove godine, tako da su i ukupne potrebe za inozemnim financiranjem zemlje za oko 1 mlrd. eura manje nego u 2011. godini. Ipak, one su i dalje izuzetno velike (17,2 mlrd. eura) i ne moe se oekivati da e se lako realizirati. (5) Dakle, ni u 2012. godini nee biti nikakve eksterne "lokomotive" ekonomskog rasta, dok e eksterno financiranje biti prilino "tvrdo". (6) Sve to dodatno naglaava potrebu mnogo racionalnijeg koritenja vlastitih financijskih i drugih potencijala i njihovog usmjeravanja u razvoj, autonomno i u kombinaciji s poticanjem izravnih stranih ulaganja u nefinancijski sektor. (7) Kod toga posebnu teinu ima pitanje fiskalne konsolidacije, odnosno nunost smanjenja fiskalnog deficita i promjena u strukturi fiskalnih rashoda. Promjene na tom podruju nije, meutim, mogue ostvariti bez ozbiljnog zapoinjanja dugo najavljivanih strukturnih reformi. Neovisno od relativno ogranienih pa potencijalno i negativnih kratkoronih uinaka takvih reformi, od njih jednostavno zavisi mogunost uspostavljanja dugorono odrivog rasta. Kako to uraditi, pitanje je na koje e nova Vlada brzo trebati nai odgovor. (8) to se tie monetarne politike, ona e, kao i do sada, biti odreena s dva operativna cilja:  odravanje dostatne likvidnosti financijskog sustava i u uvjetima eksternih ogranienja, te  odravanje stabilne vrijednosti novca. Pored postojeih instrumenata, u toj e funkciji HNB ponovo aktivirati i mehanizme operacija na otvorenom tritu. (9) Monetarna projekcija: plasmani banaka 6%, novana masa 7%, inflacija 2,5%, prosjeni teaj 7,50 (10) Dakle, suma sumarum, 2012. godina e, uz umjereni optimizam, biti po ekonomskim performansama dosta slina 2011. godini. To, meutim, nije najvanije. Bitno je hoe li se u njoj konano poeti formirati zdrave osnove za budui rast i razvoj. Zbog dosadanje inertnosti, taj proces ozbiljno kasni; a svako daljnje kanjenje moe imati dalekosene i dugorono negativne posljedice.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation of the governor of the CNB, prof. Dr. Boris Vuji at the 24th conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange
text: Boris Vujcic Notes for presentation at the conference of the Zagreb Stock Exchange, Rovinj, 16.10.2014. 1) BDP Based on new outputs and information, the expected rate of change in real GDP for 2014 is -0.6%, i.e. it has been corrected to lower. This is the result of a further decrease in the annual rate of change in GDP in the first quarter due to the transition to the ESA 2010 methodology (-0.6 compared to the previous -0.4%) and the less favourable developments in economic activity in the second quarter. Seasonally adjusted data also point to a decrease in economic activity in the second quarter -0.3%), primarily due to a decrease in domestic demand and, to a lesser extent, exports of goods and services. Real exports of goods and services could increase by 6.4% in 2014, higher than previous expectations. The changes in the expected growth rate reflect good outputs of exports of goods in the second quarter (growth of 7.9% year-on-year) as well as a noticeable increase in the expected growth of real imports of foreign trade partners. On the other hand, the assessment of annual growth in service exports (tourism) decreased due to less favourable outputs than expected, which was largely influenced by adverse weather conditions. Imports of goods and services could increase by 4.2% in 2014 and the increase in the evolution of total imports relates mainly to the import component of exports, given the increase in the expected growth rate of exports. Personal consumption could decrease by 0.6% in real terms in 2014. Seasonally adjusted personal consumption decreased by 0.2% during the second quarter, amid a further decline in household purchasing power given a slight decrease in employment (0.2%) and a slightly stronger decline in real net wages (0.6%). In the rest of the year, personal consumption is not expected to recover significantly, given the continued deleveraging of the population and the projected further decrease in real net wages and employment. Household disposable income could fall by 0.8 per cent in real terms amid a slight real rise in real average wages and a continuation of the trend of decreasing employment by around 1.5 per cent a year. Government spending could decrease by 1.3%, a more pronounced drop from previous expectations (-0.6%). This change is the result of a noticeable decrease in government spending in the second quarter, which is associated with a decrease in the number of employees in public and state services compared to the same period of the previous year (-4.6%). In the second half of 2014, government spending is expected to continue to fall, due to a further decrease in the number of employees in state and public services, as well as a further decline in the use of goods and services. GFCF could decrease by 3.6% in 2014 , which is also a stronger decrease than previous expectations (2.7%). Outputs in the second quarter are noticeably less favourable than expected (annual rate of change -5.2% compared to -3.1%). The first available monthly indicators for July and August also point to the continued decrease in fixed capital investments in the second half of the year. The growth prospects of this year and next are also not favourably affected by the lowering of the growth forecast for EU countries as the main foreign trade partner, which was widely discussed this weekend at the IMF-World Bank annual meeting. 2) Monetary developments Excess liquidity on the market remains very high and ranges at the level of about HRK 6 billion, and interest rates on the money market of about 0.5%, as well as interest rates on the treasury records of the Ministry of Finance are still at, or around, historical minimums. By the end of the year, we expect the supply of money to grow by about 6.5 percentage points. Under the current conditions, the CNB intends to continue to maintain a very expansionary monetary policy, maintaining a high excess of liquidity and keeping interest rates on the market low, and will buy mandatory treasury records from banks that achieve an increase in corporate lending. In this way, monetary policy affects the reduction of the cost of financing on the domestic market for all sectors, and in particular for the budget, which generates approximately 40% of the financing needs per year in the treasury bills market, and another 25% in the domestic bond and loan market. The CNB will continue to pursue such a policy to the extent that it does not jeopardise the stability of the exchange rate, which, due to the very high degree of euroisation, remains, together with capital adequacy and adequate reservations of poor placements, the basis of financial stability in the country. In addition to the stability of the banking system, such a policy is also enabled by very high coverage of monetary aggregates to international reserves. This coverage is 156% of the reserve money and 171% of the money supply, with 8.5 months of import coverage. This policy allowed, despite six years of recession and the consequent large increase in bad placements, which reached 16%, with the increase in poor placements to the corporate sector to as much as 30%, to maintain stability and avoid the financial system crisis recorded by many EU countries (and the US). However, it should be noted that the unfavourable prospects for a stronger economic recovery greatly limit the reach of expansionary monetary policy action. Loans to businesses increased cumulatively in Croatia during the crisis than in any other EU country. GDP, however, has fallen more than in any EU country, except Greece. This negative link between credit growth and GDP growth in Croatia is further proof that credit growth is not a sufficient condition for GDP growth. On the other hand, many countries with cumulative declines in loans have seen positive GDP growth rates, which shows that credit growth is not a condition for GDP growth. Research shows that after the crisis, credit growth is followed by GDP growth, not the other way around. In other words, in the recovery period, loans are the next variable, and in periods of expansion the leading variable.
