Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a 29.10.2012. Godinja ekonomska konferencija 2012. Zagreb, Ekonomski fakultet 26.10.2012. Hrvatska je ve etiri godine de facto u recesiji. Od 2009. do 2011. godine BDP se smanjio za 8,3 posto, a ove godine oekujemo da e se smanjiti za daljnjih otprilike 1,9 posto, to e kumulativni pad BDP-a u zadnje etiri godine poveati na otprilike 10 postotnih poena. Tek idue godine mogue je oekivati poetak blagog oporavka. Rast je, meutim, tek zbirni iskaz mnogih znaajki ekonomije. Model rasta u Hrvatskoj u desetak godina prije poetka krize, zasnivao se prvenstveno na znatnom koritenju inozemnog kapitala. Strana izravna ulaganja - 'dobar kolesterol' - veim dijelom su zavrila u sektoru meunarodno neutrivih dobara i usluga, dok je 'lo kolesterol' - priljev kapitala dunikog karaktera - preteito zavrio u rastu plaa, kreditima, odnosno rastu osobne potronje, ili pak u infrastrukturnim dravnim investicijskim projektima, koji u velikoj mjeri nisu u stanju generirati novane tijekove za servisiranje tog dunikog kapitala. Prema istraivanju MMF-a, u razdoblju od 2000-2011. doprinos kapitala rastu BDP-a u Hrvatskoj bio je prosjeno 2,3 posto godinje, tehnolokog napretka 0,2 posto, a rada 0 posto. Nije, dakle, nikakvo udo daje Hrvatska poetkom krize, kad je prestao priljev kapitala, izgubila sposobnost rasta. Angaman rada, proizvodne i procesne inovacije i tehnoloki napredak, naime, u Hrvatskoj, naalost, nisu djelotvorni faktori rasta. Danas se Hrvatska nalazi na vanom, rekao bih, iako ne volim prejake rijei, gotovo sudbonosnom raskriju. Ovaj put ne bira politiku sudbinu, poput naputanja Jugoslavije i osamostaljivanja 1991., niti ulaska u EU dvadeset godina poslije, ve svoju buduu ekonomsku sudbinu. Dosadanji model ekonomskog razvoja, koji se temeljio preteito na priljevu dunikog kapitala, je slomljen i nepopravljiv. Ne samo to, on u naslijee ostavlja bitna ogranienja za brz i uspjean rast u budunosti. Vanjski dug od 100 posto BDP-a, javni dug koji se brzo pribliava granici od 60 posto BDP-a, lou ekonomsku strukturu, bez dovoljnog broja dovoljno velikih poduzea koja su ukljuena u meunarodne lance ponude, spor i nepouzdan dravno-administrativni i pravosudni sustav, sustav mirovinskog osiguranja s rastuim deficitom, neefikasno strukturiran zdravstveni sustav, obrazovni sustav pri dnu europskih ljestvica izvrsnosti, velik dio poljoprivrede s niskom produktivnosti i relativno visokom zaduenou, rigidno radno zakonodavstvo s niskom ukupnom zaposlenou i zaposlenou s djelominim radnim vremenom, da nabrojim samo neke od najznaajnijih strukturnih problema. Kao posljedica brojnih strukturnih neefikasnosti, Hrvatskoj ve godinama pripada neprihvatljivo nisko mjesto na ljestvicama koje ocjenjuju poslovnu klimu u pojedinim zemljama, a zadnje izvjee Svjetske banke pokazuje da u tom pogledu nikakvog napretka nema. To su vrlo ozbiljna ogranienja za budui razvoj nae zemlje. Meutim, nisu nepremostiva, uz odlunu promjenu modela ekonomskog razvoja. Ono to je zabrinjavajue je da se umjesto nove, drukije ekonomske politike, u zadnje vrijeme ponovo nude obrasci starih propalih politika. Katkad iz neznanja, katkad iz populizma, a esto kao kombinacija jednog i drugog. Neznanje je uvijek loe, nekad opasno, a populizam je osobito opasan u vremenima krize. Ljudi, nezadovoljni neuspjenim politiarima, izmoreni krizom, padom standarda i dunikim problemima, postaju skloniji prihvaati naoko jednostavna i bezbolna rjeenja tekih problema, a onih koji ih nude nikad ne nedostaje. Sugestije da se rjeenje problema u Hrvatskoj danas moe nai izvan okvira makroekonomske stabilnosti su vrlo opasna iluzija. I politika devalvacije teaja domae valute i fiskalne ekspanzije i monetarnog financiranja deficita isprobana je puno puta za vrijeme Jugoslavije, a djelomino i u neovisnoj Hrvatskoj. I svaki puta je propala. Zato ju onda neki ponovo zazivaju? Ili zato to nisu u stanju uiti, ili zato jer je to najlake rjeenje za ponuditi. Ne treba provoditi teke i nepopularne strukturne reforme - sve se lako rjeava tiskanjem novca, devalvacijom i zaduivanjem za dravnu potronju. Vrlo zavodljivo, osobito za one koji zaboravljaju povijest. Kada bi bili u pravu, moram priznati, bilo bi to sjajno. Zato bi se Nijemci, Danci, Nizozemci, Austrijanci i druge uspjene zemlje EU desetljeima nakon Drugog svjetskog rata drali politike vrste valute, niskih deficita, kontrole politike plaa, i podizanja proizvodnosti kroz tehnoloke inovacije i poboljanje proizvodnih procesa? Kad su jednostavno mogli konkurentnost i socijalno blagostanje postii visokim domaim i vanjskim deficitima, tiskanjem novca i devalvacijama. Zbog ega je u tim zemljama stopa zaposlenosti izmeu 70 i 75 posto (postotak zaposlenih u dobi 15-64 godine), naspram hrvatskih 52,4 posto, to je nia stopa zaposlenosti od ijedne zemlje EU, ukljuujui Grku, koja je sa stopom zaposlenosti od 56 posto najloija zemlja u EU? Zbog ega, uostalom, Jugoslavija nije postala izvozna sila uz tolike devalvacije dinara? U situaciji u kojoj je vanjski dug 102 posto BDP-a, u kojoj je godinja ukupna potreba inozemnog (re)financiranja 35-36 posto BDP-a, i u kojoj samo drava mora financirati jo otprilike dodatnih cca. 5 milijardi eura deficita u ovoj i idue dvije godine, svako gubljenje makroekonomske stabilnosti, fiskalne ili monetarne, u obliku brzog nastavka rasta javnog duga preko 60 posto i/ili devalvacije teaja domae valute, dovelo bi do gubljenja povjerenja investitora i nemogunosti refinanciranja obveza po odrivim uvjetima. Javni dug je od 2008. do danas porastao s 29,3 posto BDP-a, na otprilike 53 posto i oito je na neodrivoj putanji, to upozoravaju i rejting agencije i MMF i investitori. Zanemariti to upozorenje i pozivati se, u ovim uvjetima, na takozvana keynesijanska rjeenja znai ne razumjeti ekonomske i financijske rizike za zemlju i nuditi ljudima vrlo opasnu iluziju da i dalje moe biti po starom. Slino je i s prizivanjem devalvacije u uvjetima ne samo visoke vanjske zaduenosti, ve i vrlo visoke domae tednje u stranoj valuti, odnosno euru. Direktna posljedica devalvacije domae valute bila bi kvarenje svih pokazatelja zaduenosti bitnih za ocjenu ranjivosti domae ekonomije, kreditni rejting i time povjerenje investitora. Takoer, devalvacija u uvjetima valutne supstitucije, odnosno visoke euroiziranosti pasivne strane bilanci drave, poduzea i veine zaduenih kuanstava, djeluje prorecesijski, smanjujui rast BDP-a kroz smanjenje investicijske, osobne i dravne potronje zbog rasta relativne zaduenosti. Ve e i u novom izdanju Handbook of monetary economics posebno poglavlje biti posveeno specifinostima monetarne politike u uvjetima visoke valutne supstitucije, a na zadnjem sastanku skupine G-30, najrespektabilnijeg svjetskog skupa ekonomista, u Tokiju proli tjedan, svim sudionicima je podijeljen upravo papir koji objanjava zato je aktivna teajna politika neefikasna u sluaju malih otvorenih zemalja. Osobito ukoliko su visoko dolarizirane/euroizirane. Naalost, suvremenu literaturu izgleda ne prate niti oni kojima bi to trebao biti posao, lako, ne bi ju trebalo niti itati. U ovoj zemlji ju moemo pisati, nakon svih greaka iz prolosti. Jedna od njih, koja se ovih dana ponovo javlja, je nostalgija za dravnim bankarstvom. Godinama smo sluali kako su Hrvatskoj potrebne dravne banke, kako je Hrvatska pogrijeila privatizirajui ih, kako bi se trebalo ugledati na Sloveniju, kako dravne banke postoje i drugdje u Europi. No, danas, nakon svega to se dogodilo s dravnim bankama od bive Jugoslavije, Hrvatske, Slovenije, panjolske ili ak Austrije i Njemake, i dalje zazivati povratak dravnom bankarstvu stvarno znai da je krivulja uenja za neke ljude diskontinuirana. No, maknimo se od rasprava koje, u biti, pripadaju prolosti. Gdje smo danas i to moemo oekivati? Rekao bih da su pred Hrvatskom dva imperativa. Prvi je sauvati makroekonomsku stabilnost, jer bez nje e se kriza samo produbiti. Ono to je pozitivno ove jeseni je injenica da je sauvan kreditni rejting i povjerenje investitora, u tekim uvjetima. To je posljedica sjedne strane poetka provoenja fiskalne konsolidacije i najavljenog smanjenja proraunskog deficita i uvoenja fiskalne discipline a, s druge, injenice daje financijski sustav u Hrvatskoj stabilan i profitabilan, prvenstveno zbog odgovarajuih makroprudencijalnih politika provoenih prije poetka krize. Dio zemalja u Europi zapao je u ozbiljne potekoe i izgubio povjerenje trita zbog toga to im je fiskalna situacija postala neodriva uslijed visokih proraunskih deficita i visokog javnog duga, te je refinanciranje tih deficita postalo toliko skupo da ne uspijevaju zaustaviti rast javnog duga. Radi se o takozvanom efektu grude snijega, kad zbog visokog duga zemlja gubi povjerenje investitora i mora se zaduivati po sve viim kamatnim stopama, to zahtijeva sve veu fiskalnu kontrakciju kako bi se zaustavio daljnji rast javnog duga uslijed poveanja kamatnih trokova njegovog servisiranja. Drugi dio zemalja, poput Islanda, Irske, panjolske i Slovenije zapao je u ozbiljne probleme prvenstveno zato jer nisu uspjele sauvati stabilnost financijskog sustava, pa su zbog gubitaka bankarskog sustava i ostvarenih ili potencijalnih fiskalnih trokova povezanih s tim gubicima, izgubile povjerenje financijskih trita i suoile se sa smanjenjem rejtinga i velikim poveanjem trokova zaduivanja. Da bi zadrala povjerenje trita, Hrvatska, meutim, mora kredibilno nastaviti proces fiskalne konsolidacije koji e udjel javnog duga u BDP-u staviti na silaznu putanju. Pri tome valja voditi rauna o tome da je smanjenje deficita kroz smanjenje rashoda manje tetno za rast nego putem poveanja porezne presije. Fiskalna konsolidacija ove godine dogaa se preteito na prihodnoj, umjesto rashodnoj strani prorauna, to e uz vei od oekivanog pada inozemne potranje i podbaaj investicija, dovesti do toga da e pad BDP-a biti vei od oekivanog, a upitno je i izvrenje planiranog smanjenja deficita. Ukoliko eli smanjiti negativan utjecaj fiskalne konsolidacije na rast, Vlada ga mora usmjeriti na rashodnu, umjesto prihodne strane prorauna. to ne iskljuuje promjenu strukture poreza. Drugi imperativ je nalaenje novog modela rasta. Vrijeme "lakog" rasta na temelju poveanja dunikog kapitala je prolo. Razine vanjske i javne zaduenosti od 102 posto i 53 posto BDP-a, jednostavno vie ne doputaju taj model rasta. to to znai? To znai da u kratkom roku ne moemo niti od javne, niti od osobne potronje oekivati da budu glavna poluga rasta. Uz domae, naalost, niti vanjsko okruenje nije poticajno i ne moe znaajno potaknuti domai rast: za Italiju se ove godine oekuje pad BDP-a od 2,3 posto, u 2013. godini pad od -0,7 posto, s tek blagim oporavkom od 0,5 posto rasta u 2014. Drugi glavni vanjskotrgovinski partner, Njemaka, usporila je rasts lanjskih 3,1 posto, na oekivanih 0,9 posto ove i idue godine, te na 1,4 posto 2014. Za najznaajnijeg trgovinskog partnera u susjedstvu - Sloveniju - oekuje se pad BDP-a od 2,2 posto ove godine i -0,4 posto idue godine, te umjereni oporavak 2014. od 1,7 posto rasta BDP-a. Dakle, inozemna potranja nije ta koja e sama po sebi biti u stanju generirati znaajan rast, usprkos ulasku u EU idue godine. Jedini nain da izvoz uinimo djelotvornim imbenikom gospodarskog rasta u kratkom/srednjem roku je, dakle, poveanjem udjela hrvatskog izvoza na meunarodnim tritima, budui da agregatna inozemna potranja na tradicionalnim izvoznim tritima nee znaajnije rasti. To e, pak, biti vrlo teko ostvariti bez privlaenja inozemnih ulaganja u izvozni sektor, a odreenu ulogu u poveanju neto izvoza moe igrati i poveano ulaganje u domae primarne izvore energije. Openito, ini se daje prevelik naglasak stavljen na dravne investicijske projekte, osobito imajui na umu ogranien kapacitet za zaduivanje drave i kvazidrave, a premali na privatne investicije. A upravo su privatne investicije, a osobito privlaenje privatnog kapitala u izvozno ili uvozno supstitutivne sektore ono to je neophodno potrebno za brzu promjenu modela rasta u Hrvatskoj. To je ono to u srednjem roku moe podii potencijalnu stopu rasta BDP-a. Iskustva malih otvorenih zemalja koje su uspjeno razvile izvoznu industriju pokazuju da su u tome kljunu ulogu odigrala strana ulaganja. Od Irske, preko Estonije, Maarske i eke, do Slovake, udio poduzea u stranom vlasnitvu u ukupnom ili robnom izvozu tih zemalja na razini je od oko 80, pa i vie, posto. U Hrvatskoj je to iskljuujui INA-u 47 posto, a ukljuujui INA-u 53 posto, i to na nioj razini udjela izvoza u BDP-u. Za one koji i dalje misle da rjeenje problema hrvatskog izvoza lei u devalvaciji teaja domae valute, treba rei i to da je do poetka krize najbre stope rasta izvoza u srednjoj i istonoj Europi ostvarila Slovaka, zemlja koja je bila suoena i s daleko najjaom realnom aprecijacijom teaja domae valute od preko 40 posto, dok je Hrvatska, uz znatno blau aprecijaciju realnog teaja, od desetak posto, ostvarila najsporiji rast izvoza. Kada bi teaj bio dominantna determinanta izvoza, teko da bi to bilo mogue. Glavna razlika izmeu dvije zemlje- izravna strana ulaganja u izvozni sektor. Drugim rijeima, Hrvatska opet mora temeljiti rast na priljevu kapitala, no ovaj put ne dunikog, nego izravnog. Treba rei da je do sada Hrvatska imala i objektivno znaajan nedostatak u privlaenju inozemnih izvozno orijentiranih ulaganja zbog toga to nije bila lanica EU. Od idue godine taj nedostatak nestaje i Hrvatska mora iskoristiti tu priliku ukoliko se eli relativno brzo vratiti na putanju rasta i kreiranja novih radnih mjesta. Okolina nam ne ide na ruku, jer ovo nije niti 2004. niti 2007., ve vrijeme duboke krize u Europi, no to samo znai da je potrebno razmiljati hrabro i biti odluan u ruenju prepreka za poslovanje i investiranje u Hrvatskoj. U tom pogledu ovotjedna injenica da je Hrvatska s vrlo loe pozicije pala za dodatna etiri mjesta na jednoj od rang- lista koje mjere poslovnu/investicijsku klimu ne ohrabruje. Ona bi trebala biti alarm i pomo za redefiniranje prioriteta ekonomske politike. Ako je gdje potrebno vui radikalne poteze onda je to upravo na tom podruju. Nee, naime, biti dovoljno samo rjeavati postojee prepreke za poslovanje/ulaganja u Hrvatsku, ve biti i inovativan i poduzetan u stvaranju uvjeta koji su bolji nego u drugim zemljama. Ne uspije li postati atraktivna za poslovanje i privui znaajnije investicije, Hrvatska e, uz ogranienja visoke razine duga, teko uspostaviti funkcionalan model rasta. To bi zemlju moglo osuditi na relativno niske stope rasta u iduim godinama. To e onda definirati i standard ivljenja ove i buduih generacija. Mirovinski sustav je ve dugo u dubokoj krizi, a stopa zaposlenosti najnia u Europi. To su problemi koji mogu dugorono utjecati na relativan pad standarda ivota u Hrvatskoj naspram drugih zemalja. Najgore bi bilo da najbolje obrazovani, vi mladi, suoeni sa slabim mogunostima zapoljavanja, odluite bolje sutra potraiti u inozemstvu. Vi ste onaj kapital, ljudski, koji je najvaniji, i bez kojeg nema razvoja. Da se na kraju vratim na poetak. Izbor ekonomske budunosti, redefiniranje modela rasta i izbor sukladnih ekonomskih politika toliko je danas vaan za Hrvatsku, da je ponovo poeljan i politiki i opedrutveni konsenzus oko cilja i naina dolaska do njega. Barem meu najrelevantnijim drutvenim i politikim snagama. Ne bude li on postojao, partikularni interesi i populistiki porivi prijete blokadom procesa koji su dugorono u interesu Hrvatske, svih njenih graana, a najvie vas, pred kojima je, nadam se, i cijela radna karijera (vjerojatno do 70te godine ivota) i, potom, ugodna mirovina u najljepoj zemlji u Europi.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Speech at the Ceremonial Academy
text: Speech by Governor Boris Vujcic at the Ceremonial Academy Published: 21.12.2021. Speech by Governor Vujcic at the Ceremonial Academy on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of the Croatian National Bank held on 20 December 2021. Dear President of the Republic, Mr. Milanovic, respected Prime Minister, Mr. Plenkovic, respected delegates to the Speaker of the Parliament, Vice-President, Mr. Reiner, former President of the Republic, Mr. Josipovic, esteemed Minister of Finance and Vice-President of theGovernment, Mr. Maric, Minister of Defense, Mr. Banozic, former ministers and prime ministers, former governor, former vice governors, former vice governors and members of the Council, dear guests, dear colleagues and colleagues! It is a special honor to address you on the occasion of the 30th anniversaryof the Croatian National Bank, and thus the celebration of three decades of our monetary independence and independence, and to celebrate this significant jubilee with you together. I am often, as you know, able to talk about what the Croatian National Bank is doing - about our policies and measures, about our analyses and economic forecasts, about regulatory requirements and decisions. On this occasion, I decided to deviate from my usual topics and say a few words about the Croatian National Bank itself, as one of the key institutions for the Croatian economy and society. I really haven't said much about her so far, guided by the fact that it's better for others to talk about you, but on the occasion of this 30th anniversary, as the head of an institution that has reached its full maturity, let me give my visionof the reasons that contributed to its development, reputation and success. I hope that I will not sound immodest if I say that over the past thirty years we have been very successful and that through our actions we have contributed to general stability and the creation of favorable conditions forthe development of the economy. This is simply evidenced by the facts. Croatian society has entrusted us with two great tasks - to safeguard price stability and to ensure the stability of the financial system, goals that, as we have been explaining for years, in Croatian conditionsand the stability of the exchange rate. We have been successfully achieving our first goal for almost three decades, i.e. since the stabilisation programme. In the young transition economy, in the conditions of war and with the legacy of a different system and the enthusiasm of the new, initially under-understood, it was more difficult to achieve the stability of the financial system, but we also achieved this and successfully maintained it. The best test of all that we have been doing for years on financial stability was during the recent global financial crisis, which has shaken the banking sustsof Ave and many more substantially developed countries and caused very high bank resolution costs in a large number of EU countries. Croatia went through this shock at no cost, thanks precisely to the CNB's good policies. The second test shortly after was the bankrot of the largest not only Croatian but also regional company, which also did not withdraw any Croatian banks. We have also reacted in a timely and strong manner during the last, atypical crisis, caused by the pandemic, a crisis that has brought many unsafestiti, and unfortunately a great loss of human lives. We are all the more particularly pleased that we have ensured not only financial and macroeconomic stability, through the stability of exchange rates and banks, but also a financial framework in which the Government could prevent andexploit the negative consequences of the crisis through its measures, and citizens feel that the system is working. We are one of the few small central banks that have implemented quantitative easing measures to stabilise the sovereign debt market, which has certainly contributed to a very rapidrecovery of the domestic economy. In fact, the CNB was one of the banks that do not print international currencies, the second largest intervention in the world last year. Without previously built solid monetary and financial stability funds, this would not have been possible. In addition to the appropriate macroecnomic policies, the second cornerstone of the stability of the financial system is certainly a stable and well-capitalised banking system: the CNB has continuously done work on this front that has little precedent among EU countries. Theconsolidation of whose banking system was carried out on time, through adequate bank supervision policies, which is a very demanding task and easily creates opponents and dissatisfied. On we are used to dissatisfactions and criticisms, sometimes it seems almost to me and have developed a Stockholm sindrom, but this is not and will not sway us, stable banks and at the same time monitoring consumer protection are our enduring goal. I have not talked about this before, but the distinguished international awards won by all those who have led the CNB over the past 25 years - my predecessors, Marko 8akreb and 8eeljko Rohatinski, and I, are also an indicator of our success. I have never seen these awards as recognitions for us personally, but as international recognitions and commendations for the work of the institution, the joint work of all who have made up the CNB. For anyone who knows international opportunities and financial markets, I don't think there is any doubt about the CNB's reputation. And it's certainly not an accident. I would say that probably the most important reason for our successful work and duration is that we have nurtured ourunbiasedness and independence, and have solely dedicated ourselves to achieving the goals set for us, without the need to ingratiate ourselves with or favor someone, it is easy to have the independence of the value on which we always insist, considering it a necessary condition for our successful work, although nyen importance is the result of experience and the undeniable empirical conclusion of the entire literature on this issue, this independence would not have been if the elected representatives of all the previous authorities had not been supported. By ensuring the independence of the CNB, they too, and through them Croats as awhole, have shown their maturity and responsibility. And today, not so far from us, we can see how devastating consequences can have the erosion of the central bank's credibility that occurs when power takes control of it. Of course, independence brings additional responsibility - it is not a self-improvement; at all times we are aware that it should serve to achieve our mandate as well as possible, for the betterment of the Croatian state and society. To paraphrase my colleague Christine Lagarde: The Croatian National Bank is also listening... We are not confined to a tower of expertise, we want to hear not only professional economic milieus, but also citizens/consumers, media, civil society organizations, elected political representatives of different worldviews. We strive to achieve dialogue, andremda key decisions must eventually always be made by ourselves based on concrete expert insights and our own assessments. If I were to describe what makes the CNB a developed and, by objective standards, a successful institution, I would single out a few elements. I would put first all those factors concerning our employees and the standards of their work - throughout the 30-year period we have nurtured and encouraged professionalism, education and professional development, and improved employees rewardingbut also improving them solely on the basis of their professional merits (women). That would be hard to achieve without independence. With our characteristic and element of success, I also consider the fact that we have achieved continuity, we did not allow the changes of the leading peopleto this to the suppression of the good that the predecessors created during their mandates. It never leads to building a good institution. Many of us still know what Ante left us in our legacy, what traditions Pero started, how the CNB was formed by Marko, and what Roha insisted on. All this is valuable to us, everything forms part of our institutional culture that we will leave to those who come after us. It's really pleasing to talk to our employees who have great respect for institutional continuity, and they alwaystalk about former colleagues with a lot of attention. Contributions to the quality of this institution in the CNB are not forgotten, we are proud of them and we are building a future for them. Although we received awards for our work, our activities and measures, as I mentioned before, did not always meet praise. In fact, we have often experienced criticism of our policies and activities - let's just remember the long-standing attacks over the conduct of stable exchange rate policies, negative reactions when we prevented credit expansion in the years before the Globbying financial crisis, ignoring warnings regarding Swiss franc loans, or frequent remarks about the way we invest funds from the international reserves we manage, not to mention some more paradoxical criticism. We were criticised even by those we expected to be our allies because we acted in the general interest and interest of the most vulnerable groups of residents. Here, too, independence has proved crucial to success. It was thanks to independence, and the associated privilege of usrto commit to achieving our goals in the long term, that the attacks did not sway us. Not only did we not be distracted from the journey, which we believed in professionally, but, I think, we did the most harmonious and best work in turbulent and crisis periods. As the English saying goes - when the going gets tough, the tough get going. When I think back to what the predecessors did during the war, the stabilization program, and the measures we took in the period of strong credit before theglobal financial and economic crisis, and then their timely dismissal during the recession that arose afterwards, our procedures for preserving the stability of the banking system in the run-up to agrokor's bankruptcy as well as the rapid reactions to the emergence of the pandemic pandemic crisis, I would say that we at the CNB showed our character precisely when it was most difficult. New crises, there should be no doubt about that, are upon us. If we return to institutional memory, it tells us that at the very beginning of its journey, the Croatian central banclearly represented and put it to the need for Croatia to simultaneously adopt, in addition to building its own monetary system, the principled commitment to enter integration processes as soon as possible in order to pursue its own social and economic interests, and finally to the monetary union with other European countries. What I'm saying is that the idea of monetary integration is not new in Croatia. It has been present since the beginning of monetary sovereignty, through negotiations to join the EU, to this day. Now we have finally, after a long job, created intothe news to make this idea come true. The Croatian National Bank is now a member of the European System of Central Banks, a member of the banking union and, we believe, soon to be a member of the Eurosystem. In this company, the CNB is already an equal partner, which gives us the confidence that we willnot only participate in the central bank within the euro area, but also contribute substantively to its further development, for the benefit not only of the Croatian but also of the common European economy and society. However, the effort and effort to be an equal EU slave partner in every fieldis only valid if the citizens of Croatia feel it as their own betterment. And for the betterment of citizens, the development of institutions is boiling, without good institutions it is impossible to achieve. Many words have been written and spoken about the importance of institutions ina democratic society. Vlado Gotovac once said with a passion of sincere faith and feeling: "We must create such institutions that will enable all our citizens, at every point in Croatia, to feel that they are at the center, to participate in the essential issues of the homeland and to consider their personal life alive, effective, free and active." And we, in the CNB, as I have said before, strive to do so - and we will continue to do so in the future - to incorporate into the Croatian institutional mosaic those values and results that are aslave to all our citizens at the age of all our citizens. Institutions, in turn, form an institutional framework, but ultimately, always and most importantly - people. That is why I thank all those who have invested their professional efforts in this goal, 30 years of building the institution, wherever they may be, in or outside the CNB , as well as all those who are yet to come, and who we hope will have the same love for the profession, and for the common public good that we all serve. Thank you.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Govor guvernera Borisa Vujia na Sveanoj akademiji Objavljeno: 21.12.2021. Govor guvernera Vujia na Sveanoj akademiji u povodu 30 godina Hrvatske narodne banke odranoj 20. prosinca 2021. Potovani predsjednie Republike, gospodine Milanoviu, potovani predsjednie Vlade, gospodine Plenkoviu, potovani izaslanie predsjednika Sabora, potpredsjednie, gospodine Reineru, bivi predsjednie Republike, gospodine Josipoviu, cijenjeni ministru financija i potpredsjednie Vlade, gospodine Mariu, ministru obrane, gospodine Banoiu, bivi ministri i predsjednici Vlada, bivi guverneru, bivi viceguverneri i lanovi Savjeta, dragi gosti, drage kolegice i kolege! Osobita mi je ast obratiti vam se u povodu 30. obljetnice Hrvatske narodne banke, a time i proslave tri desetljea nae monetarne samostalnosti i neovisnosti, i s vama zajedno proslaviti ovaj za nas znaajan jubilej. esto sam, kao to znate, u prilici govoriti o onome to Hrvatska narodna banka radi - o naim politikama i mjerama, o naim analizama i ekonomskim prognozama, o regulatornim zahtjevima i odlukama. Ovom prilikom odluio sam odstupiti od mojih uobiajenih tema i rei nekoliko rijei o samoj Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci, kao jednoj od kljunih institucija za hrvatsko gospodarstvo i drutvo. O njoj do sada doista nisam puno govorio, rukovodei se onime da je bolje da drugi govore o tebi, no povodom ove 30. obljetnice, kao elnik institucije koja je doivjela svoju punu zrelost, dopustite mi da dam svoje vienje razloga koji su pridonijeli njezinom razvoju, ugledu i uspjehu. Nadam se da neu zvuati neskromno ako kaem da smo u proteklih trideset godina bili vrlo uspjeni i da smo svojim djelovanjem pridonijeli opoj stabilnosti i stvaranju povoljnih uvjeta za razvoj gospodarstva. O tome jednostavno svjedoe injenice. Hrvatsko nam je drutvo povjerilo dva velika zadatka - uvati stabilnost cijena i osiguravati stabilnost financijskog sustava, ciljevi koji, kao to godinama objanjavamo, u hrvatskim uvjetima znae i stabilnost teaja. Prvi cilj uspjeno ostvarujemo ve gotovo tri desetljea, odnosno od stabilizacijskog programa. U mladoj tranzicijskoj ekonomiji, u uvjetima rata i s nasljeem drukijeg sustava i entuzijazmom novog, u poetku nedovoljno shvaenog, bilo je tee postii stabilnost financijskog sustava, no i to smo ostvarili i uspjeno odrali. Najbolji test svega onoga to smo godinama radili na financijskoj stabilnosti bio je tijekom nedavne globalne financijske krize koja je uzdrmala bankovne sustave i mnogih bitno razvijenijih zemalja i uzrokovala vrlo visoke trokove sanacije banaka u velikom broju zemalja EU-a. Hrvatska je kroz taj ok prola bez ikakvih trokova, upravo zahvaljujui dobroj politici HNB-a. Drugi test nedugo nakon toga bio je bankrot najvee ne samo hrvatske nego i regionalne kompanije, koji za sobom takoer nije povukao niti jednu hrvatsku banku. Pravovremeno i snano reagirali smo i za vrijeme zadnje, atipine krize, uzrokovane pandemijom, krize koja je donijela brojne nesigurnosti, a naalost i velik gubitak ljudskih ivota. Tim vie nam je posebno drago da smo osigurali ne samo financijsku i makroekonomsku stabilnost, kroz stabilnost teaja i banaka, ve i financijski okvir u kojem je Vlada mogla svojim mjerama spreavati i ublaavati negativne posljedice krize, a graani osjetiti da sustav funkcionira. Jedna smo od rijetkih malih sredinjih banaka koja je primijenila mjere kvantitativnog poputanja kako bi stabilizirala trite dravnog duga, to je sigurno pridonijelo vrlo brzom oporavku domaega gospodarstva. Dapae, HNB je bio od banaka koje ne tiskaju meunarodne valute, druga na svijetu po veliini intervencije prole godine. Bez ranije izgraenih vrstih fundamenata monetarne i financijske stabilnosti, to ne bi bilo mogue. Uz odgovarajue makroeknomske politike, drugi kamen temeljac stabilnosti financijskog sustava svakako je stabilan i dobro kapitaliziran bankovni sustav: HNB je na tom planu kontinuirano radio posao kakav ba i nema presedana meu zemljama EU-e. Konsolidacija bankarskog sustava obavljena je na vrijeme, kroz adekvatne politike nadzora banaka koji je vrlo zahtjevan zadatak i lako stvara protivnike i nezadovoljnike. Na nezadovoljstva i kritike smo navikli, ponekad mi se ini gotovo i razvili stockholmski sindrom, no, to nas nije i nee nas pokolebati, stabilne banke i istovremeno praenje zatite potroaa na su trajni cilj. O tome isto nisam do sada priao, no ugledne meunarodne nagrade koje smo osvojili svi koji smo vodili HNB u proteklih 25 godina - moji prethodnici, Marko kreb i eljko Rohatinski, i ja, takoer su pokazatelj nae uspjenosti. Nikada te nagrade nisam doivljavao kao priznanja nama osobno, ve kao meunarodna priznanja i pohvale za rad institucije, zajedniki rad svih koji smo inili HNB. Za sve koji poznaju meunarodne prilike i financijska trita mislim da nema sumnje u reputaciju HNB-a. I to sasvim sigurno nije sluajno. Rekao bih da je vjerojatno najvaniji razlog naega uspjenog rada i trajanja u tome to smo njegovali nau nepristranost i neovisnost, te se iskljuivo posvetili ostvarivanju ciljeva koji su nam zadani, bez potrebe da se nekome dodvorimo ili mu pogodujemo, lako je neovisnost vrednota na kojoj uvijek inzistiramo smatrajui je nunim uvjetom za na uspjean rad, iako je njena vanost rezultat iskustva i neprijeporan empirijski zakljuak cjelokupne literature o tom pitanju, te neovisnosti ne bi bilo daje nisu poduprli izabrani predstavnici svih dosadanjih vlasti. Osiguravajui neovisnost HNB-a, i oni, a preko njih i hrvatsko drutvo u cjelini, pokazalo je svoju zrelost i odgovornost. I danas, ne tako daleko od nas, moemo vidjeti kako razorne posljedice moe imati erozija kredibiliteta sredinje banke do koje dolazi kada vlast preuzme kontrolu nad njom. Naravno, neovisnost donosi i dodatnu odgovornost - ona nije samosvrha; u svakom smo trenutku svjesni da ona treba sluiti to kvalitetnijem ostvarenju naeg mandata, radi boljitka hrvatske drave i drutva. Da parafraziram svoju kolegicu Christine Lagarde: I Hrvatska narodna banka slua... Nismo zatvoreni u kulu ekspertnosti, elimo uti ne samo profesionalni ekonomski milje, nego i graane/potroae, medije, organizacije civilnog drutva, izabrane politike predstavnike razliitih svjetonazora. Trudimo se ostvariti dijalog, premda kljune odluke naposljetku uvijek moramo donijeti sami na temelju konkretnih strunih uvida i vlastitih ocjena. Kada bih trebao opisati to HNB ini razvijenom i, po objektivnim mjerilima, uspjenom institucijom, izdvojio bih nekoliko elemenata. Na prvo mjesto stavio bih sve one faktore koji se tiu naih zaposlenika i standarda njihova rada - tijekom cijeloga tridesetogodinjeg razdoblja njegovali smo i poticali profesionalnost, obrazovanje i struno usavravanje, te zaposlene nagraivali i unapreivali iskljuivo na osnovi njihovih profesionalnih zasluga (ene). To bi bilo teko postii bez neovisnosti. Naom karakteristikom i elementom uspjeha smatram i injenicu da smo postigli kontinuitet, nismo doputali da promjene vodeih ljudi dovode do zatiranja dobrog to su prethodnici stvorili tijekom svojih mandata. To nikada ne vodi izgradnji dobre institucije. Jo uvijek mnogi od nas znaju to nam je u nasljee ostavio Ante, koje je tradicije zapoeo Pero, kako je HNB ustrojio Marko, a na emu inzistirao Roha. Sve nam je to vrijedno, sve ini dio nae institucionalne kulture koju emo ostaviti onima koji dolaze nakon nas. Stvarno je ugodno razgovarati s naim zaposlenicima koji izuzetno potuju institucionalni kontinuitet, i uvijek s puno potovanja govore o bivim kolegicama i kolegama. Doprinosi kvaliteti ove institucije u HNB-u se ne zaboravljaju, na njih smo ponosni i na njima gradimo i budunost. lako smo za svoj rad dobivali nagrade, nae aktivnosti i mjere, kako sam ve spomenuo, nisu uvijek nailazile na pohvale. Dapae, esto smo doivljavali kritike na nae politike i aktivnosti - sjetimo se samo dugogodinjih napada zbog voenja politike stabilnog teaja, negativnih reakcija kada smo spreavali kreditnu ekspanziju u godinama prije globalne financijske krize, ignoriranja upozorenja u vezi s kreditima u vicarskim francima ili estih primjedbi na nain na koji ulaemo sredstva iz meunarodnih priuva kojima upravljamo, da ne spominjem neke paradoksalnije kritike. Kritizirali su nas ak i oni od kojih smo oekivali da nam budu saveznici jer smo djelovali u opem interesu i interesu najranjivijih skupina stanovnika. I ovdje se neovisnost pokazala kljunom za uspjeh. Upravo zahvaljujui neovisnosti, i s njom povezanom povlasticom da se usredotoimo na ostvarivanje ciljeva u dugom roku, napadi nas nisu pokolebali. to se na kraju pokazalo ispravnim. Ne samo da nas s puta, u koji smo profesionalno vjerovali, nisu skrenule kritike nego smo, ini mi se, najusklaenije i najbolje radili u burnim i kriznim razdobljima. Kao to kae engleska izreka - when the going gets tough, the tough get going. Kada se prisjetim to su prethodnici inili jo za vrijeme rata, stabilizacijskog programa, pa mjera koje smo poduzimali u razdoblju snanoga kreditnog rasta prije globalne financijske i ekonomske krize, a zatim njihovog pravodobnog otputanja tijekom recesije nastale nakon toga, naih postupaka za ouvanje stabilnosti bankarskog sustava uoi steaja Agrokora kao i brzih reakcija na nastupanje pandemijske krize, rekao bih da smo mi u HNB-u svoj karakter pokazali upravo onda kad je bilo najtee. Nove krize, u to ne treba sumnjati, pred nama su. Vratimo li se institucionalnom pamenju, ono nam kazuje da je ve na samom poetku svog puta hrvatska sredinja banka jasno zastupala i stavo potrebi da Hrvatska uz izgradnju vlastitoga monetarnog sustava istodobno usvoji i naelno opredjeljenje da radi ostvarivanja vlastitih drutvenih i ekonomskih interesa to prije ue u integracijske procese, a konano i u monetarnu uniju s drugim europskim zemljama. Ono to elim rei je da ideja monetarne integracije nije nova u Hrvatskoj. Ona je prisutna od poetka monetarne suverenosti, preko pregovora za ulazak u EU, sve do danas. Sada smo napokon, nakon dugog posla, stvorili uvjete da se ta ideja ostvari. Hrvatska narodna banka danas je lanica Europskog sustava sredinjih banaka, lanica bankovne unije i, vjerujemo, uskoro lanica eurosustava. U tom drutvu HNB je ve sada ravnopravni partner, to nam daje uvjerenje da emo kao sredinja banka unutar europodruja ne samo sudjelovati nego i sadrajno pridonositi njezinom daljnjem razvoju, na dobrobit ne samo hrvatskoga ve i zajednikoga europskoga gospodarstva i drutva. No, trud i napor da na svakom polju budemo ravnopravan europski partner vrijedi samo ako graani Hrvatske to osjete i kao vlastiti boljitak. A za boljitak graana kljuanje razvoj institucija, bez dobrih institucija to je nemogue postii. Puno je rijei napisano i izgovoreno o vanosti institucija u demokratskom drutvu. Vlado Gotovac je sa strau iskrene vjere i osjeaja jednom lijepo rekao: "Moramo stvarati takve institucije koje e svim naim graanima, u svakoj toki Hrvatske, omoguiti osjeaj da su u sreditu, da sudjeluju u bitnim pitanjima domovine i da svoj osobni ivot smatraju ivim, djelotvornim, slobodnim i aktivnim." I mi, u HNB-u, kao to sam ve rekao, teimo tako raditi - a to emo nastaviti i u budunosti - da u hrvatski institucionalni mozaik ugradimo one vrijednosti i rezultate koji su na dobrobit svih naih graana. Institucije, pak, ini institucionalni okvir, no naposljetku, uvijek i najvanije - ljudi. Zato zahvaljujem svima koji su u ovaj cilj, tridesetogodinju izgradnju institucije, uloili svoj profesionalni trud, gdjegod bili, u HNB-u ili izvan njega, kao i svima onima koji tek dolaze, i za koje se nadamo da e gajiti istu ljubav za struku, i za ope javno dobro kojemu svi sluimo. Hvala.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: The Governor of the CNB answered all the questions in the Parliament
text: CNB Governor responds to all inquiries in Parliament Published: 4.3.2016. Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, Governor 3.3.2016. CNB's annual report for 2014 Session of the Croatian Parliament Zagreb During the debate on the 2014 annual report of the Croatian National Bank, members of the Croatian Parliament sent a number of questions and criticisms regarding the work of the CNB to Governor Vujcic. In the debate on topics concerning the entire Croatian economy,MPs Ivan Lovrinovic (Most), Goran Maric (HDZ), Gordan Maras (SDP), Ivan Suker (HDZ), Ivan Vilibor Sincic (Living Wall), Miro Bulj (Most) and Ivan Kovacic stood out. After discussing whether the Croatian Parliament can accept or reject the report, the governorner recalled that the amendments to the Law on the Croatian National Bank, which is in line with European regulation, the Constitution of the Republic of Croatia and the basic treaties of the European Union, do not accept or reject the CNB report in parliament, but the central bank informs the Parliament about the financial state of play, the degree of realisation of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy, and parliament takes note of such a report. The Governor called on the political groups to introduce a continuous CNB dialogue with parliamentarians in Croatia on current economic topicsaimed at improving communication between the Croatian Parliament and the CNB, in line with the practice of the European Central Bank and some other central banks. The governor answered lawmakers' questions about deflation, arguing that the recorded slight drop in prices does not lead to thenegative effects of deflation. "What is the problem when we have deflation? The first is the delay in consumer spending in anticipation of further price falls. So you're not spending today expecting the price to fall tomorrow, so that deepens the recession. Is this happening in Croatia? No. Why? Because consumers cannot put off food and energy consumption, and these are two components that prices are falling at the moment in Croatia so that there are certainly no negative effects on aggregate consumption since the fall of these components. In fact, it is good for Croatian citizens and for the Croatian economy that food and energy prices are falling and this is one of the reasons why we achieved higher GDP growth rates than expected in 2015. Another possible reason for deflation to have negative effects is the rise in real interest rates. This is not a problem in Croatia. The share of interest expense in consumers' disposable income is decreasing rather than increasing, as is the loan-to-income ratio.' Boris Vujcic continued that "for Croatia it is a positive supply shock that improves the conditions of the exchange of the Croatian economy. For the Croatian export unit, we can now get more than one unit of imports" and this is good for Croatian citizens and the economy, the governor explained. To the criticism of some MPs about the lack of expansion ofmonetary policy, the CNB Governor responded by comparing the measures implemented by the Croatian National Bank and those implemented by the European Central Bank. He stressed that the monetary policy of the Croatian central bank is more expansionary than that implemented by ESB. "The share of excess liquidity in Croatia is 6% of GDP. In the eurozone, it is 2.5 times smaller. The balance sheet of the Central Bank of Croatia as a percentage of GDP is higher than the balance sheet of the European Central Bank. Croatian monetary policy is more expansionary than the monetary policy of the European SilverAviation Bank. Those are the facts." "Banks will not take the money if they have no one to place it with. So we can do what we want, but while obstacles are on the market side, the banks just won't take them. We do weekly repo operations at an interest rate of half a percent. Interest is 100 to 200 million kuna. When we lower the reserve requirement rate, we provide liquidity to banks by 0%. Their cost is to keep money in the CNB at 0% vis-a-vis benefits at an average interest rate of 5% to companies. And what do they do? He's being held at the CNB." Problem in the further placement of money the governor sees in the poor creditworthiness of the enterprise. "Do you know at what interest rates they receive loans from good companies in Croatia at the moment? Two to three percent, that's the interest rate at which good companies in Croatia are borrowing today. Those who are not, cannot get a loan at all or receive it at higher interest rates. And these are problems that we need to solve. Weak private sector balance sheets." "If the average level of interest is compared and corrected for thecountry's rating, it is evident that in Croatia the interest rates are lower than the country's rating predicts," Vujcic said. The Governor also proposes the introduction of a guarantee scheme for small and medium-sized enterprises as a measure that can ensure the passability of money, as it can replace whatis not there at the moment and why the money does not go towards companies, which is the lack of capital and collateral. Boris Vujcic also addressed complaints about the privatisation of the banking system and long-standing recommendations that we should have looked to Sloveni. "I have heard for years that we should have looked up to Slovenia. There you see they kept the state banks and you see how much better it goes there, they said. And what happened now? All these Slovenian banks collapsed just as our banks did when they were state-owned. And it's It directly cost Slovenian taxpayers lOtak % of GDP and even more in indirect cost." He stated to the Governor that the Croatian Postal Bank, which is now doing well, with high operating profits, should have been recapitalized twice. "If state banks were so good then we would have learned it already. However, history teaches us the opposite - it is better that they are private." He also referred to the role of supervision and explained that the Croatian National Bank does not decide to whom they are assignedto order, but is decided by the credit committees of banks. "The role of supervision is to protect the stability of the banking system, to protect deposits in the banking system, all so that people are sure that they can take their money to banks." Boris Vujcic also explained that supervision determines the minimum capital adequacy for banks, the minimum capital they must have in relation to the risks they take and periodically checks whether banks maintain this capital adequacy, assessing the riskiness of theirplacements and by which they reduce capital. He also recalled the banks' attacks on the demand for an increase in provisions and pointed out that 56% of bad placements are reserved, ensuring the stability of the banking system, and reducing the risk to Croatian taxpayers from the cost of poor banking operations. The Governor replied to remarks that we have too high international reserves in relation to some central and eastern European countries: "Why don't we look to Slovenia or the Baltic states? Well, because these countries are in the eurozone, andwe're not even about yet. Governor Vujcic reiterated that we are not yet in the eurozone and that it will take some time to get in. "I've been explaining for the last two days how much and how. And to get in there, we haveto do our homework. We need to make structural reforms that will allow the public debt-to-GDP ratio to be reduced and that's what everyone tells us. That's what the IMF says, so does the European Commission, so do investors who care about their money. I don't remember anyonementioning monetary reforms about them, everyone mentioning structural reforms and fiscal adjustment. And then we will be able to reduce the international reserves and we will do it." MPs were particularly interested in why long-term (structural) repo auctions started now, not in 2013 or 2014. "There are several reasons. First, in 2013 and 2014, as since the beginning of the crisis, monetary policy has been extremely countercyclical. So she was creating a huge excess of liquidity even then. However, why not a long-term repo? Because at that time wewere still in a situation of recession, then the foreign liabilities of banks were higher than the foreign assets of banks, so there was a risk of further deleveraging of banks, the amount of capital abroad, from providing long-term repurchase operations to the bank'sava. At that time, we still did not have such a surplus in the current account of the balance of payments." In addition, the Governor stressed, there was a danger that this would act on the depreciation of the exchange rate, then we were not in the phase of gdp recovery and there was no demand for kuna chalkas it exists today, when kuna loans are growing faster than euro loans. Governor Vujcic also described the reasons why Croatia was euroised and stated that the process of deeurization could take place in the conditions of chalk of THE ECONOMIC AND FISCAL POLICY in which people will have confidence and in conditions of gradual appreciation of the exchange rate of the domestic currency, since the long process of depreciation and led to a high degree of euroization. When asked about the salary of the Governor of the Croatian National Bank and employment,the Governor pointed out that the salary of the governor is not financed from the budget of the Republic of Croatia, and all employment is carried out through public tenders, which are very fair and very rigorous, and on which the best are chosen and that is why the quality of people in the CNB is so good. On the problem of loans with the currency clause in the Swiss franc and the conversion of these loans, the Governor pointed out that on January 20, 2015, a week after leaving the policy of fixing the exchange rate of the franc, the Croatian National Bank published a comprehensive report on the causes, structure and possible effects of some proposals for resolving the problem of these loans, and a new report was sent to the Croatian Parliament before the adoption of the Act on Amendments to the Consumer Credit Act in September 2015. The Governor reiterated that banks have so far shown a loss of HRK 7 billion, but that the stability of the banking system is not compromised, which the CNB pointed out in September 2015. The governor pointed out that as he warned in 2005 about the risks of lending to the CHF, when he was deputy governor, he has now warned about the risks associated with resolving the franc loan problem. "They did not support me then or now," Boris Vujcic concluded in response to a question about Swiss franc loans. In response to a question about the loans of austrianedions, the Governor stressed that borrowing abroad was and is allowed, and that these are loans that were made in Austria and that the Croatian National Bank does not have jurisdiction or is not able to control them. The discussion also mentioned the sale of gold in 2001no, and the governor explained that the Croatian budget would have received 1 billion kuna less payments from the Croatian National Bank to date if we had kept the gold in reserves that we inherited from the Bank for International Equalization. In conclusion, Boris Vujcic stated the importance of agreeing monetary and fiscal policy. He stressed: "Monetary policy and fiscal must be aligned. The task of monetary and fiscal policy is to act countercyclically. What's that mean? When the cycle goes down economically, when the GDP growth rate starts to fall, to prevent a sharp decline. Monetary policy could have done this because it was restrictive before the crisis. So we had a very restrictive policy until 2009 and then we could start firing it from 2009 to the present day and have this countercyclicalfect. As a result, Croatia did not end up in the programme, which is why Croatia was not governed by the IMF, the European Commission, but was able to conduct politics on its own." "Neither monetary nor fiscal policy can raise productivity, they will not solve the structural orthinner efficiency of the state administration, the poor business climate in Croatia, the inability to invest, legal uncertainty. These are things that have to happen if we want to see faster GDP growth, but then we will have a more efficient monetary policy, becauseall this money that is created will be able to move towards the economy. Monetary policy at the moment provides the domestic historically cheapest financing of the state, but the risk of a state with this public debt and rating is still high and we have to work on that, this will not be solved by monetary policy." Boris Vujcic reiterated his invitation to debate with members of parliament and outside the parliamentary session, and said that this discussion is always useful and one of the ideas of the CNB is to invite political groups to the CroatianPeople's Nu Bank for talks on certain topics. "So, when the Parliament is not in session, you can choose the topics that you want to discuss with us in the CNB, with presentations, with explanations, whatever questions you have," concluded the Governor of the Croatian National Bank.
