text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Guverner HNB-a u Saboru odgovorio na sve upite Objavljeno: 4.3.2016. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Tema Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner 3.3.2016. Godinje izvjeee HNB-a za 2014. Sjednica Hrvatskog sabora Zagreb Tijekom rasprave o godinjem izvjeu Hrvatske narodne banke za 2014. zastupnici Hrvatskog sabora uputili su guverneru Vujiu brojna pitanja i kritike vezane uz rad HNB-a. U raspravi o temama koje se tiu cjelokupnog hrvatskog gospodarstva posebno su se pitanjima istakli zastupnici Ivan Lovrinovi (Most), Goran Mari (HDZ), Gordan Maras (SDP), Ivan uker (HDZ), Ivan Vilibor Sini (ivi zid), Miro Bulj (Most) i Ivan Kovai. Nakon rasprave o tome moe li Hrvatski sabor prihvatiti ili odbiti izvjee, guverner je podsjetio da se izmjenama Zakona o Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci, koji je usklaen s europskom regulativom, Ustavom RH i temeljnim ugovorima Europske unije, izvjee HNB-a u Saboru ne prihvaa niti odbija, ve sredinja banka obavjetava Sabor o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike, a Sabor prima na znanje takvo izvjee. Guverner je pozvao klubove zastupnika da se u Hrvatskoj uvede kontinuirani dijalog HNB-a s parlamentarcima o aktualnim ekonomskim temama u cilju poboljanja komunikacije Sabora RH i HNB-a, a u skladu s praksom Europske sredinje banke i nekih drugih sredinjih banaka. Guverner je odgovorio na pitanja zastupnika o deflaciji, argumentirajui da zabiljeeni blagi pad cijena ne dovodi do negativnih uinaka deflacije. "Koji je problem kad imamo deflaciju? Prvi je odlaganje potronje od strane potroaa u oekivanju daljnjeg pada cijena. Znai, ne troite danas oekujui da e sutra pasti cijena pa to produbljuje recesiju. Da li se to dogaa u Hrvatskoj? Ne. Zato? Zato to potroai ne mogu odlagati potronju hrane i energije, a to su dvije komponente kojima cijene u ovom trenutku u Hrvatskoj padaju tako da sigurno ne dolazi do negativnih uinaka na agregatnu potronju od pada tih komponentni. Dapae, dobro je za hrvatske graane i za hrvatsko gospodarstvo da cijene hrane i energije padaju i to je jedan od razloga zato smo 2015. godine ostvarili vee stope rasta BDP-a nego to je to bilo oekivano. Drugi mogui razlog da deflacija ima negativne uinke je rast realnih kamata. To nije problem u Hrvatskoj. Udjel rashoda na kamate u raspoloivom dohotku potroaa se smanjuje, a ne poveava, isto kao i omjer kredita i dohotka." Boris Vuji je nastavio da se "za Hrvatsku radi o pozitivnom oku ponude koji popravlja uvjete razmjene hrvatskog gospodarstva. Za jedinicu hrvatskog izvoza sada moemo dobiti vie od jedne jedinice uvoza" I to je dobro za hrvatske graane i gospodarstvo, pojasnio je guverner. Na kritike nekih zastupnika o nedovoljnoj ekspanzivnosti monetarne politike, guverner HNB-a odgovorio je usporedbom mjera koje je provodila Hrvatska narodna banka i onih koje provodi Europska sredinja banka. Naglasio je daje monetarna politika hrvatske sredinje banke ekspanzivnija od one koju provodi ESB. "Udio vika likvidnosti u Hrvatskoj je 6% BDP-a. U eurozoni je 2,5 puta manji. Bilanca sredinje banke Hrvatske u postotku BDP-a je vea od bilance Europske sredinje banke. Hrvatska monetarna politika je ekspanzivnija od monetarne politike Europske sredinje banke. To su injenice." "Banke nee uzeti novce ako ih nemaju kome plasirati. Znai, mi moemo raditi to hoemo, no dok su prepreke na strani plasiranja, banke ih jednostavno nee uzeti. Radimo tjedne repo operacije po kamatnoj stopi od pola posto. Interes je 100 do 200 milijuna kuna. Kad sputamo stopu obvezne rezerve, osiguravamo likvidnost bankama po 0%. Njihov troak je dranje novca u HNB-u po 0% vis-a-vis davanja po prosjenoj kamatnoj stopi od 5% poduzeima. I to rade? Dre ga u HNB-u." Problem u daljnjem plasiranju novca guverner vidi u slaboj kreditnoj sposobnosti poduzea. "Znate li po kakvim kamatnih stopama dobivaju kredite dobra poduzea u Hrvatskoj trenutno? Dva do tri posto, to je kamatna stopa po kojoj se danas zaduuju dobra poduzea u Hrvatskoj. Ona koja nisu, ne mogu uope dobiti kredit ili ga dobivaju po viim kamatnim stopama. I to su problemi koje trebamo rijeiti. Slabe bilance privatnog sektora." "Ako se usporede prosjena razina kamata i korigira za rejting zemlje vidljivo je da su u Hrvatskoj kamatne stope nie nego to rejting zemlje to predvia", naglasio je Vuji. Guverner takoer predlae uvoenje garancijske sheme za mala i srednja poduzea kao mjeru koja moe osigurati prohodnost novca jer ona moe nadomjestiti ono to u ovom trenutku ne postoji i zbog ega novac ne ide prema poduzeima, a to je nedostatak kapitala i kolaterala. Boris Vuji osvrnuo se i na prigovore o privatizaciji bankovnog sustava i dugogodinje preporuke o tome da smo se trebali ugledati na Sloveniju. "Godinama sam sluao da smo se trebali ugledati na Sloveniju. Eto vidite oni su zadrali dravne banke i vidite kako tamo puno bolje ide, govorili su. I to se sad dogodilo? Sve te slovenske banke su propale kao to su propale i nae banke kad su bile u dravnom vlasnitvu. I to je Slovenske porezne obveznike direktno kotalo lOtak % BDP-a i jo vie u neizravnom troku." Naveo je guverner da je i Hrvatsku potansku banku koja sada dobro posluje, s visokom operativnom dobiti, trebalo dva puta dokapitalizirati. "Kad bi dravne banke bile tako dobre onda bismo to ve nauili. Meutim, povijest nas ui suprotno - bolje je da su privatne." Takoer se osvrnuo na ulogu supervizije te objasnio da Hrvatska narodna banka ne odluuje kome se dodjeljuju krediti, ve o tome odluuju kreditni odbori banaka. "Uloga supervizije je tititi stabilnost bankovnog sustava, da bi zatitila depozite u bankovnom sustavu, a sve zato da ljudi budu sigurni da svoje novce mogu odnijeti u banke." Boris Vuji objasnio je i da supervizija bankama odreuje minimalnu kapitalnu adekvatnost, minimum kapitala koji moraju imati u odnosu na rizike koje preuzimaju i periodino provjerava odravaju li banke tu kapitalnu adekvatnost, ocjenjujui rizinost njihovih plasmana za koji umanjuju kapital. Podsjetio je i na napade banaka na zahtjevza poveanjem rezervacija i istaknuo daje 56% loih plasmana rezervirano, ime se osigurava stabilnost bankovnog sustava, i umanjuje rizik za hrvatske porezne obveznike od trokova loeg bankarskog poslovanja. Na primjedbe da imamo previsoke meunarodne priuve u odnosu na neke zemlje sredinje i istone Europe guverner je odgovorio: "Zato se ne ugledamo na Sloveniju ili baltike zemlje? Pa zato jer su te zemlje u eurozoni, a mi jo nismo. U trenutku kada Hrvatska ue u eurozonu mi neemo morati drati vie takve priuve." Guverner Vuji je ponovio da jo nismo u eurozoni i da e biti potrebno neko vrijeme da uemo. "Objanjavao sam zadnja dva dana koliko i kako. A da uemo tamo moramo odraditi domau zadau. Moramo napraviti strukturne reforme koje e omoguiti smanjivanje udjela javnog duga u BDP-u i to nam kau svi. To kae i MMF, to kae i Europska komisija, to kau i investitori koji se brinu za svoje novce. Ne sjeam se da je itko od njih spominjao monetarne reforme, svi spominju strukturne reforme i fiskalnu prilagodbu. I tada emo moi smanjiti meunarodne priuve i uinit emo to." Zastupnike je posebno zanimalo zato se s dugoronim (strukturnim) repo aukcijama krenulo sada, a ne 2013. ili 2014. godine. "Nekoliko je razloga. Prvo, 2013. i 2014. godine, kao i od poetka krize monetarna politika je bila izrazito kontraciklika. Znai stvarala je ogroman viak likvidnosti ve i tada. Meutim, zato ne dugoroni repo? Zato, jer tada smo bili jo uvijek u situaciji recesije, tada je inozemna pasiva banaka bila vea od inozemne aktive banaka, znai postojala je opasnost od daljnjeg razduivanja banaka, iznosa kapitala u inozemstvo, od osiguravanja dugoronih repo operacija bankovnom sustavu. Tada jo uvijek nismo imali ovakav suficit na tekuem raunu platne bilance". Osim toga, naglasio je guverner, postojala je opasnost da to djeluje na deprecijaciju teaja, tada nismo bili u fazi oporavka BDP-ai nije postojala potranja za kunskim kreditima kakva postoji danas, kada kunski krediti rastu bre od eurskih. Guverner Vuji opisao je i razloge zbog kojih je Hrvatska eurizirana te je naveo da bi se proces deeurizacije mogao odvijati u uvjetima kredi bi Ine ekonomske i fiskalne politike u koju e ljudi imati povjerenje i u uvjetima postupne aprecijacije teaja domae valute, budui da je dugotrajni proces deprecijacije i doveo do visokog stupnja eurizacije. Na pitanja o plai guvernera Hrvatske narodne banke te zapoljavanju, guverner je istaknuo da se plaa guvernera ne financira iz prorauna RH, a sva se zapoljavanja provode putem javnih natjeaja, koji su vrlo poteni i vrlo rigorozni, i na kojima se izabiru najbolji i zato je kvaliteta ljudi u HNB-u tako dobra. O problemu kredita s valutnom klauzulom u vicarskom franku i konverziji tih kredita guverner je naglasio da je 20. sijenja 2015. godine, tjedan dana nakon naputanja politike fiksiranja teaja franka uzeuro, Hrvatska narodna banka objavila sveobuhvatno izvjee o uzrocima, strukturi i moguim uincima nekih prijedloga za rjeavanje problema tih kredita, a novo izvjee poslano je Hrvatskom saboru prije donoenja Zakona o izmjeni i dopunama Zakona o potroakom kreditiranju u rujnu 2015. godine. Guverner je ponovio da su banke do sada iskazale gubitak od 7 mlrd. kuna, no da stabilnost bankovnog sustava nije ugroena, to je HNB istaknuo i u rujnu 2015. godine. Guverner je istaknuo da, kako je 2005. godine upozoravao na rizike kreditiranja u CHF, dok je bio zamjenik guvernera, tako je i sada upozorio na rizike povezane s rjeenjem problema kredita u francima. Nisu me podrali ni onda, a niti sada, zakljuio je Boris Vuji odgovor na pitanje o kreditima u vicarskim francima. Guverner je u odgovoru na pitanje o kreditima austrijskih tedionica naglasio da je zaduivanje u inozemstvu bilo i jest dozvoljeno, te da su to krediti koji su sklopljeni u Austriji i da ih Hrvatska narodna banka nije nadlena, odnosno nije u mogunosti nadzirati. U raspravi je spomenuta i prodaja zlata 2001. godine, te je guverner pojasnio da bi hrvatski proraun do danas bio dobio milijardu kuna manje uplata iz Hrvatske narodne banke da smo u priuvama zadrali zlato koje smo naslijedili iz Banke za meunarodnaporavnanja. U zakljuku je Boris Vuji naveo vanost usuglaavanja monetarne i fiskalne politike. Naglasio je: "Monetarna politika i fiskalna moraju biti usklaene. Zadaa monetarne i fiskalne politike je da djeluju kontracikliki. to to znai? Kad ciklus krene dolje ekonomski, kad stopa rasta BDP-a pone padati, da sprijee snaan pad. Monetarna politika je to mogla raditi zato jer je bila restriktivna prije krize. Znai, imali smo vrlo restriktivnu politiku do 2009. godine i onda smo je mogli poeti otputati od 2009. do danas i imati taj kontracikliki efekt. Zbog toga Hrvatska nije zavrila u programu, zbog toga Hrvatska nije bila upravljana od MMF-a, Europske komisije nego je mogla samostalno voditi politiku." "Ne mogu ni monetarna ni fiskalna politika dii produktivnost, one nee rijeiti strukturna pitanja efikasnosti dravne administracije, lou poslovnu klimu u Hrvatskoj, nemogunost investiranja, pravnu nesigurnost. To su stvari koje se moraju dogoditi ukoliko elimo vidjeti bri rast BDP-a, ali onda emo imati i efikasniju monetarnu politiku, jer e svi ti novci koji se stvore moi krenuti prema gospodarstvu. Monetarna politika u ovom trenutku osigurava domae povijesno najjeftinije financiranje drave, ali rizik drave s ovim javnim dugom i rejtingom jo je uvijek visok i na tome moramo raditi, to nee rijeiti monetarna politika." Boris Vuji ponovio je svoj poziv na raspravu sa saborskim zastupnicima i izvan zasjedanja Sabora, te je rekao da je ovakva diskusija uvijek korisna i jedna od ideja HNB-a je da pozove klubove zastupnika u Hrvatsku narodnu banku na razgovore o pojedinim temama. "Znai, kad Sabor ne zasjeda vi moete birati teme koje elite s nama raspraviti u HNB-u, uz prezentacije, uz objanjavanja, kakva god pitanja imali", zakljuio je guverner Hrvatske narodne banke.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: The CNB preserved price stability and financial stability
text: The CNB has preserved price stability and financial stability Published: 4.11.2016. Type Speech Speaker Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, Governor Topic Semiannual information on the financial situation, the degree of realization of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy for the second half of 2015 Event Session of the Croatian Parliament Date 4.11.2016. events Semi-annual information on the financial situation, the degree of realisation of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy forthe second lever is rising in 2015 Dear Mr. President, Distinguished Representatives and Representatives, dear ladies and gentlemen, It is my honor and pleasure to welcome the distinguished members of the 9th Term of the Croatian Parliament. In accordance with the legal obligation, I wouldbriefly present the Semiannual Information on the financial situation, the degree of realization of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy relating to the second six months of 2015. I will begin my presentation by looking at the most important macroeconomic trends in the second half of 2015, in which the CNB achieved its legally prescribed goals, price stability and financial stability, and with the available monetary policy measures acted in the direction of creating the conditions for stronger growth of lending, primarily the management, and therefore stronger economic growth. I will also look at the process of converting loans in the Swiss franc. Macroeconomic developments and policy monets Economic activity in Croatia, after six consecutive years of contraction, finallyentered the recovery phase in 2015. Growth in economic activity continued to accelerate in the second half of 2015, when it reached 1.5% compared to the first half of the year. All components of domestic demand, as well as exports, continued to grow in the second half of 2015. age. Favourable outputs on the service export side primarily mirror exceptionally good achievements in tourism. The growth in personal consumption can largely be linked to favourable labour market developments, tax reform and further falls in oil prices as well as prehrane. This has strengthened household consumer opportunities, as well as consumer optimism and contributed to an increase in consumer appetite. In terms of investments, growth in the second half of 2015 was mainly generated by private investment. Growth in exports and domestic for demand also led to a sharp increase in imports. At the level of the entire second semester of 2015 economic activity was 2.4% higher than in the same period of the previous year, while full-year growth of 1.6%. The strengthening of economic activityand encouraged somewhat more favourable developments in the labour market, seen as the number of employees continued to grow, especially in service industries, during the second half of 2015. Employment also increased year-on-year, growing by 0.7%, breakingthe years-long negative trend in employment developments. Also, in the second half of 2015, a slight increase in gross wages continued. I will now look at inflationary developments. Consumer price inflation decreased in the second half of 2015, from 0% in June 2015 to -0.6% in December 2015, mainly as a result of the spillover of lower global crude oil and food commodity prices to domestic prices. The annual decline in energy prices accelerated slightly to -5.0% in December 2015, and the annualrate of price changes in food products and services decreased. On the other hand, the annual rate of change in the prices of industrial products has increased. If, however, the annual rate of change in the GDP deflator, a broadly defined price index excluding import prices from the calculation, is observed, it averaged -0.1% in the second half of 2015, which is similar to the previous period. When moving in the balance of payments, I would point out that the excess current account balance of the balance of payments in the whole of 2015 reached 5.2% of GDP . In the second half of 2015, foreign capital flows were marked by net capital outflows in the balance of payments financial account as a result of a noticeable improvement in the net debt position of domestic sectors. Consequently, the relative showngross and net foreign indebtedness (expressed as the ratio to gross domestic product) improved compared to the end of June 2015. The biggest influence on capital flows with foreign countries was the reaction of banks to the adoption of amendments to the Consumer Act on lending at the end of September. In particular, during September and October 2015, banks deposited abroad or repaid foreign loans in the amount of over HRK 12 billion. In these months, the effects of the seasonal increase in the net foreign assets of the bank sector under the influence of the tourist season are usually already exhausted, so it can be established that the activities undertaken by the banks in order to reconcile currency positions after the legalization of the conversion of loans in francs resulted in a large outflow of funds into the inozemstvo. This also moves on to the activities of the Croatian National Bank, which was largely marked by the aforementioned outflow of funds abroad. In difficult conditions in the financial market, the CNB continued to implement an expansionary monetary policy, while maintaining the stability of the exchange rate of the kuna against the euro. With a series of related measures in the second half of September and the beginning of October, the CNB further increased the liquidity of the monetary system in order to calm the exchange rate pressures and interest rates that have occurred in the financial market as a result of legislative changes regulating the conversion and partial write-off of loans with a currency clause in the Swiss franc. The nominal exchange rate of the kuna against the euro for most of the third quarter remained at slightly lower levels compared to the first half of the year. However, in the second half of September, the kuna weakened against the euro. The weakening of the kuna was driven by increased demand from banks for foreign exchange related to the adjustment of their foreign exchange position to the imbalance caused by the posting of the expected write-off of some loans related to the Swiss franc. The CNB's foreign exchange intervention ensured liquidity on the foreign exchange market, thereby calming the pressures on the exchange rate of the domestic currency. Following foreign exchange intervention and other CNB measures, the flowstabilised, with the average exchange rate in the second half of 2015 being EUR 7.59/HRK, which is 0.6% lower than the average achieved in the same period in 2014. In parallel with the pressures on the exchange rate, tensions in the money market were manifested in the increase overovernight interest rates to about 2% in the second half of September. The CNB eased these tensions by increasing liquidity through the reintroduction of regular reverse repo operations and the abolition of mandatory treasury bills. In doing so, the CNB acted in relatively favourable conditions, regarding the strengthening of the current account surplus, strong fiscal adjustments and the inflow of large foreign direct investment at the very time when the banks were posting the first estimates of the effects of conversion and carrying out related transactions. Monetary policy sat on the side of the reagto address as much as possible the distortions that occurred in the cash and foreign exchange markets at the end of September. At the same time, they sought to take advantage of the additional degrees of freedom to introduce monetary policy, which have provided a continued strengthening of the non-pricecompetitiveness of the economy and an improvement in the current account balance of the balance of payments, as well as the strong fiscal adjustment we have seen in the past year. Speaking about the financing conditions of the state and other domestic sectors, in conditions of high liquidityunder the expansionary monetary policy of the CNB, domestic financing costs in the second half of 2015 remained at historically low levels. In addition, the Bank Lending Survey shows that credit underwriting standards have also continued to be post-easing. Nevertheless, deleveraging of the population and businesses sectors in the domestic market continued during the second half of 2015. Nevertheless, there is a noticeable shift towards kuna lending, primarily citizens. At the end of 2015, the CNB's gross international reserves amounted to EUR 13.7 billion. euro and were almost at the same level as in the middle of the year, while they grew by EUR 1.0 billion compared to the end of 2014. EUR or 8.0%. Net available reserves decreased in the second half of the year (by EUR 0.2 billion). eur or by 1.7%) as a result of the CNB's foreign exchange interventions carried out with the aim of stabilising the exchange rate. But at the year-on-year level, their increase of EUR 0.5 billion was achieved. (4.4%), therefore reached EUR 11.2 billion at the end of 2015. EUR. Gross and net international reserves continue to significantlyoutweigh the amounts of the narrowest monetary aggregates - primary money (M0) and monetary mass (Ml. The CNB invests the funds of international reserves mainly in US and German state securities and in the securities of other developed countries that are considered to be sigurnima, primarily managed by the principles of liquidity and security. The rate of return of the CNB's dollar portfolio for trading in 2015 was 0.25%, while the rate of return of the CNB's euro trading portfolio in the same period was 0.00%. It should be noted that the negative interest rates of almost all countries on the CNB's investment spectrum significantly limit the possibility of achieving more favourable rates of return. Something more about developments in the banking sector. In total, in 2015, banks' assets decreased by 1.2% inthe end of excluding the impact of exchange rate developments. This is due to the absence of credit growth, the sale of non-performing receivables and the continuation of bank deleveraging, but also the application of legal changes related to loans in Swiss francs, which resultedin a loss in the business. Banks reported a loss (before tax) of EUR 4.7 billion in the whole year. marten. Excluding the impact of conversion costs, bank profits show a slight increase in 2015, mainly due to lower provisioning costs for loan portfolio losses . Speaking of partially and completely non-performing loans, in 2015 their growth stopped to start more 2008. The share of loans from risk groups B and C decreased from 17.1%, at the end of 2014, to 16.6% at the end of 2015. Sales of receivables, especially in the companies sector, had a key impact on the evolution of loan quality. The ageing of the portfolio, strengthened by the impact of regulatory rules on the gradual increase in value corrections for long-term messy placements, has had a noticeable increase in group B and C loan coverage through value corrections (from 51.3% to 56.6%). The application of legal provisions on the conversion of loans in Swiss francs has also affected the fall in the rate of total capital of banks, sitting by the decrease in own funds due to the loss of the current year, and on the other hand by increasing banks' exposure to currency risk. In addition, the decrease in own funds was also influenced by higher dividend payments. Nevertheless, the total capital rate remainshigh in the soil axis - at the end of 2015 it was 20.9%, noticeably higher than the prescribed minimum total capital rate of 8% and other regulatory capital requirements and capital buffers. What were the main characteristics of fiscal policy in the observed gap ofthe rounds? In the second half of last year, the general government deficit continued to shrink year-on-year, both due to further revenue growth and the fall in expenditure. Indirect tax revenues continued to contribute the most to the growth of total revenues, whilethe expenditure side of the budget continued to strongly reduce general government investments. If the whole of 2015 is observed, the general government deficit amounted to EUR 10.7 billion. (3.2% of GDP), which is up by EUR 7.4 billion. (2.3 percentage points of GDP) lower than in 2014. Kad is a general government debt, at the end of December 2015 it amounted to 289.7 billion. kuna or 86.7% of GDP. I would like to continue this presentation with a few notes on the conversion of loans in Swiss francs. Immediately after the entry into force of the CCP WALL, the CNB began to carry outits legal obligation to supervise the conversion in all credit institutions to which the conversion obligation was concerned. The CNB's supervision has been continuous throughout the process of preparing and carrying out the conversion, and all the banks involved are dailyabout the requested notices, documentation and observations on all the circumstances relevant for the implementation of the conversion as well as reports on the execution of all conversion obligations. In this way, draft annexes of contracts, conversion calculation forms, reviews of interest rates, exchange rates, types and models of loans, loan terms and conditions were obtained from banks, both for approved CHF loans and for "parnjak" loans in EUR. In cases where, on the basis of the received documentation and information from banks,corrections of documents and observed irregularities in the presented actions were requested. In this way, during the implementation of the conversion, and in connection with the supervisory activities of the CNB, the following was done: 1. several banks excluded the disputed from the order from the contract annex proposaland the amended annexes were resubmitted to customers, amending, offering and resubmitting to bank customers 27,220 contract annexes; 2. The two banks reiterated the conversion calculations for all customers who were entitled to conversion inorder not to disadvantage their customers compared to the customers of other banks, 6,954 new ones, i.e. repeated calculations of the conversion, which are offered and delivered to the clients of these banks; 3. the two banks subsequently produced and submitted conversion calculations for cancelled credit agreements to customers, which prepared and offered customers 544 additional conversion calculations; 4. the subsequent calculation of the conversion was carried out for the debtors of one bank wherethe conversion was incorrectly applied and the interest rate was valid on the day of approval, and not on the day of the contracting of the loan, which prepared and offered clients 400 new conversion calculations; 5. Formal measures have been initiated against banks in cases of identified illegalities in the application of zidzpk (recordci, solutions and misdemeanour procedures) - the CNB issued five minutes and two solutions, and three misdemeanour proceedings were initiated. These activities covered more than 35,000 conversion calculations, i.e. contract annexes, which represents a significant share of the total number of 54,663 accepted conversions (according to data provided Ministry of Finance). At the same time, from mid-November 2015 to the second half of April 2016, 2,251 consumer complaints related to conv ersion were received and processed in the CNB. Please note that this number of processed consumer complaints related to the conversion exceeds the three-year average of consumer complaints received in the CNB. Concluding considerations Although the debate in the past few days in parliament has been much broader, in the end I willfocus on only a few issues in the middle - with full appreciation of the right of members of parliament to discuss everything they hold important - that seem to me to be the most urgent for citizens. The first question is transparency of the work of the CNB. Over the past two days, there has been a lot of discussion about transparent, but the discussion clearly did not understand what was being discussed, which is clear from quoting one study in the wrong context. Let me briefly explain how the CNB ranks according to different transparency measures. Economists have developed a series of andmonetary policy transparency annexes that try to measure the precision with which central banks quantify targets, specify instruments and elaborate details of the mechanisms by which they achieve their goals. Openness can be measured in a more dimensionalija - one can measure transparency in monetary policy management, as well as in the transparency of policies aimed at maintaining financial stability. According to the Dincera and Eichengreena index, which constructed one of the indicators of transparency of monetar politics, which I assume was mentioned in the debate over the last two days, the CNB is indeed one of the least transparent central banks in Europe. For which there are very clearly specified reasons. On the other hand, however, Horvath and Vasko, in2013 constructed an index of policy transparency aimed at maintaining financial stability, show that the CNB is one of the most transparent or open central banks in the world. Such a combination of high transparencyin both matters of financial stability and low transparency in the monetary policy dimension is relatively unusual - the two dimensions of transparency usually go together, hand in hand whereas institutional development improves all areas of central bank activity. What's this about? Transparency, as a desirable determinant of monetary policy conduct, is usually associated with the monetary inflation targeting regime. Inflation targeting assumes a flexible exchange rate since exchange rate interventionsare considered a highly opaque monetary policy instrument, especially if they are not announced in advance. Before for twenty years, however, the CNB began to lead the exchange rate regime of managed fluctuation of the kuna; in such conditions, if the central bank is transparent, speculators are very cheap to bet against the exchange rate regime, and it can be very expensive for the central bank to defend the stability of the exchange rate. Why? Because he's announcing to speculators what he's going to do. And that is why the CNB's monetary policy cannot be transparentna to this extent by the theorist Eichengreen. If it were, the CNB would lose money from the Republic of Croatia for the account of speculators. Considering the amount of foreign exchange debt of all sectors (population, enterprises and the state), which amounts to almost HRK 550 billion, or approximately 160% of GDP - a stable exchange rate is an absolute prerequisite for preserving financial stability. On the other hand, the CNB has never advocated fixing the exchange rate - which would also be a transparent form of monetary policy - and has left the possibility for the exchange rate to gradually adapt to economic funds. For transparency and success in maintaining financial stability - which is of course closely related to the conduct of the correct monetary policy - Croatia is ranked among the most transparent and successful countries in the world. But much more urgent is the fact that financial stability does not relate, as it is often irresponsibly criticised, only to the security of the banking system, but consequently to every citizen of our country. The citizens of Croatia - and we are glad - see financial stabilityas your normal everyday life. They can wake up safely every day, and know the real value of their salary, and calculate what they can buy with it, and how they can plan for their future and the future of their families. They don't have to look forward to you with anxiety, and be afraid of whether tomorrow or the day after tomorrow their income will be twice or three times less value. They don't even have to be afraid that their savings will be worth less, as has happened many times in the past. The same certainty is essential for the functioning of theeconomy in our country, for every entrepreneur, for all those who have to earn money on the open market to pay workers and all their obligations or invest. Thus, the CNB is transparent where it can and can be, given the monetar and exchange rate regime and the necessity of preserving financial stability. However, the necessity of preserving the exchange rate regime and financial stability are sometimes a dam to communication openness, which the CNB wants at least as much as some critics. Within the frameworkof such a certain space of manoeuvre regarding transparency, the Croatian National Bank has been and remains open to communication with the public, including for a reasoned public debate on all aspects of the central bank's activities. Furthermore, I will devote a few words to the cost-effectiveness of the CNB. First, I must point out that, contrary to the claims heard in recent days, the CNB is not financed from the state budget, but from its own income. The CNB produces financial statements about its operations every year, which are subject toaudit in accordance with international accounting standards and domestic audit regulations . and submits the same audit report to the Parliament of the Republic of Croatia. This means that the Croatian Parliament has for years had all the data on the work and operations of the CNB, and an audit assessment of the efficiency of the business, and the additionof no data from the auditor it appoints at any time could and can request. In addition, the CNB, in line with best practice in central banks, has also established an external Audit Committee, consisting of independent experts, which assesses the quality of workof the independent external auditor. It is important to point out that the CNB earns enough to cover the costs of its operations and for transfers to the Ministry of Finance in conditions of historically lowest interest rates, i.e. negative euro interest rates for up to six years untilthe mention. This is achieved through a good policy of managing financial resources, notably the correct decision to buy long-term securities since 2011, thereby extending the maturity of the portfolio, which proved to be the correct investment decision, given the sharp fall in euro bond yields that followed. With this move, the CNB's revenues for the period 2012-2015 increased by about HRK 1800 million, which was de facto all transferred to the Ministry of Finance. In the following years, that is, from 2012 onwards, decisions were also taken to increase the same portfolio as well as to extend its maturity, ensuring stable incomes in the years from 2016 onwards. The Croatian National Bank stands out among EU countries as a bank with below average operating costs and above averageprofits. Although profits are not the objective of central banks' actions, the profits generated by the CNB are one of the highest if it is put in relation to the size of the bank's assets or GDP; Thus, in 2014, the CNB made a profit of about 0.8% of GDP and only the central banks of the Czech Republic,Ireland and Cyprus had a higher level of profit. If the CNB's operating costs (0.09% of GDP) are compared with those of central banks of countries with relatively similar populations, for example Latvia (0.15% of GDP), Bulgaria (0.12% of GDP), Ireland and Lithuania (0.11% of GDP), Austria and Slovakia (0.1%), Hungary (0.09% of GDP) and Slovenia (0.08% of GDP), it is obvious that the CNB has settled among the more frugal and economical central banks. If the absolute amount of the cost of doing business per employee is observed - which was the most discussed in the previous two days - it can be noted that among comparable countries only the Central Bank of Bulgaria (which has the lowest level of GDP per capita and the lowest wages) has lower costs than the CNB, while the CNB's costs are similar to those in RomaniaUnjska and the Czech Republic and lower than in Hungary and Poland. Also, regarding the costs of doing business, the CNB, as a public procurement payer, presents them very transparently on its website, therefore this data is publicly available. The involvementof the state audit could contribute to the additional transparency in the CNB's operations, if it were to assess whether Croatia has an efficient, economical and efficient central bank by method of comparative European value criteria (benchmarking), and on the operating cost plan. For the same purpose and in the same way, the Office for State Audit has, of course, the possibility to analyse and evaluate all the other institutions it audits, thus showing citizens in the best way the effectiveness of state institutions, whether they have too many or too few employees, whether they have higher or lower costs than comparable institutions in the EU, and so on. Therefore, contrary to the claims heard in recent days, the CNB does not in any way close before the State Audit, but would like - that its activities, not withwhich it is legally aligned with the European acquis, that is, with the prescribed principles in the control of central bank institutions in the EU - but also to contribute to the assessment of the effectiveness of the CNB in the usual way of benchmarking the CNB with comparable European institutions. That's for sure the highest quality information that citizens can get about both the CNB and other state institutions. Finally, I must reflect on the extent to which the objectives of price stability and financial stability have been achieved in the period to which thereport relates. In terms of price stability, as could be heard in the previous days in the debate, Croatia has seen a very slight decrease in the general level of consumer prices. However, it is necessary to know that this fall in consumer prices is entirely the result of a fall in import prices. The GDP deflator - the broadest price measure that deflases all economic activity and excludes import prices, was stable at a level of about zero. As export prices fell less than imported prices, the conditions of the international spreadfor Croatia were improving, or in simple terms, for one unit of export goods, Croatia was able to import more units of imported goods than before. This fall in prices increased the purchasing power of households and it is no coincidence that personal consumption in the observednom period continued to rise strongly. Likewise, there has been a recovery in corporate profits, as well as a decrease in the burden of indebtedness of the economy and citizens and easier servicing of interest rates - phenomena that are exactly contrary to the increase in the real debt burden that occurs at a time of deflation. In terms of financial stability, the CNB also achieved this goal in circumstances that were extremely difficult - a long-standing recession that was the second strongest in the EU in intensity, after Greece. The CNB is so extremely efficient if the efficiency is measured by the absence of the cost of remediation of commercial banks in the Republic of Croatia. Most European countries, despite the milder recession, had high fiscal bailout costs during this period, i.e. helping banks. Thus, and according to this criterion, the CNB is cost-effective. Also, with full respect for all the critical appearances of respected MPs and MPs in the past two days, I am extremely sorry that falsehoods have been told, which ultimately affect all CNB employees. I will say only briefly: the CNBpays no one for saunas and massages, we do not serve shrimp and lobsters, nor do we pay christmas bonuses and recourses. Likewise, we do not employ any Masterchefs and sommeliers, but we have outsourced the services of restaurants and some other services, thus making the CNB savings between 20 and 40 percent compared to the fact that it employs these employees itself. By cost, we are at the bottom of the European central bank rankings, and in terms of efficiency at the top - as I informed you today.
