text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA HNB je sauvao stabilnost cijena i financijsku stabilnost Objavljeno: 4.11.2016. Vrsta Govor Govornik Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner Tema Polugodinja informacija o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike za drugo polugodite 2015. godine Dogaanje Sjednica Hrvatskog sabora Datum 4.11.2016. dogaanja Polugodinja informacija o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike za drugo polugodite 2015. godine Potovani gospodine Predsjednie, uvaene zastupnice i zastupnici, potovane dame i gospodo, ast mi je i zadovoljstvo pozdraviti uvaene zastupnike i zastupnice 9. saziva Hrvatskog sabora. Sukladno zakonskoj obvezi, ukratko bih predstavio Polugodinju informaciju o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike koja se odnosi na drugih est mjeseci 2015. godine. Zapoet u svoje izlaganje osvrtom na najvanije makroekonomske trendove u drugoj polovini 2015. godine, u kojem je HNB ostvario svoje zakonom propisane ciljeve, stabilnost cijena i financijsku stabilnost, i raspoloivim mjerama monetarne politike djelovao u pravcu stvaranja uvjeta za jai rast kreditiranja, u prvom redu gospodarstva, a time i snaniji gospodarski rast. Osvrnut u se i na proces konverzije kredita u vicarskom franku. Makroekonomska kretanja i monetama politika Gospodarska aktivnost u Hrvatskoj je, nakon est uzastopnih godina kontrakcije, u 2015. godini konano ula u fazu oporavka. Rast gospodarske aktivnosti nastavio se ubrzavati i u drugom polugoditu 2015. godine, kada je dosegnuo 1,5% u odnosu na prvu polovinu godine. Sve sastavnice domae potranje, kao i izvoz, nastavile su rasti u drugom polugoditu 2015. godine. Povoljna ostvarenja na strani izvoza usluga poglavito zrcale iznimno dobra ostvarenja u turizmu. Rast osobne potronje u najveoj se mjeri moe povezati s povoljnim kretanjima na tritu rada, poreznom reformom i daljnjim padom cijena nafte kao i prehrane. To je ojaalo potroake mogunosti kuanstava, kao i optimizam potroaa i pridonijelo poveanju sklonosti potronji. Kad je rije o investicijama, rast u drugoj polovini 2015. preteito su generirale privatne investicije. Rast izvoza i domae potranje doveo je i do snanog porasta uvoza. Na razini cijeloga drugog polugodita 2015. gospodarska je aktivnost bila za 2,4% via nego u istom razdoblju prethodne godine, dok je na razini cijele godine zabiljeen rast od 1,6%. Jaanje ekonomske aktivnosti potaknulo je neto povoljnija kretanja na tritu rada vidljiva u nastavku rasta broja zaposlenih, posebno u uslunim djelatnostima, tijekom drugog polugodita 2015. godine. Zaposlenost se takoer poveala na godinjoj razini ostvarivi rast od 0,7%, ime je prekinut viegodinji negativan trend kretanja zaposlenosti. Takoer, u drugoj polovini 2015. nastavljen je i blagi rast bruto plaa. Osvrnut u se sada na inflacijska kretanja. Inflacija potroakih cijena u drugom se polugoditu 2015. snizila, s 0% u lipnju 2015. na -0,6% u prosincu 2015. i to uglavnom kao rezultat prelijevanja niih svjetskih cijena sirove nafte i prehrambenih sirovina na domae cijene. Godinji pad cijena energije tako se blago ubrzao na -5,0% u prosincu 2015., a smanjila se i godinja stopa promjene cijena prehrambenih proizvoda te usluga. S druge strane, poveala se godinja stopa promjene cijena industrijskih proizvoda. Ako se pak promatra godinja stopa promjene deflatora BDP-a, iroko definiranog indeksa cijena koji iz izrauna iskljuuje uvozne cijene, ona je u drugom polugoditu 2015. prosjeno iznosila -0,1%, to je slino kao i u prethodnom razdoblju. Kod kretanja u platnoj bilanci istaknuo bih da je viak salda tekueg rauna platne bilance u cijeloj 2015. dosegnuo 5,2% BDP-a. Rezultat je to ve spomenutih dobrih turistikih rezultata, kao i snanijeg koritenja raspoloivih sredstava iz fondova EU-a, ali i statistikog tretmana konverzije kredita u vicarskim francima kroz poboljanje salda primarnog dohotka (od otprilike 2 postotna boda). Tokove kapitala s inozemstvom u drugoj je polovini 2015. obiljeio neto odljev kapitala na financijskom raunu platne bilance, i to kao rezultat zamjetnog poboljanja neto dunike pozicije domaih sektora. Posljedino, relativni pokazatelji bruto i neto inozemne zaduenosti (izraeni kao omjer prema bruto domaem proizvodu) poboljali su se u odnosu na kraj lipnja 2015. Najvei utjecaj na tokove kapitala s inozemstvom je imala reakcija banaka na usvajanje izmjena i dopuna Zakona o potroakom kreditiranju krajem rujna. Konkretno, tijekom rujna i listopada 2015. banke su poloile u inozemstvo ili vratile inozemne kredite u iznosu od preko 12 milijardi kuna. U navedenim su mjesecima uinci sezonskog porasta neto inozemne aktive bankarskog sektora pod utjecajem turistike sezone obino ve iscrpljeni, pa se moe utvrditi da su aktivnosti koje su banke poduzimale u cilju usklaivanja valutnih pozicija nakon ozakonjivanja konverzije kredita u francima rezultirale velikim odljevom sredstava u inozemstvo. Time ujedno prelazim na djelovanje Hrvatske narodne banke, koje je u velikoj mjeri bilo obiljeeno upravo navedenim odljevom sredstava u inozemstvo. HNB je u oteanim uvjetima na financijskom tritu nastavio provoditi ekspanzivnu monetarnu politiku, istodobno odravajui stabilnost teaja kune prema euru. Nizom povezanih mjera u drugoj polovini rujna i poetkom listopada HNB je dodatno poveala likvidnost monetarnog sustava kako bi se smirili pritisci na teaj i kamatne stope koji su se javili na financijskom tritu kao posljedica zakonskih izmjena kojima se regulira konverzija i djelomian otpis kredita s valutnom klauzulom u vicarskom franku. Nominalni teaj kune prema euru tijekom veeg dijela treeg tromjeseja zadravao se na malo niim razinama u odnosu na prvu polovinu godine. Meutim, u drugoj polovini rujna kuna je oslabjela u odnosu na euro. Slabljenje kune bilo je potaknuto poveanom potranjom banaka za devizama vezanom uz prilagodbu njihove devizne pozicije neravnotei uzrokovanoj knjienjem oekivanog otpisa dijela kredita vezanih uz vicarski franak. HNB je deviznom intervencijom osigurao likvidnost na deviznom tritu, ime je smirio pritiske na teaj domae valute. Nakon devizne intervencije i drugih mjera HNB-a teaj se stabilizirao pa je prosjeni teaj u drugoj polovini 2015. iznosio je 7,59 EUR/HRK, to je za 0,6% nie od prosjeka ostvarenog u istom razdoblju 2014. godine. Usporedno s pritiscima na teaj tenzije na novanom tritu oitovale su se u porastu prekononih kamatnih stopa na oko 2% u drugoj polovini rujna. HNB je te tenzije ublaio poveanjem likvidnosti kroz ponovno uvoenje redovitih obratnih repo operacija i ukidanje obveznih blagajnikih zapisa. Pri tome je HNB djelovao u razmjerno povoljnim uvjetima jaanja vika na tekuem raunu, snane fiskalne prilagodbe i priljeva velikog inozemnog izravnog ulaganja upravo u vrijeme kad su banke knjiile prve procjene uinaka konverzije i provodile povezane transakcije. Monetarna politika sjedne je strane reagirala kako bi u to veoj mjeri otklonila poremeaje koji su se javili na novanom i deviznom tritu krajem rujna. Istovremeno su se nastojali iskoristiti dodatne stupnjeve slobode uvoenju monetarne politike koje su pruili kontinuirano jaanje necjenovne konkurentnosti gospodarstva i poboljanje salda tekueg rauna platne bilance, kao i snana fiskalna prilagodba koju smo vidjeli u protekloj godini. Govorei o uvjetima financiranja drave i ostalih domaih sektora, u uvjetima visoke likvidnosti koje podrava ekspanzivna monetarna politika HNB-a, domai trokovi financiranja u drugoj polovini 2015. godine zadrali su se na povijesno niskim razinama. Usto, Anketa o kreditnoj aktivnosti banaka pokazuje da su se i standardi odobravanja kredita nastavili postupno ublaavati. Unato tome, razduivanje sektora stanovnitva i poduzea na domaem tritu nastavilo se i tijekom druge polovine 2015. Ipak, vidljivo je okretanje prema kunskom kreditiranju, prvenstveno graana. Bruto meunarodne priuve HNB-a na kraju 2015. iznosile su 13,7 mlrd. EUR i bile su gotovo na istoj razini kao i sredinom godine, dok su u odnosu na kraj 2014. godine porasle za 1,0 mlrd. EUR ili 8,0%. Neto raspoloive priuve smanjile su se u drugoj polovini godine (za 0,2 mlrd. EUR ili za 1,7%) kao rezultat deviznih intervencija HNB-a provedenih s ciljem stabilizacije teaja. No na razini godine ostvarenje njihov porast od 0,5 mlrd. EUR (4,4%), stoga su na kraju 2015. dosegnule 11,2 mlrd. EUR. Bruto i neto meunarodne priuve i dalje znatno nadmauju iznose najuih monetarnih agregata - primarnog novca (M0) i novane mase (Ml). Sredstva meunarodnih priuva HNB ulae preteito u amerike i njemake dravne vrijednosne papire te u vrijednosne papire drugih razvijenih zemalja koje se smatraju sigurnima, pri emu se poglavito rukovodi naelima likvidnosti i sigurnosti. Stopa povrata dolarskog portfelja HNB-a za trgovanje u 2015. iznosila je 0,25%, dok je stopa povrata eurskog portfelja HNB-a za trgovanje u istom razdoblju iznosila 0,00%. Pritom valja naglasiti kako negativne kamatne stope gotovo svih zemalja iz spektra ulaganja HNB-a znaajno ograniavaju mogunost ostvarivanja povoljnijih stopa povrata. Neto vie o kretanjima u bankarskom sektoru. Ukupno se u 2015. imovina banaka smanjila za 1,2% nakon iskljuivanja utjecaja teajnih kretanja. To je posljedica izostanka kreditnog rasta, prodaje nenaplativih potraivanja i nastavka razduivanja banaka, ali i primjene zakonskih izmjena vezanih uz kredite u vicarskim francima, koja je rezultirala gubicima u poslovanju. Banke su u cijeloj godini iskazale gubitak (prije poreza) u visini od 4,7 mlrd. kuna. Iskljui li se utjecaj troka konverzije, dobit banaka pokazuje blagi porast u 2015., to je uglavnom rezultat niih trokova rezerviranja za gubitke u kreditnom portfelju. Govorei o djelomino i potpuno nenaplativim kreditima, tijekom 2015. zaustavio se njihov rast za poet jo 2008. godine. Udio kredita rizinih skupina B i C smanjio se sa 17,1%, koliko je iznosio na kraju 2014., na 16,6% na kraju 2015. Kljuan utjecaj na kretanje kvalitete kredita imale su prodaje potraivanja, osobito u sektoru trgovakih drutava. Starenje portfelja, ojaano utjecajem regulatornih pravila o postupnom poveavanju ispravaka vrijednosti za dugotrajno neuredne plasmane, utjecalo je na zamjetan rast pokrivenosti kredita skupina B i C ispravcima vrijednosti (s 51,3% na 56,6%). Primjena zakonskih odredbi o konverziji kredita u vicarskom francima utjecala je i na pad stope ukupnoga kapitala banaka, sjedne strane smanjenjem regulatornoga kapitala zbog gubitka tekue godine, a s druge strane poveanjem izloenosti banaka valutnom riziku. Usto, na smanjenje regulatornoga kapitala utjecale su i vee isplate dividendi. Unato tome, stopa ukupnoga kapitala i dalje je ostala visoka - na kraju 2015. iznosila je 20,9%, zamjetno vie od propisane minimalne stope ukupnoga kapitala od 8% i ostalih regulatornih kapitalnih zahtjeva i zatitnih slojeva kapitala. Koja su bila osnovna obiljeja fiskalne politike u promatranome razdoblju? U drugoj polovini prole godine nastavilo se smanjivanje manjka ope drave na godinjoj razini, kako zbog daljnjeg rasta prihoda i tako i zbog pada rashoda. Rastu ukupnih prihoda i dalje su najvie pridonosili prihodi od neizravnih poreza, dok se na rashodnoj strani prorauna nastavilo snano smanjivanje investicija ope drave. Promatra li se cijela 2015. godina, manjak ope drave iznosio je 10,7 mlrd. kuna (3,2% BDP-a), to je za 7,4 mlrd. kuna (2,3 postotna boda BDP-a) manje u odnosu na 2014. Kad je rije o dugu ope drave, on je na kraju prosinca 2015. iznosio 289,7 mlrd. kuna ili 86,7% BDP-a. Nastavio bih ovo izlaganje s nekoliko napomena o konverziji kredita u vicarskim francima. Odmah po stupanju na snagu ZID ZPK, HNB je zapoela sa izvravanjem svoje zakonske obveze nadzora provoenja konverzije u svim kreditnim institucijama na koje se je odnosila obveza konverzije. Nadzor HNB je bio kontinuiran tijekom itavog postupka pripreme i provoenja konverzije te su od svih ukljuenih banaka dnevno traene obavijesti, dokumentacija i oitovanja o svim okolnostima relevantnim za provoenje konverzije kao i izvjea o izvrenju svih obveza vezano uz konverziju. Na taj nain su od banaka pribavljani nacrti aneksa ugovora, obrasci izrauna konverzija, pregledi kamatnih stopa, teajeva, vrsta i modela kredita, uvjeta kredita i to kako za odobrene CHF kredite, tako i za parnjake" kredite u EUR. U sluajevima kada je na osnovi zaprimljene dokumentacije i informacija od banaka ocijenjeno potrebnim, zatraene su korekcije dokumenata i uoenih nepravilnosti u iskazanim postupanjima. Na taj nainje tijekom provedbe konverzije, te u vezi sa supervizorskim aktivnostima HNB-a uinjeno sljedee: 1. nekoliko banaka je iz prijedloga aneksa ugovora iskljuilo sporne odredbe te su izmijenjeni aneksi ponovo dostavljeni klijentima, ime je izmijenjeno, ponueno i ponovno dostavljeno klijentima banaka 27.220 aneksa ugovora; 2. dvije banke ponovile su izraune konverzije za sve klijente koji su imali pravo na konverziju kako svoje klijente ne bi doveli u nepovoljniji poloaj u odnosu na klijente drugih banaka, na osnovi ega su izraena 6.954 nova, tj. ponovljena izrauna konverzije, koji su ponueni i dostavljeni klijentima tih banaka; 3. dvije su banke naknadno izradile i dostavile klijentima izraune konverzije za otkazane ugovore o kreditu ime su pripremljena i klijentima ponuena 544 dodatna izrauna konverzije; 4. naknadni izraun konverzije proveden je za dunike jedne banke kod kojih je u konverziji pogreno primijenjena kamatna stopa vaea na dan odobravanja, a ne na dan ugovaranja kredita ime je pripremljeno i klijentima ponueno 400 novih izrauna konverzije; 5. pokrenute su formalne mjere protiv banaka u sluajevima utvrenih nezakonitosti u primjeni ZIDZPK-a (zapisnici, rjeenja i prekrajni postupci) - HNB je izdao pet zapisnika i dva rjeenja, a pokrenuta su i tri prekrajna postupka. Spomenutim aktivnostima bilo je obuhvaeno vie od 35.000 izrauna konverzije, odnosno aneksa ugovora, to ini znaajan udio u broju ukupnom broju od 54.663 prihvaenih konverzije (prema podacima dostavljenima Ministarstvu financija). Istodobno, od sredine studenog 2015. godine do druge polovine travnja 2016. godine, u HNB-uje zaprimljen i obraen 2.251 prigovor potroaa vezan uz konverziju. Napominjemo da ovaj broj obraenih prigovora potroaa uvezi sa konverzijom prelazi trogodinji prosjek zaprimljenih prigovora potroaa u HNB-u. Zakljuna razmatranja Premda je rasprava proteklih dana u Saboru bila znatno ira, za kraj u se usredotoiti samo na nekoliko pitanja - uz puno uvaavanje prava saborskih zastupnika da raspravljaju o svemu to dre vanim - koja mi se ine najhitnijima za graane. Prvo pitanje je transparentnost rada HNB-a. Protekla se dva dana puno raspravljalo o transparentnosti, no u raspravi se oito nije razumjelo o emu se govori, to je jasno iz citiranja jednog istraivanja u pogrenom kontekstu. Dopustite mi da kratko obrazloim kako HNB kotira prema razliitim mjerama transparentnosti. Ekonomisti su razvili niz indeksa transparentnosti monetarne politike kojima se pokuava mjeriti preciznost s kojom sredinje banke kvantificiraju ciljeve, specificiraju instrumente i razrauju detalje mehanizama kojima postiu svoje ciljeve. Otvorenost se moe mjeriti u vie dimenzija - moe se tako mjeriti transparentnost u voenju monetarne politike, kao i u transparentnosti politika usmjerenih na odravanja financijske stabilnosti. Prema indeksu Dincera i Eichengreena^, koji su konstruirali jedan od pokazatelja transparentnosti monetarne politike, a za koji pretpostavljam da se spominjao u raspravi zadnja dva dana, HNB je doista jedna od najmanje transparentnih sredinjih banaka u Europi. Za to postoje vrlo jasno specificirani razlozi. S druge strane, meutim, Horvath i Vako^, koji su 2013. godine konstruirali indeks transparentnosti politika usmjerene na odravanje financijske stabilnosti, pokazuju da je HNB jedna od najtransparentnijih odnosno najotvorenijih sredinjih banaka na svijetu. Takva kombinacija visoke transparentnosti u pitanjima financijske stabilnosti i niske transparentnosti u dimenziji monetarne politike razmjerno je neuobiajena - dvije dimenzije transparentnosti obino idu zajedno, ruku pod ruku, budui da institucionalni razvoj unaprjeuje sva podruja djelovanja sredinje banke. O emu se tu radi? Transparentnost se kao poeljna odrednica voenja monetarne politike obino povezuje s monetarnim reimom ciljanja inflacije. Ciljanje inflacije pretpostavlja fleksibilan teaj budui da se teajne intervencije smatraju izrazito netransparentnim instrumentom monetarne politike, pogotovo ukoliko se ne najavljuju unaprijed. Prije dvadesetak godina, meutim, HNB je zapoeo voditi teajni reim upravljanog fluktuiranja kune; u takvim uvjetima, ukoliko je sredinja banka transparentna, pekulantima se vrlo jeftino kladiti protiv teajnog reima, a sredinjoj banci moe biti vrlo skupo braniti stabilnost teaja. Zato? Zato to najavljuje pekulantima to e raditi. I zato HNB-ova monetarna politika ne moe biti transparentna po toj mjeri teoretiara Eichengreena. Kada bi bila, HNB bi gubio novce RH za raun pekulanata. S obzirom na iznos deviznog duga svih sektora (stanovnitva, poduzea i drave), a koji iznosi gotovo 550 milijardi kuna, odnosno otprilike 160% BDP-a - stabilan teaj apsolutni je preduvjet ouvanja financijske stabilnosti. S druge strane, HNB se nikada nije zaloio za fiksiranje teaja - to bi takoer bio transparentan oblik monetarne politike - i ostavio je mogunost da se teaj postupno prilagoava ekonomskim fundamentima. Za transparentnost i uspjeh u odravanju financijske stabilnosti - koji je naravno usko vezan i uz voenje ispravne monetarne politike - Hrvatska je rangirana meu najtransparentnije i najuspjenije zemlje na svijetu. No, puno je hitnija injenica da se financijska stabilnost ne odnosi, kako se esto neodgovorno kritizira, samo na sigurnost bankovnog sustava, ve posljedino i na svakog graanina nae zemlje. Graani Hrvatske - i to nam je drago - financijsku stabilnost doivljavaju kao svoju normalnu svakodnevicu. Mogu se sigurno probuditi svakog dana, i znati kolika je stvarna vrijednost njihove plae, i izraunati to s njom mogu kupiti, i kako mogu planirati svoju budunost i budunost svojih obitelji. Ne moraju sa zebnjom gledati prema naprijed, i bojati se hoe li sutra ili prekosutra njihova primanja biti dvaput ili triput manje vrijednosti. Ne moraju se bojati niti da e im tednja manje vrijediti, kao to se u prolosti vie puta dogaalo. Ista ta sigurnost je od kljune vanosti za funkcioniranje ekonomije u naoj zemlji, za svakog poduzetnika, za sve one koji moraju zaraditi na otvorenom tritu da bi platili radnike i sve svoje obveze ili investirali. Dakle, HNB je transparentan tamo gdje smije i moe biti, s obzirom na monetarni i teajni reim i nunost ouvanja financijske stabilnosti. No, nunost ouvanja teajnog reima i financijske stabilnosti ponekad su brana komunikacijskoj otvorenosti, koju HNB eli barem isto toliko koliko i pojedini kritiari. U okviru tako odreenog manevarskog prostora u pogledu transparentnosti, Hrvatska narodna banka bila je i ostaje otvorena za komunikaciju s javnou, ukljuivo za argumentiranu javnu raspravu o svim aspektima djelovanja sredinje banke. Nadalje, nekoliko u rijei posvetiti trokovnoj uinkovitosti HNB-a. Prvo, moram istaknuti da se, suprotno tvrdnjama koje su se zadnjih dana ule, HNB ne financira iz dravnog prorauna, ve iz vlastitih prihoda. HNB o svom poslovanju svake godine izrauje financijska izvjea, koja su podlona reviziji u skladu s meunarodnim raunovodstvenim standardima i domaim propisima o reviziji. to se revizije poslovanja sredinje banke tie, ona, dakle, i svih ovih godina postoji, i provodi ju, sukladno zakonu koji je donio Sabor RH, vanjski revizor kojeg imenuje Sabor RH, putem svog Odbora za proraun i financije, te isti izvjee o reviziji podnosi Saboru RH. To znai da Sabor RH ve godinama raspolae svim podacima o radu i poslovanju HNB-a, te revizorskom ocjenom uinkovitosti poslovanja, a dodatne podatke je od revizora kojeg imenuje u svakom trenutku mogao i moe zatraiti. Osim toga, HNB je, u skladu s najboljom praksom u sredinjim bankama, uspostavio i vanjski Revizorski odbor, koji ine nezavisni strunjaci, a koji ocjenjuje kvalitetu rada neovisnog vanjskog revizora. Bitno je istaknuti kako HNB dovoljno zarauje za pokrie trokova svojega poslovanja i za transfere Ministarstvu financija u uvjetima povijesno najniih kamatnih stopa, odnosno negativnih eurskih kamatnih stopa do est godina dospijea. To postie dobrom politikom upravljanja financijskim sredstvima, ponajprije ispravnom odlukom o kupnji dugoronih vrijednosnica od 2011. godine, ime je produeno dospijee portfelja, to se pokazalo ispravnom investicijskom odlukom, s obzirom na jak pad prinosa na eurske obveznice koji je uslijedio. Tim su potezom prihodi HNB-a za razdoblje 2012. - 2015. poveani za oko 1800 milijuna kuna, to je de facto sve preneseno Ministarstvu financija. U iduim godinama, dakle od 2012. nadalje, donesene su i odluke o poveanju istog portfelja kao i o produenju njegove ronosti, ime su osigurani stabilni prihodi i u godinama od 2016. nadalje. Hrvatska narodna banka meu zemljama EU-a izdvaja se kao banka s ispod prosjenim trokovima poslovanja i natprosjenom dobiti. Premda dobit nije cilj djelovanja sredinjih banaka, dobit koju ostvaruje HNB jedna je od najviih stavi li se u odnos s veliinom aktive banke ili BDP-om; tako je u 2014. HNB ostvario dobit od oko 0,8% BDP-a te su samo sredinja banke eke, Irske i Cipra imale viu razinu dobiti. Ako se trokovi poslovanja HNB-a (0,09% BDP-a) usporede s trokovima sredinjih banaka zemalja s relativno slinim brojem stanovnika, primjerice s Latvijom (0,15% BDP-a), Bugarskom (0,12% BDP-a), Irskom i Litvom (0,11% BDP-a), Austrijom i Slovakom (0,1%), Madarskom (0,09% BDP-a) i Slovenijom (0,08 % BDP-a), oito je da se HNB smjestio meu tedljivije i ekonominije sredinje banke. Promatra li se apsolutni iznos troka poslovanja po zaposlenom - o kojima je u prethodna dva dana bilo najvie rijei - moe se primijetiti da meu usporedivim zemljama samo sredinja banka Bugarske (koja ima najniu razinu BDP-a po glavi stanovnika i najnie plae) ima nie trokove od HNB-a, dok su trokovi HNB-a slini onima u Rumunjskoj i ekoj te nii nego u Madarskoj i Poljskoj. Takoer, to se tie trokova poslovanja, HNB ih, kao obveznik javne nabave, vrlo transparentno iskazuje na svojoj internetskoj stranici, dakle ti su podaci javno dostupni. Angaman dravne revizije mogao bi pridonijeti dodatnoj transparentnosti u poslovanju HNB-a, kad bi ona metodom usporednih europskih vrijednosnih kriterija (benchmarking), a na planu operativnih trokova, procjenjivala ima li Hrvatska efikasnu, ekonominu i uinkovitu sredinju banku. U istu svrhu i na isti nain, Ured za dravnu reviziju ima, naravno, mogunost analizirati i ocijeniti i sve ostale institucije koje revidira, ime graanima moe na najbolji nain ukazati na uinkovitost dravnih institucija, na to imaju li previe ili premalo zaposlenih, imaju li vie ili nie trokove od usporedivih institucija u EU i tako dalje. Dakle, suprotno tvrdnjama koje su se ule zadnjih dana, HNB se ni na koji nain ne zatvara pred Dravnom revizijom, ve bi volio - da njezino djelovanje, ne samo bude zakonski usklaeno s europskom pravnom steevinom, odnosno s propisanim naelima u kontroli institucije sredinjih banaka u EU - ve i da doprinese ocjeni uinkovitosti HNB- a na uobiajen nain benchmarkinga HNB-a s usporedivim europskim institucijama. To je sigurno najkvalitetnija informacija koju graani mogu dobiti kako o HNB-u, tako i o ostalim dravnim institucijama. Konano, moram se osvrnuti na mjeru u kojoj su ostvareni ciljevi stabilnosti cijena i financijske stabilnosti u razdoblju na koje se odnosi izvjee. U pogledu stabilnosti cijena, kako se moglo uti prethodnih dana u raspravi, Hrvatska biljei vrlo blagi pad ope razine potroakih cijena. Meutim, potrebno je znati daje taj pad potroakih cijena u cijelosti rezultat pada uvoznih cijena. Deflator BDP-a - najira mjera cijena kojom se deflacionira cjelokupna gospodarska aktivnost i koja iskljuuje uvozne cijene, bio je stabilan na razini od otprilike nule. Budui da su izvozne cijene padale manje od uvoznih, uvjeti meunarodne razmjene za Hrvatsku su se popravljali, ili pojednostavljeno, za jednu jedinicu izvozne robe, Hrvatska je mogla uvesti vie jedinica uvoznih roba nego ranije. Taj pad cijena je poveavao kupovnu mo kuanstava i nije sluajno to je osobna potronja u promatranom razdoblju nastavila snano rasti. Isto tako, zabiljeen je oporavak korporativnih profita, kao i smanjenje tereta zaduenosti gospodarstva i graana i lake servisiranje kamata - pojave koje su upravo suprotne porastu realnog tereta duga koji se dogaa u vrijeme deflacije. U pogledu financijske stabilnosti, HNB je ostvario i taj cilj u okolnostima koje su bile izuzetno teke - dugogodinje recesije koja je po intenzitetu bila druga najsnanija u EU, nakon Grke. HNB je tako iznimno uinkovit ukoliko se uinkovitost mjeri odsustvom troka sanacije poslovnih banaka u RH. Veina europskih zemalja, unato blae izraenoj recesiji, u tom je razdoblju imala visoke fiskalne trokove sanacije odnosno pomoi bankama. Dakle, i po ovom kriteriju, HNB je trokovno vrlo uinkovit. Takoer, uz puno potovanje svih kritikih istupa uvaenih zastupnica i zastupnika u protekla dva dana, izuzetno mi je ao to su izreene i neistine, koje u krajnjoj liniji, pogaaju i sve djelatnike HNB-a. Rei u samo kratko: HNB nikome ne plaa saune i masae, ne sluimo kampe i jastoge, niti isplaujemo boinice i regrese. Isto tako, ne zapoljavamo nikakve Masterchefove i sommeliere ve smo usluge restorana i nekih drugih usluga eksternalizirali, ime HNB ostvaruje utede izmeu 20 i 40 posto u odnosu na to da sam zapoljava te djelatnike. Po trokovima smo pri dnu ljestvice europskih sredinjih banaka, a po uinkovitosti pri vrhu - kao to sam vas danas izvijestio. Gospodine Predsjednie, uvaene zastupnice i zastupnici, zahvaljujem na vaoj pozornosti. [1] N. Nergiz Dincer & Barry Eichengreen, 2O14."Central Bank Transparency and Independence: Updates and New Measures," International Journal of Central Banking, International Journal of Central Banking, vol. 10(1), stranice 189.-259., oujak. [2] Roman Horvath & Dan Vako, 2013. "Central Bank Transparency and Financial Stability: Measurement, Determinants and Effects," FIW Working Paper series 113, FIW.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: The CNB continues with an expansive monetary policy
text: CNB continues expansionary monetary policy Published: 9.11.2016. Type Speaker Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor Date of publication of the declaration 9.11.2016. Topic Event Venue Event Date of events Economic outlook and monetary policy 24th Consultation of the Croatian Society of Economists "Economic Policy of Croatia in 2017" Abbey 9.11.2016.-11.11.2016. Croatia's economy is recovering, but this recovery is still lagging behind comparable countries in Central and Eastern Europe, said The Governor of the Croatian National Bank Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic in the opening part of the presentation held on November 9, 2016 at the 24th International Film Festival. consultation of the Croatian Society of Economists in Opatija. Among these countries, only Croatia has not yet reached the pre-crisis level of GDP. However, it is positive that the recovery of economic activity in Croatia was mostly contributed by the noticeable growth in exports of goods and services withthe recovery of personal consumption and investments, which is visible and related to both favorable trends in consumer and business optimism. The increase in exports had a positive impact on the realization of the current and capital account surplus of the balance of payments, which, even with theforeign deleveraging paragraph, supported the stability of the exchange rate of the domestic currency. Croatia has seen a drop in the general price level, which was mostly contributed by import prices, which is why it can be argued that the risks of deflation are not present, the governor stressed. Thus, the proportionalityof the price decline is gradually decreasing, that is, the share of products, whose prices are rising, the burden of debt repayment for the population is increasing and the increase in nominal wages is accelerating. Likewise, there is a noticeable recovery in corporate profits, which in 2015 almost reached the level of pre-crisis 2008. The CNB's multiannual expansionary policy orientation continues. After a strong the CNB's countercyclical responses in the crisis, and in the recent phase of recovery, the CNB continued its highly expansionary monetarn policy and a reduction in regulatory cost for banks. In doing so, the scale of monetary policy expansion is not really different from that of the euro area, but there are different channels of action and instruments. In 2016, the CNB's expansionary monetary policy was further strengthened by structural repo operations, Governor Vujcic said. So far, three auctions have been held in which almost HRK 1bn has been placed in total. The aim of these operations was to provide banks with longer-term sources of kuna liquidity (the maturity of the operations is four years) with a low interest rate of 1.8% at the first auction and then reduced to 1.4% (interest rates on regular repo operations, decreased from 0.8 to 0.5% and to 0.3%). Structural repo operations contribute to the loweringof the kuna yield curve on medium/longer maturity, the development of the domestic market for kuna government securities and motivate banks to increase lending in KUNA. In addition to structural operations, the CNB also supports the kuna's figure of vision of the system through regular weekly operations. It is noticeable that most small banks, which participated in structural repo operations, have halted the decline in lending and increased kuna loans in contrast to the previous year. Financing conditions on the domestic market for all fromthe ectors are continuously improving. Banks' interest rates for households and businesses have been steadily declining and are at historical minimums. Yields on Treasury bills from the Treasury Department have also reached all-time lows, with yield curves for governmente bonds dropping for all futures. Favourable developments are also recorded for credit undermining standards, which are being mitigated, and there is a noticeable jump in credit demand. In such conditions, in 2016 there was an increase in domestic placements to enterprises. In doing so, more and more activities are achieving growth in placements, thus seeing an increase in lending to agriculture, the processing industry, trade, the real estate sector and tourism activities. The new moment is also a noticeable jump in kuna lending, especially in the case ofapartments, as well as businesses. It contributes in particular to the recovery of domestic credit activity and is also linked to the gradual deposit deeurisation. Banks have intensified the cleaning of balance sheets over the past two years through write-offs and sales of placements, especially inplacements to companies, which have been partly encouraged by the CNB's prudential measures to increase provisions for poor placements. Namely, in 2013, the standards for covering bad placements with reservations were tightened. If the bank does not actively address the NPLs problem, it is forced to gradually increase provisions for these placements, regardless of their collateral coverage. The process of solving and cleaning up the accumulated NPLs on banks' balance sheets is certainly a favourable trend that could mitigate the scale of the problem of over-indebtednessand thus create the basics of a new credit cycle on a sound basis for all domestic sectors. In conclusion, it should be noted once again that the CNB will continue its expansionary monetary policy, the governor said. Thus, the high liquidity of the banking system willcontinue to be supported by structural repo operations, regular repo operations and, where appropriate, foreign exchange transactions. Such a policy favors the improvement of domestic financing conditions and supports the recovery of domestic credit activity. This is what the CNB can do in the circumstances and what it can influence, taking into account the stability of the exchange rate of the domestic currency and the overall financial stability of the system. In the end, said Governor Vujcic, it should not be forgotten that the current situation also opens up some mediumterm risks for financial stability both in Europe and in the domestic market, and that it is uncertain by which time the situation on the international market will allow for this degree of accommodativeness, that is, the expansion of monetary policy. For this reason, it would be derogatoryto rely on this degree of monetary policy expansion as the basis for medium-term growth. The basis of a stronger recovery of the economy must be an increase in the competitiveness of the domestic economy based on structural reforms and export growth, while containing macroeconomic imbalances or continuing to consolidate public finances.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA HNB nastavlja s ekspanzivnom monetarnom politikom Objavljeno: 9.11.2016. Vrsta Govornik Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a Datum objave izjave 9.11.2016. Tema Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Gospodarski izgledi i monetarna politika 24. savjetovanje Hrvatskog drutva ekonomista "Ekonomska politika Hrvatske u 2017.' Opatija 9.11.2016.-11.11.2016. Gospodarstvo Hrvatske se oporavlja, no taj oporavak jo uvijek zaostaje za usporedivim zemljama Srednje i Istone Europe, istaknuo je guverner Hrvatske narodne banke prof. dr. Boris Vuji u uvodnom dijelu izlaganja odranog 9. studenog 2016. godine na 24. savjetovanju Hrvatskog drutva ekonomista u Opatiji. Meu tim zemljama jedino jo Hrvatska nije dosegnula pretkriznu razinu BDP-a. Meutim, pozitivno je to je oporavku ekonomske aktivnosti u Hrvatskoj najvie pridonio zamjetan rast izvoza roba i usluga zajedno s oporavkom osobne potronje i investicija koji je vidljiv i povezan i s povoljnim kretanjima potroakog i poslovnog optimizma. Poveanje izvoza se pozitivno odrazilo na ostvarenje vika na tekuem i kapitalnom raunu platne bilance, to je i uz nastavak inozemnog razduivanja poduprlo stabilnost teaja domae valute. U Hrvatskoj se biljei pad ope razine cijena emu su najvie pridonijele uvozne cijene, zbog ega se moe ustvrditi da rizici deflacije nisu prisutni, naglasio je guverner. Tako se rasprostranjenost pada cijena postupno smanjuje, odnosno poveava se udio proizvoda, ije cijene rastu, teret otplate duga za stanovnitvo sve je manji te se porast nominalnih plae ubrzava. Isto tako, primjetan je oporavak korporativnih profita, koji su u 2015. gotovo dosegnuli razinu iz pretkrizne 2008. godine. Viegodinje ekspanzivno usmjerenje monetarne politike HNB-a se nastavlja. Nakon snane protuciklike reakcije HNB-a u krizi, i u recentnoj fazi oporavka HNB je nastavio s izrazito ekspanzivnom monetarnom politikom i smanjenjem regulatornog troka za banke. Pritom se razmjer ekspanzivnosti monetarne politike zapravo ne razlikuje od onoga u euro podruju, no razliiti su kanali djelovanja i instrumenti. U 2016. godini ekspanzivna monetarna politika HNB-a dodatno je osnaena strukturnim repo operacijama, istaknuo je guverner Vuji. Do sada su odrane tri aukcije na kojima je ukupno plasirana gotovo 1 mlrd. kuna. Cilj ovih operacija je bio osigurati bankama dugoronije izvore kunske likvidnosti (ronost operacija je etiri godine) uz nisku kamatnu stopu koja je na prvoj aukciji iznosila 1,8%, a potom je sniena na 1,4% (kamatne stope na redovitim repo operacijama, smanjivane su sa 0.8, na 0.5, pa na 0.3%). Strukturne repo operacije pridonose sputanju kunske krivulje prinosa na srednjoj/duoj ronosti, razvoju domaeg trita za kunske dravne vrijednosne papire te motiviraju banke da poveaju kreditiranje u kunama. Uz strukturne operacije, HNB redovitim tjednim operacijama takoer daje podrku kunskoj likvidnosti sustava. Primjetno je da je kod veinom malih banaka, koje su sudjelovale u strukturnim repo operacijama, zaustavljen pad kreditiranja te da su poveale kunske kredite za razliku od prethodne godine. Uvjeti financiranja na domaem tritu za sve sektore kontinuirano se poboljavaju. Kamatne stope banaka za stanovnitvo i poduzea u kontinuiranom su padu i na povijesnim su minimumima. Prinosi na trezorske zapise Ministarstva financija takoer su dosegnuli najnie razine, a krivulje prinosa za dravne obveznice se sputaju za sve ronosti. Povoljna kretanja biljee se i za standarde odobravanja kredita koji se ublaavaju, a primjetan je i skok kreditne potranje. U takvim uvjetima, u 2016. godini biljei se rast domaih plasmana poduzeima. Pritom sve vie djelatnosti ostvaruje rast plasmana te se tako biljei prirast kreditiranja poljoprivrede, preraivake industrije, trgovine, sektora nekretnina te turistikih djelatnosti. Novi moment je i zamjetan skok kunskog kreditiranja, posebno u sluaju stanovnitva, ali i poduzea. Ono posebno pridonosi oporavku domae kreditne aktivnosti, a povezano je i s postupnom depozitnom deeuroizacijom. Banke su u posljednje dvije godine intenzivirale ienje bilanci kroz otpise i prodaje plasmana, posebice kod plasmana poduzeima, to su dijelom potaknule i bonitetne mjere HNB-a za poveanje rezervacija za loe plasmane. Naime, 2013. godine postroeni su standardi pokria loih plasmana rezervacijama. Ako banka aktivno ne rjeava problem NPL-ova, primorana je postupno poveavati rezervacije za te plasmane, neovisno o njihovoj pokrivenosti kolateralima. Proces rjeavanja i ienja nagomilanih neprihodujuih plasmana u bilancama banaka svakako je povoljan trend koji bi mogao ublaiti razmjere problema prezaduenosti i tako stvoriti osnove novog kreditnog ciklusa na zdravim osnovama za sve domae sektore. Zakljuno, valja jo jednom istaknuti kako e HNB nastaviti s ekspanzivnom monetarnom politikom, rekao je guverner. Tako e se visoka likvidnost bankovnog sustava i dalje podravati strukturnim repo operacijama, redovitim repo operacijama te prema potrebi i deviznim transakcijama. Takva politika pogoduje poboljanju domaih uvjeta financiranja i podrka je oporavku domae kreditne aktivnosti. To je ono to u danim okolnostima HNB moe napraviti i na to moe utjecati, vodei pritom rauna o stabilnosti teaja domae valute i ukupnoj financijskoj stabilnosti sustava. Na kraju, poruio je guverner Vuji, ne treba zaboraviti da trenutna situacija otvara i neke srednjorone rizike za financijsku stabilnost kako u Europi, tako i na domaem tritu, te da je neizvjesno do kada e situacija na meunarodnom tritu omoguavati ovakav stupanj akomodativnosti, odnosno ekspanzivnosti monetarne politike. Zbog toga bi bilo pogreno oslanjati se na ovakav stupanj ekspanzivnosti monetarne politike kao temelj srednjoronog rasta. Temelj snanijeg oporavka gospodarstva mora biti poveanje konkurentnosti domae ekonomije temeljeno na strukturnim reformama i rastu izvoza, uz istodobno obuzdavanje makroekonomskih neravnotea odnosno nastavak konsolidiranja javnih financija.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: The CNB conducts an extremely expansionary and countercyclical monetary policy
text: HNB pursues extremely expansive and counter-cyclical monetary policy Published: 9.3.2016. Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, Governor 9.3.2016. Half-yearly information for 2015 Session of the Croatian Parliament Zagreb Dear Mr. President, Distinguished Representatives and Representatives, dear ladies and gentlemen, following last week's debate in parliament, I believe it is necessary and useful to briefly explain the circumstances and foundations of monetary policy led by the Croatian National Bank, with the aim of maintaining financial stability and creating support for the long-term development and growth of the Croatian economy. When it comes to the possibility of monetarne policy in Croatia, its powers and achievements are discussed very lightly, and even more easily it is proposed what it should do further, with supposedly very certain positive outcomes for economic activity, employment, exports andis mild. This often ignores the conditions in which central banks implement policies and make decisions, such as the structural characteristics of economies and their financial systems, ongoing economic trends, but also the state of the global economy and the immediatecirculation. Also, risks necessarily related to certain measures and actions are very rarely taken into account in an appropriate manner. In this complex environment, it is a great challenge for central bankers to easily and understandably put forward their own activities and in general the role ofmo netar policy, which is a necessary precondition for gaining and preserving reputation. Reputation is the most important capital of the central bank, on it it critically depends on the reaction of citizens, domestic and international market participants to the actions of monetary authorities, and therefore the abilityto meet legal goals and tasks. We at the CNB continuously and persistently explain the character, actions and objective achievements of monetary policy while taking into account the current risks. Clear communication has certainly gained importance in the period of crisis as it does now in the initial phase of the recovery of the Croatian economy, burdened by numerous structural problems and a high level of indebtedness of all domestic sectors. That is why I would like to take this opportunity to invite you once again to the CNB talks on the current topicand to deepen the dialogue on long-term challenges. My colleagues in management and I will be happy to welcome you and discuss with you all current issues within the scope of the central bank's work. Now let me clarify the limitations in the conduct of monetary policy in Croatia, as well as the current orientation of monetary policy, that is, its distinct, now perennial expansion, which we have further strengthened in recent 2016. Small open developing countries, until about thirty years ago,did not have at all "a systematic theoretical framework of monetary economy or macroeconomics, except for a few sporadic papers that dealt mainly with the effects of devaluation" (Frankel, 2011). Since then, a whole "new macroeconomics of open economies" has been developed , which seeks to apply the findings of the international economy, while taking into account the characteristics of small and open economies with euroised debts (Cespedes, Chang, & Velasco, 2000).[ 1] In such conditions, monetary policy, when fulfilling its mandate , faces many challenges that are not present in large and almost closed economies, for which the classic macroeconomic models are made, and which are systematically cited as an example for Croatian monetary policy by those who do not understand the differences between the almost closed economies, which print international currencies, such as the USA, the euro area or Japan and small, open, highly euroised economies such as Croatia. Let's start in order. Croatia is a small open economy. The very definition of a small opene-conomy contains several elements, some of which are: the share of foreign trade in GDP, then that the country is the taker of world prices and does not affect global trade and capital flows, and that it cannot, as a rule, borrow in its own currency on the international market. Foreign currency borrowing in such holdings is not due to a lack of awareness of currency risk, but because of "market imperfections" where there are simply no foreign lenders willing to grant loans in a homecurrency (Eichengreen & Hausmann, 1999). The impossibility of foreign borrowing in the domestic currency in small open economies is often compounded by domestic euroisation. Borrowing of all sectors in foreign currency results in potentially large negativee-cets of a significant change in the exchange rate on the financial stability of the country and the achievement of the fundamental goal of maintaining price stability. This reduces the possibility of monetary policy acting through traditional transmission channels, as the domestic currency, whose price and quantity is managed by the central bank, has less relevance in domestic economic and financial developments than in an uneuroised country. Likewise, in a euroised economy, households link their expectations of changes in the prices of goods and services to exchange rate changes. In the end, high deposit euroisation is also due to high credit euroisation, as banks have to hedge against currency risk in accordance with the rules of the profession. They are also encouraged by the regulatory rules of Regulation 575/2013 of the European Parliament and the Councilon prudential requirements for credit institutions and investment firms directly applicable in the Republic of Croatia. Thus, credit euroisation in the conditions of deposit euroisation serves to protect the value of assets entrusted by savers to banks for safekeeping. This is very important to keep in mind, since the described properties of the financial system are not present in large monetary areas, such as the USA, Japan and the euro area, which leads to significant differences in the transmission mechanisms of monetary policy. For example, Croatia's foreign debt, if the exchange rate devalued by 10%, excluding inflation, would rise from 107% to 118% of GDP. Due to domestic euroisation, foreign currency debt of all sectors - non-financial corporations, population and the state - is even slightly higher, around a3548bn. kuna or 164% of GDP. Foreign and domestic debt in foreign currency is due to almost four fifths of total debt, so already a very slight depreciation of the exchange rate strongly increases the indebtedness of the pro-recession. Small open economies are more exposedto supply-side stocks (such as the shock of oil or commodity prices, on the formation of which have absolutely no impact) as they are exposed to the volatility of foreign demand (in Croatia, for example, this may be the case in tourism). They are also subject to changes in the direction and volume of foreign capital flows, which are, as a rule, pro-cyclical, which we ourselves have experienced extremely strongly. During periods of economic upturn, capital inflows contribute to an overheating economy, can encourage excessive credit growth to increase asset prices. During the recession, these inflows decrease or there is a turnaround in flows, so we are witnessing capital outflows. capital reversal), where the sudden cessation of inflows is usually an additional trigger of the recession. Furthermore, the internal arrangement of developing economies is 'almost by definition' characterised by weak and underdeveloped institutions and policies (Frankel, 2011) and frequent and sudden shifts ineconomic policy jera, as well as inflexible domestic macroeconomic instruments. After all, fiscal policy is generally conducted pro-cyclically, increasing the deficit and public debt in the period of growth - simply put, without taking into account possible crisis raoutcomes, which results in the absence of "fiscal space" to conduct a countercyclical (expansionary) fiscal policy during periods of recession (Frankel, 2011). Due to institutional weaknesses, foreign creditors are generally willing to tolerate lower debt levelscompared to developed economies and are demanding higher rates of return, which makes borrowing more expensive for the state and other domestic sectors. All the above characteristics of small open economies that limit the possibilities of monetary policy action, unfortunately, are well known to us. In discussing the possibilities of small open economies to successfully cope with these domestic and foreign shocks, the choice of the exchange rate regime and the resulting implications for monetary policy play a prominent role. The "textbookki" approach, according to which a flexible exchange rate can somewhat mitigate the impact of the foreign shock on the real sector by changes in the nominal exchange rate (Cespedes et al., 2000) versus maintaining a stable exchange rate, has recently been largely relativized. Today's experience supports the notion that, regardless of the exchange rate regime, small and open developing countries cannot be isolated from external shocks, except possibly, and only temporarily and with a questionable result, by introducing capital controls (Rey, 2013). Based on all the above facts describing the economies of many emerging market countries, experience has shown that devaluation actually leads to a decrease in economic activity (Calvo, 1999). Namely, the concept of expansionary devaluation is based on the "Caynesian approach to the trade balance" (Frankel, 2011), which is a paradigm in which higher demand for domestic goods, by increasing domestic or foreign demand, leads to an increase in production. However, assumptions that this would be worth it are not present in highly euroised, small and open countries, so we often have "contraction devaluations" in them. That is why we have stressed numerous times that the framework and manner of monetary policy implementation in Croatia cannot be the same as in large countries or currency areas. Everything that the CNB has done in the last almost two decades, and has done a lot of things, has failed to change the preference of domestic sectors to save in foreign currency. Remember, the regulatory burden in the form of additional liquidity and capital shock absorbers has always been higher for foreign exchange than for kuna sources. Even today, when the CNB has released significant liquidity and reduced the regulatory burden on banks, the costof foreign exchange for banks is twice as high as for the KUNA business. But the process of deeurization has always been slow, and if one looks at a longer period, there was almost no deeurization. There are two main limitations for faster deeurization. The main conta'sinstigation of distrust in the domestic currency is the long-standing scare of the population by the need to devalue the value of the kuna, that is, by forecasting the inevitability of the decline in its value. It is supported by insufficiently credible and frequent changes in direction subject toeconomic policy. De-euroisation of deposits (i.e. dedolarisation) is extremely rare. The Reinhart et al. survey (2014) on a sample of 85 countries 1980 to 2001 found only a few examples in which dollarization was substantially and permanently reduced (by more than 20% and to a level of no more than 20% of the foreign currency's share of total deposits in the observed period). Common to all countries that successfully de-dollarised was that they did not belong to a circle of highly dollarised countries, with deep rooteddollarisation, and that they de-dollarised in conditions of restrictive capital flows. However, theoretically, de-dollarization is not an impossible process for highly euroized economies either, although in practice none have yet been deeurized. However, for this to happen, a continuous slight appreciation of the domestic currency is needed combined with effective structural policies with the aim of reducing public debt and improving the competitiveness of the economy. Namely, trust in the domestic currency is also, among other things, about the difference of confidence in the domestic economy, that is, economic policy. Only the policy described can revitalise trust in economic policy makers and therefore in the national currency. However, because of the deep policy of euroisation and in our case it ismore evident that Croatia will introduce the euro than that it will be able to convince citizens to, say, transfer three-quarters of their savings to kunas and keep it in kunas. All the described restrictive factors for monetary policy in Croatia do not mean that it is completely powerless to affect the domestic money market and domestic interest rates. To the extent that the necessity of maintaining exchange rate stability permits, the CNB manages domestic kuna liquidity with its instruments and affects domestic interest rates. The CNB's actions during the crisis were extremely expansionary, the same as all other central banks in Europe, i.e. the ECB, but unlike most of them, the CNB acted very restrictively before the crisis, which preserved the stability of the financial system and allowed for highly countercyclical expansionnzivo action when the crisis began. For the eighth year in a row, the CNB maintains an extremely high liquidity of the monetary system. In total, in the crisis, the CNB released about 14% of the GDP of liquidity by relaxing existing measures, which was especially related to the release of foreign currency and mobi liza early in the banks' balance sheets in the pre-crisis period. The released foreign exchange liquidity was crucial to ensure exchange rate stability in the face of a sharp decline in capital inflows from abroad. The policy of liquidity release during the crisisresults in strong growth of the CNB's balance sheet, comparable to the increase in the ECB's balance sheet, i.e. even slightly stronger, as well as high surpluses of kuna and foreign exchange liquidity, so banks in Croatia in 2015 had an average of 5.9% of the GDP of excess kuna and foreign exchange liquidity, which approximately exceeds the surplus liquidity in the euro area in relation to their GDP in 2015. High liquidity is conducive to keeping interest rates low in the money market and record low yields on Treasury bills Ministry of Finance. However, the way this expansiveness was implemented was different, which is logical given that the channels and instruments of action are different. It should be stressed once again that some channels of monetary policy action cannot even be used because we see that the ECB's quantitative easing policy largely works through a weakening of the exchange rate, which in our case would not bring positive effects, but would act pro-recessionaryly. In 2016, in conditions of further repairing the balance on the current balance of payments and foreign positions of banks, we decided to further strengthen the expansionary monetary policy orientation by introducing structural reverse repo operations. The first auction was successfully held in mid-February, and we are ready to holdthree more such auctions for you later this year. The main idea of these operations is to provide banks with kuna liquidity for a period of four years under conditions more favourable than market conditions, thus providing more favourable and intensive long-term lending to the economy and the populationin the domestic currency. However, since a big problem in Croatia is the novelty of public debt, which we often point out, it should be noted that these operations will depend on the fiscal consolidation process, among other things. The tighter the fiscal consolidation,the more room we will have for such and similar monetary policy measures, especially bearing in mind that the recovery of the economy has not yet been significantly dynamited and that banks' lending activity has been suppressed. I would also like to devote a few words to achieving price stability, which is the fundamental goal of the CNB. The low inflation rate is not a phenomenon that exists only in Croatia. The trend of decreasing the annual inflation rate has been around since the end of 2012 in all European countries as well as in the USA. The average annual rate of change in consumer pricesas measured by the total ha rmo lower in the early index decreased between 2013 and 2015 in all countries under review, by 1.3 percentage points to 0% in the euro area, by 2.5 percentage points in Bulgaria and Romania to -0.7%, while in Croatia the inflation rate in 2015 was -0.3% (a decrease of 2.6 percentage points). For a better understanding of the impact of certain phenomena on the movement of inflation, it is useful to exclude from the calculations prices that are very volatile, as well as administratively regulated prices. For example, the rate of the topicof oil inflation, which is calculated excluding the prices of energy, nutrition, alcohol and tobacco, was positive in all the countries observed between 2013 and 2015. The negative rate of headline and positive core inflation in most countries over a longer period of time is one of the reasons why currently negative inflation rates cannot be considered deflation. Lower prices of oil and other raw materials on world markets (let's not forget that Croatia imports them), that is, the fall in the prices of imported products, is actually a so-called positive shock of supply that improves the conditions of international exchange, because more than one unit of imports can be obtained for the croatian export unit. However, that the negative inflation rate is not spread across the largest number of products is evidenced by the inflation distribution index. Theaforementioned index shows the share of the number of products whose prices have risen in a given month in the total number of products in the basket for calculating ha rmo lower early index of consumer prices. It is very important that such an index actually signals whether growth or a fall in the CIyen is widespread across most sectors of the economy and helps to assess whether the intensity of inflationary pressures has strengthened or weakened over a period of time. Thus, in 2015, the share of products in the index of consumer prices without energy and nutrition, andthe price grew on a monthly basis, reached almost 60%. This means that the prices of most products are rising, in large part of those products that are produced in Croatia, while the very products that we import are cheaper. The entire negative contribution andnflation comes from prices unprocessed food products and energy products. To summarize, falling food and energy prices are a positive shock to the economy as a whole. Due to the strong price decreases in these two segments of goods, personal consumption was not delayed, which would be characteristic of the deflationary spiral, but the repair of the trade balance due to the fall in the prices of imported goods allowed personal consumption to rise. Since the inflation distribution index shows that negative inflation rates in Croatian j arecaused by a concentrated drop in prices in a small group of imported goods, Croatians earn more due to "deflation" and pay less, which should not bother them. Another important feature of the deflationary spiral is derived from the so-called debt deflation theory. Thisorient finds its foundations in the 1933 work of the American economist Irving Fisher, and rests on the idea that during periods of the greatest crises there is a prolonged contraction of the economy caused by the simultaneous deleveraging of most sectors in the economy and the decline of the priceon, with the rate of price declines higher than the rate at which domestic sectors are deleveraging, and the real indebtedness of domestic sectors is increasing. However, in Croatia, recent financial developments do not show growth, but a decrease in the real debt burden. The share of interest expensein consumers' disposable income has been steadily decreasing, as is the loan-to-income ratio, and similar developments are shown by the financial indicators of companies whose profitability is improving due to cheaper food and energy. Therefore, we cannot talk about increasingthe real debt burden, which would be inherent in a deflationary spiral, but on the contrary, household indebtedness and the share of interest paid in disposable income have decreased noticeably in recent years, and the growth of real incomes facilitates the otplatu of debt. Long-term inflation expectations also suggest that inflation should return to the long-term trend. A survey of professional forecasters on the expected annual rate shows that deflation is not deeply rooted in the economy, but rather a temporary phenomenon, which is in line with the decline in volatile food and energy prices as the main causes of negative inflation. Now that oil has gone up 33% in a month, anyone worried about deflation may be relieved. Andon the other hand, I doubt that's why he'll be paying for more expensive fuel with great joy. Therefore, at the moment there can be no talk of the presence of a deflationary spiral, but solely about the negative inflation rate caused by the spillover of lower oil and food pricesin the fresh market to domestic prices in conditions of relatively low underlying inflation in the euro area. Before concluding, let me emphasize the other key task of the Croatian National Bank and refer to the fact that it is not fulfilled by itself, but isthe result of many years of systematic work - this is a contribution to the preservation of financial stability, which is one of the key preconditions for sustainable economic growth. Distorted financial stability and related banking crises can have extremely high troschores, which we have seen best in some EU member states in recent years. There was no such cost in Croatia, among other things, the result of a number of macroprudential measures, instruments and activities carried out by the CNB with the aim of strengthening the resilience of the financial system. All together, it has helped to preserve trust in the banking system, without which the economy cannot function on its own, nor can savers manage their financial assets with certainty. To conclude: the CNB's monetary policyis three times extremely expansionary and is certainly neither a brake nor an obstacle to reviving the economy and accelerating its recovery. Despite the noticeable fall in GDP, Croatia achieved relatively favourable dynamics of corporate lending, especially in relation to some comparable countries where deleveraging was very pronounced. Monetary policy remains oriented towards lowering financing costs for all sectors of the economy, which are currently at historically low levels. This also facilitated the financing of new projects and the refinancing of existing debts. Structural repo operations give an extra flywheel to lending in the domestic currency. However, it should also be noted that the CNB, with the new measures, does not give up its credible management of the stable exchange rate of the domestic currency, which remains the main nominal anchor for achieving our legal mandate to maintain low and stable inflation, and also financial stability. In this way, the central bank will continue to be the guarantor of maintaining macroeconomic stability in terms of preserving the value of money and real incomes of all sectors, which can only facilitate the implementation of much-needed reforms in many segments of the Croatian economy, which go beyond the reach of monetary policy and the legalh tasks of monetary authority. Therefore, if all economic policy actors make quality decisions that will go towards fixing the structural weaknesses of the Croatian economy, monetary policy efforts to facilitate the recovery will be more successful.
