The first limbof the macroeconomics that focuses on developing countries is the 1995 "Development Macroeconomics" by Pierre-Richard Agenor and Peter J. Montiel, which had its 4th editions until 2015. Among the recent textbooks it is worth singling out "Open Economy Macroeconomics in Developing Countries" by Carlos A. Vegha.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA HNB vodi izrazito ekspanzivnu i protuciklinu monetarnu politiku Objavljeno: 9.3.2016. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Tema Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner 9.3.2016. Polugodinja informacija za 2015. Sjednica Hrvatskog sabora Zagreb Potovani gospodine Predsjednie, uvaene zastupnice i zastupnici, potovane dame i gospodo, slijedom prolotjedne rasprave u Saboru, vjerujem daje potrebno i korisno ukratko objasniti okolnosti i temelje monetarne politike koju vodi Hrvatska narodna banka, u cilju odranja financijske stabilnosti i stvaranja podrke za dugoroni razvoj i rast hrvatskoga gospodarstva. Kada se govori o mogunosti djelovanja monetarne politike u Hrvatskoj, vrlo se olako raspravlja o njezinim moima i dosezima, a jo se s veom lakoom predlae to bi ona dodatno trebala poduzimati, s navodno vrlo izvjesnim pozitivnim ishodima za gospodarsku aktivnost, zaposlenost, izvoz i blagostanje. Pritom se esto zanemaruju uvjeti u kojima sredinje banke provode politike i donose odluke, kao to su strukturna svojstva gospodarstava i njihovih financijskih sustava, tekui gospodarski trendovi, ali i stanje globalnoga gospodarstva i neposrednog okruja. Takoer, rizici koji su nuno vezani uz odreene mjere i poteze vrlo se rijetko uvaavaju na primjeren nain. U tom kompleksnom okruju velik je izazov za sredinje bankare jednostavno i razumljivo iznoenje vlastitog djelovanja i openito uloge monetarne politike, to je nuan preduvjet za stjecanje i ouvanje reputacije. Reputacija je najvaniji kapital sredinje banke, o njoj kritino ovisi reakcija graana, domaih i meunarodnih trinih sudionika na poteze monetarnih vlasti, a time i sposobnost ispunjavanja zakonskih ciljeva i zadaa. Mi u HNB-u kontinuirano i ustrajno objanjavamo karakter, djelovanje i objektivne dosege monetarne politike uz uvaavanje aktualnih rizika. Jasna komunikacija zasigurno je dobila na vanosti u razdoblju krize kao i sada u poetnoj fazi oporavka hrvatskoga gospodarstva, optereenoga brojnim strukturnim problemima te visokom razinom zaduenosti svih domaih sektora. Upravo zato, iskoristio bih ovu priliku da vas jo jedanput pozovem na razgovore u HNB o aktualnim temama i produbljivanje dijaloga o dugoronim izazovima. Kolege iz rukovodstva i ja sa zadovoljstvom emo vas primiti i s vama raspraviti o svim aktualnim pitanjima iz djelokruga rada sredinje banke. Dopustite da sada pojasnim ogranienja u voenju monetarne politike u Hrvatskoj, kao i aktualnu orijentaciju monetarne politike, odnosno njezinu izrazitu, sada ve viegodinju ekspanzivnost, koju smo u recentnoj 2016. godini dodatno osnaili. Male otvorene zemlje u razvoju, jo do prije tridesetak godina, zapravo uope nisu imale "sustavan teorijski okvir monetarne ekonomije ili makroekonomije, osim nekoliko sporadinih radova koji su se bavili uglavnom uincima devalvacije" (Frankel, 2011.). Od tada, razvijena je cijela "nova makroekonomija otvorenih ekonomija" koja nastoji primijeniti saznanja meunarodne ekonomije, uvaavajui pritom karakteristike malih i otvorenih gospodarstava s euroiziranim dugovima (Cespedes, Chang, & Velasco, 2000.).[1] U takvim se uvjetima monetarna politika pri ispunjavanju svog mandata suoava s mnogim izazovima koji nisu prisutni u velikim i gotovo zatvorenim gospodarstvima, za koje su klasini makroekonomski modeli i napravljeni, a koje sustavno kao primjer za hrvatsku monetarnu politiku navode oni koji ne razumiju razlike izmeu velikih, gotovo zatvorenih ekonomija, koje tiskaju meunarodne valute, poput SAD-a, europodruja ili Japana i malih, otvorenih, visokoeuroiziranih gospodarstava poput Hrvatske. Krenimo redom. Hrvatska je mala otvorena ekonomija. Sama definicija male otvorene ekonomije sadrava vie elemenata, a neki su od njih: udio vanjskotrgovinske razmjene u BDP-u, zatim da je zemlja preuzimatelj svjetskih cijena te da ne utjee na globalne trgovinske i kapitalne tokove, kao i to da se na meunarodnom tritu, u pravilu, ne moe zaduiti u vlastitoj valuti. Zaduivanje u stranoj valuti u takvim gospodarstvima ne nastaje zbog manjka svijesti o valutnom riziku, nego zbog nesavrenosti trita" na kojima jednostavno ne postoje inozemni kreditori spremni odobravati kredite u domaoj valuti (Eichengreen & Hausmann, 1999.). Na nemogunost inozemnog zaduivanja u domaoj valuti u malim otvorenim ekonomijama esto se nadovezuje i domaa euroizacija. Zaduivanje svih sektora u stranoj valuti rezultira potencijalno velikim negativnim efektima znatnije promjene teaja na financijsku stabilnost zemlje i ostvarivanje temeljnog cilja odravanja stabilnosti cijena. To smanjuje mogunost djelovanja monetarne politike putem tradicionalnih transmisijskih kanala jer domaa valuta, ijom cijenom i koliinom upravlja sredinja banka, ima manju vanost u domaim gospodarskim i financijskim kretanjima nego u neeuroiziranoj zemlji. Isto tako, u euroiziranom gospodarstvu kuanstva svoja oekivanja o promjenama cijena dobara i usluga vezuju uz promjene teaja. Na kraju, posljedica visoke depozitne euroizacije jest i visoka kreditna euroizacija jer se banke u skladu s pravilima struke moraju zatititi od valutnog rizika. Na to ih potiu i regulatorna pravila iz Uredbe 575/2013 Europskog parlamenta i Vijea o bonitetnim zahtjevima za kreditne institucije i investicijska drutva koja se izravno primjenjuju u Republici Hrvatskoj. Dakle, kreditna euroizacija u uvjetima depozitne euroizacije slui za zatitu vrijednosti imovine koju su tedie povjerile bankama na uvanje. To je vrlo vano imati na umu, jer opisana svojstva financijskog sustava nisu prisutna u velikim monetarnim podrujima, kakva su SAD, Japan i europodruje, to dovodi do bitnih razlika u transmisijskim mehanizmima monetarne politike. Tako bi, primjerice, inozemni dug Hrvatske, kad bi teaj devalvirao za 10%, bez inflacije, narastao sa 107% na 118% BDP-a. Zbog domae euroizacije dug u stranoj valuti svih sektora - nefinancijskih poduzea, stanovnitva i drave - jo je i malo vei, oko 548 mlrd. kuna ili 164% BDP-a. Na inozemni i domai dug u stranoj valuti odnose se gotovo etiri petine ukupnog duga, pa ve i vrlo blaga deprecijacija teaja snano poveava zaduenosti djeluje prorecesijski. Mala otvorena gospodarstva u veoj su mjeri izloena okovima na strani ponude (kao npr. ok cijena nafte ili sirovina, na formiranje kojih apsolutno nemaju utjecaja) kao to su izloena i kolebljivosti inozemne potranje (u Hrvatskoj to moe npr. biti sluaj u turizmu). Takoer su podlona promjenama smjera i obujma inozemnih kapitalnih tokova, koji su u pravilu prociklini, to smo i sami iznimno snano iskusili. Tijekom razdoblja ekonomskog uzleta kapitalni priljevi pridonose pregrijavanju ekonomije, mogu poticati prekomjerni kreditni rasti poveavati cijene imovine. Tijekom recesije ti se priljevi smanjuju ili dolazi do preokreta u tokovima, pa svjedoimo odljevu kapitala (engl. capital reversal), pri emu je nagli prestanak priljeva obino dodatni okida recesije. Nadalje, unutarnje ureenje gospodarstava u razvoju "gotovo po definiciji" obiljeeno je slabim i nerazvijenim institucijama i politikama (Frankel, 2011.) te estim i naglim zaokretima smjera ekonomske politike, kao i nefleksibilnim domaim makroekonomskim instrumentima. Naposljetku, fiskalna politika u pravilu se vodi prociklino, poveavajui manjak i javni dug u razdoblju rasta - jednostavno reeno, ne vodei rauna o moguim kriznim razdobljima, to ima za posljedicu ostajanje bez "fiskalnog prostora" za voenje kontracikline (ekspanzivne) fiskalne politike u razdobljima recesije (Frankel, 2011.). Zbog institucionalnih slabosti, strani vjerovnici uglavnom su spremni tolerirati niu razinu duga u odnosu na razvijena gospodarstva i trae vie stope povrata, to poskupljuje zaduivanje drave, ali i drugih domaih sektora. Sva navedena obiljeja malih otvorenih ekonomija koja ograniavaju mogunosti djelovanja monetarne politike, naalost, dobro su nam poznata. U raspravi o mogunostima malih otvorenih gospodarstava da se uspjeno nose s navedenim domaim i inozemnim okovima, izbor teajnog reima i implikacije koje iz toga proizlaze za monetarnu politiku imaju prominentnu ulogu. "Udbeniki" pristup, prema kojemu fleksibilan teaj moe donekle ublaiti uinak inozemnog oka na realni sektor promjenama nominalnog teaja (Cespedes et al., 2000.) naspram odravanja stabilnog teaja, u novije je vrijeme uvelike relativiziran. Dananja iskustva govore u prilog tezi da se, neovisno o teajnom reimu, male i otvorene zemlje u razvoju ne mogu izolirati od vanjskih okova, osim eventualno, i to samo privremeno i s upitnim rezultatom, uvoenjem kapitalnih kontrola (Rey, 2013.). injenica da smo lanica EU-a, meutim, stavlja kapitalne kontrole izvan domaaja ekonomske politike u sluaju okova. Na temelju svih nabrojanih injenica koje opisuju gospodarstva brojnih zemalja s tritima u nastajanju, iskustva su pokazala da devalvacija zapravo dovodi do smanjenja gospodarske aktivnosti (Calvo, 1999.). Naime, koncept ekspanzivne devalvacije temelji se na "kejnezijanskom pristupu trgovinskoj bilanci" (Frankel, 2011.), to je paradigma u kojoj vea potranja za domaim dobrima, poveanjem domae ili inozemne potranje, dovodi po porasta proizvodnje. Meutim, pretpostavke da bi to vrijedilo nisu prisutne u visokoeuroiziranim, malim i otvorenim zemljama, pa u njima esto imamo kontrakcijske devalvacije". Upravo zbog toga nebrojeno smo puta naglaavali da okvir i nain provoenja monetarne politike u Hrvatskoj ne mogu biti isti kao u velikim zemljama ili valutnim podrujima. Sve to je HNB radio u posljednja gotovo dva desetljea, a inio je mnogo toga, nije uspjelo promijeniti sklonost domaih sektora tednji u stranoj valuti. Podsjetimo, regulatorno optereenje u obliku dodatnih amortizera likvidnosti i kapitala oduvijek je vee za devizne nego za kunske izvore. I danas, kad je HNB otpustio znatnu likvidnost i smanjio regulatorno optereenje banaka, troak poslovanja s devizama za banke dvostruko je vei nego za poslovanje s kunama. No, proces deeuroizacije uvijek je bio spor, i ako se promatra due razdoblje, gotovo da deeuroizacije nije ni bilo. Dva su glavna ogranienja za bru deeuroizaciju. Glavni je kontinuirano poticanje nepovjerenja u domau valutu dugogodinjim plaenjem stanovnitva potrebom devalvacije vrijednosti kune, odnosno prognoziranjem neizbjenosti pada njezine vrijednosti. On je podran nedovoljno kredibilnom i estim promjenama smjera podlonom ekonomskom politikom. Deeuroizacija depozita (odnosno dedolarizacija) iznimno je rijetka. Istraivanje Reinhart et al. (2014.) na uzorku od 85 zemalja u razdoblju od 1980. do 2001. pronalazi samo nekoliko primjera u kojima je dolarizacija bitno i trajno smanjena (za vie od 20% i na razinu od najvie 20% udjela strane valute u ukupnim depozitima u promatranom razdoblju). Zajedniko svim zemljama koje su se uspjeno dedolarizirale bilo je da one nisu pripadale krugu visokodolariziranih zemalja, s duboko ukorijenjenom dolarizacijom, te da su se dedolarizirale u uvjetima restriktivnih tokova kapitala. Meutim, teoretski, dedolarizacija nije nemogu proces ni za visokoeuroizirana gospodarstva, iako se u praksi jo niti jedno nije deeuroiziralo. No, da bi se ona dogodila, potrebna je kontinuirana blaga aprecijacija domae valute u kombinaciji s uinkovitim strukturnim politikama s ciljem smanjenja javnog duga i poboljanja konkurentnosti gospodarstva. Naime, povjerenje u domau valutu ujedno je, meu ostalim, odraz povjerenja u domau ekonomiju, odnosno ekonomsku politiku. Jedino se opisanom politikom moe revitalizirati povjerenje u nositelje ekonomske politike, a time i u nacionalnu valutu. No, zbog duboke uko rije nje nosti euroizacije i u naem je sluaju izglednije da e Hrvatska uvesti euro nego da e biti u stanju uvjeriti graane da, recimo, tri etvrtine tednje prebace u kune i da je zadre u kunama. Svi opisani ograniavajui initelji za monetarnu politiku u Hrvatskoj ne znae daje ona potpuno nemona utjecati na domae novano trite i domae kamatne stope. U mjeri u kojoj nunost odravanja stabilnosti teaja doputa, HNB svojim instrumentima upravlja domaom kunskom likvidnou te utjee na domae kamate. Djelovanje HNB-a u razdoblju krize bilo je izrazito ekspanzivno, jednako kao i svih drugih sredinjih banaka u Europi, odnosno ESB-a, no za razliku od veine njih, HNB je djelovao vrlo restriktivno prije krize, to je sauvalo stabilnost financijskog sustava i omoguilo izrazito protucikliko ekspanzivno djelovanje kad je kriza poela. Ve osmu godinu u nizu HNB odrava iznimno visoku likvidnost monetarnog sustava. Ukupno je HNB u krizi relaksiranjem postojeih mjera oslobodio oko 14% BDP-a likvidnosti, to se posebno odnosilo na otputanje deviza i mobi lizi ranih u bilancama banaka u pretkriznom razdoblju. Otputena devizna likvidnost bila je krucijalna za osiguravanje stabilnosti teaja u uvjetima snanog pada kapitalnih priljeva iz inozemstva. Politika otputanja likvidnosti tijekom krize rezultirala je snanim rastom bilance HNB-a, usporedivim s porastom bilance ESB-a, odnosno jo i neto snanijim, kao i visokim vikovima kunske i devizne likvidnosti, pa su banke u Hrvatskoj tijekom 2015. prosjeno raspolagale s 5,9% BDP-a vika kunske i devizne likvidnosti, to priblino za dva i pol puta premauje vikove likvidnosti u europodruju u odnosu na njihov BDP. Visoka likvidnost pogoduje odravanju niskih kamatnih stopa na novanom tritu te rekordno niskim prinosima na trezorske zapise Ministarstva financija. No, nain provedbe te ekspanzivnosti bio je drugaiji, to je i logino s obzirom na to da su kanali i instrumenti djelovanja razliiti. Tu valja jo jednom naglasiti kako se pojedinim kanalima djelovanja monetarne politike ni ne moe koristiti jer vidimo da politika kvantitativnog poputanja ESB-a u velikoj mjeri djeluje kroz slabljenje teaja, to u naem sluaju ne bi donijelo pozitivne uinke, ve bi djelovalo prorecesijski. U 2016. godini, u uvjetima dodatnog popravljanja salda na tekuem raunu platne bilance i inozemne pozicije banaka, odluili smo dodatno osnaiti ekspanzivno usmjerenje monetarne politike uvoenjem strukturnih obratnih repo operacija. Prva aukcija uspjeno je odrana sredinom veljae, a u nastavku godine spremni smo odrati jo tri takve aukcije. Glavna zamisao ovih operacija jest da se bankama pod uvjetima povoljnijima od trinih osigura kunska likvidnost na razdoblje od etiri godine te tako omogui povoljnije i intenzivnije dugorono kreditiranje gospodarstva i stanovnitva u domaoj valuti. No kako je velik problem u Hrvatskoj od ri vost javnog duga, to uestalo istiemo, valja naglasiti da e ove operacije meu ostalim ovisiti i o procesu fiskalne konsolidacije. to je vra fiskalna konsolidacija, to emo imati vie prostora za ovakve i sline mjere monetarne politike, posebice imajui na umu da se oporavak gospodarstva jo nije znatno dinamizirao, a da je kreditna aktivnost banaka potisnuta. Nekoliko bih rijei elio posvetiti i ostvarenju stabilnosti cijena, to je temeljni cilj HNB-a. Niska stopa inflacije nije fenomen koji postoji samo u Hrvatskoj. Trend smanjivanja godinje stope inflacije prisutan je jo od kraja 2012. u svim europskim zemljama kao i u SAD-u. Prosjena godinja stopa promjene potroakih cijena mjerena ukupnim ha rmo nii ranim indeksom smanjila se izmeu 2013. i 2015. u svim promatranim zemljama, i to u europodruju za 1,3 postotna boda na 0%, za 2,5 postotnih bodova u Bugarskoj i Rumunjskoj na -0,7% , dok je u Hrvatskoj stopa inflacije u 2015. iznosila -0,3% (smanjenje od 2,6 postotnih bodova). Za bolje razumijevanje utjecaja pojedinih fenomena na kretanje inflacije korisno je iz izrauna iskljuiti cijene koje su vrlo kolebljive, kao i administrativno regulirane cijene. Primjerice, stopa temeljne inflacije, koja se izraunava bez cijena energije, prehrane, alkohola i duhana, bila je pozitivna u svim promatranim zemljama izmeu 2013. i 2015. Negativna stopa ukupne i pozitivna stopa temeljne inflacije u veini zemalja u duem razdoblju jedan je od razloga zato se trenutno negativne stope inflacije ne mogu smatrati deflacijom. Nie cijene nafte i drugih sirovina na svjetskim tritima (ne zaboravimo da ih Hrvatska uvozi), odnosno pad cijena uvoznih proizvoda, zapravo je tzv. pozitivan ok ponude koji popravlja uvjete meunarodne razmjene, jer se za jedinicu hrvatskog izvoza moe dobiti vie od jedne jedinice uvoza. Meutim, da negativna stopa inflacije nije rasprostranjena na najvei broj proizvoda svjedoi i indeks rasprostranjenosti inflacije. Spomenuti indeks pokazuje udio broja proizvoda ije su cijene rasle u odreenom mjesecu u ukupnom broju proizvoda u koarici za izraun ha rmo nii ranog indeksa potroakih cijena. Vrlo je bitno da takav indeks zapravo signalizira je li rast odnosno pad cijena rasprostranjen na veinu sektora u gospodarstvu te pomae pri procjeni je li intenzitet inflacijskih pritisaka tijekom odreenog razdoblja ojaao ili oslabio. Tako je tijekom 2015. udio proizvoda u indeksu potroakih cijena bez energije i prehrane, ija je cijena rasla na mjesenoj razini, dostigao gotovo 60%. To znai da cijene veine proizvoda rastu, i to velikim dijelom ba onih proizvoda koji se proizvode u Hrvatskoj, dok pojeftinjuju ba oni proizvodi koje uvozimo. Cjelokupan negativan doprinos inflaciji dolazi od cijena nepreraenih prehrambenih proizvoda i energenata. Da sumiramo, pad cijena hrane i energije pozitivan je ok za gospodarstvo u cjelini. Zbog snanog smanjenja cijena u ta dva segmenta dobara nije dolo do odgaanja osobne potronje, to bi bilo karakteristino za deflacijsku spiralu, nego je popravljanje trgovinske bilance zbog pada cijena uvoznih dobara omoguilo rast osobne potronje. Budui da indeks rasprostranjenosti inflacije pokazuje da su negativne stope inflacije u Hrvatskoj uzrokovane koncentriranim padom cijena u maloj skupini uvoznih dobara, Hrvati zbog deflacije" zarauju vie, a plaaju manje, to im ne bi trebalo smetati. Drugo vano obiljeje deflacijske spirale izvodi se iz takozvane teorije deflacije dugova. Ova teorija svoje temelje nalazi u djelu amerikog ekonomista Irvinga Fishera iz 1933., a poiva na ideji da u razdobljima najveih kriza dolazi do dugotrajne kontrakcije gospodarstva uzrokovane istodobnim razduivanjem veine sektora u gospodarstvu i padom cijena, pri emu je brzina pada cijena vea od brzine kojom se domai sektori razduuju, pa se realna zaduenost domaih sektora poveava. No, u Hrvatskoj recentna financijska kretanja ne pokazuju rast, nego smanjenje realnog tereta duga. Udio rashoda na kamate u raspoloivom dohotku potroaa kontinuirano se smanjuje, isto kao i omjer kredita i dohotka, a slina kretanja pokazuju i financijski pokazatelji poduzea ija se profitabilnost popravlja zbog jeftinije hrane i energije. Stoga ne moemo govoriti o poveanju realnog tereta duga, to bi bilo svojstveno deflacijskoj spirali, nego upravo suprotno, zaduenost kuanstava i udio plaenih kamata u raspoloivom dohotku zamjetljivo su se smanjili u posljednjih nekoliko godina, a rast realnih dohodaka olakava otplatu duga. Dugorona inflacijska oekivanja takoer upuuju na to da bi se inflacija trebala vratiti na dugoroni trend. Anketa profesionalnih prognostiara o oekivanoj godinjoj stopi pokazuje da deflacija nije duboko ukorijenjena u gospodarstvu, ve da je rije o privremenoj pojavi, to je u skladu s padom kolebljivih cijena prehrane i energije kao glavnih uzronika negativne inflacije. Sada kada je nafta poskupjela za 33% u mjesec dana, svima zabrinutima za deflaciju moe laknuti. Ipak, sumnjam da e zato s velikim veseljem plaati skuplje gorivo. Prema tome, u ovom trenutku ne moe se govoriti o prisutnosti deflacijske spirale, ve iskljuivo o negativnoj stopi inflacije uzrokovane prelijevanjem niih cijena nafte i prehrane na svjetskom tritu na domae cijene u uvjetima relativno niske temeljne inflacije u europodruju. Prije samog zakljuka, dopustite mi da naglasim drugu kljunu zadau Hrvatske narodne banke te uputim na injenicu kako se ona ne ispunjava sama od sebe, nego je takoer plod dugogodinjega i sustavnog rada - to je doprinos ouvanju financijske stabilnosti, koja je jedan od kljunih preduvjeta odrivoga gospodarskog rasta. Naruena financijska stabilnost i s njom povezane bankovne krize mogu imati iznimno visoke trokove, to smo najbolje vidjeli u pojedinim zemljama lanicama EU-a tijekom posljednjih godina. Tog troka u Hrvatskoj nije bilo, stoje meu ostalim plod niza makrobonitetnih mjera, instrumenata i aktivnosti koje je HNB provodio s ciljem jaanja otpornosti financijskog sustava. Sve skupa pomoglo je ouvanju povjerenja u bankovni sustav, bez kojega gospodarstvo ne moe samostalno funkcionirati, niti tedie mogu sa sigurnou upravljati svojom financijskom imovinom. Da zakljuimo: monetarna politika HNB-a trenutano je izrazito ekspanzivna te zasigurno nije ni konica ni prepreka oivljavanju gospodarstva i ubrzavanju njegova oporavka. Pritom je u Hrvatskoj unato zamjetljivom padu BDP-a ostvarena relativno povoljna dinamika kreditiranja korporativnog sektora, posebice u odnosu na pojedine usporedive zemlje gdje je razduivanje bilo jako izraeno. Monetarna politika i nadalje je orijentirana na sniavanje trokova financiranja za sve sektore gospodarstva, koji su trenutano na povijesno najniim razinama. Tako se ujedno olakalo financiranje novih projekata i refinanciranje postojeih dugova. Strukturne repo operacije daju dodatni zamanjak kreditiranju u domaoj valuti. No, isto tako valja naglasiti da HNB uz nove mjere ne odustaje od vjerodostojnog voenja politike stabilnog teaja domae valute koji je i nadalje glavno nominalno sidro za ostvarivanje naega zakonskog mandata odravanja niske i stabilne inflacije, a usto i financijske stabilnosti. Na taj e nain sredinja banka i nadalje biti jamac odravanja makroekonomske stabilnosti u smislu ouvanja vrijednosti novca i realnih dohodaka svih sektora, to moe samo olakati provedbu prijeko potrebnih reformi u mnogim segmentima hrvatskoga gospodarstva, a koje izlaze izvan dosega monetarne politike i zakonskih zadaa monetarne vlasti. Stoga, ako svi akteri ekonomske politike budu donosili kvalitetne odluke koje e ii u smjeru popravljanja strukturnih slabosti hrvatskoga gospodarstva, i nastojanja monetarne politike da olaka oporavak bit e uspjenija. Title: Croatia - a look ahead
text: Croatia - Forward View After six consecutive years of contraction, the Croatian economy is in a recovery phase. Signs of such developments were evident as early as the second half of 2014. In 2015, in order to intensify growth in early 2015, and especially in the second quarter, primarily due to strong growth in exports of goods and services, but also a slightly more favourable development in domestic demand. We expect similar trends, albeit with a slightly lower intensity, to continue for the remainder of 2015, as in the coming years. In line with such an improved macroeconomic outlook, the CNB's growth projection in this year and next has been revised higher for the second time. The CNB now expects that this year the domestic economy could grow by 1.2%, and in the next year it could grow slightly faster (1.5%). This revision primarily reflects the noticeable growth in exports of goods, which was previously expected to slow to the usual levels seen in recent years, as well as the export of services due to this year's exceptionally good tourist results. Furthermore, the CNB also corrected the projections of domestic demand, which are also more optimistic than before. This primarily refers to the expected stronger growth of personal consumption influenced by the decrease in the tax burden on labour income and the fall in the prices of petroleum products and consequently the faster growth of real net disposable income. In addition, since the second half of the last year, there has been a change in trend, i.e. slightly more favourable developments in the labour market, and they have intensified further in 2015. There was thus employment growth as well as favourable flows in and out of unemployment, where outflows due to employment now dominate. It is also interesting how consumer confidence returned to pre-crisis levels in the middle of this year, suggesting a slightly higher propensity to spend from disposable income. Capital investments also show the first signs of a reversal of the trend, but it should be said that investments are cumulatively reduced by about one third compared to the last pre-crisis year and these levels will be almost impossible to reach in the medium term even with these slightly more favorable growth rates. Inflation rebounded after June this year, and in September 2015 it was 1.5% higher than in September 2015. amounted to -0.8%, for which the decrease in energy prices due to the cheapening of petroleum products was crucial. On the other hand, pressures to reduce consumer prices from other sources are weak, as indicated by a slight acceleration of the annual rate of change in producer prices in the domestic market (excluding energy) and underlying inflation compared to the end of 2014. Inflation could increase at the end of the year and take on a positive value in December 2015, primarily due to the gradual increase in the prices of petroleum products and the effect of the base period (the price of petroleum products cheaper in the same period of the previous year), as well as the increase in the annual rate of growth in food prices. In 2016, the average annual rate of consumer price inflation is expected to accelerate to 1.1% (from -0.3% estimated in 2015). Import inflationary pressures could increase slightly, primarily due to rising crude oil prices and an increase in inflation in the euro area. Although domestic inflationary pressures resulting from personal consumption growth are also expected to increase in 2016, they are also expected to remain mild. In 2015, the CNB continued to pursue a very expansionary monetary policy while maintaining the stability of the exchange rate of the kuna against the euro. This policy continued during the increased uncertainty in the markets resulting from the adoption of legislative amendments regulating the conversion and partial write-off of loans to households with a currency clause in the Swiss franc. Thus, in the second half of September, the kuna weakened against the euro, and the overnight interest rate on the money market reached almost 2.0%, so the CNB calmed the pressures on the foreign exchange and money markets through a series of related measures. The CNB intervened on the foreign exchange market, providing banks with almost EUR 270 million in additional foreign currency liquidity, while the abolition of mandatory treasury bills in early October released HRK 3.4 billion in kuna funds. Also, at the end of September, for the first time since 2009, the CNB reintroduced regular reverse repo operations, at a fixed rate of 0.8%, to further support the liquidity of the banking system. In order to increase the effectiveness of this instrument, the list of eligible collateral for government bonds issued on the domestic market and repurchase arrangements has also been extended. In addition to all the above measures, in the second half of October the rate on lombard loans was lowered from 5% to 2.5%. Thanks to the CNB's comprehensive and decisive measures, excess liquidity today is around EUR 8.5 billion. which is significantly above the average for the first nine months of this year, which amounted to HRK 6.4 billion. Interbank interest returned to levels of around 0.5%, and the exchange rate also stabilised at a slightly lower level than it was in early October. The CNB will continue to pursue a highly expansionary monetary policy to the extent that this does not jeopardise the stability of the exchange rate, which, due to a very high degree of euroisation, remains the basis of financial stability in the country. Perceptions of state risk remain high, and have deteriorated further in recent weeks. Credit default swap or, for short, CDS) for Croatia has been the highest of all comparable Central and Eastern European countries for two years. Croatia has risen sharply, possibly reflecting the reaction of financial markets to uncertainties about the implementation and potential effects of the conversion of loans in Swiss francs. Preliminary results of the CNB's analysis of cds spreads determinants suggest that the risk premium for Croatia is currently close to the level implied by macroeconomic funds, and the foreign environment is currently extremely favorable. But unless economic growth is dynamited and fiscal sustainability ensured, it could have an adverse effect on the country's credit rating in the medium term. This risk is also indicated by the recent deterioration of the outlook for Croatia by two rating agencies (Standard and Poor's and Fitch), which in July lowered the expected trend of Croatia's rating from "stable" to "negative". Financing conditions with domestic banks have been gradually improving for several years. This is also compounded by an expansionary monetary policy reflected in maintaining highly favourable liquidity conditions in the market. Banks' interest rates on loans to non-financial corporations have been below their pre-crisis levels for some time and remained slightly below 5% for short-term loans in the first eight months of 2015 and just above 5% for long-term loans loans. Interest rates for the population were broadly relatively stable in 2015, with the exception of interest rates on short-term loans to households, which decreased by about half a percentage point on average in August, which was due to legal changes in the way effective interest rates are set (changes to the zoo and the CCP). On the other hand, these changes did not affect interest rates on home loans, which are around 5%. Compared to other Central and Eastern European countries, interest rates on loans to businesses in Croatia are among the highest, while interest rates for the population are around or below the average for the region. The level of interest rates in Croatia is in line with weaker investment rating, or even slightly more favourable than might be expected based on the current rating. At the same time, it is noticeable that interest rates in almost all countries in the region are noticeably higher than in the old EU member states. This suggests that there is still room for a fall in interest rates, but this depends on a number of elements beyond the reach of domestic monetary policy, including macroeconomic funds and the general perception of the country's riskiness. Despite relatively favourable financing conditions, companies continued to deleverage with domestic banks in 2015, but their total debt has been rising for the second year in a row, primarily due to foreign borrowing. It is expected that such trends could continue, so companies could continue to rely on alternative sources of financing beyond banks in Croatia, and significant dynamism of domestic credit activity is not expected in the coming year. However, it should be borne in mind that the substitution of bank financing by more favourable sources is only available to companies with better creditworthiness and financial capabilities that have access to foreign markets. Nevertheless, it also opens up more space for smaller companies that have to rely on financing with domestic banks. Entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises1 - those that generate almost 2/3 of employment in the non-financial sector - systematically warn2 about the poor business environment as the main obstacle in business. The highest-ranking problems are due to weak policies and institutions, which includes the problem of "inability to collect". The frequency of changes in regulations, i.e. the uncertainty of the business environment, makes business even more difficult than bad and inconsistent, but stable regulations. The difficulties in accessing finance were highlighted by 2/3 of the entrepreneurs as a factor that, extremely or partially, makes it difficult for them to do business. Accordingly, asked about the priorities of structural reforms, companies unanimously allocate the institutional environment, but also further reforms of labour legislation, especially important to small businesses. Nevertheless, a small number of entrepreneurs express at least a principled interest in diversifying the source of financing and the intention to think beyond the "borrowing of the owner". In doing so, they clearly express the need to further improve the financial environment, which is a broader and more complex process than providing financial support to individual companies. As regards fiscal policy, the sustainability of public debt should be highlighted as the greatest macroeconomic risk of the domestic economy. Today, Croatia stands out as the country with the highest projected level of deficit in the EU and the highest level of public debt among central and eastern European countries, with the debt of most of the countries observed below the benchmark level of 60% of GDP. General government debt in the Republic of Croatia has been increasing sharply since the beginning of the crisis, and is currently close to the level of 90% of GDP. The application of the European methodology (ESA 1995 and 2010) further shed light on the size of fiscal imbalances in Croatia, notably through the amendment of the rules on the sectoral classification of institutional units, on the basis of which motorways (HAC), Rijeka-Zagreb Motorway (ARZ), Croatian Radio Television (HRT), H8e Infrastructure (H8e's) and HBOR reclassified from the public companies sector to the general government sector. The impact of these reclassifications on general government debt in 2014 was almost 15 percentage points of GDP. The aforementioned reclassifications have largely determined the continuous increase in the CNB's projections of public debt over time. 1 SMEs participate with almost 60% in the creation of added value (in the non-financial sector). 2 Survey on SMEs' access to finance, CNB 2015 In addition to the high primary deficit, in recent years the growth of public debt has been greatly influenced by the so-called effect of the snowball, which results from the difference between the interest rate on public debt and the rate of economic growth. The larger the aforementioned difference, the greater the negative effect of the snowball and the greater the primary surplus is also needed to stop the rise of public debt. It should also be noted that the amount of the primary surplus needed to stabilise public debt will also depend on the level of public debt itself. That is, the higher the public debt, the higher the primary surplus will be needed to stabilize it. In Croatia, over the past few years, the interest rate on public debt has been higher than that of economic growth, which has led to an automatic increase in public debt. Analysis of fiscal developments shows that the impact of snowballs can explain almost half of the increase in public debt over the past six-year period, and the same effect will largely determine the dynamics of public debt in the coming period. In order to reverse the negative effect of snowballs over the next two years, Croatia could grow by 1.5% in 2016. and 2017. had to achieve a cumulative primary surplus of about 3.0% of GDP or about HRK 10.0bn, while according to current projections, a cumulative primary deficit of almost HRK 3.0bn could be achieved during this period, which clearly shows the magnitude of fiscal imbalances in Croatia. With interest rates in global financial markets returning to normal levels, these challenges will only increase further. Thus, the simulation of an increase in the implicit interest rate on new debts by 1 percentage point shows that on this basis alone the debt will increase by about HRK 11 billion by 2020 compared to the level without an interest rate change. Accelerating fiscal consolidation and returning debt to a sustainable trajectory should therefore be a priority for fiscal policy makers. Although the beginning of the year was marked by some positive trends, it should be noted that Croatia's long-term growth potentials are much worse today than before the crisis. Moreover, even these almost half the rates of potential growth are surrounded by significantly greater uncertainty, as they largely depend on accelerating investment growth and productivity. In addition, it is clearly evident that Croatia lags behind most other economies of Central and Eastern Europe and the question is how much growth the economy of this structure can generate in the medium and long term. Indeed, despite positive trends, the relatively low share of exports of goods to GDP still limits its positive contribution to overall economic developments. Furthermore, without significant capacity growth in tourism, this year's growth rates will be difficult to continue, especially taking into account the volatility inherent in this sector, which is determined by external factors (e.g. weather conditions, political unrest, war conflicts). As regards consumption, on the household side, it will be limited by the continued high unemployment and continued deleveraging of household deleveraging after the favourable effects of the tax changes, while at some point a significant fiscal adjustment will still need to be started in the state, either by a conscious decision of the holders of power or under the influence of market pressure. Furthermore, private and public sector investment, despite the slight positive developments seen in the middle of the year , remain much lower than before the crisis and their significant growth will primarily depend on the success of attracting foreign direct investment, especially those in the activities of internationally exchangeable goods, but also on the dynamics of withdrawals from EU funds. Under such conditions, the CNB will continue with expansionary monetary policy, but it should be borne in mind that it cannot solve structural problems, but only buy the time necessary to carry out the necessary reforms in order to improve the prospects for long-term growth. In doing so, exchange rate stability will be maintained, which underpins the preservation of the overall financial stability, and thus a necessary precondition for investment recovery and sustainable economic growth. Namely, the European Commission also assesses that, along with Slovenia and Lithuania, Croatia has the worst growth prospects in the long term. Although at first glance the differences between countries seem small, it should be said that over time they are cumulated, so by 2040 the difference in living standards between Croatia and the most successful countries in the observed group could almost double. Behind these developments is the low employment rate, which is the lowest in the EU in Croatia after Greece, as well as very low labour productivity growth. Considering the accelerated aging of the population, which negatively affects the size of the population capable of work, it is clear that the Croatian growth perspective is not good at the moment. We can add to this the low quality of human capital, as measured by various internationally comparable indicators. For example, the International Assessment of Numeracy, Natural Science and Reading Literacy (PISA 2012) showed that Croatian 15-year-olds are significantly below the average of students from the 65 countries surveyed, and are at the back of EU countries, with only worse students in Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. In addition, Croatian universities are low ranked in different world rankings, so in the top 1000 world universities according to the World University Rankings (CWUR 2015), the only University of Zagreb is ranked 551st. Total R&D expenditure, as measured as a share of GDP, is also well below the European average. Again, fewer people in working age, a low employment rate and a relative lag in the quality of human capital that limits, already low, productivity growth, together constitute an obstacle to long-term economic growth. So what do we do? How to respond to the challenges described and change the currently poor perspective of the Croatian economy? Let's try to illustrate this first in a few examples. If we look at the economic developments in the so-called GIIPS countries in the post-crisis period, it is evident that the strongest recovery, after the initial strongest decline, was achieved in Ireland. This was mainly conducive to the better initial structure of the economy, which placed Ireland at a high position in various global competitiveness rankings in the years before and after the crisis. A similar conclusion can be drawn if the EU economy is compared with that of the US. If we compare Croatia with the countries of Central and Eastern Europe, we see that despite some progress it still lags significantly behind, both in economic developments and in the structural position. According to the World Bank, based on the Doing Business 2015 report, Croatia, despite significant progress over the last decade, remains in an unenviable last place among European Union countries in a ranking measuring ease of doing business. In doing so, it lags the most behind comparable central and eastern European countries in the processes of obtaining a building permit and registering ownership, which can be linked to the inefficiency of public administration. According to the Global Competitiveness Index Global Competitiveness Index) in Croatia particularly pronounced shortcomings in the market of goods and labour and stressed the insufficient innovation capacity of domestic companies. This also highlights as a particular problem the fact that innovation, along with the functioning of institutions and the sophistication of business, are the areas in which these comparable countries are also the most lagging behind the EU's 'older' member states. Let us stress that the general business environment is a fundamental factor in stimulating investment in a particular country. In doing so, we see that structural conditions are correlated with the success in attracting funds from EU funds, as countries that are better ranked in the world competitiveness rankings have managed to attract relatively more funds from EU funds. Likewise, the business environment is encouraged by foreign direct investment, which empirical literature recognizes as a key factor in increasing competitiveness. In doing so, they help transfer knowledge to domestic companies, moving them towards world best practices and developing a competitive set of suppliers, and the role of multinational companies for integrating the domestic economy into global value chains is further important. If we compare Croatia with the countries of Central and Eastern Europe, we can say that they have been extremely successful in attracting foreign direct investments in production and export-oriented branches. In Croatia , however, a significant part of the inflow of investments was achieved in non-export activities, such as financial intermediation, trade, real estate and telecommunications operations. Although FDI companies generate about half of the total goods exports of the Republic of Croatia, this is still lower than in most of the mentioned countries. Let us mention that it is the barriers to trade and investment and the administrative burden on new entrepreneurs (startups) that are the main causes of the extremely unfavorable rating according to the product market regulation index. Product Market Regulation index), which puts Croatia at the back of EU countries. As the country's structurally disadvantaged position is linked to lagging economic growth, in the long run only structural reforms to improve the investment and business environment in general could create assumptions of stronger economic growth. But what are structural reforms and why are they important? In their understanding, we can use a quote from The Economist magazine: "In short, structural reforms imply changes in the way the state works... most economists believe that the role of the state is to support the efficiency of the market... Structural reforms are important for ensuring growth in the long term. But even in the short term, more radical measures are sometimes needed." Empirical research confirms the small effects of structural reforms in the short term with significant potential benefits in the medium and long term. Varga et al (2013)3, following the example of reforms in Greece, Italy, Spain and Portugal, states that the greatest benefits are possible from product market reforms and labour market reforms (education reform, tax system reform). Andre9s et al (2014)4 using the DSGE model show that structural reforms targeting product markets can deliver positive effects faster by improving investment and employment, while labour market reforms have a slower impact as they improve only employment. The level of positive effects of reforms depends primarily on whether the country can increase exports or not. 3 Varga J., Roeger W. and In 't Veld J. (2013) "Growth Effects of Structural Reforms in Southern Europe: The case of Greece, Italy, Spain and Portugal", European Economy Economic Paper No. 511 4 Andre9s J., Arce O. and Thomas C. (2014) "Structural reforms in a debt overhang", Documentos de Trabajo N.ba 1421, Banco de Espana The recent global crisis has prompted various countries to rapidly launch structural reforms in many areas of the economy, with the aim of boosting productivity and employment, and ultimately potential economic growth. Reforms have been implemented in the areas of public finances, social welfare systems (pension, health), financial sector, labour market, product and services market, education, administration, social inclusion. The implementation of structural reforms has been particularly intensive in EU countries that have become in difficulty servicing public debt, such as Greece, Ireland and Portugal, so we can describe in more detail what different measures have been taken on their examples. As regards changes to the tax system, some of the reforms implemented include increasing the tax base for individual taxes and reducing tax deductions, fiscally neutral changes to tax legislation aimed at reducing the tax burden on labour, reforming the asset taxation system (which included introducing a property tax or increasing it), reducing tax evasion, increasing penalties for tax fraud, auditing the employment of tax supervisors and strengthening their powers. A number of changes to the pension system have also been adopted, notably in Greece5, such as increasing the statutory and minimum retirement age and the periods for achieving a full pension, increasing early retirement penalties and generally reducing the generousness of pensions, and tying pensions to life expectancy. As regards social policies and active measures in the labour market, unemployment benefits and their duration have been reduced, benefits related to the level of assets have been introduced or the base to which they relate has been increased. Active employment measures have also been strengthened through an increase in education and practice benefits, improving the efficiency of national employment offices, and increasing sanctions in case of non-attendance at education. In addition, a multitude of measures have been adopted with an effect on wage setting, employment protection, working hours (reduction and freezing of minimum wages, extension of the probationary period for new employees to 12 months, allowing other workers' representatives besides trade unions to negotiate collective agreements if they represent 3/5 of the workers). Some of the measures in the product market included carrying out privatisation and launching public private partnerships and granting concessions, simplifying procedures for starting new businesses and obtaining licenses, abolishing the regulation of certain prices (e.g. electricity and fuel) and increasing competitiveness in certain activities (in Greece, for example, regulations on Sunday work, sales of pharmaceutical products in retail, were changed, car rental). The aim of the measures related to the public sector was to greatly increase its efficiency. Thus, these states reorganized the local and central governments, rationalized employee benefits, improved the management of public enterprises, reformed the public procurement process. In addition, measures to improve the healthcare system included, among other things, stronger control over 5 Europska komisija (travanj 2014.), The Second Economic Adjustment Programme for Greece, Fourth Review prescribing medicines and streamlining public procurement, increasing participation and introducing certain limits on health costs. As an example of structural reforms already implemented in Croatia, we recall the amendments to the Labour Act 2013. and 2014. age. They reduced long-standing rigidities in the labour market in Croatia, which was reflected in the improvement of Croatia's relative position vis-e0-vis other countries according to internationally comparable indices of legal protection of OECD employment and the World Bank's ease of employment index. Among other things, it facilitated the use of fixed- and indefinite employment contracts, shortened the collective redundancy procedure and simplified the procedure for dismissing workers indefinitely. However, Croatia's relative position shows that there is still room for further reforms. The importance of labour market reforms can be seen in the example of investments in IT and communication activities, which mostly go to countries with more flexible labour markets, and therefore have a higher share of employees and higher labour productivity in this propulsive activity (Bartelsman et al 2010. 6). In the end, we conclude that it takes much more than just defining the source of the problem to implement reforms. Empirical proven small effects in the short term with significant potential benefits in the medium and long term lead to problems of time inconsistency of reforms. For example, the change of the system of education and investments in human capital, gives results only in 6-8 years, the change of the pension system only by more than a decade, which is far longer than the horizon of the electoral interest of politicians. Populism always offers unreserved rewards, benefits on shortness of breath, and does not lead to facing problems, and then proactively solving them. If the benefits of the reform are not clearly explained to the public, including the consequences of their failure to implement them, experience teaches us that the likelihood of them being implemented is low. And this task requires knowledge, vision, determination, political capital... 6 Bartelsman, Eric J, Pieter A Gautier, and Joris de Wind (2010), "Employment Protection, Technology Choice, and Worker Allocation", IZA DP No. 4895

Title: Idiosyncratic shocks, economic governance in the euro area and the role of member states
text: Idiosyncratic shocks, economic governance in the euro area and the role of member states Published: 6/10/14 Last updated on: 10.12.2014. Type Speaker Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor Publish Date 6.10.2014. Statements Event The Role of the State in Economic Growth conference, organized by Columbia University's Center for Global Economic Governance Venue Event Date of events Paris, Columbia University 5.10.2014.-6.10.2014. Summary The economic and debt crisis in Europe has triggered a comprehensive institutional reform that seeks to prevent similar catastrophic scenarios in the future, but also to ensure systematic income support for member states, if this does happen. In this regard, consideration was given to the different mechanisms for sharing fiscal risks, such as the common budget for the euro area, direct interstate transfers, certain mutual guarantees of government debt and joint insurance during unemployment, all in an effort to establish a link between individual risk and fiscal transfers. However, all these mechanisms would only apply to emergencies and would not bring relief to member states with idiosyncratic shocks affecting member states in "normal" times. Such a smoothing of consumption, in order to be effective, would have to distinguish between the European business cycle and the idiosyncratic cycle, specific to that particular member state. This boundary is extremely arbitrary. The magnitude of the risk dividedamong canadian provinces, German federal states and U.S. states was estimated by various empirical surveys at an order of magnitude of about 39% through capital markets and about 23% through credit mechanisms. However, capital markets in the euro areabroke it during the financial crisis, just when risk sharing was most needed. The current debate in the EU foresees severely limited fiscal capacity, mainly ranging from 1% to 2% of euro area GDP, which even in the context of the fiscal community could not bring relief to a country hit by an idiosyncratic shock, in terms of easing the decline in consumption and income. On the contrary, the key is in the balance of revenue smoothing and risk-sharing both through capital markets and through fiscal transferas, with strict control over the moral hazard of member states.

Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a Datum objave 6.10.2014. izjave Dogaanje Konferencija Uloga drave u gospodarskom rastu, u organizaciji Centra za globalno ekonomsko upravljanje Sveuilita Columbia Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Pariz, Sveuilite Columbia 5.10.2014.-6.10.2014. Saetak Ekonomska i dunika kriza u Europi pokrenula je sveobuhvatnu institucionalnu reformu kojom se nastoje sprijeiti slini katastrofalni scenariji u budunosti, ali i osigurati sustavna dohodovna potpora zemljama lanicama, ako do toga ipak doe. U tom smislu razmiljalo se o razliitima mehanizmima dijeljenja fiskalnih rizika, kao to su zajedniki proraun za europodruje, izravni meudravni transferi, odreeno uzajamno jamenje dravnog duga i zajedniko osiguranje za vrijeme nezaposlenosti, a sve to u nastojanju da se uspostavi veza izmeu individualnog rizika i fiskalnih transfera. Meutim, svi ti mehanizmi vrijedili bi samo za izvanredne situacije i ne bi donijeli olakanje zemljama lanicama pri idiosinkratskim okovima koji utjeu na zemlje lanice u "normalnim" vremenima. Takvo bi izglaivanje potronje, da bi bilo uinkovito, moralo praviti razliku izmeu europskoga poslovnog ciklusa i idiosinkratskog ciklusa, specifinog upravo za tu zemlju lanicu. Ta granica izrazito je proizvoljna. Veliinu rizika podijeljenog meu kanadskim provincijama, njemakim saveznim zemljama i amerikim dravama razliita empirijska istraivanja procijenila su na red veliine od oko 39% putem trita kapitala i oko 23% putem kreditnih mehanizama. Meutim, trita kapitala u europodruju slomila su se tijekom financijske krize, upravo kada je dijeljenje rizika bilo najpotrebnije. Trenutana rasprava u EU-u predvia izrazito ogranien fiskalni kapacitet, uglavnom u rasponu od 1% do 2% BDP-a europodruja, to ak ni u kontekstu fiskalne zajednice ne bi moglo donijeti olakanje zemlji pogoenoj idiosinkratskim okom, u smislu ublaavanja pada potronje i dohotka. Naprotiv, klju je u ravnotei izglaivanja prihoda i podjele rizika i putem trita kapitala i putem fiskalnih transfera, uz strogi nadzor nad moralnim hazardom zemalja lanica.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Inflation is heading towards the target, but the path will be neither fast nor even
text: HPVATSk'A NAPODNA RANKA Inflation is heading towards the target, but the path will be neither fast nor even Published: 30/11/2023 Column by Governor Boris Vuji for Poslovni dnevnik, published on 29 November 2023 The steel rule of forecasting formulated by the American economist Edgar Fiedler - how we can be sure that we are wrong at the moment we make a forecast, but we cannot know when and how much we will be wrong - has manifested itself in an unusually cruel way in the past two years. Down abnormal disruptions affected the functioning of economic mechanisms and rendered projections obsolete at the time of publication. Inflation projections, which have persistently and noticeably exceeded projections since mid-2021, were particularly wrong. Professional forecasters - including those from central banks - have nevertheless partially repaired their eroded credibility in recent months. Since peaking at the end of last year, the downward trajectory of inflation in the euro area has strengthened, as projections have repeatedly predicted. However, the process of inflation returning to the target will not be quick or even. Inflation will thus continue to fluctuate from month to month due to the interaction of still elevated uncertainty and energy and commodity prices, but also the "leaching" of past volatility from annual inflation rates. Risks to inflation deviating significantly from the projections remain highlighted, but they are much more balanced than last year. The danger of inflation showing up more stubborn than expected, in addition to the risks to energy and commodity prices stemming from global geopolitical tensions, is mainly related to extremely strong labour market and record-low unemployment rates. For the time being, such a situation on the labor market keeps wage growth above levels that are in line with the return of inflation to the target level of 2 percent, if profit margins do not at least partially absorb wage growth, which is also expectations of the European Central Bank. However, it cannot be ruled out that the tightening of monetary policy and the slowdown in economic activity will bring inflation closer to the target even before 2025, as is currently projected. That is why the Governing Council of the European Central Bank will continue to closely monitor any new data that is released and, if necessary, adjust our monetary policy to the changing inflation outlook. So far, central bankers have shown that they are able to tame inflation without undue damage to the economy or the financial system. Growth slowed significantly as a result of higher energy prices and more expensive sources of financing, but the euro area did not sink into recession. The continued slowdown in inflation and the gradual recovery in real wages should push growth in private consumption. Growth should also be supported by foreign demand driven by the strengthening of the global economy. If there are no major new shocks, and a recession does occur, it will be one of the shortest and shallowest ever recorded recession. The domestic economy is coping exceptionally well with the headwinds of an unfavourable international environment and tight financing conditions. When a year ago there were signs of a slowdown under the influence of the faltering of large European economies, a sharp jump in foreign demand for services has boosted growth again. In the middle of this year, fiscal expansion, largely focused on wage growth, and the consequent strengthening of consumption, proved decisive in similar circumstances. The improvement in terms of trade related to rising prices in tourism and the decline in prices of imported energy products and raw materials also contributes to income growth and consumption. The role of record disbursements of funds from European funds that finance the growth of public investments is also important. In the fourth quarter, the strengthening of domestic demand is already visible, and the domestic economy should maintain its momentum next year, with growth that could surpass this year's. The expected acceleration of growth partly reflects the downward revision of expectations for this year, given the fact that the Croatian Bureau of Statistics recently lowered its growth estimates for the first half of this year. In the conditions of falling unemployment to lows in the time span of the past few decades, despite strong labor imports, the domestic labor market is also experiencing increasingly pronounced deficits that limit economic growth and further stimulate wage growth. At the same time, the growth of employment at the rate follows the expansion of economic activities, which means that the growth of productivity, which is the only long-term sustainable source of increasing the standard of living, has stopped. The stagnation in productivity is probably partly related to the structure of growth, which is currently based on the segment of service activities with lower value added. Nevertheless, the slowdown in productivity growth could also be partly structural in nature, linked to changes in workers' preferences after the pandemic, such as the desire to work shorter hours or a greater tendency to work from home. In addition to stagnating productivity, the fight against inflation is also hampered by the strengthening of consumer optimism, which is supported by strong lending to households, for housing and consumer purposes. On the other hand, the transmission of monetary policy is strong where it matters most to fight inflation. Interest rates on loans and deposits of companies grew quickly and strongly, so loans to companies stopped growing in the middle of the year. Inflation differentials in relation to the euro area, which are currently determined by the higher representation of expensive food in consumption and the success of the tourism sector, certainly cannot remain elevated for too long if they are not accompanied by a corresponding increase in the attractiveness of the goods and services we offer to the world market, as they lead to a loss of competitiveness and deflationary pressures on prices. Whichever path the economy takes in the coming year, as the aforementioned Fiedler noted, it is certain that the public will continue to expect greater precision from forecasters than they can deliver. And forecasters, in accordance with Fiedler's advice, will continue to frequently revise their projections. The text is available on the website of Poslovni dnevnik. CROATIAN NATIONAL BANK
text_original: HPVATSk'A NAPODNA RANKA Inflacija ide prema ciljanoj, ali put nee biti ni brz ni ravnomjeran Objavljeno: 30.11.2023. Kolumna guvernera Borisa Vujia za Poslovni dnevnik, objavljena 29. studenoga 2023. elino pravilo prognoziranja koje je formulirao ameriki ekonomist Edgar Fiedler - kako moemo biti sigurni da smo u krivu ve u trenutku kada napravimo prognozu, ali zato ne moemo znati kada i koliko emo pogrijeiti - neobino se okrutno manifestiralo u protekle dvije godine. Niz neuobiajenih poremeaja odrazio se na funkcioniranje gospodarskih mehanizama i projekcije inio zastarjelima ve u trenutku objavljivanja. Osobito su grijeile projekcije inflacija koje su od sredine 2021. ustrajno i zamjetno nadmaivala projekcije. Profesionalni prognozeri - ukljuujui i one iz sredinjih banaka - ipak su proteklih mjeseci djelomino popravili naruenu vjerodostojnost. Otkad je krajem prole godine dosegla vrhunac, silazna putanja inflacije u europodruju se uvrstila, kao to su projekcije opetovano i navjeivale. Proces povratka inflacije prema cilju ipak nee biti brz ni ravnomjeran. Inflacija e tako i dalje oscilirati od mjeseca do mjeseca zbog meudjelovanja jo uvije poviene neizvjesnosti i cijena energenata i sirovina, ali i "ispiranja" prole volatilnosti iz godinjih stopa inflacije. Rizici da inflacija znatnije odstupa od projekcija i dalje su naglaeni, ali su znatno uravnoteeniji no lani. Opasnost da se inflacija pokae tvrdokornijom od oekivanja je, uz rizike za cijene energenata i sirovina koji proizlaze iz globalnih geopolitikih tenzija, uglavnom povezana s iznimno snanim tritem rada i rekordno niskim stopama nezaposlenosti. Takvo stanje na tritu rada za sada odrava rast plaa iznad razina koje su u skladu s povratkom inflacije na ciljanu razinu od 2 posto, ukoliko profitne mare barem djelomino ne apsorbiraju rast plaa, to su i oekivanja Europske sredinje banke. No, ne moe se iskljuiti ni mogunost da e zaotravanje monetarne politike i usporavanje gospodarske aktivnosti pribliiti inflaciju cilju i prije od 2025. godine, kako se trenutno predvia. Zato emo u Upravnom vijeu Europske sredinje banke i dalje pomno pratiti svaki novi podatak koji se objavi i po potrebi prilagoavati monetarnu politiku promjeni izgleda za inflaciju. Sredinji bankari za sada su pokazali da su u stanju ukrotiti inflaciju bez pretjerane tete za gospodarstvo ili financijski sustav. Rast se znatno usporio kao posljedica viih cijena energenata i skupljih izvora financiranja, ali europodruje nije potonulo u recesiju. Nastavak usporavanja inflacije i postupni oporavak realnih plaa trebali bi pogurati rast osobne potronje. Rast bi trebala potpomoi i inozemna potranja potaknuta jaanjem globalnog gospodarstva. Ako ne bude veih novih okova, a do recesije ipak doe, to e biti jedna od najkraih i najpliih ikad zabiljeenih recesija. Domae se gospodarstvo iznimno dobro nosi s "eonim vjetrovima" nepovoljnog meunarodnog okruja i zaotrenih uvjeta financiranja. Kad su prije godinu dana postale vidljive naznake usporavanja pod utjecajem posustajanja velikih europskih gospodarstava, snaan skok inozemne potranje za uslugama ponovno je potaknuo rast. Sredinom ove godine u slinim se okolnostima presudnom pokazala fiskalna ekspanzija, uvelike usmjerena na rast plaa, i posljedino jaanje potronje. Rastu dohodaka i potronji pridonosi i popravljanje uvjeta razmjene povezano s rastuim cijenama u turizmu i smanjenjem cijena uvoznih energenata i sirovina. Vana je i uloga rekordnih isplata sredstava iz europskih fondova koje financiraju rast javnih investicija. U etvrtom je tromjeseju tako ve vidljivo jaanje domae potranje, a domae gospodarstvo bi zamah trebalo odrati i naredne godine, uz rast koji bi mogao nadmaiti ovogodinji. Oekivano ubrzavanje rasta djelomino odraava i reviziju oekivanja za ovu godinu na nie s obzirom na injenicu da je Dravni zavod za statistiku nedavno spustio procjene rasta za prvu polovicu ove godine. U uvjetima pada nezaposlenosti na minimume u vremenskom rasponu od nekoliko proteklih desetljea, i na domaemu su tritu rada, unato snanom uvozu radne snage, sve izraeniji manjkovi koji ograniavaju gospodarski rast i dodatno potiu rast plaa. Pritom rast zaposlenosti u stopu prati ekspanziju ekonomskih aktivnosti, to znai da se zaustavio rast proizvodnosti, koji predstavlja jedini dugorono odrivi izvor poveanja ivotnog standarda. Stagnacija proizvodnosti vjerojatno je djelomino vezana uz strukturu rasta koji se trenutno temelji na segmentu uslunih djelatnosti s niom dodanom vrijednosti. Ipak, usporavanje rasta proizvodnosti djelomino bi moglo biti i strukturne naravi, povezano s promjenama preferencija radnika nakon pandemije poput elje za kraim radnim vremenom ili vee sklonosti za radom od kue. Uz stagnaciju proizvodnosti, borbu s inflacijom oteavaju i jaanja potroakog optimizma koju podupire snano kreditiranje stanovnitva, za stambene kao i potroake svrhe. S druge strane, transmisija monetarne politike snana je tamo gdje je za borbu s inflacijom najvanije. Kamatne stope na kredite i depozite poduzea rasle su brzo i snano pa su krediti poduzeima jo sredinom godine prestali rasti. Inflacijski diferencijali u odnosu na europodruje, koji su trenutno odreeni veom zastupljenosti skupe hrane u potronji i uspjesima turistikog sektora, svakako ne mogu predugo ostati povieni ako nisu praeni odgovarajuim rastom atraktivnosti roba i usluga koje nudimo svjetskom tritu jer dovode do gubitka konkurentnosti i deflacijskih pritisaka na cijene. Kojim god putem gospodarstvo krenulo u narednoj godini, kako je zamijetio jo spomenuti Fiedler, sigurno je da e javnost od prognozera i dalje oekivati veu preciznost nego je oni mogu isporuiti. A prognozeri e, u skladu s Fiedlerovim savjetom, i dalje uestalo revidirati svoje projekcije. Tekst je dostupan na internetskim stranicama Poslovnog dnevnika.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary policy challenges and securities purchase programs in emerging economies
text: Monetary policy challenges and asset purchase programmes in emerging economies Published: 6.4.2021. Governor Talk - Croatia: Asset Purchase Programs in Emerging Markets - Yes, We Can! Kind Speaker Date of publication of the Event statement Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor 6.4.2021. 2021 Spring Assembly of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Boris Vujcic, governor of the CNB, argued in his speech that the programmes for buying securities in emerging economies managedto stabilise the financial shocks caused by the pandemic. According to him, asset purchase programmes have worked in emerging economies in a very similar way to developed economies, reducing returns on NICE liabilitiesand improving financing conditions for domestic economies. Their impact on stock prices, the governor said, was somewhat weaker, due to the fact that emerging economies generally have less developed capital markets, so this channel of buying valuablepapers was not so important. "In addition, emerging economies are less exposed to deflationary risk, so the main objectives of the asset purchase programme were to prevent the financial destabilisation of the sovereign bond market, rather than the floorthreatened by inflation. Finally, asset purchase programmes did not trigger exchange rate depreciation in emerging economies, which could have damaged the economy, undermined market confidence and reduced the bulk of the positive effects of these programmes. exchange, the so-called currency swap that allows the exchange of kunas for euros, in the amount of 2 billion euros," the governor stressed. He said that the securities purchase programmes were temporary in nature and could be reactivated in Croatia ifthe conditions they were to be met again at the beginning of this crisis caused by the coronavirus pandemic and epidemiological measures. See Governor Boris Vujcic's speech on the International Monetary Fund's website.
