Proljetna skuptina Meunarodnog monetarnog fonda i Svjetske banke 2021. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a je u svom govoru ustvrdio kako su programi kupnje vrijednosnih papira u gospodarstvima u nastajanju uspjeli stabilizirati financijske okove uzrokovane pandemijom. Prema njegovim rijeima, programi kupnje vrijednosnih papira funkcionirali su u gospodarstvima u nastajanju na vrlo slian nain kao i u razvijenim gospodarstvima, te su smanjili prinose na obveznice i poboljali uvjete financiranja za domaa gospodarstva. Njihov je utjecaj na cijene dionica, istaknuo je guverner, bio neto slabiji i to zbog toga to gospodarstva u nastajanju openito imaju slabije razvijena trita kapitala pa taj kanal kupnje vrijednosnih papira nije bio toliko vaan. "Osim toga, gospodarstva u nastajanju manje su izloena deflacijskom riziku, pa su glavni ciljevi programa kupnje vrijednosnih papira bili sprijeiti financijsku destabilizaciju trita dravnih obveznica, a ne poduprijeti inflaciju. Naposljetku, programi kupnje vrijednosnih papira nisu u gospodarstvima u nastajanju potaknuli deprecijaciju teaja, koja je mogla nanijeti tetu gospodarstvu, naruiti trino povjerenje i umanjiti glavninu pozitivnih uinaka tih programa. U Hrvatskoj je teaj ostao stabilan zahvaljujui visokoj razini meunarodnih priuva koje su omoguile snanije intervencije na deviznom tritu te zbog toga to je HNB dogovorio s Europskom sredinjom bankom (ESB) uspostavljanje linije za valutni ugovoro razmjeni, tzv. valutni swap koji omoguuje razmjenu kuna za eure, u iznosu od dvije milijarde eura", naglasio je guverner. On je kazao kako su programi kupovine vrijednosnih papira bili privremene prirode, te da bi se u Hrvatskoj mogli opet aktivirati samo ako bi se opet stekli uvjeti kakvi su bili na poetku ove krize uzrokovane pandemijom koronavirusa i epidemiolokim mjerama. Govor guvernera Borisa Vujia pogledajte na internetskim stranicama Meunarodnog monetarnog fonda.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Avoiding the paradox of savings in the liquidity trap
text: Avoiding the austerity paradox in liquidity traps Published: 15.4.2021. Kind Speaker Source Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor The EUROFI Magazine The COVID-19 pandemic has sent an unprecedented shock to European economies at a time when Europe was already concerned about problems related to secular stagnation. At the time of the impact of the pandemic, the conventional transmission mechanism of monetary policy was not working, and monetary policyrelied for a long time on unconventional measures that led to an increase in the balance sheet of the European Central Bank (ECB). Although the effectiveness of unconventional measures continues to be discussed, numerous empirical studies show that in the post-global financialcrisis, reliance on non-standard instruments helped to avoid the liquidity trap. It is therefore not surprising that the initial phase of the pandemic crisis was characterised by a huge increase in the ECB's balance sheet, which has contributed significantly to the stabilisation of financial markets. It goesbottom with a strong fiscal policy response, the ECB's reaction prevented the collapse of the labour market and the collapse of businesses. Nevertheless, despite the ECB's performance during the first wave of the pandemic, the shock it caused highlighted the inevitability of a strong reliance on quantitative easing and low interest rates over a longer period of time: the scope for monetary action has been widely exploited without triggering significant growth in productive investment. While the pandemic continues to adversely affect European economies, heightened hopes thata recovery close to economic policymakers puts some new and some old challenges. First, inflation remained below the medium-term target despite accommodative monetary policy. As low inflation may indicate low growth in buduty, the pandemic shock has heightened concerns about secular stagnation as inflation has fallen further below target. Therefore, in the post-crisis period, monetary policy holders will continue to deal with unresolved issues related to low inflag and rising asset prices related to quantitative easing. Second, ultra-low interest rates over a long period of time have fuelled rising public and private sector indebtedness and cash holdings, but neither have they driven significant growth in productivelying. The long-term implications of the growing public debt linked to the COVID-19 pandemic, which has accumulated to already high indebtedness in some countries, remain uncertain. On the one hand, low interest rates alleviate concerns related to highligancy, which can lead to lower growth in the future, and on the other hand can threaten financial stability. Adding to concern is the sustainability of the link between quantitative easing and rising indebtedness. Third, the COVID-19 pandemic has caused ahitherto notable increase in the EU's savings rate, which has intensified concerns about the adverse economic implications of the Keynes austerity paradox. In such a situation, monetary policy should be aimed at reducing uncertainty in order toeducate motives for austerity and encourage investment. While trying to avoid the savings paradox, it is important to ensure that investment activity is not constrained by banks' strict credit conditions. Investments not only affect the search side of the LordArity but also determine the future offer. Finally, while it is difficult to answerthe old question about the 'appropriate policy mix' the current crisis has put before economic policymakers, the post-crisis recovery requires a clear commitment to countercyclical policies that would reduce uncertainties and adverse effects of precautionary austerity. As some empirical evidence shows that monetary policy efficiency in promoting recovery is limited, fiscal expansion will become essential to support demand and reduce the cost of the pandemic. The concernsof monetary policy constraints and high public sector indebtedness, which will inevitably arise after the end of the crisis, constitute the targeted and efficient use of funds from the Recovery and Resilience Facility under the "NextGenerationEU" instrument with a narrow instrument to stimulate productive investment. Although countercyclical policies may be needed for a longer period after the end of the current crisis, they should not divert attention from regulatory and institutional factors thatlimit private investment in some emblems. The priority for these countries is to "not let a good crisis fail" by implementing reforms aimed at factors to boost investment. Without these reforms, the effects of macroeconomic policies are likely to be very limited andatocratic. The article was published in The EUROFI Magazine.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izbjegavanje paradoksa tednje u zamci likvidnosti Objavljeno: 15.4.2021. Vrsta Govornik Izvor Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a The EUROFI Magazine Pandemija bolesti COVID-19 izazvala je nezapamen ok za europska gospodarstva u vrijeme kad je Europa ve bila zabrinuta zbog problema povezanih sa sekularnom stagnacijom. U trenutku udara pandemije konvencionalni transmisijski mehanizam monetarne politike nije funkcionirao, a monetarna se politika dulje vremena oslanjala na nekonvencionalne mjere koje su dovele do poveanja bilance Europske sredinje banke (ESB). lako se o uinkovitosti nekonvencionalnih mjera i dalje raspravlja, brojna empirijska istraivanja pokazuju da je u razdoblju nakon globalne financijske krize oslanjanje na nestandardne instrumente pomoglo u izbjegavanju zamke likvidnosti. Stoga ne iznenauje daje poetnu fazu pandemijske krize obiljeilo golemo poveanje bilance ESB-a, koje je znatno pridonijelo stabilizaciji financijskih trita. Zajedno sa snanom reakcijom fiskalne politike reakcija ESB-a sprijeila je slom trita rada i propadanje poduzea. Ipak, unato uspjenosti ESB-a tijekom prvog vala pandemije, ok koji je izazvala naglasio je neizbjenost snanog oslanjanja na kvantitativno poputanje i niske kamatne stope tijekom duljeg razdoblja: prostor za monetarno djelovanje uvelike je iskoriten, a pritom nije potaknut znatan rast produktivnih ulaganja. Dok pandemija i dalje nepovoljno utjee na europska gospodarstva, pojaane nade da je oporavak blizu pred nositelje ekonomskih politika stavljaju neke nove i neke stare izazove. Prvo, inflacija je ostala ispod srednjoronog cilja unato akomodativnoj monetarnoj politici. S obzirom na to da niska inflacija moe upuivati na nizak rast u budunosti, pandemijski ok pojaao je zabrinutosti glede sekularne stagnacije jer je inflacija dodatno pala ispod ciljane razine. Stoga e se nositelji monetarne politike u postkriznom razdoblju nastaviti baviti nerijeenim pitanjima povezanima s niskom inflacijom i rastom cijena imovine povezanim s kvantitativnim poputanjem. Drugo, iznimno niske kamatne stope tijekom dugog razdoblja potaknule su rast zaduenosti javnog i privatnog sektora i dranje gotovine, ali ni su potaknule znaajan rast produktivnih ulaganja. Dugorone implikacije rastuega javnog duga povezanog s pandemijom COVID-19, koji se u nekim zemljama akumulirao na ionako visoku zaduenost, i dalje su neizvjesne. S jedne strane, niske kamatne stope ublaavaju zabrinutosti povezane s visokom zaduenosti koja moe dovesti do nieg rasta u budunosti, a s druge strane mogu ugroziti financijsku stabilnost. Dodatnu zabrinutost izaziva odrivost veze izmeu kvantitativnog poputanja i rasta zaduenosti. Tree, pandemija COVID-19 izazvala je dosad nezabiljeeno poveanje stope tednje u EU-u koje je intenziviralo zabrinutosti povezane s nepovoljnim ekonomskim implikacijama Keynesova paradoksa tednje. U takvoj bi situaciji monetarna politika trebala biti usmjerena na smanjenje neizvjesnosti kako bi se reducirali motivi za tednju zbog opreza i potaknula ulaganja. Dok se pokuava izbjei paradoks tednje, vano je osigurati da investicijska aktivnost ne bude ograniena strogim kreditnim uvjetima banaka. Investicije ne utjeu samo na potranu stranu gospodarstva ve odreuju i buduu ponudu. injenica da jo uvijek ne moemo biti sigurni u razmjere tete koju je pandemija COVID-19 nanijela potencijalnom BDP-u i rastu dodatno naglaava nunost poticanja produktivnih ulaganja. Konano, iako je teko odgovoriti na staro pitanje o "odgovarajuoj kombinaciji politika" koje je trenutana kriza postavila pred nositelje ekonomskih politika, oporavak nakon krize zahtijeva jasnu opredijeljenost za protuciklike politike kojima bi se smanjile neizvjesnosti i nepovoljni uinci tednje zbog opreza. S obzirom na to da neki empirijski dokazi pokazuju daje efikasnost monetarne politike pri promicanju oporavka ograniena, fiskalna e ekspanzija postati neophodna za podupiranje potranje i smanjenje trokova pandemije. Zabrinutosti glede ogranienja monetarne politike i visoke zaduenosti javnog sektora, koje e se neminovno pojaviti nakon zavretka krize, ine ciljanu i efikasnu upotrebu sredstava iz Mehanizma za oporavak i otpornost u sklopu instrumenta "NextGenerationEU" kljunim instrumentom za poticanje produktivnih ulaganja. lako e protuciklike politike moda biti potrebne u duljem razdoblju nakon zavretka trenutane krize, njima se ne bi smjela skrenuti pozornost s regulatornih i institucionalnih faktora koji u nekim zemljama ograniavaju privatna ulaganja. Prioritet je tim zemljama da "ne dopuste da propadne dobra kriza" provedbom reforma usmjerenih na faktore za poticanje ulaganja. Bez tih reforma uinci makroekonomskih politika vjerojatno e biti vrlo ogranieni i kratkoroni. Tekst je objavljen u asopisu The EUROFI Magazine.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation in the Croatian Parliament
text: Presentation by Governor Boris Vujcic at the Croatian Parliament Published: 22.4.2021. Type Speech Speaker Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, Governor Topic Semiannual information on the financial situation, the degree of realization of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy for the first half of 2020 Event Session of the Croatian Parliament Date 22.4.2021. events Semi-annual information on the financial situation, the degree of realisation of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy for the first half of2020 Dear Mr. President, Distinguished Representatives and Representatives, dear ladies and gentlemen, I greet you all warmly. In accordance with the legal obligation, I will briefly present the Semiannual Information on the financial situation, the degree ofrealization of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy relating to the first half of 2020. The whole of last year was marked decisively by the COVID-19 pandemic. The pandemic caused a global crisis, and unlike previous financial oreconomic crises, this one really covered the whole world, easily had no origin in the economy, there is not a single economic segment left untouched by it - from oil prices and inflation, to personal consumption and supply chains everythingchanged before the night. An economic crisis of this character and intensity needed to be addressed urgently and strongly. The CNB did so by providing extraordinarily strong support to the state and economy with the whole package of measures. I remind you that with the decision to close the economy (decisionm on lockdown) we found ourselves in a situation that is not described in any textbook - the economy almost stopped, all earlier projections of economic developments became pointless, and international financial markets reacted with a sharp decline and/or a highvolatile rate. As I said at the time, a situation that is not foreseen in any textbook or manual, and is most similar to the war situation. In such circumstances, complete uncertainties, we had to develop completely new methods of monitoring current economic developments andto transfer them to markets and the public. If we had relied on the usual statistical indicators and models, it would have meant that we were behind real economic developments. Description of the situation in the foreign exchange and government bond markets In order to refer to these problems, since the beginning of March 2020, the CNB has taken a number of monetary policy measures, in three directions: a) Through foreign exchange interventions (and bilateral transactions), we have preserved the stability of the exchange rate and ensured sufficient foreign exchange liquidity. This prevented the pandemic from being a trigger for the realisation of exchange rate risks and thus large losses in the financial system and economy. From 9 March to the beginning of July, the CNB placed EUR 2.7 billion to banks. eur of foreign exchange funds, which accounts for 5.7% of GDP. Along the way, I will mention that despite this management of international reserves in the first six months of 2020, we made a profit of EUR 54.1 million. eur, although 60% of government securities carried a negative yield. In doing so, liquidity and security have been successfully achieved as the main objectives in the management of international reserves. The currency exchange agreement, the currency swap, which we concluded with the European Central Bank on 15 April, had a particularly favourable impact on the calming of exchange rate movements, and which made another EUR 2bn available to Croatia. b) Structural and regular operations (later partially restored) as well as the reduction of the reserve requirement from 12% to 9%, we increased kuna liquidity of thebank's attitude, in order to keep interest rates at low levels and so that banks can continue lending to citizens and the economy. Interest rates have even decreased further over the past year despite the crisis. c) We supported the stability of the sovereignbottom paper market by buying government bonds on the secondary market, working closely with fiscal policy makers. This was necessary in order for the state to be able to finance itself relatively favourably on the domestic and foreign markets in difficult conditions and thus provide, on thepart, support economy, primarily for the preservation of jobs, and on the other hand to enable the normal functioning of vital public systems, in particular healthcare. In addition to the aforementioned monetary policy measures, we have also taken supervisory measures, the use of which we have provided room for optimal use of monetary policy instruments. By temporarily allowing banks to use the liquidity buffer liquidity coverage ratio - LCR) below the prescribed minimum amount of 100% we directly resistedthe liquidity of the economy and thus further facilitated the financing conditions, but also contributed to preserving the stability of the exchange rate of the kuna against the euro. Also, the CNB has temporarily provided a more flexible approach to supervisory rules on the classification of existing and new exposures according to the degree of their collectability. Namely, we have allowed credit institutions to continue to treat non-risk clients as such until then, regardless of payment deferrals or new financing to mitigate the effects of the pandemic. At the same time, in order to preserve solvency and liquidity, we have instructed credit institutions to keep the profits made in 2019 and allocate them to capital and to adjust the payments of variable remuneration (various bonuses, rewards and the like). As a result, banks' profits in the first halfand 2020 decreased due to a decline in almost all operating income, as well as rising costs caused by an increase in credit risk. In addition, we have taken a number of direct measures to make it easier for citizens to do business, such as the abolition of cash withdrawal feesat ATMs from the network of other banks, the urgent issuance of cards for protected accounts, an increase in the limit for contactless payments without a PIN to HRK 250.00, and the like. We have dedicated special care to consumer protection and, in relation to the moratoriums onconsumer chalk, we have determined that the new conditions and repayment periods must not violate existing consumer rights and that consumers must be informed of their rights in a timely and clear manner. I would point out that foreign exchange reserves have returned to pre-crisis levels since the first half of 2020 , and that given the monetary and supervisory measures taken and the high capital reserves, there was no need to take macroprudential policy measures to preserve financial stability. In other words, despite the extraordinary circumstancesand there was no need to apply all the measures at our disposal, because by prudent policies of previous years we have made the financial system resilient enough to withstand a shock of this magnitude and intensity. I would add that we in Croatia, in addition to the pandemic, had an earthquake in Zagreb (and later, a pokup earthquake, which is outside the scope of this biannual information), we have extended some measures to citizens and businesses affected by the earthquake. And all this took place simultaneously with intensive preparations for entry into the ERM II, close cooperation or the Single Resolution Mechanism, which was implemented on 10 July 2020. At that point, few believed it was possible. In the end, the CNB was also affected internally by the pandemic. We had to organise specific work regimes to take care of the health of employees at the same time and to ensure the seamless continuity of key functions, such as payment or cash supply to citizens and the economy. The earthquake severely damaged the officesfrom which we work, which, along with the pandemic, made it even more difficult to organize the work. I will provide more details about the current economic situation, the current situation in the banking and financial system and monetary developments in the answers to your questions, and with ashort time going through the key economic indicators in the first half of 2020. As expected, there was an exceptional decline in real GDP, even by 7.8% compared to the same period of the previous year, specifically due to the decrease in personal consumption, investments and total exports, especially exports of services (tourism). Government spending rose slightly and personal consumption decreased by 6.8% year-on-year. The decline in personal consumption was the result of a decrease in disposable income due to negative developments in the labour market. Willingmovements in the labour market in early 2020 were recorded until March, i.e. until the pandemic flare-up. At the end of the first semester, the decrease in the number of employees in particular in the activities of providing accommodation and food service. The perennial volatilityn trend of falling unemployment has also stopped and wage growth has slowed significantly. In mid-2020, the average nominal gross salary was slightly higher compared to the same period of the previous year due to strong measures of the Government of the Republic of Croatia for the preservation of employment, in theform of payment of aid to companies. The spread of the pandemic has had an impact on reducing inflationary pressures in general and tourism-related services in particular due to a significant drop in passenger numbers and in durable consumables, due to a decrease in investment. Potr inflationslowed from 1.4% in December 2019 to -0.2% in June 2020 mainly due to a significant decrease in energy prices, especially petroleum products. Core inflation slowed slightly from 1.2% in December 2019 to 1.1% in June 2020. The pandemic hasalso affected the dynamics in economic relations with foreign countries. The decrease in the surplus in the current and capital account of the balance of payments primarily due to the significant decrease in net exports of services, is particularly affected by tourism. By completing this cross-section of the first semester of 2020,I would like to invite you back to the CNB for an open exchange of views. To the parliamentary caucuses that have come on a working visit to the CNB, which are three clubs so far, I thank you for accepting the invitation, and I cordially invite the others and I hope that you will respond soon. Finally,they wish them all good health and I thank you for your attention. I'd be happy to answer your questions.

Boris Vuji, guverner Tema Polugodinja informacija o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike za prvo polugodite 2020. godine Dogaanje Sjednica Hrvatskog sabora Datum 22.4.2021. dogaanja Polugodinja informacija o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike za prvo polugodite 2020. godine Potovani gospodine Predsjednie, uvaene zastupnice i zastupnici, potovane dame i gospodo, sve vas srdano pozdravljam. U skladu sa zakonskom obvezom, ukratko u predstaviti Polugodinju informaciju o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike koja se odnosi na prvo polugodite 2020. godine. Cijelu prolu godinu presudno je obiljeila pandemija bolesti COVID-19. Pandemija je uzrokovala globalnu krizu, a za razliku od prethodnih financijskih ili gospodarskih kriza, ova je doista obuhvatila ba cijeli svijet, lako nije imala ishodite u gospodarstvu, ne postoji ni jedan ekonomski segment koji je ostao njome netaknut - od cijena nafte i inflacije, do osobne potronje i opskrbnih lanaca sve se preko noi promijenilo. Na gospodarsku krizu ovakvoga karaktera i intenziteta bilo je potrebno odgovoriti hitno i snano. HNB je to i uinio pruajui izvanredno veliku potporu dravi i gospodarstvu cijelim paketom mjera. Podsjeam da smo se odlukom o zatvaranju ekonomije (odlukom o lockdownu) nali u situaciji koja nije opisana ni u jednom udbeniku - ekonomija je gotovo stala, sve ranije projekcije gospodarskih kretanja postale su bespredmetne, a meunarodna financijska trita reagirala su snanim padom i/ili visokom kolebljivou. Kao to sam tada rekao, situacija koja nije predviena ni u jednom udbeniku ili priruniku, a najslinija je ratnoj situaciji. U takvim okolnostima potpune neizvjesnosti morali smo razviti sasvim nove metode praenja tekuih ekonomskih kretanja i istodobno ih prenijeti tritima i javnosti. Da smo se oslanjali na uobiajene statistike pokazatelje i modele, znailo bi da kasnimo za stvarnim gospodarskim kretanjima. Opis situacije na deviznom tritu i tritu dravnih obveznica Kako bi uputio na te probleme, od poetka oujka 2020. HNB je poduzeo niz mjera iz podruja monetarne politike, i to u tri smjera: a) Deviznim intervencijama (i bilateralnim transakcijama) ouvali smo stabilnost teaja i osigurali dovoljnu deviznu likvidnost. Time smo sprijeili da pandemija bude okida za realizaciju teajnih rizika, a time i velikih gubitaka u financijskom sustavu i gospodarstvu. HNB je od 9. oujka do poetka srpnja bankama plasirao 2,7 mlrd. EUR deviznih sredstava, to ini 5,7% BDP-a. Usput u spomenuti da smo unato tome upravljanjem meunarodnim priuvama u prvih est mjeseci 2020. ostvarili zaradu od 54,1 mil. EUR, iako je 60% dravnih vrijednosnih papira nosilo negativan prinos. Pritom su likvidnost i sigurnost kao osnovni ciljevi u upravljanju meunarodnim priuvama uspjeno ostvareni. Na smirivanje kretanja teaja posebno je povoljan utjecaj imao sporazum o valutnoj razmjeni, valutni swap, koji smo zakljuili s Europskom sredinjom bankom 15. travnja, i kojim su Hrvatskoj na raspolaganje stavljene jo 2 mlrd. EUR. Sporazum je dva puta produljen i prema trenutnom aranmanu traje do oujka 2022. b) Strukturnim i redovnim operacijama (kasnije djelomino vraenima) kao i smanjenjem obvezne priuve s 12% na 9% poveali smo kunsku likvidnost bankovnog sustava, kako bi se kamatne stope zadrale na niskim razinama i kako bi banke mogle nastaviti kreditiranje graana i gospodarstva. Kamatne su se stope tijekom protekle godine unato krizi ak dodatno smanjile. c) Podupirali smo stabilnost trita dravnih vrijednosnih papira otkupom dravnih obveznica na sekundarnom tritu, usko suraujui s nositeljima fiskalne politike. To je bilo nuno kako bi se drava mogla relativno povoljno financirati na domaem i inozemnom tritu u tekim uvjetima i tako osigurati, sjedne strane, potporu gospodarstvu, ponajprije za ouvanje radnih mjesta, a s druge strane omoguiti normalno funkcioniranje vitalnih javnih sustava, a osobito zdravstva. Osim spomenutih mjera monetarne politike poduzeli smo i supervizorske mjere, ijom smo upotrebom osigurali prostor za optimalno koritenje instrumenata monetarne politike. Privremenim doputanjem bankama da se koriste zatitnim slojem likvidnosti (engl. liquidity coverage ratio - LCR) ispod propisanoga najmanjeg iznosa od 100% izravno smo podupirali likvidnost gospodarstva i time dodatno olakavali uvjete financiranja, ali i pridonijeli ouvanju stabilnosti teaja kune prema euru. Takoer, HNB je privremeno omoguio fleksibilniji pristup supervizorskim pravilima o klasifikaciji postojeih i novih izloenosti prema stupnju njihove naplativosti. Naime, kreditnim institucijama omoguili smo da dotad nerizine klijente i nadalje tako tretiraju, neovisno o odgodama plaanja ili novom financiranju za ublaavanje posljedica pandemije. Istodobno smo radi ouvanja solventnosti i likvidnosti kreditnim institucijama naloili da zadre dobit ostvarenu u 2019. i rasporede je u kapital te da prilagode isplate varijabilnih primitaka (raznih bonusa, nagrada i slino). Posljedino, dobit banaka u prvoj polovini 2020. smanjena je zbog pada gotovo svih prihoda iz poslovanja, kao i rasta trokova uzrokovanog poveanjem kreditnog rizika. Dodatno, poduzeli smo niz izravnih mjera kojima smo nastojali graanima olakati poslovanje, kao to su ukidanje naknada za podizanje gotovine na bankomatima iz mree drugih banaka, hitno izdavanje kartica za zatiene raune, poveanje limita za beskontaktna plaanja bez PIN-a na 250,00 HRK i slino. Posebnu smo brigu posvetili zatiti potroaa te smo, vezano uz moratorije na kredite potroaa, odredili da novi uvjeti i rokovi otplate ne smiju naruiti postojea prava potroaa te da potroai moraju biti pravodobno i jasno obavijeteni o svojim pravima. Naglasio bih da su se devizne priuve od prve polovine 2020. do danas vratile na pretkriznu razinu, a da s obzirom na poduzete monetarne i supervizorske mjere te visoke rezerve kapitala, nije bilo potrebe za poduzimanjem mjera makrobonitetne politike za ouvanje financijske stabilnosti. Drugim rijeima, unato izvanrednim okolnostima nije bilo potrebe da primijenimo sve mjere koje su nam bile na raspolaganju, jer smo razboritim politikama prethodnih godina uinili financijski sustav dovoljno otpornim da uspije izdrati ok ovakvih razmjera i intenziteta. Dodao bih jo, kako smo mi u Hrvatskoj osim pandemije imali i potres u Zagrebu (i kasnije, pokupski potres, koji je izvan okvira ove polugodinje informacije), neke smo mjere proirili na graane i poduzea pogoene potresom. A sve se to odvijalo istodobno s intenzivnim pripremama za ulazak u ERM II, blisku suradnju odnosno u jedinstveni sanacijski mehanizam, to je realizirano 10. srpnja 2020. U tom trenutku, malo je tko vjerovao daje to mogue. Na kraju, HNB je interno takoer bio pogoen pandemijom. Morali smo organizirati posebne reime rada, kako bismo se istodobno brinuli o zdravlju zaposlenika i osigurali besprijekoran kontinuitet kljunih funkcija, kao to su primjerice platni promet ili opskrba graana i gospodarstva gotovinom. Potres je teko otetio zgrade i urede iz kojih radimo, to je uz pandemiju dodatno otealo organizaciju posla. Vie detalja o aktualnoj gospodarskoj situaciji, trenutnom stanju u bankarskom i financijskom sustavu te monetarnim kretanjima izloit u u odgovorima na vaa pitanja, a sada bih kratko proao kroz kljune ekonomske pokazatelje u prvom polugoditu 2020. godine. Oekivano, zabiljeen je izniman pad realnog BDP-a, ak za 7,8% u odnosu na isto razdoblje prethodne godine, konkretno zbog smanjenja osobne potronje, investicija i ukupnog izvoza, osobito izvoza usluga (turizma). Potronja drave blago je porasla, a osobna potronja smanjila se za 6,8% na godinjoj razini. Pad osobne potronje bio je rezultat smanjenja raspoloivog dohotka zbog negativnih kretanja na tritu rada. Povoljna kretanja na tritu rada poetkom 2020. zabiljeena su do oujka, odnosno do razbuktavanja pandemije. Na kraju prvog polugodita smanjenje broj zaposlenih osobito u djelatnosti pruanja smjetaja te pripreme i usluivanja hrane. Viegodinji povoljan trend pada nezaposlenosti takoer se zaustavio, a rast plaa znatno se usporio. Sredinom 2020. godine prosjena nominalna bruto plaa bila je malo via u odnosu na isto razdoblje prethodne godine zbog snanih mjera Vlade RH za ouvanje zaposlenosti, u obliku isplata potpora poduzeima. irenje pandemije utjecalo je na smanjenje inflatornih pritisaka openito, a osobito kod usluga povezanih s turizmom zbog znatnog pada broja putnika i kod trajnih potronih dobara, zbog smanjenja investicija. Inflacija potroakih cijena usporila se s 1,4% u prosincu 2019. na -0,2% u lipnju 2020. uglavnom zbog znatnog smanjenja cijena energije, poglavito naftnih derivata. Temeljna se inflacija blago usporila s 1,2% u prosincu 2019. na 1,1% u lipnju 2020. Pandemija je utjecala i na dinamiku u ekonomskim odnosima s inozemstvom. Smanjenje viak na tekuem i kapitalnom raunu platne bilance ponajprije zbog znatnog smanjenja neto izvoza usluga, na stoje osobito utjecao turizam. Zavravajui ovaj presjek prvog polugodita 2020. htio bih vas ponovo pozvati u HNB na otvorenu razmjenu miljenja. Saborskim klubovima koji su doli u radni posjet HNB-u, a to su dosad tri kluba, zahvaljujem na prihvaanju poziva, a ostale srdano pozivam i nadam se da ete se uskoro odazvati. Na kraju, elim vam svima dobro zdravlje i zahvaljujem na vaoj pozornosti. Rado u odgovoriti na vaa pitanja.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation in the Croatian Parliament
text: Presentation by Governor Boris Vujcic at the Croatian Parliament Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, Governor 3.3.2016. CNB Annual Report 2014 Session of the Croatian Parliament Zagreb Dear Mr. President, Distinguished Representatives and Representatives, dear ladies and gentlemen, in accordance with the Law, the Croatian National Bank informs the Croatian Parliament twice a year about the financial situation, the degree of realization of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy. For this purpose, this Annual Report of the Croatian National Bank was submitted to parliament. In my further presentation with the above information on the financial situation, the achievementof price stability and the implementation of monetary policy, I will once again look at the possibilities and role of monetary policy in croatia's economic recovery and growth. On this track, I start by assessing the general dynamics of economic activity in the proteclog period. Real GDP mostly stagnated at a low level at the end of 2013, and on an annual basis gross domestic product in the Republic of Croatia decreased by 0.4% in real terms, due to the decline in economic activity in the second half of 2013. In doing so, the gross tothe limit decreased in the value (GVA) in most activities, most notably in construction and primary activities (agriculture, forestry and fisheries). On the other hand, the manufacturing industry has shown signs of recovery. Overall, since the beginning of the crisis, there has beena 12.4% drop in economic activity. In 2014, the positive contribution to economic developments came primarily from export growth. In contrast, domestic demand continued to decrease, with the main reasons being the re-intensification of investment declines, household deleveraging and unfavourable expectations of future economic developments. Such developments in real economic activity were also reflected in the labour market. The number of people employed stagnated at a low level reached at the end of 2013, and na decreased by 0.9% year-on-year (excluding administrative deletion in October 2014) due to a sharp decline in the second half of 2013. The number of registered unemployed persons at the CES, by contrast, decreased sharply. This was primarily dueto the strengthened deletion of those unemployed persons from the CCC records who did not comply with the legal provisions. When it comes to the average registered unemployment rate in 2014, it decreased slightly to 19.7% compared to 20.3% in 2013 The relevant, internationally comparable survey unemployment rate was maintained at an average level of 17.3%. In terms of labour prices, nominal wages stagnated (0.2%), while real wages increased slightly (0.4%) due to a decrease in consumer prices. What happened to the generalprice r azine? The average annual rate of consumer price inflation decreased from 2.2% in 2013 to -0.2% in 2014. The average annual rate of change in the basic index of consumer prices, from which, among other things, the prices of energy products and oilsof agricultural products, but not processed food products, were excluded, was in 2014 -0.4%, and was more pronounced than the rate of decline of the overall index. It is important to point out that the evolution of inflation was mainly influenced by the decrease in commodity prices on the world's trations, in particular the prices of food raw materials that spilled over into domestic prices. Thus, the contribution of food products to total annual inflation decreased from 1.5 percentage points in 2013 to -0.3 percentage points in 2014. In addition, the sharp fall in the prices of sirove oil on the world market in the last quarter of 2014 was transferred to domestic prices. The downward trend in global crude oil prices has been present since July and intensified during November and December, with the price of a 56 Brent barrel of oil recorded at the end of the year 50% lower than the price recorded in the middle of the year. Weak foreign and domestic economic activity and low core inflation in the euro area also contributed, but to a lesser extent, to a decrease in domestic inflation in 2014. Theabsence of domestic cost pressures, reflected in the stagnation of unit labour costs, further contributed to the achievement of low inflation. I will now refer to the international exchange of the Republic of Croatia, capital flows and foreign debt. For the second year in a row, the current account of the balance of payments recorded a surplus of 0.7% of GDP for the second year in a row compared to 0.8% of GDP achieved in 2013. This was mainly contributed by the export of services, due to the growth of tourism revenues, and the faster growth of goods exports from goods imports. Atthe time, the growth in profits of foreign-owned banks and foreign-owned enterprises and increased interest expenses on foreign liabilities, primarily states, reduced the current account surplus. In addition, the surplus decreased compared to the previous year due to the weaker distribution of the heartsreceived from EU funds to final beneficiaries compared to the country's payments to the EU budget. It should be noted that only funds paid to end-users are recorded in the current and capital account of the balance of payments, while the received but nerallocated funds are recorded in the financial account. Taking unallocated funds into account, the total balance of transactions with the EU was positive in 2014. Capital flows with foreign countries in 2014 were mostly influenced by the improvement in the net debt positionof both banks, which at the same time reduced their foreign liabilities and increased foreign assets. On the other hand, the debt of the state has increased, although much less than in 2013, since the state provided part of its financial needs at the end of 2013. Net foreign direct investment increased compared to 2013, but primarily due to the growth in profits of foreign-owned domestic banks, while the inflow of equity investments, excluding the impact of circular direct investment in 2014, was weaker than the year before. The majority oflying was achieved in other business activities, real estate and hotels and restaurants. Looking at Croatia's net debt position, its improvement, which began back in 2011, continued in 2014. Net foreign debt decreased slightly to EUR 25.2 billion at the end of the year. 58.5% of GDP, respectively. By contrast, in 2014 gross foreign debt increased by EUR 0.8 billion. eur and reached EUR 46.7 billion. EUR. Its growth is solely due to the adverse effect of inter-currency changesdue to the strengthening of the US dollar against the euro, although most bond issues incorporate exchange rate risk hedging. Due to the growth of the debt situation and the decrease in GDP, the relative indicator of gross foreign indebtedness also deteriorated, which in 2014 amounted to 108.4% of BDP. At the end of 2014, the international reserves of the Republic of Croatia amounted to EUR 12.7 billion. 80, which is 1.7% lower than at the end of the previous year. The fall in reserves was influenced by net foreign exchange sales totalling EUR 0.2 billion. EUR and the decrease in the foreign currency deposit of the state with the CNB, up tothe increase in reserves, the earned earnings from their investment and the positive exchange rate difference acted. Unlike gross reserves, net available reserves increased by EUR 0.1 billion in 2014. 801.3%) and reached EUR 10.7 billion at the end of the year. Eur. Ina tie-up to the reduction of gross international reserves, an indicator of their sufficiency, as measured by covering short-term foreign debt towards its remaining maturity, improved slightly. At the end of 2014, this indicator was 92.2% or 0.7 percentage points higher than beforethe end of the year. As before, in 2014 the international reserves of the Republic of Croatia continued to be managed on the principles of high security and liquidity. The rate of return of the CNB's dollar portfolio for trading in 2014 was 0.24%, while the rate of return of theCNB's euro portfel for trading in the same period was 0.42%. The better result compared to the same period in 2013 was due to falling yields and rising prices of German and US bonds, as well as the increase in prices of other euro bonds in which foreign exchange reserves were invested. The euro portfolio held to maturity, the funds of which are invested in longer-term, higher-yielding bonds, made a return of 2.06% in 2014. Now let's move on to the banking sector, which was also reflected before the descriptionon, unfavourable macroeconomic developments. Bank profitability indicators in 2014 are well below levels considered good, although they improved slightly from 2013 and bank profits recovered in 2014 after a strong decrease in 2013. Reduced provisions for losses were the most important factor in increasing profits, although they continued to weigh heavily on banks' business performance. In addition to lower provisioning costs, higher operating profits, predominantly achieved uslid falling passive interest rates and lower financing source costs, and further efforts towards business optimization also contributed to the recovery in earnings. Revenues generated by the sale of parts of the business increased, general costs continued to decline, and revenues from commissions and fees significantly porespoured in. However, the underlying source of earnings, interest income, continued to fall due to weak credit activity, a rise in problematic receivables and new consumer lending rules. In accordance with the above trends, profitability indicators recovered from the previous year, with the profitability of average assets (ROAA) rising to 0.6% and the profitability of average capital (ROAE) to 3.6%. Profitability has been marred by growing losses in banks' loan portfolios. Namely, the quality of credit perbank district was adversely affected by macroeconomic developments and the lack of recovery in economic and credit activity. At the end of 2014, the share of partially recoverable and completely irreparable placements in total placements was 16.9% and an increase in comparisonwith the 15.7% recorded at the end of 2013, thus keeping the cost of credit risk at an elevated level. After three years of consecutive cuts, banks increased their off-balance sheet liabilities by EUR 2.7 billion in 2014. kuna, with anincrease in liabilities to companies having a key impact on their growth. The structure of off-balance sheet commitments was predominantly about increasing framework loans and financing commitments made to public companies, and according to other companies banks increased their out-of-averageexposure the most on the basis of guarantees issued. But banks have a high capital adequacy that makes them resistant to possible macroeconomic disruptions. The rate of total (regulatory) capital of banks increased slightly at the end of 2014 to 21.4% versus the 21.0% recorded at the end of the previous year. With the introduction of the new capital regime (CRR/CRD IV) in 2014, business risks remained adequately covered, and this was contributed by the high level and quality of capital items andthe d onesene measures on capital buffers. At the same time, regulatory capital and overall risk exposure were reduced, although the decrease in overall risk exposure was more pronounced due to the decline in credit risk exposure. The capitalisation of bankswas positively influenced by the growth of NPLs coverage, which increased from 46.2% to 51.3% in 2014, thereby reducing the negative potential impact of credit risk on banks' stability. The adequacy rate of residential savings capitalincreased noticeably from 20.5% at the end of 2013, to 23.5% at the end of 2014, mainly due to a decrease in exposure to credit risk, similar to banks. Finally, very briefly on fiscal indicators and public finances. Public finances in 2014 were largely marked by Croatia's entry into the excessive deficit procedure. Namely, in conditions of economic stagnation and low inflation, and despite the consolidation efforts carried out, there was a further deterioration of the main fiscal indicators. The introduction of the statistical methodology of ESA 2010 in October 2013 at the same time in all EU member states also noticeably worsened the quantifications of fiscal indicators (especially the level of public debt), which happened in only a fewEU articles including Croatia. I would now focus on monetary policy and the role of the Croatian National Bank. The Croatian National Bank is in In 2014, it continued to pursue an expansionary monetary policy, while maintaining a stable exchange rate of the kuna against the euro, whichis a key precondition for preserving financial stability. The expansionary nature of monetary policy was primarily reflected in ensuring a high level of kuna liquidity of the monetary system. However, high liquidity is not an end in itself, but the central bank contributesto improving the financing conditions of all entities in the domestic market. Thus, in 2014, credit institutions had on average more excess kuna liquidity than in 2013, and as a result, overnight interest rates on the interbankand treasury bills market remained at extremely low levels. In addition, high liquidity had a beneficial effect on the fall in active and passive interest rates of domestic banks. In addition to maintaining high liquidity, the CNB also sought to stimulate the growth of bank placements to the economy and the purchase of mandatory treasury records. Since the end of 2013, the central bank has encouraged credit activity by purchasing compulsorily registered treasury records before the maturity from banks that recorded rast loans granted to companies. Despite the efforts, the dynamism of domestic credit activity in 2014 was absent. The reasons should be sought in the suppressed investment demand in conditions of high over-indebtedness of enterprises, insufficient collateral during the period of falling real estate prices, continued deleveraging of the population, a low level of business and consumer optimism, and a large proportion of bad placements and the reluctance of banks and businesses towards risk-taking. Thus, placements of credit institutions to domestic sectors (excluding central government) fell by 3.0% in 2014 (excluding exchange rate changes), their largest annual decrease since the beginning of the crisis. To summarize: The CNB supported the improvement of financing conditions of the state, banks and the private sector with monetary policy instruments, and encouraged lending on the domestic market while maintaining the stability of the nominal exchange rate of the kuna against the euro as a key precondition for preserving financial stability. Nevertheless, Croatia haslagged noticeably behind in its reversal of the reversal of the negative trends and dynamism of real growth compared to new EU member states. The areas in which it is necessary to continue andintensify efforts to implement structural reforms are, in particular, improving the business climate and raising the competitiveness of the domestic economy, then increasing foreign direct investment, which will consequently affect the increase in exports. Monetary policy will support such efforts with all available monetary policy instruments and adequate financial system liquidity, provided that the stability of the domestic currency exchange rate continues to be maintained.

Boris Vuji, guverner 3.3.2016. Godinje izvjee HNB-a za 2014. Sjednica Hrvatskog sabora Zagreb Potovani gospodine Predsjednie, uvaene zastupnice i zastupnici, potovane dame i gospodo, sukladno Zakonu, Hrvatska narodna banka dva puta godinje obavjetava Hrvatski sabor o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike. S tom svrhom dostavljeno je Saboru i ovo Godinje izvjee Hrvatske narodne banke. U svom daljnjem izlaganju uz navedenu informaciju o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike, osvrnut u se jo jednom i na mogunosti i ulogu monetarne politike u gospodarskom oporavku i rastu Hrvatske. Na tome tragu zapoinjem s ocjenom ope dinamike gospodarske aktivnosti u proteklom razdoblju. Realni BDP uglavnom je stagnirao na niskoj razini s kraja 2013. godine, a na godinjoj razini bruto domai proizvod u Republici Hrvatskoj realno se smanjio za 0,4%, zbog pada gospodarske aktivnosti u drugoj polovini 2013. Pritom se bruto domaa vrijednost (BDV) smanjila u veini djelatnosti, a ponajvie u graevinarstvu i primarnim djelatnostima (poljoprivreda, umarstvo i ribarstvo). S druge strane, preraivaka industrija pokazala je znakove oporavka. Ukupno, od poetka krize dolo je do kumulativnog pada gospodarske aktivnosti od 12,4%. U 2014. godini pozitivan doprinos gospodarskim kretanjima doao je prvenstveno od rasta izvoza. Nasuprot tome, domaa potranja nastavila se smanjivati, a glavni razlozi su bili ponovno intenziviranje pada investicija, razduivanje kuanstava te nepovoljna oekivanja o buduim gospodarskim kretanjima. Takva kretanja realne gospodarske aktivnosti odrazila su se i na trite rada. Broj zaposlenih osoba stagnirao je na niskoj razini dosegnutoj krajem 2013., a na godinjoj se razini smanjio za 0,9% (iskljuujui administrativno brisanje u listopadu 2014.) zbog snanog pada u drugoj polovini 2013. Broj registriranih nezaposlenih osoba pri HZZ-u, nasuprot tome, snano se smanjio. To je prvenstveno bila posljedica pojaanog brisanja onih nezaposlenih osoba iz evidencije HZZ-a koje se nisu pridravale zakonskih odredbi. Kada govorimo o prosjenoj stopi registrirane nezaposlenosti u 2014., ona se blago smanjila na 19,7% u odnosu na 20,3% u 2013. Relevantna, meunarodno usporediva anketna stopa nezaposlenosti zadrana je na prosjenoj razini od 17,3%. Kada je rije o cijeni rada, nominalne plae su stagnirale (0,2%), dok su realne plae blago poveane (0,4%) uslijed smanjenja potroakih cijena. to se dogaalo s opom razinom cijena? Prosjena godinja stopa inflacije potroakih cijena smanjila se s 2,2% u 2013. na -0,2% u 2014. godini. Prosjena godinja stopa promjene temeljnog indeksa potroakih cijena iz kojeg su, izmeu ostalog, iskljuene cijene energenata i poljoprivrednih proizvoda, ali ne i preraenih prehrambenih proizvoda, iznosila je u 2014. -0,4%, te je bila izraenija od stope pada ukupnog indeksa. Vano je istaknuti da je na kretanje inflacije najvei utjecaj imalo smanjenje cijena sirovina na svjetskom tritu, i to posebice cijena prehrambenih sirovina koje su se prelile na domae cijene. Tako se doprinos prehrambenih proizvoda ukupnoj godinjoj inflaciji smanjio s 1,5 postotnih bodova u 2013. na -0,3 postotna boda u 2014. Dodatno, snani pad cijena sirove nafte na svjetskom tritu u posljednjem tromjeseju 2014. prenio se na domae cijene. Trend pada cijena sirove nafte na svjetskom tritu bio je prisutan od srpnja, a pojaao se tijekom studenog i prosinca pa je cijena barela nafte tipa Brent od 56 USD zabiljeena krajem godine bila za 50% nia od cijene zabiljeene sredinom godine. Slaba inozemna i domaa gospodarska aktivnost i niska temeljna inflacija u euro podruju takoer su, ali u manjoj mjeri, pridonijele smanjenju domae inflacije u 2014. Odsustvo domaih trokovnih pritisaka, koje se ogleda u stagnaciji jedininih trokova rada, dodatno je pridonosilo ostvarivanju niske inflacije. Osvrnut u se sada na meunarodnu razmjenu Republike Hrvatske, tokove kapitala i inozemni dug. Tekui raun platne bilance u 2014. ve je drugu godinu zaredom zabiljeio viak koji je iznosio 0,7% BDP-a u usporedbi s 0,8% BDP-a ostvarenih u 2013. Tome je najvie pridonio izvoz usluga, i to uslijed rasta prihoda od turizma, te bri rast robnog izvoza od robnog uvoza. Istovremeno su rast dobiti banaka i poduzea u stranom vlasnitvu te poveani kamatni trokovi po inozemnim obvezama, prvenstveno drave, umanjivali viak tekueg rauna. Osim toga, viak se smanjio u usporedbi s prethodnom godinom zbog slabije raspodjele sredstava primljenih iz EU fondova krajnjim korisnicama u odnosu na uplate drave u proraun EU-a. Pritom treba istaknuti da se na tekuem i kapitalnom raunu platne bilance evidentiraju samo sredstva isplaena krajnjim korisnicima, dok se primljena, ali nerasporeena sredstva biljee na financijskom raunu. Uzmu li se u obzir i nerasporeena sredstva, ukupan saldo transakcija s EU-om bio je pozitivan u 2014. Na tokove kapitala s inozemstvom u 2014. u najveoj je mjeri utjecalo poboljanje neto dunike pozicije banaka, koje su istovremeno i smanjile svoje inozemne obveze i poveale inozemnu imovinu. S druge strane, dug drave je porastao, premda znatno manje nego 2013. godine jer je drava dio financijskih potreba osigurala potkraj 2013. godine. Neto inozemna izravna ulaganja poveala su se u odnosu na 2013., no prije svega zbog rasta dobiti domaih banaka u stranom vlasnitvu, dok je priljev vlasnikih ulaganja, iskljui li se utjecaj krunog izravnog ulaganja u 2014., bio slabiji nego godinu prije. Najvie ulaganja ostvareno je u ostalim poslovnim djelatnostima, poslovanju nekretninama te hotelima i restoranima. Promatra li se neto dunika pozicija Hrvatske, njezino poboljanje, koje je zapoelo jo 2011., nastavljeno je i u 2014. Neto inozemni dug blago je smanjen te je na kraju godine iznosio 25,2 mlrd. EUR, odnosno 58,5% BDP- a. Nasuprot tome, tijekom 2014. bruto inozemni dug porastao je za 0,8 mlrd. EUR i dosegnuo 46,7 mlrd. EUR. Njegov rast iskljuivo je posljedica nepovoljnog uinka meuvalutnih promjena uslijed jaanja amerikog dolara prema euru, iako je u veini izdanja obveznica ugraena zatita od teajnog rizika. Zbog rasta stanja duga i smanjenja BDP-a, pogorao se i relativni pokazatelj bruto inozemne zaduenosti, koji je u 2014. iznosio 108,4% BDP-a. Na kraju 2014. meunarodne priuve RH iznosile su 12,7 mlrd. EUR, to je za 1,7% manje nego na kraju prethodne godine. Na pad priuva utjecale su neto prodaje deviza u ukupnom iznosu od 0,2 mlrd. EUR i smanjenje deviznog depozita drave kod HNB-a, dok je u smjeru porasta priuva djelovala ostvarena zarada od njihovog ulaganja te pozitivne teajne razlike. Za razliku od bruto priuva, neto raspoloive priuve poveale su se u 2014. za 0,1 mlrd. EUR (1,3%) i na kraju godine dosegnule su 10,7 mlrd. EUR.Unato smanjenju bruto meunarodnih priuva, pokazatelj njihove dostatnosti, mjeren pokriem kratkoronog inozemnog duga prema preostalom dospijeu, blago se poboljao. Ovaj je pokazatelj na kraju 2014. iznosio 92,2% ili 0,7 postotnih bodova vie nego prethodne godine. Kao i do sada, i u 2014. godini meunarodnim priuvama RH nastavilo se upravljati na naelima visoke sigurnosti i likvidnosti. Stopa povrata dolarskog portfelja HNB-a za trgovanje u 2014. iznosila je 0,24%, dok je stopa povrata eurskog portfelja HNB-a za trgovanje u istom razdoblju iznosila 0,42%. Bolji rezultat u odnosu na isto razdoblje 2013. godine posljedica je pada prinosa te porasta cijena njemakih i amerikih obveznica, kao i porasta cijena ostalih eurskih obveznica u koje su se devizne priuve ulagale. Eurski portfelj koji se dri do dospijea, ija su sredstva uloena u dugoronije obveznice koje nose vie prinose, u 2014. godini ostvario je povrat od 2,06%. Prijeimo sada na bankarski sektor, na koji su se takoer odrazila prije opisana, nepovoljna makroekonomska kretanja. Pokazatelji profitabilnosti banaka u 2014. znatno su ispod razina koje se smatraju dobrima, iako su se blago poboljali u odnosu na 2013., a dobit banaka se oporavila u 2014. nakon snanog smanjenja u 2013. Smanjeni trokovi rezerviranja za gubitke bili su najvaniji imbenik poveanja dobiti, premda su i dalje znatno optereivali poslovne rezultate banaka. Uz manje trokove rezerviranja, oporavku zarada pridonijeli su i vea operativna dobit, preteito ostvarena uslijed pada pasivnih kamatnih stopa i niih trokova izvora financiranja, te daljnji napori ka optimizaciji poslovanja. Porasli su prihodi ostvareni prodajom dijelova poslovanja, opi trokovi nastavili su pad, a prihodi od provizija i naknada osjetno su porasli. Meutim, osnovni izvor zarade, kamatni prihod, nastavio je pad uslijed slabe kreditne aktivnosti, rasta problematinih potraivanja i novih pravila potroakog kreditiranja. Sukladno navedenim kretanjima, pokazatelji profitabilnosti oporavili su se u odnosu na prethodnu godinu, pri emu je profitabilnost prosjene imovine (ROAA) porasla na 0,6%, a profitabilnost prosjenog kapitala (ROAE) na 3,6%. Profitabilnost su naruili rastui gubici u kreditnim portfeljima banaka. Naime, na kvalitetu kreditnih portfelja banaka nepovoljno su utjecali makroekonomska kretanja i izostanak oporavka gospodarske i kreditne aktivnosti. Udio djelomino nadoknadivih i potpuno nenadoknadivih plasmana u ukupnim plasmanima je na kraju 2014. iznosio 16,9% i poveanje u usporedbi s 15,7% zabiljeenih na kraju 2013., ime je i troak kreditnog rizika zadran na povienoj razini. Nakon tri godine uzastopnog smanjenja, banke su u 2014. godini poveale svoje izvanbilanne obveze za 2,7 mlrd. kuna, pri emu je kljuan utjecaj na njihov rast imalo poveanje obveza prema trgovakim drutvima. U strukturi izvanbilannih obveza preteito se radilo o poveanju okvirnih kredita i preuzetih obveza financiranja javnih trgovakih drutava, a prema ostalim trgovakim drutvima banke su izvanbilannu izloenost najvie poveale na osnovi izdanih garancija. No, banke imaju visoku adekvatnost kapitala koja ih ini otpornima na mogue makroekonomske poremeaje. Stopa ukupnoga (regulatornoga) kapitala banaka blago se poveala na kraju 2014. i iznosila je 21,4% naspram 21,0% zabiljeenih na kraju prethodne godine. Uvoenjem novog kapitalnog reima (CRR/CRD IV) u 2014. rizici poslovanja i dalje su ostali pokriveni na odgovarajui nain, a tome je pridonijela visoka razina i kvaliteta stavki kapitala te donesene mjere o zatitnim slojevima kapitala. Pritom su istodobno smanjeni regulatorni kapital i ukupna izloenost riziku, premda je smanjenje ukupne izloenosti riziku bilo izrazitije zbog pada izloenosti prema kreditnom riziku. Na kapitaliziranost banaka pozitivno je djelovao rast pokrivenosti neprihodujuih kredita koja je tijekom 2014. godine porasla s 46,2% na 51,3% te na taj nain smanjila negativni potencijalni uinak kreditnog rizika na stabilnost banaka. Stopa adekvatnosti kapitala stambenih tedionica zamjetno se poveala s 20,5%, koliko je iznosila na kraju 2013., na 23,5% na kraju 2014., ponajvie zbog smanjenja izloenosti kreditnom riziku, slino kao i kod banaka. Naposljetku vrlo kratko o fiskalnim pokazateljima i javnim financijama. Javne financije u 2014. uvelike je obiljeio ulazak Hrvatske u proceduru pri prekomjernom manjku. Naime, u uvjetima ekonomske stagnacije i niske inflacije, a unato provedenim konsolidacijskim naporima, dolo je do daljnjeg pogoranja glavnih fiskalnih pokazatelja. Uvoenje statistike metodologije ESA 2010 u listopadu 2013. godine istovremeno u svim lanicama EU takoer je zamjetno pogoralo kvantifikacije fiskalnih pokazatelja (naroito razinu javnog duga), to se dogodilo u svega nekoliko lanica EU ukljuujui Hrvatsku. Usmjerio bih se sada na monetarnu politiku i ulogu Hrvatske narodne banke. Hrvatska narodna banka je u 2014. godini nastavila voditi ekspanzivnu monetarnu politiku, uz istodobno odravanje stabilnog teaja kune prema euru, to je kljuni preduvjet ouvanja financijske stabilnosti. Ekspanzivnost monetarne politike ogledala se prvenstveno u osiguravanju visoke razine kunske likvidnosti monetarnog sustava. Meutim, visoka likvidnost nije sama sebi svrhom, nego sredinja banka nastoji pridonijeti poboljanju uvjeta financiranja svih subjekata na domaem tritu. Tako su kreditne institucije u 2014. u prosjeku raspolagale s veim vikom kunske likvidnosti nego 2013., pa su se zahvaljujui tome, prekonone kamatne stope na meubankovnom tritu i na tritu trezorskih zapisa zadravale na izuzetno niskim razinama. Usto, visoka je likvidnost imala povoljan uinak na pad aktivnih i pasivnih kamatnih stopa domaih banaka. HNB je, uz odravanje visoke likvidnosti, takoer nastojao potaknuti rast plasmana banaka gospodarstvu i otkupom obveznih blagajnikih zapisa. Naime, sredinja banka je od kraja 2013. poticala kreditnu aktivnost otkupljivanjem obvezno upisanih blagajnikih zapisaprije roka dospijea od banaka koje su zabiljeile rast kredita odobrenih poduzeima. Unato nastojanjima, dinamiziranje domae kreditne aktivnosti u 2014. je izostalo. Razloge treba traiti u potisnutoj investicijskoj potranji u uvjetima velike prezaduenosti poduzea, nedovoljnim kolateralima u razdoblju padajuih cijena nekretnina, nastavku razduivanja stanovnitva, niskoj razini poslovnog i potroakog optimizma, te velikom udjelu loih plasmana i nesklonosti banaka i poslovnih subjekata prema preuzimanju rizika. Tako su plasmani kreditnih institucija domaim sektorima (iskljuujui sredinju dravu) u 2014. pali za 3,0% (iskljuujui teajne promjene), to je njihovo najvee godinje smanjenje od poetka krize. Da sumiram: HNB je instrumentima monetarne politike podupirao poboljanje uvjeta financiranja drave, banaka i privatnog sektora, te poticao kreditiranje na domaem tritu uz odravanje stabilnosti nominalnog teaja kune prema euru kao kljunog preduvjeta za ouvanje financijske stabilnosti. Bez obzira na to, Hrvatska je zbog neprovoenja strukturnih reformi tijekom 2014. (ali i ranije) zamjetno zaostajala u preokretanju negativnih trendova i dinamiziranju realnoga rasta u usporedbi s novim zemljama lanicama EU-a. Podruja u kojima je nuno nastaviti i intenzivirati napore za provoenje strukturnih reformi su napose poboljanje poslovne klime i podizanje konkurentnosti domaeg gospodarstva, zatim poveanje inozemnih izravnih ulaganja to e posljedino utjecati na porast izvoza. Monetarna politika poduprijet e takva nastojanja svim raspoloivim instrumentima monetarne politike i primjerenom likvidnosti financijskog sustava, uz uvjet nastavka odravanja stabilnosti teaja domae valute.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation in the Croatian National Assembly
text: Presentation of the CNB Governor Dr. Marko 8akreba in the Croatian State Parliament Published: 12.4.2000. Type Speaker Date release statements Venue Date of events Speech Dr. Marko 8akreb, served as CNB Governor from March 1996 to July 2000. 12.4.2000. Zagreb 12.4.2000. -21.4.2000. Mr. President, distinguished representatives, dear ladies and gentlemen, After a relatively long time, I am honored to have the opportunity to address the House of Representatives of the Croatian State Parliament again on the occasion of the materials of the Croatian National Bank (CNB) that are on the agenda of this session. The Annual Report of the Croatian National Bank for 1998, which was submitted to parliament in June last year, as well as in other materials, detailed thepledges on monetary policy, economic developments and the state of banking. Since about a year has passed from the writing of the report to this debate in the Croatian State Parliament, I will limit myself to only some of the most important topics, while also relying onmore important indicators and findings. There is no controversy for banks in our country's financial system to play a central role. Therefore, in today's presentation I want to say more about the banking system first, and in the second part I would like to look at monetary policy and thus cover the two most important tasks of the CNB. 1. Banking system It is worth reminding this high house that we are not the only country facing high banking costs in transition. Almost all transition countries have gone through two banking crises: 95 the first crisisof the so-called tar banks with heritage (poor assets) from the previous economic system 95 the second crisis of some banks established after a change in the economic system that failed to survive due to poor governance and/or strengthening competition in the market with the progress of the transition. The first banking crisis, the crisis of the so-called old banks, began with the beginning of the transition process (even before that), and it is about to end with the sale of rehabilitated state banks to foreign strategic investors. The costs of this crisis, caused by the legacy of the past and, in myopinion, the enormous consequences of war that are too often forgotten, include: 95 issuance of so-called large bonds in 1991 in the amount of about 990 million US dollars, 95 converting foreign currency savings into public debt in 1992 in the amount of about 3.190 million Americandollars and 95 the resolution of Slavonska, Splitska, Rijeka and Privredna banka Zagreb, between 1995 and 1996, totaling about 473 million US dollars. In total, the cost of the so-called first banking crisis can be estimated at about 4.653 million AMerric dollars. The exact amount of the cost of the first banking crisis is difficult to determine because the above estimates should not forget the revenues, i.e. revenues should not be forgotten. items that reduce the total cost, such as, for example, revenues from the privatisation of banks, and salaries, profits and tax revenues that the sanitized banks would not have achieved, or paid, if they had failed. There is no doubt that these costs are very high and place Croatia among the countries with the highest costs of resolving the banking crisis in relation to gross domestic product (GDP), which is moretimes analyzed and highlighted in more detail in the works of the CNB, as well as in the public statements of central bank employees. Such high costs are typical of countries caught up in war, such as Kuwait (45%) and Israel (25%) in one part of their history. At the beginning of 1998 , the second banking crisis occurred in Croatia, in which the then Government of the Republic of Croatia decided to bail out Dubrovnik and Croatia Bank. The cost of these two resolutions can be estimated at 347 million U.S. dollars, whereby, of course, waveand expect revenues from what I hope will be the imminent privatization of these banks. Another expression of this crisis is the cost of disbursement of secured savings in banks over which bankruptcy proceedings are opened. I remind you that in 1998 and 1999 the Croatian National Bank requested the opening ofbankruptcies for 9 banks and 4 savings banks. In addition, in 2000, the CNB requested the opening of bankruptcies over 3 other banks and one savings bank and revoked the authorisation to operate one branch of a foreign bank, one bank and 6 savings banks. The cost of disbursing insured savings to banksand savings banks over which bankruptcy proceedings have already been opened can be estimated at about 400 million US dollars. It's about judgment again. If and when the proposed bankruptcies are filed, it could increase costs by an additional 50 million andmeerical dollars. Thus, the total cost of the second banking crisis could be estimated at about 800 million U.S. dollars. If we add up the costs of the first and second crises (with repeated fencing that these are gross costs and indicative amounts), we come to the amount of about 5.45 billion U.S. dollars. Of these, the first banking crisis accounts for about 85 per cent, and the second is about 15 per cent of the cost. The first banking crisis was therefore much bigger and more dangerous for the entire economic system than the crisis of 1998. I want to point out that this crisis is for the most part behind us. Here I will not look at the causes of the first banking crisis because I believe that the socialist heritage and the consequences of the war are well known to the general public. However, it is not known that in 1990 we started on independence with thenegative capital of all banks, at US2bn. I will say more about the causes of the second banking crisis. What, in my estimation, are its main causes? First and foremost, the second banking crisis began long before 1998 and even before I was appointed governor. It began with too broad-ranging approvals for banks in the first half of the 1990s. Caution was absent both in terms of the number of banks, and about the people who were appointed to management positions in banks. Amongthese, it should be recalled that at that time the Act did not seek the so-called prior consent of the central bank when appointing managers, that is, the management of banks, but only a non-binding opinion. By the time I was elected governor, in March 1996, 55 bank authorisations had already been issued . Too many banks and/or poor management and supervisory boards in the part of the banks that deliberately violated not only regulations, but also all the principles of healthy banking operations, put part of the banks in a hopeless situation in a few years. Whatshould be obvious, but it seems that it needs to be repeated over and over again, is the simple fact that the bad business of failed banks is the responsibility of before all those who managed these banks - meaning their boards and supervisory boards. The CNB did not make bad moneydecisions, i.e. placed funds so that they could not be returned, but the management of banks. And it does not serve the supervision of banks in advance to prevent poor placement, but to spot and sanction it. Let me point out that in the very essence of the market economy that each psingle entity makes business decisions for itself and, and this is crucial, bears for these decisions all the consequences, including the possible opening of bankruptcy. The CNB cannot and should not manage commercial banks, except when the situation already becomes so serious it also gives the necessary andchange of the interim manager in order to protect the creditors (meaning savers) of the bank, and this is made possible only by the new Bank Act of the end of 1998. It should be noted that no supervisory institution can control in advance every single requestfailure in a commercial bank. It is in the very essence of the market to be a risk, so even any business decision, however well-intentioned, does not have to be a success. Moreover, I have already often pointed out that there is almost no country in the world that has not been in the last fifteen years facing a banking crisis, from the US to Sweden, from Finland to Japan, from Estonia and Latvia to the Czech Republic and Hungary. Once again, I must say publicly that the actions of individual members of the boards of banks and supervisory boards who call out the CNB for the mishandling ofbanks that they managed or supervised are absurd. This is similar to when a director of a company called out the financial police for being responsible for him mismanaging the company or for engaging in prohibited activities by law. Or when the driver, after being stopped by a traffic cop, accused the officer of speeding. I must say that it is precisely amazing that such logical bravura can be issued in the day and from case to case to public. And the real height of the absurd , I consider the calls of some politicians and businessmen to remove the governor of the Croatian National Bank under pressure from this kind of accusations. Secondly, the CNB began to build most of its functions with Croatia's independence practically from zero. In the early 1990s, sektora supervision and control trained for effective supervision of banks in the modern sense was not there. And when I took over as governor in March 1996, the sector, although already much better teamed, was clearly not ready enough to deal with the problemof having a very fast-growing but already swollen transitional banking system with almost 60 banks and two dozen savings banks. It is known that there is no way to create a highly capable and effective surveillance and control system in a short time. This requiresyears of education, work and experience gain. Thirdly, an objective obstacle to a more efficient bank supervision system was the then Bank and Savings Bank Act, which did not sufficiently allow for the active role of the CNB. Only the new Law since the end of 1998 has allowed us to have a faster and more efficient influence on banks. Therefore, only then were we able to take more effective measures towards banks, in which we have seen indications of problems before. It was at the insistence of the CNB that the previous Government proposed such a law that gave us the necessary powers. Fourth, what certainly did not help the central bank in overseeing banking institutions, at least since I have been head of that institution, was the political climate in which the banking system has grown, which is the political climate, which recidsyou can clearly see in recent days. In the vast majority of cases, this is enough for the bank to change its behavior. Unfortunately, this was not the case with us, partly because some bank administrations deliberately violated regulations out of their own interests, and partly because a climate of political "protection" of individual administrations was created. I must, thistrawler, remind MPs that I warned about this in my address to this venerable house on June 4, 1998. At the time, I said, "I am committed to eliminating the impact of any policy on banks and for them to place the va in the middle of the va only on the basis of professional banking decisions. Banks must not be social institutions, nor local development funds, but business institutions. Therefore, let's leave the management of the banks to the bankers, as this is a complex and highly skilled business. Also, let's not all of us fall into the trap of politically creating a distrustof banks because there are no grounds for it. Only in this way can banks preserve the money entrusted to them and only in this way can the stability of the overall financial system be preserved, which is the basis of economic progress." That appeal, unfortunately, and after two years, I can only repeat. The four reasons mentioned above are the main causes of what we now call the second banking crisis in Croatia. Could the CNB have prevented the second banking crisis? No. The most that might have been done in the situation described is that some ofthe ban aka that failed could have been closed a little sooner. I am sure, however, that in this case the attack on the CNB, both public and political, would be even stronger, with claims that it was the CNB that destroyed the banks that were otherwise good. With fierce attacks, after all, we have been continuously burned outfor two and a half years. Those who think that the crisis of part of the banking system could be completely avoided in the situation in which I came to this post, unfortunately, are wrong. I've never shied away from responsibility for consolidating the banking system, soI'm still running away today. Someone had to eliminate bad banks from the market because the problems were there. What was the main goal in this business, we achieved this: we avoided the systemic crisis of Croatian banking, which could have been, had it not been avoided, a lot ofmore expensive than the approximately 800 million that now amounts to the cost of the second banking crisis. There were certainly things along the way that we could have done better, which is easier to spot today with historical detachment. But I am also convinced that the amount of the second banking crisis would have been much higher if we had been guided by many of the advice and procedures suggested to us by critics of the policies that, for all the limitations I mentioned before, we have pursued towards the banking sector. I repeat, and this is not only the CNB's assessment, but also the independenth of foreign analysts, the CNB fulfilled the basic task: it prevented the crisis from taking on systemic proportions, and thus causing much higher costs. Today, standing in front of this honorable home, I can responsibly say that the work of resolving the situation in the Croatian bankingattitude is successfully flowing and that we are beginning to reap the first fruits of the consolidation, which continues. The situation in Croatian banking is much better than in the past two years, especially 5 or 10 years ago. The improvement can be seen by the performance of banks and by the fact that interest rates in the banking market have started to gradually fall, before any monetary policy moves. Today, interest rates have been halved compared to the period from the beginning of my mandate. This is a sign that restructuring in the banking sector hasfinally yielded an increase in efficiency. I must say that at the CNB we are very satisfied with this and we see a good perspective of our entire banking system in the years to come: we see a further increase in efficiency, a drop in interest rates, a decrease in credit risotowards and, as a consequence, a much more stable banking system. After, I want to believe, the rapid privatization of Rijeka and Splitska Banka, foreign strategic investors in the Croatian banking market will be even more present than in Hungary, whose banking market is considered the most efficient among the transition countries of Central and Eastern Europe. This is a guarantee of the stability of the domestic banking system in the future and something that can have a calming effect on savers after the consolidation problems our banking system has gone through over the past two years. At the end of 1998, this high house passed a new Law on Banks, which allows the CNB to act much faster and more efficiently, and thus reduce the cost of banking difficulties in the future. The surveillance and control sector, although still"emerging", today is at about the same level as in other advanced transition countries with which we must compare. He is able to cope with the current situation in the banking system. I would like to reiterate that I am proud of the strides that have been made in these partsin the last few years. All this, dear ladies and gentlemen MPs, was done in no easy institutional and economic conditions, with the situation I described at the beginning and in the ambience of constant pressure from interest groups that directed and directed the public's attention towards the CNB, in order to hide their own objective responsibility for the situation in individual banks and savings banks. In particular, I point out that those who believe that the Croatian National Bank itself could have replaced years of accumulated financial indiscipline through its work, that it could prevent corruption and economic crime, that it could have corrected errors in privatisation, that it could substitute unclear laws and the slowness of the judiciary and the work of bad auditors, and replace the absence of a special institution that would deal with financial fraud of the most complex form, that could replace the inadequate work of supervisory boards in banks and, finally, the work of those who made decisions on the placement of funds - the management of banaka. We've been warning about all this publicly for years. I don't want to get away from my share of responsibility with this. I just want to have the role of all institutions in Croatia in the past period in the construction of financial discipline and the rule of law to be fairly weighed. Beobctiv, ask the Croatian National Bank and the governor a lot, but do not expect the impossible. What I cannot accept is that without arguments and an objective assessment of the profession on what banking supervision can and cannot do, it seeks to hide the true causes of problems and difficulties in our banking, including in the overall economy. Do such views contribute to addressing the real causes of difficulties? 2. Monetary policy I would devote the second part of my presentation, much shorter, to the implementation of monetary policy. Its fundamental objective is the stability of exchange rates and prices. Over recent years, we have performed extremely well in preserving price and exchange rate stability. The average inflation rate was lower in Croatia in the last medium term than in anothertransitional country. Let's be proud of that. I must point out that this was achieved in a situation where we did not fix the exchange rate, but let it adapt to changes in economic funds, but so that it does not compromise stability.
