For years, the CNB has rejectedideas of devaluation as a solution to the economy's problems. In addition to the idea of devaluation, recently the idea of euroization has arisen, i.e. the complete replacement of the kuna with the euro as the exclusive legal means of payment in Croatia. Without entering into more detailed raslaw here on the reasons for and against euroisation, it should be made clear that no exchange rate regime can compensate for or replace structural changes. With or without a fool, we need to work harder, better and more efficiently. In those circumstances, I'd say a few words aboutwho we at HNB are seeing monetary policy this year. The correct combination of macroeconomic policy does not mean - as was the case in a significant part of transition countries, and also in Croatia - a combination of restrictive monetary and expansive fiscal policies, but a more balanced combination of these two levers of macroeconomic policy. This year's budget follows what we from the CNB have been pledging for over the last few years, meaning for limiting the growth of public spending and for bringing order to the statefinances, i.e. for settling state obligations on time, on maturity. This gave the CNB more room for manoeuvre to conduct monetary policy. Interest rates in Croatia are high today, especially compared to interest rates in developed countries. However,it is worth remembering that in March 1996 the interest on the overnight market was almost 30 percent, that the active interest of commercial banks was about 25 percent, and today they are almost in the single digits overnight, and the active interest rates of banks are exactly half the n ego four years ago. However, I would like to reiterate that monetary policy is not the main determinant of the level of interest rates on the Croatian market. The level of interest rates, as we repeat year after year, is the result of a number of structural factors such as: microeconomic efficiency of banks, i.e. their restructuring and cost reduction, the structure of the banking market that is segmented, the efficiency of the judicial system in the protection of creditors, etc. Following numerous reports on economic problems, onthe eve of the fact that I have recently been something that has been of particular concern to me, which is to offer seemingly easy and quick solutions to the complex and deep problems of the Croatian economy. Most often, a change in monetary policy is offered towards its much greater expansion. The logic of theseimportant considerations is that a greater supply of money will reduce interest rates, solve the problem of "illiquidity" (which in its essence is a problem of insolvency and financial indiscipline), increase investments, increase growth, reduce the value of the "overpriced" kuna and thus stimulate exports, and thanks to all this will solve the issue of very high unemployment and, of course, provide the standard that all citizens of this country justifiably want. Ladies and gentlemen, how lucky the solutions are so easy. So if problems inthe real ostrich sphere, in the functioning of the rule of law, in the structure of our exports, in high unemployment, etc., could be solved by printing money, then why should we, publicly ask, struggle with cost reductions, efficiency, competitive struggle and the like? So why is the Euro, which we constantly refer to and aspire to, not applying such solutions, but working intensively on the new economy of the XXI century, increasing knowledge, spreading over the Internet, new technologies and restructuring? Monetary policy is a powerful instrument, psensible in maintaining price stability. So let's not give her tasks she can't do satisfactorily. For the abuse of monetary policy leads to inflation, which, I repeat, is nothing more than a rip-off, and it robs the very poorestjih. 3. Final I stress again, there are no quick and easy solutions. The CNB should do the following: First, to preserve the stability of exchange rates and prices. Second, continue structural changes in the banking sector by completing the privatisation of rehabilitated state banks andconsolidating the benefits of the rest of the sector. Third, continue to intensively strengthen the function of banking supervision. Fourth, in the conditions created by the new fiscal policy, seek to reduce the reserve requirement rate as much as the main objectives allow. Fifth, improveregulation, including the central bank law, which needs to be modernised in accordance with European standards. Seventh, keep and continue to increase international reserves, which have played an important role as a guarantor of stability in recent years. It is especially important to accelerate the payment of secured savings, which is the responsibility of the government, which will directly affect trust in the Croatian financial system. The independence of the Croatian National Bank in the future must not mean its loneliness. It can only fully achieve its objectives in cooperation with others. The implementation of the CNB's objectives depends, among other things, on: first, institutional conditions, such as the functioning of the Croatian judiciary; second, on the existence of barem approximate consensus on the optimal combination of monetary and fiscal policy; third, on strengthening all institutions that are necessary for equal competition, with particular emphasis on strengthening financial discipline and institutional sanctioning of korupcije; fourth, on attracting foreign direct investment and entering into trade and economic associations (WTO, CEFTA, OECD, EU); fifth, about a stable political environment and even greater openness to the world, because this path simply has no alternative. Implementation onveiled goals certainly depends largely on the degree of public support. Because, without the clear and unequivocal support of the widest public with the healthy policies and tasks I mentioned, they certainly will not be able to be implemented. In particular, I ask you, ladies and gentlemen of the Representatives, to step forwardtogether this most important speaker in Croatia for sending a message to Croatian savers and the Croatian public that croatian banking today is more stable than it was two years ago and much more stable than it was five years ago. The difficulties we have encountered and will certainly encounter must not be the reason for giving up the cause. On the contrary, they must be an additional motive for us to persevere in this, primarily for the sake of us, our children and for the sake of their children. Ladies and gentlemen MPs, I call for a mirnin, an expert and reasoned debate on the state of the banking system and the work of the central bank at the place where this debate is to be held, in this high house. Monetary policy and the stability of the banking system are too serious things for judgments to be made about withoutone such discussion. Let's try to transcend the artificially created environment in which the central bank and its governor, seated by the sides, are accused of helping so-called tycoons, and, on the other hand, these same tycoons want to place themselveson the accusation bench as the cause of their collapse. Let's be above the flat-rate assessments that, sitting on the side, suggest that a robust monetary policy brought down the previous Government, while, on the other hand, it is suggested that this same policy was obedient towards this Government. On the one hand, they accuse us of leaving the boards of troubled banks alone for too long, while on the other hand they say that we are hastily taking measures without allowing them to find their own way out of difficulties. And when it comes to the latest avalanche of attacks for sending a temporaryg manager to the Istrian Bank, let it be finally said whether anything was against the current laws of this country. Let's answer today to the question: what is this policy really like? The public has the right to get a serious answer to that question. Behind the Croatian central bank during the past four years of my governorship are four years of price and exchange rate stability, a historical maximum of international reserves, the preserved international liquidity of the country, the contribution to Croatia's investment rating with the world's most importantagencies and the difficult consolidation of the banking system in which the systemic crisis was averted, which led to half the interest rates that at the beginning of my mandate. That is why I cannot resign until the public, the Council of the Croatian National Bank, its employees and I are personally told what has had more weight than the facts counted in our work so far. For such a discussion on the reports of the Croatian National Bank, I am here today at your disposal.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a dr. Marka kreba u Hrvatskom dravnom saboru Objavljeno: 12.4.2000. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Govor Dr. Marko kreb, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od oujka 1996. do srpnja 2000. 12.4.2000. Zagreb 12.4.2000. -21.4.2000. Gospodine Predsjednie, uvaeni zastupnici, potovane dame i gospodo, ast mi je to nakon relativno dugog vremena ponovno imam priliku obratiti se Zastupnikom domu Hrvatskog dravnog sabora u povodu materijala Hrvatske narodne banke (HNB-a) koji su na dnevnom redu ovog zasjedanja. U Godinjem izvjeu Hrvatske narodne banke za 1998. godinu, koje je Saboru dostavljeno u lipnju prole godine, kao i u ostalim materijalima, iscrpno su iznijeti pokazatelji o novanoj politici, gospodarskim kretanjima i stanju u bankarstvu. Kako je od pisanja izvjea do ove rasprave u Hrvatskom dravnom saboru proteklo otprilike godinu dana, ograniit u se samo na neke, najvanije teme, oslanjajui se pritom i na najnovije pokazatelje i saznanja. Nema prijepora da banke u financijskom sustavu nae zemlje imaju sredinju ulogu. Stoga u dananjem izlaganju elim najprije neto vie rei o bankovnom sustavu, a u drugom bih se dijelu osvrnuo na monetarnu politiku i time bih obuhvatio dvije najvanije zadae HNB-a. 1. Bankovni sustav Valja podsjetiti ovaj visoki dom da nismo jedina zemlja suoena s visokim trokovima bankarstva u tranziciji. Gotovo sve tranzicijske zemlje prole su kroz dvije bankovne krize:  prvu krizu tzv. starih banaka s naslijeem (loom aktivom) iz prolog ekonomskog sustava  drugu krizu dijela banaka osnovanih nakon promjene ekonomskog sustava koje nisu uspjele opstati zbog slabog upravljanja i/ili jaanja konkurencije na tritu s napretkom tranzicije. Prva je bankovna kriza, kriza tzv. starih banaka, zapoela s poetkom procesa tranzicije (pa i prije toga), a upravo zavrava prodajom rehabilitiranih dravnih banaka stranim stratekim ulagaima. U trokove te krize, izazvane naslijeem prolosti i, djelomino, golemim posljedicama rata na koje se preesto zaboravlja, ubrajam:  izdavanje tzv. velikih obveznica 1991. godine u iznosu od oko 990 milijuna amerikih dolara,  pretvaranje devizne tednje u javni dug 1992. godine u iznosu od oko 3.190 milijuna amerikih dolara i  sanaciju Slavonske, Splitske, Rijeke i Privredne banke Zagreb, u razdoblju od 1995. do 1996. godine, u ukupnom iznosu od oko 473 milijuna amerikih dolara. Ukupno, trokove tzv. prve bankovne krize moemo procijeniti na oko 4.653 milijuna amerikih dolara. Toan je iznos troka prve bankovne krize teko utvrditi jer u navedenim procjenama ne treba zaboraviti prihode, tj. stavke koje ukupan troak umanjuju, a to su, primjerice, prihodi od privatizacije banaka, te plae, dobit i porezne prihode to ih sanirane banke ne bi ostvarile, odnosno uplatile, da su propale. Nema sumnje da su ti trokovi vrlo visoki i svrstavaju Hrvatsku meu zemlje s najviim trokovima rjeavanja bankarske krize u omjeru prema bruto domaem proizvodu (BDP-u), to je vie puta detaljnije analizirano i isticano u radovima HNB-a, kao i u javnim istupima djelatnika sredinje banke. Tako visoki trokovi tipini su za zemlje zahvaene ratom, poput Kuvajta (45%) i Izraela (25%) u jednom dijelu njihove povijesti. Poetkom 1998. godine nastupila je u Hrvatskoj druga bankovna kriza, u kojoj je tadanja Vlada Republike Hrvatske donijela odluku o sanaciji Dubrovake i Croatia banke. Trokovi tih dviju sanacija mogu se procijeniti na 347 milijuna amerikih dolara, pri emu dakako valja oekivati prihode od, nadam se, skore privatizacije tih banaka. Drugi izraz te krize su trokovi isplate osigurane tednje u bankama nad kojima je otvoren steajni postupak. Podsjeam daje u 1998. i 1999. godini Hrvatska narodna banka zatraila pokretanje steajeva za 9 banaka i 4 tedionice. Uz to, u 2000. godini HNB je zatraio otvaranje steajeva nad jo 3 banke i jednom tedionicom i ukinuo odobrenje za rad jednoj podrunici strane banke, jednoj banci i 6 tedionica. Troak isplate osigurane tednje kod banaka i tedionica nad kojima je ve otvoren steajni postupak moe se procijeniti na oko 400 milijuna amerikih dolara. Opet se radi o procjeni. Ako i kada predloeni steajevi budu pokrenuti, to bi moglo poveati trokove za dodatnih 50-ak milijuna amerikih dolara. Dakle, ukupni bi se trokovi druge bankovne krize mogli procijeniti na oko 800 milijuna amerikih dolara. Zbrojimo li trokove prve i druge krize (uz ponovljenu ogradu da se radi o bruto trokovima i okvirnim iznosima), dolazimo do iznosa od oko 5,45 milijardi amerikih dolara. Od toga na prvu bankovnu krizu otpada oko 85 posto, a na drugu oko 15 posto troka. Prva je bankovna kriza bila dakle mnogo vea i opasnija za cjelokupni gospodarski sustav nego kriza iz 1998. godine. elim naglasiti da je ta kriza svojim najveim dijelom iza nas. Ovdje se neu osvrtati na uzroke prve bankovne krize jer vjerujem da su socijalistiko naslijee i posljedice rata dobro poznati iroj javnosti. Dodue, nije poznato da smo u samostalnost 1990. godine krenuli s negativnim kapitalom svih banaka i to od 2 mlrd US $. Neto vie u rei o uzrocima druge bankovne krize. Koji su, po mojoj procjeni, njezini glavni uzroci? Prvo i najvanije, druga je bankovna kriza poela mnogo prije 1998. godine, pa ak i prije nego sam ja imenovan guvernerom. Ona je poela previe irokogrudnim davanjem odobrenja za rad banaka u prvoj polovici devedesetih godina. Oprez je izostao i u pogledu broja banaka, i u pogledu ljudi koji su postavljani na rukovodea mjesta u bankama. Meutim, valja podsjetiti da tada Zakon i nije traio tzv. prethodnu suglasnost sredinje banke pri imenovanju rukovodeih ljudi, odnosno uprava banaka, ve samo neobvezujue miljenje. U asu kad sam izabran za guvernera, u oujku 1996., ve je bilo izdano 55 odobrenja za rad banaka. Prevelik broj banaka i/ili loe uprave i nadzorni odbori u dijelu banaka koje su namjerno krile ne samo propise ve i sva naela zdravoga bankarskog poslovanja doveli su za nekoliko godina dio banaka u bezizlaznu situaciju. Ono to bi trebalo biti oito, no izgleda da treba stalno ponavljati, jest jednostavna injenica da su za loe poslovanje propalih banaka odgovorni prije svih oni koji su tim bankama upravljali - znai njihove uprave i nadzorni odbori. Nije HNB donosio loe poslovne odluke, odnosno plasirao sredstva tako da se ne mogu vratiti, ve uprave banaka. I ne slui nadzor banaka tomu unaprijed da sprijei lo plasman, ve da ga uoi i sankcionira. Dopustite mi istaknuti daje u samoj biti trinoga gospodarstva da svaki pojedini subjekt za sebe donosi poslovne odluke i, a to je kljuno, snosi za te odluke sve posljedice, ukljuujui i mogue otvaranje steaja. HNB ne moe i ne smije upravljati poslovnim bankama, osim kada situacija ve postane tako ozbiljna daje potrebno imenovati privremenog upravitelja kako bi se zatitili vjerovnici (znai i tedie) banke, a i to je omogueno tek novim Zakonom o bankama s kraja 1998. godine. Valja znati da niti jedna nadzorna institucija ne moe unaprijed kontrolirati svaku pojedinu transakciju u poslovnoj banci. U samoj je biti trita rizik, pa ni svaka poslovna odluka, ma kako dobronamjerna bila, ne mora poluiti uspjeh. tovie, ve sam esto isticao da gotovo i nema zemlje na svijetu koja nije bila u posljednjih petnaestak godina suoena s bankarskom krizom, od SAD-a do vedske, od Finske do Japana, od Estonije i Latvije do eke i Maarske. Jo jednom moram javno rei da su apsurdni postupci pojedinih lanova uprava banaka i nadzornih odbora koji prozivaju HNB za loe poslovanje banaka kojima su oni upravljali ili koje su nadzirali. To je slino kao kada bi direktor nekog poduzea prozvao financijsku policiju da je odgovorna za to to je on loe upravljao poduzeem ili to se uputao u zakonom zabranjene aktivnosti. Ili kada bi voza, nakon to gaje zaustavio prometni policajac, policajca optuio za to to je on prebrzo vozio. Moram rei da je upravo nevjerojatno da se takve logike bravure mogu izdana u dan i iz sluaja u sluaj plasirati javnosti. A pravim vrhuncem apsurda smatram pozive nekih politiara i poslovnih ljudi da se pod pritiskom takve vrste optuaba smijeni guverner Hrvatske narodne banke. Drugo, HNB je veinu svojih funkcija poeo graditi s osamostaljenjem Hrvatske praktino od nitice. Poetkom devedesetih Sektora nadzora i kontrole osposobljenog za djelotvoran nadzor banaka u suvremenom smislu i nije bilo. I kada sam preuzeo dunost guvernera u oujku 1996. godine, taj je sektor, iako ve znatno bolje ekipiran, bio oito nedovoljno spreman da se nosi s problemima vrlo brzo rastueg, ali ve nabujaloga tranzicijskog bankarskog sustava s gotovo 60 banaka i dvadesetak tedionica. Poznato je da ne postoji nain da se u kratkom vremenu stvori visokoosposobljen i djelotvoran sustav nadzora i kontrole. Za to su potrebne godine obrazovanja, rada i stjecanja iskustva. Tree, objektivna prepreka uinkovitijem sustavu nadzora banaka bio je tadanji Zakon o bankama i tedionicama koji nije u dovoljnoj mjeri omoguavao aktivnu ulogu HNB-a. Nama je tek novi Zakon od konca 1998. godine omoguio bri i efikasniji utjecaj na banke. Stoga smo tek tada mogli poduzeti djelotvornije mjere prema bankama, u kojima smo i ranije uoavali naznake problema. Upravo je na inzistiranje HNB-a prethodna Vlada predloila takav zakon koji nam je dao potrebne ovlasti. etvrto, ono to zacijelo nije pomagalo sredinjoj banci u nadzoru bankarskih institucija, barem od kada sam ja na elu te institucije, bila je politika klima u kojoj je bankovni sustav rastao, a to je politika klima, koje se recidivi mogu jasno vidjeti posljednjih dana. iroj javnosti sigurno nije poznato da se u veini razvijenih zemalja najvei dio supervizijskog posla sredinje banke obavlja posredstvom tzv. moralnog uvjeravanja. U velikoj veini sluajeva to je dovoljno da banka promijeni svoje ponaanje. Kod nas to, naalost, nije bio sluaj, dijelom zbog toga to su pojedine uprave banaka namjerno krile propise iz vlastitih interesa, a dijelom zbog toga to je stvarana klima politike "zatienosti" pojedinih uprava. Moram, takoer podsjetiti zastupnike da sam na to upozorio u svom obraanju ovom asnom domu 4. lipnja 1998. Tada sam rekao: Zalaem se za to da se eliminira utjecaj bilo kakve politike na banke i da one samo na temelju strunih bankarskih odluka plasiraju sredstva. Banke ne smiju biti ni socijalne ustanove, ni lokalni razvojni fondovi, ve poslovne ustanove. Stoga ostavimo upravljanje bankama bankarima, jer je to sloen i visokostruan posao. Isto tako nemojmo svi mi upasti u zamku politikanskog stvaranja nepovjerenja u banke jer za to nema osnova. Samo tako banke mogu sauvati novac koji im je povjeren i samo se tako moe ouvati stabilnost ukupnoga financijskog sustava, a to je osnovica gospodarskog napretka. Taj apel, naalost, i nakon dvije godine, mogu samo ponoviti. Prethodno navedena etiri razloga glavni su uzroci onoga to danas u Hrvatskoj nazivamo drugom bankovnom krizom. Da li je HNB mogao sprijeiti drugu bankovnu krizu? Ne. Najvie to se u opisanoj situaciji moda moglo uiniti jest to da se dio banaka koje su propale mogao zatvoriti neto prije. Siguran sam, meutim, da bi u tom sluaju napad na HNB, i javni i politiki, bio jo jai, uz tvrdnje kako je upravo HNB unitio banke koje su inae bile dobre. estokim smo napadima, uostalom, neprekidno izloeni ve dvije i pol godine. Oni koji misle da je krizu dijela bankovnog sustava bilo mogue sasvim izbjei u situaciji u kojoj sam doao na ovu dunost, naalost, nisu u pravu. Od odgovornosti za konsolidaciju bankovnog sustava nisam bjeao nikada, pa ne bjeim ni danas. Netko je eliminiranje loih banaka s trita morao provesti jer su problemi bili tu. Ono to je u tom poslu bio glavni cilj, to smo postigli: izbjegli smo sistemsku krizu hrvatskog bankarstva, koja je mogla biti, da nije izbjegnuta, mnogo skuplja od oko 800 milijuna dolara koliko sada iznosi troak druge bankovne kriza. Sigurno je da je na tom putu bilo stvari koje smo mogli uiniti bolje, to je danas s povijesnom odmakom lake uoiti. No isto sam tako uvjeren da bi iznos druge bankovne krize bio mnogo vei da smo se rukovodili mnogim savjetima i postupcima koje su nam sugerirali kritiari politike koju smo, uza sva ogranienja koja sam prije spomenuo, prema bankarskom sektoru vodili. Ponavljam, a to nije ocjena samo HNB-a, ve i neovisnih stranih analitiara, temeljnu je zadau HNB ispunio: sprijeio je da kriza poprimi sistemske razmjere, a time prouzroi i znatno vee trokove. Danas, stojei pred ovim asnim domom, mogu odgovorno rei da posao sreivanja stanja u hrvatskom bankovnom sustavu uspjeno tee i da poinjemo ubirati i prve plodove konsolidacije, koja se nastavlja. Situacija u hrvatskom bankarstvu je mnogo bolja nego u protekle dvije godine, a posebice prije 5 ili 10 godina. Poboljanje je mogue vidjeti po rezultatima banaka i po tome to su kamatne stope na bankarskom tritu poele postupno padati, prije ikakvih poteza monetarne politike. Danas su kamatne stope prepolovljene u usporedbi s razdobljem s poetka moga mandata. To je znak da je restrukturiranje u bankovnom sektoru konano urodilo poveanjem efikasnosti. Moram rei da smo u HNB-u vrlo zadovoljni time i vidimo dobru perspektivu cijeloga naeg bankarskog sustava u godinama koje dolaze: vidimo daljnje poveanje efikasnosti, pad kamatnih stopa, smanjenje kreditnog rizika i, kao posljedicu, puno stabilniji bankarski sustav. Nakon, elim vjerovati, brze privatizacije Rijeke i Splitske banke, strani e strateki ulagai na hrvatskom bankarskom tritu biti ak prisutniji nego u Maarskoj, ije se bankarsko trite smatra najefikasnijim meu tranzicijskim zemljama Srednje i Istone Europe. To je jamstvo stabilnosti domaega bankarskog sustava u budunosti i neto to moe djelovati smirujue na tedie nakon konsolidacijskih problema kroz koje je proao na bankovni sustav u protekle dvije godine. Koncem 1998. godine ovaj je visoki dom izglasao novi Zakon o bankama, koji HNB-u omoguuje mnogo bre i uinkovitije djelovanje, a time i smanjenje trokova bankarskih tekoa u budunosti. Sektor nadzora i kontrole, iako jo uvijek "u nastajanju, danas je na priblino istoj razini kao u drugim naprednim tranzicijskim zemljama s kojima se moramo usporeivati. Sposoban je nositi se s trenutanom situacijom u bankovnom sustavu. elim ponoviti da se ponosim pomacima koji su u tom dijelu uinjeni u posljednjih nekoliko godina. Sve je to, potovane dame i gospodo zastupnici, uinjeno u nimalo lakim institucionalnim i gospodarskim uvjetima, sa zateenim stanjem koje sam opisao na poetku i u ambijentu stalnih pritisaka interesnih skupina koje su usmjeravale i usmjeravaju panju javnosti prema HNB-u, ne bi li skrile vlastitu objektivnu odgovornost za stanje u pojedinim bankama i tedionicama. Posebno istiem da u iluziji ive oni koji smatraju da je sama Hrvatska narodna banka mogla svojim radom nadomjestiti godinama gomilanu financijsku nedisciplinu, daje mogla sprijeiti korupciju i privredni kriminal, da je mogla ispraviti pogreke u privatizaciji, daje mogla supstiturati nejasne zakone i sporost pravosua te rad loih revizora, daje mogla nadomjestiti nepostojanje posebne institucije koja bi se bavila financijskim prijevarama najsloenijeg oblika, daje mogla zamijeniti neadekvatan rad nadzornih odbora u bankama i, konano, rad onih koji su odluke o plasmanima sredstava donosili - uprava banaka. Na sve to smo godinama javno upozoravali. Ovime ne elim pobjei od svoga dijela odgovornosti. Jedino elim neka se pravedno vagne uloga svih institucija u Hrvatskoj u proteklom razdoblju u izgradnji financijske discipline i pravne drave. Budite objektivni, traite od Hrvatske narodne banke i guvernera puno, ali ne oekujte nemogue. Ono to ne mogu prihvatiti jest da se bez argumenata i objektivne ocjene struke o tome to nadzor nad bankama moe, a to ne moe, nastoji sakriti prave uzroke problema i tekoa u naem bankarstvu, pa i u ukupnom gospodarstvu. Da li takva stajalita pridonose rjeavanju stvarnih uzroka tekoa? 2. Monetarna politika Drugi dio svoga izlaganja, znatno krai, posvetio bih provoenju monetarne politike. Njezin je temeljni cilj stabilnost teaja i cijena. Tijekom posljednjih godina imali smo izuzetno dobre rezultate u ouvanju cjenovne i teajne stabilnosti. Prosjena stopa inflacije u posljednjem je srednjoronom razdoblju u Hrvatskoj bila nia nego i u jednoj drugoj tranzicijskoj zemlji. Budimo na to ponosni. Moram naglasiti kako je to ostvareno u situaciji u kojoj nismo fiksirali teaj, ve smo ga putali da se prilagouje promjenama ekonomskih fundamenata, ali tako da ne ugrozi stabilnost. HNB ve godinama odbacuje ideje o devalvaciji kao rjeenju problema gospodarstva. Uz ideju devalvacije, u posljednje se vrijeme javila ideja eurizacije, odnosno potpune zamjene kune eurom kao iskljuivim zakonitim sredstvom plaanja u Hrvatskoj. Ne ulazei ovdje u podrobniju raspravu o razlozima za i protiv eurizacije, valja jasno rei kako nikakav teajni reim ne moe nadoknaditi ili zamijeniti strukturne promjene. Sa ili bezeura, valja nam raditi vie, bolje i efikasnije. U tim bih okolnostima rekao nekoliko rijei i o tome kako mi u HNB-u vidimo monetarnu politiku ove godine. Ispravna kombinacija makroekonomske politike ne znai - kao to je bio sluaj u znaajnom dijelu tranzicijskih zemalja, a i u Hrvatskoj - kombinaciju restriktivne monetarne i ekspanzivne fiskalne politike, ve uravnoteeniju kombinaciju tih dviju poluga makroekonomske politike. Ovogodinji proraun na tragu je onoga za to smo mi iz HNB-a pledirali posljednjih nekoliko godina, znai za ograniavanje rasta javne potronje i za uvoenje reda u dravne financije, tj. za podmirivanje dravnih obveza na vrijeme, o dospijeu. Time je HNB dobio vie manevarskog prostora za voenje monetarne politike. Kamatne su stope u Hrvatskoj danas visoke, posebice u usporedbi s kamatnim stopama u razvijenim zemljama. No, vrijedi podsjetiti da je u oujku 1996. godine kamata na prekononom tritu iznosila gotovo 30 posto, da su aktivne kamate poslovnih banaka iznosile oko 25 posto, a danas su one prekonone gotovo jednoznamenkaste, a aktivne su kamate banaka tono upola manje nego prije etiri godine. elio bih, meutim, ponovno naglasiti da monetarna politika nije glavna determinanta visine kamatnih stopa na hrvatskom tritu. Visina kamatnih stopa, kako to ponavljamo iz godine u godinu, rezultat je brojnih strukturnih faktora poput: mikroekonomske efikasnosti banaka, tj. njihova restrukturiranja i smanjenja trokova, strukture bankovnog trita koje je segmentirano, uinkovitosti pravosudnog sustava u zatiti vjerovnika itd. Pratei brojne napise o gospodarskim problemima, uoio sam u posljednje vrijeme neto to me osobito zabrinjava, a to je nuenje naoko lakih i brzih rjeenja za sloene i duboke probleme hrvatskog gospodarstva. Najee se nudi promjena monetarne politike u smjeru njezine znatno vee ekspanzivnosti. Logika takvih razmiljanja jest da e vea ponuda novca smanjiti kamate, rijeiti problem "nelikvidnosti (koji je u svojoj biti problem insolventnosti i financijske nediscipline), poveati investicije, poveati rast, smanjiti vrijednost "precijenjene kune i time potaknuti izvoz, a zahvaljujui svemu tome rijeit e se i pitanje vrlo velike nezaposlenosti i, naravno, osigurati standard kakav svi graani ove zemlje opravdano ele. Dame i gospodo, koje li sree da su rjeenja tako laka. Pa kada bi se problemi u realnoj sferi, u funkcioniranju pravne drave, u strukturi naeg izvoza, u visokoj nezaposlenosti itd. mogli rjeavati tiskanjem novca, zato bismo se onda, javno pitam, muili sa smanjenjem trokova, efikasnou, konkurentskom borbom i slino? Zato onda Europa, na koju se stalno pozivamo i kojoj teimo, ne primjenjuje takva rjeenja, ve intenzivno radi na novoj ekonomiji XXI. stoljea, poveanju znanja, irenju preko Interneta, novim tehnologijama i restrukturiranju? Monetarna je politika moan instrument, posebice u odranju stabilnosti cijena. Zato joj nemojmo davati zadatke koje ne moe obaviti na zadovoljavajui nain. Jer, zloporaba monetarne politike dovodi do inflacije, koja je, ponavljam, nita drugo nego pljaka, i to pljaka upravo onih najsiromanijih. 3. Zakljuno Ponovo naglaavam, nema brzih i lakih rjeenja. HNB treba initi sljedee: Prvo, ouvati stabilnost teaja i cijena. Drugo, nastaviti strukturne promjene u bankarskom sektoru dovretkom privatizacije rehabilitiranih dravnih banaka i konsolidacije ostaloga dijela sektora. Tree, nastaviti intenzivno jaati funkciju nadzora nad bankama. etvrto, u uvjetima koje je stvorila nova fiskalna politika nastojati smanjiti stopu obvezne rezerve koliko to doputa postizanje glavnih ciljeva. Peto, unaprijediti regulativu, ukljuujui i zakon o sredinjoj banci koji treba modernizirati u skladu s europskim standardima. esto, nastaviti i okonati promjene u sustavu platnog prometa. Sedmo, uvati i dalje poveavati meunarodne priuve, koje su i u proteklim godinama odigrale vanu ulogu jamca stabilnosti. Posebno je vano ubrzati isplatu osigurane tednje, to je odgovornost Vlade, a to e izravno utjecati na povjerenje u hrvatski financijski sustav. Neovisnost Hrvatske narodne banke u budunosti, ne smije znaiti i njezinu osamljenost. Ona svoje ciljeve moe u potpunosti postii samo u suradnji s drugima. Provedba ciljeva HNB-a ovisi, naime, izmeu ostalog i o: prvo, institucionalnim uvjetima, poput funkcioniranja hrvatskog pravosua; drugo, o postojanju barem priblinog konsenzusa o optimalnoj kombinaciji monetarne i fiskalne politike; tree, o jaanju svih institucija koje su nune za ravnopravnu trinu utakmicu, uz poseban naglasak na jaanje financijske discipline i institucionalno sankcioniranje korupcije; etvrto, o privlaenju stranih izravnih investicija i ulasku u trgovake i ekonomske asocijacije (WTO, CEFTA, OECD, EU); peto, o stabilnom politikom okruenju i jo veoj otvorenost prema svijetu, jer taj put jednostavno nema alternative. Provedba navedenih ciljeva svakako uvelike ovisi i o stupnju podrke javnosti. Jer, bez jasne i nedvojbene podrke najire javnosti zdravim politikama i zadacima koje sam spomenuo, oni se sigurno nee moi provesti. Posebno vas molim, dame i gospodo zastupnici, iskoristimo zajedno ovu najvaniju govornicu u Hrvatskoj za to da hrvatskim tediama i hrvatskoj javnosti uputimo poruku daje hrvatsko bankarstvo danas stabilnije nego to je bilo prije dvije godine i puno stabilnije nego prije pet godina. Tekoe na koje smo nailazili i na koje emo jamano nailaziti sigurno ne smiju biti razlog odustajanja od cilja. Naprotiv, one moraju biti dodatni motiv da u tome ustrajemo, i to ponajprije radi nas, nae djece i radi njihove djece. Dame i gospodo zastupnici, pozivam na mirnu, strunu i argumentiranu raspravu o stanju u bankovnom sustavu i radu sredinje banke na mjestu na kojem se ta rasprava treba voditi, u ovom visokom domu. Monetarna politika i stabilnost bankovnog sustava previe su ozbiljne stvari da bi se prosudbe o njima mogle donijeti bez jedne takve rasprave. Pokuajmo nadii umjetno stvoreni ambijent u kojem se sredinju banku i njezina guvernera, sjedne strane, optuuje da je pomagala takozvanim tajkunima, a, s druge je strane, ti isti tajkuni ele postaviti na optueniku klupu kao uzrok njihova kraha. Budimo iznad paualnih ocjena koje, sjedne strane, sugeriraju da je vrsta monetarna politika sruila prethodnu Vladu, dok se, s druge strane, sugerira da je ta ista politika bila prema toj Vladi poslunika. S jedne nas strane optuuju da predugo putamo na miru uprave problematinih banaka, dok s druge strane govore da ishitreno poduzimamo mjere ne doputajui im da same pronau izlaz iz tekoa. A i kad je rije o najnovijoj lavini napada zbog upuivanja privremenog upravitelja u Istarsku banku, neka se konano kae je li pritom ita bilo protivno vaeim zakonima ove zemlje. Odgovorimo danas na pitanje: kakva je stvarno ta politika? Javnost ima pravo dobiti ozbiljan odgovor na to pitanje. Iza hrvatske sredinje banke tijekom protekle etiri godine mog guvernerskog mandata stoji etiri godine stabilnosti cijena i teaja, povijesni maksimum meunarodnih priuva, sauvana meunarodna likvidnost zemlje, doprinos investicijskom rejtingu Hrvatske kod najvanijih svjetskih agencija i teka konsolidacija bankovnog sustava u kojoj je izbjegnuta sistemska kriza, a to je dovelo do upola niih kamatnih stopa nego na poetku moga mandata. Upravo zbog toga, ostavku ne mogu podnijeti dok se javnosti, Savjetu Hrvatske narodne banke, njezinim djelatnicima i meni osobno jasno ne kae to je to u naem dosadanjom radu imalo veu teinu od pobrojanih injenica. Za takvu raspravu o izvjeima Hrvatske narodne banke stojim vam danas ovdje na raspolaganju.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation at the opening of the exhibition "Kuna  25 years of the monetary unit of the Republic of Croatia" in the Archaeological Museum in Zagreb, May 30, 2019.
text: Presentation by the Governor of the Croatian National Bank Boris Vuj?i? at the opening of the exhibition "Kuna - 25 years of the monetary unit of the Republic of Croatia" at the Archaeological Museum in Zagreb, 30 May 2019. Published: 31.5.2019. Type Speech Speaker Prof. Dr. Boris Vuj?i?, CNB Governor Event Exhibit at the opening of the exhibition "Kuna - 25 years of the monetary unit of the Republic of Croatia" at the Archaeological Museum in Zagreb Archaeological Museum site in Zagreb events Date 30.5.2019. events Respected on this occasion, I sincerely thank all those who participated in the project of establishing the Croatian currency a quarter of a century ago; we are glad that many of them are still here today, with us, so that together with the entire Croatian public we can mark this significancen date. I am especially pleased that today, when we are marking a quarter of a century of the introduction of the kuna, I will present a commemorative edition of the circulation coin of 25 kuna. 25 kuna for the 25th birthday of the kuna. The success of this edition is, I would say, guaranteed, given the order to buy these coins in front of the CNB from early morning. But let's go back a moment. On May 30, 1994, he marked not only a new era, the entry into the croatian currency scene and thus the strengthening of Croatian statehood, but at the same time he was also the crowning achievementof the excitation of the dubious preparations that created the preconditions that the temporary money, the Croatian dinar, which was released into circulation on December 23, 1991, could be replaced by a kuna. The political battle began in the early 1990s when the NBJ became a voting machine in which decisions were made, no longer by consensus, but by imposing the interests of Serbia, Vojvodina, Kosovo and Montenegro with the decisive, fifth vote of the NBJ governor himself to the other members of the monetary union. It was a time of frequent intrusions by Serbia into the common monetary system and the unauthorised creation of a common currency, used to cover its deficits and finance preparations for aggression. The abuse and decommissioning of the monetary system culminated in the decision of the NBJ Board of Governors to expel Croatia and Slovenia fromthe primary money show trials in the summer of 1991. This was intended to bring the Croatian and Slovenian financial systems to its knees with all the wider consequences on their economies. The emerging response of the Croatian state has been swift and effective. InMay 1990, the first multiparty Sab or appointed Prof. Dr. Ante ?i?in-8aain as governor of the National Bank of Croatia. The new management has set its goal: accelerated work on the design of a new monetary model, on the independence of monetary policy and on the introduction of the Croatian waveof ute. In August 1991, President Tudjman established a Commission for the preparation of the concept of the monetary system and the production of banknotes of the Republic of Croatia. The President of the Commission was Dr. Marijan Han9eekovi?, and the commission was attended by representatives of the Croatian National Bank led by the Governor and experts from various fields as well as representatives of the Government and parliament. The invitation competition for the appearance of banknotes opens in April 1992, and at the end of October the execution of the procedure for the selection of the art solution. In the next six months it was defined withall the essential characteristics of the banknotes and in March 1993 an international tender for the printing of kuna banknotes was carried out. In March 1993, the opening and invitational competition for the development of an art solution for coins, and at the same time preparations for the organization of the mint nsheep in Zagreb, which in January 1994 officially began with the discovery of kuna and linden coins, so this year we are also marking a quarter of a century of business of the Croatian Monetary Institute. In addition to the aforementioned technical preparations, it was necessary to end high inflation expectations. Inflation, in fact, has become so high that it has been devastating for the economy. Work was launched on the stabilisation programme and in October 1993 the programme was activated. Until its introduction, average monthly inflation in 1993 was 1.5%. was 28 percent per month! The programme was successful and quickly broke inflation expectations. Inflation was defeated and the introduction of the Croatian kuna could finally be started. The logistical preparation of the introduction of the kuna and the replacement of the Croatian dinar was carried out by theDirectorate of the Vault of the Croatian National Bank. In wartime conditions, on the territory that was partially occupied, partially isolated, it was necessary to organize in the short term safely at the grip of finished banknotes, it was HRK 92.7 billion in quantitiesand of 622 million pieces weighing almost 1200 tons, and to provide assumptions for the exchange of money. Taking into account the time and war circumstances in which the introduction of the kuna was carried out, as well as the fact that the exchange of money is an extremely important event for each state and its monetary system, it is clear that this was one of the most complex projects of the Croatian National Bank, in which numerous institutions and individuals outside the central bank also participated. Therefore, even today we are proud that this complex task, despite the difficult conditionsand, was done impeccably and we are sincerely grateful to all the participants who invested their knowledge, effort and energy in the introduction of the mink, then as well as after the reintegration of the occupied territories. Institutional memory tells us that at the very beginning of this journey , the Croatian central bank clearly represented and positioned the need for Croatia to simultaneously adopt, in addition to building its own monetary system, the principled commitment to enter into integration processes as soon as possible, and finally into the monetary union with other European countries, in order to pursue its own social and economic interests. What I'm saying is that the idea of monetary integration is not new in Croatia, it was not invented yesterday. It has been repeated since the beginning of monetary sovereignty, through negotiations to join the EU, to this day. It'sbottom we've finally got into a situation where it can come true. Unlike previous currencies, the kuna was and remains stable from the beginning. A currency that does not lose value; today it is a currency fully covered (predominantly) by the Euro internationalreserves. It may seem to someone that 25 years is not much, but in monetary history it is certainly not small. To illustrate: our kuna is the longest-lasting in design and denominations in this area since the beginning of the twentieth century, that is, since the abandonment of gold money. For slow education, in Europe the longest-running was the German brand (the so-called third series) with "eagles", which in design and denominations was unchanged in use from 1960 to 1995. Very popular in these parts, too. Ernest Hemingway, of all, interestingly, just him, onewell noticed that the panacea of all poorly run states is money printing, or, worse, war. Both give the people a temporary sense of success, both lead to lasting damage, and both are usually a haven of economic and political opportunisthat. We can be proud that in the imposed war we managed and won and during the war introduced a currency, the stability of which we have maintained to this day and whose stability we will maintain until the introduction of the euro, at the same time not subject to - and neither will this be the case in the future - economic or political opportunism. Therefore, we are proud of the successful history of the kuna, but we do not want to run away from responsibility for tomorrow. Just as we don't want a future that cuts ties with the past. And that is why happy birthday swears, because it already is, and always will remain, an important symbol of the security and independence of the Croatian state, but also a bridge on its journey into the future. a9
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera Hrvatske narodne banke Borisa Vujia na otvorenju izlobe "Kuna - 25 godina novane jedinice Republike Hrvatske" u Arheolokom muzeju u Zagrebu, 30. svibnja 2019. Objavljeno: 31.5.2019. Vrsta Govor Govornik Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a Dogaanje Izlaganje na otvorenju izlobe "Kuna - 25 godina novane jedinice Republike Hrvatske" u Arheolokom muzeju u Zagrebu Mjesto Arheoloki muzej u Zagrebu dogaanja Datum 30.5.2019. dogaanja Potovani, u ovoj prilici iskreno zahvaljujem svima koji su sudjelovali u projektu uspostave hrvatske valute prije etvrt stoljea; drago nam je da su mnogi od njih i danas ovdje, s nama, kako bismo zajedniki s cjelokupnom hrvatskom javnou obiljeili ovaj znaajan datum. Posebno mi je zadovoljstvo da danas, kada obiljeavamo etvrt stoljea uvoenja kune, predstavim i prigodno izdanje optjecajnoga kovanog novca od 25 kuna. 25 kuna za 25. roendan kune. Uspjeh ovog izdanja je, rekao bih, zagarantiran, s obzirom na red za kupovinu ovih kovanica pred HNB-om ve od ranog jutra. No, vratimo se za trenutak u prolost. 30. svibnja 1994. nije oznaio samo novu eru, stupanje na scenu hrvatske valute i time osnaivanje hrvatske dravnosti, ve je istovremeno bio i kruna uzbudljivih priprema koje su stvorile preduvjete da bi privremeni novac, hrvatski dinar, koji je u optjecaj puten 23. prosinca 1991., mogao biti zamijenjen kunom. Politika bitka poela je ranih devedesetih kada je NBJ postala glasaki stroj u kojem su odluke bile donoene, ne vie konsenzusom, nego nametanjem interesa Srbije, Vojvodine, Kosova i Crne Gore uz odluujui, peti glas samog guvernera NBJ-a ostalim lanicama monetarne unije. Bilo je to vrijeme uestalih upada Srbije u zajedniki monetarni sustav i neovlatenog kreiranja zajednike valute, koritenog za pokrivanje njezinih deficita i financiranje priprema za agresiju. Zloporaba i razgradnja monetarnog sustava kulminirala je odlukom Savjeta guvernera NBJ-a o izbacivanju Hrvatske i Slovenije iz sudjelovanja u emisiji primarnog novca u ljeto 1991. Time se hrvatski i slovenski financijski sustav htjelo baciti na koljena sa svim irim posljedicama na njihova gospodarstva. Odgovor hrvatske drave u nastajanju bio je brz i efikasan. Prvi je viestranaki Sabor u svibnju 1990. na dunost guvernera Narodne banke Hrvatske imenovao prof. dr. Antu iin-aina. Novo je rukovodstvo postavilo svoj cilj: ubrzan rad na osmiljavanju novoga monetarnog modela, na osamostaljenju novane politike i na uvoenju hrvatske valute. U kolovozu 1991. predsjednik Tuman osnovao je Komisiju za pripremu koncepcije monetarnog sustava i izradu novanica RH. Predsjednik Komisije bio je dr. Marijan Hanekovi, a u radu Komisije sudjelovali su predstavnici Hrvatske narodne banke predvoeni guvernerom te strunjaci iz raznih podruja kao i predstavnici Vlade i Sabora. Pozivni natjeaj za izgled novanica otvorenje u travnju 1992., a krajem listopada izvrenje postupak odabira likovnog rjeenja. U sljedeih est mjeseci definirana su sva bitna obiljeja novanica te je u oujku 1993. proveden meunarodni natjeaj za tiskanje novanica kuna. U oujku 1993. otvorenje i pozivni natjeaj za izradu likovnog rjeenja za kovani novac, a istovremeno su zapoete i pripreme za ustroj kovnice novca u Zagrebu, koja je u sijenju 1994. slubeno zapoela s otkovom kovanog novca kuna i lipa, tako da ove godine ujedno obiljeavamo i etvrt stoljea poslovanja Hrvatskoga novarskog zavoda. Osim spomenutih tehnikih priprema, bilo je nuno i prekinuti visoka inflacijska oekivanja. Inflacija je, naime, postala toliko visoka daje bila razarajua za gospodarstvo. Pokrenut je rad na stabilizacijskom programu i u listopadu 1993. program je aktiviran. Do njegovog uvoenja prosjena mjesena inflacija u 1993. iznosila je 28 posto mjeseno! Program je bio uspjean i vrlo brzo je slomio inflacijska oekivanja. Inflacija je bila pobijeena i konano se moglo krenuti u uvoenje hrvatske kune. Logistiku pripremu uvoenja kune i zamjenu hrvatskog dinara provodila je Direkcija trezora Hrvatske narodne banke. U ratnim uvjetima, na teritoriju koji je bio djelomino okupiran, djelomino prometno izoliran, trebalo je u kratkom roku organizirati siguran pri hvat gotovih novanica, radilo se o 92,7 milijardi kuna u koliini od 622 milijuna komada tekih gotovo 1200 tona, te osigurati pretpostavke za zamjenu novca. Uzimajui u obzir vrijeme i ratne okolnosti u kojima je izvreno uvoenje kune, kao i injenicu daje zamjena novca izuzetno vaan dogaaj za svaku dravu i njezin monetarni sustav, jasno je da je to bio jedan od najsloenijih projekata Hrvatske narodne banke, u kojem su sudjelovale i brojne institucije te pojedinci izvan sredinje banke. Stoga smo i danas ponosni da je ovaj kompleksan zadatak, unato tekim uvjetima, bio obavljen besprijekorno i iskreno smo zahvalni svim sudionicima koji su svoje znanje, trud i energiju uloili u uvoenje kune, tada kao i nakon reintegracije okupiranih podruja. Institucionalno pamenje kazuje nam daje ve na samom poetku tog puta hrvatska sredinja banka jasno zastupala i stavo potrebi da Hrvatska uz izgradnju vlastitoga monetarnog sustava istodobno usvoji i naelno opredjeljenje da radi ostvarivanja vlastitih drutvenih i ekonomskih interesa to prije ue u integracijske procese, a konano i u monetarnu uniju s drugim europskim zemljama. Ono to elim rei je da ideja monetarne integracije nije nova u Hrvatskoj, nije juer izmiljena. Ona se ponavlja od poetka monetarne suverenosti, preko pregovora za ulazak u EU, sve do danas. Jednostavno smo napokon doli u situaciju kada se ona moe ostvariti. Za razliku od prijanjih valuta, kuna je od poetka bila i ostala stabilna. Valuta koja ne gubi na vrijednosti; danas je to valuta potpuno pokrivena (preteno) eurskim meunarodnim priuvama. Nekome se moe uiniti da 25 godina nije puno, no u monetarnoj povijesti sigurno nije malo. Da ilustriram: naa kuna je najdugovjenija po dizajnu i apoenima na ovom podruju od poetka dvadesetog stoljea, odnosno od naputanja zlatnog novca. Za usporedbu, u Europi je najdugovjenija bila njemaka marka (takozvana trea serija) s "orlovima", koja je u dizajnu i apoenima bila nepromijenjena u uporabi od 1960. do 1995. Vrlo popularna i u ovim krajevima. Ernest Hemingway, od svih, zanimljivo, ba on, jednom je dobro primijetio da je panaceja svih loe voenih drava tiskanje novca, ili, jo gore, rat. Jedno i drugo daje narodu privremeni osjeaj uspjeha, jedno i drugo vodi u trajnu tetu, a jedno i drugo je obino utoite ekonomskih i politikih oportunista. Moemo biti ponosni da smo u nametnutom ratu uspjeli i pobijediti i tijekom rata uvesti valutu, iju smo stabilnost odrali do dananjeg dana i iju emo stabilnost zadrati sve do uvoenja eura, istovremeno ne podlijeui - a niti e to biti sluaj u budunosti - ni ekonomskom ni politikom oportunizmu. Ponosni smo, dakle, na uspjenu povijest kune, no ne elimo ni bjeati od odgovornosti za sutranjicu. Kao to ne elimo ni budunost koja e prekinuti veze s prolou. I zato sretan roendan kuni, jer ona ve sada jest, a uvijek e i ostati, vaan simbol sigurnosti i samostalnosti hrvatske drave, ali i most na njezinom putovanju u budunost.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation at the "Period of low interest rates" conference
text: Period of low interest rates Introductory presentation at the interest rate conference organised by Hanza Media and HUB 5 December 2017 What are the reasons for low interest rates? What in the global environment has been conducive to extending the period of low interest rates? What cyclical and what structural factors influence that the period of low interest rates lasts so long? What happens to risk premiums? How can one reverse the trend of low interest rates and return interest rates towards long-term averages? We are witnessing a long period of relatively weak economic activity and stubbornly low inflation that has been going on for almost a decade, since the outbreak of the Great Financial Crisis. Such developments have been responded to by the central banks of the world's largest economies - the US, the euro area and Japan - through extremely accommodative monetary policies, lowering benchmark interest rates to or even below zero levels, as well as quantitative easing and high liquidity creation policies. As a result of these policies, global interest rates remain at historically low levels. Thus, today, 18% of the global economy, weighted by GDP, operates in an environment of negative central bank rates, and this share increases to 40% if countries with rates of zero to 1% are included (Draghi, 2016). However, some of the largest central banks have started gradually raising benchmark interest rates (US Fed) or announcing the imminent start of monetary policy normalisation (ECB). Such a shift in the direction of monetary policies is taking place in an environment of still relatively low inflation rates, they are largely still lower than the declared targets, and are not expected to reach them any time soon. The causes of the turnaround are twofold - on the one hand, the perception prevails that the momentum of the world's largest economies has strengthened sufficiently that it no longer needs monetary stimulus to this extent, while on the other hand, awareness of a number of negative consequences of a long period of extremely low interest rates has strengthened. They create a problem for banks, which, due to lower interest rates, have to turn to non-interest income or to look for riskier investment opportunities. Pension funds can hardly provide adequate returns for future retirees under these conditions. Citizens who receive no or minimal compensation on their deposits are also a problem. Finally, low interest rates can lead to inappropriate risk-taking, which is taken by investors "in search of yield" creating bubbles in individual sectors. When you know that: ... one painting sold for 450 million these days 95 that one bitcoin, which can be worthless tomorrow, the price has increased by 1000% ... it is no wonder that the fear of balloons is increasingly creeping into rational market watchers. Another important issue related to the expected shift in monetary policies concerns the pace and intensity of the growth of benchmark and market interest rates for the world's major currencies. The global recovery was triggered by, not to a small extent, unprecedented monetary measures, which prevented a complete collapse in demand and the collapse of financial markets, and provided (and still provide) adequate liquidity to strengthen the recovery. However, the question remains whether potential economic growth has fallen steadily below pre-crisis levels, and whether secular factors can forever change the economy we are used to before 2008. age. In the professional public, therefore, the view has been strengthened that the new post-crisis "normal" will differ from the pre-crisis one, although its outlines are so far not entirely clear. In this new "normal", interest rates, despite some rise, could also be kept at significantly lower levels than they were before the crisis. This is due to deep, structural changes in the global economy reflected in excess savings relative to investments. Demand for investment funds around the world has been insufficient for a long time to absorb excess global savings. Excess savings compared to profitable investments, i.e. "global savings saturation", global savings glut (Bernanke, 2015) kept interest rates at a very low or even negative level. The explanations for this global imbalance are different and can be roughly grouped into cyclical and structural ones, and future interest rate movements will largely depend on which of these hypotheses proves correct. The first, cyclical causes of low interest rates include post-crisis "balance sheet cleaning" and global deleveraging. As the corporate and household sectors "recover" their balance sheets and deleverage, they are not inclined to borrow further. The financial sector also recovers balance sheets by clearing them of non-performing assets, so there is a stalemate in the transmission mechanism - liquidity has, but banks have no one to place it with. The recovery after the financial crisis can be long, and if it is a so-called "financial crisis". "balance sheet recession" balance sheet recession) recovery may extend for a period of more than ten years. Then the borrowing cycle occurs again and the wheel turns again to the expansion phase of the cycle that Rogoff called the "super debt cycle" (Rogoff, 2015). A hypothesis that emphasizes the meaning of cyclical agents emphasizes that the cycle, whether ordinary or "supercycle", will be reversed at some point, even before countercyclical economic policies are more efficient. In contrast, there are also structural "secular" factors, namely demographic trends, a decline in the (relative) price of investment goods, a possible reduced pace of technological innovation, an increase in the savings rate, scarcity of collateral (safe assets) and an increase in wealth and income inequality. According to this group, the hypothesis of the global financial crisis only further stimulates the fall in interest rates in conditions of already very low equilibrium interest rates. (Ferrero, Gross and Neri, 2017). Of course, the story does not stop there, because the role of accumulating official international reserves, geographical determinants (for example, the impact of integration china into the global economy), as well as the fact that in a globalized world it is easier to equalize yields, which, as I already pointed out at the beginning, are low everywhere today. Demographic trends affect both aggregate demand and aggregate supply. Lower natural gain and longer life expectancy lead to a higher ratio of the older to the younger population. This requires an increase in old age savings unless this trend is reversed by a proportional increase in the retirement age. Demographic trends also affect the demand for investments, because lower population growth implies that a lower rate of investment growth is needed to maintain the given capital-to-work ratio , thereby reducing the real interest rate. An increasing proportion of older people leads to a decrease in the working-age population; in addition to the given level of capital, the increase in the capital/labour ratio or the growth of capital intensity also reduces the real interest rate. On the other hand, with the passage of time, older people can spend their assets, i.e. savings, thereby potentially increasing the pressure towards rising real interest rates (Ferrero, Gross and Neri, 2017). The implications for the conduct of economic and monetary policy vary depending on what is the cause of excess savings in relation to investments. If these are cyclical factors, interest rates will ultimately return to previous levels (although they may remain low for a long period during Rogoff's supercycle). On the other hand, if the influence of these structural factors dominates, which are unaffected by central banks, interest rates could remain low as long as the structural factors that led to their reduction act. But let's go home. In addition to all these global factors, a number of local factors are also affected by the cost of financing in Croatia, such as the intensity of competition and movements in interest margins, the cost of regulation as well as the orientation of monetary policy, as well as the quality of debtors, the value of collateral and others. These factors in Croatia are still fuelling the trend of decreasing bank interest rates, on both loans and deposits. The CNB's expansionary monetary policy and a reduction in regulatory cost by more than 50% have continuously encouraged a drop in interest rates on the domestic market. Given the still short-lived economic recovery and its link to export sector activity, and a slight recovery in lending, this expansionary monetary policy orientation will continue for some time to come. Another important factor is the riskiness of the country. Thanks to the recovery of the domestic economy and the improvement of the fiscal position, Croatia's risk is on a downward trajectory, which has also allowed domestic debtors to have historically low interest rates. To the extent that structural reforms strengthen the economic recovery and fiscal position, this factor, while deepening the domestic investment base, could mitigate the effects of tightening global financial conditions. Also important for the Croatian economy is the finding that euro area Member States, with the same macroeconomic indicators, have a lower borrowing price and a higher credit rating (Kunovac and Pavic, 2017) on average. This is just one of the reasons why we have launched a debate on Croatia's accession to the euro area. The evolution of the cost of borrowing by the state significantly affects the interest on bank loans, so Croatia's accession to the euro area will lead to an additional reduction in interest on borrowing by citizens and businesses. In the end, after a long time, the global economy seems to be slowly emerging from a period of low interest rates. But it is only possible to count some of the factors that could influence the speed and intensity of the rise in global interest rates, but not accurately predict their movements. For Croatia, the smartest thing to do is to pursue policies that will prevent or mitigate the spillover of possible negative trends on the domestic economy. This is the policy of structural reforms necessary to raise productivity growth and continue to reduce public and external debt. Otherwise, what today looks like a healthy recovery of the economy can very well be questioned, and another recession, in the near future, would further deepen social and political issues that threaten populist solutions and are able to perpetuate the crisis much longer than is economically conditional. With that in mind, we must all act. Thank you! Literature Bernanke, B. (2015., 2015-04-01). Why are interest rates so low, part 3: The Global Savings Glut. Title: Presentation in the Croatian Parliament
text: Presentation of CNB Governor Dr. Zeljko Rohatinski in the Croatian Parliament Published: 28.6.2006. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Venue Event Date 28.6.2006. Zagreb 28.6.2006. Mr. President of Parliament, ladies and gentlemen MPs! Let me reflect in a few words on the work of the Croatian National Bank and the current monetary and, more broadly, economic situation in The CroatianTska. At this time six years ago we were faced not only with the long-term consequences of war, the transition crisis, international isolation, but also with the short-term consequences of two economic shocks. The first are the events in Kosovo, their implications on canvas andthe gross domestic product, and the second is the crisis in the banking system. The consequences of this were the fall and then the very slow growth of GDP, the slowdown of all reforms, the acceleration of inflation, and in the monetary sphere the loss and then the stagnation of foreign exchange reserves, low liquidity or, rather, high illiquidity in the system and high interest rates. Today, after six years, this situation looks very different. In mid-2000, the CNB's foreign exchange reserves amounted to around 803 billion and covered 29% of annual imports of goods and services. Today, they amount to 809.3 billion and cover almost 50% of the annual value of imports. Cash mass, as the main monetary aggregate, increased by 2.7 times over that period, with an annual growth rate of over 17 percent, which is twice as fast as the nominal gross domestic product grew. The speed of money circulation has halved from 10 trades in 2000 to today's 6 trades per year. The ratio of total liquid assets to GDP increased from 41 per cent to 63 per cent. Confidence in the national currency has also increased, with theshare of kuna savings in total savings doubling from 14 to 14 Thirty percent. The average interest rate on loans with a currency clause, which is the dominant form of credit in Croatia, it fell from 12 per cent to 6.3 per cent. The money market interest rate has fallen from 7 per cent to 1.7 per cent. Inflation measured by consumer prices decreased from 5.5% in 2000 to an average of 2.4% from 2001 to the fifth month of 2006. Finally, and most importantly, the average GDP growth rate increased from 1 per cent to 4.7 per cent. What do these figures show? Showthat throughout this period, contrary to the general belief, monetary policy has been extremely expansionary, directly supporting economic growth while keeping inflation at very low levels. Why, with such monetary expansion, economic growth was not even faster? This is the result of the structure of demand for money, and it is not, as you know, a monetary phenomenon. It depends on the overall situation in the real sector and on the overall economic policy of the country. At the same time as all this, significant transformations of the monetaryand wider financial system have been made. The legislation was amended, the new CNB Act, the Bank Act, the Foreign Exchange Act, the Payment Transactions Act, etc. were adopted. Modern interbank systems have been introduced, including the Croatian System of LargePayments and the National Clearing System. New monetary policy instruments have been introduced, including open market operations, overnight deposits, intraday loans, etc. Prudential control of banks has been improved and, to put it briefly, the money market and the country's financial market have been shaped and stabilised. In short, the monetary situation today is very different from six years ago. However, this kind of comparative static, a comparison of two static states, in 2000 and 2006, actually very little govori about what was really going on within this period. What were the determinants of this event, what were the problems and negative consequences of such movements? During this period of six years we distinguish in fact three fundamentally different sub-periods. The first is with2000 and 2001. This was a time when the CNB led a strong expansionary monetary policy by giving a monetary injection to the financial and real sectors to which it was necessary at the time. This was done primarily by reducing the reserve requirement rate. Krajem in 1999 it was 30.5 percent, by the end of 2000 it was reduced to 23 percent, and by the end of 2001 it was to 19 percent. In those two years, the increase in primary money was 66 per cent, the cash mass increased by 71 per cent, the total cash by 87 per cent. That was an important part of why there was never any talk of illiquidity in the system again. At the same time as such an expansionary CNB policy, we broke with the old dogma of elevating the exchange rate of the national currency as the object of strong, permanent interventions. We have let theexchange rate freely form in the market under these conditions of monetary expansion. That's what happened. The exchange rate stabilised at the level of HRK 7.56 per euro in those two years. Then there was a speculative attack on the kuna, at a time when there was usually a period of foreign exchange shortages, the exchange rate was appreciated to HRK 7.12, and after that, in the peak of the tourist season, jumped to 7.70. The CNB then intervened within two weeks with a total of 400 million euros and defended the exchange rate. After that, the exchange rate remained mostly stable. What course was that? This is the bio exchange rate at which, under those conditions in 2000/2001, the current account deficit of the balance of payments amounted to only 3% of GDP. This, in other words, even in such imperfect conditions was a equilibrium exchange rate. Inflation, of course, was immediately reduced. Core inflaciI fell to just 1.2 percent in 2001 and remained at that level for the next two years. The second period within these six years begins in late 2001 and early 2002, when we were faced with another shock caused by the introduction of the euro and the conversionof in-o-currencies into euros. In just one month, more than 1 billion euros have poured into the banking system from the pockets of citizens. The system and the CNB managed to offset this influx, there was no impact on inflation or exchange rates. However, then there was another inflow of1.2 billion euros in the second part of 2002, which banks borrowed abroad. The consequences were noticeable even then. The exchange rate averaged by 2.8 per cent in real terms, the deficit of goods and services doubled from 5.5 per cent to 11 per cent of GDP, and the current trance deficitof the balance of payments reached a record 8.6 per cent of GDP. It was just a hint of the events that followed and that continue to this day. The CNB also responded immediately to them, with fierce criticism from all interest groups at home and abroad, including the IMF. Thatwe have been accused of stifling development, limiting consumption, slaveing to low inflation dogma as the central bank's only economic objective. Since then, we have had movements and relationships that have been maintained to this day. And about which there is a lot of talk every day. Why are you aboutthe bottoms just like that? There are several causes and all of them began to come to the fore as early as 2003. First, which is seemingly absurd in some ways, previous successes in reducing inflation and stabilizing the exchange rate have reduced the perception of risk for foreign investors, and also for domestic borrowers with a currency clause. Foreign banks that had already taken over 90 percent of the domestic banking system by then had positioned themselves and organized their operations. At the same time, there was stagnation in the European Union with a drop in atmoatma rates, which increased the difference between the yields generated in Croatia and the yields in the EU. In fact, foreign banks began to do the work that led them to come to Croatia, which is why they bought domestic banks. They started selling abundant and relativelycheap EU money on the Croatian market. This is simply a standard picture of the effects of globalization of financial systems on the national economy. On the other hand, after decades and more sacrifices, the preference for consumption in the country has also increased, and the populationof the VA and businesses and the state. Simply because the increased spending was now funded by bank loans. Increase and budget deficit due to accelerated infrastructure construction. As a result of all this, there were also known consequences. From the twelfth month of 2002 to the end of the fifth month of 2006, banks borrowed net of 806.7 billion. Their external debt is growing at an average rate of 35 percent per year. Banks say that this is, among other things, the result of the CNB's measures, if it were not for these measures we would borrow lessor. However, even without these measures, they borrowed more than 5 billion euros, with annual growth of 29 percent. Their debt-to-GDP ratio doubles from 15 per cent to 31 per cent. At the same time, borrowing of other sectors is also growing: the state and businesses, thus giving the country's external debt increased from 15 billion euros to 27 billion euros in these three and a half years. It means for 12 billion euros, and its share of GDP from 62 percent to 85 percent. What are the consequences of this, which, of course, we still feel today? They're twoakes. First, the direct consequences of the external debt achieved are potential and real. Potential risks are: the vulnerability of the country to possible changes in interest rates, exchange rates, flows of international capital. The second are the real ones we feel, which is the high growth in the cost of servicing that debt. And in our analysis, we pointed out that with existing tendencies, the amount of interest paid would reach the level of possible GDP growth in a relatively short time frame. What's that mean? First, a substantial reduction in the country's own financial potential. And comradeo, her even greater dependence on foreign sources of funding. And we know that economic dependence is usually accompanied by some other addictions. The second is the indirect consequences of such debt. The first of these are constant pressures on the appreciation of the course. And the basic thing that the CNB has been doing in the last three and a half years is to prevent the strengthening of the kuna, emitting money through interventions in the foreign exchange market. However, even with these interventions, kuna has realistically applied in these three and a half years by almost 10 percent. That's how much cheaper imports are, that's how much oursand the exporters in kunas realistically get less. Secondly, the dynamic growth of domestic loans at rates of over 18 percent, with a tendency to strengthen the kuna, has of course a negative impact on the balance of payments. The deficit is not as high as it was in a record 2002, but peisrmantly high. On average, the deficit in the exchange of goods and services is 7.5% of GDP, the current account deficit is 6.5% of GDP. Of course, the deficit in the exchange of goods and services and directly negatively affects the slowdown in gross domestic product. Next, inflationa. It is still low and under control and will remain so. But the figures stubbornly suggest that inflation is accelerating slightly but steadily: from 1.7 percent in 2003 to 3.6 in 2005 and to 4 percent in the five months of 2006. (I've got a light on, which means I have to cut it short. I'll try to do it, but let me do one thing. In these six years I have very rarely been here and that is why now I am not just talking about the annual report but I want to point out the essence of the problem, it has not been since yesterday. That's why I started my term. And ohsim of that, this may be my last address.) It is not only consumer price inflation that is due to the described growth in foreign debt. Even higher is inflation in the sphere of property prices, which is not shown in consumer prices, except for rents. Let's keep in mind that rents have increased by 32 per cent in the last 12 months. Of course all this - appreciation, inflation - exacerbates the balance of payments, and through it it has a rebound effect on debt. This is a set of interrelated problems that the CNB seeks to act on with the limitedinstrations at its disposal, dosing these instruments in such a way as not to jeopardise the achievement of the underlying economic objective, which is high, sustainable economic growth. Thus, the CNB's activities are much broader than its legally established goal. We strive to act simultaneously on all these problems, not to limit ourselves solely to inflation, as there are many meals. If that were the case, then it would be easiest to let the exchange rate continue to apreciate, not to act pro-inflationary by printing money. One moreprecisely, we are guided by the logic of the lesser evil. How exactly does the CNB work? In the system of connected vessels, it is difficult to say precisely what is the cause and what is the consequence. However, as a monetary institution, the CNB primarily follows what is called the money trail. And in this halfof the azi from the fact gives the difference in the yields that banks make in Croatia and in the European Union the basic driver of capital imports. This capital turns into an aggressive supply of loans, which then stimulates the demand for loans as well. That is why our fundamental goal is toreduce the motivation for borrowing by buying foreign sources of funds. We started this already in 2003 with a 35% cover of foreign exchange liabilities to liquid foreign exchange receivables of banks, as well as the mandatory registration of treasury records for the growth of placements above 16 percent. With, again, criticism from all sides. We gave up 16 percent, but because of this, in 2004, we introduced a marginal reserve requirement - a direct form of capital restriction on bank borrowing. That is why we are the only ones in Europe and of course we are still experiencing criticism in Brussels and other places today. We started slightly, with a rate of 24 percent and then lifted it to today's 55 percent. The measure is neither mild nor harmless, although banks are still trying not to address it publicly. At the present moment, based on the action of this measure, in the CNB there is also a mobi licking early 1.5 billion euros of bank funds, of course, without interest. And this measure began to affect the operations of banks. Due to the preservation of their liquidity, they no longer transfer paradise profits abroad, they have increased interest rates on domestic deposits, they have ceased to further relax the terms of the granting of loans. We hope that this will be enough to slow the expansion into frameworks that will have no further negative implications. We also act with prudential measures and in this context today we have made aneli decision to increase general bookings for fast-growing placements. If necessary, other measures will be taken, not only on the liability side, but also on the assets side of banks. However, even with that I would finish, what the HNB can do applies only to the sphere of money and credit offers. The possibility of our influence on the sphere of demand is only indirect and much lower intensity. That is why on several occasions we have pointed out the necessity of harmonising all aspects of the country's economic policy. Forgive me for thisif long exposure. By submitting this report, my term as governor of the CNB actually ends. I tried to do my job to the best of my ability and could. We made our decisions autonomously, based on our own assessments, we were no one's expose9. How successful we've been is not for me to judge, but I don't think there was anything in my line of work to be ashamed of. Thank you for making that possible. a9
