Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 28.6.2006. Zagreb 28.6.2006. Gospodine predsjednie Sabora, dame i gospodo zastupnici! Dopustite mi da se u nekoliko rijei osvrnem na rad Hrvatske narodne banke i na aktualnu monetarnu i, ire, ekonomsku situaciju u Hrvatskoj. U ovo doba prije est godina bili smo suoeni ne samo sa dugoronim posljedicama rata, tranzicijske krize, meunarodne izolacije, nego i sa kratkoronim posljedicama dvaju ekonomskih okova. Prvi su dogaaji u Kosovu, njihove implikacije na platnu bilancu i bruto domai proizvod, a drugi kriza u bankovnom sustavu. Posljedice toga bile su pad, a zatim vrlo spori rast BDP-a, usporavanje svih reformi, ubrzanje inflacije, a u monetarnoj sferi gubitak i zatim stagnacija deviznih rezervi, niska likvidnost ili, bolje reeno, visoka nelikvidnost u sustavu i visoke kamatne stope. Danas, nakon est godina, ta situacija izgleda bitno drugaije. Sredinom 2000. devizne rezerve HNB-a su iznosile oko 3 milijarde eura i pokrivale 29% godinjeg uvoza roba i usluga. Danas one iznose 9,3 milijarde eura i pokrivaju gotovo 50% godinje vrijednosti uvoza. Novana masa, kao glavni monetarni agregat, u tom je razdoblju poveana za 2,7 puta, uz godinju stopu rasta od preko 17 posto, to je dvostruko bre nego to je rastao nominalni bruto domai proizvod. Brzina optjecaja novca je prepolovljena s 10 obrtaja u 2000. na dananjih 6 obrtaja godinje. Odnos ukupnih likvidnih sredstava i BDP-a je povean s 41 na 63 posto. Poveano je i povjerenje u nacionalnu valutu, pa je i udio kunske tednje u ukupnoj tednji udvostruen sa 14 na 30 posto. Prosjena kamatna stopa na kredite s valutnom klauzulom, to je dominantan oblik kredita u Hrvatskoj, smanjena je sa 12 na 6,3 posto. Kamatna stopa na tritu novca je pala sa 7 na 1,7 posto. Inflacija mjerena potroakim cijenama smanjena je s 5,5 posto u 2000. na prosjeno 2,4 posto od 2001. do petog mjeseca 2006. godine. Konano, i najvanije, prosjena stopa rasta BDP-a poveana je sa 1 na 4,7 posto. to pokazuju te brojke? Pokazuju daje u cijelom ovom razdoblju, suprotno opem uvjerenju, monetarna politika bila izrazito ekspanzivna, izravno podravajui gospodarski rast, a istodobno odravajui inflaciju na vrlo niskim razinama. Zato uz takvu monetarnu ekspanziju gospodarski rast nije bio i bri? To je rezultat strukture potranje za novcem, a ona nije, kao to znate, monetarni fenomen. Zavisi od ukupnog stanja u realnom sektoru i od ukupne ekonomske politike zemlje. Istodobno sa svim ovim, izvrene su bitne transformacije monetarnog i ire financijskog sustava. Izmijenjena je zakonska regulativa, donesen novi Zakon o HNB-u, Zakon o bankama, Zakon o deviznom poslovanju, Zakon o platnom prometu itd. Uvedeni su moderni sustavi meubankovnog poslovanja, ukljuujui Hrvatski sustav velikih plaanja i Nacionalni klirinki sustav. Uvedeni su novi instrumenti monetarne politike, ukljuujui operacije na otvorenom tritu, prekononi depoziti, unutardnevni krediti itd. Unaprijeena je bonitetna kontrola banaka i, kratko reeno, oblikovano je i stabilizirano trite novca i financijsko trite u zemlji. Ukratko, monetarna situacija danas je bitno razliita od one prije est godina. Meutim, ovakva komparativna statika, usporedba dvaju statinih stanja, 2000. i 2006. godine, zapravo vrlo malo govori o tome to se unutar tog razdoblja stvarno zbivalo. Koje su bile determinante tog zbivanja, koji su bili problemi i negativne posljedice takvih kretanja? U tom razdoblju od est godina razlikujemo u stvari tri bitno razliita podrazdoblja. Prvo je sama 2000. i 2001. godina. To je bilo vrijeme kad je HNB vodio izrazito ekspanzivnu monetarnu politiku dajui monetarnu injekciju financijskom i realnom sektoru kojem je ona tada bila neophodna. To se uradilo prije svega smanjenjem stope obvezne priuve. Krajem 1999. ona je iznosila 30,5 posto, do kraja 2000. je smanjena na 23, a do kraja 2001. na 19 posto. U te dvije godine porast primarnog novca bio je 66 posto, novana masa je poveana za 71 posto, ukupna novana sredstva za 87 posto. To je bio bitan razlog zato se nakon toga vie nikad nije govorilo o nelikvidnosti u sustavu. Istodobno s tako ekspanzivnom politikom HNB-a prekinuli smo sa starom dogmom uzdizanja teaja nacionalne valute kao objekta snanih, permanentnih intervencija. Pustili smo da se u takvim uvjetima monetarne ekspanzije teaj slobodno formira na tritu. To se i dogodilo. Teaj se u te dvije godine stabilizirao na razini od 7,56 kuna za euro. Tada je uslijedio spekulativni napad na kunu, u vrijeme kad je obino razdoblje nestaica deviza, teaj je aprecirao na 7,12 kuna, a nakon toga, u pici turistike sezone, skoio na 7,70. HNB je onda intervenirao u roku od dva tjedna s ukupno 400 milijuna eura i obranio teaj. Nakon toga teaj je uglavnom ostao stabilan. Koji je to bio teaj? To je bio teaj uz koji je u onim uvjetima 2000/2001. deficit tekuih transakcija platne bilance iznosio samo 3 posto BDP-a. To je, drugim rijeima, ak i u takvim imperfektnim uvjetima bio ravnoteni teaj. Inflacija je, naravno, odmah smanjena. Temeljna inflacija je pala na samo 1,2 posto u 2001. i na toj je razini ostala i u sljedee dvije godine. Drugo razdoblje unutar tih est godina poinje krajem 2001. i poetkom 2002. godine, kad smo bili suoeni s jo jednim okom izazvanim uvoenjem eura i konverzijom ino-valuta u eure. U samo mjesec dana u bankovni sustav se iz depova graana slilo vie od milijardu eura. Sustav i HNB su taj priljev uspjeli neutralizirati, nije bilo utjecaja ni na inflaciju ni na teaj. Meutim, tada je uslijedio jo jedan priljev od preko 1,2 milijardu eura u drugom dijelu 2002. godine, to su se banke zaduile u inozemstvu. Posljedice su bile uoljive ve tada. Teaj je realno aprecirao za 2,8 posto, deficit roba i usluga je udvostruen s 5,5 na 11 posto BDP-a, a deficit tekuih transakcija platne bilance je dostigao rekordnih 8,6 posto BDP-a. To je bio samo nagovjetaj dogaaja koji su slijedili i koji traju i danas. I HNB je odmah reagirao na njih, uz estoku kritiku svih interesnih skupina u zemlji i u inozemstvu, ukljuujui MMF. Tada smo bili optuivani da guimo razvoj, ograniavamo potronju, robujemo dogmi niske inflacije kao jedinog ekonomskog cilja sredinje banke. Od tada imamo kretanja i odnose koji su zadrani i do danas. I o kojima se svakodnevno mnogo govori. Zato su ti odnosi upravo takvi? Postoji vie uzroka i svi oni su poeli dolaziti do izraaja ve 2003. godine. Prvo, to je na neki nain naizgled apsurd, prethodni uspjesi u smanjivanju inflacije i stabilizaciji teaja smanjili su percepciju rizika za strane ulagae, a isto tako i za domae korisnike kredita s valutnom klauzulom. Strane banke koje su do onda ve preuzele 90 posto domaeg bankovnog sustava su se pozicionirale i organizirale svoje poslovanje. Istodobno, u Europskoj uniji je vladala stagnacija uz pad kamatnih stopa, to je povealo razliku izmeu prinosa koji se ostvaruju u Hrvatskoj i prinosa u EU-u. Zapravo, strane banke su poele obavljati posao zbog kojeg su i dole u Hrvatsku, zbog kojeg su i kupovale domae banke. Poele su prodavati obilan i relativno jeftin novac EU-a na hrvatskom tritu. To je jednostavno standardna slika djelovanja globalizacije financijskih sustava na nacionalnu ekonomiju. S druge strane, nakon desetljea i vie odricanja, poveana je i sklonost potronji u zemlji, i stanovnitva i poduzea i drave. Jednostavno zato to je poveana potronja sada bila financirana bankovnim kreditima. Poveanje i proraunski deficit zbog ubrzane izgradnje infrastrukture. Kao rezultat svega toga, bile su i znane posljedice. Od dvanaestog mjeseca 2002. do kraja petog mjeseca 2006. godine banke su se zaduile neto za 6,7 milijardi eura. Njihov vanjski dug raste po prosjenoj stopi od 35 posto godinje. Banke kau daje to, izmeu ostalog, i rezultat mjera HNB-a, da nema tih mjera mi bi se manje zaduili. Iskljuimo efekte mjera HNB- a na zaduivanje banaka. Ipak, one su se i bez tih mjera zaduile za vie od pet milijardi eura, uz godinji rast od 29 posto. Udio njihovog duga u BDP-u udvostruenje s 15 na 31 posto. Istodobno, raste i zaduivanje ostalih sektora: drave i poduzea, tako daje u ove tri i pol godine vanjski dug zemlje povean s 15 na 27 milijardi eura. Znai za 12 milijardi eura, a njegov udio u BDP-u sa 62 na 85 posto. Koje su posljedice toga, koje, naravno, osjeamo i danas? One su dvojake. Prvo su izravne posljedice dostignutog vanjskog duga, potencijalne i stvarne. Potencijalne su rizici: ranjivost zemlje na mogue promjene kamatnih stopa, teaja, tokova meunarodnog kapitala. Drugo su stvarne koje osjeamo, a to je visok rast trokova servisiranja tog duga. I u naoj smo analizi ukazali da bi uz postojee tendencije iznos plaenih kamata dostigao razinu mogueg prirasta BDP-a u relativno kratkom roku. to to znai? Prvo, bitno smanjenje vlastitog financijskog potencijala zemlje. I drugo, njezinu jo veu ovisnost od stranih izvora financiranja. A znamo da je ekonomska ovisnost obino praena i nekim drugim ovisnostima. Drugo su neizravne posljedice takvog duga. Prva od njih su stalni pritisci na aprecijaciju teaja. I osnovno to je HNB u posljednje tri i pol godine radio je sprjeavanje jaanja kune, emitirajui novac kroz intervencije na deviznom tritu. Ipak, i uz te intervencije, kuna je realno aprecirala u ove tri i pol godine skoro za 10 posto. Toliko je uvoz jeftiniji, toliko nai izvoznici u kunama realno dobiju manje. Drugo, dinamian rast domaih kredita po stopama od preko 18 posto, uz tendenciju jaanja kune, ima naravno negativan utjecaj na bilancu plaanja. Deficit nije tako visok kao to je bio u rekordnoj 2002., ali je permanentno visok. U prosjeku deficit u razmjeni roba i usluga iznosi 7,5 posto BDP-a, deficit tekuih transakcija 6,5 posto BDP-a. Naravno da deficit u razmjeni roba i usluga i izravno negativno utjee na usporavanje bruto domaeg proizvoda. Dalje, inflacija. Ona je jo uvijek niska i pod kontrolom i takva e i ostati. No, brojke tvrdoglavo govore da se inflacija lagano, ali konstantno ubrzava: sa 1,7 posto u 2003. na 3,6 u 2005. i na 4 posto u pet mjeseci 2006. godine. (Upaljeno mi je svjetlo, to znai da moram skratiti. Nastojat u to uraditi, ali dopustite mi jednu stvar. U ovih est godina vrlo rijetko sam bio ovdje i zato sada ne govorim samo o godinjem izvjeu ve elim ukazati na bit problema, on nije od juer. Zato sam poeo s poetkom mandata. A osim toga, ovo mi je moda i zadnje obraanje.) Nije samo inflacija potroakih cijena posljedica opisanog rasta inozemnog duga. Jo vea je inflacija u sferi cijena nekretnina koja se ne iskazuje u potroakim cijenama, osim kod najamnina. Imajmo na umu da su najamnine u posljednjih 12 mjeseci poveane za 32 posto. Naravno da sve to - aprecijacija, inflacija - pogorava platnu bilancu, a preko nje povratno utjee na dug. To je skup meusobno povezanih problema na koje HNB nastoji djelovati ogranienim instrumentima koji mu stoje na raspolaganju, dozirajui pri tome te instrumente na nain da ne ugroze ostvarivanje temeljnog ekonomskog cilja, a to je visok, odrivi ekonomski rast. Tako je i djelovanje HNB-a mnogo ire nego to je njegov zakonom utvreni cilj. Mi nastojimo simultano djelovati na sve ove probleme, ne ograniiti se iskljuivo na inflaciju, kao to ima mnogih objeda. Da je tako, onda bi bilo najjednostavnije pustiti da teaj i dalje aprecira, a ne da tampanjem novca djelujemo proinflacijski. Jednostavno, rukovodimo se logikom manjeg zla. Kako u stvari HNB djeluje? U sistemu spojenih posuda teko je precizno kazati to je uzrok, a to posljedica. Meutim, kao monetarna institucija HNB prije svega slijedi ono to se naziva tragom novca. I u tome polazi od injenice daje razlika u prinosima koje banke ostvaruju u Hrvatskoj i u Europskoj uniji osnovni pokreta uvoza kapitala. Taj kapital se pretvara u agresivnu ponudu kredita koja onda potie i potranju za kreditima. Zato je na temeljni cilj da poskupljenjem inozemnih izvora sredstava smanjimo motivaciju za zaduivanje. To smo poeli ve 2003. s 35-postotnim pokriem deviznih obveza likvidnim deviznim potraivanjima banaka, kao i obaveznim upisom blagajnikih zapisa za rast plasmana iznad 16 posto. Uz, opet, kritike sa svih strana. Odustali smo od 16 posto, ali smo zbog toga 2004. uveli graninu obveznu priuvu - izravni oblik kapitalske restrikcije na zaduivanje banaka. Po tome smo jedini u Europi i naravno da doivljavamo i danas kritike u Bruxellesu i na ostalim mjestima. Poeli smo blago, sa stopom od 24 posto i onda ju dizali do dananjih 55 posto. Ta mjera nije ni blaga ni bezazlena, iako se banke jo uvijek nastoje ne osvrtati javno na nju. U dananjem trenutku, po osnovi djelovanja te mjere, u HNB-u je i mobi lizi rano 1,5 milijardi eura sredstava banaka, naravno, bez kamata. I ta mjera poela je djelovati na poslovanje banaka. Zbog ouvanja svoje likvidnosti vie ne transferi raju dobit u inozemstvo, poveale su kamate stope na domae depozite, prestale su sa daljnjom relaksacijom uvjeta odobravanja kredita. Nadamo se da e to biti dovoljno da se ekspanzija uspori u okvire koji nee imati daljnje negativne implikacije. Djelujemo i prudencijalnim mjerama i u tom kontekstu danas smo donijeli odluku o poveanju opih rezervacija za brzorastue plasmane. Bude li potrebno, poduzet e se i druge mjere i to ne samo na strani pasive, nego i na strani aktive banaka. Meutim, i s time bih i zavrio, ono to HNB moe uraditi odnosi se iskljuivo na sferu ponude novca i kredita. Mogunost naeg utjecaja na sferu potranje je samo indirektna i mnogo slabijeg intenziteta. Zato smo u nekoliko navrata i ukazivali na nunost usklaenog djelovanja svih aspekata ekonomske politike zemlje. Oprostite mi na ovako dugom izlaganju. Podnoenjem ovog izvjea zapravo prestaje moj mandat kao guvernera HNB-a. Nastojao sam obavljati svoj posao najbolje to znam i mogu. Odluke smo donosili autonomno, na bazi vlastitih procjena, nismo bili niija ekspozitura. Koliko smo bili uspjeni, nije na meni da sudim, ali mislim da u mom poslu nije bilo niega ega bih se trebao stidjeti. Hvala vam to ste mi to omoguili.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation in the Croatian Parliament
text: Presentation of CNB Deputy Governor Relja Martic at the Croatian Parliament Speech Relja Martic, Deputy Governor of the CNB 26.3.2015. Zagreb 26.3.2015. Introductory presentation of the Deputy Governor of the Croatian National Bank Relja Martic at the Croatian Parliament on 26 March 2015, during the debate on the Semiannual Information on the Financial Situation, the Degree of Realization of Price Stability and the Implementation of Monetary Policy (in the first six months of 2014) During the first half of 2014, the Croatian National Bank, as it did for years after 2008, pursued an expansionary monetary policy. This was also reflected in the real growth of money and wider monetary aggregates, and especially in large and unprecedented kuna liquidity surpluses in banks' accounts with the central bank and historically low interest rates in the money market. quantitative easing policies, the US FED, the Bank of Japan, the European Central Bank (ECB) and other major central banks. Why? Because the structure of the CNB's balance sheet is very different, the structure of the domestic financial system in relation to the financial systems of the developed economies and finally, but most urgently, because in its tool collection the CNB still has an efficient instrument that is not available to the aforementioned central banks. This instrument is a reserve requirement. At the beginning of the crisis, the central bank released huge foreign exchange and kuna liquidityt, lifting various restrictions, which it was imposing in a boom phase in order to slow banks' lending activity through monetary tightening, but also unconventional measures. It then gradually lowered the reserve requirement rate, partly conditional and in combination with certainlending programmes of the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Until it has exhausted the possibility of lowering the reserve requirement rate to the levels at which the reserve requirement rate and the importance of the reserve requirement as a monetary policy instrument is present in the Eurosystem or, for example, in the United States or the United Kingdom or Japan, etc., there is no need and it would be irrational to generate new money through other channels. Reserve requirement is still a huge reservoir of potential new liquidity of over HRK 31 billion . This money, when released and released into the system, is released permanently, without a maturity or repurchase, as opposed to repo auctions or asset purchases, which are done by these large central banks. In addition, this money is free, there is no payment of kamate, it is not a loan. In addition, reducing the reserve requirement rate directly increases the credit multiplier. Quantitative easing has not been able to drive significant credit growth in Croatia, just as the ECB's expansionary cash policy so far has failed to do in the Eurosystem. In developed market economies with developed financial systems, quantitative easing has led and leads primarily to the rise in the prices of financial instruments and shares and the creation of new stock bubbles. Stock indexes are higher than before the crisis, and growth in economies is subdued. The problem is the same everywhere - how to make this new money end up in the real sector, in productive investments and jobs. Due to the absence of such an efficient cash transfer, quantitative easing is most beneficial to financial investors and in fact leads to further inequalities and sows the seeds of a new crisis, if its stimulating effects are not accompanied by real reforms. And that is why, when ECB leaders recently announced the latest rundu quantitative easing, their message was: loose monetary policy is not a panacea, further reforms are needed. Quantitative easing appears to have yielded some results in the U.S., by targeting the private securities market. In the European uniji, where the debt market is relatively underdeveloped and where banks, rather than the capital market, play a major role in financing companies (80% of the financing goes through banks, up to only 30% in the US), such a market for private securities on a significant scale is in fact absent, and perhaps, in some opinions, newly printed money would be used more directly and efficiently in investments in the bonds of the European Investment Bank and similar institutions and mechanisms that accompany development and mechanisms investment programmes and provide guaranteeschemes specifically for SMEs. The Croatian National Bank, however, has already done so. She sought solutions to revive the financing of the company in cooperation with HBOR, through the well-known loan models of HBOR. At the very end of 2013, the CNBre-encountered a similar mechanism, but directly, without HBOR. The reserve requirement rate was lowered by 1.5% (from 13.5%) and thus released almost 4 billion kuna - but conditionally. Banks had to enter the freed kunas in cash registers that do not carry interest and which theCNB then bought from banks, i.e. monetized in accordance with the increase in their credit activity. Therefore, since the beginning of last year, banks have been available for credit activity on average 8 billion kuna of surplus in their giro accounts per day, with almost 4 billion kuna in cashier's records, ready to be cashed in at the pace at which banks would grant new loans. It's a huge credit potential. Research conducted in the CNB, shows that during this period the offer was only in a small part a limiting factor of loan growth. The main problem is weak creditworthy demand with too many over-indebted and under-capitalized sectors in an atmosphere of economic pessimism. The population continued to deleverage, and loans to businesses actually stagnated in the first half. Thus, it is obvious that the problem does not lie in the lack of liquidity and cannot be solved in isolation by monetary policy. Thus, in the first half of 2014, economic activity stagnated, but due to the slowdown at the end of 2013, theinterim gdp growth rates in the first and second quarters were negative and were -0.6% for the first and -0.8% for the second quarter. The main problem is investment. By far the strongest negative contribution to GDP came from a further decline in investment (even by -3.6% and -5.2%) and only then much less than the decline in government and personal consumption. The positive contribution came only from foreign relations due to the dynamism of export growth. From the production side, the decline occurred especially in the activities of construction, agricultureedi, forestry and fishing, information and communications, and the best results were the processing industry, but it also faltered in the second quarter, so that in the second quarter only trade achieved growth in gross value added. Stagnacand economic activity in the first half of last year was accompanied by a weakening of unfavourable developments in the labour market. The number of people in employment stabilised at a low level after a sharp decline in the second half of 2013, and the number of unemployed did not change significantly either. The unemployment rate remained at the level of 16.6%. Despite the lack of growth, nominal and real gross and net wages increased slightly in the first half of 2014. Inflation has entered negative territory during this period. The annual inflaof whose consumer prices fell from 0.3% in December 2013 to -0.4% in June 2014. The decline or stagnation of economic activity, investment, the decrease in disposable income and the deleveraging of the population and other factors that dampen the growth of prices, were utni all the time after 2008, so it is obvious that external factors and the movement of volatile elements of the index such as the prices of agricultural products and nutrition were decisive. The annual rate of change in the deflator of imports of goods and services during this period was -1% and this shows that the significant downward pressure on prices stemmed from the cheapening of raw materials and final products from abroad and an increase in competition after Croatia joined the EU. Deflation can be dangerous because it can trigger a spiral of falling prices, wages and demand. But what we mean by the concept of deflation in the classical sense is not present in Croatia. So-called underlying inflation, therefore an indicator of price movements that does not include volatile prices of agricultural products and energy, wasstill in positive territory in the observed period. With us, there are transient reasons on the scene, while deflation is a longer-term trend of decreasing price levels accompanied by the general expectations of its further decline, which then in theory leads to the delay of consumption. However, the reasons for the decline in personal consumption in Croatia since the beginning of 2009 lie in other factors, and certainly not in the delay of consumption due to the expectation of further declines in the prices of food or petroleum products. In fact, the fall in these prices, especially when it is not accompanied by a drop in real wagesand will encourage consumption rather than delay, except - of course - if this effect is not focused on even faster deleveraging, which unfortunately is quite possible. There is a clear limit to the conduct of the CNB's expansionary monetary policy, which - I must stress -is not attainable and has not been and so far is not a limiting factor of loose monetary policy. What's the limit? It's a mink exchange rate. And there is also a difference between the degrees of freedom to conduct monetary policy of the CNB and the ECB. The CNB has no choice but to continue with the policy of the relativeand continuous exchange rate of the kuna against the euro for very well-known reasons. If an expansionary monetary policy is to have to be chosen and the relative stability of the exchange rate is maintained, the exchange rate will be chosen, at least at the cost of monetary tightening. For this reason, current account developments and the financial account of the balance of payments are of particular importance. The current account was negative at 801.8 billion seasonally in the first half. However, looking at the year as a whole, and this is necessary due to the characteristic seasonal factors, therefore, including the third quarter with the majority of tourist revenues, it was positive again, as in 2013. In the conditions of a marked slowdown in the growth of total foreign debt, the balance of payments was closed partly by an increase in borrowing, butby eating and decreasing the CNB's gross international reserves. Foreign debt stood at EUR 45.9 billion at the end of 2013. euro and 8046.3 billion at the end of June. In the banks sector, debt fell from 9.2bn to 1.5bn. at 8.9 billion, other sectors increased debt slightly. Gross internationalnon-reserves stood at eur 12.9 billion at the end of 2013, to be EUR 12.3 billion at the end of June. (decrease of 572 million). Net reserves remained at the level of EUR 10.5 billion. Euros. The exchange rate of the euro (CNB's median exchange rate) at the end of 2013 was HRK 7.64 and at the end of June 2014 it was HRK 7.57. During this period, the CNB sold foreign currency to the European Commission (a total of 292 million) and banks (240 million euros at auction in February), and bought a total of 417 million euros from the Finance Ministry. Developments in the balance sheet of monetary institutions were under the crucial influence of the deleveraging of the population, by EUR 0.9 billion nominally and HRK 262 million respectively effectively (without the influence of the exchange rate), then the very slow growth of loans of private companies (751 m.) and at the same time a strong sothat loans from state-owned companies (-2.3 billion), which partially compensated for this through foreign borrowing and at the end of a significant increase in the net receivables of banks from the state. In total, net domestic assets increased by only 659 million, practically stagnatingla. Cash mass increased by three billion or 5.1%, quasi money fell by 3.4 billion euros, primarily due to a decline in foreign currency deposits, kunas achieved a slight increase. The end result was a marked increase in banks' foreign assets and an even faster decline in banaka's foreign liabilities. This movement in foreign assets and bank liabilities was still far stronger during the second half of the year, and this also shows the limitations of expansionary monetary policy. Thus, in developed financial markets, quantitative easing inflates the priceof financial instruments and shares, while in our country it accelerates the deleveraging of banks to foreign countries. The European Union is also facing strong euro outflows into other currencies and other markets following this latest additional money printing programme. In all these cases, the effects on domestic credit growth are modest. In addition to such a decrease in balance sheets, the banking system's operations in the first half of 2014 were marked by further growth in non-performing loans. The share of non-performing loans (groups B and C) rose from 15.7% at the end of 2013 to 16.6% at the end of June 2014. The biggest impact on the decline in the quality of total loans was loans to enterprises, where the share of non-performing loans reached 29.6%. The Croatian National Bank, in accordance with the requirements of the European Banking Authority (EBA), in cooperation with the competent supervisory authorities of other countries, conducted an asset quality review ,which confirmed our view of the situation in the banks covered by the verification. The findings indicate that the accounting statements of banks' operations are realistic and no significant risks have been found hidden. The need for supplementary provisions and corrections with a value of about 1.5 billion kuna was observed, which is not small, but not significant compared to the size of the reviewed portfolio. Accordingto provisional data, banks' profits amounted to HRK 1.6 billion in the first half of 2014, which is a quarter higher than in the same period of the previous year. Indicators of profitability of assets and capital improved compared to 2013, when provisioning costs were higher and weighed more heavily on their profits. Despite the deterioration in the quality of the loan portfolio, the risks of banks' operations remained adequately covered. Profit growth and recapitalisations carried out strengthened the capitalisation of the domestic bankingg system. This was achieved thanks to the conservative approach of previous years, which ensured a high level and quality of capital items. At the end of June 2014, all capital rates were significantly higher than the prescribed minimums (the total capital rate carried21.1 %). Thus, the banking system as a whole, on average, has maintained a profiteabi Inost and a strong capital position, with an corresponding increase in the coverage of non-performing loans with provisions. The system is therefore relatively healthy, it does not pose a problem and a burden on the public finances, but unfortunately it does not contribute to solving problems in other sectors of the economy satisfactorily Banks are underactive in reviving credit expansion and, in particular, are insufficiently enterprising in tackling NPL. A large and growing share of their assets are frozen in non-performing, non-performing or only partially recoverable receivables. These bad assets are the result of their loose credit policies and poor business decisions in previous years. Banks must approach the faster resolution of these assets and the clearing of balance sheets, at the expense of their costs, i.e. they must suffer certain losses on this basis. This will free them from the ballast of the wrong moves of the past, facilitate the position of over-indebted sectors and open the way for new loans to growthem. As before, the CNB will provide liquidity, and will be ready to modify regulatory requirements depending on the selected balance sheet cleaning modalities. I have repeatedly reminded at this pulpit that in the years before the crisis, the Croatian National Bank mademoves quantitatively, thanks to which we now have financial stability and fewer problems in the financial sector in the crisis in the crisis, and that after entering the crisis, the CNB again actively acted, within its powers, to facilitate its exit from the crisis. CNB policy is bila and is- countercyclical. Monetary policy can be supportive and part of the solution, but it alone cannot be the solution. In order to increase investment activity, employment and productivity and to take advantage of the monetary stimulus, further double reforms are needed. Monetary policies, both by the ECB and the CNB, can only buy time to implement reforms that would increase the competitiveness of EU countries lagging behind in economic growth and development. In Croatia, until this is done, the potential growth will bevery low and the recovery very slow.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje zamjenika guvernera HNB-a Relje Martia u Hrvatskom saboru Objavljeno: 26.3.2015. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Govor Relja Marti, zamjenik guvernera HNB-a 26.3.2015. Zagreb 26.3.2015. Uvodno izlaganje zamjenika guvernera Hrvatske narodne banke Relje Martia u Hrvatskom saboru 26. oujka 2015., u prigodi rasprave o Polugodinjoj informaciji o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike (u prvih est mjeseci 2014. godine) Tijekom prvog polugodita 2014. godine Hrvatska narodna banka je, kao i godinama nakon 2008., vodila ekspanzivnu monetarnu politiku. To se ogledalo i u realnom rastu novane mase i irih monetarnih agregata, a posebno u velikim i dotad nezabiljeenim vikovima kunske likvidnosti na raunima banaka kod sredinje banke i povijesno niskim kamatnim stopama na tritu novca. injenica da HNB de facto provodi svojevrsnu politiku tzv. kvantitativnog poputanja, promie dijelu ak i strune javnosti, jer se naa sredinja banka pri tome ne koristi istim instrumentima kreiranja novca kakvim se koriste u politikama kvantitativnog poputanja ameriki FED, Japanska sredinja banka, Europska sredinja banka (ESB) i druge velike sredinje banke. Zato? Zato jer je struktura bilance HNB-a bitno drugaija, drugaija je i struktura domaeg financijskog sustava u odnosu na financijske sustave razvijenih gospodarstava i konano te najhitnije, jer u svojoj zbirci alata HNB jo uvijek ima efikasan instrument koji nije na raspolaganju spomenutim sredinjim bankama. Taj instrument je obvezna priuva. Na poetku krize sredinja banka je oslobodila ogromnu deviznu i kunsku likvidnost, ukidajui razna ogranienja, koja je bila uvodila u fazi buma kako bi monetarnim stezanjem, ali i nekonvencionalnim mjerama usporila kreditnu aktivnost banaka. Zatim je postupno sputala stopu obvezne priuve, dijelom uvjetovano i u kombinacijama s odreenim programima kreditiranja Hrvatske banke za obnovu i razvitak. Dok ne iscrpi mogunost sputanja stope obvezne priuve do razina na kojima je stopa obvezne priuve i znaaj obvezne priuve kao instrumenta monetarne politike prisutan u Eurosustavu ili, primjerice, u Sjedinjenim Amerikim Dravama ili Velikoj Britaniji ili Japanu itd., nema potrebe i bilo bi neracionalno kreirati novi novac drugim kanalima. Obvezna priuva je jo uvijek ogroman rezervoar potencijalne nove likvidnosti od preko 31 milijarde kuna. Taj novac kad se oslobaa i puta u sustav, oslobaa se trajno, bez roka dospijea ili reotkupa, za razliku od repo aukcija ili kupovina vrijednosnih papira, to rade navedene velike sredinje banke. K tome, taj je novac besplatan, nema plaanja kamate, to nije kredit. Povrh toga, smanjenjem stope obvezne priuve izravno se poveava kreditni multiplikator. Kvantitativno poputanje nije bilo u stanju potaknuti znaajniji rast kredita u Hrvatskoj, jednako kao to to niti dosadanja ekspanzivna novana politika ESB-a nije uspjela uiniti u Eurosustavu. U razvijenim trinim ekonomijama s razvijenim financijskim sustavima, kvantitativno poputanje vodilo je i vodi prije svega do rasta cijena financijskih instrumenata i dionica i stvaranja novih burzovnih balona. Burzovni indeksi su vii nego prije krize, a rast je gospodarstava priguen. Problem je svugdje isti - kako da taj novi novac zavri u realnom sektoru, u produktivnim investicijama i poslovima. Zbog izostanka takvog uinkovitog novanog prijenosa, kvantitativno poputanje najvie pogoduje financijskim ulagaima i u stvari vodi u daljnje nejednakosti i sije sjeme nove krize, ako njegovi stimulativni uinci nisu praeni stvarnim reformama. I zato, kad su elnici ESB nedavno bili najavili najnoviju rundu kvantitativnog poputanja, njihova je poruka bila: labava monetarna politika nije panacea, potrebne su daljnje reforme. Izgleda da je kvantitativno poputanje dalo odreene rezultate u SAD-u, ciljanjem na trite privatnih vrijednosnica. U Europskoj uniji, gdje je trite duga relativno nerazvijeno i gdje banke, a ne trite kapitala, imaju glavnu ulogu u financiranju poduzea (80% financiranja ide preko banaka, prema samo 30% u SAD-u), takvog trita privatnih vrijednosnica u znaajnijem obimu u stvari i nema, te bi moda, prema nekim miljenjima, izravnije i efikasnije bio upotrijebljen novotiskani novac u ulaganja u obveznice Europske investicijske banke i slinih institucija i mehanizama koji prate razvojne i ulagake programe i osiguravaju garancijske sheme posebno za mala i srednja poduzea. Hrvatska narodna banka je, meutim, i to ve radila. Traila je rjeenja za oivljavanje financiranja poduzea u suradnji s HBOR-om, preko poznatih kreditnih modela HBOR-a. HNB je na samom kraju 2013. ponovno pokrenuo slian mehanizam, ali izravno, bez HBOR-a. Sputena je stopa obvezne priuve za 1,5% (sa 13,5%) i time je osloboeno gotovo etiri milijarde kuna - ali uvjetno. Banke su osloboene kune morale upisati u blagajnike zapise koji ne nose kamate i koje je onda HNB otkupljivao od banaka, odnosno unovavao sukladno poveanju njihove kreditne aktivnosti. Dakle, od poetka prole godine bankama je za kreditnu aktivnost bilo na raspolaganju dnevno u prosjeku osam milijardi kuna vika na njihovim iro raunima, uz tih gotovo etiri milijarde kuna u blagajnikim zapisima, spremnih da budu unoveni tempom kojim bi banke odobravale nove kredite. To je ogroman kreditni potencijal. Istraivanja provedena u HNB-u, pokazuju daje u ovom razdoblju ponuda bila samo manjim dijelom ograniavajui faktor rasta kredita. Glavni problem je slaba kreditno sposobna potranja uz previe prezaduenih i pod kapitaliziranih sektora u atmosferi ekonomskog pesimizma. Stanovnitvo se nastavilo razduivati, a krediti poduzeima su u prvom polugoditu u stvari stagnirali. Dakle, oito je da problem ne lei u manjku likvidnosti i da se ne moe rijeiti izolirano monetarnom politikom. Tako je i u prvom polugoditu 2014. gospodarska aktivnost stagnirala, no zbog usporavanja krajem 2013. meugodinje stope rasta BDP-a u prvom i drugom kvartalu bile su negativne i iznosile su -0,6% za prvi i -0,8% za drugi kvartal. Glavni su problem investicije. Daleko najjai negativni doprinos BDP-u dolazio je od daljnjeg pada investicija (ak za -3,6% i -5,2%) i tek zatim mnogo manje od pada dravne i osobne potronje. Pozitivni doprinos dolazio je jedino iz odnosa s inozemstvom uslijed dinamiziranja rasta izvoza. Gledano sa proizvodne strane, do pada je dolo naroito u djelatnostima graevinarstva, poljoprivredi, umarstvu i ribarstvu, informacijama i komunikacijama, a najbolje rezultate imala je preraivaka industrija, ali je i ona u drugom tromjeseju posustala, tako da je u drugom tromjeseju jedino trgovina ostvarila rast bruto dodane vrijednosti. Stagnaciju gospodarske aktivnosti u prvom polugoditu prole godine pratilo je slabljenje nepovoljnih kretanja na tritu rada. Broj zaposlenih stabilizirao se na niskoj razini nakon snanog pada ostvarenog u drugoj polovici 2013., a ni broj nezaposlenih nije se bitno mijenjao. Stopa nezaposlenosti zadrana je na razini od 16,6%. Unato izostanku rasta, nominalne i realne bruto i neto plae u prvoj polovici 2014. godine blago su porasle. Inflacija je tijekom tog razdoblja zala u negativno podruje. Godinja inflacija potroakih cijena pala je sa 0,3% u prosincu 2013. na -0,4% u lipnju 2014. godine. Pad odnosno stagnacija gospodarske aktivnosti, investicija, smanjenje raspoloivog dohotka i razduivanje stanovnitva i drugi faktori koji priguuju rast cijena, prisutni su cijelo vrijeme nakon 2008., pa je oito da su vanjski faktori i kretanje volatilnih elemenata indeksa poput cijena poljoprivrednih proizvoda i prehrane bili odluujui. Godinja stopa promjene deflatora uvoza robe i usluga u tom razdoblju iznosila je -1 % i to pokazuje da je znatan pritisak na smanjenje cijena proizlazio iz pojeftinjenja sirovina i finalnih proizvoda iz inozemstva i poveanja konkurencije nakon ulaska Hrvatske u EU. Deflacija moe biti opasna jer moe pokrenuti spiralu pada cijena, plaa i potranje. No, ono to podrazumijevamo pod pojmom deflacije u klasinom smislu nije prisutno u Hrvatskoj. Tzv. temeljna inflacija, dakle pokazatelj kretanja cijena koji ne ukljuuje volatilne cijene poljoprivrednih proizvoda i energije, bila je u razmatranom razdoblju i dalje je u pozitivnom podruju. Kod nas su na sceni prolazni razlozi, dok je deflacija dugoroniji trend smanjivanja razine cijena praen opim oekivanjima njenog daljnjeg pada, to onda u teoriji vodi odlaganju potronje. Meutim, razlozi pada osobne potronje u Hrvatskoj jo od poetka 2009. lee u drugim imbenicima, a svakako ne u odlaganju potronje zbog oekivanja daljnjeg pada cijena hrane ili naftnih derivata. Dapae, pad tih cijena, posebno kad nije praen padom realnih plaa prije e potronju potaknuti nego odgoditi, osim - naravno - ako se taj uinak ne usmjeri na jo bre razduivanje, to je naalost sasvim mogue. Za voenje ekspanzivne monetarne politike HNB-a postoji jasna granica, koja - moram naglasiti - nije dostignuta i nije bila i zasad nije ograniavajui faktor labave monetarne politike. Koja je to granica? To je teaj kune. I tu je takoer razlika izmeu stupnjeva slobode voenja monetarne politike HNB-a i ESB-a. HNB nema izbora nego nastaviti s politikom relativno stabilnog teaja kune prema euru iz itekako dobro poznatih razloga. Ako e se morati birati izmeu ekspanzivne monetarne politike i odravanja relativne stabilnosti teaja, izabrat e se teaj, makar po cijenu monetarnog zaotravanja. Zbog toga su od posebne vanosti kretanja tekueg rauna i financijskog rauna platne bilance. Tekui raun je sezonski u prvom polugoditu bio negativan na razini od 1,8 milijardi eura. Meutim, gledajui godinu u cjelini, a to je potrebno zbog karakteristinih sezonskih faktora, dakle, ukljuujui tree tromjeseje s glavninom turistikih prihoda, on je ponovno, kao i u 2013. bio pozitivan. U uvjetima osjetnog usporavanja rasta ukupnog inozemnog duga platna bilanca je bila zatvorena dijelom poveanjem zaduivanja, ali dijelom i smanjenjem bruto meunarodnih priuva HNB-a. Inozemni dug je na kraju 2013. iznosio 45,9 mlrd. eura, a na kraju lipnja 46,3 milijarde eura. U sektoru banaka dug je pao sa 9,2 mlrd. na 8,9 mlrd., ostali sektori su dug blago poveali. Bruto meunarodne priuve iznosile su na kraju 2013.12,9 mlrd., da bi na kraju lipnja iznosile 12,3 mlrd. (smanjenje od 572 milijuna). Neto priuve su ostale na razini od 10,5 mlrd. eura. Teaj eura (srednji teaj HNB-a) na kraju 2013. iznosio je 7,64 kn, a krajem lipnja 2014. godine 7,57 kn. HNB je u tom razdoblju prodavao devize Europskoj komisiji (ukupno 292 milijuna) i bankama (na aukciji u veljai 240 milijuna), a od Ministarstva financija kupilo je ukupno 417 milijuna eura. Kretanja u bilanci monetarnih institucija bila su pod presudnim utjecajem razduivanja stanovnitva, za 0,9 mlrd. nominalno odnosno 262 milijuna kuna efektivno (bez utjecaja teaja), zatim vrlo sporog rasta kredita privatnih trgovakih drutava (751 m.) i ujedno izrazitog pada kredita dravnih trgovakih drutava (-2,3 mlrd.), koja su to djelomino nadoknadila inozemnim zaduivanjem te na kraju znaajnog rasta neto potraivanja banaka od drave. Ukupno je neto domaa aktiva porasla za svega 659 milijuna, praktiki je stagnirala. Novana masa je porasla za tri milijarde ili 5,1%, kvazi novac je pao za 3,4 mlrd., prije svega zbog pada deviznih depozita, kunski su ostvarili blagi rast. Krajnji rezultat bio je osjetan rast inozemne aktive banaka i jo bri pad inozemnih obveza banaka. Takvo kretanje u inozemnoj aktivi i pasivi banaka jo je daleko jae bilo tijekom druge polovice godine, i to takoer pokazuje ogranienja ekspanzivne monetarne politike. Tako na razvijenim financijski tritima kvantitativno poputanje napuhava cijene financijskih instrumenata i dionica, dok kod nas ubrzava razduivanje banaka prema inozemstvu. Europska unija se takoer, nakon ovog zadnjeg dodatnog programa tiskanja novca, suoava sa snanim odljevom eura u druge valute i na druga trita. U svim tim sluajevima, uinci na domai kreditni rast su skromni. Uz takvo smanjivanje bilanci, poslovanje bankovnog sustava u prvoj polovici 2014. obiljeio je daljnji rast loih kredita. Udio loih kredita (skupine B i C) porastao je s 15,7% na kraju 2013. na 16,6% na kraju lipnja 2014. Najvei uinak na pad kvalitete ukupnih kredita imali su krediti poduzeima, kod kojih je udio loih kredita dosegnuo 29,6%. Hrvatska narodna banka je sukladno zahtjevima Europskog nadzornog tijela za bankarstvo (European Banking Authority - EBA), u suradnji s nadlenim nadzornim tijelima drugih drava, provela ispitivanje kvalitete imovine (Asset Quality Review), koje je potvrdilo nae vienje stanja u bankama obuhvaenima provjerom. Nalazi ukazuju na to da su knjigovodstveni iskazi poslovanja banaka realni i da nisu naeni skriveni znaajni rizici. Uoena je potreba dopunskih rezervacija i ispravaka vrijednosti od oko milijardu i pol kuna, to nije malo, ali nije ni znaajno u usporedbi s veliinom pregledanog portfelja. Dobit banaka je prema privremenim podacima, u prvom polugoditu 2014. iznosila 1,6 mlrd. kuna, to je za etvrtinu vie nego u istom razdoblju prethodne godine. Pokazatelji profitabiInosti imovine i kapitala poboljali su se u odnosu na 2013. godinu, kada su trokovi rezerviranja bili vei i snanije su opteretili njihovu dobit. Unato pogoranju kvalitete kreditnog portfelja, rizici poslovanja banaka ostali su adekvatno pokriveni. Rast dobiti i provedene dokapitalizacije osnaili su kapitaliziranost domaega bankovnog sustava. To je postignuto zahvaljujui konzervativnom pristupu prethodnih godina, koji je osigurao visoku razinu i kvalitetu stavki kapitala. Na kraju lipnja 2014. sve su stope kapitala bile osjetno vie od propisanih minimuma (stopa ukupnoga kapitala iznosila je 21,1 %). Dakle, bankovni sustav je u cjelini, u prosjeku, zadrao profitabi Inost i jaku kapitalnu poziciju, uz odgovarajui rast pokrivenosti loih kredita rezervacijama. Sustav je, dakle, relativno zdrav, ne predstavlja problem i teret za javne financije, ali naalost niti ne pridonosi rjeavanju problema u drugim sektorima gospodarstva na zadovoljavajui nain Banke su nedovoljno aktivne u oivljavanju kreditne ekspanzije i naroito, nedovoljno su poduzetne u rjeavanju problema loih kredita. Velik i rastui dio imovine zamrznut im je u neprihodujuim, nenaplativim ili tek djelomino naplativim potraivanjima. Ta loa imovina je rezultat njihovih labavih kreditnih politika i loih poslovnih odluka u prijanjim godinama. Banke moraju pristupiti brem rjeavanju te imovine i ienju bilanci, na teret svojih trokova, odnosno moraju pretrpjeti odreene gubitke po toj osnovi. To e ih osloboditi balasta krivih poteza iz prolosti, olakati poloaj prezaduenih sektora i otvoriti prostor za rast novih kredita. HNB e kao i do sada osiguravati likvidnost, a bit e i spreman modificirati regulatorne zahtjeve ovisno o odabranim modalitetima ienja bilanci. Vie puta sam za ovom govornicom podsjeao da je Hrvatska narodna banka u godinama prije krize aktivno vukla poteze, zahvaljujui kojima sada u krizi imamo financijsku stabilnost i manje problema u financijskom sektoru i da je nakon ulaska u krizu HNB ponovno aktivno djelovao, u okvirima svojih ovlasti, da olaka izlazak iz krize. Politika HNB-a je bila i jest- protuciklika. Monetarna politika moe biti podrka i dio rjeenja, ali sama ne moe biti rjeenje. Da bi se poveala investicijska aktivnost, zaposlenost i produktivnost i da bi se,dakle, iskoristio monetarni stimulus, potrebne su daljnje duboke reforme. Monetarne politike, kako ESB-a tako i HNB-a, mogu samo kupovati vrijeme za implementaciju reformi koje bi poveale konkurentnost zemalja EU-a koje zaostaju u ekonomskom rastu i razvoju. U Hrvatskoj, dok se to ne napravi, potencijalni rast bit e vrlo nizak, a oporavak vrlo spor.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: We are not out of danger yet
text: We're not out of danger yet. Published: 22.9.2021. Article by Governor Vujcic for views - The EUROFI Magazine, september 2021 edition In horror movies, every time the protagonist seemingly escapes from a tense situation, we can expect to be immediately ambushed by a new shock. On the way out of the dark forest of the protagonist, there is always something waiting for her own edge. The audience knows this, and yet time and time again they are surprised when the plot of the film meets their expectations. This scenario seems to be the sequenceof the outbreak of the pandemic after we have been through the global financial crisis, and could now be followed by the potential implications of the current pandemic crisis for financial stability. A remarkable economic recovery supported by vaccines and exceptional support from economic policies have mitigated the negative effects of the pandemic on the financial sector. Reforms implemented in the decade after the global financial crisis have also contributed to making the financial system part of the solution, not the source of the problem. Nevertheless, the worryof numbness is caused by potential problems lurking as we set foot towards the exit of the pandemic. And very similar to horror movies, we can not know in advance whether the sudden unusual noise in the bushes is just a small animal in passing or the "mother of all crises" as Roubini proclaims to us. "Complete torment" is the first warning sign of impending troubles - the number of corporate bankruptcies fell sharply during the pandemic, which is in complete contrast to all past crises. Exceptional public support and temporary favourable regulatory treatmenthave hampered the continuation of operations even for companies that would normally exit the market. Of course, in the conditions of such a major disruption, it is justified to postpone the bankruptcies of the enterprise until the uncertainty caused by the pandemic is somewhat reduced, and the inevitable bankruptcies are stretched over time to facilitate the redistribution of the workforce. But holding back for too long leads to the risk of zombification in much of the enterprise sector - another apt comparison with the film industry. Also,we can't know for sure what the final cost of the company's bankruptcies will be, once they do come due. Banks have created significant reserves for potential risks arising from covert NPLs, but residual risks will notbe able to be sufficiently reliably assessed until the very end of the pandemic. An unprecedented fiscal expansion has underpinned the business sector and protected household incomes from the crisis. The expansion has also burdened states with significant additional debt. The increase in indebtednesstakes place in the context of an unfinished banking union, with interdependence between the state and the banks still being one of the key vulnerabilities of the monetary union. The environment of long-term low interest rates has, however, facilitated the management of public debt, but the stateor budgets have already largely absorbed savings on interest costs, leaving only the risk that central banks will stop buying securities and that interest rates will increase. interest rates and thus facilitate interest payments, in such a scenario the risks of a sudden fall in the prices of financial assets are reinforced. For movie heroes, there is a long and growing list of things they should be doing, as well as those they should avoid. Unfortunately, the list of tasks for policyholders in the event of a financial crisis consists mainly of measures to be taken well in advance. Still, something can still be done to soften the blow. Bankruptcy proceedings are at the top of this list. In many Europeanemblems, the implementation of bankruptcies takes too long, creating losses for creditors while destroying economic value. Improving these procedures might not achieve much under normal conditions, but it would be very useful in the context of the post-crisis economic recovery . We also need to look again at risks that are gradually strengthening, such as price bubbles in the housing market. Macroprudential measures targeting the property market have been tightened again in a number of countries, contrary to the action of thisin the wake of the pandemic crisis. After all, the same principle applies to all other tools: in order to be able to apply them effectively in another crisis, we must begin to recreate the space for their use as soon as possible realistically. Only if we take thoseoracks will we be able to resist the monster that awaits us somewhere before we leave the forest, on the very edge of it.

Potpuni muk" prvi je znak upozorenja na predstojee nevolje - broj steajeva poduzea snano je pao tijekom pandemije, to je u potpunoj opreci sa svim prolim krizama. Iznimne javne potpora i privremeni povoljan regulatorni tretman omoguili su nastavak poslovanja ak i poduzeima koja bi u normalnim uvjetima izala s trita. Naravno, u uvjetima tako velikog poremeaja opravdano je odgoditi steajeve poduzea sve dok se neizvjesnost izazvana pandemijom donekle ne smanji, a neizbjene steajeve rastegnuti kroz vrijeme kako bi se olakala preraspodjela radne snage. Ali predugo zadravanje potpora dovodi do rizika zombifikacije u velikom dijelu sektora poduzea - to je jo jedna prikladna usporedba s filmskom industrijom. Takoer, trenutano ne moemo sa sigurnou znati koliki e biti konaan troak steajeva poduzea, kada jednom ipak dou na naplatu. Banke su stvorile znatne rezerve za potencijalne rizike koji proizlaze iz prikrivenih neprihodonosnih kredita, ali rezidualne rizike neemo moi dovoljno pouzdano procijeniti do samoga kraja pandemije. Dosad nezabiljeena fiskalna ekspanzija poduprla je sektor poduzea i zatitila prihode kuanstava od krize. Ekspanzija je ujedno opteretila drave znatnim dodatnim dugom. Poveanje zaduenosti odvija se u kontekstu nedovrene bankovne unije, pri emu je meuovisnost izmeu drave i banaka i nadalje jedna od kljunih ranjivosti monetarne unije. Okruje dugotrajno niskih kamatnih stopa olakalo je, dodue, upravljanje javnim dugom, ali su dravni prorauni ve uvelike apsorbirali utede na trokovima kamata, pa jo preostaje samo rizik da e sredinje banke prestati s kupovinom vrijednosnih papira i da e se kamatne stope poveati. ak i u sluaju da stope gospodarskog rasta prate poveanje inflacije i kamatnih stopa i tako olakaju plaanje kamata, u takvom scenariju jaaju rizici iznenadnog pada cijena financijske imovine. Za filmske junake postoji dug i rastui popis stvari koje bi trebali initi, kao i onih koje bi trebali izbjegavati. Naalost, popis zadataka za nositelje politike u sluaju financijske krize uglavnom se sastoji od mjera koje treba poduzeti znatno unaprijed. Ipak, jo se moe neto uiniti kako bi se ublaio udarac. Steajni postupci na vrhu su tog popisa. U mnogim europskim zemljama provedba steajeva predugo traje, to stvara gubitke vjerovnicima i pritom unitava ekonomsku vrijednost. Poboljanjem tih postupaka moda se ne bi mnogo postiglo u normalnim uvjetima, ali bi ono bilo vrlo korisno u kontekstu gospodarskog oporavka nakon krize. Isto tako, moramo ponovo sagledati rizike koji postupno jaaju, kao to su cjenovni baloni na tritu stambenih nekretnina. U nizu zemalja ponovo su pootrene makrobonitetnih mjere usmjerene na trite nekretnina, to je suprotno djelovanju tijekom pandemijske krize. Naposljetku, isto naelo vrijedi za sve ostale alate: da bismo ih mogli djelotvorno primijeniti u nekoj drugoj krizi, moramo zapoeti ponovo stvarati prostor za njihovo koritenje to je prije realno mogue. Samo ako poduzmemo te korake, moi emo se oduprijeti udovitu koje nas eka negdje prije izlaska iz ume, na samom njezinu rubu.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation at the conference Financing investments in Croatia - how can the European Investment Bank help?
text: Presentation by CNB Governor Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic at the conference Financing investments in Croatia - how can the European Investment Bank help? Published: 25.3.2014. Type Speaker Release Date Statement Event Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor 24.3.2014. Conference Financing investments in Croatia - how can the European Investment Bank help? Venue Zagreb Event date 24.3.2014. Dear guests, your Excellencies, distinguished representatives of the Government of the Republic of Croatia, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, I wish you a good day, I greet you nicely and thank you for your response to today's conference - the fourth in a series of conferences that we began to organize at the end of 2012, and the intention of which is to try to promote what we can call a 'new growth model' in Croatia. In cooperation with our Irish counterparts, we organized the first conference presenting the Irish experience in attracting foreign direct investment and promoting the financial center, we continued towork with the World Bank and the OECD in an effort to raise awareness of what structural reforms are, why they are important and where Croatia lags behind the most in creating a stimulating business climate. Finally, in November last year, we organized conferenceson the Swiss model of business climate and investment promotion, which had a more regional/cantonal character, to show how stimulating conditions for investments can be created at the local level. This time, the CNB organises the conference in cooperation with Europskom investment bank. The theme of today's conference is "Financing investments in Croatia - how can the European Investment Bank help?". You saw it on the billboard outside the entrance to the hall, given illustrated by a picture of the plane taking off. The previously announced Croatianplane investment was, unfortunately, lost even before takeoff. Investments have been in sharp decline for five years. Cumulatively, they decreased by 38.3 percent and thus, of all the components of GDP, contributed the most strongly to the recession . The belief, from the beginning of the mandate of this Vlada, as I warned back in 2012, that state investment would achieve economic recovery, turned out to be an illusion. This does not mean that public investments are necessary and always bad, although history teaches us that they are often very inefficient, but they cannot be the basis of what should be a 'sustainable growth model' of Croatia. Such a model must be based on private investments. The lack of private investments, namely, signals an unfavorable business climate, and in such conditions there will be no satisfactory maintenanceof vog growth. It seems that this has not yet been understood enough in Croatia, despite all the experiences closer and further past. It is my special honor and pleasure to extend my greeting and welcome to our guests from the European Investment Bank, Mr Scannapieco, Vice Presidentand Mrs. Revoltella, Director of Economic Research European Investment Banks, and our panelists today. The European Investment Bank has been present in Croatia for many years and does not need to be represented specifically. I would like to point out, however, its strong and growing activity in Croatia, which stands out among other international financial institutions in both absolute and relative terms. Namely, the EIB accounts for almost 50% of the total active investments in Croatia byamong national financial institutions. That is, as much as 75 percent, if one looks exclusively at net new financing of international financial institutions from the beginning of the global financial crisis to the present day, which in financial terms represents the amount of almost 1.5 billion euros. These figures speak best for themselves and here I take the opportunity to thank our guests from the European Investment Bank for their activities in Croatia so far. In addition to greatly appreciating their efforts so far, especially during the crisis, we also believe that in the coming period there is a wide scope for further intensification of EIB activities in Croatia, especially given the prolonged recession and the challenges facing the domestic economy, and the fact that Croatia as a new member of the European Union has limited experience and knowledge with the use of EU structural funds for now. In this sense, this conference today is a good opportunity to further emphasize the areas and needs for investments and financing m through open dialogue and discussion, which can also be a useful roadmap for the EIB for its further activities in Croatia. Before I leave my word to our guests, let me briefly address three issues in the context of the EIB's role in Croatia. First, when asked about establishing a(sustainable) growth model in Croatia. Secondly, the importance of investments in internationally exchangeable sectors as critical determinants of the establishment of a new growth model, and the possibility of financing them. And third, on the issue of financing small and medium-sized enterprises(SMEs). The current crisis shattered illusions, if any, that sustainable growth could be based on the "old" model, which relied largely on borrowing, consumption and investment in international indistinguishable sectors. The consequences of this previous growth model are felt in the form of rising unemployment, largely as a result of the contraction process of oversized and internationally weakly competitive sectors, which, along with still high indebtedness, and increased risk aversion , puts a significant strain on consumption and investment. This undoubtedly makes it difficult to emerge from the recession. And neither is the relatively weak and uncertain economic outlook in our environment, especially our major trading partners, in hand. Given these aggravating circumstances, for the dynamism of the transition to a new growth model, but also its success, the consistent and high-quality implementation of structural reforms aimed at establishing a more competitive business environment and a more favorable investmentclimate, which we talked about at previous conferences, has critical importance. These efforts should certainly be added to the importance of establishing a stable and predictable business environment, and to carrying out a credible consolidation of public finances, based on prudent reductionsin expenditure wounds. The goal of all these efforts is unique - to create preconditions for the dynamism of investment activities, especially those in export-oriented sectors. The goal of the entire state administration from central to local would have to be to encourage and help those who can and want to create new jobs. And here, as part of the second mentioned question, I come to the question of the possibilities and conditions of financing these investments. In doing so, large infrastructure investments, which normally require the support of the State and/or international financial institutions, should be distinguished from those of others. In the context of the latter, the Croatian National Bank plays an undisputed role. Since the beginning of the crisis, we have created a huge amount of additional liquidity, de facto at the zero interest rate, and we have reduced the regulatorni cost to banks to a third of that of the pre-crisis era, which has crucially affected that interest rates on loans have been at their historically low levels for some time. On the other hand, the central bank insists on preserving the high drop oftalization of the banking system, so that banks are willing to credit the new investment cycle once it starts. It should be noted that the new investment cycle and the related economic recovery is the one that entails the credit rast, and not vice versa, as suggested by numerous international experiences and research. But this does not mean that one should stand and wait in the conditions of stalled credit activity. With this in mind, the Croatian National Bank has tried several times since 2010 to wavewith unconventional monetary policy measures to support banks' lending activity. We took the last such initiative last November. Our experience so far, however, shows that such initiatives have partial success, which ismeager, since we are in a situation of reduced demand sitting down, and a high degree of aversion to risk-taking, on the other hand. But this is nothing new, monetary policy is often compared to a rope - 'it is easier to tighten it than to push it'. Under theseconditions, the revitalisation of banks' lending activities can be helped by the establishment of risk-sharing mechanisms, and this important role of catalyst can also be played by international financial institutions such as the EIB. In addition to being able to offer funds on termsmore substantial than market conditions, they can provide risk allocation mechanisms, thereby supporting access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises in particular. Finally, I would like to touch on the EIB's initiative for financing small and medium-sized enterprises, whichunfortunately for now in the EU, including in Croatia, has not aroused sufficient attention and thus received adequate support. Given the economic importance of SMEs in Croatia, which is reflected in the fact that they employ two-thirds of the employed workforce, that unlike large enterprises they generate new jobs and generate 50% of the total revenue according to the data for 2012, and also in view of the fact that during the current economic crisis (in conditions of increased ave risk appetite) it is these companies that have been most affected by reduced access to finance, this is also an opportunity to re-update the issue of the guarantee scheme for lending to SMEs, for which EU funds would be used. Such a scheme band could encourage lending to small and medium-sized enterprises, which have a problem of lack of capital and collateral. The modalities of the use of structural funds for this purpose, through the EIB, HBOR, or otherwise, should be decided by the Government, but believeme that the use of part of the funds for this purpose would make it easier for the use of loans to this vital sector of the economy, and on the other hand increase the utilization of EU funds. In the belief that these and some similar initiatives can come to life in Croatia, I would like to thank you for your attention and invite Mr. scannapieco and asked him to present us with an EIB report on investments and financing in Europe with a special focus on EIB activities in Croatia.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a prof. dr. Borisa Vujia na konferenciji Financiranje ulaganja u Hrvatskoj - kako Europska investicijska banka moe pomoi? Objavljeno: 25.3.2014. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a 24.3.2014. Konferencija Financiranje ulaganja u Hrvatskoj - kako Europska investicijska banka moe pomoi? Mjesto dogaanja Zagreb Datum dogaanja 24.3.2014. Potovani uzvanici, vae ekselencije, uvaeni predstavnici Vlade Republike Hrvatske, dame i gospodo, elim vam dobar dan, lijepo vas pozdravljam i zahvaljujem na vaem odzivu na dananju konferenciju - etvrtu u seriji konferencija koje smo poeli organizirati krajem 2012., a namjera kojih je pokuati promovirati ono to moemo nazvati 'novim modelom rasta' u Hrvatskoj. U suradnji s irskim kolegama organizirali smo prvu konferenciju predstavljajui irsko iskustvo u privlaenju stranih izravnih ulaganja i promociji financijskog centra, nastavili smo u suradnji sa Svjetskom bankom i OECD-om u nastojanju buenja svijesti o tome to su to strukturne reforme, zato su vane i gdje to Hrvatska najvie zaostaje u kreiranju poticajne poslovne klime. Napokon, u studenom prole godine, organizirali smo konferenciju o vicarskom modelu promocije poslovne klime i investicija, koji je imao vie regionalni/kantonalni karakter, da bi pokazali kako se na lokalnoj razini mogu stvarati poticajni uvjeti za ulaganja. Ovog puta HNB konferenciju organizira u suradnji s Europskom investicijskom bankom. Tema dananje konferencije je "Financiranje ulaganja u Hrvatskoj - kako Europska investicijska banka moe pomoi?". Vidjeli ste na panou pred ulazom u dvoranu, daju ilustrira slika aviona koji polijee. Ranije najavljivani hrvatski avion investicija se, naalost, izgubio i prije polijetanja. Investicije su u snanom padu ve pet godina. Kumulativno su se smanjile za 38,3 posto i time, od svih komponenti BDP-a, najsnanije pridonijele recesiji . Vjerovanje, s poetka mandata ove Vlade, na to sam upozoravao jo 2012., da e se dravnim investicijama ostvariti gospodarski oporavak, pokazalo se iluzijom. To ne znai da su javne investicije neophodno i uvijek loe, iako nas povijest ui da su esto vrlo neefikasne, no one ne mogu biti temelj onoga to bi trebao biti 'odriv model rasta' Hrvatske. Takav model se mora temeljiti na privatnim investicijama. Nedostatak privatnih investicija, naime, signalizira nepovoljnu poslovnu klimu, a u takvim uvjetima nee biti ni zadovoljavajueg odrivog rasta. Izgleda da to u Hrvatskoj jo nije dovoljno shvaeno, unato svim iskustvima blie i dalje prolosti. Posebna mi je ast i zadovoljstvo uputiti pozdrav i dobrodolicu naim gostima iz Europske investicijske banke, gospodinu Scannapieco-u, potpredsjedniku i gospoi Revoltella, direktorici za ekonomska istraivanja Europske investicijske banke, te naim dananjim panelistima. Europska investicijska banka prisutna je u Hrvatskoj ve dugi niz godina i nije ju potrebno posebno predstavljati. Izdvojio bih ipak njenu snanu i rastuu aktivnost u Hrvatskoj, koja se istie meu ostalim meunarodnim financijskim institucijama i u apsolutnom i u relativnom pogledu. Naime, na EIB otpada gotovo 50 posto od sveukupnih aktivnih ulaganja u Hrvatsku od strane meunarodnih financijskih institucija. Odnosno, ak 75 posto, ako se promatra iskljuivo neto novo financiranje meunarodnih financijskih institucija od poetka globalne financijske krize do danas, to u financijskom smislu predstavlja iznos od gotovo 1,5 mlrd. eura. Te brojke najbolje govore same za sebe i ovdje koristim prigodu zahvaliti se naim gostima iz Europske investicijske banke na njihovim dosadanjim aktivnostima u Hrvatskoj. Osim to iznimno cijenimo njihove dosadanje napore, napose tijekom krize, ujedno vjerujemo da u nadolazeem razdoblju postoji irok prostor za daljnje intenziviranje aktivnosti EIB-a u Hrvatskoj, posebice s obzirom na produljenu recesiju i izazove s kojima se domae gospodarstvo susree, te injenicu da Hrvatska kao nova lanica Europske unije ima za sada ograniena iskustva i znanja s koritenjem strukturnih fondova EU. U tom smislu je ova dananja konferencija dobra prigoda da se kroz otvoren dijalog i raspravu dodatno naglase podruja i potrebe za investicijama te financiranjem, to ujedno moe biti koristan putokaz EIB-u za njegove daljnje aktivnosti u Hrvatskoj. Prije nego to prepustim rije naim gostima, dozvolite mi da se kratko osvrnem na tri pitanja u kontekstu uloge EIB-a u Hrvatskoj. Prvo, na pitanje uspostavljanja novog (odrivog) modela rasta u Hrvatskoj. Drugo, na vanost investicija u meunarodno razmjenljive sektore kao kritine odrednice uspostavljanja novog modela rasta, te mogunosti njihova financiranja. I tree, na pitanje financiranja malih i srednjih poduzea (SME). Aktualna kriza je razbila iluzije, ako su one uope postojale, da se odriv rast moe zasnivati na "starom" modelu, koji se najveim dijelom oslanjao na zaduivanju, potronji i investicijama u meunarodno nerazmjenljive sektore. Posljedice tog prijanjeg modela rasta osjeamo u vidu rastue nezaposlenosti, u velikoj mjeri kao posljedice procesa kontrakcije predimenzioniranih i meunarodno slabo konkurentnih sektora, koja, uz jo uvijek visoku zaduenost, te poveanu averziju prema riziku, znaajno optereuje potronju i investicije. To bez sumnje oteava izlazak iz recesije. A, ne idu mu na ruku ni jo uvijek relativno slabi i neizvjesni gospodarski izgledi u naem okruenju, posebice naim glavnim trgovinskim partnerima. Imajui u vidu te otegotne okolnosti, za dinamiziranje prelaska na novi model rasta, ali i njegov uspjeh, kritinu vanost ima dosljedno i kvalitetno provoenje strukturnih reformi usmjerenih k uspostavljanju konkurentnijeg poslovnog okruenja i povoljnije investicijske klime, o emu smo govorili na prethodnim konferencijama. Tim naporima svakako treba pridodati vanost uspostavljanja stabilnog i predvidivog poslovnog okruja, te provoenje vjerodostojne konsolidacije javnih financija, temeljene na razboritom reduciranju rashoda. Cilj svih tih napora je jedinstven - stvaranje preduvjeta za dinamiziranje investicijskih aktivnosti, posebice onih u izvozno orijentirane sektore. Cilj cjelokupne dravne administracije od centralne do lokalne morao bi biti poticaj i pomo onima koji mogu i ele otvarati nova radna mjesta. I tu, u okviru drugospomenutog pitanja, dolazim do pitanja mogunosti i uvjeta financiranja tih investicija. Pritom treba razlikovati velike infrastrukturne investicije, koje uobiajeno zahtijevaju potporu drave i/ili meunarodnih financijskih institucija, od onih ostalih. U kontekstu potonjih, Hrvatska narodna banka ima nespornu ulogu. Mi smo od poetka krize kreirali ogromnu koliinu dodatne likvidnosti, de facto po nultoj kamatnoj stopi, te smo regulatorni troak za banke smanjili na treinu onog iz vremena prije krize, to je kljuno utjecalo na to da se kamatne stope na kredite ve neko vrijeme nalaze na njihovim povijesno niskim razinama. S druge strane, sredinja banka ustraje na ouvanju visoke kapitaliziranosti bankovnog sustava, da bi banke bile spremne kreditno podrati novi investicijski ciklus jednom kad on otpone. Valja pritom naglasiti daje novi investicijski ciklus i s njime povezani gospodarski oporavak taj koji za sobom povlai kreditni rast, a ne obratno, to sugeriraju brojna meunarodna iskustva i istraivanja. No, to ne znai da treba stajati i ekati u uvjetima zastoja kreditne aktivnosti. Imajui upravo to u vidu, Hrvatska narodna banka je jo od 2010. godine u nekoliko navrata pokuavala nekonvencionalnim mjerama monetarne politike potpomoi kreditnu aktivnost banaka. Posljednju takvu inicijativu smo poduzeli u studenom prole godine. Nae dosadanje iskustvo, meutim, pokazuje da takve inicijative imaju djelomian uspjeh, to je razumljivo, budui da se nalazimo u situaciji smanjene potranje sjedne, te visokog stupnja odbojnosti prema preuzimanju rizika, s druge strane. No, to nije nita novo, monetarna politika se esto usporeuje s uetom - "lake ga je zatezati, nego gurati'. U takvim uvjetima, revitalizaciji kreditne aktivnosti banaka moe pomoi uspostavljanje mehanizama podjele rizika, a tu vanu ulogu katalizatora mogu igrati i meunarodne financijske institucije poput EIB-a. One osim to mogu ponuditi sredstva po uvjetima povoljnijim od trinih, mogu osigurati mehanizme raspodjele rizika, potpomaui time pristup financiranju naroito manjim i srednje velikim poduzeima. Time se, na kraju, elim dotaknuti i EIB-ove inicijative za financiranje malih i srednjih poduzea, koja naalost za sada u EU, pa tako ni u Hrvatskoj, nije pobudila dostatnu panju, a time ni zadobila adekvatnu potporu. S obzirom na gospodarski znaaj malih i srednjih poduzea u Hrvatskoj, koji se ogleda u injenici da ona zapoljavaju dvije treine zaposlene radne snage, da za razliku od velikih poduzea ona generiraju nova radna mjesta i da ostvaruju 50 posto ukupnog prihoda prema podacima za 2012. godinu, te isto tako s obzirom na injenicu da su se tijekom aktualne gospodarske krize (u uvjetima pojaane averzije prema riziku) upravo ta poduzea najvie nala na udaru smanjenog pristupa financiranju, ovo je prigoda i za ponovnu aktualizaciju pitanja garancijske sheme za kreditiranje malih i srednjih poduzea, za koju bi se koristila sredstva EU. Takva shema bi mogla potaknuti kreditiranje malih i srednjih poduzea, koja imaju problem nedostatka kapitala i kolaterala. O modalitetima koritenja strukturnih fondova za tu namjenu, putem EIB-a, HBOR-a, ili na neki drugi nain, odluku treba donijeti Vlada, no vjerujem da bi koritenje dijela sredstava za tu namjenu sjedne strane omoguilo laku dostupnost kredita tom vitalnom sektoru gospodarstva, a s druge povealo iskoritenost EU fondova. U uvjerenju da ta kao i neke sline inicijative mogu zaivjeti u Hrvatskoj, zahvalio bih vam se na panji i pozvao gosp. Scannapieco-a i zamolio ga da nam predstavi EIB-ovo izvjee o investicijama i financiranju u Europi s posebnim naglaskom na EIB-ove aktivnosti u Hrvatskoj.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation at the conference of the Croatian Exporters Association
text: Presentation by CNB Governor Dr. Zeljko Rohatinski at the conference of the Croatian Exporters Association Published: 10.11.2008. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 7.11.2008. Conference of the Association Croatian Exporters Zagreb 7.11.2008. 1) Three questions are most often asked of the monetary authority from among the exporters: 95 whether the CNB will encourage exports and restrict imports through real exchange rate depreciation; 95 whether to selectively treat export credits and exempt them from general restrictions on placement growth; 95 will it create the conditions for a selective reduction in interest rates on such loans? The answer to all three questions is negative. Mala, open, highly euroised, but also highly indebted and taxes-heavy country cannot afford this kind of selectivity, nor would it be of much use. That is why, instead of bidding on what others should learn in the current situationor for us, let's ask ourselves the question of our own responsibility for the economic situation in the country and what each of us can do to change it. Not out of patriotic altruism, but out of pure egotism, because we all share the same fate. And without the IMF, it is now at least clear, or it should be clear, that we can only solve problems through the coordinated efforts of all economic actors. States, banks, funds, trade unions, entrepreneurs. Otherwise, the problems will escalate and take us back many years. 2) Existing situation: (a) 2008 is a turning point year, which many are already comparing with 1929, after which more nothing stayed the same. Neither economically nor politically, although in these comparisons it should not go too far. (b) However, the fact is that the current financial crisis has not only "hindered" investment banking and significantly weakened the overall financial sector, but is: 95 "demolished" the key lever of the entire economic expansion financing pattern over the last 20 years, a pattern that has increasingly taken on the characteristics of financial engineering, independent of economic funds; 95 discredited this and neoliberalist ideology, which has since become global, and the problems have become global. These changes will have a long-term effect, both in the material-financial andregulatory, as well as in psychological terms. (c) Direct effects of the crisis: 95 The 'blowing of the bubble' in the real estate and capital markets had a negative 'welfare effect', i.e. it reduced the assets of market players, which was not only collateral for their liabilities but also the basis for further investments. The pumping of liquidity by states and central banks to the resolution of some of these losses has only partly reduced the problem of reduced availability and mobility of capital to finance future development. My own, especially the wayin. 95 Falling prices in these markets have redirected some of the speculative capital to the market for lower elasticity commodities (oil, food), stimulating first rapid growth and then volatility of their prices. This has hit current incomes and slowed the real demand of financiranu these incomes. 95 The combination of these two elements has resulted in the appearance of stagflation, which threatens to escalate into a recession with deflation. Thus, the financial crisis radicalized problems in the sphere of funds that were previously relatively subdued and significantly complicated the possibility and increased the social cost of solving them. In general, and above all in the countries of net importers of capital. 3) The impact on Croatia so far (two aspects supported by its own "efforts"): (a) Increase in input costs on a basis per energyand raw material accumulation for the food industry from imports. This, in turn, was "successfully followed up" by domestic factors in the supply sphere, as well as by factors in the sphere of demand induced by an increase in disposable income in the time before and immediately after a coupleof lamentary elections. Consequence: the average inflation rate in the second half of 2007 and the first half of 2008 of 0.7% per month. Twice as much as in the euro zone, not only in the aggregate, which is influenced by differences in the structure of consumer baskets, but also by themajority of individual products and services.
