This trend has now stopped, with the annual inflation rate estimated to be "only" around 4.2% in December (5.8%) a year earlier, but the average annual inflation rate has increased from 2.9% to 6.2%. This is areal stagnation of the average wage as a basic component of the disposable income of the population, and as capital incomes have also decreased, personal consumption slows growth from 6.2% in 2007 at just 2.1% in 2008. This, despite faster growthinvesticies and government spending, also slows down the growth of aggregate demand in the domestic market from 5.8% last year to 4.4% this year. The slowdown would have been even greater had it not been for "restrictive" monetary policy. Namely, although the ongoing nominal growth in bank placements is flatand corporate slowed from 15% in 2007 to about 10% in 2008, the average real level of these placements is higher this year by 4.7% compared to last year, so credit growth continues to provide significant support for the financing of domestic consumption. To this should be addedthe effect of substitution of domestic borrowing of the corporate sector to foreign ones, so that total loans to the private non-financial sector, although slow, are still growing in real terms at a high annual rate of about 12% (b) The slowdown in export demand, to which - similar todomestic demand - the negative contribution was made by domestic price policy. Especially in the services sector. Thus, real growth in exports of goods and services slowed from 5.7% in 2007 to 3.8% in 2008. At the same time, imports (from 5.8% to 5.0%) also slowed somewhat ,but the rast negative balance in foreign exchanges accelerated in real terms from 6.1% in 2007 to 12.1% in 2008. (c) In such a combination of degressive movements in domestic demand and exchanges with foreign countries, gross domestic product growth slows from 5.6% in 2007 toa noticeable 3.3% in 2008, within which the annual rate slows from 3.8% in the first half to, it is estimated, only 2.8% in the second half of this year. Together with the slowdown in economic activity, foreign exchange imbalances are also increasing, with the deficit in the exchange of goods and services increasing from 8.4% to 9.4%, and the current account deficit of the balance of payments from 8.6% to 10% of gross domestic product (804.2bn). In order to finance such a trade deficit with an overdue repayment of the principal of foreign debt of 807.3bn and interest of 801.5bn, in addition to foreign direct investment, Croatia used foreign credit sources totalling 8012.1bn in 2008, net increasing its foreign debt from 8033.3bn to 8037bn(88.2% of GDP) While, from the point of view of the impact of the global financial crisis, the increase in the average annual inflation rate can be treated as a short-term "episode", foreign trade imbalance and high dependence on foreign sources of financing of debtare timeline structural problems that substantially determine the economic vulnerability of the country and which are radically potentiated by the current financial crisis in the world. 4) Three key issues to go into 2009 (a) Security of the banking system, which implies: resistantst to internal shocks It has been successfully demonstrated by banks over the past month thanks to liquidity reserves and high capitalisation and it will remain unquestionable. In this regard, all measures of prudential and monetary character that have contributed to this resilience, including decisions on capital adequacy and limiting placement growth, remain in place and, where appropriate, will be further tightened in terms of currency-induced credit risk. On the other hand, we expect that the next tone CNB Council will adopt a new Decision on a short-term liquidity loan, which significantly simplifies the possibility of granting such loans to solvent banks on the basis of pledges of securities of the Ministry of Finance, bonds of the Republic of Croatia and other acceptanceof able debt instruments. 95 protection against systemic risk Given the degree of euroisation of the banking system, the basic systemic risk is a change in the exchange rate. Both in bank assets in loans with a currency clause, as well as in savings in the liabilities of banks where depreciation expectations can trigger currency substitution and withdrawal of deposits. That is why it is in the interest of the banks themselves to maintain the stability of the exchange rate, in which the CNB will fully support them. 95 spillover of problems with parent banks to their branches With theview that over 90% of the banking system in Croatia is owned by foreign banks, the activities undertaken by the EU to consolidate their operations in their home countries significantly reduce the risk spillover of their problems to branches in Croatia, including the risk of extracting supplementary capital and deposits from the domestic banking system. So far, there are no indications to suggest this, and as a clear precaution, the CNB also has safeguards in place under Article 47 and 48. Foreign Exchange Act to prevent this. However, even assuming a realistic assumption of a completely responsible relationship between mother banks and the operations of their subsidiaries in Croatia, it is difficult to expect their previous generousness in supplying branches with liquidvima and capital that significantly increased their credit potential. This brings us to a fundamental problem in 2009: (b) External financial constraints As the repayment of the principal of foreign debt of EUR 9.4 billion is due in the coming year. euro and interest of EUR 1.7 billion. euro, which is 27% higher in total than in 2008, keeping the gross use of foreign loans at this year's level of around 8012bn leaves no room for financing from this source of any deficit growth in the exchange of goods and services with foreign countries. Given the increasing constraints in the sphere of export demand, this practically requires a significant slowdown in imports and an adjustment in domestic demand, with an appropriate impact on a further slowdown in economic activity. Not only that: in the conditions of the financialcrisis in the world, the possibility of obtaining credit funds will depend more than ever not only on their availability on global financial markets, but also on the credibility of the debtor country regarding its ability to properly service allobligations. Previously, stand-by arrangements with the IMF were an indicator of this credibility, now we must provide this credibility ourselves through coordinated and consistent action of all economic factors in the country. At the same time, due to the expected decrease in foreign direct investment, for the orderly financing of reproduction flows in the country and current payments to foreign countries, it will be necessary to engage to some extent its own liquidity reserves, and significantly increase the efficiency of their use. In this regard, the CNB isable to pursue a very active policy of maintaining the liquidity of the financial system to limits that will not stimulate inflation, using, if necessary, all available instruments: reducing the reserve requirement rate, reducing the degree of minimum necessary foreign exchangerisks of livelihoods, expanding operations on the open market and to part of the bonds of the Republic of Croatia and, as a last line of defense, hiring the foreign reserves of the central bank. However, in order for such liquidity broadcasting to be productive, it is necessary to meet some key conditions: 1. maintaining the stability of the exchange rate If it did not become everyone's concern, the CNB would have to defend it itself, in which case - choosing the lesser evil - it would withdraw kuna liquidity instead of broadcasting. 2. keeping your own financial resources safe We will propose to the Government to revoke theprocedure for amending the Foreign Exchange Act in terms of deferring 1.1.2009. envisaged liberalisation of part of capital affairs with foreign countries (opening accounts of legal entities abroad and using foreign loans through these accounts, granting shortterm-term financial loans not residents, carrying out transactions in foreign exchange markets abroad, dealing with derivative financial instruments, entering and presenting materialised securities, payment and collection in cash, giving a pokl she and help abroad...). We expect HANFA to also take appropriate measures in the sphere of pension and investment fund operations. 3. preventing the effect of crowding companies out of financial markets - balancing the budget of the consolidated general state, including any late payments that reduce the liquidity of the real sector. 4. Effective changes in banks' credit and interest rate policy in accordance with the intentions of the Credit Risk Management Guidelines resulting from placements to households. 5. the contribution of trade unions towards reducing the deficit in foreign exchanges and pressures on liquidity. (c) Movements in a real environment According to the usually quite accurate forecasts from Deutsche Bank's World Outlook as of 3 October, the euro zone is forecast for 2009: 95 GDP and personal consumption -0.2% (2008 rating 1.0% and 0.2%) 95 Investment-2.8% (1.4%) 95 Exports 2.3% (3.6%) 95 Imports 2.1% (3.0%) 95 Unemployment rate 8.0% (7.4%) 95 Inflation 2.3% (3.5%) These are key real problems that domestic exporters will have to deal with and in which the CNB can only help them by maintaining the general liquidity of the domestic financial system and price stability, and not by some specific, selective, measures. If we succeed in solving these problems, in 2009 we can expect: a growth in gross domesticg products of about 2%, in which personal consumption of 1.6%, exports of goods and services by 3.1%, and imports for 1.4%. The balance of payments deficit would drop to 9.2% of GDP, while foreign debt would reach the level of EUR 38.5bn. euro or about 89% of GDP. The average annual rate of inflawould drop to 3.5%. So, nothing that would make us happy, but also far less bad than what is in some other countries, and that can come here if we do not snap in time. In that case, even an arrangement with the IMF would not be likely to be enoughto prevent the country from entering stagnation or even recession.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a dr. eljka Rohatinskog na konferenciji udruge Hrvatski izvoznici Objavljeno: 10.11.2008. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 7.11.2008. Konferencija udruge Hrvatski izvoznici Zagreb 7.11.2008. 1) Tri pitanja najee se postavljaju monetarnoj vlasti iz redova izvoznika:  hoe li HNB realnom deprecijacijom teaja poticati izvoz i ograniavati uvoz;  hoe li selektivno tretirati kredite za izvoz i izuzeti ih iz opih ogranienja rasta plasmana;  hoe li stvoriti uvjete za selektivno smanjenje kamatnih stopa na takve kredite? Odgovor na sva tri pitanja je negativan. Mala, otvorena, visoko eurizirana, ali i visoko zaduena te porezima visoko optereena zemlja ne moe si priutiti takvu vrstu selektivnosti, niti bi od nje bilo neke velike koristi. Zato, umjesto da licitiramo to bi u postojeoj situaciji drugi trebali uiniti za nas, postavimo si pitanje vlastite odgovornosti za ekonomsko stanje u zemlji i to svatko od nas moe uiniti da se ono promijeni. Ne iz domoljubnog altruizma, ve iz istog egoizma, jer svi dijelimo istu sudbinu. I bez MMF-a, sada je barem jasno, ili bi trebalo biti jasno, kako probleme moemo rjeavati jedino koordiniranim naporima svih ekonomskih aktera. Drave, banaka, fondova, sindikata, poduzetnika. U protivnom, problemi e eskalirati i vratiti nas dosta godina unatrag. 2) Postojea situacija: (a) 2008. je prijelomna godina, koju mnogi ve usporeuju sa 1929. nakon koje vie nita nije ostalo isto. Ni u ekonomskom ni u politikom smislu, iako u tim usporedbama ne treba ii predaleko. (b) Meutim, injenica je da aktualna financijska kriza ne samo da je "pomela" investicijsko bankarstvo i bitno oslabila ukupan financijski sektor, ve je:  "sruila" kljunu polugu cijelog obrasca financiranja ekonomske ekspanzije u posljednjih 20-tak godina, obrasca koji je sve vie poprimao obiljeja financijskog inenjeringa, neovisnog od ekonomskih fundamenata;  diskreditirala time i neoliberalistiku ideologiju, koja je u meuvremenu postala globalna, pa su i problemi postali globalni. Te promjene imat e dugoroni uinak, kako u materijalno- financijskom i regulatornom, tako i u psiholokom pogledu. (c) Neposredni efekti krize:  "Ispuhavanje balona" na tritima nekretnina i kapitala imalo je negativni "welfare uinak" tj. smanjilo je imovinu aktera na tritima, koja ne samo da je bila kolateral za njihove obveze ve i osnova za daljnja ulaganja. Upumpavanje likvidnosti od strane drava i sredinjih banaka u sanaciju dijela tih gubitaka tek je dijelom umanjiloproblem smanjene raspoloivosti i mobilnosti kapitala za financiranje budueg razvoja. Vlastitog, a pogotovo tueg.  Pad cijena na tim tritima preusmjerio je dio spekulativnog kapitala na trite roba nie elastinosti (nafta, hrana), potaknuvi prvo brzi rast, a zatim volatilnost njihovih cijena. To je pogodilo tekue dohotke i usporila realnu potranju financiranu tim dohocima.  Kombinacija tih dvaju elemenata rezultirala je pojavom stagflacije koja prijeti prerastanjem u recesiju s deflacijom. Dakle, financijska kriza radikalizirala je probleme u sferi fundamenata koji su prije bili relativno prigueni i znatno oteala mogunost te poveala socijalnu cijenu njihovog rjeavanja. Openito, a nadasve u zemljama neto uvoznicama kapitala. 3) Dosadanji utjecaj na Hrvatsku (dva aspekta podrana i vlastitim "naporima"): (a) Rast ulaznih trokova po osnovi poskupljenja energenata i sirovina za prehrambenu industriju iz uvoza. Na to su se pak "uspjeno nadovezali" domai initelji u sferi ponude, ali i initelji u sferi potranje inducirani poveanjem raspoloivih dohodaka u vrijeme prije i neposredno nakon parlamentarnih izbora. Posljedica: prosjena stopa inflacije u drugom polugoditu 2007. i prvom polugoditu 2008. od 0,7% mjeseno. Dvostruko vie nego u euro zoni, i to ne samo u agregatu, na koji utjeu razlike u strukturi potroakih koarica, ve i kod veine pojedinanih proizvoda i usluga. Taj je trend sada zaustavljen, pa se ocjenjuje da e godinja stopa inflacije u prosincu iznositi "samo" oko 4,2% (godinu dana ranije 5,8%), ali je prosjena godinja stopa inflacije poveana sa 2,9% na 6,2%. To je dovelo do realne stagnacije prosjene plae kao osnovne komponente raspoloivog dohotka stanovnitva, a kako su istodobno smanjeni i kapitalski prihodi, osobna potronja usporava rast sa 6,2% u 2007. na samo 2,1% u 2008. godini. To, unato brem rastu investicija i potronje drave, usporava i rast agregatne potranje na domaem tritu sa 5,8% u proloj na 4,4% u ovoj godini. Usporavanje bi bilo jo vee da nije bilo "restriktivne" monetarne politike. Naime, iako je tekui nominalni rast plasmana banaka stanovnitvu i poduzeima usporen sa 15% u 2007. na oko 10% u 2008. godini, prosjena realna razina tih plasmana via je u ovoj u odnosu na prolu godinu za 4,7%, tako da rast kredita i dalje prua znaajnu podrku financiranju domae potronje. Tome treba dodati i efekt supstitucije domaeg zaduivanja sektora poduzea inozemnim, tako da ukupni krediti privatnom nefinancijskom sektoru, iako usporeni, jo uvijek realno rastu po visokoj godinjoj stopi od oko 12% (b) Usporavanje izvozne potranje, emu je - slino kao i kod domae potranje - negativni doprinos dala i domaa politika cijena. Posebno u sektoru usluga. Tako je realni rast izvoza roba i usluga usporio sa 5,7% u 2007. na 3,8% u 2008. godini. Istodobno, neto je usporen i uvoz (sa 5,8% na 5,0%), ali je rast negativnog salda u razmjeni s inozemstvom u realnom izrazu ubrzan sa 6,1% u 2007. na 12,1% u 2008. godini. (c) U takvoj kombinaciji degresivnog kretanja domae potranje i razmjene s inozemstvom, rast bruto domaeg proizvoda usporava se sa 5,6% u 2007. na prosjenih 3,3% u 2008. godini, unutar koje se godinja stopa usporava sa 3,8% u prvom polugoditu na, ocjenjuje se, samo 2,8% u drugom polugoditu ove godine. Zajedno s usporavanjem ekonomske aktivnosti, poveavaju se i neravnotee u razmjeni s inozemstvom, u okviru kojih se deficit u razmjeni roba i usluga poveava sa 8,4% na 9,4%, a deficit tekueg rauna platne bilance sa 8,6% na 10% bruto domaeg proizvoda (4,2 mlrd. eura). Da bi mogla financirati takav trgovinski deficit uz dospjelu otplatu glavnice inozemnog duga od 7,3 mlrd. eura i kamata od 1,5 mlrd eura, pored izravnih stranih ulaganja, Hrvatska je u 2008. godini koristila inozemne kreditne izvore u ukupnom iznosu od 12,1 mlrd. eura, neto poveavi svoj inozemni dug sa 33,3 na 37 mlrd. eura (88,2% BDP-a) I dok se, promatrano s aspekta utjecaja svjetske financijske krize, poveanje prosjene godinje stope inflacije moe tretirati kao kratkorona "epizoda", vanjskotrgovinska neravnotea i visoka ovisnost od inozemnih izvora financiranja dugoroni su strukturni problemi koji bitno determiniraju ekonomsku ranjivost zemlje i koje aktualna financijska kriza u svijetu radikalno potencira. 4) Tri kljuna pitanja s kojima se ulazi u 2009. godinu (a) Sigurnost bankovnog sustava, koja podrazumijeva: otpornost na unutarnje okove Nju su banke uspjeno demonstrirale tijekom proteklih mjesec dana zahvaljujui rezervama likvidnosti i visokoj kapitaliziranosti i ona e i dalje ostati neupitna. S tim u vezi, sve mjere prudencijalnog i monetarnog karaktera koje su pridonijele toj otpornosti, ukljuujui odluke o adekvatnosti kapitala i ograniavanju rasta plasmana, i dalje ostaju na snazi, a po potrebi e biti i dodatno zaotrene u pogledu valutno induciranog kreditnog rizika. S druge strane, oekujemo da e idui tjedan Savjet HNB-a donijeti novu Odluku o kratkoronom kreditu za likvidnost, kojom se bitno pojednostavljuje mogunost odobravanja takvih kredita solventnim bankama na osnovi zaloga vrijednosnih papira Ministarstva financija, obveznica RH i drugih prihvatljivih dunikih instrumenata.  zatitu od sistemskog rizika S obzirom na stupanj euriziranosti bankovnog sustava, osnovni sistemski rizik predstavlja promjena teaja. Kako u aktivi banaka kod kredita s valutnom klauzulom, tako i kod tednje u pasivi banaka gdje deprecijacijska oekivanja mogu potaknutu valutnu supstituciju i povlaenje depozita. Zato je u interesu samih banaka odravati stabilnost teaja, u emu e ih HNB potpuno podravati.  prelijevanje problema s matinih banaka na njihove podrunice S obzirom da je preko 90% bankovnog sustava u Hrvatskoj u vlasnitvu inozemnih banaka, aktivnosti koje EU poduzima za konsolidaciju njihovog poslovanja u matinim zemljama znaajno smanjuje i rizik prelijevanja njihovih problema na podrunice u Hrvatskoj, ukljuujui rizik izvlaenja dopunskog kapitala i depozita iz domaeg bankovnog sustava. Za sada nema nikakvih naznaka koje bi na to upuivale, a iz iste predostronosti HNB ima u pripremi i zatitne mjere po lanku 47. i 48. Zakona o deviznom poslovanju kojima bi to sprijeio.Meutim, i uz realnu pretpostavku o potpuno odgovornom odnosu banaka-majki prema poslovanju njihovih podrunica u Hrvatskoj, teko se moe oekivati njihova dosadanja izdanost u opskrbljivanju podrunica likvidnim sredstvima i kapitalom kojim se znatnije poveao kreditni potencijal. To nas dovodi do temeljnog problema u 2009. godini: (b) Vanjska financijska ogranienja Kako u iduoj godini dospijeva otplata glavnice inozemnog duga od 9,4 mlrd. eura i kamata od 1,7 mlrd. eura, to je ukupno za 27% vie nego u 2008. godini, zadravanje bruto koritenja inozemnih kredita na ovogodinjoj razini od oko 12 mlrd. eura ne ostavlja prostor za financiranje iz tog izvora bilo kakvog rasta deficita u razmjeni roba i usluga s inozemstvom. S obzirom na sve izraenija ogranienja u sferi izvozne potranje, to praktiki zahtijeva bitno usporavanje uvoza i prilagoavanje domae potranje, s odgovarajuim utjecajem i na daljnje usporavanje privredne aktivnosti. I ne samo to: u uvjetima financijske krize u svijetu, mogunost pribavljanja kreditnih sredstava vie e nego ikada zavisiti ne samo od njihove raspoloivosti na svjetskim financijskim tritima nego i od vjerodostojnosti zemlje dunika u pogledu njezine sposobnosti da uredno servisira svoje obveze. Prije su indikator te vjerodostojnosti bili i stand-by aranmani s MMF-om, sada tu vjerodostojnost moramo pruiti sami koordiniranim i konzistentnim djelovanjem svih ekonomskih initelja u zemlji. Istodobno e, zbog oekivanog smanjenja izravnih stranih ulaganja, za uredno financiranje tokova reprodukcije u zemlji i tekua plaanja prema inozemstvu biti potrebno u odreenoj mjeri angairati i vlastite rezerve likvidnosti, te bitno poveati efikasnost njihovog koritenja. S tim u vezi, HNB je spreman voditi vrlo aktivnu politiku odravanja likvidnosti financijskog sustava do granica koje nee poticati inflaciju, koristei prema potrebi sve raspoloive instrumente: smanjenje stope obvezne priuve, smanjenje stupnja minimalno potrebnih deviznih potraivanja, proirenje operacija na otvorenom tritu i na dio obveznica RH te, kao zadnja linija obrane, angairanje deviznih priuva sredinje banke. Meutim, da bi takvo emitiranje likvidnosti bilo produktivno, potrebno je da se ispune neki kljuni uvjeti: 1. zadravanje stabilnosti teaja Ako ona ne bi postala briga sviju, HNB bi je morao braniti sam, u kom bi sluaju - birajui manje zlo - umjesto emitiranja povlaio kunsku likvidnost. 2. uvanje vlastitih financijskih resursa Predloit emo Vladi da pokrene postupak izmjene Zakona o deviznom poslovanju u smislu odgode za 1.1.2009. predviene liberalizacije dijela kapitalnih poslova s inozemstvom (otvaranja rauna pravnih osoba u inozemstvu i koritenje inozemnih kredita preko tih rauna, odobravanje kratkoronih financijskih kredita ne rezidenti ma, obavljanje transakcija na deviznim tritima u inozemstvu, poslove s izvedenim financijskim instrumentima, unoenje i iznoenje materijaliziranih vrijednosnih papira, plaanje i naplate u gotovini, davanje poklona i pomoi u inozemstvo...). Oekujemo da e i HANFA poduzeti odgovarajue mjere u sferi poslovanja mirovinskih i investicijskih fondova. 3. sprjeavanje efekta istiskivanja poduzea s financijskih trita - uravnoteenje prorauna konsolidirane ope drave, ukljuujui sva kanjenja u plaanjima koja smanjuju likvidnost realnog sektora. 4. efektivne promjene u kreditnoj i kamatnoj politici banaka sukladno intencijama iz Smjernica za upravljanje kreditnim rizikom koji proizlazi iz plasmana stanovnitvu. 5. doprinos sindikata u pravcu smanjenja deficita u razmjeni s inozemstvom i pritisaka na likvidnost. (c) Kretanja u realnom okruenju Prema dosad obino dosta tonim prognozama iz World Outlook-a Deutsche Bank od 3. listopada, za euro zonu predvia se u 2009.:  BDP i osobna potronja -0,2 % (ocjena 2008.1,0% i 0,2%)  Investicije-2.8% (1.4%)  Izvoz 2.3% (3.6%)  Uvoz 2.1% (3.0%)  Stopa nezaposlenosti 8.0 % (7.4%)  Inflacija 2.3 % (3.5%) To su kljuni realni problemi s kojima e se morati nositi domai izvoznici i u kojima im HNB moe pomoi jedino odravajui opu likvidnost domaeg financijskog sustava i stabilnost cijena, a ne nekim posebnim, selektivnim, mjerama. Uspijemo li u rjeavanju navedenih problema, u 2009. moemo oekivati: rast bruto domaeg proizvoda od oko 2%, u emu osobne potronje 1,6%, izvoza roba i usluga za 3,1%, te uvoza za 1.4%. Deficit platne bilance spustio bi se na 9.2% BDP-a, dok bi inozemni dug dosegao razinu od 38,5 mlrd. eura ili oko 89% BDP-a. Prosjena godinja stopa inflacije spustila bi se na 3,5%. Dakle, nita to bi nas inilo sretnima, ali i daleko manje loe od onoga to je u nekim drugim zemljama, a to moe doi i ovdje ako se ne trgnemo na vrijeme. U tom pak sluaju, niti aranman s MMF-om ne bi vjerojatno bio dovoljan da sprijei ulazak zemlje u stagnaciju ili ak recesiju.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Presentation at the press conference
text: Presentation by CNB Governor Dr. Zeljko Rohatinski at a press conference Published: 13.11.2007. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Date of publication of the statement Event Venue Event Date of events 13.11.2007. Press conference Zagreb, CNB 13.11.2007. Today we met at our already traditional gathering at the end of the year, which we use to present to you our views on current economicdevelopments and our assessments of the future period, and to give an indication of how and by what measures the central bank will affect these flows. Nothing more and especially new compared to the standard way of all our previous gatherings is now there, except for the timing itself. And he was chosen because we are all aware of the existence of some new elements that affect economic flows and that need to be discussed without delay. Introductoryly, I would like to recall some of these new elements. The first group is of course global developments and their possible impact on the situation in Croatia. Two elements are crucial. The first is the rise in the price of oil, as well as some other raw materials on the world market, which directly and without a time shift has an impact on both current transactions of the balance of paymentson import inflation. Another, still potential, element is the spreading effects of the crisis in the mortgage market, reflecting losses in banks and funds, the decline in stock indices in both America and Europe, and the possible slowdown in economic growth inthese large markets. And this may have implications for countries such as Croatia in the form of a decrease in inflows under the capital account of the balance of payments and slowing demand for their export products. If both of these elements were to be effectedand I hope not, of course there could be problems in external liquidity and even a substantial slowdown in credit growth, reflecting a significant slowdown in overall economic activity. These are the warnings that are contained in that often quoted materiyal of the IMF and there is nothing particularly new about it. The second group of elements is tied to some domestic flows. I'd like to mention three. The first is the high growth in food prices, which also significantly determines the acceleration of headline inflation. We are aware that if this accelerated inflation were to beincorporated into factor incomes, it could trigger a spiral of inflation that has not been present in Croatia for a long time. The second moment is the increased volatility of interest rates in the money market, which was originally determined by monetary flows under the saleof THT shares, and subsequently by the temporary absence of reverse repo auctions of the central bank. The third element is the very high stability of the nominal exchange rate, which is actually in the gap between the occasional anti-appreciation action of the central bank and antidepreciational effects of the measure on the mandatory registration of treasury records for faster growth of placements than allowed. In any case, such stability exchange rate, which of course has its upsides, creates a situation in which the growth of costs on both the basis of energy products and on the basis of interest rates can be offset only by an adjustment in the real sphere. An additional element, of course, is the election. Not only from the point of view of the uncertainty that they carry, but also because of the individual attempts to hunt in the murky, using the sensitivity of the pre-election situationije, by which I mean the behavior of some banks. In addition to these material and financial elements, there are some other issues that require some clarification. They are related to the clear definition of the operational objectives and instruments used by the central bank in achieving these objectives. Inquiries come from many institutions and grounders abroad as well. They are related in particular to the alignment of our regulations with the standards of the European Union and preparations for the implementation of Basel II, and we know that, for both reasons, someof the existing regulations should be relaxed in a certain way. Another question is the relationship between prudential and monetary measures, i.e. whether it is permissible and rational to use prudential measures to achieve some purely monetary objectives, and whether this means somehow de-enacting the basic function of supervision. The third question is the character of open market operations and the impact of their volatility on liquidity management by commercial banks. I'd like to address those questions as well. As for the actof the al operational objective, I believe that it will not change until we enter the European Union. It is: to limit external and internal imbalances in the part where excess demand is financed by credit multiplication of foreign sources, regardless ofwhether it is financial borrowing, deposits, bank recapitalisation, hybrid instruments or any other way of entering foreign capital into the country. Why? Because although this influx has slowed over the past two years, it is still tense enoughto produce growth in the balance of payments deficit, debt, costs of its servicing, reduces disposable income and increasingly stimulates inflation in sectors where there is no foreign supply, i.e. the increase in the prices of goods and services marketable exclusively in the domesticem market, real estate, and even securities, and has also started to act on the general inflation rate. The notion that the balance of payments deficit is only a function of the economic growth rate completely ignores the impact of supply on the size and structure of demand. For us, this thesis ofnon-acceptable wattles. With these deficits, high economic growth in the long run is unsustainable, and all global flows really only point even more to its high risk. As regards the instruments for achieving the stated operational objective, the CNB will use alllive instruments, which means capital controls, credit controls, prudential measures and open market operations, as only their integral action can be sufficiently effective. In doing so, prudential measures cannot be viewed statistically and in isolation from the growth of monetary aggregates. On the contrary, the rapid growth of monetary aggregates in itself poses a risk, which, as a rule, is effective only in the future. It is america's mortgage crisis that confirms this. Statically they were all low-risk, dmeal insured, and dynamically this turned out not to be the case. As for open market operations and criticism that their volatility has a significant negative impact on banks' operations, I would say that these operations are an instrument of fine-tuning liquidity and a reduction inshort-term interest rate volatility. Their usefulness especially comes to the fore in moments of shocks of supply or demand. The sale of THT shares was just one such shock, and the CNB, as you know, responded appropriately to this shock. However, open market operationsare not and cannot be a permanent source of liquidity for banks in the function of supporting their credit expansion, and certainly not a disguised form of state lending and interest subsidization by the central bank, and some bankers have taken it thatway. As regards the European Union, it is not disputed that at the time of entry our legislation, instruments and measures must be fully aligned with the legislation, measures and instruments of the European Union. However, there can be no a priori convergence in bothnstruments, if the flows are divergent and the risks are fundamentally different. It is out of the question that a priori we relax any instrument simply because it is less restrictive in the European Union than it is in Croatia. Of course there is a problem of exit strategye, which has its own special weight in the release of now and mobi licks of early funds both through the high rate of reserve requirement and through 32% minimum foreign exchange claims, but from this exit strategy the question of the entry strategy in terms of - what kind of apartmentthis country will teach it into the European Union is more important. It would not be good to repeat the case of some new members, who did not take enough care of this and now have problems, which are also the problems of the European Union itself. Everything we're doing and what we're going to do is of course related to certain risks. I'd like to mention three such risks. The first is purely hypothetical, but lately it has been talked about more often. Due to the alleged disintermediation policy, which according to some is implemented by the CNB, it is theoretically possible to turn branches into branches of foreign banks, which would effectively leave them out of the CNB's control. This threat is not new, nor has it been made exclusively in Croatia, but so far it has not been a single case that it has been achieved. There are a number of reasons why this is not worth it to foreign banks and I believethat this will not happen in Croatia either. Another risk is the effect of all these global distortions in terms of radically reducing foreign capital inflows. This risk cannot be excluded, but in this case the CNB would not substantially change either the operational cand the instruments of its policy. Under such conditions, sustainable credit activity and payments to foreign countries would be supported in the short term by releasing part and mobi lisi of early assets on the basis of the reserve requirement and on the basis of the minimum foreign exchange claims, while further defending the stability of the exchange rate. This is essentially an option that two, three years ago we offered to the commercial banks themselves, and without any external shocks. The third risk is sizing our measures. The fact is that - in addition to supporting economic growth, but also deepening imbalances - the intensive inflow of foreign capital has so far directly and strongly affected both the stability of the exchange rate and the stability of interest rates and the stability of domestic prices. That is why any excessive restrictiveness in politics could trigger warsprecisely the risks associated with this area. This is why the CNB clearly and rationally needs to sizing the intensity of its measures, and even at the cost that they are less effective than they could objectively be. As for the current timing and the conduct of monetary policy in the coming year, I would point to some of the latest indicators and our estimates of developments by the end of this year, easily for known reasons both in September and October loans to households and businesses grew aggregated at a rate of 1% per month, the tendency to slow them down is evident. By the end of June, the average monthly rate of their growth was 1.4%, and since July, when the measure on the mandatory registration of treasury bills entered into force in an integral form, this rate has slowed to 0.6 %. Inthe cup, these placements increased by 11.4% in the first ten months, which is a third slower than in 2006. We estimate that their annual growth at the end of the year will be reduced from 22.9% in 2006 to about 13.5% in 2007. In parallel, the growth of basic monetarary aggregates slows down: cash mass from 25% to 14.5%, total liquid assets from 18% to 14%. In the structure of the loan, exactly what was expected happened - more slowed lending to the enterprise than the population. Companies, and this was expected, are substitutedby some of the slower growth of domestic loans through foreign direct borrowing. For the first ten months, their debt to abroad increased by 2.7 billion euros or by 29%. It's nothing new. The tendency to quick direct borrowing of enterprises abroad has existed since 2005, in 2006 the annual rate was 30%, and now it is 33%, which is not a big change. However, in parallel with such growth in loans from abroad to businesses, the operation of the marginal reserve requirement and the related bank recapitalisations (which will be more than 1 billion euros this year), as well as the slowdown in total loans, result in a decrease in banks' foreign debt in the first ten months by 1.6 billion euros, or about 16%. Combined with faster corporate borrowing, reducing bank debt and stagnating foreign government borrowing, total foreign debt rose by 1.7 billion euros for the first ten months to reach 30.9 billion euros at the end of October, with an annual growth rate of 10.7%. In the remaining two months, we expect similar t endencies, so the total debt amount of 32.3 billion euros is expected at the end of the year, which would mean a stagnation of the debt-to-gross domestic product relationship to approximately 85.5 percent. From the above, we could deduce a few things. The combinedincidence of capital restrictions and credit control so far has slowed the growth of both loans and foreign debt, but has also produced some structural changes that need to be respected when considering future measures. First, by recapitalizing banks (substitution of foreign borrowingwith the aim of avoiding the marginal reserve requirement), encouraging domestic sources by increasing passive interest rates and using corporate deposits, the strong credit potential of the banking sector remains maintained. It can still meet the demand for loans with similar growth as before. Secondly, the substitution of the domestic borrowing of part of the enterprise through foreign borrowing has quite certainly increased the risk of the domestic loan market - practically, outside go to borrow those who are the least at risk. Thirdly, theriskiness and the rise of passive interest rates, in addition to the cost of treasury bills, of course puts pressure on the rise of active interest rates. This also reduces the potential effectiveness of mandatory registration of cashier's records. The developments in the ninth monthclearly illustrate this: when the demand for expensive cash loans jumped, the banks approved them, paid the fine and still made good money on it all. The effectiveness of treasury bills in 2008 will also be influenced by the return of records entered by banks in 2007. These are the elements that we must bear in mind in conceiving measures for next year. In addition to such monetary developments, I would like to briefly present our assessments of the overall economic developments in 2007. In order for them to be better understood, I would first refer to the very notion of therestorative rickiness of monetary policy that everyone is talking about and for which many accuse us. There is one short-term semblance in this regard that the slowdown in ongoing growth in both loans and money supply has been really very restrictive. There are a number of ways in which thisrestrictiveness can be determined. The simplest thing is to look at the average real annual growth of key aggregates. We have ten months: the average annual real growth of loans is 17.6%, the money mass is 17.2%, the total liquid assets are 15.5%. This is approximately 2.5pfaster than real GDP growth. In other words, although monetary policy was supposedly restrictive, the relative liquidity of the economy was not reduced at all in 2007; on the contrary, it is also enlarged. That is why there were no monetary constraints on accelerating 100PE economic growth from 4.8 in 2006 to, we estimate, 5.9% in 2007, with approximately the same dynamics of personal consumption growth, the share of which in the GDP growth rate is 3.5 percentage points, meaning almost two thirds. By contrast, due to faster import growth than exports, the negative contribution of net exports to the GDP growth rate increases from -1.1% in 2006 to around -1.7% in 2007. This also results in an increase in the deficit of exchange of goods and services, and we estimate that it will be about 3.2 billion euros, which is a growth of 20%. Consequently , the current account deficit of the balance of payments also increases from 7.7% of GDP in 2006 to about 8.6% in 2007. The annual inflation rate is expected to exceed 4% in October, and could approach an annual growth rate of about 5% in December. This will only be reflected in the average annual inflation rate in 2007, although it will be an already respectable 2.8%. But due to the high transfer of prices from this year to next year, approximately 2.5%, this will be significantly reflected in the average inflation rate in 2008. By fairly conservative projections, it could be around 4.5%, the highest inflation rate since 2000. All this indicates that in 2007 the corresponding results achieved both on the slowdown in credit growth and on the slowdown in the growth of foreign debt, but that the longer-term relationships formed in the economy, which also result in deficits and debt, cannot change significantly only in one year. That is why the CNB has no doubts about the need to continue the current policy, taking into account all the structural changes that this policy caused in 2007. Based on these assessments, it will be proposed to the CNB Council to adopt the following monetary policy bases for 2008. The marginal reserve requirement shall remain in force in its current form. An eventual rate hike, which nowbears 55%, would have no major effects because even at this rate, as we see, banks reduce their external debt. 31.12.2007. while maintaining a separate pristup for the balance sheet and off-balance sheet part of the bank's position. At the same time, in order to minimise the impact of raising interest rates and recovering treasury bills entered in 2007 on the effectiveness of this measure, mandatory enrolment will be increased from the existing 50% to 75% of the overdraft in rastu placements. At the same time, the interest rate on OBZs is decreasing from 0.75% to 0.25% per year. There are no selective rates. The third group of measures refers to prudential measures. Due to the increased risk in the credit market and to limit the "cost-effectiveness" of substitution anddomestic debt by recapitalising banks as sources of funds for placement growth faster than allowed, and to limit the high use of secondary liquidity sources to finance placements, the Capital Adequacy Decision will prescribe the relationship between maximum permitted placement growth rates and adequate levels of capital adequacy corrected for the share of secondary sources in the liabilities structure of banks. The basic idea is that faster growth of placements requires a higher capital adequacy rate than the legally prescribedminimal 10%. There is an opportunity that we are thinking about, but which is not easy to realize, to incorporate a selective approach for lending to borrowing and for lending to the population within the framework of such changes in the Capital Adequacy Decision. There are a number of problems here and it is not certain that in real life we can solve them satisfactorily. And without their resolution, a selective approach would only open up space for all sorts of speculation. In this case, there is also the question of the position of small banks, given the impression that is created in public, that they are in some way at a disadvantage than large banks because they do not have foreign sources of funds and base their potential solely on local deposits, and that each linear measure affects them harder than the big banks. There's truth to that for some of the small banks, but not for everyone. When we incorporated the share of secondary sources as a corrective factor (these are all sources except capital and long-term savings of the population), the idea was to try to facilitate the business of small banaka in this way. But it turned out that some of these banks practically operate as commissaries.. They borrow money on the market, take deposits from the big banks and place that money to their customers. This is not a practice that should be honored in any way. Anotheramendment will be made to the Decision on Ad equity of capital, in order to reduce the motivation of banks to approve some potentially riskier but now more profitable placements. Weightings for currency-induced credit risk will be increased, from 75% to 100% at kr edita todebtors who have an inconsistent foreign exchange position and where the loans are fully covered by the mortgage, and from 125% to 150% for such loans that are not covered by the mortgage. Operations on the open market will be carried out as appropriate, in a manner appropriate by the CNB. This will not be any self-service or source of liquidity that banks can permanently count on. Finally, the interest rate on CNB's lombard loans will increase 7.5% to 9% at what level it was until recently. Our forecasts for 2008are about to see a rise in monetary aggregates approaching this year's, somewhere between 11 and 13%, both in which. Of course, due to the fundamentally different transfer of their 2007 level to 2008, their average situation will be aligned with the expected GDP growth. For this growth, we estimate that it could be about 5%, which includes a growth in personal consumption of about 4%. Exports and imports could move at rates of around 4.5%, which would also bring the negative contribution of net exports to the GDP growth rate from -1.7% in 2007 to -0.6% in 2008. I estimatethat the balance of payments deficit could be slightly reduced to 8.2% of GDP and foreign debt stabilised at 85%. What do you deduce from this? A lot of torment, a lot of trying to act to the best of your ability, so that the situation does not deteriorate further. But there is no alternative,one can also act when it shows how limited the possibilities of acting are solely through monetary policy. And to conclude. We all know the desire to accelerate economic growth in 2008, especially in the coming years, you know which rates are alreadymentioned. That's not impossible. But that growth would have to be based on a very different basis than has been the case so far.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a dr. eljka Rohatinskog na konferenciji za novinare Objavljeno: 13.11.2007. Vrsta Govornik Govor Dr. eljko Rohatinski, na dunosti guvernera HNB-a od 12. srpnja 2000. do 7. srpnja 2012. Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja 13.11.2007. Konferencija za novinare Zagreb, HNB 13.11.2007. Danas smo se sastali na naem ve tradicionalnom okupljanju potkraj godine, koje koristimo da vam prezentiramo svoje stavove o aktualnim ekonomskim kretanjima i nae ocjene budueg razdoblja, te damo naznake na koji nain i kojim mjerama e sredinja banka utjecati na te tokove. Nita vie i posebno novog u odnosu na standardni nain svih naih prijanjih okupljanja sada nema, osim samog tajminga. A on je izabran zbog toga to smo svi svjesni postojanja nekih novih elemenata koji utjeu na ekonomske tokove i o kojima je potrebno razgovarati bez odlaganja. Uvodno bih podsjetio na neke od tih novih elemenata. Prva skupina su naravno globalna kretanja i njihov mogui utjecaj na situaciju u Hrvatskoj. Dva su elementa presudna. Prvi je rast cijene nafte, ali i nekih drugih sirovina na svjetskom tritu, koji izravno i bez vremenskog pomaka ima utjecaj kako na tekue transakcije platne bilance tako i na uvoznu inflaciju. Drugi, jo uvijek potencijalni, element je rasprostiranje efekata krize na tritu hipotekarnih kredita, s odrazom na gubitke u bankama i fondovima, na pad burzovnih indeksa i u Americi i u Europi i na mogue usporavanje gospodarskog rasta na tim velikim tritima. A to za zemlje kao to je Hrvatska moe imati implikacije u vidu smanjenja priljeva u okviru kapitalnog rauna platne bilance i usporavanja potranje za njihovim izvoznim proizvodima. Ako bi se oba ova elementa efektuirala, a ja se nadam da nee, naravno da bi mogli nastupiti i problemi u vanjskoj likvidnosti pa ak i bitno usporavanja rasta kredita, s odrazom na znatno usporavanje ukupne ekonomske aktivnosti. To su upozorenja koja su sadrana u i onom esto citiranom materijalu MMF-a i tu nema nieg posebno novog. Druga skupina elemenata vezana je za neke domae tokove. Spomenuo bih tri. Prvi je visok rast cijena hrane, koji bitno determinira i ubrzanje ukupne inflacije. Svjesni smo da, ako bi se ta ubrzana inflacija ugradila u faktorske dohotke, to bi moglo pokrenuti spiralu inflacije kakva ve dugo nije bila prisutna u Hrvatskoj. Drugi moment je poveana volatilnost kamatnih stopa na novanom tritu, koja je prvobitno bila determinirana monetarnim tokovima u okviru prodaje dionica THT-a, a nakon toga i privremenim izostankom obrnutih repo aukcija sredinje banke. Trei element je vrlo visoka stabilnost nominalnog teaja koji se zapravo nalazi u procjepu izmeu povremenog antiaprecijacijskog djelovanja centralne banke i antideprecijacijskih uinaka mjere o obaveznom upisu blagajnikih zapisa za bri rast plasmana od doputenog. U svakom sluaju, takva stabilnost teaj, koja naravno ima i svojih dobrih strana, stvara situaciju u kojoj se rast trokova i po osnovi energenata i po osnovi kamatnih stopa moe neutralizirati iskljuivo prilagodbom u realnoj sferi. Dodatni element su, dakako, izbori. Ne samo s aspekta neizvjesnosti koji oni nose nego i zbog pojedinih pokuaja lova u mutnom, koristei osjetljivost predizborne situacije, pri emu mislim na ponaanje nekih banaka. Osim ovih materijalnih i financijskih elemenata, postoje i neka druga pitanja koja trae odreeno razjanjenje. Vezani su uz jasno definiranje operativnih ciljeva i instrumenata koje centralna banka koristi u ostvarivanju tih ciljeva. Upiti dolaze od mnogih institucija i uzemlji i u inozemstvu. Vezani su posebno uz usklaivanje naih propisa sa standardima Europske unije i pripreme za implementaciju Basela II, a znamo da bi, i zbog jednog i zbog drugog, neke nae postojee propise trebalo na odreeni nain relaksirati. Drugo je pitanje odnosa izmeu prudencijalnih i monetarnim mjera, odnosno je li dopustivo i racionalno koristiti prudencijalne mjere za ostvarivanje nekih isto monetarnih ciljeva, te znai li to na neki nain dezavuiranje osnovne funkcije supervizije. Tree je pitanje karaktera operacija na otvorenom tritu i utjecaj njihove volatilnosti na upravljanje likvidnou od strane poslovnih banaka. Htio bih se osvrnuti i na ta pitanja. to se tie aktualnog operativnog cilja, vjerujem da se on nee mijenjati sve do naeg ulaska u Europsku uniju. On je: ograniavati vanjske i unutranje neravnotee u dijelu u kojem se viak potranje financira kreditnom multiplikacijom inozemnih izvora, neovisno o tome je li rije o financijskom zaduivanju, depozitima, dokapitalizaciji banaka, hibridnim instrumentima ili bilo kom drugom nainu ulaska inozemnog kapitala u zemlju. Zato? Zato to, iako je taj priljev u zadnje dvije godine usporen, jo uvijek je dovoljno intenzivan da producira rast deficita platne bilance, duga, trokova njegovog servisiranja, smanjuje raspoloivi dohodak i sve vie potie inflaciju u sektorima gdje ne postoji inozemna ponuda, odnosno rast cijena dobara i usluga utrivih iskljuivo na domaem tritu, nekretnina, pa i vrijednosnica, a poeo je djelovati i na opu stopu inflacije. Teza da je deficit platne bilance samo funkcija stope privrednog rasta potpuno zanemaruje utjecaj ponude na veliinu i strukturu potranje. Za nas je ta teza neprihvatljiva. Uz ovakve deficite visok ekonomski rast na dugi rok je neodriv, a svi globalni tokovi zapravo samo jo vie ukazuju i na njegovu visoku rizinost. to se tie instrumenata za ostvarivanje navedenog operativnog cilja, HNB e koristiti sve raspoloive instrumente, to znai kapitalne kontrole, kreditne kontrole, prudencijalne mjere i operacije na otvorenom tritu, jer samo njihovo integralno djelovanje moe biti dovoljno uinkovito. Pri tome se prudencijalne mjere ne mogu promatrati statistiki i izolirano od rasta monetarnih agregata. Naprotiv, brzi rast monetarnih agregata sam po sebi predstavlja rizik, koji se u pravilu efektuira tek u budunosti. Upravo amerika kriza hipotekarnih kredita to i potvruje. Statiki svi oni su bili niskorizini, dobro osigurani, a dinamiki se pokazalo da to nije sluaj. to se tie operacija na otvorenom tritu i kritika da njihova volatilnost bitno negativno utjee na poslovanje banaka, rekao bih da su te operacije instrument finog podeavanja likvidnosti i smanjenja kratkorone volatilnosti kamatnih stopa. Njihova korisnost posebno dolazi do izraaja u trenucima okova ponude ili potranje. Prodaja dionica THT-a je bila upravo jedan takav ok, a HNB je, kao to znate, na taj ok primjereno reagirao. No, operacije na otvorenom tritu nisu i ne mogu biti trajni izvor likvidnosti banaka u funkciji podravanja njihove kreditne ekspanzije, a pogotovo ne prikriveni oblik kreditiranja drave i subvencioniranja kamata od strane centralne banke, a neki bankari su to upravo tako shvatili. to se tie Europske unije, nije sporno da u trenutku ulaska nae zakonodavstvo, instrumenti i mjere moraju biti potpuno usklaeni sa zakonodavstvom, mjerama i instrumentima Europske unije. Meutim, ne moe biti a priori konvergencije u instrumentima, ako su tokovi divergentni, a rizici bitno razliiti. Ne dolazi u obzir da a priori relaksiramo bilo koji instrument samo zato to je on u Europskoj unije manje restriktivan nego to je u Hrvatskoj. Naravno da postoji problem izlazne strategije koji ima svoju posebnu teinu u oslobaanju sada i mobi lizi ranih sredstava i kroz visoku stopu obvezne priuve i kroz 32-postotna minimalna devizna potraivanja, ali od te izlazne strategije vanije je pitanje ulazne strategije u smislu - u kakvom stanju e ova zemlja ui u Europsku uniju. Ne bi bilo dobro da se ponovi sluaj nekih novih lanica, koje o tome nisu vodile dovoljno rauna i sad imaju probleme, koji su ujedno i problemi same Europske unije. Sve ovo to radimo i to emo raditi naravno da je vezano i uz odreene rizike. Spomenuo bih tri takva rizika. Prvi je isto hipotetski, ali u zadnje vrijeme se o njemu ee govori. Zbog navodne politike disintermedijacije, koju po nekima provodi HNB, teoretski je mogue pretvaranje podrunica u filijale stranih banaka, ime bi one praktiki izale iz kontrole HNB-a. Ta prijetnja nije nova, niti je izreena iskljuivo u Hrvatskoj, ali do sada nije bio niti jedan sluaj da je i ostvarena. Postoji niz razloga zato se to stranim bankama ne isplati i ja vjerujem da se to nee dogoditi ni u Hrvatskoj. Drugi rizik je efektuiranje svih ovih globalnih poremeaja u smislu radikalnog smanjenja priljeva inozemnog kapitala. Taj rizik se ne moe iskljuiti, ali ni u tom sluaju HNB ne bi bitno mijenjao ni operativne ciljeve ni instrumente svoje politike. U takvim uvjetima odrivu kreditnu aktivnost i plaanja prema inozemstvu kratkorono bi se podravalo oslobaanjem dijela i mobi lizi ranih sredstava po osnovu obvezne priuve i po osnovu minimalnih deviznih potraivanja, uz daljnju obranu stabilnosti teaja. To je u biti opcija koju smo prije dvije, tri godine nudili samim poslovnim bankama, i bez ikakvih eksternih okova. Trei rizik je dimenzioniranje naih mjera. injenica je daje - uz podravanje gospodarskog rasta, ali i produbljivanje neravnotea - intenzivan priljev inozemnog kapitala do sada izravno i snano utjecao i na stabilnost teaja i na stabilnost kamatnih stopa i na stabilnost domaih cijena. Zato bi svaka prevelika restriktivnost u politici mogla aktivirati upravo rizike koji su vezani uz to podruje. To je razlog zbog ega HNB jasno i racionalno treba dimenzionirati intenzitet svojih mjera, pa ak i po cijenu da su one manje uinkovite nego to bi objektivno mogle biti. to se tie sadanjeg trenutka i voenja monetarne politike u iduoj godini, ukazao bih na neke najnovije pokazatelje i nae procjene kretanja do kraja ove godine, lako su iz poznatih razloga i u rujnu i u listopadu krediti stanovnitvu i poduzeima agregatno rasli po stopi od 1% mjeseno, evidentna je tendencija njihovog usporavanja. Do kraja lipnja prosjena mjesena stopa njihova rasta iznosila je 1,4%, a od srpnja, kad je mjera o obaveznom upisu blagajnikih zapisa stupila na snagu u integralnom obliku, ta stopa je usporena na 0,6 %. Ukupno su ti plasmani u prvih deset mjeseci poveani za 11,4%, to je za treinu sporije nego u 2006. Ocjenjujemo da e njihov godinji rast na kraju godine biti smanjen sa 22,9% u 2006. na oko 13,5% u 2007. Usporedo s time usporava se i rast osnovnih monetarnih agregata: novane mase sa 25% na 14,5%, ukupnih likvidnih sredstava sa 18% na 14%. U strukturi kredita dogodilo se upravo ono to se i oekivalo - vie je usporeno kreditiranje poduzea nego stanovnitva. Poduzea, i to je bilo oekivano, supstituiraju dio sporijeg rasta domaih kredita izravnim inozemnim zaduivanjem. Za prvih deset mjeseci njihov dug prema inozemstvu poveanje za 2,7 milijardi eura ili za 29%. To nije nita novo. Tendencija brzog izravnog zaduivanja poduzea u inozemstvu postoji od 2005. godine, u 2006. godinja stopa iznosila je 30%, a sada iznosi 33%, to nije velika promjena. Meutim, usporedo s takvim rastom kredita iz inozemstva poduzeima, djelovanje granine obvezne priuve i s tim povezane dokapitalizacije banaka (koja e u ovoj godini biti vea od milijardu eura), kao i usporavanje ukupnih kredita, ima za posljedicu smanjenje inozemnog duga banaka u prvih deset mjeseci za 1,6 milijardi eura, odnosno za otprilike 16%. U kombinaciji breg zaduivanja poduzea, smanjenja duga banaka i stagnacije inozemnog zaduivanja drave, ukupni inozemni dug porastao je za prvih deset mjeseci za 1,7 milijardi eura i dosegao je krajem listopada 30,9 milijardi eura, uz godinju stopu rasta od 10,7%. I u preostala dva mjeseca oekujemo sline tendencije, tako da se oekuje krajem godine iznos ukupnog duga od 32,3 milijarde eura, to bi znailo stagnaciju odnosa duga prema bruto domaem proizvodu na priblino 85,5 posto. Iz prethodno iznijetoga mogli bi zakljuiti nekoliko stvari. Dosadanja kombinacija kapitalskih restrikcija i kreditne kontrole usporila je rast i kredita i inozemnog duga, ali je proizvela i neke strukturne promjene koje treba respektirati kod razmatranja buduih mjera. Prvo, dokapitalizacijom banaka (supstitucija inozemnog zaduivanja s ciljem da se izbjegne granina obvezna priuva), poticanjem domaih izvora poveanjem pasivnih kamatnih stopa i koritenjem depozita poduzea zadran je i dalje snani kreditni potencijal bankarskog sektora. On i dalje moe udovoljavati potranji za kreditima uz slian rast kao i do sada. Drugo, supstitucija domaeg zaduivanja dijela poduzea inozemnim zaduivanjem sasvim je izvjesno poveala rizinost domaeg trita kredita - praktiki, vani se idu zaduiti oni koji su najmanje rizini. Tree, poveana rizinost i rast pasivnih kamatnih stopa, uz trokove blagajnikih zapisa, naravno da vre pritisak na rast aktivnih kamatnih stopa. Time se smanjuje i potencijalna uinkovitost obveznog upisa blagajnikih zapisa. Kretanja u devetom mjesecu to jasno ilustriraju: kad je skoila potranja za skupim gotovinskim kreditima, banke su ih odobrile, platile kaznu i jo na svemu tome dobro zaradile. Na uinkovitost blagajnikih zapisa u 2008. utjecat e i povrat zapisa koje su banke upisale u 2007. To su elementi koje moramo imati na umu u koncipiranju mjera za iduu godinu. Uz takva monetarna kretanja htio bih ukratko iznijeti i nae ocjene ukupnih ekonomskih kretanja u 2007. godini. Da bi se one mogle bolje shvatiti, najprije bih se osvrnuo na sam pojam restriktivnosti monetarne politike o kojoj svi priaju i zbog koje nas mnogi i optuuju. Kod toga postoji jedan kratkoroni privid da je usporavanje tekueg rasta i kredita i novane mase bilo stvarno vrlo restriktivno. Postoji niz naina na koje se ta restriktivnost moe utvrditi. Najjednostavnije je da pogledamo prosjeni realni godinji rast kljunih agregata. Imamo deset mjeseci: prosjean godinji realni rast kredita iznosi 17,6%, novane mase 17,2%, ukupnih likvidnih sredstava 15,5%. To je priblino 2,5 puta bre od realnog rasta BDP-a. Drugim rijeima, iako je monetarna politika bila navodno restriktivna, u 2007. uope nije smanjena relativna likvidnost ekonomije; naprotiv, ona je jo i poveana. Zato nije bilo nikakvih monetarnih ogranienja ubrzanju stope gospodarskog rasta sa 4,8 u 2006. na, mi ocjenjujemo, 5,9% u 2007., uz priblino istu dinamiku rasta osobne potronje, iji udjel u stopi rasta BDP-a iznosi 3,5 postotnih poena, znai skoro dvije treine. Nasuprot tome, zbog breg rasta uvoza od izvoza, negativni doprinos neto izvoza stopi rasta BDP-a se poveava s -1,1 % u 2006. na oko -1,7% u 2007. To ima za posljedicu i poveanje deficita razmjene roba i usluga, a mi ocjenjujemo da e on iznositi oko 3,2 milijarde eura, to je rast od 20%. Posljedino tome, poveava se i deficit tekuih transakcija platne bilance sa 7,7% BDP 2006. na oko 8,6% u 2007. godini. Prema oekivanjima, godinja stopa inflacije u listopadu premaite 4%, a u prosincu bi se mogla pribliiti godinjoj stopi rasta od oko 5%. To e se samo manjim dijelom odraziti na prosjenu godinju stopu inflacije u 2007., iako e ona biti ve respektabilnih 2,8%. No, zbog visokog prijenosa cijena iz ove u sljedeu godinu, otprilike 2,5%, to e se bitno odraziti na prosjenu stopu inflacije u 2008. Po dosta konzervativnim projekcijama ona bi mogla iznositi oko 4,5%, to je najvia stopa inflacije od 2000. godine. Sve ovo ukazuje da se u 2007. ostvareni odgovarajui rezultati i na usporavanju rasta kredita i na usporavanju rasta inozemnog duga, ali da se dugoronije formirani odnosi u ekonomiji, koji i rezultiraju deficitima i dugom, ne mogu bitno promijeniti samo u jednoj godini. Zato HNB nema nikakvih dilema o potrebi nastavka dosadanje politike, vodei rauna i o svim strukturnim promjenama koje je ta politika izazvala u 2007. godini. Na temelju ovakvih ocjena, Savjetu HNB-a bit e predloeno da za 2008. usvoji sljedee osnove monetarne politike. Granina obvezna priuva ostaje na snazi u postojeem obliku. Eventualno podizanje stope, koja sada iznosi 55%, ne bi imalo vee uinke jer i pri ovoj stopi, kao to vidimo, banke smanjuju svoj vanjski dug. to se tie obveznog upisa blagajnikih zapisa, dozvoljeni kumulativni rast iznosit e 1 poen mjeseno na bazu 31.12.2007., uz zadravanje odvojenog pristupa za bilanni i vanbilanni dio pozicije banaka. Istodobno, da bi se umanjio uinak podizanja kamatnih stopa i povrata blagajnikih zapisa upisanih u 2007. na uinkovitost ove mjere, poveat e se obvezni upis s postojeih 50% na 75% prekoraenja u rastu plasmana. Istodobno, smanjuje se kamatna stopa na OBZ-e sa 0,75% na 0,25% godinje. Nema selektivnih stopa. Trea grupa mjera odnosi se na prudencijalne mjere. Zbog poveanog rizika na tritu kredita i da bi se ograniila "isplativost" supstitucije inozemnog duga dokapitalizacijom banaka kao izvora sredstava za rast plasmana bri od doputenog, te da bi se ograniilo visoko koritenje sekundarnih izvora likvidnosti za financiranje plasmana, u Odluci o adekvatnosti kapitala propisat e se odnos izmeu maksimalno dozvoljene stope rasta plasmana i odgovarajue razine adekvatnosti kapitala korigirane za udio sekundarnih izvora u strukturi pasive banaka. Osnovna ideja je da bri rast plasmana trai i veu stopu adekvatnosti kapitala od zakonom propisanih minimalnih 10%. Postoji mogunost o kojoj razmiljamo, ali koju nije jednostavno realizirati, da se u okviru takvih izmjena u Odluci o adekvatnosti kapitala ugradi selektivni pristup za kreditiranje pouzea i za kreditiranje stanovnitva. Tu ima niz problema i nije sigurno da ih moemo u stvarnom ivotu rijeiti na zadovoljavajui nain. A bez njihovog rjeavanja selektivni pristup bi samo otvorio prostor za svakakve pekulacije. Kod toga postoji jo i pitanje poloaja malih banaka, s obzirom na dojam koji se stvara u javnosti, da su one na neki nain u nepovoljnijem poloaju od velikih banaka jer nemaju inozemne izvore sredstava i svoj potencijal temelje iskljuivo na lokalnim depozitima, te da njih svaka linearna mjera pogaa tee nego velike banke. U tome ima istine za neke od malih banaka, ali ne za sve. Kad smo ugradili udjel sekundarnih izvora kao korektivni faktor (to su svi izvori osim kapitala i dugorone tednje stanovnitva), ideja je bila da se na taj nain pokua olakati poslovanje malih banaka. No, pokazalo se da neke od tih banaka praktiki posluju kao komisionari.. Posuuju novac na tritu, uzimaju depozite velikih banaka i taj novac plasiraju svojim komitentima. To nije praksa koju bi na bilo koji nain trebalo honorirati. U Odluci o adekvatnosti kapitala izvrit e se jo jedna izmjena, da bi se smanjila motiviranost banaka za odobravanje nekih potencijalno rizinijih ali sada profitabilnijih plasmana. Poveat e se ponderi za valutno inducirani kreditni rizik i to sa 75% na 100% kod kredita dunicima koji imaju neusklaenu deviznu poziciju a kod kojih su krediti potpuno pokriveni hipotekom, a sa 125% na 150% kod takvih kredita koji nisu pokriveni hipotekom. Operacije na otvorenom tritu provodit e se prema potrebi, na nain koji HNB smatra primjerenim. To nee biti nikakvo samoposluivanje ili izvor likvidnosti na koji banke mogu permanentno raunati. Konano, kamatna stopa na lombardne kredite HNB poveat e se 7,5 na 9% na kojoj razini je donedavno i bila. Nae prognoze za 2008. predviaju rast monetarnih agregata priblian ovogodinjemu, negdje izmeu 11 i 13%, kako kod kojeg. Naravno, zbog bitno drugaijeg prijenosa njihove razine iz 2007. u 2008., njihovo prosjeno stanje e biti usklaeno s oekivanim rastom BDP-a. Za taj rast ocjenjujemo da bi mogao iznositi oko 5%, u to je ukljuen rast osobne potronje oko 4%. Izvoz i uvoz bi se mogli kretati po stopama od oko 4,5%, ime bi se i negativni doprinos neto izvoza stopi rasta BDP-a spustio s -1,7% u 2007 na -0,6% u 2008.. Ocjenjujemo da bi se deficit platne bilance mogao lagano smanjiti na 8,2% BDP-a, a inozemni dug stabilizirati na 85%. to iz ovoga zakljuiti? Mnogo muke, mnogo pokuaja da se djeluje najbolje to se moe, da se situacija dalje ne pogorava. Ali alternative nema, mora se djelovati i kad se pokazuje koliko su ograniene mogunosti djelovanja iskljuivo monetarnom politikom. I da zakljuim. Svima su nam poznate elje da se i u 2008., a naroito u narednim godinama, ubrza ekonomski rast, znate i sami koje se stope ve spominju. To nije nemogue. No, taj bi rast morao biti utemeljen na sasvim drugaijim osnovama nego to je do sada bio sluaj.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: A crisis that didn't happen
text: HPVATRKA ON THE MORNING A crisis that did not happen Published: 27/11/2023 Column by Governor Boris Vuji for the weekly Nacional, published on November 23, 2023 "If you wanted people to love you, you should have become a doctor, not a central banker," is the benevolent, albeit rather belated, advice that a friend gave me a few years ago. Indeed, every life saved by doctors brings not only eternal gratitude from the lucky person and his family, but also recognition from the wider society. By contrast, crises that central bankers successfully avoid are, by definition, invisible. Monetary and financial stability are generally taken for granted, as an immanent feature of the financial system or a consequence of good luck. On the other hand, elevated inflation is painfully visible, and the public is unceremoniously assigning copious portions of blame to central bankers, even if even a crystal ball that would herald epidemics and wars would not help them much in accomplishing their tasks. This extensive and self-reflective introduction has only one purpose - to provide context for the observation that we are just failing to notice a crisis that has been successfully averted, not because of our own qualities or sheer luck, but because of a deliberate long-term policy of regulators stretched over a decade. The episode of global tightening of monetary policy unprecedented in living memory has so far passed without any serious shocks on the domestic market. Too mild an increase in deposit rates (for individuals) and increased profitability of banks are the main neuralgic points of the current financial landscape that attract the attention of financial commentators and inflame public discontent. Such - in my opinion - a very benign outcome of the monetary tightening was not guaranteed. Previous experiences with tightening global financing conditions have been exactly the opposite - domestic interest rates would usually dance to the slightest breeze that would come from global financial markets, and macroeconomic vulnerabilities of the domestic economy would especially strengthen the effects of stronger global earthquakes. This time, the story took an unusual and much better course - despite the fact that With the global rise in interest rates, domestic companies are borrowing on similar terms as their competitors in the euro area for the first time, and housing loans are even slightly cheaper for citizens than for Germans or Austrians. This is a question that I have been asked countless times since I started working at the central bank, back in 1998 - when will we in Croatia be able to borrow at the same price as the Germans? Here, we have achieved that. Even consumers who have "old" housing loans have felt the tightening of monetary conditions only with the cessation of the recently steady trend of reducing the war Loan. In contrast to a large number of consumers in the euro area, whose interest rates rose sharply and sharply by 4-5 percentage points. Crises that central bankers successfully avoid are, by definition, invisible. Monetary stability is taken for granted. A small - practically on a laboratory scale - reflection of what could have taken place in Croatia is shown by the existing general-purpose cash loans tied to the Euribor. Interest rates on these loans, which account for only three percent of all general-purpose cash loans, have risen from about 6 percent at the beginning of the year to almost 8 percent today. Given the small number and relatively short maturity of these loans, as well as the fact that interest rates on existing loans to individuals fell until the beginning of this year, the financial discomfort of these borrowers goes almost unnoticed. However, it is quite easy to conclude what would happen if, by any chance, most loans were approved with variable interest rates tied to the Euribor. Increase Repayment by 20, 30, or even more percent - in proportion to the remaining maturity of the loan - would become the norm, although the intensity of the increase in loan installments in such a hypothetical scenario would be slightly weaker than at the time of the strengthening of the Swiss franc, the overall effect on consumers would undoubtedly be stronger because installments on almost all loans would increase. As a mirror image of rising interest rates on loans, bank profitability would rise much more strongly, even if slightly higher interest rates on deposits somewhat offset the impact of higher interest rates on loans. The hypothetical scenario I have described is a reality in a number of euro area members - Finland, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Ireland... as well as in some EU countries outside the euro area. In the Baltic countries, for example, interest rates on housing loans reached 6 percent, and the return on equity of banks exceeded 30 percent in the first half of the year, which is almost twice as high as the profitability of Croatian banks. How did we manage to catch Kairos' tuft this time? And why do we not need the legal setting (limitation) of interest rates to be discussed in the Parliament at the moment, as is the case in Latvia? Why, as in Ireland, does the Government not have to introduce reduced tax rates for those whose loan installments have risen sharply this year? "Criticism of the central bank is necessary and desirable, but a balance in approach is also important. It allows us to recognize the elements of successful work of regulators and build the future on them," said Boris Vuji. Happiness rarely falls on its own, and so it was this time. We closely monitored the movements of the youngest son of Zeus and reacted quickly when the opportunity arose. The foundations were laid back in 2012 when the National Reference Rate was legally determined as one of the key parameters for determining variable interest rates. However, the very prevalence of the NRR would have been of little help if the CNB had not focused its efforts on raising consumer awareness of the risk of interest rate hikes and the available protection options. Market interest rates could have remained at relatively low levels in some alternative sequence of events, even without the pandemic and the attack on Ukraine. Therefore, we have never advocated a fixed or variable interest rate, nor any specific parameter for determining it as the optimal choice for each consumer. The choice of credit must be the own decision of each consumer adapted to his personal circumstances. However, as a regulator, we have made consumers aware of the risks they take and encouraged the offer of instruments to protect against these risks. Back in 2017, we issued a recommendation to banks to expand the offer of fixed-rate loans, and we regularly updated the comparative list of banks offering fixed interest rates on the CNB's website and application. Also, in publications and public appearances, we have continuously warned of the risks and monitored the effects of the measures taken. Finally, the legal limitation of interest rates also helped to contain interest rates, which significantly slowed down the growth of a smaller part of interest rates linked to the Euribor, which would otherwise have reacted much more strongly to changes in market conditions. As a result of the CNB's continuous work at all levels, today approximately 120,000 consumers with housing loans have protection against interest rate risk in the form of fixed rates or a certain, mostly multi-year period, during which rates do not change. Last year alone, five thousand consumers switched from variable interest rates linked to the Euribor to fixed rates, largely thanks to information campaigns undertaken by individual banks prompted by the CNB's efforts. The system of setting interest rates that currently exists in Croatia protects consumers from sudden disruptions, but allows enough flexibility for the system to gradually adapt to market circumstances without major breakdowns. But the work of regulators never ends. The system of setting interest rates, as currently exists in Croatia, protects consumers from sudden disruptions, it is easy for citizens to be predominantly granted loans with fixed rates, this can change very quickly. Also, interest rate risk is not the only one, and the housing market is specific because it is mostly attended by young people, without experience with financial institutions, who need to be re-educated and warned. This story of an averted crisis also testifies to the fact that the simultaneous protection of financial stability and consumers can very well represent a common interest of all stakeholders of the financial system. Together, we will all promote this interest even better if the education system, as well as society as a whole, pay more attention to financial literacy. As Pele concluded, success is not a coincidence, but the result of dedicated and persistent work, learning and sacrifice, and most of all love for work. Criticism of the central bank is necessary and desirable, but balance in approach is also important. It also allows us to recognize the elements of successful regulatory work and build on them a future in which we will continue to do everything to ensure that the financial system and consumers are spared to the greatest extent possible dramatically negative consequences of possible unpredictable economic and financial crises. The text is available on the Nacional website. CROATIAN NATIONAL BANK
text_original: HPVATRKA NAPODNA RANKA Kriza koja se nije dogodila Objavljeno: 27.11.2023. Kolumna guvernera Borisa Vujia za tjednik Nacional, objavljena 23. studenoga 2023. Ako si elio da te ljudi vole, trebao si postati lijenik, a ne sredinji bankar, dobrohotan je, iako poprilino zakanjeli savjet koji mi je pred koju godinu udijelio prijatelj. Doista, svaki ivot koji lijenici spase ne donosi samo vjenu zahvalnost sretnika i njegove obitelji, ve i priznanje ireg drutva. Za razliku od toga, krize koje sredinji bankari uspjeno izbjegnu po definiciji su nevidljive. Monetarna i financijska stabilnost uglavnom se uzimaju zdravo za gotovo, kao imanentno svojstvo financijskog sustava ili pak posljedica dobre sree. S druge strane, poviena inflacija bolno je vidljiva te javnost sredinjim bankarima bez mnogo krzmanja dodjeljuje obilne porcije krivnje, ak i ako im u ostvarivanju zadaa ne bi puno pomogla ni kristalna kugla koja bi navijestila epidemije i ratove. Ovaj opsean i autorefleksivan uvod ima samo jednu svrhu - pruiti kontekst zapaanju da upravo proputamo primijetiti krizu koja je uspjeno sprijeena, i to ne zbog naih osobina ili puke sree, nego zbog promiljene dugorone politike regulatora protegnute kroz itavo desetljee. Epizoda globalnog zaotravanja monetarne politike bez presedana u ivom sjeanju za sada prolazi bez iole ozbiljnijih potresa na domaem tritu. Preblag porast depozitnih stopa (za graane) i poviena profitabilnost banaka glavne su neuralgine toke trenutnog financijskog pejzaa koje privlae pozornost financijskih komentatora i raspaljuju nezadovoljstvo javnosti. Takav - po mom miljenju - vrlo benigan ishod monetarnog zaotravanja niim nije bio zajamen. Dosadanja iskustva sa zatezanjem globalnih uvjeta financiranja bila su upravo suprotna - domae kamatne stope obino bi zaplesale i na najmanji povjetarac koji bi dolutao s globalnih financijskih trita, a makroekonomske ranjivosti domaeg gospodarstva osobito bi ojaale uinke snanijih globalnih potresa. Ovaj je put pria krenula neuobiajenih i puno boljim tokom - unato globalnom rastu kamatnih stopa, domaa poduzea prvi se put zaduuju po slinim uvjetima kao njihovi konkurenti u europodruju, a graanima su stambeni krediti ak i neto jeftiniji nego Nijemcima ili Austrijancima. To je pitanje koje su me nebrojeno puta pitali od kad sam poeo raditi u sredinjoj banci, davne 1998. - kada emo se mi u Hrvatskoj moi zaduivati po istoj cijeni kao Nijemci? Evo, ostvarili smo i to. ak su i potroai koji imaju stare stambene kredite zaotravanje monetarnih uvjeta osjetili samo prestankom do nedavno postojanog trenda smanjivanja rata kredita. Za razliku od velikog broja potroaa u europodruju, ije su kamatne stope naglo i snano porasle po 4-5 postotnih poena. Krize koje sredinji bankari uspjeno izbjegnu po definiciji su nevidljive. Monetarna stabilnost uzima se zdravo za gotovo Malen - praktiki na laboratorijskoj skali - odraz onoga to se moglo odigravati u Hrvatskoj pokazuju postojei gotovinski nenamjenski krediti vezani uz Euribor. Kamatne stope na te kredite, a rije je o tek tri posto svih gotovinskih nenamjenskih kredita, porasle su s otprilike 6 posto poetkom godine na gotovo 8 posto danas. S obzirom na malen broj i relativno kratku ronost tih kredita, kao i injenicu da su kamatne stope na postojee kredite graanima padale sve do poetka ove godine, financijska nelagoda tih dunika prolazi gotovo nezapaeno. Ipak, prilino je lako zakljuiti to bi se dogaalo da je kojim sluajem veina kredita odobrena s varijabilnim kamatnim stopama vezanima uz Euribor. Poveanje otplata za 20, 30, pa i vie postotaka - proporcionalno preostaloj ronosti kredita - postalo bi norma, lako bi intenzitet poveanja rata kredita u takvom hipotetskom scenariju bio neto slabiji nego u vrijeme jaanja vicarskog franka, ukupan bi uinak na potroae nesumnjivo bio snaniji jer bi porasle rate na gotovo sve kredite. Kao zrcalna slika rasta kamatnih stopa na kredite, profitabilnost banaka bi mnogo snanije porasla, ak i ako bi neto vie kamatne stope na depozite donekle ponitile utjecaj viih kamatnih stopa na kredite.
