Hipotetski scenarij koji sam opisao predstavlja stvarnost u nizu lanica europodruja - Finskoj, Litvi, Latviji, Estoniji, Portugalu, panjolskoj, Italiji, Irskoj... kao i u nekim zemljama EU-a izvan europodruja. U baltikim zemljama, na primjer, kamatne stope na stambene kredite su dostigle 6 posto, a povrat na kapital banaka u prvoj je polovini godine nadmaio 30 posto, to je gotovo dvostruko vie od profitabilnosti hrvatskih banaka. Kako smo ovaj put uspjeli uhvatiti Kairosov uperak? I zato nam nije potrebno da se u Saboru trenutno raspravlja o zakonskom odreivanju (ograniavanju) kamatnih stopa, kao to je sluaj u Latviji? Zato, kao u Irskoj, Vlada ne mora uvoditi smanjene porezne stope za one kojima su snano porasle rate kredita ove godine? Kritinost prema sredinjoj banci je nuna i poeljna, no balans u pristupu je takoer vaan. On nam omoguuje da prepoznamo i elemente uspjenog rada regulatora i gradimo na njima budunost, istie Boris Vuji. Srea rijetko sama pada u krilo, a tako je bilo i ovoga puta. Budno smo pratili kretanje najmlaeg Zeusova sina i brzo reagirali kada se prilika otvorila. Temelji su postavljeni jo 2012. godine kada je Nacionalna referentna stopa zakonski odreena kao jedan od kljunih parametara za odreivanje promjenjivih kamatnih stopa. No sama rasprostranjenost NRS-a bila bi od slabe pomoi da HNB nije usmjerio napore na jaanje svijesti potroaa o riziku poveanja kamatnih stopa i raspoloivim mogunostima zatite. Trine kamatne stope mogle su ostati na razmjerno niskim razinama u nekom alternativnom slijedu dogaaja, i bez pandemije i napada na Ukrajinu. Stoga nikada nismo zagovarali fiksnu ili varijabilnu kamatnu stopu, niti bilo koji konkretan parametar za njezino odreivanje kao optimalan izbor za svakog potroaa. Izbor kredita mora biti vlastita odluka svakog potroaa prilagoena njegovim osobnim okolnostima. No kao regulator smo osvijestili potroae na rizike koje preuzimaju i potaknuli ponudu instrumenata za zatitu od tih rizika. Jo 2017. godine bankama smo izdali preporuku da proire ponudu kredita s fiksnim stopama, a na internetskim stanicama i aplikaciji HNB-a redovito smo aurirali usporednu listu banaka koje nude fiksne kamatne stope. Takoer, u publikacijama i javnim istupima kontinuirano smo upozoravali na rizike i pratili uinke poduzetih mjera. Konano, obuzdavanju kamatnih stopa pomoglo je i zakonsko ogranienje kamata koje je znatno usporilo rast manjeg dijela kamatnih stopa vezanih uz Euribor, koje bi inae znatno snanije reagirale na promjenu trinih uvjeta. Kao rezultat kontinuiranog djelovanja HNB-a na svim razinama, danas otprilike 120 tisua potroaa sa stambenim kreditima ima zatitu od kamatnog rizika u vidu fiksnih stopa ili odreenog, uglavnom viegodinjeg razdoblja, u kojemu se stope ne mijenjaju. Samo je lani pet tisua potroaa prelo s varijabilnih kamatnih stopa vezanih uz Euribor na fiksne stope, dobrim dijelom zahvaljujui informativnim akcijama koje su pojedine banke poduzele potaknute HNB-ovim nastojanjima. Sustav odreivanja kamatnih stopa kakav trenutno postoji u Hrvatskoj titi potroae od naglih poremeaja, ali omoguava dovoljno fleksibilnosti da se sustav postupno, bez velikih lomova, prilagodi trinim okolnostima. No posao regulatora nikada ne zavrava. Sustav odreivanja kamatnih stopa kakav trenutno postoji u Hrvatskoj, titi potroae od naglih poremeaja lako se graanima trenutno dominantno odobravaju krediti s fiksnim stopama, to se vrlo brzo moe promijeniti. Takoer, kamatni rizik nije jedini, a stambeno trite je specifino jer se na njemu uglavnom javljaju mladi ljudi, bez iskustva s financijskim institucijama, koje treba iznova educirati i upozoravati. Ova pria o izbjegnutoj krizi svjedoi i o tome da istovremena zatita financijske stabilnosti i potroaa itekako moe predstavljati zajedniki interes svih dionika financijskog sustava. Taj emo interes svi zajedno jo bolje promicati ako obrazovni sustav, ali i drutvo u cjelini, posvete veu panju financijskoj pismenosti. Kao to je Pele zakljuio, uspjeh nije sluaj, nego rezultat predanog i ustrajnog rada, uenja i odricanja, a najvie ljubavi prema poslu. Kritinost prema sredinjoj banci je nuna i poeljna, no balans u pristupu je takoer vaan. On nam omoguuje da prepoznamo i elemente uspjenog rada regulatora i gradimo na njima budunost u kojoj emo i nadalje initi sve da financijski sustav i potroai u najveoj mjeri budu poteeni dramatino negativnih posljedica moguih nepredvidivih ekonomskih i financijskih kriza. Tekst je dostupan na internetskim stranicama Nacionala.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Stepping Through Policy Normalization: Managing the Recovery and Weighing the Risks
text: Taming through policy normalization: managing recovery and weighing risks Published: 22.9.2021. Article by Governor Vujcic for views - The EUROFI Magazine, september 2021 edition The coronavirus pandemic has all the elements of a good Hollywood film. First, there is the threat of "the end of the world as we know it." There are also the heroes of the pandemic: scientists who quickly developed vaccines and the pharmaceutical industry that hastily produced them. Finally, there is a happy ending, the rapid pace of recovery exceeding expectations during the repeated waves of the pandemic, with vaccinations as an additional boost to economic growth as the population of developed countries moves closer to achieving collective immunity. Efforts to boost the Mr. Podar recovery through vaccinations have nevertheless had strong accomplices: fiscal and monetary policies that underpinned the global economy during a critical period. Unlike the global financial crisis, when monetary policy was practically the "only game in town," strong fiscal stimulus this time was aligned with an unprecedented monetary policy accommodation. Fiscal and monetary policies reinforced each other in a positive vicious circle. Fiscal expansion financing was facilitated by favourable UVfinancing jets maintained by central banks, and larger budget deficits amplified the impact of monetary policy. However, despite the improved outlook, the recovery remains uneven within individual countries as well as among different parts of allaspects. There are still significant downside risks associated with new variants of the virus and the limited availability of vaccines, as well as the indecision of citizens to get vaccinated. Most policy makers in developed economies are therefore in no hurry to abolish emergency policiesa. For the first time since the beginning of the pandemic, the improved outlook has opened the way for discussion on the path to monetary policy normalisation. There is broad consensus on the sequence of steps on the path to monetary policy normalisation: first, purchasesworthy of sni-paper will be abolished, interest rate hikes will follow, while at a later stage the maturity of government bonds, and perhaps even direct sales, the size of central banks' balance sheets will gradually decrease. However, there is much less agreement when it comes to the beginning and pace of monetary policy normalisation. Central banks from the two largest economic blocs have so far avoided talking about the start of normalisation, assuming that a debate on the issue itself would encourage a tightening of monetary conditions. However, several central banks from smaller developed economies, such as Canada or Australia, have already announced or even begun reducing monetary stimulus. Some differences between central banks regarding the start of implementation of measures can be attributed to idiosyncratic factors related to the economic funds of each country. However, much of the differences in central banks' communication can be attributed tothese different risk attitudes. Among the central banks of the largest economic blocs, the prevailing view is that the current rise in inflation is transient in nature. Stabilising energy and commodity prices and gradually recovering overstretched production chains and addressing labour market mismatches are considered sufficient to contain inflationary pressures. Likewise, inflation expectations seem to be firmly anchored - regardless of what indicator of inflation expectations they are looking at. Finally,it is considered that a monetary policy error resulting in slightly higher inflation than the target level would be less costly than a premature tightening of monetary policy, especially bearing in mind that we have the appropriate tools and knowledge to deal with the probleprosy of excessive inflation. The relaxation of central banks of large developed countries in conditions of increasing inflationary pressures is not surprising. Low inflation has surprised us many times over the last ten years, so many times it gives a continuousunderperformance of inflation relative to the target in central bankers has created fears of deflation. However, the determinants of inflation, which we obviously do not fully understand, can also act in the opposite direction. The pandemic has opened up cracks in the process of globalization, which can lead to the loosening of disinflationary forces. And inflation expectations can change quickly-we know that consumers, businesses and financial market participants are no better at forecasting inflation than central banks. After a prolonged gap inthe round of ultra-low interest rates, elevated levels of public and private debt and strained asset prices can affect surprising market reactions if central banks are forced to act strongly. Finally, recent adjustmentsto Mon Etar policy strategies may also complicate the situation, as markets do not yet know the new monetary policy reaction functions, which could force central banks to act even in situations that would not otherwise require it. In conclusion, it is important to emphasize that we should carefully step through recovery, weigh risks over and over again and avoid strategies that at some point may require overreactions.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Kroenje kroz normalizaciju politike: upravljanje oporavkom i vaganje rizika Objavljeno: 22.9.2021. lanak guvernera Vujia za publikaciju Views - The EUROFI Magazine, izdanje rujan 2021. Pandemija koronavirusa ima sve elemente dobrog holivudskog filma. Prvo, tu je prijetnja kraja svijeta kakvog poznajemo". Tu su i heroji pandemije: znanstvenici koji su brzo razvili cjepiva i farmaceutska industrija koja ih je urno proizvela. Naposljetku, tu je i sretan zavretak, brz tempo oporavka premaivao je oekivanja tijekom opetovanih valova pandemije, s cijepljenjem kao dodatnim poticajem gospodarskom rastu kako se stanovnitvo razvijenih zemalja pribliava postizanju kolektivnog imuniteta. Napori da se cijepljenjem potakne gospodarski oporavak imali su ipak i snane pomagae: fiskalne i monetarne politike koje su podupirale globalno gospodarstvo tijekom kritinog razdoblja. Za razliku od globalne financijske krize, kada je monetarna politika bila praktiki "jedina igra u gradu", snaan fiskalni poticaj ovaj je put bio usklaen s dosad nezabiljeenom akomodacijom monetarne politike. Fiskalne i monetarne politike meusobno su se pojaavale u pozitivnom zaaranom krugu. Financiranje fiskalne ekspanzije bilo je olakano povoljnim uvjetima financiranja koje su odravale sredinje banke, a vei proraunski manjkovi pojaavali su uinak monetarne politike. Ipak, unato poboljanim izgledima, oporavak je i nadalje neujednaen unutar pojedinih zemalja kao i meu razliitim dijelovima svijeta. Jo su prisutni znatni negativni rizici povezani s novim varijantama virusa i ogranienom dostupnou cjepiva, kao i neodlunou graana da se cijepe. Veina nositelja politika u razvijenim gospodarstvima stoga ne uri s ukidanjem izvanrednih politika. Prvi put od poetka pandemije poboljani izgledi otvorili su prostor za raspravu o putu prema normalizaciji monetarne politike. Postoji irok konsenzus u pogledu slijeda koraka na putu normalizacije monetarne politike: prvo e se ukinuti kupnje vrijednosnih papira, potom e uslijediti poveanje kamatnih stopa, dok e u kasnijoj fazi dospijea dravnih obveznica, a moda ak i izravne prodaje, postupno smanjivati veliinu bilance sredinjih banaka. Meutim, znatno je manje suglasja kada je rije o poetku i tempu normalizacije monetarne politike. Sredinje banke iz dvaju najveih gospodarskih blokova dosad su izbjegavale govoriti o poetku normalizacije, pretpostavljajui da bi i sama rasprava o tom pitanju potakla zaotravanje monetarnih uvjeta. Meutim, nekoliko sredinjih banaka iz manjih razvijenih gospodarstava, kao to su Kanada ili Australija, ve je najavilo ili je ak zapoelo smanjivanje monetarnih poticaja. ak je i japanska sredinja banka stabilizirala veliinu svoje bilance u okviru kontrole krivulje prinosa. Neke razlike meu sredinjim bankama vezane uz poetak provedbe mjera mogu se pripisati idiosinkratskim imbenicima vezanima uz gospodarske fundamente pojedine zemlje. Ipak, vei dio razlika u komunikaciji sredinjih banaka moe se pripisati razliitim stavovima o rizicima. Meu sredinjim bankama najveih gospodarskih blokova prevladava stav da je trenutni porast inflacije prolaznog karaktera. Stabilizacija cijena energije i sirovina te postupan oporavak prenapregnutih lanaca proizvodnje i rjeavanje neusklaenosti na tritu rada smatraju se dovoljnim za obuzdavanje inflacijskih pritisaka. Isto tako, ini se da su inflacijska oekivanja vrsto usidrena - bez obzira na to koji pokazatelj inflacijskih oekivanja promatrali. Naposljetku, smatra se da bi pogreka u monetarnoj politici koja bi rezultirala neto viom inflacijom od ciljane razine bila manje skupa od preuranjenog pootravanja monetarne politike, osobito imajui u vidu da raspolaemo primjerenim alatima i znanjem za rjeavanje problema prekomjerne inflacije. Oputenost sredinjih banaka velikih razvijenih zemljama u uvjetima jaanja inflatornih pritisaka ne iznenauje. Niska inflacija mnogo nas je puta iznenadila tijekom posljednjih deset godina, toliko puta daje kontinuirano podbacivanje inflacije u odnosu na cilj kod sredinjih bankara stvorilo strah od deflacije. Meutim, odrednice inflacije, koje oito ne razumijemo u potpunosti, jednako tako mogu djelovati i u suprotnom smjeru. Pandemija je otvorila pukotine u procesu globalizacije, to moe dovesti do poputanja dezinflacijskih sila. I inflacijska oekivanja se mogu brzo promijeniti-znamo da potroai, poduzea i sudionici na financijskim tritima nisu bolji u prognoziranju inflacije od sredinjih banaka. Nakon dugotrajnog razdoblja iznimno niskih kamatnih stopa, poviene razine javnog i privatnog duga i napregnute cijene imovine mogu utjecati na iznenaujue reakcije trita ako sredinje banke budu prisiljene na snano djelovanje. Naposljetku, nedavne prilagodbe strategija monetarne politike takoer mogu zakomplicirati situaciju jer trita jo ne poznaju nove reakcijske funkcije monetarne politike, to bi sredinje banke moglo primorati na djelovanje ak i u situacijama koje to inae ne bi zahtijevale. U zakljuku vano naglasiti da trebamo paljivo kroiti kroz oporavak, stalno iznova vagati rizike i izbjegavati strategije koje bi u nekom trenutku mogle zahtijevati pretjerane reakcije.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Human capital and economic growth in Croatia: How to move forward faster?
text: Human capital and economic growth in Croatia: How to move forward faster? Published: 6/9/2016 Type Speech Speaker Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor Date of publicationof the statement 9.6.2016. Human Capital and Economic Growth in Croatia: How to move forward faster? Dogadanje Konferencija "An Enterprise Odyssey: Saving the Sinking Ship Through Human Capital" Venue Of events Faculty of Economics, Zagreb Guverner Boris Vujcic danas je na medunarodnoj konferenciji "An Enterprise Odyssey: Saving the Sinking Ship Through Human Capital" u organizaciji zagrebackog Ekonomskog fakulteta, na plenarnoj sjednici odr9eao uvodno izlaganje pod naslovom "Human Capital and Economic Growth in Croatia: Howto Make the Ship Move Faster". In his speech, the Governor introductoryly referred to the definition of human capital, which includes education, experience, training, intelligence, but also work habits, initiative, credibility, etc. There are still difficulties in measuring human capital, because while, for example, measuring years of education standard, it is much more difficult to measure human motivation, or e.g. the impact of personality on possible educational achievements. However, in the last twenty years it has become possible to measure the quality of human capital thanks to standardised tests at an internationally comparable level. Human capital, too, the governor noted, has its own micro and macroeconomic aspects. At first glance, it is immediately clear that every person when thinking about his investment in education, he is actually thinking about his the future and the possible financial situation, and less often human capital is referred to as a necessary precondition for productivity and economic growth. Scientific research in the mid-1990s found that in the educational process quality is more important than quasi-i.e. years of education. In the case of Croatia, as regards the quantity of education, the years of schooling, that is, the percentage of people of working age with a certain level of education, the percentage of students leaving education early, as well as the percentage ofnatural history or engineering studies, Croatia is not far behind the Central and Eastern European (CEE) average, or even the EU28. However, according to the quality of education, i.e. according to the results of internationally standardized tests, Croatia isfor both CEE countries and the EU28 average. Education spending is not too different from the European average, but the distribution gap is key. In Croatia, much more is spent on preschool and primary education, while the results of tests onpupils lag far behind the European average. Croatia also lags far behind the average of both the EU and CEE in the field of lifelong learning. Lifelong learning is increasingly important, as changes in the economy are getting faster and knowledge gained into shapeeducation is becoming more and more obsolete. If we compare us with the countries in environment - Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Romania - in Croatia there is a significantly lower impact of education, i.e. human capital on potential GDP growth. In Summary human capital measurement results, including recognised international educational tests PISA and TIMSS as well as the human capital index, Croatia has results below the EU average, which is one of the main causes of weaker productivity growth, and the lastbut also the level of GDP per capita. Croatia is also significantly behind in R&D investments, patent applications and knowledge transfer to the business sector. In conclusion, Croatia is close to the EU average in terms of quantity of education, but lags behind in the results, i.e. the quality of education, as well as in the transfer of knowledge primarily to the business sector, which speaks in support of the need for structural reforms of both the education system and the link between the education and business system in order to strengthen theverge and medium-term potential growth of the country.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Ljudski kapital i ekonomski rast u Hrvatskoj: Kako bre naprijed? Objavljeno: 9.6.2016. Vrsta Govor Govornik Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a Datum objave izjave9.6.2016. Tema Ljudski kapital i ekonomski rast u Hrvatskoj: Kako bre naprijed? Dogaanje Konferencija "An Enterprise Odyssey: Saving the Sinking Ship Through Human Capital" Mjesto dogaanja Ekonomski fakultet, Zagreb Guverner Boris Vuji danas je na meunarodnoj konferenciji "An Enterprise Odyssey: Saving the Sinking Ship Through Human Capital" u organizaciji zagrebakog Ekonomskog fakulteta, na plenarnoj sjednici odrao uvodno izlaganje pod naslovom "Human Capital and Economic Growth in Croatia: Howto Make the Ship Move Faster". U govoru se guverner uvodno osvrnuo na definiciju ljudskog kapitala koji ukljuuje obrazovanje, iskustvo, obuavanje, inteligenciju, ali i radne navike, inicijativnost, vjerodostojnost, itd. Jo postoje tekoe u mjerenju ljudskog kapitala, jer dok je npr. mjerenje godina obrazovanja standard, puno je tee mjeriti ljudsku motivaciju, ili npr. utjecaj osobnosti na mogua obrazovna postignua. Meutim u zadnjih dvadeset godina postalo je mogue mjeriti kvalitetu ljudskog kapitala zahvaljujui standardiziranim testovima na meunarodno usporedivoj razini. Ljudski kapital, takoer, istaknuo je guverner, ima svoje mikro i makroekonomske aspekte. Na prvi je pogled odmah jasno da svaka osoba kada razmilja o svojem ulaganju u obrazovanje, ustvari razmilja o svojoj budunosti i moguoj financijskoj situaciji, a rjee se o ljudskom kapitalu govori kao nunom preduvjetu za produktivnost i ekonomski rast. U znanstvenim istraivanjima sredinom devedesetih ustanovljeno je daje u obrazovnom procesu kvaliteta vanija od kvantitete, odnosno godina obrazovanja. U sluaju Hrvatske, to se tie kvantitete obrazovanja, godina kolovanja, odnosno postotka ljudi u radno aktivnoj dobi s odreenom razinom obrazovanja, postotka uenika koji rano naputaju obrazovanje, kao i postotka onih koji upisuju prirodoslovne ili inenjerske studije, Hrvatska ne zaostaje za prosjekom Sredinje i istone Europe (SIE), pa ak ni EU28. Meutim prema kvaliteti obrazovanja, odnosno prema rezultatima meunarodno standardiziranih testova, Hrvatska zaostaje kako za zemljama SIE, tako i prosjeka EU28. Izdvajanje za obrazovanje ne razlikuje se previe od europskog prosjeka, ali je zato kljuna razlika u distribuciji. U Hrvatskoj se puno vie troi za predkolsko i osnovno obrazovanje, dok rezultati testova osnovnokolskih uenika znatno zaostaju za europskim prosjekom. Hrvatska takoer znatno zaostaje za prosjekom i EU i SIE u podruju cjeloivotnog uenja. Cjeloivotno uenje je sve vanije, jer su promjene u ekonomiji sve bre i znanje koje se stjee u formalnom obrazovanju sve bre zastarijeva. Ukoliko nas usporedimo sa zemljama u okruenju - Bugarskom, ekom, Maarskom, Poljskom i Rumunjskom - u Hrvatskoj je znaajno nii utjecaj obrazovanja, odnosno ljudskog kapitala na potencijalni rast BDP-a. U zbirnim rezultatima mjerenja ljudskog kapitala, to ukljuuje priznate meunarodne obrazovne testove PISA i TIMSS kao i indeks ljudskog kapitala, Hrvatska ima rezultate ispod prosjeka EU to je jedan od glavnih uzronika slabijeg rasta produktivnosti, a posljedino i visine BDP-a per capita. Hrvatska takoer znaajno zaostaje u ulaganjima u istraivanja i razvoj, prijavama patenata i transferu znanja u poslovni sektor. Zakljuno, Hrvatska je blizu EU prosjeka s obzirom na kvantitetu obrazovanja, ali zato znaajno zaostaje u rezultatima, odnosno kvaliteti obrazovanja, kao i u transferu znanje prvenstveno u poslovni sektor, to govori u prilog o potrebi za strukturnim reformama kako obrazovnog sustava, tako i veze obrazovnog i poslovnog sustava kako bi se ojaala konvergencija i srednjoroni potencijalni rast zemlje. Conclusion 16 Literature Census 17 Author Information 18 Abstract 18 Summary 18 Keywords 19 Introduction Consumer protection is considered to be the main, if not the only, objective of the supervision of1 securities market and supervision of insurance companies. Unlike these two sectors of the financial system, the belief is that consumer protection is not and cannot be the objective of banking supervision due to: (i) the nature of the banking business, (ii) the role and importance of banks in the financial system and (iii) the available supervisory resources. All of the above led to two approaches to supervision of the financial sector, so that the prudential approach to supervision was identified with banks, while supervision of compliance with the legality of the business was identified with the other two sectors. However, some countries have also prescribed consumer protection as an objective or task through banking supervisors, in addition to already declared objectives such as concern for the stability of the system and for the safety, stability and solvency of individual banks. Why did individual countries prescribe consumer protection as a goal and others not to do so, and which countries are they? This paper tried to look at the issue of consumer protection in the provision and use of banking services from three aspects. The first aspect concerns the question of whether consumer protection is essentially the goal of banking supervision or not, and whether different approaches to supervision have different goals, and vice versa. We can consider the answers to these questions as the first hypothesis posed in this paper. Another aspect concerns the fact-finding that the issue of consumer protection has been resolved by other countries. Due to the strategic commitment of the Republic of Croatia to join the European Union, EU Member States were taken as a sample, with the division into "old" and "new" members being made (it was taken as a border in 2004). This division was made because of the mutual similarity and development of the structure of the economic and financial system of the "old", that is, the "new" members individually, and because of the multiple similarities and desirable comparison of the "new" members with the Republic of Croatia. The analysis of how individual countries have addressed the issue of consumer protection has gone from the way financial and banking supervision is organised - whether it is within one unified institution responsible for the entire financial system or according to the sectoral principle - and whether consumer protection is prescribed as an objective, i.e. the task of banking supervision. In addition, attempts have been made to determine whether individual supervisory institutions that are responsible for banks have a specific organisational part established that deals exclusively with consumer protection activities. This is due to the existence of significant differences between the declarative commitment to the prescribed objective and the actual treatment in practice. The existence of a special organizational part in this work is considered to be higher, one might say real, a form of fulfillment of the prescribed goal, although this sometimes does not have to mean in practice. The analysis of this section tried to answer the question of whether there is a correlation between the model of organization of financial supervision and commitment to the goal of consumer protection, and we can consider a positive answer to this question as the second hypothesis of this work. The third aspect concerns Croatian conditions and the question of how consumer protection when using banking services in Croatia is legislatively and organizationally resolved. In the first part of this paper, the arguments of whether consumer protection is the objective of banking and financial supervision are theoretically considered, while in the second and third part the 1 Supervision, in the relevant case, shall further be used as a common name for regulation and supervision. financial supervision organisations and a focus on consumer protection by EU country. In the fourth part, Croatian conditions were analyzed, while in the fifth part conclusions are made on the basis of the hypotheses set. I. Is consumer protection the goal of supervision by banks and other financial institutions? It is widely known that banks and almost all other financial institutions around the world receive special treatment regarding the regulation and supervision of their operations. However, the question may arise as to why their business is specifically regulated and supervised, i.e. why their business is specifically regulated and supervised. objectives to be achieved and, consequently, why specific supervisory institutions are being set up. Without entering into at this time the economic reasons (such as, for example, the need to eliminate market imperfections and asymmetry of information, unfavourable externalities, moral hazard, etc.) that are intended to achieve certain goals, although they somewhat determine what goals will be set in the first place, we adhere to the widespread opinion (Goodhart and others2, 1998). and Llewellyn3, 1999. these are the three main objectives: - care for the stability of the system - security, stability and solvency of individual financial institutions and - consumer protection. However, until recently, and traces of this way of thinking can still be found, there was a different interpretation of the goals to be achieved, depending on the supervisory approach towards banks, and to some extent towards other financial institutions. Namely, there are originally two approaches to supervision: (i) prudential supervision, which focuses on the security, stability and solvency of an individual institution, and therefore, consequently, on the stability of the system and (ii) the supervision of compliance with the legality of the business, which focuses on in the way of providing services to the users of those services. There is a belief, which has been particularly pronounced in the near past, that consumer protection is not the objective of prudential supervision, but that it is only the security, stability and solvency of individual financial institutions, and therefore concern for the stability of the system. On the other hand, the supervisory approach aimed at respecting the legality of the business is to protect consumers. This was particularly pronounced for the supervision of banks, so that "... the jobs of a bank supervisor are sometimes described as the jobs of a doctor who takes care of the overall health of the patient, while the tasks of supervising the securities market are described as the affairs of a financial police officer tasked with preventing fraud and misrepresentation"4. In addition to the different approach to work, due to the specificities of banks' operations compared to other financial market institutions, it was pointed out that consumer protection activities in banks are far more demanding in their volume and time needed to carry them out, so that 2 Goodhart, C., Hartmann, P., Llewellyn, D., Rojas-Suarez, L. i Weisbrod, S., Financial Regulation: Why, how and where now? , Routledge, London, 1998. 3 Llewellyn, D., The Economic Rationale for Financial Regulation, Finanical Services Authority Occasional Paper, br. 1., 1999. 4 Abrams, R. i Taylor, M., Issues in the Unification of Financial Sector Supervision, IMF Working Paper, br. 213, International Monetary Fund, Monetary and Exchange Affairs Department, 2000., str. 18. the majority of resources would be allocated to such jobs and would result in a lack of resources for prudential supervision, resulting in weaker concern for the stability of the banking system and the security and solvency of individual banks (Abrams and Taylor5, 2000 and Goodhart6, 2000). This issue comes to the fore in particular when considering the arguments in support of, i.e. against the consolidation of individual supervisory institutions responsible for a particular segment of the system into a new, single institution responsible for the entire financial system. Because of this thinking in the mid-1990s, the so-called "Taylor7, 1995" was created (Taylor 7, 1995). The Twin peaks model, which starts from the objective of supervision, i.e. whether its objective is the stability of the financial system or the protection of consumers. According to this model, supervision aimed at the stability of the financial system, would apply a prudential approach to supervision and its scope of work would include banking and its associated payment transactions and, possibly, some other parts of the system. On the other hand, supervision aimed at protecting consumers would base its approach to supervision on monitoring the legality of business and the application of regulations, and would apply, when it comes to consumer protection, to all other institutions, including banks. The application of this model is very rare, and it was introduced, according to the available information, only by the Netherlands and Australia and, in part, by South Africa. However, some authors (Davies8, 2003 and Llewellyn9, 2000) consider consumer protection to be a common objective of both approaches to supervision - both prudential, and respect for the legality of business. Namely, caring for the stability of the system or financial stability is not an end in itself or a theoretical category, and it actually serves to create conditions in which the value of deposits and investments of individual savers and investors will be preserved. Furthermore, this creates preconditions for their continued willingness to hold and invest their financial assets over the long term, thereby affecting the preservation and strengthening of trust in the financial system. It is undeniable that the failure of a bank or other financial institution has an impact on financial stability, but it also has an effect on consumer protection, as this leads to a loss of the value of deposits and investments of individual depositors and investors. It is therefore concluded that financial stability is merely a means of achieving the ultimate objective: consumer protection and that these two objectives cannot be viewed separately. On the basis of what has been put forward, it can be concluded that consumer protection is indisputably one of the fundamental objectives of supervision of banks and other financial institutions, but that a certain combination and balance is also needed in the application of both approaches, both the prudential approach to supervision and the one based on respect for the legality of the business, in order to achieve all the main objectives as they are impossible to observe separately. The Croatian National Bank62, in addition to conducting monetary policy activities as the original affairs of the central bank, is also responsible for banking supervision on the basis of the provisions of the Law on the Croatian National Bank63 and the Bank Law64. Banking supervision includes prescribing business conditions by issuing bylaws, issuing authorisations for work and carrying out supervision. Entities of regulation and supervision mean banks and housing savings banks as depository or credit institutions. Prescribing business conditions includes the issuance of authorisations for work and consents for certain legal activities, and bylaws related to ways of managing risks and certain business procedures. The performance of supervision is based, first of all, on prudential supervision, i.e. on prudential supervision. supervision of the stability and sustainability of the business, and on the supervision of respect for the legality and correctness of the business in prudential terms. Banks Act 2002 In 2015, he adopted, the first in the history of banking regulation in Croatia, provisions on the protection of consumers - users of banking services - and dedicated an entire chapter to this matter. Consumer protection provisions include minimal transparency of banks' operations through the publication of general terms and conditions, the way services are contracted and the way of informing users or consumers. However, in the provisions relating to consumer complaints for non-compliance with contracts, as well as in the manner of their resolution, the legislator did not impose this obligation on the supervisor of banks, i.e. for non-compliance with the contract. Already in such cases, the individual consumer is referred to the bank concerned and its organizational part of the internal audit, then to consumer protection associations and to the State Inspectorate and other competent authorities. Of course it is not necessary to point out that the consumer can always turn to the competent court to protect his interests and rights. The Croatian National Bank is not obliged to deal with individual complaints of the bank's clients, but is obliged, within the framework of its supervisory powers, to check whether the bank generally adheres to good business practices, published general terms and conditions of business and concluded contracts. In addition, the cited law introduced the possibility of applying a special law governing consumer protection, which at the time of the adoption of the Act had not yet been adopted (mid-2002), with the aim of better protecting consumers when using banking services. Therefore, it is assumed, the legislature did not prescribe the obligation to deal with individual complaints, which, by their volume and time needed to carry out this type of work, are very demanding. Since there was no legal institute of consumer protection at the time, since the Consumer Protection Act66 was adopted only in mid-2003, it was assumed that this was also one of the reasons for the relatively large number of complaints about the operations of banks addressed to the CNB. V. Conclusion On the basis of the conducted research, the following conclusions can be drawn and answers to the hypotheses set from the beginning of work can be given. First, consumer protection, in addition to concerning the stability of the system and for the security, stability and solvency of individual financial institutions, is one of the main objectives of supervision of banks and other financial institutions. The prudential approach to supervision and the approach that prioritises respect for the legality of the business have no different objectives and a combination of the two approaches and balances in the application of both is needed, which again depends on the current circumstances and the priorities set in order to achieve all objectives. Secondly, it has established a trend of bringing supervisory institutions together into a new, single institution responsible for the entire financial system, so that almost half of the observed states already apply this model of financial supervision organization. Thirdly, consumer protection is the prescribed goal, that is, the task of banking supervision in most of the observed countries. For "old" EU members, this is 66 per cent, while in the "new" it is 50 per cent, and on the aggregate sample it is 60 per cent. Indirectly, one can draw the conclusion that consumer protection becomes a prescribed objective with a higher degree of development of the financial system. Fourth, the existence of an organisational part exclusively engaged in consumer protection activities within a banking supervisory institution, as a higher level in achieving the objective of consumer protection, was established in just over half of the countries where consumer protection is prescribed as the objective of bank supervision. So there's a difference between declarative and actual commitment to achieving that goal. Fifth, a correlation between the organisation of financial supervision and the commitment to consumer protection has been established. In all observed countries where financial supervision is pooled and organised within one institution, responsible for the entire financial system, consumer protection is laid down as an objective. In addition, all countries that have an organisational part to protect consumers within the banking supervision institution are in this group of countries with a unified supervision of the financial sector. Thus, consumer protection is better achieved in those countries that have pooled financial supervision within one institution. This paper did not answer the question of whether this is the result of the commitment of regulatory creators (dependent on civilizational achievements or on the development of the financial system) or whether this is due to the inclusion of supervision of the securities market and insurance companies in a single institution, whose main goal is to protect consumers. In this regard, further research into the topic will be interesting. Sixthly, by analyzing Croatian conditions, we come to the realization that consumer protection is not a directly prescribed goal of banking supervision and that there is no specific organizational part for these jobs, but that this goal is given considerable importance in everyday business, which has resulted in significant progress. Summary This paper tried to determine whether consumer protection is essentially the objective of banking supervision and how this issue has been regulated by EU countries. In addition, the legislative and organizational regulation of consumer protection when using banking services in Croatia was observed. On the basis of the sample under review, it was found that consumer protection is prescribed as an objective in most EU countries, but that there are differences in their operational approach. A positive correlation was found between the organisation of financial supervision and the commitment to consumer protection in all countries where financial supervision is consolidated and organised within one institution. Summary This paper tried to establish whether consumer protection is in its essence the aim of banking supervision and to determine how this issue is dealt with in the EU countries. It is also examined how the issue of consumer protection in the use of banking services is dealt with in Croatia in terms of legislative and organisational framework. On the basis of the observed sample, it has been established that consumer protection is the prescribed objective in most countries, with differences existing in operative approach. We have established a positive correlation between the organisation of financial supervision and a commitment towards consumer protection in all the countries with consolidated financial supervision, organised within a single institution. Significant improvement has been made in Croatia in terms of the available legislative and operative framework for consumer protection in the use of banking services. Zato su pojedine zemlje zatitu potroaa propisale kao cilj, a druge to nisu uinile, te koje su to zemlje? Ovaj je rad problematiku zatite potroaa u pruanju i koritenju bankovnih usluga pokuao sagledati iz tri aspekta. Prvi aspekt odnosi se na pitanje je li zatita potroaa u svojoj biti cilj bankovne supervizije ili nije, te imaju li razliiti pristupi superviziji razliite ciljeve, i vice versa. Odgovore na ta pitanja moemo smatrati prvom hipotezom postavljenom u ovom radu. Drugi aspekt odnosi se na utvrivanje injenica kako su pitanje zatite potroaa rijeile druge drave. Zbog stratekog opredjeljenja Republike Hrvatske o pristupanju Europskoj uniji za uzorak su uzete drave lanice EU, s time da je napravljena podjela na "stare" i "nove" lanice (kao granica uzeta je 2004. godina). Ova podjela napravljena je zbog meusobne slinosti i razvijenosti strukture gospodarskoga i financijskog sustava "starih", odnosno "novih" lanica ponaosob, te zbog viestruke slinosti i poeljne komparacije "novih" lanica s Republikom Hrvatskom. U analizi kako su pojedine drave rijeile pitanje zatite potroaa polo se od naina organizacije financijske i bankovne supervizije  je li to unutar jedne objedinjene institucije nadlene za cjelokupni financijski sustav ili je to prema sektorskom naelu  te da li je zatita potroaa propisana kao cilj, odnosno zadaa bankovne supervizije. Uz to, pokualo se utvrditi da li pojedine supervizijske institucije koje su nadlene za banke, imaju ustrojen poseban organizacijski dio koji se bavi iskljuivo poslovima zatite potroaa. Je li zatita potroaa cilj supervizije banaka i ostalih financijskih institucija? Ope je poznato da banke i gotovo sve ostale financijske institucije diljem svijeta imaju poseban tretman u pogledu regulacije i nadzora svoga poslovanja. Meutim, moe se postaviti pitanje zato se njihovo poslovanje posebno regulira i nadzire, tj. koji se ciljevi ele postii te, posljedino, zato se osnivaju posebne supervizijske institucije. Ne ulazei u ovom trenutku u ekonomske razloge (kao to su, na primjer, potreba za otklanjanjem trine nesavrenosti i asimetrinosti informacija, nepovoljnih eksternalija, moralnog hazarda itd.) zbog kojih se ele postii odreeni ciljevi, premda oni donekle determiniraju koji e se ciljevi uope postaviti, priklanjamo se rairenom miljenju (Goodhart i ostali2, 1998. i Llewellyn3, 1999.) da su ovo tri glavna cilja:  briga za stabilnost sustava  sigurnost, stabilnost i solventnost pojedinanih financijskih institucija i  zatita potroaa. Meutim, sve donedavno, a jo se mogu nai tragovi takvog naina razmiljanja, postojalo je razliito tumaenje ciljeva koje treba postii, ovisno o supervizijskom pristupu prema bankama, a donekle i prema ostalim financijskim institucijama. Naime, izvorno postoje dva pristupa superviziji: (i) bonitetna supervizija, koja je usredotoena na sigurnost, stabilnost i solventnost pojedinane institucije, a time, posljedino, i na stabilnost sustava i (ii) nadzor nad potivanjem zakonitosti poslovanja, koji je usredotoen na nain pruanja usluga korisnicima tih usluga. Meutim, pojedini autori (Davies8, 2003. i Llewellyn9, 2000.) smatraju da je zatita potroaa zajedniki cilj oba pristupa superviziji  i bonitetnog, i potivanja zakonitosti poslovanja. Naime, briga za stabilnost sustava ili financijska stabilnost nije cilj sam za sebe ili neka teoretska kategorija, te on zapravo slui za stvaranje uvjeta u kojima e se sauvati vrijednost depozita i investicija pojedinanih tedia i ulagaa. Nadalje, to stvara pretpostavke za njihovu daljnju spremnost za dranje i ulaganje svoje financijske imovine na dui rok, a ime se utjee na ouvanje i jaanje povjerenja u financijski sustav. Neosporno je da propast banke ili druge financijske institucije ima uinak na financijsku stabilnost, ali isto tako ima uinak i na zatitu potroaa jer time dolazi do gubitka vrijednosti depozita i investicija pojedinanih deponenata i investitora. Stoga se zakljuuje da je financijska stabilnost samo sredstvo za ostvarenje konanog cilja: zatitu potroaa i da se ova dva cilja ne mogu promatrati odvojeno. Na osnovi iznesenoga moe se izvesti zakljuak da je zatita potroaa neosporno jedan od temeljnih ciljeva supervizije banaka i ostalih financijskih institucija, ali da je isto tako potrebna odreena kombinacija i ravnotea u primjeni obaju pristupa, i bonitetnog pristupa superviziji i onog koji se bazira na potivanju zakonitosti poslovanja, kako bi se postigli svi glavni ciljevi jer ih je nemogue promatrati zasebno. Zatita potroaa pri koritenju bankovnim uslugama u Hrvatskoj Financijska supervizija u Republici Hrvatskoj organizirana je prema sektorskom naelu s izravnom ukljuenou sredinje banke u bankovnu superviziju, te je ukupno pet institucija61 nadleno za superviziju financijskih institucija i trita: Hrvatska narodna banka, Komisija za vrijednosne papire, Direkcija za nadzor drutava za osiguranje, Agencija za nadzor mirovinskih fondova i osiguranja i Ministarstvo financija  Uprava za financijski sustav. Hrvatska narodna banka62 je, osim za voenje poslova monetarne politike kao izvornih poslova sredinje banke, nadlena i za superviziju banaka na osnovi odredaba Zakona o Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci63 i Zakona o bankama64. Supervizija banaka obuhvaa propisivanje uvjeta poslovanja izdavanjem podzakonske regulative, izdavanje odobrenja za rad i obavljanje nadzora. Pod subjektima regulacije i nadzora podrazumijevaju se banke i stambene tedionice kao depozitne, odnosno kreditne institucije. Propisivanje uvjeta poslovanja obuhvaa izdavanje odobrenja za rad i suglasnosti za odreene pravne poslove, te podzakonsku regulativu vezanu za naine upravljanje rizicima i odreenim postupcima poslovanja. Obavljanje supervizije temelji se, prije svega, na bonitetnoj superviziji, tj. nadzoru stabilnosti i odrivosti poslovanja, te na nadzoru potivanja zakonitosti i ispravnosti poslovanja u bonitetnom smislu. Zakon o bankama iz 2002. godine donio je, prvi u povijesti regulacije bankovnog poslovanja u Hrvatskoj, odredbe o zatiti potroaa  korisnika bankovnih usluga  i cijelo jedno poglavlje posvetio toj materiji. Odredbe o zatiti potroaa obuhvaaju minimalnu transparentnost poslovanja banaka kroz objavu opih uvjeta poslovanja, nain ugovaranja usluga te nain obavjetavanja korisnika, odnosno potroaa. Meutim, u odredbama koje se odnose na reklamacije potroaa zbog nepotivanja ugovora, kao i na nain njihova rjeavanja, zakonodavac tu obvezu nije nametnuo supervizoru banaka, tj. Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci, ve se u takvim sluajevima pojedinani potroa upuuje na dotinu banku i njezin organizacijski dio unutarnje revizije, zatim na udruge za zatitu potroaa te na Dravni inspektorat i druga nadlena tijela. Naravno da nije potrebno isticati kako se potroa uvijek moe obratiti nadlenom sudu radi zatite svojih interesa i prava. Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci nije nametnuta obveza rjeavanja pojedinanih reklamacija klijenata banke, ve je ona duna, u okviru svojih nadzornih ovlatenja, provjeravati pridrava li se banka openito dobrih poslovnih obiaja, objavljenih opih uvjeta poslovanja i sklopljenih ugovora. Osim navedenoga, citirani je zakon uveo mogunost primjene posebnog zakona kojim se ureuje zatita potroaa, a koji u vrijeme donoenja Zakona jo nije bio donesen (sredina 2002.), u cilju bolje zatite potroaa pri koritenju bankovnim uslugama. Ovako postavljeno zakonsko ureenje donekle uspostavlja ravnoteu u postizanju osnovnih ciljeva bankovne supervizije, tj. osim brige za stabilnost financijskog sustava te sigurnost, 61 Prema Odluci Vlade RH od 27. listopada 2004., a na temelju ranije preuzete obveze prema MMF-u iskazane u Pismu namjere, odlueno je da e se nadzorne institucije nebankarskog sektora objediniti u jednu instituciju i koja e za svoj rad odgovarati Vladi i Saboru. 62 Vidi http://www.hnb.hr 63 Vidi Zakon o Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci, NN 36/01. 64 Vidi Zakon o bankama, NN 84/02. 14 stabilnost i solventnost pojedinanih banaka, u odreenoj je mjeri obuhvatio i zatitu potroaa, ali tako da ipak prevladava bonitetni pristup superviziji. Zbog toga, pretpostavlja se, zakonodavac nije propisao obvezu rjeavanja pojedinanih pritubi, koje su svojim obujmom i vremenom potrebnim za obavljanje te vrste poslova vrlo zahtjevne. Iako rjeavanje pojedinanih pritubi potroaa nije posao i zadaa bankovne supervizije, one i nadalje, usprkos tome, u nemalim koliinama dolaze u HNB, gdje se rjeavaju, prije svega, zbog reputacijskog rizika banke, HNB-a i bankovnog sustava u cjelini. Pored rjeavanja pojedinanih pritubi potroaa u mjeri koja ne prelazi u arbitrau izmeu suprotstavljenih strana, HNB je samoinicijativno donio neke podzakonske propise radi bolje zatite potroaa, kojima se podrobnije regulira i utvruje jedinstveni nain izraunavanja i iskazivanja cijene kredita i depozita65. U HNB-u je sredinom 2002. godine (do stupanja na snagu Zakona o bankama) izvreno mjerenje pojedinanih pritubi potroaa, te je utvreno da svakodnevno dolazi prosjeno jedna pisana prituba i nekoliko telefonskih. Kako u to vrijeme nije postojao pravni institut zatite potroaa, jer je Zakon o zatiti potroaa66 donesen tek sredinom 2003., pretpostavljalo se da je i to jedan od razloga relativno velikog broja pritubi na poslovanje banaka upuenih HNB-u. Prilikom pisanja ovog rada, koncem 2004. godine napravljeno je novo mjerenje pritubi potroaa koje dolaze u HNB te je utvreno da se broj pritubi prepolovio. Je li uzrok padu broja pritubi postojanje pravnog instituta zatite potroaa kroz odredbe Zakona o bankama ili Zakona o zatiti potroaa, ili je on posljedica sve vee konkurencije izmeu banaka, ili neega treeg, u ovom se radu ne pokuava utvrditi. U svakom sluaju, bit e zanimljivo vidjeti rezultate ovakvoga ili slinog istraivanja. 65 Odluka o jedinstvenom iskazivanju efektivne kamatne stope na kredite i depozite, NN, br. 74/2003., prvi put je bila propisana poetkom 2001. 66 Vidi Zakon o zatiti potroaa, NN, br. 96/2003. 15 V. Zakljuak Na osnovi provedenog istraivanja mogu se izvui sljedei zakljuci te dati odgovori na postavljene hipoteze s poetka rada. Prvo, zatita potroaa, osim brige za stabilnost sustava te za sigurnost, stabilnost i solventnost pojedinanih financijskih institucija, jedan je od glavnih ciljeva supervizije banaka i ostalih financijskih institucija. Bonitetni pristup superviziji i pristup koji prioritet daje potivanju zakonitosti poslovanja nemaju razliite ciljeve te je potrebna kombinacija tih dvaju pristupa i ravnotea u primjeni oba, koja opet ovisi o trenutanim okolnostima i utvrenim prioritetima kako bi se postigli svi ciljevi. Drugo, utvren je trend objedinjavanja supervizijskih institucija u novu, jedinstvenu instituciju nadlenu za cjelokupni financijski sustav, tako da ve gotovo polovina promatranih drava primjenjuje taj model organizacije financijske supervizije. Tree, zatita potroaa propisani je cilj, odnosno zadaa bankovne supervizije u veini promatranih drava. Kod "starih" lanica EU to iznosi 66 posto, dok je kod "novih" 50 posto, a na agregiranom uzorku iznosi 60 posto. Neizravno se moe izvui zakljuak da zatita potroaa postaje propisani cilj s viim stupnjem razvoja financijskog sustava. etvrto, postojanje organizacijskog dijela koji se iskljuivo bavi poslovima zatite potroaa unutar bankovne supervizijske institucije, kao vieg stupnja u ostvarenju cilja zatite potroaa, utvreno je u neto vie od polovine drava u kojima je zatita potroaa propisana kao cilj bankovne supervizije. Znai, postoji razlika izmeu deklarativnoga i stvarnog opredjeljenja u postizanju toga cilja. Peto, utvrena je korelacija izmeu organizacije financijske supervizije i opredjeljenja za zatitu potroaa. U svim promatranim dravama u kojima je financijska supervizija objedinjena i organizirana unutar jedne institucije, nadlene za cjelokupni financijski sustav, zatita potroaa propisana je kao cilj. Uz to, sve drave koje imaju organizacijski dio za zatitu potroaa unutar institucije za bankovnu superviziju, nalaze se u ovoj grupi drava s objedinjenom supervizijom financijskog sektora. Znai, zatita potroaa bolje se ostvaruje u onim zemljama koje imaju objedinjenu financijsku superviziju unutar jedne institucije. Ovaj rad nije dao odgovor na pitanje je li to rezultat opredjeljenja kreatora regulative (ovisan o civilizacijskim dostignuima ili o razvoju financijskog sustava) ili je to posljedica ukljuivanja supervizije trita vrijednosnih papira i drutava za osiguranje u jedinstvenu instituciju, kojima je osnovni cilj zatita potroaa. U tom smislu bit e zanimljiva daljnja istraivanja te teme. esto, analizirajui hrvatske uvjete, dolazimo do spoznaje da zatita potroaa nije izravno propisani cilj bankovne supervizije i da ne postoji poseban organizacijski dio za te poslove, ali da se tom cilju pridaje znatna vanost u svakodnevnom poslovanju, to je rezultiralo znaajnim napretkom. 16 Popis literature Abrams, Richard i Taylor, Michael: Issues in the Unification of Financial Sector Supervision, IMF Working Paper, br. 213, International Monetary Fund, Monetary and Exchange Affairs Department, 2000. Godine 1997. postao je direktorom Direkcije platnog prometa. Sredinom 1998. godine postaje izvrnim direktorom Sektora nadzora i kontrole s ciljem ublaavanja izraenih i sprjeavanja daljnjih problema u bankovnom sustavu te unapreenja funkcije bankovne supervizije. Glavni je urednik i suautor nekoliko knjiga, autor vie strunih i znanstvenih lanaka, te glavni urednik Biltena o bankama.
