Viceguverner edo Maleti u HNB koordinira i rukovodi poslovima iz podruja Sektora bonitetne regulative i nadzora banaka i Sektora platnog prometa. Saetak Ovaj rad pokuao je utvrditi je li zatita potroaa u svojoj biti cilj bankovne supervizije te kako su ovu problematiku uredile zemlje EU. Uz to, promatrano je zakonodavno i organizacijsko ureenje zatite potroaa pri koritenju bankovnim uslugama u Hrvatskoj. Na osnovi promatranog uzorka utvreno je da je zatita potroaa propisana kao cilj u veini zemalja EU, ali da kod njih postoje razlike u operativnom pristupu. Utvrena je pozitivna korelacija izmeu organizacije financijske supervizije i opredjeljenja za zatitu potroaa kod svih drava gdje je financijska supervizija objedinjena i organizirana unutar jedne institucije. U Hrvatskoj je ostvaren znaajan napredak u zakonodavnom i operativnom ureenju zatite potroaa pri koritenju bankovnim uslugama. Summary This paper tried to establish whether consumer protection is in its essence the aim of banking supervision and to determine how this issue is dealt with in the EU countries. It is also examined how the issue of consumer protection in the use of banking services is dealt with in Croatia in terms of legislative and organisational framework. On the basis of the observed sample, it has been established that consumer protection is the prescribed objective in most countries, with differences existing in operative approach. We have established a positive correlation between the organisation of financial supervision and a commitment towards consumer protection in all the countries with consolidated financial supervision, organised within a single institution. Significant improvement has been made in Croatia in terms of the available legislative and operative framework for consumer protection in the use of banking services. 18 Kljune rijei bankovna supervizija  banking supervision zatita potroaa  consumer protection bonitetna supervizija  prudential supervision nadzor nad potivanjem zakonitosti poslovanja  conduct of business supervision

Title: Monetary policy cannot be a substitute for structural reforms and fiscal policy
text: Monetary policy cannot be a substitute for structural reforms and fiscal policy Published: 27.10.2016. Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor 26.10.2016. Monetary policy cannot be a substitute for structural reforms and fiscal policy, Effectus College, Zagreb 26.10.2016. The Croatian National Bank will continue to pursue an expansionary monetary policy in 2017, announced CNB Governor Boris Vujcic as part of the fifth forum of effectus university. In his presentation entitled "Characteristics and challenges of monetary policy of the Republic of Croatia", he explained that central banks, as a reactionon the financial crisis, began to pursue an expansionary monetary policy using conventional and unconventional measures, but economic growth remained weak and inflation remained low. In this context, the risks of expansionary monetary policies are increasing, and withama monetary policy - conventional as well as unconventional, cannot be a substitute for structural reforms and fiscal policy - in the upward phase of the cycle must be restrictive in order to create space for countercyclical action in the downward phase, said je governor, stressing that due to the absence of structural reforms, the risks will grow more and more. He also stated that the limitations of monetary policy in Croatia are high euroisation of deposits and placements and high foreign exchange indebtedness of all sectors, which poses a risk to financial stability, and at high levels there is also an import dependency of the economy because Croatia is a small and open economy with a high share of exports and imports to GDP (about 50%). In such conditions, the CNB achieves its basic goal of maintaining price stability, towardsthe objective of preserving financial stability, by maintaining the stability of the nominal exchange rate of the kuna against the euro. As the most important causes of euroisation, the Governor singled out experiences of high inflation from the past, the proximity of large economies, the level of openness of the domestic economy, transfers, the quality of institutions, network externalities. network externalities), the so-called original sin the original son) - the inability to borrow in the domestic currency abroad, but also the prominent public space occupied by the long-standing lawmakers forthe devaluation of the kuna, according to the governor, who also contributed to keeping euroization at a high level. The CNB continuously implements the policy of disincentive to euroisation through a higher relative regulatory cost and by encouraging kunalending, while preserving the stability of the exchange rate. The reduction of euroisation benefits the CNB the most, since the lower the degree of euroisation, the higher the pillars of the CNB's freedom of action, the governor said. The CNB will continue to implement an expansionary policy of supporting high liquidityand the monetary system through structural and regular repo operations, and, where appropriate, foreign exchange transactions. Thus, the CNB favors the improvement of domestic financing conditions and supports the recovery of domestic credit activity. The CNB's expansionary monetary policy was thelowering of the kuna yield curve, especially on the medium/longer gender, the development of the domestic market for kuna government securities and the motivation of banks to increase lending in KUNA. Thus, banks that participated in structural repo ope raidshalted the decline in lending. In addition to favourable developments in credit supply and demand, the results of expansionary monetary policy are evident in the continuous improvement of financing conditions and lower interest rates for all sectors. In doing so, more and more mastersof business are achieving credit growth, while only the construction sector does not follow trends because it has been hit hardest by the crisis and has the most non-performing loans. In addition to pursuing an expansionary monetary policy, the CNB will continue to work strongly to preserve the financial withtability, where the policy of strengthening bank bookings, which has also encouraged banks to step up activities to deal with bad placements, is highlighted. In conclusion, the Governor reiterated that the basis of a stronger recovery in the economy is the increase in competitiveness ofthe home of the economy, based on structural reforms and export growth, while containing macroeconomic imbalances and continuing to consolidate public finances. After the presentation, the Governor answered questions from vice-dean Dr. Sc. Neven Vidakovic, as well asnumerous questions from students of effectus university.
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna politika ne moe biti zamjena za strukturne reforme i fiskalnu politiku Objavljeno: 27.10.2016. Vrsta Govor Govornik Datum objave izjave Tema Mjesto dogaanja Datum dogaanja Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a 26.10.2016. Monetarna politika ne moe biti zamjena za strukturne reforme i fiskalnu politiku Visoko uilite Effectus, Zagreb 26.10.2016. Hrvatska narodna banka nastavit e voditi ekspanzivnu monetarnu politiku i u 2017. godini, najavio je guverner HNB-a Boris Vuji u sklopu petog po redu foruma Visokog uilita Effectus. U svom izlaganju pod nazivom "Obiljeja i izazovi monetarne politike Republike Hrvatske" objasnio je kako su sredinje banke, kao reakciju na financijsku krizu, poele voditi ekspanzivnu monetarnu politiku koristei konvencionalne i nekonvencionalne mjere, no gospodarski rast ostao je slab, a inflacija niska. U takvom kontekstu sve vie rastu rizici ekspanzivnih monetarnih politika, a sama monetarna politika - konvencionalna, kao i nekonvencionalna, ne moe biti zamjena za strukturne reforme i fiskalnu politiku - u uzlaznoj fazi ciklusa mora biti restriktivna kako bi se stvorio prostor za protucikliko djelovanje u silaznoj fazi, rekao je guverner te naglasio da e zbog izostanka strukturnih reforma rizici sve vie rasti. Naveo je i da su ogranienja monetarne politike u Hrvatskoj visoka euroiziranost depozita i plasmana te visoka devizna zaduenost svih sektora, to predstavlja rizik za financijsku stabilnost, a na visokim je razinama i uvozna zavisnost gospodarstva jer Hrvatska je mala i otvorena ekonomija s visokim udjelom izvoza i uvoza u BDP-u (oko 50%). U takvim uvjetima HNB postie svoj osnovni cilj odravanja stabilnosti cijena, kao i cilj ouvanja financijske stabilnosti, odravanjem stabilnosti nominalnog teaja kune prema euru. Kao najvanije uzroke euroizacije guverner je izdvojio iskustva visoke inflacije iz prolosti, blizinu velikih gospodarstava, razinu otvorenosti domaega gospodarstva, transfere, kvalitetu institucija, mrene eksternalije (engl. network externalities), tzv. izvorni grijeh (engl. original sin) - nemogunost zaduivanja u domaoj valuti u inozemstvu, ali i istaknut javni prostor koji zauzimaju dugogodinji zagovaratelji devalvacije kune, smatra guverner, a koji su takoer doprinijeli zadravanju euroizacije na visokoj razini. HNB kontinuirano provodi politiku destimuliranja euroizacije s pomou viega relativnog regulatornog troka i poticanjem kunskoga kreditiranja, uz uvanje stabilnosti teaja. Smanjenje euroizacije najvie koristi HNB-ujerto je stupanj euroizacije nii, stupovi su slobode djelovanja HNB-a vei, rekao je guverner. HNB e nastaviti provoditi ekspanzivnu politiku podravanja visoke likvidnosti monetarnog sustava strukturnim i redovitim repo operacijama, a prema potrebi i deviznim transakcijama. Time HNB pogoduje poboljanju domaih uvjeta financiranja i podrka je oporavku domae kreditne aktivnosti. HNB-ova ekspanzivna monetarna politika pridonijela je sputanju kunske krivulje prinosa, osobito na srednjoj/duoj rodnosti, razvoju domaeg trita za kunske dravne vrijednosne papire te motiviranju banaka da poveaju kreditiranje u kunama. Tako su banke koje su sudjelovale u strukturnim repo operacijama zaustavile pad kreditiranja. Uz povoljna kretanja kreditne ponude i potranje, rezultati ekspanzivne monetarne politike vidljivi su u kontinuiranom poboljavanju uvjeta financiranja i niim kamatnim stopama za sve sektore. Pritom sve vie gospodarskih djelatnosti ostvaruje rast kredita, dok jedino sektor graevinarstva ne prati trendove jer je najjae bio pogoen krizom i ima najvie loih kredita. HNB e uz voenje ekspanzivne monetarne politike nastaviti snano djelovati na ouvanju financijske stabilnosti, gdje se istie politika jaanja rezervacija banaka, koja je ujedno potaknula banke na jaanje aktivnosti rjeavanja loih plasmana. Guverner je zakljuno ponovno naglasio da je temelj snanijeg oporavka gospodarstva poveanje konkurentnosti domae ekonomije, zasnovano na strukturnim reformama i rastu izvoza, uz istodobno obuzdavanje makroekonomskih neravnotea i nastavak konsolidiranja javnih financija. Nakon izlaganja guverner je odgovarao na pitanja prodekana dr. sc. Nevena Vidakovia, kao i na brojna pitanja studenata Visokog uilita Effectus.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Monetary reform would raise interest rates, and citizens would again flee to euros
text: Monetary reform would raise interest rates, and citizens would flee to the euro again Published: 3/10/2016 Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, Governor 9.3.2016. Half-yearly information for 2015 Session of the Croatian Parliament Zagreb Following the address of the Governor of the Croatian National Bank Boris Vujcic, members of the Croatian Parliament discussed on 9 March 2016 the Semiannual Information on the Financial Situation, the degree of realisation of price stability and the implementation of monetary policy for the first half of 2015. Goran Maric (HDZ), Ivan Lovrinovic (Most), Gordan Maras (SDP), Anka Mrak-Tarita9a (HNS), Miro Bulj (Most), Ivan 8auker (HDZ), Ruzica Vukovac (Most), Boris Lalovac (SDP), Mi lorad Pupovac (SDSS), Irena Petrijevcanin Vuksanovic (HRID), Ivica Mi9aic (Most), 8eeljko Glasnovic (HDZ), Josip Leko (SDP), Radimir Cacic (Reformists), Goran Dodig (BM 365), participated in the debate. Giovanni Sponza (IDS), Ingrid Anticevic Marinovic (SDP), Maro Kristic (Most), Miroslav 8aimic, Josip Kri9eanic (HDZ) and Branimir Glavas (HDSSB). In his responses to the parliamentary debates, the Governor singled out the position of the Croatian National Bank with the most important and practically only intrinsic criticism of monetary policyand explained the position of the Croatian National Bank. The governor explained the problems posed by the inflation target regime, stressing that "the policy of target inflation, which can be guided, and in some countries is run, implies runninga policy of the ike flexible exchange rate. In other words, in such a monetary policy regime, the exchange rate of the kuna against the euro would no longer be used as an instrument to anchor the inflation expectations and expectations of savers." He added that the proposal for the inflation target is consistent and consistent with the proposal for gradual depreciation and explained that the reaction of Croatian citizens if the Croatian National Bank announces such a change in monetary policy would be to transfer their assets from kuna to euro. "The only source of the euro in circumstancesno matter when people start converting their kunas into the euro - because it pays off more for them, because the euro will be worth more to them than the kuna tomorrow - are the foreign exchange reserves of the Croatian National Bank. So, at that moment, we should start selling foreign exchange reserves of the Republic of Croatia. In order for the foreign exchange reserves of the Republic of Croatia to fall, the rating of the Republic of Croatia would fall because they are now rated, as you know, marginally sufficient, even insufficient by the IMF. In order for the rating to fall, so would the kamatne rates rise." He concluded that such a policy of deprecation would lead to rising interest rates and warned that in that case, loans would become more expensive and harder to access. 'What would the banks do? They would say: Well, if the governor announced that this is a new policyof the Croatian National Bank, then we also want to shorten our position in kunas, banks would start selling kunas and buying euros. Whereof? Again from the Croatian National Bank because only we with our foreign exchange reserves at that moment could fit into the sale, the relationshipbut the defence of the kuna exchange rate so that there would not be a sudden devaluation and then again the result would eventually be a rise in interest rates." The governor gave an example of what a 10% depreciation of the kuna would mean using data for 2014. "In addition to the unchanged other conditions, exporters of goods and services would receive HRK 15.2 billion more, while for existing imports of goods and services, all economic operators would have to pay HRK 14.5 billion more. So there's some kind of positive billion and 300 million. Foreign currency deposit holders, including the central government, would be nominally 18.3 billion kuna richer. At the same time, the kuna equivalent of foreign debt of all sectors would increase by HRK 35.6 billion, while domestic foreign currency debt and indexation into foreign currency would increase by HRK 25.3 billion. So the net effect of the 10% depreciation of the kuna would be deeply negative, HRK 41.9 billion. It means practically HRK 42 billion, or 12.8% of GDP. That is why I say that such a policy leads to recession, not to betterment for the Croatian economy and for Croatian citizens." The decision on the legal abolition of the currency clause can only be taken by parliament, not by the Croatian National Bank, the governor said, adding: "If you decided to abolish the currency clause and not abolish foreign currency savings - what would happen? Banks would suddenly have a huge open foreign exchange position because they would have savings in the euro and loans in kunas. Now, they have no place to close this open foreign exchange position and are fully exposed to foreign exchange risk so that op et interest rates wouldrise and loans would simply become less accessible." "At the end of June 2015, the total domestic and foreign debt of all sectors amounts to 80103 billion, with 8081.3 billion or 78.7% of them in foreign currency or indexed against a foreign currency. If receivables with the currency clause of credit institutions on the domestic market against all domestic sectors were abolished, excluding the central government, the portion of the total debt affected by the exchange rate would be reduced to a still significant 8062.6 billion and amount to 60.6% of the total debt. If the currency clause were to be further abolished for credit institutions' claims against the central government, then the exchange rate would affect the debt of 60 billion euros, or 58.4% of the total debt. Here's so much about monetary reform and what monetary reform would do in Croatia." Speaking about the bank's reserve requirement rate, the governor agreed that it is high and that the Croatian National Bank is exactly why it is reducing it. "This reduces the regulatory burden on banks after the crisis and this is one of the GLAsources of monetary policy expansion, let's not forget that it has been reduced from 30.5% to the current 12% and we will continue to reduce it." He stressed that the reserve requirement rate will continue to decrease, but this cannot happen at once, so as not to provoke a speculative attack on the kuna. Boris Vujcic reiterated that structural repo auctions have started right now because there is now a high surplus in the current account of the balance of payments with an excess of foreign assets of banks in relation to othernon-liabilities, the recovery of gross domestic product and the growing demand for kuna loans. But, he stressed, structural repo auctions will not solve the problems of the Croatian economy because the problem of money's passability to the economy persists. He also recalled his long-standing proposal to introduce a guarantee scheme that can replace the lack of collateral and capital in our businesses. On the notion that the CNB overly optimistically describes the situation in the Croatian economy, the governor said that they are simply completely inaccurate and completely misguided. On the contrary, the CNB has persistently warned for years about the structural weaknesses of the Croatian economy, high deficits and the growth of public debt, and the need for stronger implementation of structural reforms. If anything could be objected to,it is the opposite, the CNB has revised its GDP growth estimates upwards several times in the past year, which means that, like other forecasters, including international financial institutions, it has been overly pessimistic rather than overly optimistic. Remarking that the Croatian National Bank is not doing enough to deeuurize, the governor stressed that the Croatian National Bank implemented a whole range of measures to encourage the recunization of the economy. "The strongest and most efficient was that we asked banks to hold additional capital to lend in foreign currency to those who do not have a so-called natural hedge, do not have income in that currency," the governor said. He pointed out that such measures "managed to reduce euroisation somewhat, so we came from 78% to some 63%, but the crisis came and within 3 months everyone was back in the euro, because people were scared." "As soon as The Croats get scared, they run into the euro, as they used to be in the brand, and it's a psychological category, there's no monetary policy to change that," the governor added, continuing that "at the moment we are twice as regulatory burdensome on the euro in the banking sector as the kuna, and again it doesn't help much." Responding to criticism of HNB's relationship with small banks, the governor said that "small banks are in exactly the sametreatment as the big banks. Small bank placements are in exactly the same regulatory treatments as the placements of the big banks." The Governor also addressed the way the annual report is submitted and described the way the European Central Bank reports on its work to the European Parliament. "We submit financial statements to parliament. Every month we submit financial statements to the Ministry of Finance and this is an established practice. I come here, I will answer your questions if you will quarterly, not half-yearly or annually, and I hope and glad that we can continue the discussion at the Croatian National Bank and we will now, given that there is interest, and I am very glad to start that as soon as there are opportunities, so after this session of parliament." Representatives also asked direct questions about the operations of the Croatian National Bank, expenditures and expenses for employees. The Governor replied that "the expenditure of the Croatian National Bank in 2010 was HRK 341.5 million, in 2014 hrk 309 million, for 2015 we do not yet have an audit report, but HRK 319 million is planned. So, there was a drop in the expenditure of the Croatian National Bank, not a growth in expenditure, and they decreased by 10% by 2014, or 8% by 2015." Governor Vujcic also reiterated that the Croatian National Bank is notresponsible for the supervision of Austrian savings banks. In response to a question about Credo Bank, Boris Vujcicje said that "Credo Bank was in the process of forced liquidation, which means that it lost its license and therefore was no longer allowed to perform the services for which it was licensed, which includes the performance of payment transactions. Because of this, it was under suspension of payment execution in our payment systems, it is the HSVP and NCS, meaning a large payment system and a small clearing system, however by law liquidation does not mean the cessationof odd companies, that is, enforcements had to be carried out." The governor pointed out that there was an investigation into this, which showed that everything was fine. Referring to the comments on loans with a currency clause in Swiss francs, he emphasized that the Croatian National Bankcared about the interest of Croatian citizens and "proposed a solution, that is, solutions that can most help those who need to be helped, indebted in the Swiss franc, and not burdened with legal and financial risks of the Croatian budget, i.e. all taxpayers." Lawmakers wanted to know how protected banks in Croatia are from the crisis in mother countries, to which the governor replied: "They are well protected. Why? Because they are Croatian banks. That should be borne in mind. Means Zagrebacka banka is a Croatian bank, founded in Croatia with capital in Croatia." The governor added that the bank "can be turned now into a branch under European laws and we cannot prevent this, but this means that then the deposits are insured from the Italian state, not from the Croatian statee." He emphasized that banks in Croatia have very high capital adequacy. "So the capital adequacy of Croatian banks is much higher than the capital adequacy of their mother banks and this gives them certainty, since the financial stability of Croatia depends on it." The Governor told the members of parliament that the Croatian National Bank warned about the use of EURIBOR in credit agreements, but its use was made possible by the Parliament, which passed the Consumer Credit Act, not the CNB. He has been lining up, still proposing possible solutions to this problem, some of which have been accepted, so the offer of kuna loans with a fixed interest rate is now widespread on the domestic market, and will continue to propose them to the new Government. In conclusion, Governor Vujcic stressed that "the CNB was buying time for governments to be able to make structural reforms to kick-start the economy. Monetary policy can do this and it is not only the monetary policy of the Croatian National Bank that works, it is done by monetary policies and, say, the European Central Bank. But if these reforms are not made, monetary policy is powerless to increase productivity."
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Monetarna reforma povisila bi kamate, a graani bi opet pobjegli u eure Objavljeno: 10.3.2016. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Tema Dogaanje Mjesto dogaanja Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner 9.3.2016. Polugodinja informacija za 2015. Sjednica Hrvatskog sabora Zagreb Nakon obraanja guvernera Hrvatske narodne banke Borisa Vujia, zastupnici u Hrvatskom saboru raspravljali su 9. oujka 2016. o Polugodinjoj informaciji o financijskom stanju, stupnju ostvarenja stabilnosti cijena i provedbi monetarne politike za prvo polugodite 2015. U raspravi su sudjelovali Goran Mari (HDZ), Ivan Lovrinovi (Most), Gordan Maras (SDP), Anka Mrak-Tarita (HNS), Miro Bulj (Most), Ivan uker (HDZ), Ruica Vukovac (Most), Boris Lalovac (SDP), Mi lorad Pupovac (SDSS), Irena Petrijevanin Vuksanovi (HRID), Ivica Mii (Most), eljko Glasnovi (HDZ), Josip Leko (SDP), Radimir ai (Reformisti), Goran Dodig (BM 365), Giovanni Sponza (IDS), Ingrid Antievi Marinovi (SDP), Maro Kristi (Most), Miroslav imi, Josip Kriani (HDZ) i Branimir Glava (HDSSB). U svojim odgovorima na zastupnike rasprave, guverner je najvanijom i praktiki jedinom sutinskom kritikom monetarne politike izdvojio prijedlog za monetarnom reformom te obrazloio stav Hrvatske narodne banke. Guverner je objasnio probleme koje nosi reim ciljane inflacije, naglasivi da "politika ciljane inflacije, koja se moe voditi, i u nekim zemljama se vodi, podrazumijeva voenje politike fleksibilnog teaja. Drugim rijeima u takvom reimu monetarne politike teaj kune prema euru vie se ne bi koristio kao instrument kojim se sidre inflacijska oekivanja i oekivanja tedia." Dodao je kako je prijedlog za ciljanom inflacijom sukladan i konzistentan prijedlogu za postupnom deprecijacijom te objasnio da bi reakcija hrvatskih graana u sluaju da Hrvatska narodna banka najavi takvu promjenu monetarne politike bila prebacivanje njihove imovine iz kune u euro. "Jedini izvor eura u okolnostima kad ljudi ponu konvertirati svoje kune u euro - zato jer im se to vie isplati, zato jer e im euro vie vrijediti u odnosu na kunu sutra - su devizne rezerve Hrvatske narodne banke. Znai, u tom trenutku, trebali bismo poeti prodavati devizne rezerve Republike Hrvatske. Kako bi devizne rezerve Republike Hrvatske padale, tako bi rejting Republike Hrvatske padao zato jer su one sada ocijenjene, kao to znate, granino dovoljnima, ak nedovoljnima od strane MMF-a. Kako bi rejting padao, tako bi rasle kamatne stope." Zakljuio je da bi tako politika deprecijacije dovela do rasta kamatnih stopa te upozorio i da bi u tom sluaju i krediti postali skuplji i tee dostupni. 'to bi banke napravile? Rekle bi: Pa dobro, ako je guverner najavio da je to nova politika Hrvatske narodne banke, onda i mi elimo skratiti svoju poziciju u kunama, banke bi poele prodavati kune i kupovati eure. Od koga? Opet od Hrvatske narodne banke jer bi jedino mi sa svojim deviznim rezervama u tom trenutku mogli stati u prodaju, odnosno obranu teaja kune da ne bi dolo stvarno do nagle devalvacije i onda bi opet rezultat na koncu bio rast kamatnih stopa." Guverner je dao primjer to bi znaila deprecijacija kune od 10% koristei podatke za 2014. godinu. "Uz nepromijenjene ostale uvjete izvoznici roba i usluga primili bi 15,2 milijarde kuna vie, dok bi za postojei uvoz roba i usluga svi ekonomski subjekti morali platiti 14,5 milijardi kuna vie. Znai tu imate nekakvu pozitivnu milijardu i 300 milijuna kuna. Vlasnici deviznih depozita, ukljuujui i sredinju dravu, bili bi nominalno bogatiji za 18,3 milijarde kuna. Istovremeno kunska protuvrijednost inozemnog duga svih sektora poveala bi se za 35,6 milijardi kuna, dok bi se domai dug u stranoj valuti i indeksiranost u stranu valutu poveao za 25,3 milijarde kuna. Tako da bi neto uinak 10%-tne deprecijacije kune bio duboko negativan, 41,9 milijardi kuna. Znai praktiki 42 milijarde kuna, odnosno 12,8% BDP-a. Zato kaem da takva politika vodi u recesiju, a ne u boljitak za hrvatsku ekonomiju i za hrvatske graane." Odluku o zakonskom ukidanju valutne klauzule moe donijeti samo Sabor, a ne Hrvatska narodna banka, rekao je guverner, te dodao: "Ako biste vi odluili ukinuti valutnu klauzulu, a ne biste ukinuli deviznu tednju - to bi se dogodilo? Banke bi odjednom imale ogromnu otvorenu deviznu poziciju zato jer bi imale tednju u euru, a kredite u kunama. E sad, nemaju otkuda zatvoriti tu svoju otvorenu deviznu poziciju i potpuno su izloene deviznom riziku tako da bi kamatne stope opet porasle, a krediti bi jednostavno postali manje dostupni." "Na kraju lipnja 2015. ukupni domai i inozemni dug svih sektora iznosi 103 milijarde eura, pri emu je od toga 81,3 milijarde ili 78,7% u stranoj valuti ili indeksirano uz stranu valutu. Ako bi se ukinula potraivanja s valutnom klauzulom kreditnih institucija na domaem tritu prema svim domaim sektorima, iskljuujui sredinju dravu, dio ukupnog duga koji bi bio pod utjecajem teaja smanjio bi se na i dalje znaajnih 62,6 milijardi eura te bi iznosio 60,6% ukupnog duga. Ako bi se dodatno ukinula valutna klauzula i za potraivanja kreditnih institucija prema sredinjoj dravi, tada bi teaj utjecao na dug od 60 milijardi eura, odnosno 58,4% ukupnog duga. Evo toliko o monetarnoj reformi i to bi monetarna reforma uinila u Hrvatskoj." Govorei o stopi obvezne rezerve banaka, guverner se sloio da je ona visoka te da je Hrvatska narodna banka upravo zato i smanjuje. "Tako smanjujemo regulatorno optereenje banaka nakon krize i to je jedan od glavnih izvora ekspanzivnosti monetarne politike, ne zaboravimo da je ona smanjena sa 30,5% na sadanjih 12% i dalje emo ju nastaviti smanjivati." Naglasio je da se e se stopa obvezne rezerve nastaviti smanjivati, no to se ne moe dogoditi odjednom, kako se ne bi provocirao pekulativni napad na kunu. Boris Vuji je ponovio da se sa strukturnim repo aukcijama zapoelo upravo sada zbog toga to je sada prisutan visok suficit na tekuem raunu platne bilance uz viak inozemne imovine banaka u odnosu na inozemne obveze, oporavak bruto domaeg proizvoda te raste potranja za kunskim kreditima. No, naglasio je, strukturne repo aukcije nee rijeiti probleme hrvatskog gospodarstva jer je i dalje prisutan problem prohodnosti novca prema gospodarstvu. Podsjetio je i na svoj dugogodinji prijedlog o uvoenju jamstvene sheme koja moe zamijeniti nedostatak kolaterala i kapitala u naim poduzeima. Na konstatacije da HNB pretjerano optimistino opisuje stanje u hrvatskom gospodarstvu, guverner je rekao da su jednostavno potpuno netone i u cijelosti promaene. Upravo suprotno, HNB uporno godinama upozorava na strukturne slabosti hrvatskog gospodarstva, visoke deficite i rast javnog duga te potrebu snanijeg provoenja strukturnih reformi. Ako se ita moglo prigovoriti, onda je to upravo suprotno, HNB je u protekloj godini nekoliko puta revidirao svoje procjene rasta BDP-a navie, to znai daje, kao i ostali prognostiari, ukljuujui meunarodne financijske institucije, bio pretjerano pesimistian, a ne pretjerano optimistian. Na primjedbe da Hrvatska narodna banka ne radi dovoljno na deeurizaciji, guverner je naglasio daje Hrvatska narodna banka provodila cijeli niz mjera na poticanju rekunizacije ekonomije. "Najsnanija i najefikasnija je bila to to smo banke traili da dre dodatni kapital za kreditiranje u inozemnoj valuti onih koji nemaju takozvani prirodni hedge, nemaju prihode u toj valuti", rekao je guverner. Istaknuo je da su takve mjere "uspjele donekle smanjivati eurizaciju, pa smo doli sa 78% na nekakvih 63%, no dola je kriza i u roku od 3 mjeseca svi su se vratili u euro, jer su se ljudi uplaili." "im se Hrvati uplae, tre u euro, kao to su nekada u marku, i to je psiholoka kategorija, nema te monetarne politike kojom emo to promijeniti", dodao je guverner te nastavio da "u ovom trenutku duplo vie regulatorno optereujemo euro u bankarskom sektoru nego kunu, i opet ne pomae puno." Na kritike o odnosu HNB-a prema malim bankama, guverner je rekao da su "male banke regulatorno u potpuno istom tretmanu kao i velike banke. Plasmani malih banaka su u potpuno istim regulatornim tretmanima kao i plasmani velikih banaka." Guverner se osvrnuo i na nain podnoenja godinjeg izvjea te opisao nain na koji Europska sredinja banka izvjeuje o svom radu Europski parlament. "Mi dostavljamo financijska izvjea Saboru. Svaki mjesec dostavljamo financijska izvjea Ministarstvu financija i to je ustaljena praksa. Ja dolazim ovdje, odgovarat u na vaa pitanja ako hoete i kvartalno, a ne polugodinje ili godinje, a nadam se i drago mi je da raspravu moemo nastaviti i u Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci i to emo sada s obzirom da postoji interes, i to mi je jako drago, pokrenuti im bude prilika, znai nakon ovog zasjedanja Sabora." Zastupnici su postavili i direktna pitanja o poslovanju Hrvatske narodne banke, rashodima i trokovima za zaposlenike. Guverner je odgovorio da su "rashodi Hrvatske narodne banke 2010. bili 341,5 milijuna kuna, 2014. 309 milijuna kuna, za 2015. jo nemamo revizijsko izvjee, ali planirana su 319 milijuna kuna. Znai, dolo je do pada rashoda Hrvatske narodne banke, a ne do rasta rashoda i oni su se revidirano smanjili za 10% do 2014., odnosno 8% do 2015." Guverner Vuji ponovio je i da Hrvatska narodna banka nije nadlena za nadzor austrijskih tedionica. Odgovarajui na pitanje o Credo banci Boris Vujije rastumaio daje "Credo banka bila u postupku prisilne likvidacije, to znai daje izgubila licencu i zbog toga vie nije smjela obavljati usluge za koje je bila licencirana, to ukljuuje i obavljanje platnog prometa. Zbog toga je bila pod suspenzijom izvrenja plaanja u naim platnim sustavima, to je HSVP i NKS, znai sustav velikih plaanja i mali klirinki sustav, meutim po zakonu likvidacija ne znai prestanak drutva, odnosno ovrhe su se morale provesti." Guverner je istaknuo da je o tome provedena istraga koja je pokazala da je sve bilo u redu. Osvrnuvi se na primjedbe o kreditima s valutnom klauzulom u vicarskim francima naglasio je da je Hrvatska narodna banka brinula za interes hrvatskih graana i "predlagala rjeenje, odnosno rjeenja koja mogu najvie pomoi onima kojima treba pomoi, zaduenima u vicarskom franku, a ne opteretiti pravnim i financijskim rizicima hrvatski proraun, odnosno sve porezne obveznike." Zastupnike je zanimalo koliko su banke u Hrvatskoj zatiene od krize u zemljama majkama, na to je guverner odgovorio: "Dobro su zatiene. Zato? Zato jer su to hrvatske banke. To treba imati na umu. Znai, Zagrebaka banka je hrvatska banka, osnovana je u Hrvatskoj s kapitalom u Hrvatskoj." Guverner je dodao da se banka "moe pretvoriti sada u poslovnicu po europskim zakonima i mi to ne moemo sprijeiti, ali to znai da su tada depoziti osigurani od talijanske drave, a ne od hrvatske drave." Naglasio je da banke u Hrvatskoj imaju vrlo visoku kapitalnu adekvatnost. "Znai kapitalna adekvatnost hrvatskih banaka je puno via nego kapitalna adekvatnost njihovih banaka majki i to im daje sigurnostjer o tome ovisi financijska stabilnost Hrvatske." Guverner je na pitanja o EURIBOR-u saborskim zastupnicima poruio daje Hrvatska narodna banka upozoravala na koritenje EURIBOR-a u kreditnim ugovorima, ali je njegovo koritenje omoguio Sabor koji je donio Zakon o potroakom kreditiranju, a ne HNB. Predlagao je, i dalje predlae i mogua rjeenja tog problema, od kojih su neka prihvaena, pa je ponuda kunskih kredita s fiksnom kamatnom stopom danas rairena na domaem tritu, a nastavit e ih predlagati i novoj Vladi. U zakljuku, guverner Vuji je naglasio da je "HNB kupovao vrijeme vladama da mogu napraviti strukturne reforme kako bi se pokrenulo gospodarstvo. To moe raditi monetarna politika i to ne radi samo monetarna politika Hrvatske narodne banke, to rade monetarne politike i recimo Europske sredinje banke. No ako se te reforme ne naprave, monetarna politika je nemona na poveanju produktivnosti."  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Economic crisis and monetary policy
text: Economic crisis and monetary policy Published: 8.7.2009. Type Speaker Speech Dr Zeljko Rohatinski, serving as CNB Governor from 12 July 2000 to 7 July 2012. Release date of the statement Topic Event Event Event Event Date of events 7.7.2009. Crisis and economic policy frameworks Round table of the Class of Social Sciences of the Croatian Academy of Sciences Zagreb, HAZU 7.7.2009. 1. A year ago, the Croatian economy grew at an annual rate of 4.3% (approximately as in the previous seven years), untilvarious gatherings of professional and political character talked about the need for even faster growth. The need for more investments, new jobs, greater incentives, development of popular shareholding, housing construction as a growth locomotive, strengthening the soci of thejal state and the like was highlighted. Today, the economy is falling at a rate of 6.7% and there is talk about how to mitigate the effects of passing the global crisis on our territories, and then return to the previous upward trajectory as soon as possible on the wave of general economic recovery. Both approaches are wrong. A year ago, the eclatative dangers of the previous type of economic growth were still underestimated, now the desire is to reestablish a pattern that only raised the effects of transmitting the world crisis to the situation and tendencies in the Croatian economy. It's like we didn't get a lesson and it's like we can't learn anything from it. Which is that economic growth cannot be based in the long run on the expansion of domestic demand, which permanently generates fundamental external and internal imbalances andthe team increases general indebtedness. Its growth also increased the risk that potential problems in capital inflows, rising prices or problems in its monocultural export supply will break the whole growth pattern and turn it into its opposite. That's what happened upravo. Hence, the exit from the current situation cannot in principle be based on the further spread of imbalances but on their substantial reduction, even if there are no long-term constraints on their further financing, especially when these limitedselves are very pronounced in the short term. For this, in general, it is necessary to pursue an "anticyclical" economic policy with a "healthy core" and built-in shock absorbers. Since we have not had such an integral policy before, we have come to a situation where we have to reduce deficits in the timeof the recession, which can deepen it even further. 2. The genesis of the problem is also well known from the experience of some other countries where intensive foreign capital inflows and credit expansion have had a strong impact on the markets of goods and services, securities and nekretnine. In the first case, the credit-supported demand for goods and services above the short-term capacity of the domestic supply was met by an increased supply from imports, which resulted in an increase in the current account deficit of the balance of payments but also maintained theelacit price stability in those markets. This was not the case, of course, in the financial market, where supply is much more limited, so the growth in demand - which was further financed and based on individual preferences on converting part of the domestic savings into capital - led to a substantial increase in prices, which ultimately resulted in a pure "bubble effect". This actually entered a "vicious circle", in which credit expansion supported by optimistic expectations led to an increase in asset prices, which ohraroused investors and increased collateral prices, all of which together supported an even stronger credit expansion. At the same time, there has been a rapid growth in loans and investments, and an increase in the prices of securities and real estate, while at the same time giving inflation measuredand the consumer price index has remained at relatively low levels. Since this process was also linked to the real growth of the economy, it increased the willingness to take risks, which gave additional momentum to the credit cycle. Conversely, when the expectations regarding risk and return on investments were changed, and the causes were both internal and external in nature, the whole process went in reverse, prices plummeted with a negative impact on the real sector, which is now burdened by high debt and lowinvestment activity. At the same time, such capital flows have also had a significant impact on changes in monetary systems and monetary policies in general, and in small, highly euroised countries in particular. The basis of these policies could no longer be the complete endogenous creation of money supply by the central bank, which then, through interaction with demand, targets the general level of prices, exchange rates and interest rates. Unlike this "neoclassical" picture, monetary policy in the conditions of liberalised financialflows has primarily become a "filter" that, through relative price-yield ratios, affects the entry and exit of global capital from the country's financial system, and primarily acts as one of the moderators of general economic performers . In doing so, this capital has its own benchmark foreign interest rate, and its conversion to the national currency has an appreciation effect on the exchange rate. Realizing all this, the CNB has for many years highlighted the high risks to which the Croatian economy is exposed inthe global anom financial system. Risks of both direct transmission of possible external shocks and internal shocks caused by processes triggered or supported by foreign capital inflows in conditions of relatively low level of disposable income and high propensity to spend in the country. That is why the primary task of the CNB's policy in recent years has been to dimension the entry of capital into the banking system in such a way that it supports sustainable economic growth, and not that the consequences of its uncontrolled expansion become its limitation. In doing so, it must have been borne in mind that all the big banks in Croatia actually operate as financial conglomerates, so in them engaged foreign capital and alternative forms of domestic savings are integrally directed to the markets, with the wholemaximizing of yields at the level of the conglomerate. Such an approach to monetary policy has put the focus in choosing its instruments on those that increase the external sources of banks' funds, limit their credit multiplication, that is, which, inits short conceit, functionally reduce the high rates of return on the capital of banks as the main motive for aggressive loan offerings. For this purpose, the CNB primarily used and gradually tightened the measures of direct impact (the marginal reserve requirement on foreign borrowing, the registration of treasury records is obligatory to register treasury records for faster growth of bank placements, minimally necessary foreign currency receivables, and the retention of a high reserve requirement rate), and then the high rate of reserve requirement), and then complementary and prudential measures, in order to strengthen and reduce the linearity of direct action. Such a policy, of course, was not well received by banks, and often by certain political structures. And just from them. International financial institutions very precisely detected the risks arising from the expansionary entry of foreign capital, but in the sphere of monetary policy they preferred solutions of prudential and "market" character, highlighting the long-term harmfulness of "administrative" measures. The CNB's ability to resist these pressures resulted in two positive effects at the time ofthe outbreak of the financial crisis. First, although monetary policy in Croatia has never been really restrictive in the sense that insufficient supply of money limits economic growth, its activities have nevertheless significantly slowed the growth of loans and foreign entities, and therefore the credit obligations of the enterprise and population sectors, compared to the one that would be without such a policy. Secondly, the use of "administrative" instruments made it possible to form liquid reserves at the level of the overall banking system, which they laterenjoyed as a necessary shock absorber at the moment of external shock. 3. The perception of the crisis widely expanded in Croatia during October 2008, primarily related to the stock market crash, after which a financial collapse of a wider scale was expected. This did not happen, because the monetary system reacted quickly and efficiently, precisely on the principles of anticyclicity. At that point, it was crucial to prevent the loss of savers' confidence in the banking system and to maintain the credibility of monetary policy. Without it, the "classof the circle" of the financial crisis would be activated, which Paul Krugman portrays as the interdependence of three elements: the loss of confidence - the depreciation of the exchange rate, the rise in interest rates, the sharp decline in demand - financial problems for businesses, banks and the population, which in turn result in a further loss of confidence, easily all these elements were, and partly still present, the intensity of their manifestation to be maintained within frameworks that did not initiate chain reaction. In this context, the CNB, by abolishing the marginal reserve requirement (effect of 450m euros). euro) and reducing the general reserve requirement rate from 17% to 14% (effect of 1115m euros). euro) released 1,555m euros to banks. euro of immobilised liquidity. In addition, by reducing minimum foreign exchange receivables from 28.5% to 20%, it allowed banks to activate their reserves in the amount of 2084m euros. Euros. Other monetary and prudential measures have been taken, such as increasing the permitted openness of banks' foreign exchange position, closing swap deals and foreign exchange market interventions (net 80200 million), which have further increased liquidity mobility within the banking and financial systems. At the same time, banks increased their foreign debt in the fourth quarter of 2008 by 2,131m euros. euro (of which a short-term debt of EUR 1898 million) euro), so that at the end of last year and at the beginning of this year the total net liquidity input by the CNB and foreign banks (45011152131200) amounted to 3896 million euros. euro, which corresponds to the value of about 8% of GDP. A third of these funds are directly or indirectly placed to the state to settle domestic obligations and pay off foreign debt, while the rest is aimed at maintaining liquidity in banks' dealings with other sectors. 4. After this first impact, the situation in the monetary sphere begins to gradually consolidate, but with significantly altered structural and dynamic characteristics. 4.1 As the greatest potential danger of direct transfer of the global financial crisis to Croatia, the risk of partial withdrawal of foreign capital from the country was assessed. - by reducing bank deposits and investments in funds, withdrawing profits or not re-financing the foreign liabilities of the company and the state due. So far to has not happened, so gross foreign debt at the end of April this year amounts to 39.8 billion euros, and is 1% higher than at the end of 2008. In doing so, corporate debt and direct investment increased by about 750m euros, while the central government reduced its debt by 610m euros. euro, with further refinancing of its borrowing obligations on the foreign market. In the current situation when one does not count on an arrangement with the IMF or some other form of foreign financial support, this undoubtedly represents a positive phenomenon, but alsoan indication of a radical halt to the current tendencies in the inflow of foreign capital through credit channels. In 2008 alone, this influx amounted to EUR 6.4 billion. (up by 19.6%) representing the main source of financing for the growth of domestic consumption and investments. 4.2. Following a sharp fall in the savings of the population in banks during October 2008 by around EUR 3.5 billion. by the end of the first quarter of 2009, it had returned to the previous level in real terms and was 8.3% higher in May than a year ago. This alsodetermines the g increase in total savings of 6.1%. However: (a) Domestic savings growth in banks is now half as slow as the average in previous years (13.5%) and is influenced by the substitution of alternative forms of savings, so the aggregate value of domestic financial andseam is significantly reduced. (b) The increased perception of currency risk resulted in an increase in the share of foreign currency savings in the structure of total savings from 66.9% in May 2008 to 72.9% in the same month of this year. This also increases the general degree of euroisation of the Croatianeconomist ije, in which the share of foreign currency funds in the structure of total liquid assets has increased from 50.0% to 56.4%. (c) Unlike household savings, the savings of the enterprise sector have decreased by 5.0% in the last year, which has also reduced its share of the total savings structure from 18.7% to 16.7%. This indicates a significant deterioration in the financial potential of the sector, which is only a reflection of the reduced liquidity in the current business sphere, where the amount of deposit money has decreased by 16.9%, also causing a decrease in cash 11.0%. 4.3. All this speaks of the pronounced limitations in the growth of credit potential from domestic sources, and related to the stagnation of foreign debt and the stock market situation and the limitations in the formation of the overall financial potential of the country. The reserves ofimmobilized liquidity, which still exist in this regard with the CNB, have already been significantly reduced in the last year (from HRK 53 billion to HRK 42 billion), with the mandatory reserve of banks in foreign exchange at the end of May being only 633m euros. euro (according to 802.4bnspent at the same time last year). Therefore, any further reduction of the reserve requirement rate could hypothetically be only in the function of domestic payments, while the conversion of kunas thus exempted into foreign currency would assume a significant decrease in the central bank's net foreign exchangereserves, with a negative impact on the perception of domestic depositors and foreign creditors. Therefore, such a move would have justification only in the case of a "credit crunch" in foreign markets and a direct threat to the country's external liquidity. 4.4. With a strong injection of liquidity by foreign banks and the CNB, total bank placements maintained an annual growth dynamic of 13.2%, at which they grew on average during the previous five years. But: (a) Within total loans, net loans to the state have increased by as much as 109.6% in the past year, increasing their share of the structure of total bank loans from 6.3% in May last year to 11.7% in May this year. At the same time, loans to other sectors are growing at an annual rate of 6.7% and slowing significantlycompared to previous years (15% in 2007; 10.5% in 2008). This also increases the gap between the effective and the CNB's non-penalty and the early growth of loans to these sectors. Namely, in relation to the base situation at the end of 2007, these loans are now up by 10.1%, while the "limit" is 17% or about HRK 14.5bn more. In part, this is the result of a slowdown in demand for loans (due to an increase in interest rates and uncertainty), but also points to the pronounced emergence of other sectors being pushed out of the credit market bythe country. (b) The increase in foreign sources of funds and shares of foreign currency savings has shortened the foreign exchange position of banks, whose net foreign liabilities have increased from 803.9 billion to 805.4 billion (at the same time, the net foreign assets of monetary institutions have decreased from 806.1 billion to EUR 3.4 billion). This also increased currency risk for them, so some banks stopped granting pure kuna loans, shifting this risk to the beneficiaries of new loans. Coupled with the increased degree of euroisation, this further underlines the importance of maintaining a stable exchange rate. 4.5. Influenced by increased demand for foreign exchange, the exchange rate of the kuna depreciated by 2% in the first quarter of this year, but then the weakening of depreciation expectations and the realization of foreign borrowing of the state returned it to the framework of relatively high stability. Inearly 2009, the CNB intervened directly on the foreign exchange market in the gross amount of about 500m euros. euro, but also by relaxing prudential measures, it has expanded the room for manoeuvre for banks to increase the supply of camelsfor them and thus engage themselves in the defence of exchange rate stability. The "incentive" for this behaviour of banks was a change in the currency structure of reserve requirement allocation and a policy of limited injections of kuna liquidity through open market operations, which occasionally resulted in very high interest rates on overnight loans on the money market. With the stabilization of the exchange rate, pressures on these rates have also been reduced, and they are consistently lower than the CNB's lombard rate and average 6.5%. 4.6. The relaxationof mon ether policy measures also reduced unit "regulation costs" for banks by around 20%. Thus, for example, to cover these costs at a passive interest rate on a foreign currency deposit of 5% and with an exchange rate risk of 2% banks should have previously achieved an average interest rateon placements of 10.2%, while now this rate has been lowered to 8.1%. The fact that, nevertheless, the active interest rates of banks have increased has a cause in the increased price of foreign borrowing (country risk), an increase in interest rates on domestic deposits due to the strengthening of the concreasionbetween banks in conditions of slow growth of deposits, and in the deterioration of the quality of placements, i.e. reduced collection of loans, especially those granted to the population. All this in the conditions of a significant slowdown in banks' credit activity towards the private sector, which in the totality of the quantity-price ratio resulted in a decrease in the rate of return on bank capital from 10.93% in 2007 to 9.91% in 2008 and 9.32% in the first quarter of 2009. 5. Thus, as a whole, the monetary sector has endured the first brunt ofthe FI Nancian crisis and is gradually consolidating. However, it no longer has the capacity to support the current dynamics of aggregate demand growth, nor are the banks themselves willing to pursue an expansionary loan supply policy indiscriminately. In contrast, the real sector is still falling, but this is not solely due to the current financial crisis, but is the result of the gradual cumulation of several factors and begins back in early 2008. Thus, since March of last year, industrial production has been decreasing at an average trend rate of 0.7% per month, while GDP practically stagnated throughout last year at the seasonally adjusted level of the last quarter of 2007. Causes: (1) The acceleration of the average annual inflation rate from 2.9% to 6.1%, which in 2008 offset the bulk of nominal growth in current incomes, easily in the second part of 2008 there was an aggregate decrease in consumer prices by about 1% compared to their level from the month of July, the ongoing increase in these prices in the first five months of this year 2.8% (in the European Union only 0.6%) is an indicator of the possible continuation of the negative impact of inflation on disposable incomes and real demand in the domestic market. This is partly the result of an increase in input costs, but also a perception of the overall actionof the economic policy, which opens the way for increasing the prices of individual products and services or for "eliminating price disparity", even if these products are subject to international exchange, and especially if they are not. All this indicates how fragile relative price stability really is and how little it takes to undermine it, even in recession conditions. (2) The decline in the value of the financial assets of the population invested in securities and non-bank institutions due to the blowing of the bubble in the stock and real estate markets. In 2008, it amounted to around HRK 43bn (down by HRK 37.1%) of which around HRK 16bn in the fourth quarter, which almost completely offset the growth in the value of these assets during the previous year. Together with the real stagnation of labour income, such a loss of capital income and liquidity, led to a decline in personal consumption and a significant slowdown in investments. (3) Strengthening illiquidity due to the inelasticity of part of current expenditure in conditions of reduced revenues and high credit obligations. And while in this the sectors of the population and enterprises had some room for manoeuvre through the reduction of their savings, the sector of the state behaved very rigidly. Thus, the deficit of the consolidated general government (including HAC and HBOR) increased from EUR 5.6 billion to EUR 5.6 billion. kuna in 2007 to EUR 9.1 billion. kuna in 2008, or from 1.8% to 2.7% of GDP, with this entire deficit concentrated in the last quarter, known at thetime of the biggest earthquakes in financial markets. Similar developments continued in the first five months of 2009, when the central government net borrowed a further EUR 13.3 billion. of which hrk 10.5 billion is on the domestic market. (as opposed to stagnationand debt of other sectors to domestic banks during this period). Of course, the initial liquidity on domestic markets was not sufficient during this period to finance so many needs of the state, and only informally "conditional" on the relaxation of monetary policy was it possible to prevent the occurrence of insolvency of the state in settling its obligations - especially towards abroad. This, however, significantly reduced the possibility of directing these previously immobilised funds directly towards the sector of the enterprise and maintaining their vision. (4) "Animal spirits", with the so-called multiplier of (in)trust, that is, general euphoria in the ascending and general panic in the downward phase of the cycle, due to which economic entities do not behave rationally. An indicator of the current situation in this sphere is also the consumer confidence index , which decreased by over 25 points during 2008 and in the first quarter of 2009 and is at its lowest level since mid-1999. (5) These dominant domestic factors were followed only at the end of 2008 by a key external impact - the decline inexport-to-demand, the negative action of which is fueled by the very limited possibility of substitution of export demand by domestic and insufficient ability to substitut import demand by domestic supply. He significantly exacerbated the problem of the key structural mismatch of the Croatian ec onomia, which is the deficit in the exchange of goods of 23% of GDP. Care, at such a level, will not be able to cover the very sensitive services and transfer sector for a long time. 6. Thus, unlike the monetary sector, which is consolidating, the real sector is yet to face the most difficult probsolders. Their main causes are a decline in aggregate demand and increased illiquidity, none of which are primarily initiated by monetary factors, nor is it due only to external causes. However, in addressing these problems, the real sector is now facinga conflict with pronounced monetary and financial constraints, which it has caused to a significant extent itself. The key is the foreign exchange constraint resulting from the disproportion between the available supply and the current operation of the generated demand for foreign exchange, whichcannot be rationally covered by any monetary "stunts", but requires an appropriate adjustment to the real sector itself. Conscious or spontaneous. The magnitude of this adjustment is indicatively determined by three externally defined assumptions, which are consistent with efective developments in the previous part of 2009. These are: (a) Contraction of export demand by about 10%; (b) A decrease in foreign investment by about 50%; (c) Stagnation of foreign debt. In addition to the estimated external constraints, the need to reduce the current account deficit of the balance of payments is imposed from 804.5bn in 2008 to "only" around 803bn this year (from 9.4% to an estimated 6% of GDP). This presupposes a decrease in imports of goods and services by about 15%, to which the overall policy of regulating domestic demand should be subordinated and where fiscal policy has a special responsibility. In these frameworks, monetary policy will support the liquidity of the system only to a level that will not destabilise the exchange rate and through it adversely affect the overall fineancia system, as has recently happened in some central and eastern European countries. Based on this, it is estimated that the net domestic assets of the banking system will increase by about 9%, but within it - if the sectoral structure of placements does not change - krediti will increase by only 4% to businesses and the population. At the same time, total liquid assets will increase by about 2%, while the cash mass will be reduced by more than 10%. If the accuracy of the initial assumptions is confirmed in practice, in 2009 one can expect a real decrease in domestic aggregate consumption by about 6%, and a decrease in GDP by about 5%. Whether this decline can be smaller will depend primarily on the development of opportunities in the world, where more favourable developments than now envisaged can to some extent alleviate external restrictions on theCroatian economy in both the financial and real sectors. However, the same core issue remains. How do you view this crisis? If we see it only as a "temporary stalemate" in the long-term positive tendencies of economic growth and development,we will solve nothing. In contrast, it should first and foremost be taken as a drastic reminder of the consequences that may and may have occurred due to the previous disregard for the sustainability problem of economic growth. A warning that would have been even more difficult if the HNB hadhad a different monetary policy in recent years. If we understand that warning, then this crisis is also a chance for a different beginning of thinking about future economic development. 7. The problems that economic policy has faced before and faces are now onlyseemingly fundamentally different. In the face of abundant supply and low foreign capital prices, the key problem was how to limit the expansionary inflow of this capital, which through the growing current account deficit of the balance of payments and increased foreign indebtedness generated neravnotes in the national economy and its vulnerability to external shocks. Now that these shocks have been effected by the global financial crisis, the problem is how to quickly and painlessly reduce these imbalances, the financing of which is shifting in large part to scarce domestic sources. So, technically, the problems seem to have evolved from "growing too fast" to "hard landing." Intrinsically, however, the problem was and remains only one. How to balance consumption with disposable income realized by domestic productionand exports, i.e. how to establish long-term sustainable economic growth. This is a problem that requires concerted action by all segments of economic policy, including in particular on the route between fiscal and monetary policy. Here, however, reportto well-known difficulties. The state budget and planning documents of some extra-budgetary central government institutions are adopted or endorsed by parliament, which also adopts laws establishing certain rights of budgetary beneficiaries and sources of funds for their financing. Thus, fiscal policy broadly sublimates the partial interests of certain social groups, which are then transferred as politically verified "needs" to the financial and monetary spheres, where sufficient liquidity is expected for theirrealization. This is where the problem arises, if the liquidity of the financial system is below the level of the established "rights". The solution is either in foreign borrowing or, when the possibilities of this borrowing are significantly limited as is now the case, in the pressures on the emission functionof the adult bank. She cannot, of course, close her eyes to the problem and therefore seeks to partially help the state finance its needs and at the level of annual aggregates and, in particular, in the sphere of intra-year overcoming disparities between the dynamics of collectingfiscal revenues and the dynamics of realization of expenditures. However, as an independent institution with clearly defined objectives of its activities, the central bank dimensiones its emission activity according to the state and needs of the overall economy, which is why anyrallying increase in the financial needs of the state usually means relatively fewer financing opportunities for other sectors. And while in conditions of general expansion this is not a particularly big problem, in conditions of contraction the problem can escalate to the emergence of the "extrusion effect" of the enterprise and household sectors from the loan market. That is why, in times of crisis, the special responsibility of fiscal policy and the policy of total public sector spending for the general economic situation in the country is always emphasized. If they do not perceive this in a sufficientera of the relevant political structure, the only solution would be, of course, to seek help from the IMF and other international financial institutions. This, however, is not a good solution for at least two reasons. First, they would have previously lost a relatively significant portion of camelreserves, which would have a limiting effect on flexibility in doing business with foreign countries over the longer term. Secondly, more importantly, the requirements that the IMF would place on Croatia in that case would not be fundamentally any different from what even withami we know that in such situations it is necessary to take to preserve the external liquidity of the country. The need to "prescribe" this to us by the IMF when there is no other way out anymore, instead of doing it ourselves in advance and thus preventing an escalation of the problem, could not be understoodas an example of responsible action by economic policy makers.
