Title: Presentation at the ceremony marking the 20th anniversary of the introduction of the kuna as the monetary unit of the Republic of Croatia
text: Presentation of the CNB Governor Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic at the ceremony marking the 20th anniversary of the introduction of the kuna as a monetary unit of the Republic of Croatia Published: 29.5.2014. Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor 29.5.2014. Ceremony marking the 20th anniversary of the introduction of the kuna as a monetary unit of the Republic Croatia Zagreb Venue , CNB Date of events 29.5.2014. Dear guests, President of the Republic of Croatia, your Excellency, distinguished representatives of the Parliament and the Government of the Republic of Croatia, ladies and gentlemen, I wish you a good day, I greet you well and thank you for your response to today's ceremony marking the 20th anniversary ofthe introduction of the kuna. The national currency, especially when introduced during the war, shortly after state independence, is a particular expression of national sovereignty. Kuna is not the first Croatian currency after state independence. The first, the temporary one, was the Croatian dinar, which replaced the Yugoslav dinar, but it was not issued by the central bank, but by the Ministry of Finance. The introduction of the kuna as a monetary unit of the Republic of Croatia and the replacement of the Croatian dinar during the war was a great logistical undertaking whose implementation wasrebalancing to ensure the smooth running of payment transactions in the country, and additionally, to anticipate and exclude all kinds of risks that may arise in cash operations of the highest volume. Taking into account the time and circumstances in which the introduction of the kuna was carried out,and the fact that the exchange of money is an extremely important event for each country and its monetary system, it can be argued that this was one of the most complex projects of the Croatian National Bank, in the realization of which a large number of employees of the CNB participated, as well as numerous institutions and individuals outside the central bank. The project to replace the temporary monetary unit of the Croatian dinar with a new monetary unit with a kuna involved a number of activities that could be classified into two categories. The first categoryof activity related to the preparation of the concept of the introduction of the kuna was carried out by the Commission for the preparation of the proposal for monetary independence of the Republic of Croatia, appointed by the decision of the President of the Republic of Croatia Dr. Franjo Tudjman in August 1991. The President of the Commission would beDr. Marijan Han9eekovic, and the work of the Commission was attended by representatives of the Croatian National Bank, led by the then Governor Dr. Ante Cicin-8aain, as well as distinguished experts from various fields and representatives of the Government and parliament. The Croatian National Bank provided technical support in the preparation of the draft solution. The then Director of the Treasury Directorate Nikola Ragu9e participated in the work of the Commission to which he regularly presented certain draft solutions, from which we highlight in particular the technical characteristics of the new monetary unit. They should have ensured ease of use for citizens (recognition of denominations, visible nominal markings, choice of protective features for the purpose of quick and easy authentication and si.), application of state-of-the-art developments that will also meet the requirement ofthe urgent needs in working with banknotes at all points (special characteristics in which the quality of the paper, type of printing, color selection, identification marks, substantially different face and reverse, special protective features, etc.) and to prevent or aggravate possiblecounterfeiting. The second category of activities related to the physical preparation of the introduction of the kuna and the replacement of the Croatian dinar, for which the Treasury Directorate was in charge. These activities included the delivery and acceptance of newly made quantities of banknotes and forged novca, distribution to branches of the then Payment Institute, and, at a later stage, the collection and destruction of replaced Croatian dinar banknotes. The introduction of the mink has been prepared for more than two years. Intensive preparations for the entire project began at the end of March 1992, when the Commission established the indicative conditions for the production of banknotes and coins, thus creating the preconditions for conducting tenders for drafting solutions for the appearance of banknotes and coins. Call tender for banknotes otvorenje in April 1992, and by the end of October the execution of the procedure for selecting an art solution. In the next six months, all the essential characteristics of the banknotes were defined so that in March 1993 an international tender for printing kuna banknotes was carried out, and at the end ofthe same month the contract for printing and delivery of kuna banknotes was concluded with the Giesecke & Devrient printing company from Munich. In March 1993, the opening and invitation competition for the development of an art solution for coins, and at the same time preparations for the organization of the mintin Zagreb were started. The Mint started its experimental production in October 1993, and on January 14, 1994, it officially began the discovery of kuna and linden coins. The production of kuna banknotes was carried out in a very short period of less than nine months. Taking into account the high quality of the banknotes, and the period within which the banknotes were made (the usual deadlines of 18 to 26 months), it can be argued that the very demanding work of preparing the introduction of the kuna was successfully brought to an end. As far as the handling of money is concerned, taking into account all the actions carried out during the collection, unloading, loading and storage of banknotes and coins, employees of the Treasury Directorate handled banknotes and coins with a total value of HRK 9 2.7 billion over a preparatory period of five months, totalling HRK 621.6 million. and a total weight of 1,191 tonnes. Of course, during the same period of preparation for the introduction of the kuna, the obligation to settle circulation in the banknotes of the Croatian dinar should have been duly done. After the introduction ofthe kuna, in the period June - December 1994 came the second part of the extensive work related to the acquisition and destruction of croatian dinar banknotes, where we took over and cancelled a total of 277.9 million euros at five locations in the country. pieces of banknotes weighing a total of 192 tonnes. Whoever works with cash, especially if it comes to operations of such a large volume, will always underline and emphasize, as we do this time, that all these operations were done flawlessly and that from a security point of view there were no propusts, nor did there be any abuses. All this at the time when the war was going on, the land was not whole, and the parts were traffic (semi)isolated. Many CNB employees were involved in the entire operation, led by then Governor Dr. PeroJurkovic, and Vice Governor Dragutin Zaninovic was directly in charge of the entire operation at the implementation stage. It also involved many outside the CNB. Perhaps on this occasion we should mention, risking that we are doing injustice to others, only academicianDalibor Brozovic, an excellent expert and connoisseur of monetary money, as well as cooperation with designers and authors of the art solution for banknotes by academician Miroslav 8autej and Dr. Vi Iko 8eiljak, author of the art solution for coins to the academic sculptor Ktake Kovacic, and the first director of the mint Dr. d0uro Crnjak. How did we come up with the appearance of the mink? Art solutions for banknotes and coins were selected on the basis of an invitation competition involving leading Croatian designers, painters and sculptors. Thecompetition was carried out by the Commission for the preparation of the proposal for monetary independence of the Republic of Croatia during 1992 and 1993. As the basis of the competition for banknotes, the Commission chose motifs that depicted portraits of greats from Croatian history on the face of banknotes, and a panorama or characteristic detail of a Croatian city on the reverse, with efforts to connect the characters on the face with the cities on the reverse. Eight selected cities form two squares, In one square four cities mark the end of theRepublic of Croatia: northwest (Vara9edin), southwest (Pula), northeast (Vukovar) and southeast (Dubrovnik), while with it intersects the second square, which is formed by four of our largest cities: Rijeka, Osijek, Split and Zagreb. It should be said that already at the time ofthe collection of motives, there was an objection that there were no portraits of any woman on the banknotes. This was also discussed by the Commission, but a choice that is known prevailed. However, later, aware of the justification of the complaint, the Croatian National Bank initiated the creation of a series witha rib coin called "Famous Croats", thus wanting to highlight the significant contribution of women in Croatian history. So far, three copies of silver coins dedicated to Ivana Brlic-Ma9euranic, Katarina Zrinskand Slavia Ra9akaj have been issued as part of this series. Although at first glance the same, the kuna banknotes changed over time. The new releases of banknotes you have in your wallet today are the result of a technical improvement in the protection of banknotes against counterfeiting, especially in the field of scanning and computer printing. Since the introduction of the kuna, regular circulation coins have been included in circulation every year with the current year of issue. We also had an additional twelve editions of commemorative coin circulation, of which we especially single out the 25 kuna coin as a technological innovation (a two-part coin of twelfth form). Taje coins issued in eleven different editions, with high demand. From May 1994 to May 2014, a total of 37 different gold and silver coin editions were issued from the program of commemorative coins and numismatic sets, as well as 25 different numismatic coin sets. Regular circulation coins and commemorative coin editions as well as banknotes, receive many praises, especially in specialist circles, as an example of successful design and superior workmanship, which contributes to the successful presentation of both the central bank and the country as a whole. A few words about the future of the mink. Kuna, as we said, was introduced as a national currency during the war, but only pwhat the conditions for this were met. And these conditions implied macroeconomic stability. To introduce a currency that would be accompanied from the beginning by the fate of the Yugoslav and then the Croatian dinar, the fate of a weak currency that is less and less valuable and therefore cannot sendany of the basic functions of money, would not be good. Kuna was introduced after the implementation of the stabilization programme from 1993, that is, only after inflation was eliminated and the exchange rate stabilized. From the beginning, this allowed kuna to be stable valuta and to assume a significant part of the functions of money that its predecessors did not have. The exchange rate of the kuna was never fixed, but, unlike the Yugoslav and Croatian dinars, it ranged in a limited range of 15.8 percent change in value against the euro, as soon asexchange rate adjustment is allowed - fifteen percent of the fluctuation range is significantly higher than zero - and left behind a two-pronged risk of exchange rate movements, which is important in trade on the foreign exchange market and the notion of exchange rate risk by participants in that market, but at the same time, stability, that is, the value of the domestic currency, is preserved. Thanks to the stability of inflation and exchange rates, kuna has been able to achieve the basic functions of money, value measures, means of exchange and value storage to a greater extent than its predecessors, the Yugoslav and Croatian dinars. Before the introduction of the kuna, the Yugoslav and Croatian dinars did not predominantly serve either as a means of storing value, nor as a measure of value, and to a large extent as a means of exchange. Instead of domesticego money, this role was played by the German brand. Why? In short, due to poor overall economic and monetary policy, which, through monetary financing of the deficit and the depreciation of the value of the domestic currency, under the banner of helping the state to finance itself more easily and takingaway them to be more competitive, devalued the value of the national currency and thereby destroyed trust in it. To the extent that even today, when it comes to the function of storing the value of money, it is not possible to fully establish it. Especially because citizens will beirresponsibly afraid of calls for devaluation. Not understanding that by doing so, she seems less possible. Kuna today, thanks to 20 years of stability, has almost completely the function of the means of exchange, to the greatest extent a measure of value, but still has a limited function of storing value. In fact, the bulk of the savings are still in euros. Mistakes serve to learn something from them. Monetary policy in the decades before the introduction of the kuna, which was based on monetizing the fiscal deficit and so-called 'kompetus devaluations', neither led to a stable fiscal situation nor a competitive economy. All she managed to do was destroy trust in domestic money. In contrast, those European countries that have stuck to the policy of a tight budget, which limits sit down and stable currencies on the other hand, have achieved much better economic performance than countries that have relied on monetary financing of deficits and devaluations. This, therefore, teaches us both our and European history. Such a policy, however, requires both appropriate institutions and sound structural policies and fiscal discipline. For this, many countries, including ours, were not ready and therefore have economic problems. How did the martens form? Kunas were primarily created in Croatia onthe act of the so-called quasi currency board, interventions on the foreign exchange market, i.e. foreign currency purchases, and for sterilization of excess liquidity, the reserve requirement rate was primarily used. As a result, sterilization was also cheaper, and the central bank madeand the profits, that is, transfers of central bank profits to the budget were higher. Other instruments of liquidity creation and sterilization were also used, but to a much lesser extent. Behind every kuna of money supply in Croatia there is foreign currency in the international reservesof the Croatian National Bank, safely and liquidly invested in the highest quality assets. This represents a stable cornerstone of exchange rate policy - high coverage of the supply of money and primary money to foreign exchange reserves. It's a stone that wouldn't be wise to undermine, andnot everything that's on it would collapse. Let's imagine, for a moment, that the heavy picture of the Croatian economy is held on the wall by four screws. Fiscal, monetary, structural and institutional. Suppose it holds only one well, and three are more or less loosea. Where should it be fixed so that the image does not collapse? Any good master should know that if we start to see the only screw that still holds tightly, instead of the other three, it could easily happen either to spread that one out or to crack, with clear consequences. Many, nevertheless, would prefer to screw up on this screwed-up, and somehow they don't really feel like it for the other three. And it is precisely on what we do with the other three screws that depends on whether we celebrate the 30th anniversary of the mink in ten years or not. If we envy them, I'd say wewon't, and if we don't, we'll envy them. Unlike some other things in life, in this case a larger anniversary could signify failure, not success. Of course, the assumption is that in ten years the eurozone will still be there, more complete and therefore stronger. Whether we can build efficient institutions, pursue a cyclically balanced budget policy and create a favourable investment climate, with as few bureaucratic obstacles as possible, legal uncertainties, unnecessary regulations, with as few (quasi)monopolies as possible in the field of the market ofgoods and services, with a well-educated workforce, not to list all the structural reforms that are needed, depends mostly on the willingness of society to reform, political economy. And she's not easy in a low-employment society, which is fast-moving. But this is something that I would not talk about today, at this priestly moment, when we celebrate one truly successful project - 20 years of the national currency of the mink. I would conclude that we can really be proud of what we have achieved with the national currency, but also dand we have to be ambitious on the other side, and on the other hand, to preserve it. Thank you!
text_original: HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA Izlaganje guvernera HNB-a prof. dr. Borisa Vujia na sveanosti obiljeavanja 20. obljetnice uvoenja kune kao novane jedinice Republike Hrvatske Objavljeno: 29.5.2014. Vrsta Govornik Datum objave izjave Dogaanje Govor Prof. dr. Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a 29.5.2014. Sveanost obiljeavanja 20. obljetnice uvoenja kune kao novane jedinice Republike Hrvatske Mjesto dogaanja Zagreb, HNB Datum dogaanja 29.5.2014. Potovani uzvanici, Predsjednie Republike Hrvatske, vae ekselencije, uvaeni predstavnici Sabora i Vlade Republike Hrvatske, dame i gospodo, elim vam dobar dan, lijepo vas pozdravljam i zahvaljujem na vaem odzivu na dananju sveanost kojom obiljeavamo 20. godinjicu uvoenja kune. Nacionalna valuta, osobito kad se uvodi tijekom rata, nedugo nakon dravnog osamostaljenja, osobit je izraz nacionalne suverenosti. Kuna nije prva hrvatska valuta nakon dravnog osamostaljenja. Prva, privremena, bio je hrvatski dinar, koji je zamijenio jugoslavenski dinar, no njega nije izdavala sredinja banka, ve Ministarstvo financija. Uvoenje kune kao novane jedinice Republike Hrvatske te zamjena hrvatskog dinara tijekom rata bio je veliki logistiki pothvat ije provoenje je trebalo osigurati nesmetano odvijanje platnog prometa u zemlji, i dodatno, predvidjeti i iskljuiti sve vrste rizike koji se mogu pojaviti u gotovinskim operacijama najveeg obujma. Uzimajui u obzir vrijeme i okolnosti u kojima je izvreno uvoenje kune, kao i injenicu da je zamjena novca izuzetno vaan dogaaj za svaku dravu i njezin monetarni sustav, moe se ustvrditi da je to bio jedan od najsloenijih projekata Hrvatske narodne banke, u ijoj realizaciji je sudjelovao velik broj zaposlenika HNB-a, te isto tako brojne institucije i pojedinci izvan sredinje banke. Projekt zamjene privremene novane jedinice hrvatskog dinara novom novanom jedinicom kunom ukljuivao je niz aktivnosti koje bi se mogle svrstati u dvije kategorije. Prvu kategoriju aktivnosti koja se odnosila na pripremu koncepta uvoenja kune provodila je Komisija za pripremu prijedloga monetarnog osamostaljivanja Republike Hrvatske, imenovana odlukom predsjednika Republike Hrvatske dr. Franje Tumana u kolovozu 1991. Predsjednik komisije bio je dr. Marijan Hanekovi, a u radu Komisije sudjelovali su predstavnici Hrvatske narodne banke predvoeni tadanjim guvernerom dr. Antom iin-ainom, te uvaeni strunjaci iz raznih podruja i predstavnici Vlade i Sabora. Hrvatska narodna banka pruala je tehniku podrku u pripremi nacrta rjeenja. Tadanji direktor Direkcije trezora Nikola Ragu sudjelovao je u radu Komisije kojoj je redovito prezentirao pojedine nacrte rjeenja iz kojih posebno izdvajamo tehnika obiljeja nove novane jedinice. Ona su trebala osigurati lakou upotrebe za graane (raspoznavanje apoena, vidljive oznake nominala, izbor zatitnih obiljeja u svrhu brze i jednostavne provjere autentinosti i si.), primjenu najsuvremenijih dostignua u izradi koja e ujedno udovoljiti zahtjevnim potrebama u radu s novanicama na svim punktovima (posebna svojstva u koja ulaze kakvoa papira, vrsta tiska, odabir boja, identifikacijske oznake, bitno razliito lice i nalije, specijalna zatitna obiljeja itd.) i o sprjeavati ili oteati mogue krivotvorenje. Druga kategorija aktivnosti odnosila se na fiziku pripremu uvoenja kune i zamjenu hrvatskog dinara, za to je bila zaduena Direkcije trezora. Ove aktivnosti ukljuivale su dopremu i prihvat novoizraenih koliina novanica i kovanog novca, distribuciju u podrunice tadanjeg Zavoda za platni promet, te, u kasnijoj fazi, preuzimanje i unitavanje zamijenjenih novanica hrvatskog dinara. Uvoenje kune pripremano je vie od dvije godine. Intenzivne pripreme za cjelokupni projekt zapoele su koncem oujka 1992. godine, kad je Komisija utvrdila okvirne uvjete za izradu novanica i kovanog novca, ime su se stvorili preduvjeti za provoenje natjeaja za izradu nacrta rjeenja za izgled novanica i kovanog novca. Pozivni natjeaj za novanice otvorenje u travnju 1992., a do konca listopada izvrenje postupak odabira likovnog rjeenja. U sljedeih est mjeseci definirana su sva bitna obiljeja novanica tako da je u oujku 1993. proveden meunarodni natjeaj za tiskanje novanica kuna, te je koncem istog mjeseca zakljuen s tiskarom Giesecke & Devrient iz Munchena ugovor o tiskanju i isporuci novanica kuna. U oujku 1993. otvorenje i pozivni natjeaj za izradu likovnog rjeenja za kovani novac, a istovremeno su zapoete i pripreme za ustroj kovnice novca u Zagrebu. Kovnica novca krenula je s pokusnom proizvodnjom u listopadu 1993. godine, a 14. sijenja 1994. slubeno je zapoela s otkovom kovanog novca kuna i lipa. Izrada novanica kuna obavljena je u izrazito kratkom roku od nepunih devet mjeseci. Uzimajui u obzir visoku kvalitetu novanica, te rok u kojem su novanice izraene (uobiajeni rokovi od 18 do 26 mjeseci), moe se ustvrditi da je vrlo zahtjevan posao pripreme uvoenja kune bio uspjeno priveden kraju. to se pak rukovanja novcem tie, uzimajui u obzir sve radnje koje su provedene prilikom preuzimanja, istovara, utovara i pohrane novanica i kovanog novca zaposlenici Direkcije trezora u pripremnom razdoblju od pet mjeseci rukovali su novanicama i kovanim novcem ukupne vrijednosti od 92,7 mlrd kuna, u ukupnoj koliini od 621,6 mil. komada i ukupnoj teini od 1.191 tone. Naravno, u istom tom razdoblju pripreme za uvoenje kune, trebalo je uredno odraivati i obvezu podmirivanja optjecaja u novanicama hrvatskog dinara. Nakon uvoenja kune, u razdoblju lipanj - prosinac 1994. uslijedio je drugi dio opsenog posla koji se odnosio na preuzimanje i unitavanje novanica hrvatskog dinara, gdje smo preuzeli i na pet lokacija u zemlji ponitili ukupno 277,9 mil. komada novanica ukupne teine 192 tone. Onaj tko radi s gotovim novcem, osobito ako su u pitanju operacije ovako velikog obujma, uvijek e podvui i naglasiti, kao to i mi to inimo ovog puta, da su sve te operacije odraene besprijekorno i da sa sigurnosnog aspekta nije bilo nikakvih propusta, niti je dolo do bilo kakvih zloupotreba. Sve to u vrijeme kad je trajao rat, zemlja nije bila cijela, a dijelovi su bili prometno (polu)izolirani. U cijelu operaciju bili su ukljueni mnogi djelatnici HNB-a, na elu s tadanjim guvernerom dr. Perom Jurkoviem, a viceguverner Dragutin Zaninovi bio je izravno nadlean za cjelokupnu operaciju u fazi provoenja. Isto tako u nju su bili ukljueni i mnogi izvan HNB-a. Moda ovom prilikom da spomenemo, riskirajui da inimo nepravdu drugima, samo akademika Dalibora Brozovia, vrsnog strunjaka i poznavatelja novarstva, kao i suradnju s dizajnerima i autorima likovnog rjeenja za novanice akademikom Miroslavom utejem i dr. Vi Ikom iljakom, autorom likovnog rjeenja za kovani novac akademskim kiparom Kuzmom Kovaiem, te prvim direktorom kovnice dr. urom Crnjakom. Kako smo doli do izgleda kune? Likovna rjeenja za novanice i kovani novac odabrana su na temelju pozivnog natjeaja u kojem su sudjelovali vodei hrvatski dizajneri, slikari i kipari. Natjeaj je provela Komisija za pripremu prijedloga monetarnog osamostaljivanja Republike Hrvatske tijekom 1992. i 1993. godine. Komisija je kao podlogu natjeaja za novanice odabrala motive koji su prikazivali portrete velikana iz hrvatske povijesti na licu novanica, a panoramu ili karakteristian detalj nekog hrvatskog grada na naliju, s tim da se nastojalo povezati likove na licu s gradovima na naliju. Osam izabranih gradova tvore dva etverokuta, U jednom etverokutu etiri grada obiljeavaju krajnje toke Republike Hrvatske: sjeverozapad (Varadin), jugozapad (Pula), sjeveroistok (Vukovar) i jugoistok (Dubrovnik), dok se s njim kria drugi etverokut to ga tvore etiri naa najvea grada: Rijeka, Osijek, Split i Zagreb. Treba rei da se ve u vrijeme odabira motiva pojavio prigovor da na novanicama nema portreta niti jedne ene. I o tome je Komisija raspravljala, no, prevladao je odabir koji je poznat. Meutim, kasnije, svjesna opravdanosti prigovora, Hrvatska narodna banka je pokrenula izradu serije srebrnog kovanog novca pod nazivom "Znamenite Hrvatice", elei na taj nain istaknuti znaajan doprinos ena u hrvatskoj povijesti. Do sada su u sklopu te serije izdana tri primjerka srebrenog kovanog novca posveena Ivani Brli- Maurani, Katarini Zrinski i Slavi Rakaj. lako na prvi pogled iste, novanice kune su se s vremenom mijenjale. Nova izdanja novanica koja danas imate u novaniku rezultat su tehnikog unapreenja zatite novanica od krivotvorenja, posebno u podruju skeniranja i kompjutorskog ispisa. Od uvoenja kune, u optjecaj je svake godine uvrtavan redovni optjecajni kovani novac s tekuom godinom izdanja. Imali smo i dodatnih dvanaest izdanja prigodnog optjecajnog kovanog novca, od kojih posebno izdvajamo kovani novac od 25 kuna kao tehnoloku inovaciju (dvodijelna kovanica dvanaesterokutnog oblika). Taje kovanica izdana u jedanaest razliitih izdanja, uz veliku potranju. Iz programa prigodnog kovanog novca i numizmatikih kompleta izdano je od svibnja 1994. do svibnja 2014. ukupno 37 razliitih izdanja zlatnog i srebrnog kovanog novca, kao i 25 razliitih numizmatikih kompleta kovanog novca. Redovni optjecajni kovani novac i prigodna izdanja kovanog novca kao i novanice, dobivaju mnoge pohvale, posebno u specijalistikim krugovima, kao primjer uspjenog dizajna i vrhunske izrade, to pridonosi uspjenom predstavljanju kako sredinje banke tako i zemlje u cjelini. Par rijei o budunosti kune. Kuna je, kako smo rekli, kao nacionalna valuta uvedena jo tijekom rata, no tek poto su se za to stekli uvjeti. A ti uvjeti su podrazumijevali makroekonomsku stabilnost. Uvoditi valutu koju bi od poetka pratila sudbina jugoslavenskog, pa zatim hrvatskog dinara, sudbina slabe valute koja sve manje vrijedi i koja zbog toga ne moe obnaati niti jednu od temeljnih funkcija novca, ne bi bilo dobro. Kuna je uvedena nakon provedbe stabilizacijskog programa iz 1993. godine, odnosno tek nakon to je eliminirana inflacija i stabiliziran teaj. To je od poetka omoguilo da kuna bude stabilna valuta i da preuzme znaajan dio funkcija novca koje njeni prethodnici nisu imali. Teaj kune nikada nije fiksiran, no, za razliku od jugoslavenskog i hrvatskog dinara, kretao se u ogranienom rasponu od 15.8 posto promjene vrijednosti u odnosu na euro, ime je doputena prilagodba teaja - petnaest posto fluktuacijskog raspona je znatno vie nego nula - i ostavljen dvostrani rizik kretanja teaja, koji je vaan u trgovini na deviznom tritu i poimanju teajnog rizika od strane sudionika na tom tritu, no, u isto vrijeme, sauvana je stabilnost, odnosno vrijednost domae valute. Zahvaljujui stabilnosti inflacije i teaja, kuna je u veoj mjeri od svojih prethodnika, jugoslavenskog i hrvatskog dinara, uspjela ostvariti temeljne funkcije novca, mjere vrijednosti, sredstva razmjene i pohrane vrijednosti. Prije uvoenja kune, jugoslavenski i hrvatski dinar nisu dominantno sluili niti kao sredstvo pohrane vrijednosti, niti kao mjera vrijednosti, a u velikoj mjeri niti kao sredstvo razmjene. Umjesto domaeg novca, tu je ulogu imala njemaka marka. Zato? Ukratko reeno, zbog loe ukupne ekonomske i monetarne politike, koja je monetarnim financiranjem deficita i deprecijacijom vrijednosti domae valute, pod parolom pomaganja dravi da se lake financira i poduzeima da budu konkurentnija, obezvrjeivala vrijednost nacionalne valute i time unitila povjerenje u nju. Do te mjere da ga ni danas, kad se radi o funkciji pohrane vrijednosti novca, nije mogue u potpunosti uspostaviti. Napose zato jer se graane esto neodgovorno plai pozivima na devalvaciju. Ne razumijevajui da se samim time ona ini manje moguom. Kuna danas, zahvaljujui 20 godina stabilnosti, ima gotovo u potpunosti funkciju sredstva razmjene, u najveoj mjeri mjere vrijednosti, no i dalje ima ogranienu funkciju pohrane vrijednosti. I dalje je, naime, najvei dio tednje u eurima. Greke slue da se neto iz njih naui. Monetarna politika u desetljeima prije uvoenja kune, koja se temeljila na monetiziranju fiskalnog deficita i takozvanim 'kompetitivnim devalvacijama', niti je dovela do stabilne fiskalne situacije niti do konkurentne ekonomije. Sve to je uspjela uiniti bilo je unitavanje povjerenja u domai novac. Nasuprot tome, one europske zemlje koje su se drale politike vrstog budetskog ogranienja sjedne i stabilne valute s druge strane, postigle su znatno bolje ekonomske rezultate od zemalja koje su se oslanjale na monetarno financiranje deficita i devalvacije. To nas, dakle, ui i naa i europska povijest. Takva politika, meutim, zahtijeva i odgovarajue institucije i dobre strukturne politike i fiskalnu disciplinu. Za to mnoge zemlje, ukljuujui nau, nisu bile spremne i zbog toga imaju gospodarske probleme. Kako su se kune stvarale? Kune su se u Hrvatskoj primarno kreirale na nain takozvanog kvazi valutnog odbora, intervencijama na deviznom tritu, odnosno otkupom deviza, a za sterilizaciju vika likvidnosti koristila se primarno stopa obvezne priuve. Zbog toga je i sterilizacija bila jeftinija, a sredinja banka je ostvarivala dobit, odnosno transferi dobiti sredinje banke u proraun bili su vei. Koristili su se i drugi instrumenti kreiranja i sterilizacije likvidnosti, no u puno manjoj mjeri. Iza svake kune ponude novca u Hrvatskoj postoji deviza u meunarodnim rezervama Hrvatske narodne banke, sigurno i likvidno investirana u najkvalitetniju imovinu. To predstavlja stabilan kamen temeljac teajne politike - visoku pokrivenost ponude novca i primarnog novca deviznim rezervama. To je kamen koji ne bi bilo mudro potkopavati, da se ne bi sruilo sve to stoji na njemu. Zamislimo, na trenutak, da nam teku sliku hrvatskog gospodarstva na zidu dre etiri vijka. Fiskalni, monetarni, strukturni i institucionalni. Pretpostavimo da dobro dri samo jedan, a tri su vie ili manje labava. Gdje treba uvrivati da se slika ne srui? Svaki dobar majstor bi trebao znati da ako krenemo viati jedini vijak koji jo vrsto dri, umjesto ostala tri, moglo bi se lako dogoditi ili da i taj raarafimo ili da pukne, uz jasne posljedice. Mnogi bi, unato tome, najradije arafili po ovom zaarafljenom, a nekako im se ba i neda po ostala tri. A upravo o tome to emo uiniti s ostala tri vijka ovisi hoemo li za deset godina slaviti 30. godinjicu kune ili ne. Budemo li ih zavidali, rekao bih da neemo, a ne budemo li, ih zavidali hoemo. Za razliku od nekih drugih stvari u ivotu, u ovom sluaju vea obljetnica bi mogla oznaavati neuspjeh, a ne uspjeh. Naravno, pretpostavka je da e eurozona za deset godina biti i dalje tu, kompletnija i time jaa. Hoemo li uspjeti izgraditi efikasne institucije, voditi politiku cikliki uravnoteenog prorauna i stvoriti povoljnu ulagaku klimu, sa to manje birokratskih zapreka, pravnih nesigurnosti, nepotrebnih propisa, sa to manje (kvazi)monopola na podruju trita roba i usluga, s dobro obrazovanom radnom snagom, da ne nabrajam sve strukturne reforme koje su potrebne, najvie ovisi o spremnosti drutva na reforme, odnosno o politikoj ekonomiji. A ona nije laka u drutvu s niskom zaposlenou, koje ubrzano stari. No, to je neto o emu ne bih danas, u ovom svearskom trenutku, kad slavimo jedan istinski uspjean projekt - 20 godina nacionalne valute kune. Zakljuio bih da stvarno moemo biti ponosni na ono to smo s nacionalnom valutom postigli, ali isto tako da moramo biti sjedne strane ambiciozni, a s druge oprezni, da to i sauvamo. Hvala!  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Thousands of financial ailments of a healthy society
text: Thousands of financial ailments of a healthy society Published: 15.4.2021. Kind Speaker Source Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor The EUROFI Magazine Although the magnitude of the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic may have exceeded the scale we have seen so far, the swift and decisive response of European economic policymakers could put them in the trap of complacency. While the closure measures sought to contain the virus, with a still scarce supply of vaccines, support in the form of unprecedented fiscal, monetary and regulatory stimulus has kept our economies afloat. Employment and incomes have shown remarkable resilience, and the financial sector, bolstered by a decade of continuous reforms, has supported businesses. But if we peek a little below the surface, old problems that require caution and vigilance are still visible. Indeed, the banking sector is operating at lower leverage, taking fewer risks, maintaining significant liquidity reserves and the generalenito has become much stronger and more resilient than it was a decade ago. Unlike the global financial crisis, when the financial system caused an initial shock and then continued to amplify it, this time the banks welcomed the blow ready, softened it and thus contributed to the stabilization of the economy. Nevertheless, profitability, which is their first protection against disruption, was subdued even before the crisis. This has gradually eroded banks' ability to finance the economy and serve as a transmissional mechanizam monetary policy. The reasons for the low profitability of banks are numerous. European regulators have not always resolutely enough to exclude unsuccessful banks with poor business models from the market. Such decisions are not always easy, as we at the Croatian National Bank know well. In the last two and a half decades, that is, since I first joined the CNB, the number of commercial banks operating in Croatia has decreased by two-thirds, from 60 to 20. This work has always been sensitive, full of legal and political meon, but it is an alternative to market oversaturation. overbanking) even worse, as we witness. Furthermore, banks are relatively slow to accept achievements in the field of information and, in particular, mobile technologies. After several decades of continuous warnings ofme that have often proven to be false alarms, the financial sector is forcing it to introduce new technological solutions faster and faster. In order to preserve the most profitable segments of the business, banks actually need to become technological centers. Technological transformation can makeyou painful for banks, especially for bankers, but it is the only way forward. Finally, a long period of highly accommodative monetary policy lowered interest margins and reduced revenues from the banks' core business. In the view of most analysts, it is notice that this pressure on margins will disappear in the near future. In addition to the business transformation, it will be particularly challenging for banks to face the consequences of the crisis. So far, a sharp increase in the number of insolvent companies has been avoided - the opposite has happened jer, and insolvency rates have even fallen below the levels recorded in good years. Nevertheless, the number of insolvent companies will gradually grow, in parallel with the withdrawal of comprehensive measures to support companies, even if the potentially destructive effects of the pre-withdrawal of measures are avoided. Banks will have to make complex decisions to restructure the debts of viable companies and stop supporting unsustainable companies. They should not take lightly the role of a "neural hub" that directs decisions to cleanse mastersof TV from "zombie" companies that survive thanks to abundant support but are not flexible enough to adapt to new circumstances. An old Indian proverb about a healthy man who has a thousand desires and a sick man who has only one can be well appliedto you to the conduct of politics. Once our societies have overcome the disease, we will again have to deal with a thousand of our ailments common in the financial sector, many of which have been exacerbated by the crisis. Ties between banks and the state are even stronger than before the crisis, corporate dynamism has decreased further, and banks may again face resolving a pile of bad debts. And the banking union isn't finished yet. And as we look forward to the cessation of the disease, we will again turn to a number of old, unresolved ailments. The article was published in The EUROFI Magazine.

Boris Vuji, guverner HNB-a The EUROFI Magazine lako je magnituda poremeaja koji je prouzroila pandemija bolesti COVID-19 moda premaila razmjere koje smo do sada imali prilike vidjeti, brza i odluna reakcija europskih nositelja ekonomskih politika mogla bi ih dovesti u zamku samozadovoljstva. Dok se mjerama zatvaranja nastojao obuzdati virus, uz jo uvijek oskudnu opskrbu cjepivima, potpora u obliku dosad nezabiljeenih fiskalnih, monetarnih i regulatornih poticaja odrala je naa gospodarstva na povrini. Zaposlenost i dohoci pokazali su iznimnu otpornost, a financijski sektor, ojaan desetljeem kontinuiranih reforma, podupro je poduzea. No, zavirimo li malo ispod povrine, i dalje su vidljivi stari problemi koji zahtijevaju oprez i budnost. Bankarski sektor doista posluje uz niu financijsku polugu, preuzima manje rizika, odrava znatne rezerve likvidnosti i openito je postao znatno snaniji i otporniji nego to je bio prije desetak godina. Za razliku od globalne financijske krize, kada je financijski sustav izazvao poetni ok i zatim ga nastavio pojaavati, ovog su puta banke udarac doekale spremne, ublaile su ga i tako pridonijele stabilizaciji gospodarstva. Ipak, profitabilnost, koja je njihova prva zatita od poremeaja, bila je priguena i prije krize. To je postupno nagrizalo sposobnost banaka da financiraju gospodarstvo i slue kao transmisijski mehanizam monetarne politike. Razlozi su za nisku profitabilnost banaka brojni. Europski regulatori nisu uvijek dovoljno odluno iskljuivali s trita neuspjene banke s loim poslovnim modelima. Takve odluke nisu uvijek lake, kao to to mi u Hrvatskoj narodnoj banci dobro znamo. U posljednja dva i pol desetljea, odnosno otkako sam se prvi put zaposlio u HNB-u, broj poslovnih banaka koje posluju u Hrvatskoj smanjio se za dvije treine, sa 60 na 20. Taj je posao oduvijek bio osjetljiv, pun pravnih i politikih mina, ali alternativa je prezasienosti trita (engl. overbanking) jo gora, emu svjedoimo. Nadalje, banke razmjerno sporo prihvaaju postignua iz podruja informacijskih i, posebice, mobilnih tehnologija. Nakon nekoliko desetljea kontinuiranih upozorenja koja su se esto pokazala lanim uzbunama, financijski sektor primoranje sve bre uvoditi nova tehnoloka rjeenja. Kako bi ouvale najprofitabilnije segmente poslovanja, banke zapravo trebaju postati tehnoloki centri. Tehnoloka transformacija moe biti bolna za banke, a pogotovo za bankare, ali ona je jedini put naprijed. Naposljetku, dugo razdoblje iznimno akomodativne monetarne politike snizilo je kamatne mare i smanjilo prihode od temeljnog posla banaka. Prema miljenju veine analitiara nije izgledno da e taj pritisak na mare nestati u bliskoj budunosti. Osim s poslovnom transformacijom, bankama e posebno izazovno biti suoiti se s posljedicama krize. Dosad je izbjegnut snaan porast broja insolventnih poduzea - dogodilo se upravo suprotno jer su stope insolventnosti ak pale ispod razina koje se biljee u dobrim godinama. Ipak, broj insolventnih poduzea postupno e rasti, usporedno s povlaenjem sveobuhvatnih mjera potpore poduzeima, ak i ako se izbjegnu potencijalno destruktivni uinci preranog povlaenja mjera. Banke e morati donijeti sloene odluke o restrukturiranju dugovanja odrivih poduzea i prestanku podupiranja neodrivih poduzea. Ne bi trebale olako shvatiti ulogu "neuralnog sredita" koje usmjerava odluke o ienju gospodarstva od "zombi" tvrtki koje preivljavaju zahvaljujui obilnoj potpori, ali nisu dovoljno fleksibilne da se prilagode novim okolnostima. Stara indijska poslovica o zdravom ovjeku koji ima tisuu elja i bolesnome koji ima samo jednu moe se dobro primijeniti na voenje politike. Nakon to naa drutva svladaju bolest, opet emo se morati baviti s tisuu naih boljki uobiajenih u financijskom sektoru, od kojih su mnoge pogorane krizom. Veze izmeu banaka i drave jo su snanije nego prije krize, dinamizam poduzea dodatno se smanjio, a banke e se moda ponovo suoiti s rjeavanjem gomile loih dugova. A bankovna unija jo nije dovrena. I dok se budemo radovali zbog prestanka bolesti, ponovo emo se okrenuti brojnim starim, nerijeenim boljkama. Tekst je objavljen u asopisu The EUROFI Magazine.  HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA

Title: Joining the banking union is a natural sequence
text: Entry into a banking union is a natural sequence Published: 18.5.2016. Speech Prof. Dr. Boris Vujcic, CNB Governor 18.5.2016. Banking Union Conference: achievements and challenges Croatian National Bank, Zagreb 18.5.2016. Banking Union Conference: achievements and challenges; Croatian National Bank, 18 May 2016 Presentation by Governor Boris Vujcic Dear guest, dear ladies and gentlemen, good morning and welcome to the Croatian National Bank. The aim of the conference is to exchange knowledge and views on the achievements achieved so far in building a banking union and the challenges ahead in its completion and full application. Just under a year ago, in the Five Presidents' Report, the completion of the banking union listed among the priorities for building a financial union, which is one of, I would agree with the Report, the main elements for achieving a full Economic and Monetary Union. It is therefore good to make an "inventory" of the progress made to discuss the phasesneeded for the banking union to fully come to life as a credible framework for crisis prevention and better crisis management. In my "inventory", I will look at three interrelated topics: 1) the reasons for building a banking union, fromwhy the European Union has decided to take such an important step in financial integration; 2) the measures taken so far in construction and the steps necessary to complete the banking union; and, finally, 3) the CNB's past experience with some elements of the banking union and attitude towards possible entry into the close cooperation mechanism before the official introduction of the euro. Reasons for the Banking Union The idea of stronger financial integration has been around since the first days of European economic integration. Already in the 1960s,elements were pouring in the then European Economic Community that, mutatis mutandis, to some extent correspond to some of the main parts of today's banking union. This was the harmonisation of the banking regulation of the EEC Member States, the cooperation of supervisory authorities and procedures for the liquidation of FInancial institutions. However, in the face of opposition from the then new Member States (in particular the United Kingdom), the Commission changed its approach in the 1970s and continued to work on individual directives that were more modest in its scope, from which a whole range of directives concerning banking originated (Mourlon-Druol, 2016). This early attempt to establish a single regulatory and supervisory framework speaks to the fact that some policymakers are already in the early stages of European integration clearly consideredbut the necessity of simultaneous financial integration, harmonisation of banking regulation and supervisory practices (although not at supranational level) and monetary integration, but these proposals were not accepted. Later, after the introduction of the single currency, it will prove that the construction of a common regulatory and supervisory framework is necessary for its functioning. The crisis has shown that the framework for European integration based on the single market and the Economic and Monetary Union, while at the same time having nation-basedpolicies on the banking issue, has failed to ensure financial stability, but has strengthened centrifugal powers. Excessive risks have been piling up in the European banking system for years, and in 2008 the financial crisis triggered by the external triggerblinked the era with full force. The materialisation of these risks with a high degree of financial integration and intensive cross-border activities by banks within the EU has threatened to strongly spill over negative financial stability shocks between Member States. This prompted the affected countries to try to stabilise national financial systems with budgetary resources. Stabilising banking systems in a situation where their assets outpace GDP many times proved too expensive for some member states, who then had to ask for international assistance themselves - which again spread waves of panic to financial markets. Thus, the stabilisation of national financial systems has clearly outgrown the fiscal capacity of individual members, and the unfavourable feedback loops betweennational banking systems and the fiscal positions of the countries in which they operate have become an important source of potential instability within the euro area. The Banking Union is therefore justified and necessary to break off the unfavourable feedback loops that threaten to maintain thevibrancy of the euro project and to the euro area itself. The situation in which the euro area finds itself is theoretically defined as a financial trilema, according to which it is impossible to achieve three objectives at the same time: financial stability, financial integration and financial policies at national level (Schoenmaker, 2011). Completion of the banking union made so far Since, we can say, the historic decisions on the establishment of the banking union in 2012 to the present day, great progress has been made in the construction of institutions and common rules. The European HeartBank has become a supervisory authority for banks, which as the fundamental assumption of the banking union has established a completely new set of functions in the institution, easily the SSM has been functioning since 2014, it remains to be seen its effects in its entirety. When thesecond pillar of the Banking Union - the Single Resolution Mechanism (SRM) is in place, its core components have been established, but its instruments have not yet been tested and there is no experience of its operation. Especially important are the challenges associated with the provedba of bail-in tools. With SRM, namely, there is a paradigm shift in terms of resolution of credit institutions. The SRM should mark a break with the application of the bail-out concept, under which bank bailouts could have required significant public funds engagement, and introduce the concept of bail-in, in which the costs of resolution are borne by unsecured creditors and specific funds for which the industry itself is gradually allocating funds. This may resultin changes in the behaviour of depositors and in banks' business models in the future. The third pillar - the common deposit insurance system - with which the banking union is just becoming complete, is still being negotiated with very modest progress. In doing so,member states' views on the preconditions and criteria that should be met before making progress with this measure of solidarity risk sharing are visible. Establishment common deposit insurance scheme, together with accompanying risk-limiting measures, n is anarrower condition for completing the banking union. The common rules and the possibility of participation in the SSM seek to preserve and further strengthen the common market for financial services. However, the introduction of two different banking supervision and resolution regimes, one for banks in the euro area, the other for banks in non-euro area countries, can undermine the level of playing field and put euro area banks in a somewhat more favourable position. Finally, this can lead to suboptimal capital realisation and introduce competitive distortions. This scenario is particularly relevant for CENTRAL and Eastern European countries that are outside the Banking Union and whose banks rely heavily on external financing. Due to the specifics in the design of the banking union, certain negative consequences for lay statesthat have not yet introduced the euro could remain if they decide to enter the banking union early. Furthermore, some elements concerning non-euro area Member States are also missing in the event of their earlier entry into the banking union. One of theh is equal treatment in relation to the issue of the common backstop (the so-called "1990s"). backstop). While there is an ESM for the euro area from which banks can be recapitalised and serves as a common backstop, non-euro area Member States cannotcount on its use. As we see, elements that are unclear in terms of implementation or simply missing may affect the overall credibility of the banking union at the present time, but also its attractiveness to Member States outside the euroarea. This brings us to the topic of the CNB's relationship with the banking union and the concluding notes. Croatian and Banking Union Croatia is obliged to adopt the euro as soon as it meets the conditions. Moreover, given the specifics of the Croatian economy, where I primarily mean a high degree of euroisation, we believe that the euro brings Croatia more benefits than costs. Deadlines are ungrateful to talk about, but the preference is to introduce the euro better sooner rather than later. Thus, entry into the banking union is a natural sequence and from such perspektiva we can certainly consider ourselves a future member of the banking union. But until we join the banking union, we still have the task of protecting our specific interests in the given environment. They are actually twofold - the seated parties in order to welcome entry into the banking union as readily as possible , it is necessary to work together on convergence towards supervisory practices defined by the European Supervisory Authority for banking (EBA), and on the other hand we will continue to do the best we can to protect taxpayers and depositors and to preserve financial stability in specific and challenging circumstances. Conclusion Finally, I would like to emphasize that the debate about the functioning of the banking union, as well as its shortcomings and ambiguities, should be understood as our interest in making the house we want to move into firm and orderly. This form of further integration is necessary to reduce fragmentation in the market, strengthen the euro area and, ultimately, build a full Economic and Monetary Union. In particular, as far as Croatia and the CNB are concerned, our previouscooperation with the SSM is of high quality and promising, which can guarantee a quality transition towards the SSM when the time comes. On the other hand, the experience of cooperation within the framework of the SRM is limited, which can be expected given that the whole mechanism hasonly started its work recently. Overall, however, we still have an incomplete banking union that needs to be completed as soon as possible. The completion of the banking union, as well as the extent to which countries that have not yet adopted the euro are taken into account, could affect the decision to enterthe banking union even before the introduction of the euro.
